[Corollary 18 of arXiv:2608.26618, 'A Unified Descriptive-Complexity Framework for Model Selection under Correlated Designs'] Suppose there exists a unique true pair \((m^*,S^*)\in\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}_n\), and for every $\lambda \geq \lambda_{\rm sel}$, assume the following conditions hold:

\begin{itemize}
\item[(\romannumeral 1)] For every \((m, S)\in \widetilde{\mathcal M}_{\mathrm{sup}}\), \(C_{(m^*, S)}\ge C_{(m^*,S^*)}\). In addition, there exist constants \(0<\widetilde c_1<c_1\) such that for all \(j\ge1\),
\[
\sum_{\substack{(m,S)\in\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}_{\mathrm{sup}}\\ \widetilde\Delta^+(S)=j}}
\exp\!\bigl\{-c_1\lambda^{\alpha/2}\bigl(C_{(m,S)}-C_{(m^*,S^*)}\bigr)\bigr\}
\le
\exp\!\bigl\{\widetilde c_1(\eta_n j)^{\alpha/2}\bigr\};
\]

\item[(\romannumeral 2)]There exists a sufficiently large constant $c_2>1$ such that, for every \((m,S)\in\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}_{\mathrm{sub}}\),
\[
\mathrm{APP}(m,S)\ge
c_2\Bigg(
\eta_n\bigl(s^*-s_{(m,S)}\bigr)
+\lambda\Bigl(C_{(m^*,S^*)}^{2/\alpha}-C_{(m,S)}^{2/\alpha}\Bigr)_+
+\log^{2/\alpha} \widetilde{N}\bigl(\widetilde\Delta^-(S)\bigr)
\Bigg);
\]

\item[(\romannumeral 3)] For every \((m,S)\in\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}_{\mathrm{w}}\) satisfying
\(2B_{(m,S)}>u_{(m,S)}\),
\[
\mathrm{APP}(m,S)\ge 2\bigl(2B_{(m,S)}-u_{(m,S)}\bigr).
\]
\end{itemize}

Then
\[
\Pr\bigl((\hat m,\hat S)=(m^*,S^*)\bigr)\to1.
\]

body: Let X be a Banach space. X is reflexive if and only if every continuous linear functional f in X* attains its supremum on the closed unit ball of X, that is, there exists x in X with ||x|| <= 1 and f(x) = ||f||. If X is reflexive, attainment follows from weak compactness of the closed unit ball together with weak continuity of f; the converse, that attainment for every functional forces reflexivity, is the deep part of the theorem. [James (1964, 1972); see Conway, A Course in Functional Analysis]
title: James's Theorem (Reflexivity via Attainment of the Norm)

body:
[Lemma 18 of arXiv:2606.09691, '\textsc{Degenerate Diffusions on Continuum Percolation and Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman Equatio'] Let $\P=\P^\zeta$ denote the supercritical Boolean model and define, for all $\omega\in\Omega_0$,
\[
B(\omega):=\mathbb R^d\setminus \mathcal C_\infty(\omega),
\qquad
\delta(\omega):=
\dist\bigl(0,B(\omega)\bigr)
=
\dist\bigl(0,\partial\mathcal C_\infty(\omega)\bigr).
\]
Then there exist constants $c,C,\varepsilon_0>0$ such that for all
$0<\varepsilon<\varepsilon_0$,
\[
c\,\varepsilon
\le
\P_0(\delta<\varepsilon)
\le
C\,\varepsilon.
\]
Consequently,
\[
\E_0[\delta^{-\chi}]<\infty
\qquad\Longleftrightarrow\qquad
\chi\in (0,1).
\]

[Lemma 15 of arXiv:2605.02771, 'Universality in Deep Neural Networks:\\ An approach via the Lindeberg exchange principle'] Let \(p\in\N\) be even, let \(n\in\N\), and let \(Y_1,\dots,Y_n\) be bounded real-valued random variables.
Set
\[
\overline Y_n:=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n Y_i,
\qquad
m:=\E[Y_1].
\]
Then there exists a constant \(C_p\), depending only on \(p\) and \(\sup_i\|Y_i\|_{L^\infty}\), such that
\[
\E\bigl[|\overline Y_n-m|^p\bigr]
\le
C_p
\sum_{\alpha=1}^p
\left|
\frac{1}{n^\alpha}
\sum_{i_1,\dots,i_\alpha=1}^{n}
\E\Bigl[\prod_{r=1}^\alpha Y_{i_r}\Bigr]
-
m^\alpha
\right|.
\]

[Lemma 12 of arXiv:2506.15159, 'Conditional central limit theorems for exponential random graphs'] (\cite[Theorem~3.7]{rollin2015})
    Let $(X, X^{\prime}, X^{\prime\prime})$ be three consecutive steps of a reversible Markov chain in equilibrium. Let $M: = M(X)$, $M^{\prime} := M(X^{\prime})$, and $M^{\prime\prime} := M(X^{\prime\prime})$ take
values on the integers $\mathbb{Z}$. Define
\begin{align*}
    &Q_{1}(x)=\mathbb{P}\left(M^{\prime}=M+1 \left.\right| X=x\right),\quad q_{1}=\IE Q_{1}(X)=\mathbb{P}(M^{\prime}=M+1),\\
    &Q_{1, 1}(x)=\mathbb{P}\left(M^{\prime}=M+1, M^{\prime \prime}=M^{\prime}+1\left.\right| X=x\right).
\end{align*}
Define $Q_{-1}(x)$ and $Q_{-1,-1}(x)$ similarly by changing all the $+1$ to $-1$.
Then, we have 
    \begin{align*}
       D(X) \leq &\frac{1}{q_{1}^{2}} \Big[2 \operatorname{Var} Q_{1}(X)+\IE\left|Q_{1, 1}(X)-Q_{1}(X)^{2}\right|\\
        &+2 \operatorname{Var} Q_{-1}(X)+\IE\left|Q_{-1,-1}(X)-Q_{-1}(X)^{2}\right|\Big].
    \end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma 12 of arXiv:2506.15159

body:
[Theorem 1.2 (McDiarmid’s inequality [18]) of arXiv:2110.05374, 'When Janson meets McDiarmid: Bounded difference inequalities under graph-dependence'] Let f : Ω → R be c-Lipschitz and let X = (X_1, ..., X_n) be a vector of independent random variables taking values in Ω. Then for every t > 0, P(f(X) − E[f(X)] ≥ t) ≤ exp(−2t²/‖c‖₂²). This is McDiarmid's bounded differences inequality (C. McDiarmid, On the method of bounded differences, Surveys in Combinatorics 1989, pp. 148-188; reference [18] of the paper), which arXiv:2110.05374 restates as its starting point; it is not a result of that paper.
c-Lipschitz (Definition 1.1 of the paper): Ω = Ω_1 × ... × Ω_n is a product of Polish spaces, c = (c_1, ..., c_n) ∈ R_+^n, and f : Ω → R is c-Lipschitz when |f(x) − f(x')| ≤ Σ_{i=1}^n c_i 1{x_i ≠ x'_i} for all x, x' ∈ Ω (Lipschitz for the c-weighted Hamming distance).

Let mu be a probability measure on R^n satisfying a logarithmic Sobolev inequality with constant C, that is Ent_mu(f^2) <= 2 C E_mu[|grad f|^2] for all locally Lipschitz f. Then for every 1-Lipschitz F with E_mu[F] finite and every real lambda, E_mu[ exp( lambda (F - E F) ) ] <= exp( C lambda^2 / 2 ), and consequently mu( F - E F >= t ) <= exp( - t^2 / (2C) ) for every t > 0, with the same bound for the lower tail. For the standard Gaussian, C = 1 by the Gaussian logarithmic Sobolev inequality, giving the sharp Gaussian concentration bound exp(-t^2/2) for 1-Lipschitz functions. The argument converts a functional inequality into an exponential moment bound and is the reason log-Sobolev, rather than Poincare, is the inequality one wants: Poincare alone yields only exponential, not Gaussian, tails. The hypothesis is a Lipschitz bound on F with respect to the EUCLIDEAN metric; changing the metric changes the effective constant. [Herbst, unpublished; see Ledoux, The Concentration of Measure Phenomenon, Chapter 5]
mu satisfies a logarithmic Sobolev inequality with constant C
F is 1-Lipschitz with respect to the Euclidean metric
E_mu[F] finite

[Theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] We have spherical coordinates in $N$ dimensions,
$$\begin{cases}
x_1\!\!\!&=\ r\cos t_1\\
x_2\!\!\!&=\ r\sin t_1\cos t_2\\
\vdots\\
x_{N-1}\!\!\!&=\ r\sin t_1\sin t_2\ldots\sin t_{N-2}\cos t_{N-1}\\
x_N\!\!\!&=\ r\sin t_1\sin t_2\ldots\sin t_{N-2}\sin t_{N-1}
\end{cases}$$
the corresponding Jacobian being given by the following formula,
$$J(r,t)=r^{N-1}\sin^{N-2}t_1\sin^{N-3}t_2\,\ldots\,\sin^2t_{N-3}\sin t_{N-2}$$
and with this generalizing the known formulae at $N=2,3$.

body:
[Proposition 25 (Exact spectral decomposition and crossover boundary) of arXiv:2609.02728, 'Momentum in large-batch training: Polyak enlarges the critical batch size, Nesterov improv'] For each coordinate $j$, the characteristic roots of the Nesterov recursion are
\[
    y_{j,\pm}
    =
    \frac{(1+\rho)(1-\eta\lambda_j)\pm\sqrt{\Delta_j^{\nesterov}}}{2},
\]
where
\[
    \Delta_j^{\nesterov}
    :=
    (1+\rho)^2(1-\eta\lambda_j)^2
    -4\rho(1-\eta\lambda_j).
\]
In the stable small-step range $0<\eta\lambda_j<1$, the critical transition $\Delta_j^{\nesterov}=0$ corresponds exactly to
\[
    \eta\lambda_j
    =
    \frac{(1-\rho)^2}{(1+\rho)^2},
\]
which is asymptotically equivalent to $\eta\lambda_j\eqsim(1-\rho)^2$. Thus the individual eigen-directions are classified as follows:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item \textbf{Overdamped Modes} $\bigl(\eta\lambda_j<(1-\rho)^2/(1+\rho)^2\bigr)$: the roots are real.
    \item \textbf{Underdamped Modes} $\bigl(\eta\lambda_j>(1-\rho)^2/(1+\rho)^2\bigr)$: the roots form a complex-conjugate pair.
\end{enumerate}
In the mixed-damping regime, the boundary index $J_{\max}$ separating the underdamped modes from the overdamped modes is defined by the crossover relation $\eta\lambda_{J_{\max}}\eqsim(1-\rho)^2$:
\begin{equation}

    J_{\max}
    \eqsim
    \left(\frac{\eta}{(1-\rho)^2}\right)^{1/\beta}.
\end{equation}
Consequently, based on the maximum eigenvalue $\lambda_{\max}$, Nesterov operates in one of two global regimes:
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Fully Overdamped Regime} $\bigl(\eta\lambda_{\max}\lesssim(1-\rho)^2\bigr)$: all spectral modes are overdamped.
    \item \textbf{Mixed-Damping Regime} $\bigl(\eta\lambda_{\max}\gtrsim(1-\rho)^2\bigr)$: the high-curvature modes $j\le J_{\max}$ are underdamped, whereas the flat modes $j>J_{\max}$ are overdamped.
\end{itemize}

[Theorem th:main of arXiv:2412.09667, 'Spatial preferential attachment with choice-based edge step'] In the model described above
\begin{enumerate}
\item if $a+d\alpha<1$, then for any $\epsilon>0$ 
$$\Pr\left(\forall n>N: n^{a+d\alpha-\epsilon}<M_1(n)<n^{a+d\alpha+\epsilon}\right)\to 1$$
as $N\to\infty$.
\item if $a+d\alpha=1$, then almost surely
$$\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{M_1(n)\ln n}{n}=\frac{2}{(d\alpha)^2}.$$
\item if $a+d\alpha>1$, then for all $k\leq K$ almost surely
$$\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{M_k(n)}{n}=x_k^{\ast}.$$
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

            \# 
            K_r(u)

    \end{equation}

[Lemma 10 of arXiv:2605.12475, 'Central limit theorem for the homozygosity of the hierarchical Pitman-Yor process'] For all $m \geq 1$ and $L \geq 1$, 
\bal
\sum_{i=1}^\infty \sum_{\bm{m} \in M_{m,L}} \E\left[ \prod_{\ell=1}^L W_{\ell i}^{m_\ell} \middle\vert \bm{V}, \gamma_{1/\beta} \right] &= \sum_{j=1}^m A_j(\beta, m, L) \gamma_{1/\beta}^j \sum_{i=1}^\infty V_i^j, \\
\sum_{i=1}^\infty \sum_{\bm{m} \in M_{m,L}} \E\left[ \prod_{\ell=1}^L W_{\ell i}^{m_\ell} \middle\vert \bm{V} \right] &= \sum_{j=1}^m A_j(\beta, m, L) \frac{\prod_{s=0}^{j-1} (\theta + s\beta)}{\beta^j} \sum_{i=1}^\infty V_i^j. 
\eal (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma 10 of arXiv:2605.12475

[Theorem 11 of arXiv:2609.01770, 'Support of Dyson Brownian Motion'] We assume that there exists a constant $K_0>0$
\begin{equation}
  \operatorname{supp}\mu_0
  \subset[-K_0,K_0]
  
\end{equation}
For every \(\varepsilon>0\) and \(\sfT>0\), there exist
\(
  C=C(\varepsilon,\sfT,K_0,\beta)>0
\)
such that, for $n$ large enough,
\begin{equation}
   \mathbb P\left(
    \Lambda_n(t)\subset S_t^{[\varepsilon]}
    \text{ for every }0\leq t\leq \sfT
  \right)
  \geq
  1-Ce^{-(\log n)^2}.
  
\end{equation}
where $S_t^{[\varepsilon]}$ denotes the closed $\varepsilon$-neighborhood
of $S_t$
\[
  S_t^{[\varepsilon]}
  :=
  \left\{
    x\in\mathbb R:
    \operatorname{dist}(x,S_t)\le\varepsilon
  \right\}.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 11 of arXiv:2609.01770

[Lemma lem:af-escape-final of arXiv:2602.21315, 'The Instability of all Backoff Protocols\thanks{For the purpose of Open Access, the author'] Fix a send sequence $\overline{p}$ with $p_0 = 1$ and finitely many strongly-exposed bins, and fix $\lambda \in (0,1)$ with $\lambda$ sufficiently small. Let $\Psi = (g,\tau,j,\overline{z},\mathcal{S},\textup{type})$ be a high-level state with $j$ sufficiently large. 
Suppose that $\mathcal{S}$ contains a set $S$ such that $|S| \ge C_{\Upsilon} \mathrm{L}(j)/(2\lambda)$ and $|S|\cdot \min\{W_k\colon k \in S\} \ge (j-1)/2$. 
Fix a tuple $\overline{a} \in (\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0})^j$
such that $\overline{a}$ is a $j^7$-AF-good beginning. Let $E$ be an escape process with high-level state $\Psi$, send sequence $\overline{p}$, and birth rate $\lambda$.
Fix $\tau' \ge \tau$. Then with probability at least 
$1 - \exp({-400 j/\lambda^2})$, conditioned on the event $\overline{b}_{[j]}^E(\tau') = \overline{a}$, the following properties hold.
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item For all $t$ in the range $\tau' \le t \le \tau' + (4/\lambda)^{2j}$, $\overline{b}_{[j]}^E(t)$ is a $(6j^{25},j^{27},2/(\xi j^3),2)$-RS-good beginning.
\item For all $t$ in the range $\tau' + j^{22} \le t \le \tau' + (4/\lambda)^{2j}$, $\overline{b}_{[j]}^E(t)$ is a $j^7$-AF-good beginning.
\item For all $t$ in the range $\tau' \le t \le \tau' + (4/\lambda)^{2j}$, $\mathcal{N}_S^E(t+1) \le \lambda|S|/80$.
\item For all $k\in [j]$ with $W_k \ge j^\chi$ and all $t$ in the range $\tau' \le t \le \tau' + (4/\lambda)^{2j}$, $p_kb_k^E(t) \le \lambda/80$.           
\end{enumerate}

[Definition def:local-sparse-four-cycle-incidence of arXiv:2607.05384, 'Well-invertible column subsets of sparse matrices are rare'] Let $G^{(k)}=(I^{(k)},J^{(k)},E^{(k)})$ be a sequence of bipartite graphs with
\[
|I^{(k)}|=k,\qquad |J^{(k)}|=n_k.
\]
For right vertices $j,j'\in J^{(k)}$, we say that $j'$ is a \hyperref[def:local-sparse-four-cycle-incidence]{\textcolor{PineGreen}{\emph{four-cycle partner}}}{} of $j$ if
\[
j'\ne j
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
|N_{G^{(k)}}(j)\cap N_{G^{(k)}}(j')|\ge2.
\]
Equivalently, the two right vertices lie together in at least one $4$-cycle.

The sequence $G^{(k)}$ has \textcolor{PineGreen}{\emph{local sparse four-cycle incidence}} if there are numbers $\varepsilon_k\to0$ such that the bad set
\[
B_{\mathrm{fc}}^{(k)}
:=
\Big\{ j\in J^{(k)}:\ j\text{ has more than }\varepsilon_k\frac{n_k}{k}\,\text{\hyperref[def:local-sparse-four-cycle-incidence]{\textcolor{PineGreen}{\emph{four-cycle partner}}}{}s}\Big\}
\]
satisfies $|B_{\mathrm{fc}}^{(k)}|=o(n_k)$.
title: Local sparse four-cycle incidence

ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Reduce to the scaling limit of the IIC itself (C0077) plus a homogenisation of the walk on the limit tree. Result: If the IIC converges (as a measure-valued process indexed by intrinsic distance) to incipient infinite super-Brownian motion, then the walk on the IIC should converge to the Brownian motion on the associated continuum random tree embedded in R^d, time-changed by the IIC volume measure, i.e. to the 'Brownian motion on the ISE-type tree' with spatial displacement given by the embedding (the Ben Arous-Cabezas-Fribergh limit). The walk on the discrete tree structure of the IIC is a random walk on a graph that is tree-like at all scales in d > 6 (the number of cycles at scale r is bounded), so the spatial position is a Brownian motion time-changed by the intrinsic clock; the intrinsic clock converges by the tree scaling limit; the embedding of the tree in R^d is a branching random walk-type embedding whose limit is the ISE embedding. Each step is known for the branching random walk trace (BCF 2016) and the difficulty for the IIC is the dependence between the tree structure and the embedding (loops, self-intersections). The rigorous reduction: the walk's scaling limit follows from (i) the IIC tree scaling limit with its embedding, (ii) a resistance estimate showing the effective resistance across the IIC at intrinsic distance r is of order r (tree-like), which is known up to constants from Kozma-Nachmias-type estimates. So the problem is subsumed by C0077 plus a resistance-form convergence theorem (Croydon's framework), which needs the convergence of the IIC as a resistance metric space, a stronger statement than the measure-valued convergence in the source. Obstruction: Resistance-metric convergence of the IIC in d > 6 is not established.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-c0074-scaling-limit-of-random-walk-on-the-high-dimensional-incipient-infinit

[Cor box-polylogarithmic-comparison of arXiv:2609.03856, 'Consensus time for asynchronous $\ell^p$ relaxation: graph dependence'] Under the hypotheses of Theorem~(thm:box-bounds of the paper), define
\[
 U_p(d,L)=
 \begin{cases}
  nd^{1/(p-1)}L^{p/(p-1)},&1<p<2,\\
  ndL^2,&p\ge2.
 \end{cases}
\]
Then
\begin{equation}
 \sup_{f_0\in[-1,1]^{[L]^d}}\mathbb{E}\tau_p(1/2;f_0)
 \ge c_p
 \begin{cases}
  U_p(d,L)/\log(en),&p\ne2,\\
  U_2(d,L),&p=2.
 \end{cases}
\end{equation}
Consequently, at fixed tolerance $1/2$, the upper and lower bounds in
Theorem~(thm:box-bounds of the paper) differ by at most
$O_p((\log n)^2)$ for $p\ne2$ and by at most $O(\log n)$ for $p=2$.
The causal-profile term by itself leaves a factor $d$.  Once the coupon term
is included, however, the pointwise discrepancy can be smaller; see

[Lemma of arXiv:2608.25065, 'Detection of first homology via random geometric graphs in the thermodynamic regime'] \label[lemma]{decomposition}
    Let $\mathcal{O}$
    be a finite open
    cover of $M$.
    
    Let $L > 0$
    be such that
    for any $x \in M$
    there exists some $U = U(x) \in \mathcal{O}$ such that
    \[
        \bar{B}(x,L) \subseteq U.
    \]

    Moreover, for some $Q, \rho \ge 1$, let
    $K = 4Q\rho r|\log r|$, and suppose that $\Delta$ satisfies
    \[
        \sup_{x \in M}
        \#
        \{U \in \mathcal{O}:B(x,(\Delta+1)K) \cap U \ne \emptyset \}
        \le 
        \Delta.
    \]

    If $L \ge (\Delta + 1)K + 2r$
    and $r$ satisfies
    (equation r small enough of the paper),
    then, on $A_{Q,\rho}(r)$, the following holds:

    For any $z \in Z_1(\mathring{G}^n_M(r))$
    such that $z = \partial \sigma$
    for some $\sigma \in C_2(M)$,
    we have a decomposition
    \[
        z = \sum_{U \in \mathcal{O}} z_U,
    \]
    where for each $U \in \mathcal{O}$ we have 
    $z_U \in Z_1(\mathring{G}^n_M(r))$
    and $|z_U| \subseteq U$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Notes: beta^{-1} = 1/log_2(4/3) = 2.40942 - the same constant as the NAE three-circuit floor, appearing here as the price of the exchange. The invariance of L under the exchange is what makes the charge additive rather than multiplicative.

body: [campaign status: partial_result - author-checked, unrefereed] Bradley, Basic properties of strong mixing conditions: a survey and some open questions (arXiv:math/0511078), Question 7 (Section 4.2, p. 19) asks: given an arbitrary nonincreasing sequence (b_1, b_2, ...) in [0,1], is there a strictly stationary sequence X with phi(n) = b_n for all n >= 1? Our result (id D0035, 2026-09-08): NO, refuted in one line from a result Bradley himself quotes - if phi(n) < 1/2 for some n >= 1 then X is phi-mixing, i.e. phi(n) tends to 0. The constant sequence b_n = 1/4 is nonincreasing and lies in [0,1] and gives phi(1) = 1/4 < 1/2, which forces phi(n) to tend to 0 and contradicts phi(n) = 1/4 for every n; the same argument rules out every sequence that dips below 1/2 without tending to zero. Verification as the source words it: this one came from the intake agent rather than from the author, and was verified by pulling the archived source, reading Question 7 at the stated locator word for word, and locating the quoted dichotomy in the survey. Honest scope, in the memo's own words: the literal general form is refuted from the survey's own material, not that a question its author believed open has been settled. Status: proof (unaudited), owner campaign claim T410-w739-C001 version 2; independent review pending. Assume a deterministic polynomial-time one-way function family secure against every polynomial-size nonuniform randomized circuit family. There is a uniformly polynomial-time weighted binary law P_L for every L, even with efficiently computable normalized probabilities and an efficient sampler, such that for every polynomial-size AR family with polynomial-bit parameters and polynomial-time absolute-precision next-bit evaluation, and every a>0, KL(P_L||Q_L)>a log L eventually. In particular the inverse-polynomial gap in Target 1 holds under this explicit circuit-secure OWF formulation. The law uses the fixed token order padded function output, uniform preimage, zero padding. The information-theoretic reduction gives ideal inversion success at least exp(-KL); rounding the n suffix kernels at precision t loses at most n*2^(1-t). This is not a proof that worst-case NP hardness alone is insufficient, and no novelty priority is asserted.
Nonuniform-secure OWF; ordinary uniform-only OWF security is not silently upgraded
Fixed output-before-preimage left-to-right binary token order
Polynomial-time next-bit probability computation to absolute precision 2^-t in poly(L,t) time
Polynomial circuit size and polynomial bit-length parameters; eventual threshold may depend on the model family

[Lemma 11 of arXiv:2604.12233, 'An upper bound on the smallest singular value of dense random combinatorial matrices'] Fix $b>0$ and $\gamma\in (0,1)$. Let $d\leq n$ be positive integers. 
    Let $v\in \R^{n}$ satisfy $\|D(v)\|_2\ge b\sqrt{n}$. Suppose that $\eta$ is a random vector uniformly distributed over $n$-dimensional $0/1$ vectors having  exactly $d$ ones.  Then for every $\alpha>0$ and $\varepsilon\ge 0$,
    \begin{equation*}
        \Ls\lr{\sum_{i=1}^n v_i\eta_i, \varepsilon\sqrt{\frac{d}{n}}}\le \frac{\varepsilon}{\gamma b}+\frac{1}{\gamma b}\sqrt{\frac{n}{d}}\cdot \frac{1}{\mbox{CLCD}_{\alpha,\gamma}(v)}+2e^{-4\alpha^2d/n^2}.
    \end{equation*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma 11 of arXiv:2604.12233

[Corollary cor:local-bi-lipschitz of arXiv:2609.03264, 'Certified Spherical MUSIC for 3D Localization under Adversarial Subspace Perturbations'] Let
\[
    d_{\rm sp}(X,Y)
    :=
    \|P_{\mathcal U_X}-P_{\mathcal U_Y}\|_2,\qquad 
  \forall  X,Y\in
    \mathfrak X_{s,\kappa}
    (\gamma,\overline\mu).
\]

Then
\[
    d_{\rm sp}(X,Y)
    \leq
    \frac{\kappa\sqrt{s}}
         {\sqrt{3(1-\overline\mu)}}
    d_{\rm match}(X,Y).
\]
If, in addition, \(d_{\rm sp}(X,Y)<\eta_\star\), then
\[
    d_{\rm match}(X,Y)
    \leq
    \frac{2}
         {\sqrt3\,c_{\rm sp}(X,Y)}
    \frac{d_{\rm sp}(X,Y)}{\kappa},
\]
where
\[
    c_{\rm sp}
    :=
    \frac23-\overline C_2
    -
    \left(\frac2{\sqrt5}+\frac23\right)d_{\rm sp}.
\]
Consequently, the configuration-to-subspace map is locally
bi-Lipschitz, with constants depending only on
\((\gamma,\overline\mu,s)\).
title: Local bi-Lipschitz stability

DRAFT scoped boundary result; written proof independently checked by w476, served-model diversity gate pending. For each 0<gamma<3, take a stationary unit-variance Gaussian field G on Z^3 with covariance R_gamma(z)=(1+|z|^2)^(-gamma/2), and set sigma_x=sign(G_x). The bounded spin field is stationary, spin-flip symmetric, positively associated, has two-point covariance (2/pi)arcsin R_gamma(z) asymptotic to (2/pi)|z|^(-gamma), and has on-site fourth cumulant -2. Yet for each finite list of compactly supported smooth tests f, the normalized sums N^(-3+gamma/2) sum_x f(x/N)sigma_x converge jointly to a centered Gaussian vector with covariance (2/pi) double_integral f(u)h(v)|u-v|^(-gamma) du dv. This refutes only a proposed implication from association, anomalous two-point decay and a local fourth cumulant to non-Gaussian smeared limits. The field is not shown to be a nearest-neighbor Ising Gibbs state or to satisfy random-current identities.

[Theorem 6 of arXiv:2606.24323, 'Conditioning of incoherent sub-dictionaries sampled from a coherent dictionary'] Let $H$ be a real $K\times K$ matrix with zero diagonal, $M$ a symmetric $K\times K$ matrix with zero diagonal and entries in $\{0,1\}$ and $p\in (0,1)^K$. 
Further, let $\wm$ be the diagonal matrix with $\wm_{ii} = \sqrt{p_i}$, $\bar M$ be the complement matrix to $M$, ie. $\bar M_{ij}: = 1- M_{ij}$, and $\hat H$ be any matrix that coincides with $H$ on $\bar M$, that is for the Hadamard (entry-wise) product we have $\bar M \odot \hat H = \bar M \odot H$. Denoting with $\P_\mu$ the coherence rejective sampling measure associated with $M$ and $p$ from Definition~\ref{coh_rej_sampling}, we then have for any $r\geq 6 \|\wm \hat H \wm \|$ 
\begin{align*}
\P_\mu(\|D_I H D_I\| \geq r) \leq 108 K \exp\left( - \min\left\{ \frac{r}{6 \|\bar M \odot\hat H\|_{\infty,1}}, \frac{r^2}{36\|\wm \hat H\|_{2,1}^2 },\frac{r^2}{36\| \hat H \wm \|_{\infty,2}^2 }\right\} \right).
\end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Proposition 21 (Partial proof of Hypothesis~\ref{hyp:red}) of arXiv:2608.15987, 'Threshold cascades of interacting diffusions on unimodular random trees: a conditional bra'] In the saturated regime of Definition~\ref{def:saturated}:
\begin{enumerate}
\item (Single-cell correctness.) For an isolated parent--child pair the transmission probability equals \eqref{eq:wald} exactly. The error from treating the pair as isolated, when embedded in a tree, is $O(\varepsilon(\delta))$ per edge: the only neighbours that could perturb $v$'s drift before it crosses are siblings of $v$, which are absent on a tree (each $v$ has a unique parent), and the grandparent, whose influence is screened by the saturated parent.
\item (Back-reaction does not couple siblings.) The back-reaction $v\to u$ adds $+\gamma$ to the already-failed parent's drift; since $u\in B_{\mathrm{fail}}$ has $\sigma(s^{(u)}-\theta_{uw})\ge1-\varepsilon(\delta)$ for every child $w$, the extra forcing changes each child's forcing by at most $\gamma\,\sigma'(\cdot)\le\gamma\,\varepsilon(\delta)$. Hence $\Cov(\chi_{uv},\chi_{uw})=O(\varepsilon(\delta))$, vanishing as $\delta\to\infty$.
\item (Short cycles vanish.) On $G_n\xrightarrow{\mathrm{BS}}T$ the probability that a fixed vertex has two distinct failed neighbours through a cycle of length $\le L$ is $O(c_L(G_n))$, the density of length-$\le L$ cycles through a uniform root, which $\to0$ for every fixed $L$ by local weak convergence to a tree.
\end{enumerate}
Consequently the per-edge marginal and the sibling-independence parts (Hypothesis~\ref{hyp:red}(i)--(ii) within a single generation, and (iii)) hold up to $O(\varepsilon(\delta)+\eta_n)$.

[Theorem th:ERB of arXiv:2510.10299, '\Large Sparse graphs and their Benjamini-Schramm limits: a spectral tour'] Let $d > 0$, $G$ be an Erd\H{o}s–Rényi graph on $n$ vertices and edge probability $\min(1,d/n)$. Let  {$\lambda_1 , \lambda_2 , \ldots $ the eigenvalues of its non-backtracking operator $B$ indexed as in (equation eq:eigB of the paper)}. Then for every $\epsilon >0$, the event 
$$
|\lambda_1 - d | \leq \epsilon \quad \text{and} \quad 
|\lambda_2| \leq \sqrt{\lambda_1}  + \epsilon
$$
has probability tending to $1$ as $n \to \infty$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

For $a<b$, define the symmetrized interval characteristic function by
\[\chi_{a,b}(y)=\one_{(a,b)}(y)+\frac{1}{2}\one_{\{a\}}(y)+\frac{1}{2}\one_{\{b\}}(y).\]
For every $\varepsilon>0$, there exist bounded, real-valued, integrable functions $g^-_{\varepsilon}$ and $g^+_{\varepsilon}$ such that
\[g^-_{\varepsilon}\leq\chi_{a,b}\leq g^+_{\varepsilon}\quad\text{and}\quad\int_{\R}(g^+_{\varepsilon}-g^-_{\varepsilon})dy<\varepsilon,\]
and both Fourier transforms are continuous and compactly supported.

body:
Let N take values in {0, 1, ..., m} and F_r = E[binom(N, r)] for r = 0, ..., m (F_0 = 1). Then for k = 0, ..., m, P(N = k) = sum_{r=k}^m (-1)^(r - k) binom(r, k) F_r, and for k = 1, ..., m, P(N >= k) = sum_{r=k}^m (-1)^(r - k) binom(r - 1, k - 1) F_r. For the number of events that occur, F_r = S_r, the r-th intersection sum, so the probability that exactly k (or at least k) of the events occur is determined by S_k, ..., S_m.

[Proposition prop_initial of arXiv:2411.16572, 'Optimal decay of eigenvector overlap for non-Hermitian random matrices'] Fix small constants $\epsilon,\tau>0$. The following hold
	\begin{align}
		&\Big| \big(G^{z_1}(\mathrm{i} \eta_1) A_1 G^{z_2}(\mathrm{i} \eta_2)-M_{12}^{A_1}\big)_{{\bm x} {\bm y}}\Big| \prec \frac{\sqrt{\rho^*}}{\sqrt{n} \eta_*^{3/2}}, \\
		&\Big|\big\langle \big(G^{z_1}(\mathrm{i} \eta_1) A_1 G^{z_2}(\mathrm{i} \eta_2)-M_{12}^{A_1}\big)A_2\big\rangle\Big|\prec \frac{1}{n\eta_*^2},
	\end{align}
	uniformly for any $|z_i| \leq 1+\tau$, $\min_{i=1}^2 \{|\eta_i| \rho_i \} \geq n^{-1+\epsilon}$, any deterministic matrices $\|A_1\|+\|A_2\|\lesssim 1$ and unit vectors ${\bm x}, {\bm y}$. Here $\rho_i : =\rho^{z_i}(\mathrm{i} \eta_i)$,
	 $\eta_*:=\min_{i=1}^2|\eta_i|$, $\rho^*:=\max_{i=1}^2\rho_i$, and $M_{12}^{A_1}$ is given in ((eq:defM12 of the paper)). 
	 Moreover, recalling $M_{121}^{A_1,A_2}$ defined in ((eq:defM121 of the paper)), we also have the following estimate for three resolvents
	 \begin{align}
	 \Big|\big(G^{z_1}(\mathrm{i} \eta_1)A_1G^{z_2}(\mathrm{i} \eta_2)A_2G^{z_1}(\mathrm{i} \eta_1)-M_{121}^{A_1,A_2}\big)_{{\bm x} {\bm y}}\Big| \prec \frac{1}{\eta_*^2}.
	 \end{align}\normalcolor (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition def:upward-boundary of arXiv:2505.02685, 'On the Spectral Expansion of Monotone Subsets of the Hypercube'] For all $f:\{0,1\}^{n}\rightarrow\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}$, we define
\[
\ensuremath{\mathcal{E}}^{-}(f)\vcentcolon= \frac{1}{4}\cdot \Exu{x\in \{0,1\}^{n}}{\sum_{i=1}^{n}\min\left\{0,f(x^{i\rightarrow 1})-f(x^{i\rightarrow 0})\right\}^{2}}.
\]
Here for $x\in\{0,1\}^{n}$ and $b\in \{0,1\}$, $x^{i\rightarrow b}$ stands for the string $(x_{1},\dots,x_{i-1},b,x_{i+1},\dots,x_{n})$.

Drinfeld--Jimbo algebra over $\Q[[h]]$, in the convention
\[
 q=e^{h/2},\qquad K_j=e^{hH_j/2}.
\]
The restriction of $\operatorname{sp}_h$ to
$\cZ_{n,\mathrm{fin}}$ extends uniquely to a continuous injective
algebra homomorphism
\begin{equation}
 \iota_h^{\cZ}:\widehat{\cZ}^{\mathrm{BG}}_n
 \lhook\joinrel\longrightarrow Z_h.
\end{equation}
It intertwines the preceding central automorphisms with
\[
 \vartheta_h(H_j)=-H_{n+1-j},\qquad
 \delta_{c,h}(H_j)=H_j+c,
\]
and their values on $E_i,F_i$ from
\eqref{eq:vartheta-definition}--\eqref{eq:delta-definition}:
\begin{equation}
 \iota_h^{\cZ}\circ\vartheta
 =\vartheta_h\circ\iota_h^{\cZ},
 \qquad
 \iota_h^{\cZ}\circ\delta_c
 =\delta_{c,h}\circ\iota_h^{\cZ}.
\end{equation}

[Defi Weighted Space of arXiv:2608.29013, 'Weighted Homology and Cohomology of Weighted Polyhedra'] A \emph{weighted space} is a pair $(X,\lambda)$ where
  $X$ is a topological space and $\lambda: X\rightarrow \mathbb Z_+$.
 Two weighted spaces $(X,\lambda)$ and $(X',\lambda')$ are called \emph{isomorphic} if there exists a homeomorphism $f: X\rightarrow X'$ such that $f$ is weight-preserving, i.e. $\lambda'(f(x))=\lambda(x)$ for any $x\in X$.

Let $N_n$ be the number of open sites $z\in \Lambda_n$ such that $z$ has an open arm that goes Euclidean distance at least $1/2$. [Lem bivpoly of arXiv:2412.00593, 'A new approach to strong convergence II.\\The classical ensembles'] For every $P\in\mathrm{M}_D(\mathbb{C})\otimes
\mathbb{C}\langle\boldsymbol{\hat s}\rangle$, 
there is a polynomial $\Phi$ so that
$$
	\mathbf{E}[\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}
        P(\boldsymbol{\hat G}^{N,T})] =
	\Phi(\tfrac{1}{N^2},\tfrac{1}{T})
	\quad\text{for all }N,T\in\mathbb{N}.
$$

[Thm thm-BBG17-4.3 of arXiv:2608.30807, 'Isodiametric-type upper bounds for Steklov eigenvalues'] {BBG17}}]
Let $\Omega\subset \mathbb{R}^n$ be a bounded Lipschitz domain. Then there exists a constant $C(n)>0$ such that for every $k\in \mathbb{N}$, we have
\begin{align}
D(\Omega)\sigma_k(\Omega)\leq C(n)k^{1+\frac{2}{n}}.
\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

UNAUDITED SOURCE QUALIFICATION. Fix alpha=1/100 and any fixed rational p in(0,1). Let n(lambda)>=1 be polynomially bounded and polynomial-time computable, h=32*n, T=ceil(h/p)+2, and let q>=2 be an efficiently samplable power of two of polynomial size. There is an efficient language model over q nonterminal symbols and END, with a uniform h-token prefix followed by a fixed legal deterministic suffix and total output length T, for which no sound, undetectable watermark can satisfy the literal full-text experiment of Golowich-Moitra Definition2.6 for all p-edit-bounded channels at threshold beta(ell)=8*n+6*alpha*ell (or its ceiling). Specifically, a word-only PPT channel deleting the first min(h,floor(p*|w|)) symbols is p-edit-bounded on every input. If eps_und bounds the support-test distinguishing advantage and eps_sound bounds soundness on the fixed surviving suffix, the probability of a high-entropy interval together with failed detection after this channel is at least1-eps_und-eps_sound. The intended substring-input experiment in the prose and C.6 Step1 is not refuted.
Fixed rational0<p<1 and alpha=1/100; polynomial computable n>=1 and polynomially samplable alphabet.
The watermark is sound on fixed key-independent strings and computationally indistinguishable from this model, even for a one-sample support test.
The literal full-text experiment uses an edit budget relative to the entire channel input, while the entropy condition may concern an arbitrary short substring.
No independence between the support event and the secret key is assumed; use the stated unconditional event inclusion.
Own-work source qualification; independent review pending; intended substring-input security is a distinct unresolved question.

Let f:{-1,1}^n -> R have E[f^2]=1 under the uniform product measure. Let p(S)=hat f(S)^2, I_i=sum_{S containing i}p(S), I=sum_i I_i, and H_e=sum_S p(S) ln(1/p(S)), with zero terms interpreted continuously. Then H_e <= I + sum_i I_i ln(1/I_i). This bound does not require f to be Boolean-valued.
n>=1

OWNER RESULT DRAFT: proof (unaudited), T336-w727-C013 v1; no novelty claim. Let d>=1,n>=0 be integers, ell,s,eps>0 and B>=0. A zero-mean GP on [0,1]^d has kernel k(x,z)=exp(-||x-z||^2/(2ell^2)), independent Gaussian observation noise variance s, and an exogenous design. Context length<=n and |y_i|<=B. Put b_mu=sqrt(s eps), b_v=min(s/2,s sqrt(eps)), C_mu=nB/s+n^2 B/s^2, C_v=1+2n/s+n^2/s^2, tau=min(1/2,b_mu/(3(1+C_mu)),b_v/(3C_v)), a=d/ell^2, t=ceil(max(1,2e a,log(1/tau)/log(2))) and p=binomial(d+t-1,d), with e Euler's number. Use the known Gaussian Taylor feature projection onto degrees<t, which has dimension p, norm<=1 and PSD omitted diagonal-tail<=tau. Its coordinate Lipschitz constant with respect to L1 distance is K=1/ell. Set E_mu=nB(3/s+6n/s^2), E_v=3+12n/s, rho=min(1,b_mu/(3(1+E_mu)),b_v/(3E_v)), g=max(1,ceil(K d sqrt(p)/rho)) and J=(g+1)^d. The finite-grid cone encoder from accepted C004 computes approximating features from raw x, using the exact minimum of phi_j(u)+K||x-u||_1 over grid u in {0,1/g,...,1}^d; fixed grid feature samples are weights. Put eps0=min(eps/9,1/36), kappa=1+4max(1,n)/s, M=4nB/s, delta0=min(1/2,s/8,sqrt(s eps0)/(1+M),s sqrt(eps0)/4), T=ceil(sqrt(kappa)log(2/delta0)/2), D=7p+6+d+Jd+pJ, H=2Jd+pJ+4p+1 and L=T+5+ceil(log_2 J). Composing this encoder with accepted C002 gives a residual N-normalized ReLU-attention transformer with tokenwise residual ReLU MLPs, N=n+1 tokens, width D, MLP hidden width<=H, L layers, <=5 heads and <=L(15D^2+2DH)+2D dense parameters. It takes only raw coordinates, observed labels, two role flags and constants, and outputs N(muhat,vhat), vhat>=s, with KL(N(mu,v)||N(muhat,vhat))<=eps uniformly for the ORIGINAL RBF noisy-query posterior. All nonlinear feature approximation is included; fixed affine input placement is excluded as in C004. Each of truncation, encoding and solver gets one third of the scalar mean/variance budgets; the final KL argument allows signed variance error. This composition uses C002/C004 as independently accepted ground and the unaudited C011/C012 elementary tail/perturbation lemmas; it does NOT require C010's pending Newton construction. Arbitrary fixed real weights are allowed. No raw feature oracle, finite-bit, training, softmax, layernorm, causal-mask or adaptive-design guarantee is asserted.
Raw domain [0,1]^d; d>=1,n>=0; ell,s,eps>0; B>=0; zero-mean RBF GP and independent observation noise variance s
Exogenous designs; context length<=n and observed labels bounded by B; new noisy observation prediction
Raw coordinates, labels, role flags and constants only; all nonlinear feature approximation counted; arbitrary real fixed weights
C002 v1 and C004 v1 accepted; C011/C012 elementary lemmas and C013 composition remain unaudited; no C010 dependency

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:50ba0470b7ac1b2acd9eb45c23ea7f0fddd957d3970798fcdbd5430049d10d44","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/50/50ba0470b7ac1b2acd9eb45c23ea7f0fddd957d3970798fcdbd5430049d10d44.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:b29fb87d98383eb3fea4b68e32b7cdd8a7f3a69b5c04aacefd6ba54f4ff7ea64","bundle_entry_key":"t336-w727-c013","bundle_id":"population.w727-t336-raw-rbf-encoder-chebyshev-008","claim_kind":"theorem","conditions":[],"domain":"Gaussian processes; raw-input transformer approximation; kernel truncation","draft":"w727/bundle_008.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:learning.transformers:draft-raw-input-gaussian-rbf-predictive-kl-grid-encoder-chebyshev","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# C013 v1: fully counted raw-input RBF predictor on the cube

Kind: bound. Target: none (reviewer-authorized RBF continuation).
Status: proof (unaudited). No novelty claim. This extends the saved
supplied-feature result to raw coordinates. It uses the independently
accepted C002 v1 solver and C004 v1 encoder, not the pending Newton
construction C010. The Taylor kernel approximation is known prior art.

## 1. Theorem and all resource parameters

Fix integers d>=1,n>=0 and real ell,s,eps>0 and B>=0. On X=[0,1]^d take
the zero-mean Gaussian process with kernel

    k(x,z)=exp(-||x-z||_2^2/(2 ell^2)).

The observation noises are independent N(0,s). Designs are exogenous;
the statement is pointwise over every design of at most n context points,
every query in X, and context labels bounded by B in absolute value.
The predicted distribution is that of a NEW NOISY observation, not the
noiseless latent value. Define

    b_mu=sqrt(s eps), b_v=min(s/2,s sqrt(eps)),
    C_mu=nB/s+n^2 B/s^2, C_v=1+2n/s+n^2/s^2,
    tau=min(1/2,b_mu/(3(1+C_mu)),b_v/(3 C_v)),
    a=d/ell^2,
    t=ceil(max(1,2 e a,log(1/tau)/log(2))),
    p=binomial(d+t-1,d).

Here e in the expression 2 e a denotes Euler's number. Below rho denotes
the encoder tolerance, so no constant is reused for two meanings.
For the feature encoder and its perturbation budget define

    K=1/ell, R=1, S=2,
    E_mu=nB(3/s+6n/s^2), E_v=3+12n/s,
    rho=min(1,b_mu/(3(1+E_mu)),b_v/(3 E_v)),
    g=max(1,ceil(K d sqrt(p)/rho)), J=(g+1)^d.

For the Chebyshev solver put

    eps0=min(eps/9,1/36),
    kappa=1+4 max(1,n)/s, M=4nB/s,
    delta0=min(1/2,s/8,sqrt(s eps0)/(1+M),s sqrt(eps0)/4),
    T=ceil(sqrt(kappa) log(2/delta0)/2).

There is a residual transformer with normalized ReLU attention and
tokenwise residual ReLU MLPs, taking ONLY raw coordinates, observed
labels, context/query flags and fixed constants, with

    N=n+1 tokens (n padded context slots and one query),
    D=7p+6+d+Jd+pJ token width,
    H=2Jd+pJ+4p+1 as an upper bound on MLP hidden width,
    L=T+5+ceil(log_2 J) total layers, at most five heads per layer,
    at most L(15D^2+2DH)+2D dense attention/MLP/readout parameters,

whose two outputs define N(muhat,vhat), vhat>=s, satisfying

    KL(N(mu,v) || N(muhat,vhat)) <= eps

uniformly for the ORIGINAL RBF noisy-query posterior and all contexts
above. Fixed affine input placement is excluded as in C004; ALL nonlinear
feature approximation is included in these layer and parameter counts.
Weights are arbitrary fixed reals depending on the prior and displayed
bounds, never on the current context. No finite-bit, training, softmax,
layernorm, causal-attention or adaptive-design guarantee is asserted.

## 2. Known Taylor projection supplies the uniform PSD tail

Use the p coordinates indexed by multi-indices alpha in N^d, |alpha|<t:

    phi_alpha(x)=exp(-||x||^2/(2ell^2))
                product_j(x_j/ell)^(alpha_j)/sqrt(product_j alpha_j!).

This is the collected-monomial version of Cotter, Keshet and Srebro,
Explicit Approximations of the Gaussian Kernel, arXiv:1109.4603v1,
Section 3, PDF pp.4-5, equations (6)-(11) and the following dimension
count. This known projection certificate is recorded in C012 Section 3;
only its feature-tail lemma is used, not C012's Newton corollary.

Write Phi for the full countable feature sequence and phi for its
degree<t coordinate projection. Its inner product is k and ||Phi(x)||=1.
Thus k_p=<phi,phi> is PSD, ||phi||<=1, and k-k_p is PSD on joint sets.
For ||x||^2/ell^2<=a its omitted diagonal is bounded by

    0<=k(x,x)-k_p(x,x)<=a^t/t!<=(e a/t)^t<=2^(-t)<=tau.

The factorial bound and feature count are the known Taylor argument,
not a new kernel-approximation theorem. In particular the conclusion is
a uniform PSD diagonal-tail certificate, not an integrated tail estimate.

## 3. The truncated feature map is Lipschitz independently of p

For any x,z in the cube, the full Hilbert feature map satisfies

    ||Phi(x)-Phi(z)||^2=2(1-k(x,z))
      =2(1-exp(-||x-z||^2/(2ell^2)))<=||x-z||^2/ell^2.

The last inequality is 1-exp(-u)<=u for u>=0. Orthogonal coordinate
projection cannot increase a Hilbert norm. Hence

    ||phi(x)-phi(z)||<=||x-z||_2/ell.

In particular every coordinate obeys
|phi_j(x)-phi_j(z)|<=K||x-z||_1 with K=1/ell, exactly the coordinate
Lipschitz hypothesis of the accepted C004 encoder. The constant does
not grow with the truncation degree or dimension p of the feature vector.

## 4. Apply the accepted grid encoder, counting its entire computation

Take G={0,1/g,...,1}^d and define the actual encoded feature coordinates

    psi_j(x)=min_{u in G}(phi_j(u)+K||x-u||_1).

C004 Sections 3-4 give both the exact residual-ReLU implementation of
this finite minimum and

    sup_x ||psi(x)-phi(x)||<=sqrt(p) Kd/g<=rho,
    ||psi(x)||<=1+rho<=2.

All phi_j(u) are finitely many constants in the network's weights.
They are not features supplied in the input and not a context-dependent
computation. C004 uses two absolute-value/cone layers, ceil(log_2 J)
minimum layers and one feature-gating layer: E=3+ceil(log_2 J).
Its context/query flags populate the solver's feature registers and set
padding contributions to zero. Its widths are precisely D and H in
Section 1. This instantiates the accepted encoder construction with
grid resolution g and tolerance rho; it does not re-audit its matrices.

Let (mu_p,v_p) be the exact noisy posterior for k_p and (mu_psi,v_psi)
the exact posterior for <psi,psi>. C004 Section 2 applies with
R=1,S=2,C_A=3n and feature error <=rho<=1. Its constants specialize to

    C_m=nB[(1+2)/s+2(3n)/s^2]=E_mu,
    C_v=1+2+2^2(3n)/s=E_v.

Therefore |mu_p-mu_psi|<=E_mu rho<=b_mu/3 and
|v_p-v_psi|<=E_v rho<=b_v/3. These are componentwise posterior bounds;
the encoded kernel need not be ordered below the RBF kernel.

## 5. Kernel truncation and solver error use the other two thirds

C011 Sections 1-2 give the absolute kernel-posterior perturbation bounds
for the PSD tail in Section 2:

    |mu-mu_p|<=C_mu tau<=b_mu/3,
    |v-v_p|<=C_v tau<=b_v/3.

For clarity, that lemma uses context covariance norm error <=n tau,
query cross-covariance vector error <=sqrt(n)tau, both context inverse
norms <=1/s, and the resolvent error <=n tau/s^2. It is independent of
C010 and uses no independence between the fixed label coordinates.
All exact noisy posterior variances here are >=s. The mean bounds also
cover n=0 and B=0, when their coefficients vanish.

Apply the independently accepted C002 Chebyshev solver to psi, whose
feature norm is <=S=2, with tolerance eps0. Its feature registers are
embedded in the larger width D as in C004; extra registers are preserved.
The kappa, M, delta0 and T in Section 1 are C002's constants for this
application. It costs T+2 attention layers, at most five heads, with
identity MLPs, and supplies

    vhat>=s,
    |mu_psi-muhat|<=sqrt(s eps0)<=b_mu/3,
    |v_psi-vhat|<=s sqrt(eps0)<=b_v/3.

The last inequality uses BOTH eps0<=eps/9 and eps0<=1/36:
s sqrt(eps0)<=min(s sqrt(eps)/3,s/6)=b_v/3.
Add the three scalar error budgets to obtain

    |mu-muhat|<=b_mu,
    |v-vhat|<=b_v<=s/2.

No triangle inequality for KL is invoked. Since vhat>=s, h=(v-vhat)/vhat
lies in [-1/2,1/2]. The accepted C002 Gaussian scalar inequality gives

    KL= (h-log(1+h))/2+(mu-muhat)^2/(2vhat)
      <=(v-vhat)^2/(2s^2)+(mu-muhat)^2/(2s)<=eps.

This allows either sign of the combined variance error, including the
possibility that the encoder or solver overestimates the exact variance.

## 6. Resource count and review boundary

The encoder costs 3+ceil(log_2 J) layers and the solver T+2, yielding L
in Section 1. The encoder attention is identity, and the solver MLPs
are identity; counting five full D-by-D Q/K/V triples and two D-by-H/H-by-D
MLP matrices at EVERY layer is therefore a valid dense upper bound.
The two-coordinate readout contributes 2D parameters. No p anchor tokens
from C010 are needed: N remains n+1 throughout.

This is a fully counted raw-input RBF theorem candidate on the cube,
not a proof of training success or a claim of novelty. C002 and C004 are
used as independently accepted ground. The elementary Taylor-tail and
kernel-perturbation components are saved in C012 and C011 and remain
unaudited, as does this composition. The least trusted new step is the
three-part scalar budget with signed variance error; an audit must also
check that all instantiated encoder/solver constants match C004/C002.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:1b2248f333568aad78f6e7e6ed6416c60f538097c15707890e956d3ba7f3e85a","revision_digest":"sha256:4992dbb075d5b5afef1a7ea9f0478ab7dda01d47173b596716ca481de64c3ae4","source_id":"owner:T336-w727-C013-v1","source_revision":"T336-w727-C013-v1; attributed Taylor approximation arXiv:1109.4603v1 Section 3","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

body:
[Lem 43 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Recall the function $V_\gamma(\by)$ from \eqref{e:def-V-gamma-y}.
For any $\gamma \ge 0$, any local maximizer of $V_\gamma(\by)$ on the sphere $\{\|\by\|^2=N\}$ is of the form
    \beq
        
        \by =\dbA_\beta\Big(\gamma^{1/2}\dbg+\dbX\by\Big)\,,
    \eeq
    where we recall $\dbA_\beta \equiv (\beta \bI_N - \dbD)^{-1}$. Furthermore, for any such $\by$ we must have $\beta \ge \hw_1$.
\begin{proof}
We apply the method of Lagrange multipliers with the Lagrangian $\Lagr(\by;\beta)$ as defined in \eqref{e:fp-y-lagrangian}. Note that the Lagrangian Hessian (with respect to $\by$) is given by
    \[
        \nabla^2 \Lagr(\by;\beta)
        = -\frac{2}{N} \Big(
            \beta \bI_N - \dbD - \dbX
        \Big)\,.
    \]
At any local maximum, this Hessian must be negative semi-definite. Recall the definitions of $\dbD$ and $\dbX$ from \eqref{e:fp.dbD} and \eqref{e:fp.dbX} respectively. Since $|B_1|\ge\iota N$ by the assumption $(\lambda,\mu) \in \Lambda$, we can find a non-zero vector $\bv$ that is zero outside the coordinates of $B_1$, and is additionally orthogonal to each of the vectors $\tbmeta^j$ ($1\le j\le r'$) in the definition \eqref{e:fp.dbX} of $\dbX$. It follows that
    \[
    0 \le \bv^\st \Big(\beta -\dbD-\dbX \Big)\bv
    =\bv^\st \Big(\beta -\dbD \Big)\bv
    =(\beta-\hw_1)\|\bv\|^2\,,
    \]
so we conclude $\beta\ge\hw_1$. 
For any local maximizer $\by$ satisfying $\|\by\|^2=N$, stationarity of $\Lagr$ at $\by$ yields the expression~\eqref{e:fp-g-prep2-stationarity}.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lem 43 of arXiv:2608.29416

Let (X_k)_{k=1}^n be a matrix martingale difference sequence adapted to a filtration (F_k), where each X_k is a d x d Hermitian matrix such that E[X_k | F_{k-1}] = 0 and X_k^2 <= C_k^2 almost surely for fixed positive-semidefinite matrices C_k. Let sigma^2 = || sum_{k=1}^n C_k^2 ||. Then for all t >= 0, P( || sum_{k=1}^n X_k || >= t ) <= 2 * d * exp( - t^2 / (8 * sigma^2) ).

[Proposition prop:diff-mt-fibr of arXiv:2609.00233, 'A survey on mapping class groups of 3-manifolds'] There is a fibration
\[
\Diff^+(M,T) \rightarrow \Diff^+(M) \rightarrow (\Emb(T,M)/\Diff(T))_T
\]
where $\Emb(T,M)/\Diff(T)$ is the moduli space of submanifolds of $M$ diffeomorphic to $T$ and $(\Emb(T,M)/\Diff(T))_T$ is the path component of $T$.

Further, $(\Emb(T,M)/\Diff(T))_T$ is either contractible $($hence $\Diff^+(M,T) \simeq \Diff^+(M))$, or $(\Emb(T,M)/\Diff(T))_T$ is homotopy equivalent to $S^1$.

body:
Own-work draft; proof (unaudited); independent mathematical, priority and target-scope review pending. Let d>=1,N>=2d+1,n>=0,K>=2 and 1<=r<K be integers. There are N contexts with K candidates each, d disjoint pairs with exactly one arbitrary A context and one systematic S context per pair, and N-2d known S contexts. All K candidates are true in S; each A has an independent uniform random r-subset of truths. A world fixes pair orientations and subsets. Its factual law p chooses contexts uniformly then a true candidate uniformly. The orientation class has VC dimension d. Training supplies n iid uniform context indices and exact A/S tags, with no candidate identities. For a partition Pi, p_Pi is uniform within each cell with that cell total p mass, and Mis_Pi(g,p)=TV(p_Pi,g) with TV half the l1 distance. Output bins depend on g alone. Competing generators g are arbitrary laws on the NK candidates. Feasibility means Mis<=c for every world compatible with the observed information; the objective is worst-world false-output mass. After training a perfect verifier discloses the orientation and all r true candidates in the A member of each of k predetermined pairs, 0<=k<=d, selected independently of tags and worlds. It covers fraction k/d of arbitrary truths by both count and factual mass. U counts the other d-k pairs untouched by training. Set kappa=1-r/K, beta=r/K, a1=(d-k)/N and m=U/N. For exact probability-level calibration Mis_infinity, the exact conditional frontier is V_k=kappa*max(a1-c,(a1+m-c)/2,0), c in [0,1]. The known-unverified-partition oracle, with the same verifier facts, is kappa*(a1-c)_+. Exact expected minimax excess is kappa/(2N)*E[(U-|d-k-Nc|)_+], where E[z^U]=sum_{j=0}^{d-k} binom(d-k,j)*(z-1)^j*(1-2j/N)^n. At c=a1 it equals kappa*(d-k)/(2N)*(1-2/N)^n. At c=d/N it equals kappa/(2N)*E[(U-k)_+]. A polynomial-representation version-space generator attains this worldwise. The same conditional value holds with the stated uniform posterior averages. The lower bound covers arbitrary coarsenings of score levels, but the matching upper bound is claimed only for infinity. No ordinary factual-training or weaker/noisy/adaptive verifier is covered.
C004 paired VC model: d>=1,N>=2d+1,n>=0,K>=2,1<=r<K,uniform factual context law
Training supplies exact partition tags but no factual candidate identities
Verifier reveals full arbitrary truth subsets and orientations in k independently predetermined pairs,0<=k<=d
Calibration robust over all compatible worlds; alternatively both quantities posterior-averaged under the stated uniform prior
All generators allowed; matching upper bound uses Kalai-Vempala exact-level Mis_infinity only

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:829f361413cea2630ea15bb564d725855a072a962a51172dbf4cad42619f9fd2","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/82/829f361413cea2630ea15bb564d725855a072a962a51172dbf4cad42619f9fd2.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:61f6c6565be7cce899cefc37a16589ec9041ee0c312ca24e3a354ad3a458d566","bundle_entry_key":"unrestricted-verifier-frontier","bundle_id":"population.t379-unrestricted-vc-verifier-frontiers-20261020","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"statistical learning; calibrated generation; minimax decision theory","draft":"w709/bundle_002.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:learning.calibration:paired-vc-unrestricted-verifier-frontier","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# Perfect verifier: an unrestricted-generator exact-level frontier

Candidate T379-C006 v1. Own-work draft, proof (unaudited).
Target 2, proposed kind narrowed; independent scope and priority audit pending.
This builds on the annotated experiment of C004, not ordinary factual data.
The most difficult remaining extension is weaker/noisy verifier information,
or finite coarse bins in the matching upper bound.

## Model and statement

Use C004's experiment: d>=1, N>=2d+1, n>=0, K>=2, 1<=r<K,
beta=r/K, kappa=1-beta. There are d pairs, each containing exactly
one arbitrary A and one systematic S context; the N-2d other contexts
are known S. The factual law chooses contexts uniformly, then uniformly
among K true candidates in S, or a uniform random r-subset of truths in A.
Training supplies n iid uniform context indices and their type tags,
but no candidate identities. The orientation class has VC dimension d.

After training, a perfect verifier operates on k PREDETERMINED pairs,
0<=k<=d, selected independently of tags, orientations and truth subsets.
In each it reveals which context is A and all its r true candidates. It
therefore verifies exactly the fraction gamma=k/d of arbitrary true facts,
both by count and factual mass. This is a strong, explicit side-information
experiment: the orientation disclosure is part of it, not hidden free data.
Let U be the number of pairs among the other d-k pairs that training
never touched. Put a'=(d-k)/N, m=U/N, w=a'-m.

Among ALL generators g, require Kalai--Vempala Mis_infinity(g,p)<=c
in every compatible world, 0<=c<=1, and minimize worst-world false mass.
The exact conditional value is

 V_k(c,U)=kappa max{a'-c, (a'+m-c)/2, 0}
         =kappa[(a'-c)_+ + (m-|a'-c|)_+/2].              (1)

The same conditional value holds with calibration and hallucination
averaged over uniform compatible orientations and independent uniform
unrevealed truth subsets. A lower bound equal to (1) holds for every
coarser grouping of output levels too; the matching upper bound is claimed
ONLY for exact levels. No equality of finite-bin statistics is asserted.

## Posterior mean and coarsening tail dominance

Condition on the training tags and verifier output. Let mu=E[p] and
s(y)=P(y is false). The atom types are:

 verified true:             mu=1/(Nr), s=0;
 known systematic:          mu=1/(NK), s=0;
 unverified known A:        mu=1/(NK), s=kappa;
 unknown pair contexts:     mu=1/(NK), s=kappa/2;
 verified false:            mu=0,      s=1.

Revealed A subsets are known; all other A subsets retain independent
uniform priors. The fixed S reservoir guarantees at least one safe context.
Let F denote verified false atoms, A unverified known-A contexts, and M
unknown pair contexts. Then mu(F union A)=w and
mu(F union A union M)=w+2m=a'+m.

For either E=F union A or E=F union A union M, every atom in E has
mu-density <= every atom outside E. This ordering, including equalities,
is the crucial replacement for the uniform posterior in C004.

For ANY finite partition Pi, write q=mu_Pi. Then q(E)>=mu(E).
Indeed, within a cell B with l inside-E atoms and h outside-E atoms,
let the two mu-sums be L and H. If l,h>0, the ordering implies L/l<=H/h,
so l(L+H)/(l+h)>=L. The same inequality is equality if l=0 or h=0.
Summing cells proves the assertion. This proof does not assume that Pi
respects atom types, contexts, verified supports, or probability levels.

Now fix any g and its bins Pi(g). Linearity and finite convexity give

 TV(mu_Pi,g)<=E[TV(p_Pi,g)].                            (2)

Thus a robust or posterior-average calibration budget implies
TV(q,g)<=c, and the event inequality yields

 g(F union A)>=(w-c)_+,
 g(F union A union M)>=(a'+m-c)_+.

The expected false mass is exactly

 E[H(g)] = g(F)+kappa g(A)+(kappa/2)g(M)
         = beta g(F)+(kappa/2)[g(F union A)+g(F union A union M)].

Discard the nonnegative beta g(F). The lower bound is
kappa[(w-c)_+ +(a'+m-c)_+]/2, which equals (1), by the three ranges
c<=w, w<=c<=a'+m, and c>=a'+m. Worst-world H dominates posterior
mean H. This lower bound covers every g, including non-context-uniform
ones, bins mixing verified and unverified atoms, and zero-score bins.
With randomized decisions and average budgets, use these two affine
event inequalities before averaging over the seed, then take their
positive parts; this avoids assuming feasibility for each seed.

## Attaining construction and the exact-level qualification

Begin from mu. Remove t1=min(c,w) uniformly from unverified known-A
contexts, and t2=min((c-w)_+,2m) uniformly from unknown pair contexts.
Set t=t1+t2 and add this mass uniformly to the N-2d fixed S contexts.
Do not change verified atoms: each verified true atom keeps 1/(Nr), and
each verified false atom keeps zero. Empty removal groups contribute zero.
All other contexts remain uniform over their K candidates. This defines
a probability law with TV(mu,g)=t<=c.

Every exact output-level cell is a union of entire unverified context
fibres and subsets of the verified true and false atoms. Every compatible
world has the same p mass as mu on each such cell, hence p_Pi=mu_Pi.
Since g is constant within exact-level cells, g_Pi=g and contraction gives

 Mis_infinity(g,p)=TV(mu_Pi,g_Pi)<=TV(mu,g)=t<=c.

This handles coinciding levels, the zero-output cell, and empty groups.
It is false to use g_Pi=g for arbitrary COARSER bins, which is why the
matching upper bound is limited to infinity. In every compatible world,

 H(g)=kappa[(w-t1)+(m-t2/2)]=V_k(c,U).

Verified atoms contribute no false mass. Unverified candidate probabilities
are uniform within context, so exactly a kappa fraction of output mass
in each actual A context is false. Exactly half the unknown contexts
are A. This proves attainment and the posterior-average version.

If the entire unverified partition were known, the same argument with
U=0 gives oracle value kappa(a'-c)_+. The comparison oracle has the SAME
verified facts; it is not secretly given all remaining truth subsets.

## Expected minimax frontier, rates, and efficient implementation

For algorithms robustly feasible conditional on every data/verifier
outcome, the exact worst-world expected value is E[V_k(c,U)]. Under a
uniform prior over original orientations and subsets, conditioning on the
verifier leaves independent uniform orientations in the unverified pairs.
Use the preceding Bayes lower bound, then worst >= average. Conversely,
the construction attains V_k for each world and outcome. U's law is
independent of the world and of the revealed subsets. Therefore the upper
and lower values match without interchanging suprema and expectations.

The joint occupancy formulas of C004 hold with d replaced by d-k and
the SAME N. In particular E[U]=(d-k)(1-2/N)^n, and the exact excess over
the corresponding known-partition oracle is

 kappa/(2N) E[(U-|d-k-Nc|)_+].                         (3)

At c=a' this is kappa(d-k)/(2N)(1-2/N)^n. At the original unverified
budget c=d/N it is kappa/(2N)E[(U-k)_+]; the oracle is zero. Consequently
k>=d-k guarantees zero hallucination at that original budget even with
no training. At k=d the posterior factual law is known everywhere;
g=p has zero exact-level miscalibration and zero hallucination. At k=0
the theorem reduces exactly to C004.

P(U>0)<=(d-k)(1-2/N)^n, by a union bound. When k<d,
n>=(N/2)log((d-k)/delta) guarantees the corresponding known-partition
frontier for every c with probability >=1-delta. For k=d it holds
deterministically. The samplewise exact certificate is the observed U.
Only version-space flags and the k revealed supports are needed. An
implementation processes tags and verifier supports in O(n+d+kr) time;
the generator samples from known groups and revealed subsets without
storing an NK array. Rational c admits exact expected polynomial-bit-time
sampling. No independence of different missing-pair events is assumed.

of pairs; arbitrary adaptive, noisy, partial-subset, or pointwise acceptance
verifiers are not covered. The row's ordinary factual-training question is
still open. Standard finite TV contraction/event inequalities and occupancy
are not claimed as novel; the proposed contribution is the exact
unrestricted frontier under this explicit side-information experiment.

For sparse critical synchronous parking with 0<p<2/5, r=p/(1-2p), h_s=E A_s(0), m_T=sum_{s<T}h_s, and D_s=E[A_s(0)^2]-E[((P A_s)(0))^2], the exact deficit (1-1/(2d))m_T-sum D_s equals E(A_T(0))_2+2Omega_T, where Omega_T counts expected simultaneous-arrival overshoots at unfilled holes. It lies between zero and r h_T+2r(p-h_T)/(2-r). If h_T tends to zero, the deficit has a finite limit; in d4 cumulative two-step energy is (7/8)m_T+O_p(1). Assumptions: d>=1; sparse iid critical signs each p; 0<p<2/5; Synchronous independent neighbor hops and capacity-one holes; P nearest-neighbor operator; D is two-step, not one-step energy; C18 Campbell bound; source h_T->0 for the limiting assertion. Limitation: Active-field averaged energy, not random hole-survival influence energy; no d4 pair bound follows. Novelty: KNOWN conditional-variance/energy methods; UNCHECKED exact parking deficit identity. Status: independently checked proof. The model is discrete-time uniform nearest-neighbor synchronous parking on Z^d with stationary capacity-one holes; A_t(x) is the active-particle count and H_t(x) the unfilled-hole indicator. In the sparse law eta(x) is initially +1 and -1 each with probability p, and zero otherwise, independently across sites. Here (n)_2=n(n-1), J_s is the next-round arrival count, and Omega_T=sum_{s<T} E[H_s(0)(J_{s+1}(0)-1)_+]; full definitions and proof are in proof_text.

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:0d2f3488485480508b7aad6039b9897258338bb0abfae524a131d18d031557a1","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/0d/0d2f3488485480508b7aad6039b9897258338bb0abfae524a131d18d031557a1.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:003ee7cd411bd14e46e167b8c6d8c2748dacb1466880217907ba41819bb91206","bundle_entry_key":"i0005-c21","bundle_id":"population.i0005-final-exploration-energy-and-charge-007","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"parking and interacting particle systems","draft":"w661/bundle_007.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.particle-hole:sparse-parking-active-energy-deficit-settling-overshoots-draft","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# I0005-C21 v2: exact two-step active-energy budget and bounded overshoots

Status: proof (unaudited). Novelty: KNOWN conditional-variance and energy
methods; UNCHECKED this exact parking budget and uniform deficit bound.

For sparse critical synchronous parking on Z^d, d>=1, let initial signs
have probabilities p,p,1-2p, with 0<p<2/5. Put r=p/(1-2p)<2,
a=1/(2d), h_s=E A_s(0)=E H_s(0), m_T=sum_{s<T}h_s,

    D_s=E[A_s(0)^2]-E[((P A_s)(0))^2],
    Omega_T=sum_{s<T}E[H_s(0)(J_{s+1}(0)-1)_+],

where J_{s+1} counts arrivals before settlement in the next round and P
is the uniform nearest-neighbor averaging operator. Then for every T>=0,

    (1-a)m_T-sum_{s<T}D_s = E(A_T(0))_2+2Omega_T,
    0<=Omega_T<=r(p-h_T)/(2-r),
    0<=(1-a)m_T-sum_{s<T}D_s
                           <=r h_T+2r(p-h_T)/(2-r).

Here D_s>=0 is a two-step energy, exactly

    D_s=(1/2)sum_z p_2(z) E[(A_s(0)-A_s(z))^2].

It is not the one-step Dirichlet energy: the period-two mode matters.
If h_T tends to zero, Omega_T has a finite limit Omega_infinity and
the energy deficit tends to 2Omega_infinity. In d4 the coefficient is
1-a=7/8. Thus the cumulative energy is (7/8)m_T+O_p(1); using the
source m_T of logarithmic order gives its logarithmic order as well.
None of these statements is a conditional hole-influence energy estimate.

## 1. Conditional mean and variance of arrivals

Given the time-s fields, every active particle makes one fresh independent
uniform neighbor step. Therefore

    E[J_{s+1}(0)|past]=(P A_s)(0),
    Var(J_{s+1}(0)|past)=(1-a)(P A_s)(0).

The signed next field is S_{s+1}=J_{s+1}-H_s (source (18)); settlement
subtracts one from both types and leaves this signed value unchanged.
Write v_s=E S_s(0)^2=E A_s(0)^2+h_s, and
C_s=E[H_s(0)(P A_s)(0)]=E[H_s(0)J_{s+1}(0)]. Expanding gives

    v_{s+1}-v_s=-D_s-2C_s+(1-a)h_s.

Summing from zero to T-1, with v_0=2p, yields

    sum_{s<T}D_s=(1-a)m_T+2p-v_T-2sum_{s<T}C_s.

## 2. Settlement losses and the exact deficit

Since holes have capacity one,

    ell_s:=h_s-h_{s+1}=E[H_s(0)1{J_{s+1}(0)>0}].

Thus C_s=ell_s+E[H_s(0)(J_{s+1}(0)-1)_+], and
sum C_s=p-h_T+Omega_T. Also v_T=E(A_T(0))_2+2h_T.
Substitute both identities into Step 1 to obtain the exact budget.

For the two-step energy formula, stationarity and convolution give
E[((P A_s)(0))^2]=sum_z p_2(z) E[A_s(0)A_s(z)]. Expanding the squared
difference proves the displayed representation, so D_s is nonnegative.

## 3. Campbell bound survives independent displacement

C18 states E[A_s(y)F(A_s-delta_y,H_s)]<=r E F(A_s,H_s)
for every nonnegative final-field F. Independently route all active
particles one step, producing J. For a nonnegative function F(J,H_s),
let Phi(A,H)=E_routes F(J(A),H). Exchangeability of the independent
routes and summation over departure sites give

    E[J(x)F(J-delta_x,H_s)]
      =sum_y p_1(x-y) E[A_s(y)Phi(A_s-delta_y,H_s)]
      <=r sum_y p_1(x-y) E Phi(A_s,H_s)
      =r E F(J,H_s).

All contributions are nonnegative and the transition column sums to one.
In particular, choose F(J,H)=H(0)J(0) and x=0 to get

    E[H_s(0)(J)_2]<=r E[H_s(0)J]=r C_s.

This step uses fresh independent displacement; it does not assume that
the active field itself is independent or Poisson.

## 4. Overshoot bound

For integer n>=0, n-1{n>0}<=(n)_2/2. Hence

    C_s-ell_s<= (r/2)C_s,
    C_s<=ell_s/(1-r/2),
    C_s-ell_s<=r ell_s/(2-r).

Summation yields Omega_T<=r(p-h_T)/(2-r). C18 also gives
E(A_T(0))_2<=r h_T. Combining these with the exact identity proves
the uniform deficit bound. Omega_T is nondecreasing and bounded; if
h_T tends to zero, its limit exists and the terminal factorial moment
vanishes, proving the limiting deficit assertion.

## Scope and source

This is an energy budget for the actual active-count field, averaged over
the stationary process. C17 concerns deterministic Green-test instruction
noise; the present D_s concerns two-step differences of active counts.
Neither controls the random conditional survival-influence energies in
Proposition 8.3. That transfer remains open, as does the initial-scenery
logarithm in dimension four.

Sources: Bou-Rabee--Panagiotis arXiv:2609.02820v1, Lemma 4.3,
signed update (18), critical mean identity (47), mean odometer identity
U_T=sum_{s<T}A_s, and source asymptotic h_T->0; C18 v1 for the
Campbell inequality. All energy and overshoot steps are written above.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:910b07332d3c65bdc4ce5cdeda4b2465d185fe70eef164a8962607b3724a5daf","revision_digest":"sha256:49ab623d30df393cab30838e68ece587079135cba0e6ba8f20c55065b6cf6abf","source_id":"own-work:w661:I0005-C21:v2","source_revision":"v2; packaged 2026-10-14T07:46:54.3984460+03:00","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

[Theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] Given i.i.d. random variables $f_1,f_2,f_3,\ldots\,$, assumed to be centered, and having common variance $t>0$, we have
$$\frac{f_1+\ldots+f_n}{\sqrt{n}}\sim g_t$$
with $n\to\infty$, with $g_t$ being the law having $F(x)=e^{-tx^2/2}$ as Fourier transform.

[Lemma Lemma_bernoulli of arXiv:2608.23202, 'Locally finite Fixed points of Branching Brownian Motion'] [Lemma 3.2 of [Shekhar_FP]]
Let $I$ be a countable set and $\{X_i\}_{ i\in I }$ be independent Bernoulli random variables such that $\mathbb E[X_i]=p_i$. Let $X_I=\sum_{i \in I}X_i.$ 
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
    \item If $\mathbb E[X_I]=\sum_{i \in I}p_i$ is finite, then for any $\epsilon \in (0,1)$,
\begin{align*}
\mathbb P(|X_I-\mathbb E[X_I]|\ge \epsilon \mathbb E[X_I])\le \frac{1}{\epsilon^2 \mathbb E[X_I]}.
\end{align*}

\item If $I$ is infinite and $\mathbb E[X_I]=\sum_{i \in I} p_i= \infty$, then  $X_I=\infty$ almost surely.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma Lemma_bernoulli of arXiv:2608.23202

body: [Definition 19 of arXiv:2604.19220, 'Split merge dynamics for expanding intervals and point processes on the real line.'] Let us consider $U$ a random variable uniformly distributed on $ (0,1) $  and independent of a random variable $ E $ with exponential distribution with parameter $1.$ Let us define the Markov chain $ \mathcal X^1 $ on $(0,+\infty)^2$ as follows. If $ \mathcal X^1 (0)=(b,t) \in (0,+\infty)^2$ and, if $ - U b + (1-U) t >0,$ $$ \mathcal X^1(1) = (b+ E,- U b + (1-U) t). $$ Else $$ \mathcal X^1(1) = (- U b + (1-U) t,t+E). $$
title: Definition 19 of arXiv:2604.19220

body: [Prop 37 of arXiv:2608.26698, 'Mapping class groups of simply connected closed spin 5-manifolds with no 2- and 3-torsion '] Let $M$ be a simply connected closed spin 5-manifold, and let $S : S^4 \hookrightarrow M$ be an embedding. Then there are two simply connected closed spin 5-manifolds, such that $M$ is the connected sum of them, and $S(S^4)$ is the meridian sphere of this connected sum operation. In particular, if $H_2(M)$ is isomorphic to $\mathbb{Z}$ or ${(\mathbb{Z}/{p^r})}^2$, where $p$ is a prime number, then $S(S^4)$ is the boundary of an embedded 5-disc.

[Prop p:geodesic-deloc of arXiv:2607.18194, 'Temperature chaos in directed polymers'] Fix $L\geqslant 1$ and $\ell>0$ and $t_0\in(0, 1]$ and $\gamma\in(0,\frac13)$.
    There exist $\varepsilon_0=\varepsilon_0(L,\ell,\gamma)>0$ and $C=C(L,\gamma)>0$ such that the following holds.

    For all $0 < \varepsilon < \min\{\varepsilon_0, (t_0/4)^{1/\gamma}\}$, all $x,y\in [-L,L]$, and all $r\in[\varepsilon^\gamma, t_0-\varepsilon^\gamma]$, we have
    \begin{multline*}
        \mathbb{P}\left(
            \sup_{|z|\leqslant \ell}
            \bigl[\mathcal{L}(0,x;r,z) + \mathcal{L}(r,z;t_0,y)\bigr]
            \leqslant
            \sup_{|z|\leqslant 2\varepsilon\log^4(1/\varepsilon)}
            \bigl[
                \mathcal{L}(0,x;r,z) + \mathcal{L}(r,z;t_0,y)
            \bigr]
            +
            \varepsilon^{1/2} \log^5(1/\varepsilon)
        \right)\\
        \leqslant 
        C \varepsilon^{1-3\gamma}.
    \end{multline*}
    Note that $[\varepsilon^\gamma, t_0-\varepsilon^\gamma]$ is non-empty, since by hypothesis $\varepsilon^\gamma <  t_0/4$.

[Theo bj of arXiv:2412.04918, 'On one dimensional weighted Poincar\'e inequalities for Global Sensitivity Analysis'] Assume that there exists some smooth function $h$ with non vanishing derivative on $(a,b)$ such that the function 
\begin{equation}

    M_{w,h} := \frac{(-L_w h )' }{h'}, 
\end{equation}
is bounded from below on $(a,b)$ by some positive constant. Then we have the following weighted Poincar\'e inequality: for every centered function $f\in H^1(\mu,w)$, 
$$
\int_{a}^b f ^2 \, d \mu \leq \int_a^b \frac{w \, (f') ^2} {M_{w,h} } \, d\mu .
$$
In particular it holds  
\begin{equation}

C_P(\mu,w)
\leq \frac{1}{\underset{(a,b)}{\inf} \, M_{w,h}} .
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Let $b(s)$ be a (regularly varying) normalizing function with index $\alpha>0$, and define

		\mathbb{V}_b = \{X\in L^0(\Omega, \Sigma, \mathbb{P}) : \forall x>0, \lim_{s\rightarrow \infty} b(s)P(X>sx)<\infty \text{ and}  \lim_{s\rightarrow \infty} b(s)P(X<-sx)<\infty\}.
		\]

body: Schwarz lemma: Let D = {z in C : |z| < 1} be the open unit disk and let f : D -> D be a holomorphic map with f(0) = 0. Then |f(z)| <= |z| for every z in D, and |f'(0)| <= 1. Moreover, if |f(z_0)| = |z_0| for some z_0 in D with z_0 nonzero, or if |f'(0)| = 1, then f is a rotation, i.e. f(z) = a z for some constant a with |a| = 1. (The Schwarz-Pick-Ahlfors generalization in complex differential geometry estimates the pointwise norm of a holomorphic map f : M -> N between Hermitian manifolds under curvature bounds: for instance, if M is complete Kaehler with Ricci curvature bounded below by -K_1 and N has holomorphic bisectional curvature bounded above by -K_2 < 0, then the squared norm of df is bounded by K_1 / K_2 (Yau 1978); under the weaker hypothesis of holomorphic sectional curvature bounded above by -K_2 < 0, Royden's version gives the same bound multiplied by 2k/(k+1), where k is the rank of df.)

body:
[Theorem 1 of arXiv:2604.05143, 'Existence of a classical solution to the integro-differential equation arising in the Cram'] Suppose that conditions \ref{assump:1}--\ref{assump:3} are satisfied. Then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
    \item \textbf{(Existence and smoothness)} The survival probability $\Phi(u)$ belongs to the class $C([0,\infty)) \cap C^1((0,\infty))$ and satisfies the IDE \eqref{eq:ide} almost everywhere. If, in addition, $F$ is continuous on $[0,\infty)$, then $\Phi \in C^2((0,\infty))$ and equation \eqref{eq:ide} holds in the classical sense for all $u > 0$.
    
    \item \textbf{(Boundary conditions)} We have $\lim_{u\to\infty} \Phi(u) = 1$. The right-hand limit at zero is strictly positive: $\Phi(0+) = \Phi_0 \in (0,1)$.

    \item \textbf{(Asymptotics)} If, in addition, $\mathbb{E}[\xi^{\gamma-1}]<\infty$, then there exists a constant $C_\infty>0$ such that  
    \[
    \lim_{u\to\infty} u^{\gamma-1}\Psi(u) = C_\infty.
    \]  
    If, on the contrary, $\mathbb{E}[\xi^{\gamma-1}]=\infty$, then  
    \[
    \lim_{u\to\infty} u^{\gamma-1}\Psi(u) = \infty,
    \]
    and in this case $\Psi(u) \sim \operatorname{const} \bar F(u)$ for subexponential distributions.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 1 of arXiv:2604.05143

body: In matrix theory, the Perron–Frobenius theorem, proved in its first part by Oskar Perron and extended by Georg Frobenius, asserts that a real square matrix with positive entries has a unique eigenvalue of largest magnitude and that eigenvalue is real. The corresponding eigenvector can be chosen to have strictly positive components, and also asserts a similar statement for certain classes of nonnegative matrices. This theorem has important applications to probability theory ; to the theory of dynamical systems ; to economics ; to demography ; to social networks ; to Internet search engines (PageRank); and even to the ranking of American football teams. The first to discuss the ordering of players within tournaments using Perron–Frobenius eigenvectors is Edmund Landau.
title: Perron–Frobenius theorem

body:
[Theorem 8 of arXiv:2609.02426, 'Deformations of the $\osp(n|2)$-action on the superspace\\ of symbols of differential oper'] Let $n\geq3$ and $\Sc^n_d$ as in \eqref{eq:8}.
\begin{itemize}
\item[i)] If $2d\notin\N$, then
$\Hd^1(\osp(n|2),\Dc^n_d)=\bigoplus_{k\geq0}\Hd^1\bigl(\osp(n|2),\Dc^n_{d-\frac k2,\,d-\frac k2}\bigr)$
and the general infinitesimal deformation of $\Sc^n_d$ is
\begin{equation}

\widetilde{L}=L+L_1,\qquad L_1=\sum_{k\geq0}\tau_k\,f_{d-\frac k2},
\end{equation}
the coefficients $\tau_k$ being even independent parameters.
\item[ii)] If $2d=m\in\N$, then
$$\Hd^1(\osp(n|2),\Dc^n_d)=\bigoplus_{k=1}^m \Hd^1\bigl(\osp(n|2),\Dc^n_{-\frac{k+n-2}{2},\frac k2}\bigr)
\oplus\bigoplus_{k=-\infty}^{m}\Hd^1\bigl(\osp(n|2),\Dc^n_{\frac k2,\frac k2}\bigr),$$
and the general infinitesimal deformation of $\Sc^n_d$ is
\begin{equation}

\widetilde{L}=L+L_1,\qquad
L_1=\sum_{k=-\infty}^{m}\tau_k f_{\frac k2}+\sum_{k=1}^m\bigl(t_kh_k+\widetilde{t}_k\widetilde{h}_k\bigr),
\end{equation}
where $\tau_k,t_k,\widetilde{t}_k$ are independent parameters,
$|t_k|=|\widetilde{t}_k|=|h_k|\equiv n\ (\mathrm{mod}\ 2)$.
\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 8 of arXiv:2609.02426

[Definition def:ofh1/2 of arXiv:2609.03980, 'Decay Rates and Domain Dependence of a Coupled Wave-Heat System with Spatially Dependant H'] Let $\Gamma$ be a relatively open subset of the boundary $\partial \Omega$ of some bounded Lipschitz domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n, n\geq 2$.
    We then define the space
    \begin{alignat}{2}
        H^{1/2}(\Gamma)& \coloneq  \left\{v\in L^2(\Gamma)~\middle|~ \|v\|_{H^{1/2}(\Gamma)}^2 <\infty \right\},  \textnormal{ where }\nonumber\\
        \|v\|_{H^{1/2}(\Gamma)}^2& \coloneq  \|v\|_{L^2(\Gamma)}^2\nonumber
        + \int_\Gamma \int_\Gamma \frac{|u(x)-u(y)|^2}{|x-y|^{n}}\;\mathrm{d}\sigma(x,y).
    \end{alignat}   
    If $n=1$, we equip $H^{1/2}(\Gamma)  \coloneq  \mathbb{C}^{|\Gamma|}$ with the Euclidean norm.
    
    Additionally, we denote by $${\operatorname{tr}}: H^1(\Omega) \to H^{1/2}(\partial \Omega)$$ the usual trace operator extending the restriction $C^1(\overline{\Omega})\to C^0(\partial \Omega), v\mapsto v|_{\partial\Omega}$, which is bounded and surjective, see Theorem 1.5.1.3 in [grisvard2011elliptic].
title: Definition def:ofh1/2 of arXiv:2609.03980

It is finite for p<1. The critical bond probability is the unique alpha_N in (0,1) satisfying alpha_N(2chi_N(alpha_N)-1)=1; there is no infinite cluster at alpha_N, and p_u(G_N)=1. Its degree is 2N+2, edge-isoperimetric infimum is exactly 2, normalized conductance is 1/(N+1), and N/(N+1)<=rho<=(N-1+sqrt(3))/(N+1)<1. Hence rho approaches one on this fixed nonamenable group while every graph has a nonempty nonuniqueness phase. For N>=2, alpha_N<0.29, established by the upper-bound quartic 4p^4-8p^3+7p^2+2p-1; its root is an upper bound, not the exact alpha_N.

\le{}& C\left(\mathbb{E}|\xi|^2 + \mathbb{E}\left[\int_0^T|f(s,0,0,\delta_0)|^2\dif s\right] + \mathbb{E}\left[\int_0^T|\psi_s|^2\dif\kappa_s\right] + K_T^2\right).
\end{aligned}
\]
title: A Priori Estimates

[Theorem 26 (Uniqueness of persistent $m$-hubs, Theorem 2.8 in~\cite{Iyer24}) of arXiv:2505.06187, 'Preferential Attachment Trees with Vertex Death: Persistence of the Maximum Degree'] Consider the CMJ branching process $(\bp(t))_{t\geq0}$ as defined in Section~\ref{sec:embed}, where the offspring $D$ and inter-birth times $(X(i))_{i\in\N}$ satisfy Assumption~\ref{ass:appendix}. Fix $m\in\N$ and suppose that $(\bp(t))_{t\geq 0}$ contains a persistent $m$-hub $\mathbb P_\cS$-almost surely. Also suppose one of the following conditions is satisfied. 
		\begin{enumerate}[label=(\arabic*)]
			\item We have 
			\be 
			\sum_{k=1}^\infty\P{0\leq \sum_{i=1}^k (X(i)'-X(i))-\sum_{i=1}^k X(i)<X(k+1)}<\infty.
			\ee  
			\item Both of the following conditions hold: 
			\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
				\item We have $\sum_{i=1}^\infty \P{X(i)\neq X(i)'}=\infty$, or there exists $i\in\N$ such that $\P{X(i)\neq X(i)'}=1$. 
				\item For any $\eps>0$ we have $\sum_{i=1}^\infty \P{X(i)>\eps}<\infty$.
				\end{enumerate}  
		\end{enumerate}
		Then, the persistent $m$-hub is $\mathbb P_\cS$-almost surely unique. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] The density of a continuous probability measure $\mu$ can be recaptured from the sequence of moments $\{M_k\}_{k\geq0}$ via the Stieltjes inversion formula
$$d\mu (x)=\lim_{t\searrow 0}-\frac{1}{\pi}\,Im\left(G(x+it)\right)\cdot dx$$
where the function on the right, given in terms of moments by
$$G(\xi)=\xi^{-1}+M_1\xi^{-2}+M_2\xi^{-3}+\ldots$$
is the Cauchy transform of the measure $\mu$.
title: Unnumbered theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'
