PROOF (UNAUDITED), w741-T422-C05 v1. Not independently checked.
# T422 Target 2: an explicit lower tail bound for instantaneous noise scales

Status: proof (unaudited), C05 v1. This strengthens the positive-probability
scope obstruction C04. It is not an upper tail estimate or a typical-scale
calibration, and it makes no literature-priority claim.

## Statement and all constants

Use the noiseless fresh Gaussian online model of C04. Let alpha>1,
gamma>alpha+1, h_j=j^(-alpha), and deterministic e_0,j satisfy
e_0,j^2=j^(-(gamma-alpha)). Each update averages B independent samples,
B>=1 integer, with a fixed step eta>0. Fix finite integer t>=1, ell in {1,2},
and integer n>=1. Let u_n denote the nth coordinate unit vector, and put

    m=gamma-alpha>1, M=||e_0||=sqrt(zeta(m)), c=M/2,
    y=c u_n, A=<e_0-y,e_0>=M^2-c e_0,n,
    u=(e_0-y)/sqrt(eta A), R=||u||+1,
    r=c h_n^((ell+1)/2)/4,
    T=(1+eta R^2)^t-1,
    rho=min(1, r R/(4 M T)).

Here A>=M^2/2>0, T>0, M,R,r,rho>0. Every division is well defined.
The norm in R is explicit:

    ||u||^2=(M^2-2c e_0,n+c^2)/(eta A).

Choose the following explicit finite truncation:

    N=ceil(max(n,1,
         [16/(eta A (m-1)rho^2)]^(1/(m-1)),
         [32/((alpha-1)rho^2)]^(1/(alpha-1)))).

For a prescribed center w equal to either 0 or u, define

    a=rho/(2 sqrt(N)),
    P_N(w)= (1/2) [rho/sqrt(2 pi N)]^N
             (product_(j=1)^N h_j^(-1/2))
             exp[-(1/2) sum_(j=1)^N (|w_j|+a)^2/h_j].

These are finite explicit strictly positive real numbers, not floating-point
certificates. Put

    pi_event=P_N(0)^(B(t-1)) P_N(u)^B >0,
    L_n=1+(9/25)zeta(ell alpha)n^(ell alpha).

For the conditional single-example instantaneous scale R_ell of C04,

    P(e_t!=0 and R_ell(e_t)>=L_n) >= pi_event.             (Q1)

In particular, for any finite L choose n with L_n>L; the same explicit
pi_event lower-bounds P(e_t!=0 and R_ell(e_t)>L).
The theorem also applies when t is any finite first EXPECTED-risk hitting
index, since that index is deterministic. It does not apply to a realized-risk
stopping time chosen from the samples without an additional stopping argument.
Fresh mutually independent Gaussian inputs
Noiseless labels
t deterministic, including any finite first expected-risk hit; not a sample-path stopping time
alpha>1 and gamma>alpha+1; fixed eta>0; B positive integer; n positive integer

Use the noiseless fresh Gaussian online model of C04. Let alpha>1,
gamma>alpha+1, h_j=j^(-alpha), and deterministic e_0,j satisfy
e_0,j^2=j^(-(gamma-alpha)). Each update averages B independent samples,
B>=1 integer, with a fixed step eta>0. Fix finite integer t>=1, ell in {1,2},
and integer n>=1. Let u_n denote the nth coordinate unit vector, and put

    m=gamma-alpha>1, M=||e_0||=sqrt(zeta(m)), c=M/2,
    y=c u_n, A=<e_0-y,e_0>=M^2-c e_0,n,

    N=ceil(max(n,1,
         [16/(eta A (m-1)rho^2)]^(1/(m-1)),
         [32/((alpha-1)rho^2)]^(1/(alpha-1)))).

For a prescribed center w equal to either 0 or u, define

    a=rho/(2 sqrt(N)),
    P_N(w)= (1/2) [rho/sqrt(2 pi N)]^N
             (product_(j=1)^N h_j^(-1/2))
             exp[-(1/2) sum_(j=1)^N (|w_j|+a)^2/h_j].

These are finite explicit strictly positive real numbers, not floating-point
certificates. Put

    pi_event=P_N(0)^(B(t-1)) P_N(u)^B >0,
    L_n=1+(9/25)zeta(ell alpha)n^(ell alpha).

For the conditional single-example instantaneous scale R_ell of C04,

    P(e_t!=0 and R_ell(e_t)>=L_n) >= pi_event.             (Q1)

In particular, for any finite L choose n with L_n>L; the same explicit
pi_event lower-bounds P(e_t!=0 and R_ell(e_t)>L).
The theorem also applies when t is any finite first EXPECTED-risk hitting
index, since that index is deterministic. It does not apply to a realized-risk
stopping time chosen from the samples without an additional stopping argument.

## Gaussian ball probabilities with an explicit finite cutoff

For every N>=n, the selected u has tail

    ||u_(j>N)||^2 = (eta A)^(-1) sum_(j>N)j^(-m)
                  <= N^(1-m)/[eta A(m-1)] <= rho^2/16.

The center 0 has zero tail. Also

    E||x_(j>N)||^2 <= N^(1-alpha)/(alpha-1) <= rho^2/32.

Thus Markov gives P(||x_(j>N)||<rho/4)>=1/2. Independently, the first N
coordinates have product Gaussian density. On the box
|x_j-w_j|<a, that density is at least

    (2pi)^(-N/2) product_(j<=N)h_j^(-1/2)
       exp[-(1/2)sum_(j<=N)(|w_j|+a)^2/h_j].

Its volume is (2a)^N. The prefix error has norm less than rho/2 on this
box; the center tail has norm at most rho/4. Intersecting the independent
prefix and tail events therefore yields ||x-w||<rho, and

    P(||x-w||<rho)>=P_N(w).                               (Q2)

No infinite product of densities is used. All sums in P_N are finite;
the two omitted tails have the displayed integral-comparison bounds.

## Quantitative continuity of the finite training history

For a batch X=(x_1,...,x_B), define

    T_X=I-(eta/B)sum_b x_b tensor x_b.

Consider the reference history with every input 0 for the first t-1 steps,
and every last-step input u. Its errors are e_0 up to its final update and
y afterward, since eta u<u,e_0>=e_0-y.

If each actual input is within rho of its reference center, both actual
and reference inputs have norm at most R, since rho<=1. The rank-one identity

    x tensor x-w tensor w
       =(x-w) tensor x+w tensor (x-w)

and ||v tensor w||=||v||||w|| give

    ||T_X||<=1+eta R^2,
    ||T_X-T_W||<=2eta R rho.

If d_s is the norm of the error difference from this reference history,
then d_0=0 and, for s<t,

    d_(s+1)<=(1+eta R^2)d_s+2eta R rho M.

Induction and the finite geometric-sum identity imply

    d_t<=2eta R rho M sum_(s=0)^(t-1)(1+eta R^2)^s
        =(2M rho/R)[(1+eta R^2)^t-1]
        <=r/2.                                            (Q3)

The geometric denominator eta R^2 is positive; the last inequality is
exactly the choice of rho. This is a deterministic perturbation argument.
It contains no multiplication of conditional probability bounds.

## Output radius forces a large instantaneous ratio

The conditional Gaussian covariance identity from C04 yields

    R_ell(e)=1+zeta(ell alpha)<e,He>/<e,H^(ell+1)e>.

For ||e-y||<=r, the operator norms of H^(1/2) and H^((ell+1)/2)
are both 1, so

    sqrt(<e,He>)>=c sqrt(h_n)-r>=(3/4)c sqrt(h_n),
    sqrt(<e,H^(ell+1)e>)<=c h_n^((ell+1)/2)+r
                          =(5/4)c h_n^((ell+1)/2).

We used h_n<=1 in the first line. The denominator is strictly positive
for e!=0, and ||e-y||<=r<=c/4 excludes e=0. Dividing gives

    R_ell(e)>=1+(9/25)zeta(ell alpha)h_n^(-ell)=L_n.       (Q4)

## Product probability and its scope

The event used above restricts B(t-1) distinct inputs to balls about 0,
and B other inputs to balls about u. These Bt inputs are mutually independent
by the fresh-sample model. Thus their intersection probability is at least
P_N(0)^(B(t-1))P_N(u)^B. Combining (Q2)--(Q4) proves (Q1).

This explicit independence is indispensable. Per-input conditional bounds
alone would not justify the product. The reference centers are fixed from
the deterministic parameters and n before any samples are drawn.

For any proposed confidence 1-delta with delta<pi_event and upper threshold
L<L_n, a bound P(R_ell(e_t)<=L)>=1-delta is impossible. The estimate can be
extremely small and says nothing about typical quantiles. At a finite
expected-risk hit it supplies a quantitative exceptional-event obstruction;
it does not give the epsilon-dependent high-probability trade-off requested
under a specified instantaneous interpretation.

## Checks and remaining work

The accompanying exact rational checks exercise (Q3), (Q4), t=1, B=1,
both ell values and the finite geometric identity. Hypothesis controls:
eta=0 or e_0=0 removes the reachable-mode construction; t=0 removes the
fresh-input event; a fixed finite-rank covariance bounds this noiseless ratio
above by 1+tr(H^ell)h_min^(-ell), so arbitrarily large n is essential.
These checks validate finite algebra only. Neither a passing finite check
nor a Lean comparison lemma certifies the infinite Gaussian theorem.

The next unpaid step is an upper small-denominator/tail bound at a specified
confidence level and hitting rule. This statement does not supply one.

Sources: C04 v1 supplies the conditional covariance convention and support
context; McCandlish et al., arXiv:1812.06162, equations (2.8)--(2.9) define
the primary instantaneous scales. All probability bounds above are derived
here from finite Gaussian densities, Markov, and actual sample independence.

[Lemma lem: assumption of arXiv:2601.05361, 'Noise sensitivity in last-passage percolation'] There exist constants $0<c,C<\infty$ such that the following holds. For every $v\in{\mathbb{Z}}^2_{\ge0}$ and $1\le s\le\frac{1}{18}|v|_1^{1/3}$ such that $\min\{v_1,v_2\} \geq C$ and $|v_2-v_1|\le s|v|_1^{2/3}$,

body:
[Thma* two and more dimensions of arXiv:2509.19809, 'Exact Limsup Growth of Rarely Visited Sites for One-Dimensional Simple Random Walk'] For $k,n\in{\mathbb N}$, let $Q_k^{(d)}(n)$ denote the number of sites visited exactly $k$ times up to step $n$ in a $d$-dimensional simple random walk $(S_n^{(d)})$ on $\mathbb{Z}^d$. Formally,
$$Q_k^{(d)}(n)=\#\{j:0\le j\le n,\,\xi(S_j^{(d)},n)=k\}.$$
Then for $k\in{\mathbb N}$, we have the following asymptotic results:
\begin{eqnarray*}
&&\lim_{n\to\infty}\dfrac{Q_k^{(2)}(n)\cdot(\log n)^2}{\pi^2n}=1~\quad\quad\quad ~~~ a.s.\\
&&\lim_{n\to\infty}\dfrac{Q_k^{(d)}(n)}{n}=\gamma_d^2(1-\gamma_d)^{k-1}~\quad\quad a.s.~~~~~\mbox{ if }~~d\ge3,
\end{eqnarray*}
where $\gamma_d:= {\mathbb P}\left(S_n^{(d)} \neq S_0^{(d)},\; \forall n\geq 1\right)$, which is the probability that a simple random walk never returns to the starting point. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

$f$ be a univalent function in the unit disc with $f(0)=0$, and

Z_{\tau}\sim f^{*}(\xi)

body:
[Lem 11 of arXiv:2606.04636, 'A Thomson-type variational principle for diffusion coefficients'] Let $V_{l}$ be the space of admissible flows $\phi\in\cH_{2}$ such
that $\left\langle \div\phi-j_{l},\div\phi-j_{l}\right\rangle =0$.
Then 
\begin{equation}
\left\langle j_{l},\cL^{-1}j_{l}\right\rangle =\sup_{\phi\in V_{l}}\left\{ -\left\langle \phi,\phi\right\rangle \right\} .
\end{equation}
The (formal) expression $\left\langle j_{l},\cL^{-1}j_{l}\right\rangle $
is defined as the term $-\int_{0}^{\infty}\dd t\sum_{x}\mu\left[\tau_{x}j_{l}\ e^{t\cL}j_{l}\right]$
appearing in the Green-Kubo formula (\ref{eq:green-kubo}).

If P is absolutely continuous with respect to Q and D_KL(P || Q) = integral log(dP/dQ) dP with natural logarithms (possibly +infinity), then 2 H^2(P, Q) <= -2 log(1 - H^2(P, Q)) <= D_KL(P || Q). The second inequality is an equality for P = delta_0, Q = (delta_0 + delta_1)/2, where both sides equal log 2.

[Thm DL-zero of arXiv:2411.16376, 'Higher order approximations in arcsine laws for subordinators'] Let $\beta\in(0,1)$. 
Let $X$ be a killed subordinator which is not identically zero.
Then the following conditions are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}[label={\upshape (\arabic*')}]
\item The drift coefficient $b$ is zero, and the tail $\Pi((x,+\infty))$ of the L\'evy measure  is regularly varying at $0+$ with index $-\beta$.

\item The Laplace exponent $\Phi:(0,+\infty)\to(0,+\infty)$ (restricted over $(0,+\infty)$) is regularly varying at $+\infty$ with index $\beta$. 

\item 	
$\displaystyle \lim_{s\to0+}
\ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}\bigg(\frac{X_{T(s)-}}{s} \leq t\bigg)=\frac{\sin(\pi\beta)}{\pi}\int_0^t x^{-1+\beta}(1-x)^{-\beta}\,dx$ for any $0\leq t\leq 1$.
\vspace{3pt}
\item 
$\displaystyle \lim_{s\to0+} s^{-1}\ensuremath{\mathbb{E}}[X_{T(s)-}]=\beta$.

\item The law of $t X_{1/\Phi(t)}$ converges weakly to a stable law with index $\beta$, as $t\to+\infty$. 

\item The distribution function $U([0,x])$ of the potential measure  is regularly varying at $0+$ with index $\beta$.  
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Every finite normal-form game (finitely many players, each with a finite nonempty pure strategy set, and real-valued payoffs) has at least one Nash equilibrium in mixed strategies: a profile sigma* = (sigma*_1,...,sigma*_n) of mixed strategies such that for every player i and every alternative mixed strategy sigma_i for that player, the expected payoff satisfies u_i(sigma*_i, sigma*_{-i}) >= u_i(sigma_i, sigma*_{-i}); that is, no player can improve their expected payoff by unilaterally deviating while the others' strategies stay fixed.

body: In mathematical logic, and theoretical computer science, type theory is the study of formal systems that classify expressions or mathematical objects by their types. Type theories are used in the study of programming languages, formal logic, and the formalization of mathematics.

body: [Theorem thm:uniqueness-of-geodesics of arXiv:2609.04140, 'The conformally invariant metric on $\CLE_4$ III:\\ uniqueness'] Let $U \subsetneq \BC$ be a deterministic simply connected domain. Then, a.s., for each $\SCL_1, \SCL_2 \in \Gamma_U$, the $D_{\Gamma_U}^U$-geodesic connecting $\SCL_1$ and $\SCL_2$ is unique in the following sense: if $P_1$ and $P_2$ are $D_{\Gamma_U}^U$-geodesics connecting $\SCL_1$ and $\SCL_2$, then they visit the same set of loops, that is, $\{\SCL \in \Gamma_U : \SCL \cap P_1 \neq \emptyset\} = \{\SCL \in \Gamma_U : \SCL \cap P_2 \neq \emptyset\}$. The same is true with a deterministic connected arc (resp.\ two deterministic disjoint connected arcs) of $\partial U$ in place of $\SCL_1$ (resp.\ $\SCL_1$ and $\SCL_2$). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Uniqueness of geodesics

[Corollary 16 (Recovery of $Z_k$ up to block-level ancestral ambiguity) of arXiv:2608.28991, 'Jigsaw-CRL: Recovering Global Latent Causal Order from Fragmented Multi-Client Interventio'] Assume Assumptions~\ref{ass: aligned intervention} and~\ref{ass:non-degeneracy} hold. Let $\hat{\bQ}_k$ be the output of Algorithm~\ref{alg:causal order client}, and define
\[
\hat Z_k=\hat{\bQ}_kX_k.
\]
For each true block $C\in\cC_k$, let $\hat C=\psi^{-1}(C)$ denote the corresponding estimated block. Then, for every $i\in\hat C$, the estimated latent variable $\hat Z_{k,(i)}$ lies in the span of the true latent variables indexed by the block ancestors of $C$, namely
\[
\hat Z_{k,(i)}\in \mathrm{span}\{Z_{(j)}:j\in C', C' \in Anc_k^\rblk(C)\}.
\]
Thus, up to the relabeling induced by $\psi$, each estimated latent variable is identified up to block-level ancestor mixing. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition def:curveinob of arXiv:2609.00978, 'Towards Categorical K\"ahler Geometry'] A \textbf{curve in $\mathrm{Ob}(\cC)$} is an exact $\mathbf k$-linear functor $F\colon \mathrm{Perf}(X)\to \cC$, where $X$ is a connected smooth projective curve over $\mathbf k$, and satisfying the following representability conditions:
\begin{enumerate}[(1)]
    \item There is a functor $R_F\colon\cC\to D^-_{\mathrm{coh}}(X)$ such that
    \[
    \operatorname{Hom}_{\cC}(F(E),A)\cong \operatorname{Hom}_{D^-_{\mathrm{coh}}(X)}(E,R_F(A))
    \]
    for $E\in \mathrm{Perf}(X)$, $A\in\cC$.
    \item There is a functor $K_F\colon\cC^{\mathrm{op}}\to D^+_{\mathrm{coh}}(X)$ such that
    \[
    \operatorname{Hom}_{\cC}(A,F(E))\cong H^0R\Gamma(X;E\otimes^LK_F(A))
    \]
    for $E\in \mathrm{Perf}(X)$, $A\in\cC$.
\end{enumerate}
title: Definition def:curveinob of arXiv:2609.00978

For every $o\in\mathscr{T}$, $F$ has a fixed point on $[o,F(o)]$.

d(c,y)=\max\{d(x,y),d(x',y)\}-\frac12d(x,x').

[Theorem t:multcltmarkedpp of arXiv:2605.28430, 'Limit theory for Lipschitz-localized statistics in random geometric models'] Consider a stationary marked point process  $\tilde{\mathcal{P}}$ on $\mathbb{R}^d\times\mathbb{K}$ with non-null, finite intensity $\rho$, having summable exponential $\mathbb{B} $-mixing correlations as in Definition~(def.A2 of the paper).  Let $\xi_i : \mathbb{R}^d \times \mathbb{K} \times \hat\mathcal{N}_{\mathbb{R}^d \times \mathbb{K}} \to \mathbb{R}$,  $i =1,\ldots,{m}$ be translation invariant  score functions. Assume  that the  vector  \(\boldsymbol{\xi} = (\xi_1, \ldots, \xi_{m}) \in \mathbb{R}^{m}\) is jointly fast \textnormal{BL}-localizing on finite windows of $\tilde{\mathcal{P}}$ in the sense that for all $p \in \mathbb{N} $, condition~(equation Lp-stab of the paper) is satisfied by \(\bk {\boldsymbol{\xi}}1p \in (\mathbb{R}^{m})^p\). 
If for {\em some} $\varepsilon > 0$, 
   $\xi_i$, $i=1,\ldots,{m}$ satisfy the $(2 + \varepsilon)$-moment condition
   (equation e:xinpmomcopied of the paper) on finite windows, then for  $f \in \mathbb{B} (W_1)$ 

\begin{equation} n^{-1/2}(\mu_n^{\xi_1}(f) - \mathbb {E} \mu_n^{\xi_1}(f),\ldots, \mu_n^{\xi_{m}}(f) - \mathbb {E} \mu_n^{\xi_{m}}(f)) \stackrel{d}{\Rightarrow} (Z_1,\ldots,Z_{m}),
\end{equation}

where $(Z_1,\ldots,Z_{m})$ is a  multivariate normal random vector
(with possibly zero components) having zero mean and covariance 

$$  {\rm{Cov}}(Z_i,Z_j) = \sigma^2_{\Upsilon}[i,j] \int_{W_1}f(x)^2 \mathrm{d} x \in (-\infty, \infty),$$

 where the matrix $(\sigma^2_{\Upsilon}[i,j])_{1 \leq i \leq j \leq {m}}$ involves the vector $\boldsymbol{\Upsilon}_{\0}$ and the matrix  $\boldsymbol{\Upsilon}_{(\0,z)}$ of probability distributions  given in~(equation e.xil-0-multi of the paper) and~(equation e.xil-xy-multi of the paper): 

\begin{align}  
& \sigma^2_{\Upsilon}[i,j]:=
\rho\mathbb {E} \bigl[\Upsilon_{\0}[i] \Upsilon_{\0}[j]\bigr]   \\
& \ \ \ + \int_{\mathbb{R}^d} \left( \mathbb {E} \Bigl[\Upsilon_{(\0,z)}[1,i] \Upsilon_{(\0,z)}[2,j]\Bigr] \rho^{(2)}(\0,z) - \rho^2
\mathbb {E} \bigl[\Upsilon_{\0}[i]\bigr] \mathbb {E} \bigl[\Upsilon_{\0}[j]\bigr] 
\right) \mathrm{d} z \in (-\infty, \infty). \nonumber
\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Multivariate CLT  for statistics of point processes with fast \BL-localizing scores  under a $(2 + \varepsilon)$-moment condition

[Definition def:OPRE-model of arXiv:2507.00329, 'Oriented bond-site percolation in random environment and contact processes with periodic r'] Fix some spatial stretches $(\xi_x)_{x\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq0}}$, $(\nu_{x,x+1})_{x\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq0}}\subset[0,\infty)$, called the \emph{environment}, and a {\em connection function} $\kappa\colon[0,\infty)\to[0,1]$. Consider the following independent bond-site percolation model on $\mathbb{L}^2$ in the environment $(\xi_x)_{x\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq0}}$, $(\nu_{x,x+1})_{x\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq0}}$, where 
    \begin{itemize}
    	\item 
    		each vertex $(t,x)\in V$ is open independently with probability \(\kappa(\xi_x)\),
		\item 
			each edge of the form \((t,x)\to(t+1,x+1)\) is open independently with probability \(\kappa(\nu_{x,x+1})\), and
		\item	
			each edge of the form \((t,x)\to(t+1,x-1)\) is open independently with probability \(\kappa(\nu_{x-1,x})\).
    \end{itemize}
    If the graph contains an infinite path consisting of open vertices and open edges only, we say that the model \emph{percolates}. 
    If the environment is given by a realisation of families of random variables, we refer to the associated percolation model as \emph{OPRE}.
title: Oriented percolation in (spatial columnar) random environment (OPRE)

\[

\]
and let \(r \in S^{-\delta}\) for some $\delta >0$. Assume that
\[
    \Op (q_0) + \Op(r) \in \mathfrak{S}_2(L^2(V_2)).
\]
Then~\(q_0(y,\eta) = 0\) for all $y \in V_2$ and all $|\eta| \geq 1$.

[Lemma 23 (Bernstein's inequality for sub-exponential variables) of arXiv:2604.23461, 'Scaling limit of Sinkhorn-rescaled Random Matrices \\ via Stability of Static Schrödinger '] Let $Y_1, \dots, Y_n$ be independent centered random variables satisfying the moment bounds
	\[
	\E\left[|Y_i|^q\right] \le \frac{q!}{2}\sigma_i^2 R_i^{q-2} \quad \text{for all integers } q \ge 2. 
	\]
	Then, for any deterministic constants $a_1, \dots, a_n \in \R$ and any $t > 0$, we have 
	\[
	\P\left(\left|\sum_{i=1}^{n}a_i Y_i\right| > t\right) \le 2\exp\left(-\frac{t^2/2}{\sum_{i=1}^{n}a_i^2\sigma_i^2 + a_{\max}R_{\max}t}\right),
	\]
	where $a_{\max} = \max_{1 \le i \le n} |a_i|$ and $R_{\max} = \max_{1 \le i \le n} R_i$.
title: Bernstein's inequality for sub-exponential variables

[Lemma lem:gaussian-shifted-ball-comparison of arXiv:2606.21006, 'Law of the Iterated Logarithm for Weighted Sums of Functionals of Long-Memory Gaussian Seq'] Let \((X,Y)\) be a centered Gaussian vector in \(\mathbb R^N\times\mathbb R^N\) such that
\(
    \operatorname{Cov}(X)=I_N,
    \qquad
    \operatorname{Cov}(Y)=I_N.
\)
Let
\(
    R:=\operatorname{Cov}(X,Y).
\)
Assume that
\(
    \|R\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le \frac12 .
\)
Then for every \(\varepsilon>0\) there exists a constant
\(C=C(N,\varepsilon)<\infty\) such that, for all \(u,v\in\mathbb R^N\),

\[
\left|
    \mathbb P\bigl(X\in B(u,\varepsilon),\,Y\in B(v,\varepsilon)\bigr)
    -
    \mathbb P\bigl(X\in B(u,\varepsilon)\bigr)
    \mathbb P\bigl(Y\in B(v,\varepsilon)\bigr)
\right|  
\]   
\[                                 
\le
C\,\|R\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\bigl(1+|u|^2+|v|^2\bigr)
\exp\left\{
    C\|R\|_{\mathrm{op}}\bigl(1+|u|^2+|v|^2\bigr)
\right\}                                      
\times
\mathbb P\bigl(X\in B(u,\varepsilon)\bigr)
\mathbb P\bigl(Y\in B(v,\varepsilon)\bigr).
\]

[Proposition 6 of arXiv:2605.30616, 'Brownian motion: the hyperbolic number setting'] Let $\mu$ be the $\mathbb{H}$-valued probability on a measurable
space $\left(X,\sigma\left(X\right)\right)$.

\noindent $\mathrm{(1)}$ If $A\in\sigma\left(X\right)$, then $\mu\left(A\right)+\mu\left(A^{c}\right)=p$, with $p\in\left\{ 1,e_{+},e_{-}\right\} $.

\noindent $\mathrm{(2)}$ If $\phi$ is the empty set of $\sigma\left(X\right)$
in $X$, then $\mu\left(\phi\right)=0$.

\noindent $\mathrm{(3)}$ If $A\subseteq B$ in $\sigma\left(X\right)$,
then $\mu\left(A\right)\leq\mu\left(B\right)$ in $\mathbb{H}$.

\noindent $\mathrm{(4)}$ If $A,B\in\sigma\left(X\right)$, then 
\[
\mu\left(A\cup B\right)=\mu\left(A\right)+\mu\left(B\right)-\mu\left(A\cap B\right),
\]
and hence, 
\[
\mu\left(A\cup B\right)\leq\mu\left(A\right)+\mu\left(B\right),\;\;\;\mathrm{in\;\;\;}\mathbb{H}.
\]

\noindent $\mathrm{(5)}$ If $A_{1}\supseteq A_{2}\supseteq A_{3}\supseteq...,\;\mathrm{\textrm{in}\;}\sigma\left(X\right)$,
and $A=\overset{\infty}{\underset{k=1}{\cap}}A_{k}$ in $X$, then
\[
\underset{k\rightarrow\infty}{\mathrm{lim}}\mu\left(A_{k}\right)=\mu\left(A\right)=\mu\left(\overset{\infty}{\underset{k=1}{\cap}}A_{k}\right).
\]

\noindent $\mathrm{(6)}$ If $A_{1}\subseteq A_{2}\subseteq A_{3}\subseteq...$,
in $\sigma\left(X\right)$, and $A=\overset{\infty}{\underset{k=1}{\cup}}A_{k}$
in $\sigma\left(X\right)$, then 
\[
\underset{k\rightarrow\infty}{\mathrm{lim}}\mu\left(A_{k}\right)=\mu\left(A\right)=\mu\left(\overset{\infty}{\underset{k=1}{\cup}}A_{k}\right).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition 6 of arXiv:2605.30616

body: The Riesz representation theorem, sometimes called the Riesz–Fréchet representation theorem after Frigyes Riesz and Maurice René Fréchet, establishes an important connection between a Hilbert space and its continuous dual space. If the underlying field is the real numbers, the two are isometrically isomorphic; if the underlying field is the complex numbers, the two are isometrically anti-isomorphic. The (anti-) isomorphism is a particular natural isomorphism.
title: Riesz representation theorem

[Thm 9 (G\texorpdfstring{\(\beta\)}{beta}E with rank-one critical deformation) of arXiv:2605.30779, '2605.30779'] Let \(H_N^{(\beta)}\) be the tridiagonal random matrix of dimension \(N\) defined in \eqref{eq:defn_H^beta}. Fix \(\beta>0\) and \(\theta\in\mathbb R\). Let
\begin{equation*}
 
\lambda_1\ge \lambda_2\ge \cdots \ge \lambda_N   
\end{equation*}
be the eigenvalues of $H_N^{(\beta)}+d e_1e_1^\top$ defined in \eqref{eq:defn_H^beta+dee},
and let \(\x_k\) be a unit eigenvector associated with \(\lambda_k\). Let \(k\ge1\) be independent of \(N\). Let \(s_{\beta,k}\) be the unique solution in
\[
\bigl(a_{\beta,k},a_{\beta,k-1}\bigr),
\qquad
a_{\beta,0}:=+\infty,
\]
of
\begin{equation} 
  \mathcal G^{(\beta)}(x)=\theta,
\end{equation}
where \(\mathcal G^{(\beta)}\) is the Airy-Green function from Proposition~\ref{prop:beta_airy_green}. Then, as \(N\rightarrow\infty\), we have the joint convergence in distribution
\begin{align}
 N^{2/3}\bigl(\lambda_k-2\bigr) \Longrightarrow {}& s_{\beta,k}, & N^{1/3}\bigl|\langle e_1,\x_k\rangle\bigr|^2
\Longrightarrow {}&
-\frac{1}{(\mathcal G^{(\beta)})'\!\bigl(s_{\beta,k}\bigr)}.
\end{align}
Moreover, for any finite $K$, \eqref{eq:limit_rank_one_beta} holds jointly for $k = 1, 2, \dotsc, K$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Assume that the action of $G$ on $\wt B$ satisfies the moment condition \eqref{moment-assumption-01},

and the continuous cocycle $\sigma_0: G \times B \to \bb R$ 
satisfies the integrability condition \eqref{moment-assumption-02} and $M_1^{\mu} = M_0^{\mu} \times \bb R$. 
Suppose that, for every $\wt b \in \wt B$ with $\eta(\wt b) \in \supp \nu$, 
we have $\wt b M \subset \overline{\Gamma_{\mu} \wt b}$. 

Let $\sigma: G \times \wt B \to \bb R$ be a continuous cocycle cohomologous to $\sigma_0$. 
Then, for every continuous compactly supported function $h: \bb R \to \bb C$, we have, 
uniformly in $\wt b \in \wt B$ and in $w_n \in \bb R$ with $|w_n| = o(\sqrt{n})$, 
\begin{align*}
 \upsilon_{\mu} \sqrt{2 \pi n} \,  \bb E  \left[ h \left(\sigma(g_n \cdots g_1, \wt b) - n \lambda_{\mu}  - w_n  \right) \right]
\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}  \int_{\bb R}   h(u) du.

[Theorem thm:positive-strip-results of arXiv:2608.18320, 'Asymptotics for Beta-Splitting Trees via Homogeneous Fragmentations and Meromorphic Potent'] Let $\beta>0$ and let $\sigma>0$ be as above. Then
    \[
            r_{\beta,\sigma}(x)
            =
            O_{\beta,\sigma}(e^{-\sigma x}),
            \qquad\text{as }x\to\infty,
    \]
    and
    \begin{equation}
            U_\beta(\mathrm{d} x)
            =
            \eta_\beta\delta_0(\mathrm{d} x)
            +
            \left[
            \frac1{\mu_\beta}
            +
            \sum_{\rho\in\mathcal Z_{\beta,\sigma}}
            u_{\beta,\rho}(x)
            +
            r_{\beta,\sigma}(x)
            \right]\mathrm{d} x.
    \end{equation}
    Consequently, as $n\to\infty$,
    \begin{equation}
            \mathsf E D_n
            =
            \frac{h_{n-1}}{\mu_\beta}
            -
            \frac{\phi_\beta''(0)}{2\mu_\beta^2}
            -
            \sum_{\rho\in\mathcal Z_{\beta,\sigma}}
            \mathcal B_{\beta,\rho}(n)
            +
            O_{\beta,\sigma}(n^{-\sigma}).
    \end{equation}
    The nonreal terms are grouped with their complex conjugates, and the displayed
    expressions are real. Thus, by moving the contour across any prescribed finite
    collection of zeros, one obtains an asymptotic expansion to arbitrary fixed
    algebraic order. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition prop:tailrl-threshold-reparameterization of arXiv:2609.02987, 'Tail Likelihood Reinforcement Learning'] Define
\begin{equation}
F_w(t)
:=
\int_0^t w(s)\,ds,
\qquad
\widetilde r(x,z):=F_w\!\left(r(x,z)\right).

\end{equation}
Then $F_w$ is a strictly increasing map from $[0,1]$ to $[0,1]$, and
\begin{equation}
J_w(\theta;x)
=
\int_0^1
\log
\Pr_{z\sim\pi_\theta(\cdot\mid x)}
\!\left(\widetilde r(x,z)>u\right)
\,du.

\end{equation}
Thus, weighted TailRL on $r$ is exactly uniform TailRL on the monotone rescaling $\widetilde r=F_w(r)$.

body: Let (X,Sigma,mu) be a probability space and T: X -> X measure-preserving. T is (strongly) mixing if mu(T^{-n}A cap B) -> mu(A)mu(B) as n -> infinity for all measurable A, B in Sigma, so that the sets T^{-n}A become asymptotically independent of B in the measure-theoretic sense. Strong mixing implies weak mixing (the Cesaro-averaged statement (1/N) sum_{n=0}^{N-1} |mu(T^{-n}A cap B) - mu(A)mu(B)| -> 0), and weak mixing implies ergodicity; neither implication reverses in general.
title: Mixing (Strong Mixing)

    p(x)=\sum_{k=0}^N x^{N-k}(-1)^k\binom{N}{k}\coef_k(p).
  \]
  Then
  \[
    \widehat{p}(s)=\frac{s^{N+1}}{N!}\Lap{p}(s).
  \]
  Consequently,
  \[
    \log \widehat{p}(s)=\log \Lap{p}(s)+(N+1)\log s-\log N!,
  \]
  and therefore
  \[
    R_p^{(N)}(s)
    =-\frac{1}{N}\frac{d}{ds}\log \Lap{p}(Ns)-\frac{N+1}{Ns}.
  \]

body:
Let M be a compact finite-dimensional real analytic manifold with a positive real analytic Riemannian metric g, and f:M->R a real analytic function. Every gradient ascent trajectory dot X=grad_g f(X) converges to one critical point. Moreover the set of starts whose limit is a critical point at which Hess_g f has a strictly positive eigenvalue has Riemannian volume zero. Thus almost every limiting point has negative semidefinite Hessian. Nonisolated critical points are allowed. For gradient descent reverse the sign convention. The convergence is the Lojasiewicz consequence used in the Appendix A proof of Theorem 4.1 of Geshkovski et al.; avoidance is their Lemma A.1, whose avoidance part only needs smooth f and compact Riemannian M.
Compact finite-dimensional real analytic M
Positive real analytic metric g
Real analytic f
Gradient ASCENT, not arbitrary dynamics

\[

$$
\{W \in \R^{d\times n} \mid \det W_I = \det W_J = 0\}
$$
is covered by finitely many images of $C^\infty$ maps defined on open subsets of
$\R^{dn-2}$. Here $W_I$ denotes the $d\times d$ submatrix of
$W$ formed by the columns indexed by $I$.

[Definition hairy of arXiv:2604.17170, 'CaTherine wheels from trees and Liouville quantum gravity'] A half-zipper is {\em hairy} if every embedded path $I\subset Z$ has branching
on both sides; i.e., there are nontrivial oriented paths $\alpha,\beta \subset Z$
that begin on $I$ and intersect $I$ only at these initial points, and which lie 
respectively to the right and to the left of the oriented interval $I$ in $S^2$.

body:
[Corollary 4 of arXiv:2506.16259, 'Two-dimensional Rademacher walk'] Let $d_1,d_2,d_3\dots,d_n$ be a sequence of positive integers, of which at least $k$ are distinct, say $d_{\ell_1},d_{\ell_2},\dots,d_{\ell_k}$, and let $T_n=\sum_{i=1}^n d_i\eps_i$ where  $\eps_i$ are i.i.d.\ Rademacher. Then for every integer $\displaystyle  m\ge \max_{1\le i\le k}d_{\ell_i}$ we have
$$
\P(T_n\equiv 0\pmod m)\le \frac{C \log k}{k}    
$$
where $C$ is the constant from the statement of Lemma~\ref{modlemma}.
title: Corollary 4 of arXiv:2506.16259

TECHNIQUE CARD (drafted from a spec by a helper model, every card read and seven corrected by the Fable agent on 2026-09-07; canonical statements only, no original claim). For a translation-invariant, ergodic percolation measure on Z^d, or more generally on an amenable transitive graph, satisfying finite energy (insertion and deletion tolerance for each edge conditionally on the rest of the configuration), the number N of infinite open clusters is almost surely a constant in {0, 1, infinity}, and Burton and Keane's argument rules out 2 <= N < infinity as well as N = infinity: if there were at least two infinite clusters with positive density, a positive density of trifurcation points (local configurations forcing at least three disjoint infinite paths) would be forced, but a discrete isoperimetric counting argument on a large box shows the number of trifurcation points cannot exceed a quantity of the order of the box's boundary, contradicting positive density in the bulk unless N <= 1. It follows that N is almost surely 0 or 1. The argument does not apply to non-amenable graphs, where coexistence of infinitely many infinite clusters is a genuine, well-studied phenomenon rather than a proof artifact, and constancy of N itself (ruling out a mixture over the value of N) is a separate ergodic-theory step, not part of the trifurcation-counting argument. Typical failure: Applying Burton-Keane uniqueness to a non-amenable graph, such as a regular tree or a graph with exponential volume growth, and expecting a unique infinite cluster; the trifurcation-point isoperimetric argument fundamentally requires amenability, and on non-amenable graphs the coexistence of infinitely many infinite clusters, studied by Haggstrom, Peres and others, is a real phenomenon that this theorem simply does not rule out. Canonical reference: Burton and Keane, 1989, Communications in Mathematical Physics; Gandolfi, Keane and Newman, 1992, Probability Theory and Related Fields.

[Corollary corlazytran of arXiv:2604.07227, 'Transition probabilities of step-reinforced random walks'] Let $S$, $G$ and $\mu$ be as in Theorem (lazyGinf of the paper) and assume that $\mu$ has finite support $\Gamma$ which generates $G$. \\
    (i).  If $G_{\Gamma}$ is of polynomial growth
$d\geq 1$ (e.g., $\mathbb{Z}^d$), then there exists a positive constant $C_1=C_1(G,\mu, \alpha)$ such that
    $$
\max_{x \in G} \mathbb{P}(S_n=x) \leq C_1 n^{-\frac{d}{2}}, \quad \forall n\geq 1,
    $$
    In particular, if $G_{\Gamma}$ is of at least cubic growth, then $S$ is transient. \\
    (ii). If $G_{\Gamma}$ is of exponential growth (e.g., the lamplighter group over $\mathbb{Z}$), then  there exist positive constants $C_2=C_2(G,\mu, \alpha)$ and $C_3=C_3(G,\mu, \alpha)$ such that
 $$
\max_{x \in G} \mathbb{P}(S_n=x) \leq C_2 e^{-C_3n^{1/3}}, \quad \forall n\geq 1,
    $$
    (iii). If $G_{\Gamma}$ is nonamenable, that is, 
    $$
  \inf\left\{\frac{|\{(x,y) \in E(G_{\Gamma}): x \in A, y \in A^c\}|}{|A|}: \emptyset \neq A \subset G\right\} >0,
    $$
    then there exist positive constants $C_4=C_4(G,\mu, \alpha)$ and $C_5=C_5(G,\mu, \alpha)$ such that
    \begin{equation}
        
        \max_{x \in G} \mathbb{P}(S_n=x) \leq  C_4 e^{-C_5 n},  \quad \forall n\geq 1.
    \end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition defn:slide-diffeo of arXiv:2609.00233, 'A survey on mapping class groups of 3-manifolds'] We define \emph{slide diffeomorphisms}.   Let $P_i$ be one of the prime components of $M$ and form $\widehat{M}$ by removing $P_i\setminus D_i$ and gluing in a 3-ball $E$ to $F_i$.  Let $a$ be an oriented arc in $\widehat M$ such that $E\cap a$  consists of the two endpoints of $a$.  Now use $a$ to define a point-pushing isotopy that moves the centre of $E$ along the arc $a$ and then back to itself.  By isotopy extension this defines a diffeomorphism of $\widehat{M}$ to itself, and, by an argument analogous to that of proving that connected sum is well-defined, we can assume that this diffeomorphism is the identity on $E$.  Hence we can cut out $E$, replace it by $P_i\setminus D_i$ and extend by the identity to obtain the \emph{slide diffeomorphism of} $P_i$ \emph{around} $a$.

There is a similar notion of a slide diffeomorphism obtained by gluing $E$ to $F_k$, for some $k = n+1,\dots,2g$  corresponding to an $S^1 \times S^2$ factor, and sliding $E$ around an arc in the resulting $\widehat{M}$, and back to itself, as before.
title: Definition defn:slide-diffeo of arXiv:2609.00233

ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Compare the two-point functions of the two random sets. Result: The pivotal set and the spectral sample have the same one-point intensity (alpha_4 at each point) and the same two-point function up to constants (both are asymp alpha_4(|x-y|) alpha_4(|x-y|, n) ...), so any singularity must come from higher-order structure. The known difference is in the third moment: E|S|^3 and E|P|^3 differ, and more precisely the conditional law of S given a point x in S has a strictly different clustering structure (spectral sample is 'more clustered'). A proof of mutual singularity of the limiting sets would follow from a law-of-large-numbers statistic that separates them, e.g. the number of points at distance < eps of a typical point normalised by eps^{-3/4}; the limits of these normalised counts are random variables whose laws differ, but singularity needs an a.s. separating statistic, not one in law. Reduction recorded, no proof. Obstruction: One needs an almost-sure local statistic separating the two sets; only distributional differences are known.

[Lemma 21 of arXiv:2608.27372, 'Universality and sharp thresholds for ellipsoid fitting'] Let $\mathcal D\subset\R^N$ be nonempty, bounded, convex, and
	relatively open in its affine hull, and let
	$\mathcal B:\mathcal D\to\R$ be a $\vartheta$-self-concordant barrier
	for some $\vartheta\ge1$. There are universal constants
	$c,c_0,\rho_0>0$ and $C>0$ such that, for every
	$\theta\in\mathcal D$ and $u\in\mathsf V_{\mathcal D}$:
	\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
		\item If $\theta+u\in\mathcal D$ and
		$D_{\mathcal B}(\theta+u,\theta)\le c_0$, then
		\[
			\|u\|_{\mathcal B,\theta}\le\rho_0,
			\qquad
			D_{\mathcal B}(\theta+u,\theta)
			\ge c\|u\|_{\mathcal B,\theta}^2.
		\]
		\item If $\|u\|_{\mathcal B,\theta}\le\rho_0$, then
		$\theta+u\in\mathcal D$ and
		\[
			\left|
			\mathcal B(\theta+u)-\mathcal B(\theta)
			-\mathrm D\mathcal B(\theta)[u]
			-\frac12\mathrm D^2\mathcal B(\theta)[u,u]
			\right|
			\le C\|u\|_{\mathcal B,\theta}^3.
		\]
	\end{enumerate}

ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Controlled generators, exact finite-state diagnostic, coupling, renewal reward or capacity comparison Result: Consider two unit-speed SRPT queues with no future arrivals: queue one holds one job of residual size 100; queue two holds ten jobs of residual size 0.1 each. A new job of size 0.05 preempts either queue and finishes in 0.05. Sending it to queue one delays one existing completion by 0.05; sending it to queue two delays ten existing completions by 0.05 each. Thus the total incremental completion cost is 0.10 versus 0.55, although queue two has much less workload. Least workload is not the correct one-step objective for this size-aware setting. Check: The newcomer is shorter than every existing residual, so every existing completion at the chosen queue shifts by exactly 0.05. Adding its own completion time gives the two displayed costs. Obstruction: Future arrivals and the stationary distribution of dispatcher states are omitted. The example is a diagnostic against a proposed greedy criterion, not the optimal dispatcher.

body: The Feynman-Kac formula represents solutions of linear parabolic PDEs probabilistically: under regularity, the solution of u_t + mu u_x + (1/2) sigma^2 u_xx - r u = 0 with terminal condition u(T, x) = g(x) is u(t, x) = E[exp(-integral of r) g(X_T) | X_t = x] for the diffusion dX = mu dt + sigma dW. It converts PDE problems into expectations (Monte Carlo methods, option pricing) and conversely; the derivation applies Ito's lemma to the discounted candidate and kills the drift term with the PDE.
title: Feynman-Kac Formula

STATEMENT
For ordinary separately bias-corrected Adam with b=.9,d=.999 and
outside-sqrt epsilon, fix positive eta,epsilon and diagonal eigenvalues.
Suppose theta_h=eta*lambda_h/epsilon>38>=theta_l>0. If BOTH physical
coordinates tend to their origins and the low-coordinate standard
initial position is nonzero, then scaled active sharpness has a
subsequence tending to theta_l. In particular it cannot converge to38
if theta_l<38. This is a whole high/low cap range result, not a fixed
numerical-window estimate. It is conditional on origin convergence.

The proof also gives: the high position pair decays at a geometric
rate q<b, while the low position pair has a geometric lower bound at
some rate nu>q. A subsequence of low positions therefore dominates the
high positions. No assumption of coordinate independence is involved.

HARDEST STEP
A bounded solution of an asymptotically hyperbolic two-dimensional
recurrence need not have an assumed stable-mode representation. We
derive its decay by a forward/backward Green contraction, then construct
an inverse-Lyapunov norm for the other coordinate. Repeated low roots
and nonnormal matrices are included.

1. EXACT POSITION-PAIR RECURSION AND ROOTS
Let a_t=eta/[(1-b^(t+1))*P_t]>0 and P_t be the corrected next variance
denominator. Eliminating raw momentum from
x_(t+1)=x_t-a_t*m_(t+1), m_(t+1)=b*m_t+(1-b)*lambda*x_t gives, for t>=1,

 Y_(t+1)=A_t Y_t, Y_t=(x_t,x_(t-1)),
 A_t=[[1+b*a_t/a_(t-1)-(1-b)*lambda*a_t,-b*a_t/a_(t-1)],
      [1,0]].                                             (1)

Origin convergence implies P_t->epsilon, so A_t converges to

 A(theta)=[[T,-b],[1,0]], T=1+b-(1-b)*theta.                 (2)

Every actual A_t is invertible. If the standard scalar initial position
is nonzero, Y_1=(x_1,x_0) is nonzero and hence every later Y_t is nonzero.

Write H=2*(1+b)/(1-b)=38 and f_theta(r)=r^2-T*r+b. For theta_h>H,
f(0)>0, f(-b)=b*(1+b+T)<0 and f(-1)=1+T+b<0. The two real roots
therefore satisfy

 -b<r_s<0, r_u<-1.                                       (3)

For 0<theta_l<H all roots have moduli strictly between b and1. Indeed
|T|<1+b; nonreal roots have modulus sqrt(b). For real roots of the same
sign, a largest modulus R>=1 would imply |T|=R+b/R>=1+b, contradiction;
thus R<1 and the other modulus b/R>b. At theta_l=H the roots are -1,-b.
In every low-cap case the minimum root modulus is at least b.

Choose |r_s|<q<nu<b. All constants below may depend on the fixed caps.

Diagonalize A(theta_h). In its fixed eigenbasis the actual recursion is
Z_(n+1)=[diag(r_s,r_u)+E_n]Z_n, with E_n->0 and a bounded actual solution.
Shift the start far enough that ||E_n||_infinity<=delta for every n>=0,
where delta is small enough for BOTH k=q and k=1 that

 delta*[1/(k-|r_s|)+1/(|r_u|-k)]<1.                      (4)

Let Z_n=(S_n,U_n). Every bounded solution with specified S_0 satisfies

 S_n=r_s^n*S_0+sum_(j<n) r_s^(n-1-j)*(E_j Z_j)_s,
 U_n=-sum_(j>=n) r_u^(n-1-j)*(E_j Z_j)_u.                (5)

The second formula follows by solving the unstable recurrence backwards
from a finite future time and letting that time tend to infinity;
boundedness kills its terminal term. In the weighted sequence space
||Z||_k=sup_n k^(-n)||Z_n||_infinity the linear perturbation in (5) has
norm at most the left side of (4), by geometric sums. Its affine part
r_s^n S_0 belongs to the space for k=q and k=1. The Neumann series gives
a unique fixed point in each space. The q-weighted fixed point is also
bounded because q<1, so uniqueness in the bounded space identifies it
with the actual solution. Thus

 ||Y_h,t||<=C*q^t                                         (6)

after absorbing the finite time shift into C. This is a deterministic
argument with the actual coefficient sequence held fixed; it does not
assume a random environment or an invariant stable graph.

3. A LOWER RATE FOR THE LOW COORDINATE
Put A=A(theta_l). All its eigenvalues have modulus at least b>nu, so

 Q=sum_(k>=0) nu^(2*k)*(A^(-k))^T*A^(-k)                 (7)

converges to a positive definite matrix. To justify convergence without
assuming diagonalizability, put the two-dimensional inverse matrix in
complex Jordan form: its powers grow at most linearly times r^k for
any r larger than its spectral radius, and choose r<1/nu. Thus the
series of quadratic matrices is absolutely convergent. Its exact
identity is

 (A^(-1))^T Q A^(-1)=(Q-I)/nu^2,
 A^T Q A=nu^2 Q+A^T A.                                 (8)

Define g_A=min_{||Y||_Q=1} ||A Y||_Q. Identity (8), invertibility
of A and compactness of the Q unit sphere give g_A>nu. Set
Delta=g_A-nu>0 and use the induced Q operator norm. Choose t0>=1
so that ||A_l,t-A||_Q<Delta for EVERY t>=t0; such a t0 exists
because A_l,t->A. Then, for every Y and every t>=t0,
 ||A_l,t Y||_Q >= (g_A-||A_l,t-A||_Q)*||Y||_Q >= nu*||Y||_Q.
The actual nonzero low pair therefore obeys, with the explicit
positive constant c=||Y_l,t0||_Q*nu^(-t0),

 ||Y_l,t||_Q>=c*nu^t, c>0.                              (9)

Equivalence of two finite-dimensional norms shows that along an
unbounded sequence t_j, |x_l,t_j|>=c'*nu^(t_j). Indeed at every large t
at least one of |x_l,t|,|x_l,t-1| has this size, up to a fixed factor.
Combine with (6) to obtain x_h,t_j/x_l,t_j->0.

FINITE ALGEBRAIC CERTIFICATE FOR THE SAME NORM
The matrix in (7) also has a closed rational form. Put

 w=nu^2*(b+nu^2)*(1+nu^2)
       /[(b-nu^2)*((b+nu^2)^2-nu^2*T^2)],
 Q=[[1+w,-b*T*w/(b+nu^2)],
    [-b*T*w/(b+nu^2),b^2*w/nu^2]].                      (10)

For |T|<=1+b and 0<nu<b<1 the denominator is positive:
b-nu^2>0 and b+nu^2-nu*|T|>=(b-nu)*(1-nu)>0.
Thus w>0, Q11>0 and

 det Q=(b^2*w/nu^2)*(b^2+nu^2)/(b^2-nu^4)>0.

Direct multiplication gives A^T Q A=nu^2 Q+A^T A. Thus (10) can replace
the infinite series and supplies a finite exact algebraic certificate
of the low-coordinate gain, including repeated-root cases. The script
check_origin_rate_algebra.py verifies the matrix identity, determinant
formula and denominator factorization as rational identities; its log
is logs/origin_rate_algebra_exact.json. No truncation or numerical
eigenvalue computation is involved.

4. ACTIVE SHARPNESS AND THE STRICT MIXED-CAP CONSEQUENCE
Both denominators tend to epsilon. Along this subsequence the low
gradient dominates and is nonzero; therefore A_(t_j)->theta_l.
This proves the statement.

Now combine conditionally with024v2 (not yet independently audited). If theta_h>38>theta_l>0 and A_t->38,024 says
the high coordinate approaches its origin or its exact cycle, while
the low coordinate tends to its origin. If its standard initial
position is nonzero, the all-origin alternative contradicts the
subsequence limit just proved. If its initial position is zero,
the low coordinate is identically zero; an all-origin high coordinate
would instead give A_t->theta_h>38 along defined times, also impossible.
Thus the high coordinate MUST approach its cycle, and S_t->38.

Hence persistent top sharpness strictly above38 is IMPOSSIBLE under
active convergence to38 on this entire strict mixed-cap range. At
theta_l=38 the subsequence limit equals38 and gives no contradiction;
024's critical gradient-alignment condition remains the valid criterion.

VALIDATION / LIMITATIONS
This extends the explicit Green argument of016 Section5 beyond its
earlier [2000,3000] high-cap window, and replaces the earlier special
complex-root Q_T identity by an inverse-Lyapunov series valid for all
low caps in(0,38], including repeated real roots. The elementary matrix
identities are supplied in full; no floating-point bound is used.

$$\binom{N}{K}\simeq\left(\frac{1}{t^t(1-t)^{1-t}}\right)^N\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi t(1-t)N}}$$
in the $K\simeq tN\to\infty$ limit, with $t\in(0,1]$. In particular we have
$$\binom{2N}{N}\simeq\frac{4^N}{\sqrt{\pi N}}$$
in the $N\to\infty$ limit, for the central binomial coefficients.

[Definition 1 ({\Cref{Def-log-HT-split}}) of arXiv:2609.00567, 'Hodge--Tate splitting and Akizuki--Nakano vanishing in positive characteristic'] We say that the pair \((X,D)\) is \emph{log Hodge--Tate split}, or \emph{log HT-split} for short, if \(F^{\dR}_{(X,D)}\) admits a splitting in \(\mcalD_{\qcoh}(X)\).  When \(D=0\), we simply say that \(X\) is \emph{HT-split}.

See \Cref{HTSplitMorphism} and \Cref{relative-vs-absolute} for the definition of HT-splitting for arbitrary \(k\)-schemes in terms of de Rham stacks.\footnote{The terminology ``Hodge--Tate splitting'' comes from the Hodge--Tate stack. In characteristic \(p\), the de Rham stack used here is canonically identified with the Hodge--Tate stack relative to the crystalline prism \((\setZ_p,(p))\).}
title: {\Cref{Def-log-HT-split}}

[Thm 4 (\cite{keel1992}) of arXiv:2609.03268, 'Poincare Polynomials of Heavy-Light Hassett Spaces'] Let $R=\Z[x_I: 2\le |I| \le n-2]$ be the polynomial ring over $\Z$ on $2^n-2n-2$ variables. Then there is a quotient map $R\onto A(\DMumford{n})$ given by $x_I\mapsto [D_I]$. Furthermore, the kernel of this quotient map is the ideal generated by the following elements:
            \begin{enumerate}
                \item $x_I-x_{I^c}$ for all $I$;
                \item $x_I x_J$ for each pair $I,J$ such that $\varnothing\notin \{I\cap J, I \cap J^c, I^c\cap J, I^c \cap J^c\};$
                \item (WDVV relations) for $\{a,b,c,d\}\in {[n]\choose 4}$, 
                $$\sum_{I: I\cap\{a,b,c,d\}=\{a,b\}} x_I - \sum_{I: I\cap\{a,b,c,d\}=\{a,c\}} x_I.$$
            \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: Let (X,d) be a compact metric space and f: X -> X continuous. For n>=1 and epsilon>0, define the dynamical metric d_n(x,y) = max_{0<=k<n} d(f^k(x),f^k(y)), and let N(n,epsilon) be the minimum number of d_n-balls of radius epsilon needed to cover X. The topological entropy of f is h(f) = lim_{epsilon -> 0+} limsup_{n -> infinity} (1/n) log N(n,epsilon). It is invariant under topological conjugacy, is nonnegative, and measures the exponential growth rate in n of the number of orbit segments of length n that are distinguishable at resolution epsilon.
title: Topological Entropy

body:
[Lemma 3 of arXiv:2609.03803, 'List-distance consistent vertices in trees are confined to a path'] Let $G=SP(w;\ell_1,\dots,\ell_k)$ with $k\ge3$. Then
\[
  \sigma_i=
  \begin{cases}
    1, & \text{if } k\ge4,\\
    \infty, & \text{if } k=3 \text{ and } \ell_{i'}=1 \text{ for some } i'\ne i,\\
    2, & \text{if } k=3 \text{ and } \ell_{i'}\ge2 \text{ for both } i'\ne i .
  \end{cases}
\]
Moreover
\begin{enumerate}
\item[\textup{(i)}] for $1\le j\le\ell_i$ one has $v_{i,j}\in S_{c_i}(G)$ if and
only if $j\ge\bigl\lceil(\ell_i-\sigma_i)/2\bigr\rceil$, so that
\[
  \bigl|S_{c_i}(G)\cap\{v_{i,1},\dots,v_{i,\ell_i}\}\bigr|
  =\min\Bigl\{\ell_i,\ \bigl\lfloor(\ell_i+\sigma_i)/2\bigr\rfloor+1\Bigr\};
\]
\item[\textup{(ii)}] $w\in S_{c_i}(G)$ if and only if $\ell_i\le\sigma_i$;
\item[\textup{(iii)}] consequently
\[
  \bigl|S_{c_i}(G)\cap\bigl(\{w\}\cup\{v_{i,1},\dots,v_{i,\ell_i}\}\bigr)\bigr|=
  \begin{cases}
    \lceil \ell_i/2\rceil+1, & \text{if } \sigma_i=1,\\
    \lfloor \ell_i/2\rfloor+2, & \text{if } \sigma_i=2,\\
    \ell_i+1, & \text{if } \sigma_i=\infty .
  \end{cases}
\]
\end{enumerate}
Here the conventions for $\sigma_i=\infty$ are that the condition in
\textup{(i)} holds for every $j$, that the count in \textup{(i)} equals
$\ell_i$, and that the inequality in \textup{(ii)} holds.

ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Relate (P)_M to the tail of the regeneration time. Result: (P)_M asks for a polynomial decay P(exit from a slab of width L against the direction l) <= L^{-M}; ballisticity is E[tau_1 | D = infinity] < infinity. A polynomial decay of the atypical exit probability with exponent M forces tail bounds P(tau_1 > n) <= n^{-M/(something)} through the standard slab decomposition, so (P)_M implies moments of tau_1 of order roughly M/d; conversely finite first moment of tau_1 gives, through the same decomposition, only the exit probability from a slab of width L bounded by L^{-1} type estimates, i.e. (P)_1, far below 15d + 5. So the question is equivalent to whether the first moment of the regeneration time automatically upgrades to moments of high order under (UE)+(IID), a self-improving property. Self-improvement is plausible because a heavy tail of tau_1 would require a trap structure incompatible with a positive velocity, but it is exactly the content of the open question and I have no proof. Recorded reduction: (P)_M for large M <=> E[tau_1^{M'}] < infinity for some M' growing with M, so the question is a moment self-improvement question. Obstruction: No self-improvement mechanism for regeneration-time moments is known.

Let (X, Y) be uniform on {-1, 1}^n x {-1, 1}^n with independent coordinate pairs and E[X_i Y_i] = rho, and let r, s >= 0 with rho^2 <= rs <= 1. Then |E[f(X) g(Y)]| <= ||f||_{1+r} ||g||_{1+s} for all real f, g. For s > 0 this two-function bound is equivalent to the one-function bound ||T_rho f||_{(1+s)/s} <= ||f||_{1+r}, and with p = 1 + r, q = (1 + s)/s the condition rho^2 <= rs is rho^2 <= (p - 1)/(q - 1). Conversely, if the bound holds for all f, g on one bit with r, s > 0, then rho^2 <= rs.

PRIVATE PARTIAL CANDIDATE, author-checked only, novelty unverified. For the hyperbolic ideal Poisson-Voronoi zero-cell hole probability H_d(u), the exact source integral implies that exp((d-1)u)*H_d(u) is strictly decreasing for u>=0. For d=2m+1, H_d(u)=exp(-2m*u)/p_m(exp(2u)), where p_m is a degree-m polynomial with strictly positive rational coefficients and p_m(1)=1. The attached proof gives explicit beta-integral coefficients and decreasing density in odd dimensions. The even-dimensional positive-power-series claim is NOT proved, and the whole source conjecture is NOT solved.

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:01d0b950eaa9261b69ef2953f04e554ad38f7a893ca54f6bc9bd87f0bb0a85aa","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/01/01d0b950eaa9261b69ef2953f04e554ad38f7a893ca54f6bc9bd87f0bb0a85aa.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:927afb676ae68f04ff269bf2890ea471aa6c7d98f43063cd34f03e1dbddf9ae5","bundle_entry_key":"hole","bundle_id":"population.probability-variance-joint-laws-and-voronoi-partials-007","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"probability theory","draft":"codex-probability-01a07a40/bundle_007.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.geometry:ideal-voronoi-boundary-hole-monotonicity-odd-positive-polynomial-partial","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# Boundary-hole monotonicity and the odd-dimensional polynomial

Status: private author-checked partial candidate. No independent review, no novelty certification, and no claim that the whole source conjecture is solved.

Source: D'Achille, Curien, Enriquez, Lyons and Unel, *Ideal Poisson--Voronoi tessellations on hyperbolic spaces*, archived as `ideal_voronoi_2023`, Proposition 5.1 and equation (5.1), PDF35; Conjecture 7.5, PDF48. The source already computes the dimension-three formula and observes rationality in odd dimensions. Those facts are credited. The claims attempted here are the all-dimensional monotonicity and positive coefficients in every odd dimension. The even-dimensional power-series coefficient claim remains unresolved.

## Exact starting identity

Let $n=d-1\ge1$ and let $H_d(u)$ be the probability that the hyperbolic ball of radius $u\ge0$ about the origin lies inside its ideal Voronoi cell. Write $J_d(u)=1/H_d(u)$. Equation (5.1) and Proposition 5.1 give

$$
J_d(u)=\frac1{c_d}\int_{\mathbb R^n}
\left(\sqrt{\cosh^2u+|x|^2}-\sinh u\right)^{-2n}\,dx,
\qquad
c_d=\frac{\pi^{n/2}\Gamma(n/2)}{\Gamma(n)}.
$$

The normalization follows independently by setting $u=0$ and integrating $(1+|x|^2)^{-n}$ in polar coordinates. In particular $J_d(0)=1$.

## Monotonicity in every dimension

Set $q=e^{2u}$ and substitute $x=e^{-u}z$. Then

$$
e^{-nu}J_d(u)=\frac1{c_d}\int_{\mathbb R^n}D_q(z)^{-2n}\,dz,
\qquad
D_q(z)=\sqrt{(q+1)^2/4+|z|^2}-(q-1)/2.
$$

The denominator is positive. For $z\ne0$,

$$
\frac{\partial D_q(z)}{\partial q}
=\frac{q+1}{4\sqrt{(q+1)^2/4+|z|^2}}-\frac12<0.
$$

Thus the integrand strictly increases with $q$ away from a null set. All integrals are finite by the exact source identity. Pointwise comparison of two values of $q$ proves that $e^{-nu}J_d(u)$ is strictly increasing; no interchange of differentiation and integration is needed. Taking reciprocals proves

$$
u\longmapsto e^{(d-1)u}H_d(u)
\quad\hbox{is strictly decreasing on }[0,\infty).
$$

The strictness follows because the difference of the positive finite integrands is strictly positive on a set of positive Lebesgue measure.

## Positive rational polynomial for odd dimensions

Let $d=2m+1$, so $n=2m$, with integer $m\ge1$. Put $a=e^{-u}$ and $s=\sinh u=(a^{-1}-a)/2$. In the radial integral make the substitution

$$
y=\sqrt{\cosh^2u+r^2}-s.
$$

Its lower endpoint is $a$, and

$$
r^2=(y-a)(y+a^{-1}),\qquad r\,dr=(y+s)\,dy.
$$

After setting $y=az$, the exact integral becomes

$$
J_{2m+1}(u)=C_m a^{-4m}
\int_1^\infty (z-1)^{m-1}(a^2z+1)^{m-1}
\bigl[a^2(2z-1)+1\bigr]z^{-4m}\,dz,
\qquad C_m=\frac{\Gamma(2m)}{\Gamma(m)^2}.
$$

Here the factor $C_m$ is half the ratio of the $(2m-1)$-sphere area to $c_d$. Expand the two bracketed factors as a polynomial in $a^2$. Every coefficient is a strictly positive integrable function of $z>1$: the only apparent subtraction is $2z-1$, which is positive on this domain. The degree is exactly $m$. The resulting integrals are rational because expanding $(z-1)^{m-1}$ reduces them to finite sums of powers of $z$ with integer exponents at most $-2$.

For an explicit formula, let $B$ denote the beta function, and interpret binomial coefficients outside $0,\ldots,m-1$ as zero. Define, for $0\le j\le m$,

$$
b_{m,j}=\binom{m-1}{j}B(3m-j,m)
+\binom{m-1}{j-1}\left[2B(3m-j,m)-B(3m-j+1,m)\right].
$$

This follows from $\int_1^\infty(z-1)^{m-1}z^{j-4m}\,dz=B(3m-j,m)$. All beta arguments are positive integers. Moreover $B(A+1,m)<B(A,m)$, so each displayed coefficient is positive. Hence

$$
p_m(q)=C_m\sum_{j=0}^m b_{m,j}q^{m-j}
$$

is a degree-$m$ polynomial with strictly positive rational coefficients, and

$$
H_{2m+1}(u)=\frac{e^{-2mu}}{p_m(e^{2u})}.
$$

The normalization gives $p_m(1)=1$. The first two cases are

$$
p_1(q)=\frac{q+2}{3},\qquad
p_2(q)=\frac{q^2}{7}+\frac{16q}{35}+\frac25.
$$

The first reproduces the already-known dimension-three formula in Remark 5.2. It is a control, not a newly solved special case.

## An additional odd-dimensional consequence

The polynomial representation makes $J_d(u)$ a positive sum of exponentials with rates in $[n,2n]$. Let $L=\log J_d$. Under the exponential weights, $L'$ is the mean rate and $L''$ its variance. Therefore $L'\ge n$ and $L''\le n^2/4$. The density $f=-H_d'=H_dL'$ satisfies

$$
f'=H_d\bigl(L''-(L')^2\bigr)<0.
$$

This proves the source's proposed decreasing-density property in odd dimensions. It also implies that the median is smaller than the mean. For completeness, if $M>0$ is the median and $v=f(M)>0$, convexity of the survival function gives

$$
H_d(x)\ge\max\{1/2-v(x-M),0\},\qquad x\ge0.
$$

Integrating yields $E X\ge(1/2+vM)^2/(2v)\ge M$, since the difference in the last inequality is $(vM-1/2)^2/(2v)$. Strict convexity makes the first inequality strict on a positive-length interval. The mean is finite by the source exponential tail bound.

## Adversarial checks and remaining gap

The load-bearing points to try to break are the factor from the radial Jacobian, the power $a^{-4m}$, and the distinction between polynomial positivity in $q=e^{2u}$ and power-series positivity in $u$. The check script compares the beta coefficients with an independent expansion and exact integration of the radial polynomial. It also compares the resulting formula with the original angular integral in Proposition 5.1, including even dimensions for the separate monotonicity calculation.

The even-dimensional positive-power-series assertion is not implied by monotonicity and is not proved here. No independent referee has checked this packet, and the bounded literature search is not a novelty certificate. [Proposition 24 of arXiv:2608.15914, 'Absorption cutoff and stationary singularities for rounded Gaussian random dynamical syste'] The threshold $A_{\mathrm{ex}}(\varrho)$ belongs to $(0,\infty)$. If
  $A>A_{\mathrm{ex}}(\varrho)$, then $V_{A,\varrho}$ has at least two
  positive fixed points in
  $(0,M_\varrho)$. There exist
  $0<\alpha_-<\alpha_+$ such that
  \begin{equation}
    A^2m_\varrho(\alpha_\pm)=\alpha_\pm^2,
  \end{equation}
  and $\widehat h_\pm:=\alpha_\pm^2/A^2$ are fixed points of
  $V_{A,\varrho}$.

  Moreover, $\mathcal O_{A,\varrho}$ is nonempty and has finitely many
  connected components. If $(h_-,h_+)$ is its rightmost positive-drift
  component, then
  \begin{equation}
    0<h_-<h_+<M_\varrho,
    \qquad
    V(h_-)=h_-,
    \qquad
    V(h_+)=h_+,
  \end{equation}
  and $V(h)>h$ on $(h_-,h_+)$. The fixed point $h_+$ is isolated, and there
  exists $\eta_0>0$ such that
  \begin{equation}
    h_+-\eta_0>h_-,
    \qquad
    h_++\eta_0<M_\varrho,
    \qquad
    V(h)<h
    \quad\mbox{for }h\in(h_+,h_++\eta_0].
  \end{equation}

[Definition 29 of arXiv:2609.03386, 'Twisted Gradient Flow Approach to Vegetation-Rainfall-Bushfire Interactions Model'] A quadruple $(u,v,w,z):=(u_{\text{{\tiny $\delta,\!\varepsilon$}}},v_{\text{{\tiny $\delta,\!\varepsilon$}}},w_{\text{{\tiny $\delta,\!\varepsilon$}}},
z_{\text{{\tiny $\delta,\!\varepsilon$}}})$ is called a strong solution to the approximate initial-boundary value problem 
$\mbox{(AP)}{}_{\text{{\tiny $\delta,\!\varepsilon$}}}$ on $[0,T]$ if and only if the following properties are satisfied:

\begin{enumerate}\leftskip12pt
\item[(a1)] $(u,w,z) \in \left(W^{1,2}(0,T\,;L^2(\Omega)) \cap L^\infty (0,T\,;H^1(\Omega)) \cap L^2(0,T\,;H^2(\Omega))\right)^3$.\\[-0.3cm]
\item[(a2)] $v \in W^{1,2}(0,T\,;L^2(\Omega))$.\\[-0.3cm]
\item[(a3)] The system \{\eqref{Equation-4-1}--\eqref{Equation-4-4}\} with the boundary condition \eqref{Equation-4-5} is satisfied in the following variational 
sense for a.e. $t \in (0,T)$:

\begin{gather}

u'(t)-D_1 \Delta_N u(t)=\beta_{\text{{\tiny $\delta$}}} (u(t))\{c_1 v(t)-c_2 w(t)\} \quad \text{in} \quad L^2(\Omega),\\

v'(t)+(M_{\text{{\tiny $\delta,\!z(t)$}}})^{-1} v(t)=v(t)\{c_3 \beta_\delta (w(t))-c_4 \beta_\delta (u(t))\} \quad \text{in} \quad L^2(\Omega),\\

w'(t)-D_2 \Delta_N w(t)+c_5w(t)=c_6-c_7 v(t) \beta_\delta (w(t)) \quad \text{in} \quad L^2(\Omega),\\

z'(t)-\varepsilon \Delta_N z(t)=v'(t) \quad \text{in} \quad L^2(\Omega).
\end{gather}

\item[(a4)] $(u(0),v(0),w(0),z(0))=(u_0,v_0,w_0,v_0) \quad \text{in} \quad (L^2(\Omega))^4$.
\end{enumerate}

[Theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] Given a normal operator $T\in B(H)$, the following hold, for both the continuous calculus and the measurable calculus morphisms:
\begin{enumerate}
\item These morphisms are $*$-morphisms.

\item The function $\bar{z}$ gets mapped to $T^*$.

\item The functions $Re(z),Im(z)$ get mapped to $Re(T),Im(T)$.

\item The function $|z|^2$ gets mapped to $TT^*=T^*T$.

\item If $f$ is real, then $f(T)$ is self-adjoint. 
\end{enumerate}

[Lemma 4 of arXiv:2608.27433, 'Scalar curvature on K\"ahler blow-ups and systolic inequalities'] Let \(d(x)=\dist_\omega(x,S)\). At every $p\in S$, there are holomorphic coordinates $(z_1,\ldots,z_k,w_1,\ldots,w_{n-k})$, centered at $p$, such that $S=\{z=0\}$,
\begin{equation}
  d^2=|z|^2(1+\rho(z,w)),
  \qquad \rho=O(|z|+|w|),
\end{equation}
with all higher derivatives of $\rho$ uniformly bounded on smaller coordinate balls, and
\begin{equation}
  \omega=\ddbar\bigl(|z|^2+|w|^2+\Phi(z,w)\bigr),
\end{equation}
where
\[
  \nabla^j\Phi=O(|z|^{3-j}+|w|^{3-j})\quad(0\le j<3),
\]
and all higher derivatives are uniformly bounded. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition 8 of arXiv:2609.03976, '2609.03976'] Let $\mathcal{M}$ be a coherent $\mathcal{D}_{Y}$ module. A V-filtration along $X \times \{0\} \subset X \times \mathbb{C}$ on $\mathcal{M}$ is a decreasing filtration $V^{\bullet}\mathcal{M}$ indexed by rational numbers satisfying the following conditions.
	
	$(1)$ It is exhaustive, i.e. $\bigcup_{\alpha \in \mathbb{Q}}V^{\alpha}\mathcal{M}=\mathcal{M}$,
	
	$(2)$ It is discrete and left continuous. This means that there exists a positive integer $N$ large enough such that for every $i \in \mathbb{Z}$ and $\alpha \in (\frac{i}{N},\frac{i+1}{N})$, $V^{\alpha}\mathcal{M}$ is constant.
	
	$(3)$ For every $\alpha \in \mathbb{Q}$ and $i \in \mathbb{Z}$, we have $V^{i}\mathcal{D}_{Y} \cdot V^{\alpha}\mathcal{M} \subset V^{i+\alpha}\mathcal{M}$.
	
	$(4)$ For every $\alpha \in \mathbb{Q}$, the operator $s+\alpha$ is nilpotent on $\mathrm{Gr}_{V}^{\alpha}\mathcal{M}:=V^{\alpha}\mathcal{M}/\bigcup_{\beta>\alpha}V^{\beta}\mathcal{M}$.
	
	$(5)$ For every $\alpha \in \mathbb{Q}$, $V^{\alpha}\mathcal{M}$ is finitely generated over $V^{0}\mathcal{D}_{Y}$.
	
	$(6)$ We have $t \cdot V^{\alpha}\mathcal{M}=V^{\alpha+1}\mathcal{M}$ for $\alpha>0$.

[Proposition 19 (Semi-concavity of the free energy) of arXiv:2606.16636, 'Free energy of non-convex multi-species spin glasses with centered Ising spins'] There exists a constant $C<+\infty$ (depending only on $\xi$) such that, for every $N\in\N$, $c>0$, $t,t'\geq c$, $q,q'\in \mcl Q^\sS_{\uparrow,c}$ with $\dot q-\dot q' \in L^2$, and $r\in[0,1]$, we have
\begin{equation}
    (1-r)\bar F_N(t,q)+ r \bar F_N(t',q') - \bar F_N\Ll((1-r)(t,q)+r(t',q')\Rr) 
    \leq Cr(1-r)c^{-2}\Ll((t-t')^2+\Ll|\dot q-\dot q'\Rr|_{L^2}^2\Rr).
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Semi-concavity of the free energy

body:
[Lemma 3.2 of arXiv:2110.05374, 'When Janson meets McDiarmid: Bounded difference inequalities under graph-dependence'] (A step in the proof of Theorem 2.1.) Let X = (X_1, ..., X_n) be G-dependent for a Rooted and Ordered dependency tree G on [n], with p_i, S_i and x^{(i)} as in the proof setting. Then for every i ∈ [n−1] and ω_{S_i} ∈ Ω_{S_i}, P(X_{S_i} = ω_{S_i} | X_{[i]} = x_{[i]}) = P(X_{S_i} = ω_{S_i} | X_{[i]} = x^{(i)}_{[i]}): given X_{[i−1]}, the conditional law of X_{S_i} does not depend on the value of X_i. The proof shows that X_{V(T_i)}, T_i the subtree rooted at i, is independent of (X_{S_i}, X_{[i−1]\V(T_i)}).
G-dependent (Definition 1.3 of the paper): X = (X_i)_{i∈V(G)} is G-dependent when for all disjoint S, T ⊂ V(G) with no edge of G between S and T, the families (X_i)_{i∈S} and (X_j)_{j∈T} are independent; this is stronger than pairwise independence of non-adjacent coordinates.
Proof setting (Section 3 of the paper): G is a dependency tree on [n] that is Rooted (rooted at vertex n, with c_n = c_min) and Ordered (j is a descendant of i only if j < i), which a topological sort always provides; p_i is the parent of a non-root vertex i, S_i := [i+1, n] \ {p_i}, and for x ∈ Ω and x'_i ∈ Ω_i, x^{(i)} := (x_1, ..., x_{i−1}, x'_i, x_{i+1}, ..., x_n). The paper writes conditional probabilities of point events; for non-discrete Ω_i read them as conditional distributions.

[Definition def:DeltaF of arXiv:2608.30166, 'Square Functions and Rectifiability\\ under Monotone Transformations of the Density'] Let $F\colon(0,\infty)\to\mathbb{R}$ be a Borel function. For $x\in\operatorname{supp}(\mu)$ and $r>0$ set
\[
\Delta^F_\mu(x,r):=F\bigl(D_\mu(x,r)\bigr)-F\bigl(D_\mu(x,2r)\bigr).
\]
For $x\notin\operatorname{supp}(\mu)$ we set $\Delta^F_\mu(x,r):=0$; since
$\mu(\mathbb{R}^d\setminus\operatorname{supp}(\mu))=0$, this convention does not affect any of the integrals
below. Given a compact interval $J\subset(0,\infty)$ and $\lambda\ge 1$, we say $F$ is
\emph{bi-Lipschitz on $J$ with constant $\lambda$} if
\[
\lambda^{-1}|s-t|\;\le\;|F(s)-F(t)|\;\le\;\lambda|s-t|
\qquad\text{for all } s,t\in J.
\]
We do not assume that $F$ is monotone; see Remark~(rem:scope of the paper).
title: Definition def:DeltaF of arXiv:2608.30166

[Proposition prop:Laplacian of arXiv:2605.01444, 'From second moments to pairwise negative correlation: \\applications to minimal and unifor'] Let $G$ be a finite graph and let $L_G$ be the associated Laplacian matrix. Then the following conclusions hold. 
\begin{enumerate}
	\item[(1)]  $L_G$ is positive semi-definite.
	
	\item[(2)] The smallest eigenvalue $\lambda_1=0$ and a corresponding eigenvector is $\mathbf{1}=(1,\ldots,1)^{\mathsf T}$. Here $M^{\mathsf T}$ denotes the transpose of $M$. 
	
	\item[(3)] The multiplicity of $0$ as an eigenvalue of $L_G$ is equal to the number of connected components of $G$. In particular, $\lambda_2>0$ if and only if $G$ is connected. 
	
	\item[(4)] The largest eigenvalue $\lambda_n\;\leqslant\; \max\left\{\deg(u;G)+\deg(v;G) \mid \{u,v\in E(G)\} \right\}$\,.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition prop:Laplacian of arXiv:2605.01444

[Theorem 17 (Variance) of arXiv:2605.14206, 'The clumsy coupon collector's problem'] The variance of $T_{m,p}$ is
  \[
    \Var(T_{m,p}) = 
      m^2 \sum_{i,j=1}^m \frac{1}{ij} \left[ \frac{1}{\left(1-p\right)^{i+j}}
      - \frac{1}{(1-p)^j} \right]
      + \sum_{\ell=1}^m \frac{m}{\ell} \left(\frac{m}{\ell}-1\right)
      \frac{1}{\left(1-p\right)^\ell}.
  \]
  This quantity increases in both $m$ and $p$. Moreover,
  the first sum vanishes for $p = 0$. For fixed $m$,
  the function $p \mapsto \Var(T_{m,p})$ is convex. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Variance

Own-work draft: C027 v2, proof (unaudited); independent audit and novelty unverified. Let d>=3, u a unit vector and W_0 uniform on S^(d-1). Consider dW_t=g_t(W_t)dt-lambda(t)(d-1)W_t dt+sqrt(2lambda(t))(I-W_t W_t^T)dB_t, with deterministic smooth tangent drift g on each compact time interval and deterministic continuous nonnegative temperature lambda. For a mean-field application, g_t is evaluated along the actual deterministic law, not another frozen candidate law. Write D(t)=E|g_t(W_t)|^2, J(t)=integral_0^t sqrt(D(s))ds<infinity and C_d=Gamma(d/2)/(sqrt(pi)Gamma((d-1)/2)). Then |Pr(u.W_t>0)-1/2| <= min(1/2,2 C_d^(2/3) J(t)^(2/3)) <= min(1/2,2 C_d^(2/3)[t integral_0^t D(s)ds]^(1/3)). Couple W to uniform stationary spherical Brownian motion V driven by the same Brownian path and initial point. With h=E|W-V|^2 and c=W.V, the exact heat contribution to h prime is -2lambda E[(d-2-c)|W-V|^2]<=0 for d>=3. Thus sqrt(h)<=J. A one-sided uniform equatorial strip has mass at most C_d a, giving mass displacement <=C_d a+h/a^2 for 0<a<=1. If the actual law is axial with a smooth overlap density and zero pole current, the signed equatorial-current integral is Pr(u.W_t>0)-1/2. This bounds the absolute value of that signed integral, not the time integral of absolute current, either flux summand separately, or its direction. It does not prove sign selection, polynomial learning, or low-temperature mixing. At positive temperature D is only the gradient-square part of risk dissipation; replacing its time integral by a risk gap requires a separate heat-term argument. Exact algebra and 15 boundary cases passed; the Lean runtime timed out, so no formal certificate is asserted.

[Definition 8 of arXiv:2609.01362, '{Double cluster swapping for spin models: \\Pfaffian relations and sharpness}'] Let $\P_{G,\beta,h}$ be the probability measure on $\R^V \times \R^V \times \left\{ 0,1 \right\}^{ \overline{E}} \times \left\{ 0,1 \right\}^E$ defining the law of $(\vpp,\vpm,\w^+,\w^-)$ in the following construction. 
	\begin{enumerate}[(1)]
	\item Sample $\vp$ and $\vp'$ from $\left< \cdot \right>_{G,\beta,h} \otimes \left< \cdot \right>_{G,\beta,h}$ and then define $\vp^+$ and $\vp^-$ as above. 
	\item We now construct the percolation model $\w^+ \in \left\{ 0,1 \right\}^{ \overline{E}}$. For each $uv \in E$, we set $\w^+_{uv} = 0$ (i.e.~close the edge) if $\vpp_u\vpp_v \leq 0$ and otherwise set $\w^+_{uv} = 1$ (i.e.~open the edge) with probability
		\[
			1 - \exp(-4\beta \xi^+_u \xi^+_v).
		\] 
		We also set $\w^+_{u\g} = 0$ if $\vpp_u \leq 0$ and otherwise set $\w^+_{u\g} = 1$ with probability $1-\exp(-4h\xi^+_u)$ for each $u \in V$. 
	\item We construct $\w^- \in \left\{ 0,1 \right\}^E$ via a similar procedure. That is, we open $\w^-_{uv}$ on an edge $uv \in E$ if and only if $\vp^-_u\vp^-_v > 0$ and then with probability $1 - \exp(-4\beta\xi^-_u\xi^-_v)$.
	\end{enumerate}
	The additional randomness used to determine if an edge of $\w^+$ or $\w^-$ is opened are all independent from one another.
title: Definition 8 of arXiv:2609.01362

body:
[Lemma 11 of arXiv:2607.13401, 'Total variation cutoff for Kac's walk on the sphere'] For every \(\varepsilon>0\), there are constants
\(n_0=n_0(\varepsilon)\) and \(C_\varepsilon<\infty\) such that, for all
\(n\ge n_0\) and all \(t\ge0\),
\begin{equation}
        \mb E W_t^2
        \le
        C_\varepsilon
        \exp\left\{-\left(\frac{29}{32}-\varepsilon\right)\frac{t}{n}\right\}.
\end{equation}
Consequently, for every \(2<p<4\) and every \(\varepsilon>0\), with
\begin{equation}
        \sigma_p
        :=
        \left(2-\frac p2\right)\frac12
        +
        \left(\frac p2-1\right)\frac{29}{32}
        =
        \frac{6+13p}{64},
\end{equation}
there are constants \(n_0=n_0(p,\varepsilon)\) and
\(C_{p,\varepsilon}<\infty\) such that, for all \(n\ge n_0\) and all
\(t\ge0\),
\begin{equation}
        \mb E W_t^{p/2}
        \le
        C_{p,\varepsilon}
        \exp\left\{-\left(\sigma_p-\varepsilon\right)\frac{t}{n}\right\}.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma 11 of arXiv:2607.13401

[Theorem 17 of arXiv:2606.22964, 'Signature McKean--Vlasov stochastic differential equations'] Let $(\mathcal{X},\rho)$ be a Polish space and $p\geq 1$. If $\{\mu_k\}_{k\in\mathbb{N}}$ is a sequence of measures in $\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{X})$, then the following statements are equivalent:
    \begin{enumerate}[i)]
        \item $\{\mu_k\}_{k\in\mathbb{N}}$ converges weakly in $\mathcal{P}^p(\mathcal{X})$ to $\mu$.
        \item $\mathcal{W}^p(\mu_k,\mu)\xrightarrow{k\rightarrow\infty}0$.
    \end{enumerate}

[Theorem 10 of arXiv:2608.00449, 'First-order phase transitions in the hard-core model'] \label[theorem]{thm:abtreedynamics}
    Fix $\lambda \ge 0$ and integers $2\le a<b$. Let $g:[0,\infty]\to[0,\infty]$ be the function $g = f_{a,\lambda}\circ f_{b,\lambda}$. There is a value $\overline{\lambda}$, defined in \Cref{lem:bifpoint}, such that the following statements hold.
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item If $\lambda < \overline{\lambda}$, then $g$ has exactly one fixed point $r^1$, which is attracting and has basin of attraction $[0,\infty]$.
        \item If $\lambda = \overline{\lambda}$, then $g$ has two fixed points $r^0 < r^1$ such that $g'(r^0)=1$ and $r^1$ is attracting.
        \item If $\lambda > \overline{\lambda}$, then $g$ has three fixed points $r^0 < r^* < r^1$ such that $r^*$ is repelling and $r^0$ and $r^1$ are attracting.
        \item We have
        \[ \lim_{\lambda\downarrow\overline{\lambda}}|r^1-r^0| > 0. \]
        \item The behavior of $h = f_{b,\lambda}\circ f_{a,\lambda}$ is similar and can be described in terms of the parameter above as follows:
        \begin{itemize}
            \item If $\lambda < \overline{\lambda}$, then $h$ has exactly one fixed point $f_{b,\lambda}(r^1)$, which is attracting.
            \item If $\lambda = \overline{\lambda}$, then $h$ has two fixed points $f_{b,\lambda}(r^1) < f_{b,\lambda}(r^0)$ such that $h'(f_{b,\lambda}(r^0))=1$ and $f_{b,\lambda}(r^1)$ is attracting.
            \item If $\lambda > \overline{\lambda}$, then $h$ has three fixed points $f_{b,\lambda}(r^1) < f_{b,\lambda}(r^*) < f_{b,\lambda}(r^0)$ such that $f_{b,\lambda}(r^*)$ is repelling and $f_{b,\lambda}(r^0)$ and $f_{b,\lambda}(r^1)$ are attracting.
        \end{itemize}
    \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 10 of arXiv:2608.00449

[Prop orth-lvl of arXiv:2608.28504, 'Global $\bm\infty$-categories and global Thom spectra'] Let $G$ be a compact Lie group. There is a unique model structure on $\cat{$\bm G$-$\textbf{\textup{L}}$-Top}$ where a map $f\colon X\to Y$ is a weak equivalence or fibration if and only if $f(V)^\varphi\colon X(V)^\varphi\to Y(V)^\varphi$ is a weak homotopy equivalence or Serre fibration, respectively, for every compact Lie group $H$, every \emph{faithful} $H$-representation $V$, and every continuous group homomorphism $\varphi\colon H\to G$.

    We call this the \emph{$\bm G$-global level model structure} and its weak equivalences the \emph{$\bm G$-global level weak equivalences}. This model category is proper, topological, and cofibrantly generated with generating cofibrations
    \[\hskip-0.6pt\hfuzz=0.6pt
        \{\textbf{\textup{L}}(V,-)\times_\varphi G\times(\partial D^n\hookrightarrow D^n) : \text{$V$\kern1pt faithful $H$\kern-1pt-representation}, \varphi\colon H\to G,n\ge0\}
    \]
    and generating acyclic cofibrations
    \[
        \{\textbf{\textup{L}}(V,-)\times_\varphi G\times( D^n\hookrightarrow D^n\times I) : \text{$V$\kern1pt faithful $H$\kern-1pt-representation},\varphi\colon H\to G,n\ge0\},
    \]
    where $\textbf{\textup{L}}(V,-)\times_\varphi G$ denotes the quotient of $\textbf{\textup{L}}(V,-)\times G$ by the diagonal of the right $H$-action on $\textbf{\textup{L}}(V,-)$ via precomposition and the right $H$-action on $G$ via $\varphi$.\qed (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
