{"artifact_digest":"sha256:d4d5f9eaff104604e82b82c90ae5affd1f40078c9d21a288b4172b361c868b0d","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/d4/d4d5f9eaff104604e82b82c90ae5affd1f40078c9d21a288b4172b361c868b0d.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:890ed54f36013dd22f1ca06470ed4711a62a3aaa3229cf8fafcfe71706f77b32","bundle_entry_key":"posterior-native-branches-all-fractions","bundle_id":"population.t379-true-posterior-native-branches-all-fractions-20261020","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"calibrated generation; verification; conditional Bayes; robust minimax","draft":"w709/bundle_018.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:learning.calibration:kalai-vempala-true-posterior-native-branch-global-minimax","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# Native branches with the true posterior: every verifier fraction

T379-C026 v2, proof (unaudited). Target1, secondary target2.
Independent mathematical, priority and scope audits pending.

## Statement and exact experiment

Integers d>=1,N>=2d+1,K>=2,1<=r<K,F=K-r,gcd(r,F)=1.
There are d pairs of variable contexts. One context in each pair is A
with an arbitrary r-subset of K truths; its sibling S has all K truths.
The other N-2d contexts are known S. The source selects a context
uniformly then a truth uniformly. Independently, a verifier supplies a
uniform ell-subset of truths in BOTH variable contexts, including S,
for ANY integer0<=ell<=r. Observe ANY n>=0 iid untagged source facts.
Every realized output generator, including each random seed realization,
must have source Mis_infinity<=c in ALL worlds compatible with these
facts/certificates, using its exact probability score bins, where
0<=c<1/(2NrK). Learning policies may randomize.

Use the uniform prior on the finite world family (independent fair
orientations and uniform A truth supports). For pair i let u,v be its
sample counts and a,b its observed-plus-certified distinct truth counts.
A pair is resolved iff max(a,b)>r. If unresolved, write h=min(a,b) and

 L(u,j)=(K/r)^u * binom(K-j,r-j)/binom(K-ell,r-ell),
 pi=L(u,a)/(L(u,a)+L(v,b)).

Here pi is the true ORIGINAL-data probability that the left context is
A. L=0 for j>r; unresolved L values are positive. Repeated facts affect
u,v even if they do not increase a,b. After any proof-only forgetting of
surplus truths, retain THIS posterior, not a recomputed surrogate.

Each unresolved pair independently chooses one of two native branches:

 PAIRED: if h<r, one object
   (m,f,p)=(2(K-h), F, (2-h/r-h/K)/N).
   If h=r, F identical units (2,1,1/(NK)).

 WHOLE: TWO objects
   (K,F*pi,1/N) and (K,F*(1-pi),1/N).

Resolved pairs contribute one object
(K-j,F,(r-j)/(Nr)) when the identified A has union size j<r;
they contribute none when j=r. Coordinates are size, posterior expected
false count, and source mass invariant across compatible worlds.

For any selected branches, partition ALL their objects into nonempty
cells S. Let m_S,f_S,p_S be coordinate sums, rho_S=f_S/m_S.
Define

 beta_c(D)=min_branches,partitions [
                 sum_S rho_S*p_S-c*max_S rho_S].          (1)

An empty native family has value0. Claim:

(A) beta_c(D) is the exact conditional BAYES optimum over all robustly
feasible generators. It need not lower-bound each actual world's loss.

(B) The global expected robust minimax frontier, where the world is
fixed before data and learning-policy randomization, is

 Gamma(c)=E_uniform_world,data beta_c(D).                 (2)

The expectation can equivalently be evaluated in any fixed actual
world, because beta is an invariant scalar statistic. Achieving equal
fixed-world risks may require randomizing the LEARNING POLICY.

This removes the half-alphabet verifier requirement for the exact finite
optimization. It DOES NOT prove an estimator polynomial in growing
VC dimension d or alphabet K. The remaining efficient-estimation step
of Target1 and the classical labeled ERM/PAC formulation remain open.

## Source rigidity and removal of universally false atoms

Let Delta=1/(NrK). Each source probability is an integer multiple of
Delta. If g has source TV-to-uniform-score-coarsening at most c in every
compatible world, the source mass of any exact g-score bin differs
between two worlds by at most2c<Delta. Thus it is identical in all worlds.
A zero-score bin must have zero source mass: any positive source mass
would be at least Delta>c.

Use C022's globally-false removal lemma: remove atoms false in EVERY
compatible world without increasing robust calibration or false mass
in any world. For a mixed bin with m atoms, f false and z universally
false, retaining its total generator mass uniformly on m-z atoms changes
the false fraction from f/m to(f-z)/(m-z)<=f/m. Pure-false bin mass is
transferred to remaining bins as in that lemma; TV does not increase.
Exact score mergers contract TV. The lemma is applied before the
component analysis. Universally false atoms can remain in the zero bin,
but cannot donate c mass: they have zero source mass.

## Pair classification, and why one consistent branch suffices

For unresolved pairs with unequal unions, apply C019's coprime
surplus-forgetting reduction to the SCORE PARTITION of the given g:
balance at h=min(a,b). This preserves each original compatible world's
source bin masses and false-count vectors for this g. It enlarges a
support family solely in the proof; it does not change the original
posterior used in Bayes expectations. The reduction includes cases
where only one sibling is saturated. It relies on gcd(r,F)=1 there.

For clarity, classify the balanced game directly. If h<r, swaps among
residual true/false atoms force ALL K-h outside atoms of a context into
one score bin. For a given bin let x,y in{0,1} indicate whether it
contains the left/right outside sets, and a0,b0 in[0,h] its numbers of
known truths from each context. Source-mass invariance under flipping
the pair is equivalent to

                   a0-b0=h(x-y).                       (3)

If x=y, then a0=b0. A bin with both outside sets is the paired residual,
possibly containing equal additional known truths. If x=1,y=0, (3)
forces a0=h,b0=0: that bin contains the entire left context and NONE of
the right context. Necessarily the right outside set belongs to another
bin containing the entire right context. These are exactly the TWO
whole-context objects. The opposite case is symmetric. If both entire
contexts share one bin, it may instead be viewed as the paired branch
with all h known truth pairs included. Hence each pair consistently
uses either a paired branch or both whole contexts; no mixed fragment
of one whole context is an additional branch.

For h=r the known truth set is the complete A support. In one bin let
a0,b0 in[0,r] count the known truths and x,y in[0,F] the outside atoms.
Invariance becomes

                  F(a0-b0)=r(x-y).                      (4)

Coprimality forces (a0-b0,x-y) to be either(0,0),(r,F),
or(-r,-F). Nonzero cases are an entire whole context and force its
sibling into another whole-context bin as above. Zero cases pair
known truths and pair outside atoms. Each outside pair is a native
unit of size2, source mass1/(NK), and exactly one false atom in each
world. Its posterior expected false count is1. Pairing in this LOWER
argument may depend on the original bin; the native UPPER may use any
canonical cross-context pairing. Units are identical objects.

For a resolved A with j<r, ordinary residual support swaps force its
outside K-j atoms into one bin. Its known truths have fixed source
density1/(Nr); resolved S atoms have density1/(NK). For j=r its
outside atoms have already been removed as universally false.

## Conditional Bayes lower bound

Fix the true posterior from the ORIGINAL data and a feasible g after
universally-false removal. Every original source bin has a common mass
P_B. For that bin let f_B be its posterior expected false count,
rho_B=f_B/|B| and G_B its generator mass. Then

 E[false mass(g)|D]=sum_B rho_B G_B
     >=sum_B rho_B P_B-c*max_B rho_B.                    (5)

This is the TV transport inequality with a relaxed zero-risk recipient;
it is a LOWER bound even when this particular partition lacks a
zero-risk bin. The small budget makes every positive-source cell large
enough to donate c. A zero-source cell is not an admissible donor.

Apply the classification pair by pair. Whole-context components have
source mean density lambda=1/(NK) and posterior false counts F*pi or
F*(1-pi). Paired residual components have mean density<=lambda and
expected false count F. Saturated units have density lambda/2 and
false count1. Identified A residuals have density<=lambda and false
count F. All remaining safe components have density>=lambda:
known unresolved truth pairs have density
sigma=(1/(Nr)+1/(NK))/2; resolved A known truths density1/(Nr);
known S truths density lambda.

In each bin analytically remove safe components. If its risk-bearing
parts have total size m and mass p with p/m<=lambda, adding a safe
component of size s and mass t>=lambda*s can only increase mean density:
(p+t)/(m+s)>=p/m. Thus removing safe parts weakly decreases baseline
Bayes false cost, preserves f and increases rho=f/m. Empty safe-only
bins disappear. For a paired residual containing additional known
truth pairs, peel ALL such pairs, each at density sigma>=lambda; the
same inequality gives the native h residual. NO whole-context-to-paired
replacement is used and NO h>=K/2 assumption enters.

The remaining objects form a partition of exactly one allowed branch
per pair plus the identified A residuals. Expected false counts are
preserved in each old bin: paired residuals/units have orientation-
independent counts, while whole contexts retain their true F*pi counts.
The support-forgetting proof did not replace these posterior weights.
If P is this mapped native partition, then

 sum_old rho_B P_B>=sum_P rho_S p_S,
 max_old rho_B<=max_P rho_S.

Together with(5), original conditional Bayes loss is at least the
objective of P, hence at least beta_c(D). This is a Bayes lower;
whole-context expected counts cannot be substituted for actual counts
in an individual world.

## Native feasible upper bound

Choose minimizing branches/partition. In a paired branch choose a
deterministic h-subset of the larger known truth union and match the
two h-subsets; unused original certificates may remain mixed into the
residual. In every original world the residual has exactly F false
atoms and the stated invariant mass. For h=r use arbitrary cross-
context outside unit pairings. Whole-context objects are the actual
entire contexts. Identified A residuals are observable.

Assign each native pool uniform score p_S/m_S. Assign peeled safe
truths their corresponding paired/source scores, known false atoms
zero. This defines a normalized generator exactly source-calibrated
in every compatible world. Move c total probability uniformly from
a cell maximizing POSTERIOR rho to the known fixed S context.
Every positive native pool has source mass>=Delta>c; fixed S has
available capacity>c since its source mass is1/N and c<1/(2NrK).
The nominal bin source/generator mass vectors have TV<=c in every
world. Actual equal-score mergers only contract this TV. Bayes loss
is exactly the objective in(1). If there are no native objects the
entire source is known and zero false mass is attainable.

There are finitely many branch/partition choices, so a minimizer exists.
The upper and lower establish(A).

## Global minimax: symmetrize policies, not generators

The finite group of sibling swaps and within-context atom permutations
acts transitively on source worlds, preserves the sampling/certificate
experiment and preserves robust feasible-generator sets and loss.
Starting with a conditional Bayes minimizing policy, sample a uniform
group element, transform the data, run the policy, then invert the
transformation on its realized generator. This is a MIXTURE OF POLICIES:
each realization remains pathwise robust. It is not an average of
generator probability vectors, which could change score bins.

The randomized policy has the same risk in every fixed world, equal
to its uniform-prior Bayes risk E beta_c. Conversely every minimax risk
is at least uniform-prior Bayes risk, and(A) supplies its exact value.
This proves(B). The scalar beta is group-invariant, so its expectation
in any one fixed world equals its uniform-prior expectation; this does
not assert pointwise world-loss equality before policy symmetrization.
This uses standard finite-group minimax methodology already in C021.

## Exact evaluation and scope

For each branch assignment, C025's marked-cell multiset DP computes
the exact partition value using rational posterior false counts.
There are at most2^d branch assignments and at most d*max(F,2) native
objects. Finite exact evaluation is possible but may be exponential in
d or K. At each FIXED d,K it takes polynomial time in the explicit
sample length/bit size; this is not efficient estimation for growing d.

Let P_m(j|u)=binom(m-ell,j-ell)/m^u times
sum_{t=0}^{j-ell}(-1)^t binom(j-ell,t)(j-t)^u,
with P=0 outside ell<=j<=m. In a pinned actual world put A on the left
of every pair. For all variable-context counts u_1,...,u_2d and
w=n-sum u>=0, their multinomial coefficient is

 n! (N-2d)^w/[w! product_x u_x! N^n].

Multiply by product_i P_r(j_Ai|u_Ai)P_K(j_Si|u_Si), then by beta_c
from the resulting observable counts/unions, and sum. This is(2)
without an independence assumption on context counts. Oracle expectations
are computed the same way from C025's supplied-partition formula.
Their difference is the exact model-specific learning penalty.

## Checks, correction and unresolved issues

Logs:
* posterior_branch_single_check.json:3006 C021 reductions,2270 below half.
* posterior_branch_atomic_check.json:20 independent full-labeled-world
  invariant-atom DP games,262 worlds,2044 cells,20056 transitions.
  At positive c the free-recipient lower excludes zero-source donors.
* posterior_branch_rigidity_check.json:80784 unsaturated and121472
  coprime saturated signatures.3008 genuine noncoprime invariant
  signatures violate the classification, a positive scope control.
* posterior_branch_global_check.json:702 native optimizations and1245
  full joint occupancy outcomes, normalized for n0..6 in N5,K3,r2,d2,
  ell0. At n6 the formula yields6216787/50625000 at c0, and
  54951287/455625000 at c1/120. These evaluations rely on the analytic
  reduction above, not an independent global-optimality certificate.

The first atomic checker incorrectly used a zero-source pure-false
cell as a donor. Its failed run is retained. The corrected checker
disallows such donors and passes; no theorem was promoted from the
incorrect run. All arithmetic is integer/Fraction.

This theorem candidate depends on the earlier C019 support-forgetting
and C022 removal lemmas, themselves unaudited. Review must particularly
check their use with the ORIGINAL posterior, the consistent whole-
context branch classification and conditional-to-global symmetry.
No Lean certificate, priority verification or independent audit exists.
Larger budgets, noncoprime saturation and a uniformly efficient
growing-VC estimator remain open. No complete Target1 or row solution
is claimed.

The atomic suite additionally constructs the generator on physical atoms:
262 actual source-world exact-score calibration checks pass, and each
game's posterior-weighted raw false mass matches beta. Native source

generator is scored. The global occupancy suite uses the native solver

[Theorem 35 of arXiv:2605.02002, 'Glauber dynamics for random field Ising models on bounded degree graphs and MLSI'] For any $\epsilon>0$, $\beta>0$ and $C_\alpha>0$, there exist constants $K_0>0$, $\kappa_0$ and $\epsilon_0>0$ (depending only on $\epsilon,\beta,C_\alpha$) such that the following holds. Let $G=(V,E)$ be a graph of maximal degree $\Delta\leq\exp(C_\alpha)$, and $\mu_G$ be the RFIM on $G$ with external field $h$ where $(|h_u|)_{u\in V}$ are i.i.d. satisfying $\mathbb{P}(|h_x|\leq K_0)\leq\epsilon_0$. Then for each $L\geq\kappa_0\ln|V|$, 
$$
\mathbf{gap}_G^{-1}\leq|V|\cdot\exp( {\epsilon} L)
$$with $\mathbb{P}_h$- probability at least $1-e^{-2L}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[campaign result 2026-09-14, author checked] This is a proved finite special case of Afonso S. Bandeira's Open Problem 11, How many deviations are needed afterall?, in Did just a couple of deviations suffice all along? (problems 10-14), Randomstrasse 101 (19 December 2024; https://randomstrasse101.math.ethz.ch/posts/HowManyDeviations/). For an n-by-n matrix A with entries in {+1,-1}, define disc(A)=min_{x in {+1,-1}^n} ||Ax||_infinity, where ||y||_infinity=max_i |y_i|, and let D_n=max_{A in {+1,-1}^{n-by-n}} disc(A). One has D_6=4. An attaining matrix is specified by its six rows --++++; +--+++; +++-++; +-++-+; -+-+-+; -----+, with each character + interpreted as +1 and each - as -1. Its discrepancy is four, yielding normalized discrepancy 4/sqrt(6). The exhaustive witness check and the next-level counting obstruction are the proof methods recorded in the memo. This is an unrefereed campaign result.
All entries are signs; discrepancy uses all sign colourings.

[Corollary 15 of arXiv:2606.09904, 'Non-explosion principles for branched rough differential equations with unbounded coeffici'] For any \(f \in \CF_{N - 1}\), we have that
  \[R^{\phi(\mathbf{Y}), f}_{st} = \delta(\partial^f_X \phi(\mathbf{Y}))_{st} -
    \sum_{k = 1}^{N - |f| - 1} \frac{1}{k!}D^k[\partial^f_X \phi(\mathbf{Y}_s)]
    \left[(\delta Y_{st})^{\otimes k}\right]
    - R^{\sharp, f}_{st}\]
  where \(R^{\sharp, f}_{st}\) has regularity \(\ge N\gamma\).
  More precisely,
  \begin{equation}
    R^{\sharp, f}_{st} =
    \sum_{k = 1}^{N - |f| - 1} \sum_{\substack{m_1 + m_2 + m_3 = k\\ m_1 \neq k}}
    \frac{(-1)^{m_2 + m_3}}{k!}\binom{k}{m_1, m_2, m_3} D^k[\partial^f_X \phi(\mathbf{Y}_s)][A_{st}^{m_1, m_2, m_3}],
  \end{equation}
  for which the \(m_1, m_2\) and \(m_3\) are summed over the non-negative integers and
  \begin{equation}
    A_{st}^{m_1, m_2, m_3} :=
    (\delta Y_{st})^{\otimes m_1} \otimes (R^{\mathbf{Y}, \mathbf{1}}_{st})^{\otimes m_2} \otimes
    \left(\sum_{\tau \in \CT_{N - 1} \setminus \CT_{N - k}} \partial^\tau_X Y_s \<\mathbf{X}_{st}, \tau\>\right)^{\otimes m_3}.
  \end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition 5 (Reflected viscosity solution) of arXiv:2606.17517, 'Killed resolvents and measure-valued stopping gains for reflected optimal stopping with ma'] Let $u:\R^2_+\to\R$ be continuous and of polynomial growth.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[\textup{(i)}]
$u$ is a \emph{reflected viscosity subsolution} of
\eqref{eq:obstacle-max}--\eqref{eq:neumann-condition} if, whenever
$\varphi\in C^2(\R^2_+)$ and $u-\varphi$ has a local maximum at $x\in\R^2_+$,
with $u(x)=\varphi(x)$, the following hold. If $x\in\interior{\R}^2_+$, then
\[
   \max\{(\mathcal L-r)\varphi(x)-c(x),\;G(x)-u(x)\}\le0.
\]
If $x_i=0$ for some $i\in\{1,2\}$, then
\[
   \min\left\{
      \max\{(\mathcal L-r)\varphi(x)-c(x),\;G(x)-u(x)\},
      \partial_i\varphi(x)
   \right\}\le0.
\]
\item[\textup{(ii)}]
$u$ is a \emph{reflected viscosity supersolution} if, whenever
$\varphi\in C^2(\R^2_+)$ and $u-\varphi$ has a local minimum at $x\in\R^2_+$,
with $u(x)=\varphi(x)$, the following hold. If $x\in\interior{\R}^2_+$, then
\[
   \max\{(\mathcal L-r)\varphi(x)-c(x),\;G(x)-u(x)\}\ge0.
\]
If $x_i=0$ for some $i\in\{1,2\}$, then
\[
   \max\left\{
      \max\{(\mathcal L-r)\varphi(x)-c(x),\;G(x)-u(x)\},
      \partial_i\varphi(x)
   \right\}\ge0.
\]
\item[\textup{(iii)}]
$u$ is a \emph{reflected viscosity solution} if it is both a reflected
viscosity subsolution and a reflected viscosity supersolution.
\end{enumerate}
title: Reflected viscosity solution

\]

body:
[Theorem thm:odd_level_products of arXiv:2411.13707, 'High-degree cubature on Wiener space \\ through unshuffle expansions'] Let $m_i \geq 1$ and $x_i \in V^{\otimes m_i}$ be palindromes for $i = 1,\ldots,n$. Let $k \geq 1$ with $k \not \equiv \sum_{i = 1}^n m_i \pmod 2$. Then
\[
\mathrm{e}^{\star k}((x_1,\ldots,x_n)) = 0 .
\]
\begin{proof}
By symmetry and the fact that each $x_i$ is a palindrome,
\begin{align*}
(x_1,\ldots,x_n) &= \frac{1}{2 \cdot n!}\sum_{\sigma \in \mathfrak S_n} \big[ x_{\sigma(1)} \ldots x_{\sigma(n)} + x_{\sigma(n)} \ldots x_{\sigma(1)} \big] \\
&= \frac{1}{2 \cdot n!}\sum_{\sigma \in \mathfrak S_n} \big[ x_{\sigma(1)} \ldots x_{\sigma(n)} + (x_{\sigma(1)} \ldots x_{\sigma(n)})^* \big] .
\end{align*}
For $y \in T(V)$ and $f \in \mathrm{End}(T(V))$, using Sweedler notation for the convolution power of $f$ (equation eq:star of the paper) and the fact that reversal is a coalgebra morphism (lem:reversal of the paper), we can write
\[
f^{\star k}(y^*) = (f((y^*)_{(1)}), \ldots, f((y^*)_{(k)})) = (f((y_{(1)})^*), \ldots, f((y_{(k)})^*)) .
\]
Let $y = (x_1,\ldots,x_n)$ and $m = \sum_{i = 1}^n m_i$. Combining the above two identities and applying the reversal property (prop:reversal of the paper) concludes the proof:
\begin{align*}
    \mathrm{e}^{\star k}(y + y^*) &= (\mathrm{e}(y_{(1)}), \ldots, \mathrm{e}(y_{(k)})) + (\mathrm{e}((y_{(1)})^*), \ldots, \mathrm{e}((y_{(k)})^*)) \\
    &= (1 + (-1)^{m - k})\mathrm{e}^{\star k}(y)\\ &= 0 . \qedhere
\end{align*}
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition 4 (Mean-one two-point distribution) of arXiv:2608.18392, 'On Samuels' Conjecture'] For $0\leq x<1<y$, define the two-point distribution with mean one
\begin{equation}
Q_{x,y} := \frac{y-1}{y-x}\delta_x + \frac{1-x}{y-x}\delta_y.

\end{equation}
To include degenerate distributions, let
$$
\Theta := \{(1,1)\} \sqcup \left\{ (x,y):0\leq x<1<y<\infty \right\},
$$
and set $Q_{1,1}:=\delta_1$.
title: Mean-one two-point distribution

[Theorem 42 of arXiv:2609.00567, 'Hodge--Tate splitting and Akizuki--Nakano vanishing in positive characteristic'] Let $k$ be a perfect field and $X$ a qcqs $k$-scheme.
We assume that $X$ is quasi-$F$-split.
Then $X$ is HT-split.
Furthermore, if $X$ is smooth over $k$ and $D$ is a simple normal crossings divisor on $X$, then $(X,D)$ is log HT-split.

[Thm t:FinMA of arXiv:2605.08983, 'A functional limit theorem for self-normalized linear processes with random coefficients a'] Let $(Z_{i})_{i \in \mathbb{Z}}$ be an i.i.d.~sequence of regularly varying random variables satisfying $((e:regvar of the paper))$ and $((eq:pq of the paper))$ with $\alpha \in (0,2)$. Assume conditions $((e:oceknula of the paper))$ and $((e:sim of the paper))$ hold. Let
 $C_{0}, \ldots, C_{q}$ be random variables, independent of $(Z_{i})$, such that condition $((eq:FiniteMAcond of the paper))$ holds.
Then, as $n \to \infty$,
\begin{equation*}
L_{n}(\,\cdot\,) \xrightarrow{d}  (C^{(1)}V(\,\cdot\,), C^{(2)}W(\,\cdot\,))
\end{equation*}
 in $D^{2}$ with the weak $M_{2}$ topology,
where $V$ is an $\alpha$--stable L\'{e}vy process with characteristic triple $(0, \mu, b)$, with $\mu$ as in $((eq:mu of the paper))$,
$$ b = \left\{ \begin{array}{cc}
                                   0, & \quad \alpha = 1,\\[0.4em]
                                   (p-r)\frac{\alpha}{1-\alpha}, & \quad \alpha \in (0,1) \cup (1,2),
                                 \end{array}\right.$$
with $p$ and $r$ defined in $((eq:pq of the paper))$, $W$ is an $\alpha/2$--stable L\'{e}vy process with characteristic triple $(0, \widetilde{\mu}, \alpha/(2-\alpha))$ with $\widetilde{\mu}(\mathrm{d} x) = (\alpha /2) x^{-\alpha/2-1} 1_{(0,\infty)}(x)\,\mathrm{d} x$,
and $(C^{(1)}, C^{(2)})$ is a random vector, independent of $(V, W)$, such that
$(C^{(1)}, C^{(2)}) \stackrel{d}{=} (C, C^{S})$.
title: Thm t:FinMA of arXiv:2605.08983

[Proposition prop-decomposition of a martingale of arXiv:2505.24043, 'Weak solutions of Navier-Stokes Equation with purely discontinuous L\'evy Noise'] Every $\mathbb{R}$-valued local martingale $M$ can be uniquely, up to indistinguishability,   represented as a sum of a continuous local martingale $M^c$ and purely discontinuous local martingale $M^d$, i.e. 
\[
M=M^c+M^d.
\]
The  continuous part $X^c$ of a semimartingale $X$   is defined as the continuous part of the martingale part of $X$, see [Jacod_Shiryaev]. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: [Definition Cad1df of arXiv:2411.16647, 'The stochastic evolution of an infinite population with logistic-type interaction'] A family of probability measures $\{P_{s,\mu}: s\geq 0, \mu\in \mathcal{P}_{\rm exp}\}$ is said to be a solution of the restricted martingale problem if, for all $s\geq 0$ and $\mu\in \mathcal{P}_{\rm exp}$, the following is true: (a) $P_{s,\mu} \circ \varpi^{-1}_s = \mu$; (b)  $P_{s,\mu} \circ \varpi^{-1}_u \in \mathcal{P}_{\rm exp}$ for all $u >s$; (c) for all $t>s$, the types $\varkappa_u$  of $P_{s,\mu} \circ \varpi^{-1}_u$ satisfy $\sup_{u\in [s, t]} \varkappa_u < \infty$; (d) $P_{s,\mu} ({\sf H}) =0$, which holds for $\sf H$ as in (equation Cad1 of the paper) with each $F\in \widetilde{\mathcal{F}}$ and every bounded function  ${\sf J}: \mathfrak{D}_{[s,+\infty)}(\Gamma_*) \to \mathds{R}$, which is $\mathfrak{F}_{s,t_1}$-measurable, $t_1>s$, see (equation Cad of the paper). The restricted martingale problem is said to be well-posed if it has a unique solution in the following sense:  if $\{P_{s,\mu}: s\geq 0, \mu\in \mathcal{P}_{\rm exp}\}$ and $\{P'_{s,\mu}: s\geq 0, \mu\in \mathcal{P}_{\rm exp}\}$ solve the problem, then all finite dimensional marginals of $P_{s,\mu}$ and $P'_{s,\mu}$ coincide for all $s$ and $\mu$, see [EK].

[Lemma 45 (Gaussian weighted translation and shifted-tail estimates) of arXiv:2608.07820, 'Linear Spectral Statistics for Entrywise-Transformed Spiked Wigner Matrices under Shifted '] Let \(\nu=\gamma\) be standard Gaussian measure.  If, for some \(\epsilon>0\),
\[
        f\in L^{4+\epsilon}(\gamma),
        \qquad \E f(\xi)=0,
        \qquad \E f(\xi)^2=1,
\]
put $L_s(\xi)=\exp(s\xi-s^2/2)$.  Then
\begin{align}
 \E\!\left[|f(\xi)|\,|L_s(\xi)-1-s\xi|\right]
 &=o(|s|),\\
 \E\!\left[|f(\xi)|^2
 \left|L_s(\xi)-1-s\xi-\frac{s^2}{2}(\xi^2-1)\right|\right]
 &=o(s^2).
\end{align}
Moreover, for every fixed $s_0>0$,
\begin{equation}
 \lim_{R\to\infty}\sup_{|s|\le s_0}
 \E\!\left[|f(\xi+s)|^4
 \one_{\{|f(\xi+s)|>R\}}\right]=0.
\end{equation}
Consequently Proposition~\ref{prop:likelihood-W} applies with
$\ell_1(\xi)=\xi$ and $\ell_2(\xi)=\xi^2-1$.

[Theorem Wick formula of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] Given independent variables $f_i$, each following the complex normal law $G_t$, with $t>0$ being a fixed parameter, we have the formula
$$E\left(f_{i_1}^{k_1}\ldots f_{i_s}^{k_s}\right)=t^{s/2}\#\left\{\pi\in\mathcal P_2(k)\Big|\pi\leq\ker i\right\}$$
where $k=k_1\ldots k_s$ and $i=i_1\ldots i_s$, for the joint moments of these variables, where $\pi\leq\ker i$ means that the indices of $i$ must fit into the blocks of $\pi$, in the obvious way.

Let  $(g_i)_{i=1}^\infty$ be an increasing sequence of continuous functions with $g_i\to g$ pointwise and $g_i|_{\mathbb{R}^n \setminus B(0,R)}\equiv \LIP[f]$ for all $i\in \mathbb{N}$. 		\[
		\Lip_a[f_i]\leq g_i(x),
		\]
		for all $i\in \mathbb{N}$ and for all $x \in \mathbb{R}^n$.

body: [Lemma 10 of arXiv:2609.04139, 'The conformally invariant metric on CLE$_4$ II:\\ existence of geodesics'] Let $z_1, z_2, z_3, z_4$ be points on $\partial\BD$ ordered counterclockwise. Let $\{\eta_{12}, \eta_{34}\}$ be a bichordal SLE$_4$ in $\BD$ with link pattern $\{\{z_1, z_2\}, \{z_3, z_4\}\}$. Then, there exists a universal constant $C \in (0,\infty)$ such that the following holds for all $\varepsilon \in (0,1)$. The probability that both $\eta_{12}$ and $\eta_{34}$ intersect $B_\varepsilon(0)$ is at most $C \varepsilon^2$. More generally, let $U \subsetneq \BC$ be a simply connected domain and let $z_1, z_2, z_3, z_4$ be prime ends of $U$ whose corresponding points of $\partial\BD$ are ordered counterclockwise. Let $\{\eta_{12}, \eta_{34}\}$ be a bichordal SLE$_4$ in $U$ with link pattern $\{\{z_1, z_2\}, \{z_3, z_4\}\}$. Then, there exists a universal constant $C \in (0,\infty)$ such that the following holds. Let $z \in U$ and $0 < \varepsilon < r < \dist(z, \partial U)$. The probability that both $\eta_{12}$ and $\eta_{34}$ intersect $B_\varepsilon(z)$ is at most $C (\varepsilon/r)^2$.

body:
Chacon's transformation is the invertible, rank-one, measure-preserving transformation T of a Lebesgue probability space produced by the following cutting-and-stacking construction. Start with the column C_0 consisting of the single interval [0,1), of height h_0 = 1. Given the column C_n, a stack of h_n disjoint intervals ('levels') of equal width w_n, cut it vertically into three subcolumns of equal width w_n/3, place one new 'spacer' interval of width w_n/3, taken from the not-yet-used part of the line, on top of the MIDDLE subcolumn, and stack the three pieces in order: subcolumn 1 at the bottom, then subcolumn 2 with its spacer on top of it, then subcolumn 3. The result is the column C_{n+1} of height h_{n+1} = 3 h_n + 1. The map T sends each point of a level to the point directly above it in the current column; the columns exhaust the space in the limit, T is defined almost everywhere, is invertible, and preserves Lebesgue measure normalised to a probability measure. The same system appears symbolically as the subshift generated by the blocks B_0 = 0, B_{n+1} = B_n B_n 1 B_n, whose lengths satisfy the same recursion. STANDARD FACTS about this system: it is ergodic; it has rank one, hence simple spectrum and ZERO entropy; it is WEAKLY MIXING but NOT strongly mixing; del Junco, Rahe and Swanson proved that it has minimal self-joinings, from which it follows that it is prime (its only factors are the trivial ones) and that its centraliser consists of the powers of T alone. WHY MIXING FAILS, in one line one can check: let I be a level of C_n and let I_1, I_2, I_3 be the three pieces into which the cut splits I inside C_{n+1}, each of measure mu(I)/3. By construction T^{h_n} carries I_1 onto I_2, and I_2 is a subset of I; hence I_1 is contained in I ∩ T^{-h_n} I, so mu(I ∩ T^{-h_n} I) >= (1/3) mu(I). The same argument applied at every later stage m >= n gives mu(A ∩ T^{-h_m} A) >= (1/3) mu(A) for every A which is a union of levels of C_n and every m >= n. Mixing would force these correlations to converge to mu(A)^2, which is smaller than (1/3) mu(A) as soon as mu(A) < 1/3. SHARP EDGES. (a) This is THE standard witness that weak mixing does not imply strong mixing; do not use it as an example of a mixing system, and do not expect quantitative decay of correlations from it - along the tower heights h_n the correlations do not decay at all. (b) Its zero entropy and simple spectrum show that weak mixing carries no entropy or spectral-multiplicity information whatsoever. (c) Rank one and minimal self-joinings are properties of this specific construction, not of cutting-and-stacking systems in general; changing the number of cuts or the spacer pattern changes the mixing behaviour (some cutting-and-stacking constructions are mixing).
the underlying space is a Lebesgue probability space (the unit interval with Lebesgue measure, after normalisation)
the construction uses three cuts and exactly one spacer above the middle subcolumn at every stage, with h_0 = 1 and h_{n+1} = 3h_n + 1
T is the induced a.e.-defined invertible measure-preserving map
title: Chacon's transformation

body:
[Lemma 12 of arXiv:2608.30178, '2608.30178'] For \(i=1,2\), let \(G_i\) be the geometric factor defined in
\eqref{eq:G2}.  Then
\(G_{i,t}>0\) for every \(t\ge0\), and
\begin{equation}
 \log G_{i,t}
 =-b_it+\sqrt{2b_{i1}}B_i(t)
 +\int_0^t\int_0^\infty
 \log(1+v)\,\widetilde M_i(\dd s,\dd v),
 
\end{equation}
where \(b_i:=b_{i0}+b_{i1}+b_{i2}\). Consequently, \(\E|\log G_{i,t}|<\infty\) and
\[
 \lim_{t\to\infty}\frac1t\log G_{i,t}=-b_i
 \qquad\text{almost surely}.
\]
If \(b_i>0\), then, for every \(q>0\),
\(\int_0^\infty G_{i,t}^q\dd t<\infty\) almost surely.

	and $\vi_n \to \vi$ in $\boldsymbol{L}^2(\R^d)$ as $n\to \infty$.

	Then $\rho_n \to \rho$ in $L^\infty(0,T; L^2(\R^d))$ as $n\to \infty$, where $\rho$ is the solution of \eqref{CE} with $\rho|_0 = \theta$.

ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Constant-factor online scheduling with subadditive batch durations structural calculation Result: Greedy batching can be arbitrarily poor for a fixed two-job queue when holding costs differ. Let S(a)=1,S(b)=L,S({a,b})=L+epsilon with0<epsilon<1 and L>1. Give a holding rate M and b rate1. Processing both immediately costs(M+1)*(L+epsilon). Processing a first and then b costs M+1+L. For M much larger than L their ratio approaches L+epsilon, although service times are strictly monotone and subadditive. Check: The individual completion times are L+epsilon for both in the batch, and1,L+1 in the sequential schedule. This compares exactly the same initial jobs without incoming work. For the actual stationary model, Campbell reasoning also gives the elementary lower bound W_*>=integral c(a)*S({a}) da, since each task must spend at least its singleton service time in its completing batch. Obstruction: Embedding the bad queue event in a stable Poisson-arrival system while controlling its frequency and other waiting costs remains necessary. The two-job calculation does not disprove existence of a different constant-factor algorithm.

[Proposition of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] Given an index set $I$, which can be finite or not, the space of square-summable vectors having indices in $I$, namely
$$l^2(I)=\left\{(x_i)_{i\in I}\Big|\sum_i|x_i|^2<\infty\right\}$$
is a Hilbert space, with scalar product as follows:
$$<x,y>=\sum_ix_i\bar{y}_i$$
When $I$ is finite, $I=\{1,\ldots,N\}$, we obtain in this way the usual space $H=\mathbb C^N$.

[Proposition prop:ehr-kraw of arXiv:2608.01253, 'The pseudo-quantum representation of \\finite reversible Markov chains'] Let $u_m$, $m=-\tfrac n2,\dots,\tfrac n2$, be the orthonormal eigenvectors of
$A_{\mathrm{sym}}$ with eigenvalue $2m/n$. Then the following hold.
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=1.7em,itemsep=2pt,topsep=2pt]
\item $u_m$ is the $J_x$ eigenvector of eigenvalue $m$. In the $J_z$ basis its
entries are, up to a column phase, the entries of the spin-$\tfrac n2$ rotation by
$\tfrac\pi2$ about the $y$ axis,

\[
u_m(k)=\langle k-\tfrac n2\rvert\,e^{-i\tfrac\pi2 J_y}\,\lvert m\rangle,
\]

the Wigner rotation matrix at $\tfrac\pi2$, which is real.
\item The rescaled entries $\mathrm K_m(k):=u_m(k)/\sqrt{\nu_k}$ are polynomials of
degree $\tfrac n2-m$ in $k$, the (normalised, symmetric) Krawtchouk polynomials,
orthogonal with respect to the binomial weight $\nu$,
$\sum_k\nu_k\,\mathrm K_m(k)\mathrm K_{m'}(k)=\delta_{mm'}$.
\item The semigroup has the exact spectral (Karlin--McGregor) form

\begin{equation}
\bigl(e^{tQ}\bigr)_{kl}
=\frac{\sqrt{\nu_l}}{\sqrt{\nu_k}}\sum_{m=-n/2}^{n/2}
e^{(2m-n)t}\,u_m(k)\,u_m(l)
=\nu_l\sum_{m}e^{(2m-n)t}\,\mathrm K_m(k)\,\mathrm K_m(l).

\end{equation}
\end{enumerate}

		\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Own-work research draft; status proof (unaudited), independent review pending. For F(u,v)=(u,v,u^2+v^2), the uniform-square pushforward has optimal N-segment continuous scalar-input generator W1 error E_N between (1/2)*(338*N)^(-2/3) and 13*N^(-2/3), for every integer N>=1. Thus the flat square's matching O(N^-1) upper rate does not extend to all bi-Lipschitz cube images. Assumptions: Fixed smooth (1,3)-bi-Lipschitz chart F:[0,1]^2 -> R3; target density w.r.t. surface area lies in [1/3,1]; uniform 1D latent; continuous piecewise affine generators with at most N pieces; Euclidean W1; no uniform slope, weight-magnitude, or precision restriction. The lower bound uses a uniform line-tube mass bound 169*r^(3/2), split by line orientation. The upper bound uses n^2 polygonal rows, n chords per row, and n^2-1 connectors with positive allotted times, totaling at most 2*n^3 pieces and error at most 2/n^2. Curvature prevents transferring the flat cube's matching upper rate through a general nonlinear bi-Lipschitz chart. No priority claim or unrestricted deep-rate solution is asserted.

body: Lemma (campaign status: audited-pass): Target-uniform two-point atom bound: with u active variables (all coefficients nonzero), the probability of hitting either of two prescribed targets is at most psi(u) = min(3/4, 2^(1-u)*binom(u, floor(u/2))) ≤ min(3/4, 2/sqrt(u)). For u = 2 the 3/4 estimate is the nondegenerate parallelogram bound; for u ≥ 3 it is twice the central-binomial one-point mass. Over Fp the correct statement is NOT merely 'no wrap': invoke the finite-group one-point Littlewood-Offord theorem when u < p and all active coefficients are nonzero, then take a union bound over the two targets. Notes: Extraction '21-u (u over floor u/2)' reconstructed as 2^(1-u)*binom(u,floor(u/2)); '2 sqrt-u' as 2/sqrt(u). Independent audit harness exhaustively checked coefficient multisets u = 2..8, primes ≤ 13 with p > u (p.37: FINITE_FIELD_LO PASS coefficient_multisets=4370).

Let {X_i : i in I} be an arbitrary family of compact topological spaces. Then the product space (the Cartesian product of the X_i with the product topology, whose subbasic open sets are the preimages of open sets under the coordinate projections) is compact. The general statement (arbitrary index sets, arbitrary compact factors) is equivalent to the axiom of choice over ZF.
each X_i is a compact topological space
the product carries the product topology
the axiom of choice

(2) Let U be an ultrafilter on the product X of the family. For each coordinate i, the pushforward of U under the projection p_i is an ultrafilter on X_i, so by compactness of X_i it converges to some point x_i (choosing one limit for each i uses the axiom of choice). (3) Let x be the point of X with coordinates x_i. body:
For probability measures P and Q on one space, TV(P, Q) = sup_A |P(A) - Q(A)| and D = D(P || Q) is the Kullback-Leibler divergence in nats (+infinity unless P << Q). For every event A, P(A^c) + Q(A) >= 1 - TV(P, Q), with equality for A = {p >= q}. So the smallest average error of a test between P and Q under equal priors is R* = (1 - TV)/2, and by the Bretagnolle-Huber inequality R* >= (1 - sqrt(1 - exp(-D)))/2 >= (1/4) exp(-D).
P and Q are probability measures on one measurable space

body: [Lemma 1 (separation) of arXiv:2606.08581, '2606.08581'] Before stabilization, let \(x\neq y\) be two vertices and put \(m=\min\{\eta(x),\eta(y)\}\). If \(m>1\), then the two vertices split the cycle into two arcs, one of which contains a hole, while the other has no vertex of height less than \(m-1\).

[Proposition prop:randomcluster-loop of arXiv:2506.10765, 'A General Coupling for Ising Models and Beyond'] Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite connected graph. Let $\Omega:=\{0,1\}^E$ be the space of bond configurations. For $A\subset V$ with $|A|$ even, let $\Sigma:=\{F\subset E: \partial F=A\}$ be the set of subgraphs of $G$ with sources $A$. Let $f:\Omega\to 2^{\Sigma}$ be defined by $f(\omega)=\{F\subset \omega: \partial F=A\}$. Let
	\[\rho[\omega]\propto 1\! \!1[\omega\in\mathcal{F}_A] \mathbb{P}_t[\omega],~\forall \omega\in \Omega, ~\gamma[\eta]\propto 1, ~\forall \eta\in \Sigma.\]
	Then, under the coupling measure $\mathscr{P}$ defined in Theorem (thm:generalcoupling of the paper), 
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item[(a)] The marginal of $\mathscr{P}$ on $\Sigma$ is $\ell^{A}$. For each $\omega\in\Omega$ with $\omega\in\mathcal{F}_A$, the conditional measure $\mathscr{P}[\;\cdot \mid \omega] = \mathtt{UG}^A[\omega] $  on $\Sigma$ is the uniform subgraph on $f(\omega)$.
		\item[(b)] The marginal of $\mathscr{P}$ on $\Omega$ is $\phi_p[\;\cdot \mid \mathcal{F}_A]$.  For each $\eta\in\Sigma$ with $\partial \eta=A$, the conditional measure $\mathscr{P}[\;\cdot \mid \eta]  = (\mathbb{P}_t \cup \delta_{\eta})[\cdot]$, that is,  $\eta$ sprinkled with Bernoulli percolation with parameters $t=(t_e)_{e\in E}$. 
	\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

where the operator $A$ is defined in \eqref{e:opA}.

body:
[Theorem thm:variable-range-eb of arXiv:2608.25551, 'Beyond Optimal Rates in Stochastic Optimization: Trajectory-Adaptive Stopping Rules'] Fix a deterministic integer $t_0 \ge 1$. Let $\{\mathcal{F}_t\}_{t \ge t_0-1}$ be a filtration. Let $\{H_t\}_{t \ge t_0}$ be a real-valued integrable adapted process, and let $\{c_t\}_{t \ge t_0}$ be an almost surely finite,\footnote{No uniform upper bound on the process $\{c_t\}_{t \ge t_0}$ is assumed.} nonnegative predictable process such that
\[
    |H_t|
    \le
    c_t
    \qquad
    \text{almost surely for every } t \ge t_0.
\]
Define
\[
    \overline H_{t_0-1}
    \coloneqq
    0,
    \qquad
    \overline H_t
    \coloneqq
    \sum_{s = t_0}^t
    \left(
        H_s - \mathbb{E}[H_s \mid \mathcal{F}_{s-1}]
    \right),
\]
and
\[
    W_{t_0-1}
    \coloneqq
    0,
    \qquad
    W_t
    \coloneqq
    \sum_{s = t_0}^t H_s^2,
    \qquad
    C_t
    \coloneqq
    \max_{t_0 \le s \le t} c_s,
    \qquad
    t \ge t_0.
\]
Then, for every $\alpha \in (0,1)$,
\begin{equation}

    \mathbb{P}\left(
        \forall t \ge t_0:\
        \overline H_t
        \le
        \mathfrak B_\alpha(W_t, C_t)
    \right)
    \ge
    1-\alpha.
\end{equation}
Moreover, the map $(v, b) \mapsto \mathfrak B_\alpha(v, b)$ is nondecreasing in each argument. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Empirical Bernstein bound with a growing predictable range

[Lemma l.law_dalpha of arXiv:2411.14105, 'Simultaneous replica-symmetry breaking \\ for vector spin glasses'] The law of $\alpha^{-1}(U)$ is $\mathrm{d}\alpha$, where $U$ is a uniform random variable over $[0,1]$. Consequently, for every bounded measurable $h:[0,T]\to \mathbb{R}$, we have that $\int_0^1 h\circ\alpha^{-1}(s)\mathrm{d} s = \int_0^T h(t)\mathrm{d}\alpha(t)$. Moreover, $\supp \mathrm{d}\alpha = \overline{\alpha^{-1}((0,1])}$ and
\begin{align}
    \alpha^{-1}\circ\alpha(t+) = t,\quad \forall t \in \{0\}\cup \supp\mathrm{d} \alpha.
\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Proposition 6 (Compatibility with separable tensor products) of arXiv:2608.30589, 'Vector-Valued Wavelet Bases as Hilbert $\mathbb{M}_m(\mathbb{R})$-Module Bases: A Construc'] Let $d_1,d_2\ge 1$ and $m\ge 1$.
Let $f,r\in L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_1},\mathbb{R}^m)$ and $g,u\in L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_2},\mathbb{R}^m)$.
Define $h,k\in L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_1+d_2},\mathbb{R}^m)$ by
\[
h(x,y):= f(x)\odot g(y),\qquad
k(x,y):= r(x)\odot u(y),
\]
where $\odot$ denotes the componentwise product: $(a\odot b)_i:=a_i b_i$.
This compatibility will be used later in our separable construction of multivariate vector-valued wavelets.
Then

\[
\langle h,k\rangle_{\mathbb{M}_m(\mathbb{R})}
=
\langle f,r\rangle_{\mathbb{M}_m(\mathbb{R})}\ \odot\ \langle g,u\rangle_{\mathbb{M}_m(\mathbb{R})},
\]
where on the right-hand side $\odot$ denotes the Hadamard (entrywise) product of matrices:
$(A\odot B)_{ij}:=A_{ij}B_{ij}$.
title: Compatibility with separable tensor products

body:
[Definition 1 of arXiv:2512.04807, 'Existence and uniqueness of the canonical Brownian motion in non-simple conformal loop ens'] Suppose that we have the setup described just above. We say that a resistance form $(\rform{\cdot}{\cdot}{\Gamma}, \rfdomain{\Gamma})$ on $\Upsilon_\Gamma$ is a \clekp{} resistance form if the following holds. For each $V \in \metregions$, there exists a resistance form $(\rformres{V}{\cdot}{\cdot}{\Gamma}, \rfdomainres{V}{\Gamma})$ on $\ol{V} \cap \Upsilon_\Gamma$  such that the following properties are satisfied.
\begin{enumerate}[I.]
\item $(\rform{\cdot}{\cdot}{\Gamma}, \rfdomain{\Gamma})$ is a local, regular resistance form, and its associated resistance metric $\rmet{\cdot}{\cdot}{\Gamma}$ is topologically equivalent to $\dpathY$.
\item Let $V_1,\ldots,V_n \in \metregions$, $n \in \N$, such that $V_i \cap V_j = \emptyset$ for $i \neq j$ and $\bigcup_i \ol{V_i} \cap \Upsilon_\Gamma = \Upsilon_\Gamma$. Then
 \begin{align*}
  \rfdomain{\Gamma} &= \{ f : f|_{\ol{V_i} \cap \Upsilon_\Gamma} \in \rfdomainres{V_i}{\Gamma} \text{ for each } i \} ,\\
  \text{and}\quad
  \rform{f}{f}{\Gamma} &= \sum_i \rformres{V_i}{f|_{\ol{V_i} \cap \Upsilon_\Gamma}}{f|_{\ol{V_i} \cap \Upsilon_\Gamma}}{\Gamma} .
 \end{align*}
 See Figure~\ref{fi:cle_rf_locality}.
\item If $V,V' \in \metregions$, $V \subseteq V'$, and $f\colon \ol{V'} \cap \Upsilon_\Gamma \to \R$ is a continuous function that is constant on each $\dpathY$-connected component of $\ol{V'} \cap \Upsilon_\Gamma \setminus \ol{V}$, then
\begin{align*}
 & f \in \rfdomainres{V'}{\Gamma} \text{ if and only if } f|_{\ol{V} \cap \Upsilon_\Gamma} \in \rfdomainres{V}{\Gamma} \\
 \text{and}\quad & \rformres{V'}{f}{f}{\Gamma} = \rformres{V}{f}{f}{\Gamma} .
\end{align*}
\item For each open, simply connected $U \subseteq \C$, the collection $(\rformres{V}{\cdot}{\cdot}{\Gamma})_{V \in \metregions[U]}$ is a.s.\ determined by $(\Gamma_{U^*}, \dpathY[U])$.
\item Let $U \subseteq \C$ be open, simply connected, and $z \in \C$. Then
\[ (\rformres{V}{\cdot}{\cdot}{\Gamma_{U^*}})_{V \in \metregions[U]} = (\rformres{V+z}{T_{z}\cdot}{T_{z}\cdot}{\Gamma_{U^*}+z})_{V \in \metregions[U]} \quad\text{a.s.,} \]
where $T_{z} f = f(\cdot -z)$ denotes translation by $z$.
\item There exists a constant $\resexp > 0$ so that the following holds. Let $U \subseteq \C$ be open, simply connected, and $\lambda > 0$. Then
\[ (\rformres{V}{\cdot}{\cdot}{\Gamma_{U^*}})_{V \in \metregions[U]} = (\lambda^{\resexp}\rformres{\lambda V}{S_{\lambda}\cdot}{S_{\lambda}\cdot}{\lambda\Gamma_{U^*}})_{V \in \metregions[U]} \quad\text{a.s.,} \]
where $S_{\lambda} f = f(\lambda^{-1}\cdot)$.
\end{enumerate}

body: [Theorem thm-Mostow rigidity of arXiv:2609.00233, 'A survey on mapping class groups of 3-manifolds'] Let $M$ and $N$ be closed, orientable, hyperbolic $3$-manifolds. If $f \colon M \to N$ is a homotopy equivalence, then $f$ is homotopic to an isometry. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Mostow rigidity

body:
[Proposition 6 (Time-dependent family of maps $G_t$: tree contraction on small balls at large times) of arXiv:2608.14802, 'Dynamical Gibbs-non-Gibbs transitions for finite-alphabet models on trees'] Let $\lambda$ denote the spectral radius of $Df(l)$ and fix $\lambda_G\in (\lambda,1)$. For each $r>0$, set $U_r=U_r(l):=\{x\in\Delta^{q-1}:\|x-l\|_l<r\}$. Then there exists a radius $r_0=r_0(\lambda_G)>0$ such that, for every $r\in (0,r_0)$, there exists a time threshold $t_R=t_R(r,\lambda_G)\geq 0$ with the following properties: for every $t\geq t_R$ and every $k\in S$, the map $G_t^{[k]}$ is a $d$-tree contraction on $U_r$ with contraction constant $\lambda_G$, where $U_r$ is equipped with the metric induced by $\|\cdot\|_l$.
    Moreover, the set $U_r$ is invariant under each map $G_t^{[k]}$ in the sense that $G_t^{[k]}\left((U_r)^d\right)\subset U_r$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Time-dependent family of maps $G_t$: tree contraction on small balls at large times

body:
[campaign result 2026-09-14, author checked, no independent read] This is the finite-moment part of Svante Janson's Conjecture 20.1 in Simply generated trees, conditioned Galton-Watson trees, random allocations and condensation, Probability Surveys 9 (2012), arXiv:1112.0510. Let pi = (pi_j)_{j>=0} be a nondegenerate offspring law on the nonnegative integers with pi_0 > 0, sum j pi_j = 1, and variance sigma^2 in (0,infinity). Let xi have law pi, let T be the ordered Galton-Watson tree in which all vertices independently have pi-distributed numbers of children, and let T_n have the law of T conditional on its total number of vertices being n, along admissible n for which that event has positive probability. For a rooted tree A define ell_k(A) as its number of vertices at graph distance k from the root. Define the Kesten tree T_hat by an infinite distinguished spine: a spine vertex has j children with probability j pi_j, one uniformly selected child continues the spine, and every other child starts an independent ordinary pi Galton-Watson tree. Fix an integer k >= 1. If r >= 1 is real and E[xi^(r+1)] < infinity, then the family {ell_k(T_n)^r}_n is uniformly integrable and E[ell_k(T_n)^r] -> E[ell_k(T_hat)^r] < infinity. Here uniform integrability means lim_{K->infinity} sup_n E[ell_k(T_n)^r; ell_k(T_n)^r > K] = 0. For 0 < r < 1 the same conclusion follows under the displayed finite-variance assumption. The critical infinite-variance case with 0 < r < 1 is not settled by this result. This is an unrefereed campaign result.
pi is critical, nondegenerate, and pi_0 > 0.
k is fixed and positive; conditioning sizes are admissible.
For r >= 1, E[xi^(r+1)] < infinity; for 0 < r < 1, Var(xi) < infinity.

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:bd2d999d3e00a51463fc179469341fd2dc4ce15d9ff3e743bb7fd43377460681","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/bd/bd2d999d3e00a51463fc179469341fd2dc4ce15d9ff3e743bb7fd43377460681.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:9d13417b75738e2fc15d10e3322f651494c6abbbfcb1c6c7d810fcc69a74ead5","bundle_entry_key":"janson-conjecture-20-1-fixed-level-moment-convergence","bundle_id":"population.probability-campaign-results-20260914-001","claim_kind":"theorem","conditions":[],"domain":"probability theory","draft":"codex-prob1000-nodes-1010/bundle_001.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.trees:janson-conjecture-20-1-fixed-level-moment-convergence","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"Write $n$ for the tree sizes along which $T_n$ is defined ($n \equiv 1 \pmod{\text{span}}$) and $S_M$ for the sum of $M$ i.i.d. copies of $\xi \sim \pi$, so $\mathbb{E}\xi = 1$ and $\sigma^2 < \infty$. Two facts about $S_M$: by the local limit theorem for lattice laws with finite variance,
$$\mathbb{P}(S_n = n - 1) \ge c\,n^{-1/2} \quad\text{for all admissible } n, \qquad \sup_j \mathbb{P}(S_M = j) \le C\,M^{-1/2} \quad\text{for all } M \ge 1, \tag{1}$$
with $c, C > 0$ depending on $\pi$ only (the second holds for large $M$ by the same theorem and for the remaining $M$ trivially).

*The weight of a truncated tree.* Let $t$ be a finite plane tree whose vertices of depth less than $k$ have prescribed outdegrees and whose vertices at depth $k$ are leaves of $t$ with unspecified subtrees; call the former the interior $I(t)$, put $N = |I(t)| = 1 + \ell_1(t) + \dots + \ell_{k-1}(t)$ and $\ell = \ell_k(t)$. Let $T^{(k)}$ denote a tree truncated at depth $k$. For $\ell \ge 1$ and $n > N$, Lemma 14.9 of the survey (with the interior vertices as $v_1, \dots, v_N$ in depth-first order, $\sum_{i \le N} d_i = N - 1 + \ell$) gives
$$\mathbb{P}\big(T_n^{(k)} = t\big) = \ell\,\frac{n}{n - N}\,\mathbb{P}(Y_i = d_i,\ i \le N),$$
where $(Y_1, \dots, Y_n)$ is the allocation $B_{n-1,n}$, i.e. $n$ i.i.d. copies of $\xi$ conditioned on $S_n = n - 1$; so
$$\mathbb{P}\big(T_n^{(k)} = t\big) = \mathbb{P}_{\mathrm{GW}}\big(T^{(k)} = t\big)\;W_n(t), \qquad W_n(t) := \frac{n\,\ell\;\mathbb{P}(S_{n-N} = n - N - \ell)}{(n - N)\;\mathbb{P}(S_n = n - 1)}, \tag{2}$$
with $\mathbb{P}_{\mathrm{GW}}(T^{(k)} = t) = \prod_{v \in I(t)}\pi_{d(v)}$ the probability that the first $k$ generations of the unconditioned Galton–Watson tree $T$ are $t$. (The formula is also the cycle lemma applied to the forest of $\ell$ subtrees with $n - N$ vertices in total; the survey proves it from Lemma 14.3.) If $\ell = 0$ then $t$ is a whole tree and contributes nothing to any expectation of $\ell_k^r$ on $\{\ell_k \ge 1\}$, so it can be ignored.

Two bounds follow from (1) and (2). First,
$$W_n(t) \le \frac{n\,\ell\,C (n-N)^{-1/2}}{(n-N)\,c\,n^{-1/2}} = C'\,\ell\Big(\frac{n}{n-N}\Big)^{3/2}, \qquad C' = C/c. \tag{3}$$
Second, since the $\ell$ vertices at depth $k$ are among the $n - N$ vertices outside the interior, $n - N \ge \ell$, and so
$$W_n(t) \le C'\,n^{3/2}\,\ell^{-1/2}. \tag{4}$$

*Moments of generation sizes of the unconditioned tree.* For $s \ge 1$ and $Z_j := \ell_j(T)$: given $Z_{j-1} = m$, $Z_j$ is a sum of $m$ i.i.d. copies of $\xi$, so by Minkowski $\mathbb{E}[Z_j^s \mid Z_{j-1} = m] \le m^s\,\mathbb{E}\xi^s$, hence $\mathbb{E} Z_j^s \le (\mathbb{E}\xi^s)^j < \infty$ when $\mathbb{E}\xi^s < \infty$. Likewise $\mathbb{E}[Z_k^s \mid Z_j = m] \le m^s(\mathbb{E}\xi^s)^{k-j}$ for $s \ge 1$, and for $0 < s < 1$ by Jensen $\mathbb{E}[Z_k^s \mid Z_j = m] \le (\mathbb{E}[Z_k \mid Z_j = m])^s = m^s$ (mean one). So in all cases, for $0 < s \le r + 1$,
$$\mathbb{E}[Z_k^s \mid Z_j = m] \le C_s\,m^s. \tag{5}$$

*Uniform integrability.* Fix $K > 1$. By (2),
$$\mathbb{E}\big[\ell_k(T_n)^r;\ \ell_k(T_n) > K\big] = \mathbb{E}_{\mathrm{GW}}\big[Z_k^r\,W_n(T^{(k)});\ Z_k > K\big],$$
where on the right $N = N_k := 1 + Z_1 + \dots + Z_{k-1}$ is the number of vertices of $T$ of depth less than $k$. Split according to $N_k \le n/2$ or $N_k > n/2$.

On $\{N_k \le n/2\}$, (3) gives $W_n \le 2^{3/2}C' Z_k$, so this part is at most
$$2^{3/2}C'\;\mathbb{E}_{\mathrm{GW}}\big[Z_k^{r+1};\ Z_k > K\big],$$
which does not depend on $n$ and tends to $0$ as $K \to \infty$ because $\mathbb{E} Z_k^{r+1} \le (\mathbb{E}\xi^{r+1})^k < \infty$.

On $\{N_k > n/2\}$, (4) gives $Z_k^r W_n \le C' n^{3/2} Z_k^{r - 1/2}$, and $N_k > n/2$ forces $Z_j > n/(2k)$ for some $1 \le j \le k - 1$ when $n > 2k$ (the root alone cannot do it). So this part is at most
$$C' n^{3/2}\sum_{j=1}^{k-1}\mathbb{E}_{\mathrm{GW}}\big[Z_k^{r-1/2};\ Z_j > n/(2k)\big] \le C' C_{r-1/2}\,n^{3/2}\sum_{j=1}^{k-1}\mathbb{E}_{\mathrm{GW}}\big[Z_j^{r-1/2};\ Z_j > n/(2k)\big]$$
by (5) with $s = r - 1/2 \in [1/2, r+1]$, and on $\{Z_j > n/(2k)\}$ we have $Z_j^{r-1/2} \le (2k/n)^{3/2} Z_j^{r+1}$, so the whole thing is at most
$$C' C_{r-1/2}\,(2k)^{3/2}\sum_{j=1}^{k-1}\mathbb{E}_{\mathrm{GW}}\big[Z_j^{r+1};\ Z_j > n/(2k)\big] \longrightarrow 0 \quad (n \to \infty),$$
again because $\mathbb{E} Z_j^{r+1} < \infty$. This part does not depend on $K$ at all.

Hence $\limsup_{n}\mathbb{E}[\ell_k(T_n)^r; \ell_k(T_n) > K] \le 2^{3/2}C'\,\mathbb{E}_{\mathrm{GW}}[Z_k^{r+1}; Z_k > K] \to 0$ as $K \to \infty$, and since each $\mathbb{E}\,\ell_k(T_n)^r$ is finite (a finite tree), the family $\{\ell_k(T_n)^r\}$ is uniformly integrable. Together with $\ell_k(T_n) \to_d \ell_k(\widehat T)$, (20.1) of the survey, this gives $\mathbb{E}\,\ell_k(T_n)^r \to \mathbb{E}\,\ell_k(\widehat T)^r$, and the limit is finite because the moments are bounded. $\square$

Consequently Conjecture 20.1 holds for every integer $r \ge 1$ and, more generally, for every real $r \ge 1$; for $0 < r < 1$ it holds whenever $\sigma^2 < \infty$ (then $\ell_k(T_n)$ itself is uniformly integrable by the case $r = 1$, and so is any smaller power). body:
[Theorem 3 (Main result; see \Cref{thm:main}) of arXiv:2604.06532, 'Random permutations from $q$-Demazure products'] Fix $q \in (0,1)$ and $p \in (0,1)$.
Let $\sigma_n \in S_n$ be the random permutation obtained by the $q$-Demazure product
with deletion probability $1-p$ applied to the standard reduced decomposition of~$w_0$.
Then:
\begin{enumerate}[\upshape(i)]
  \item The sequence of permutons $\mu_{\sigma_n}$ converges weakly, in probability,
  to a deterministic permuton $\mu_{p,q}$.
  \item $\mu_{p,q}$ coincides with the limiting permuton $\mu_{p'}$ from
  \cite{GrothendieckShenanigans2024} for the Demazure product ($q=0$) with adjusted parameter
  \[
    p' \;=\; \frac{p(1-q)}{1-qp}.
  \]
  \item The explicit height function of $\mu_{p,q}$ is given in \cref{eq:h_refl,eq:height_rescaling}.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Main result; see \Cref{thm:main}

For the Ising Hamiltonian H=-J sum_edges sigma_u*sigma_v-B sum_vertices sigma_v, assume J>0,B>=0,Jh>B and beta>0. Every reversible continuous-time single-spin chain for the Gibbs law proportional to exp(-beta H), with each spin-flip rate at most1, satisfies t_mix(1/4)>=exp[beta(Jh-B)(n-1)]/(4*n*2^n). This is exponential in n when beta(Jh-B)>log2. No general random-graph expansion or metastable exit-time law is asserted.

Ferromagnetic J>0 and B>=0 with Jh>B
Continuous per-site rates at most1; reversible Gibbs dynamics

[Theorem thm:oco-lower-dim of arXiv:2608.24731, 'Optimal Alternating Regret for Online Learning and Games\thanks{Authors are alphabetically'] For every $d\ge2$, every horizon $T\ge16$, and every possibly randomized online
algorithm $\mathcal A$, there is a sequence of continuous convex losses
$f_1,\ldots,f_T:\+X\to[0,1]$ such that
\[
  \mathbb E_{\mathcal A}\left[\operatorname{Reg}_{\mathrm{Alt}}^T\right]\ \ge\ \frac{mK}{125}
  \quad\text{where}\quad
  m:=\min\left\{\left\lfloor\frac d2\right\rfloor,\left\lfloor\frac T{16}\right\rfloor\right\},
  \quad
  K:=\left\lfloor\log_{16}\left\lfloor\frac Tm\right\rfloor\right\rfloor .
\]
In particular $\mathbb E_{\mathcal A}[\operatorname{Reg}_{\mathrm{Alt}}^T]=\Omega\!\left(d\log(1+T/d)\right)$.

[Definition def:control of arXiv:2601.21762, 'Navier-Stokes with a fractional transport noise as a limit of multi-scale dynamics'] A map $\omega:\Delta_T\to[0,\infty)$ is called a \emph{control} if it is continuous, $\omega(s,s)=0$, and
$$
\omega(s,t)\ge \omega(s,u)+\omega(u,t)
\qquad\text{for } s\le u\le t.
$$

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:fb7b9dd12f1402292e1cc556bc918d784e6f840ed881500381c6ebcf71c1951d","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/fb/fb7b9dd12f1402292e1cc556bc918d784e6f840ed881500381c6ebcf71c1951d.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:dd45cc5a37eb2bdf6ee694037d47cb625d9da2c201909daabff05ac8adbb64c5","bundle_entry_key":"draft-clipped-score-tv-stability","bundle_id":"population.w740-t411-polynomial-lsi-hardness-v1","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"posterior sampling and functional inequalities","draft":"w740/bundle_002.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.sampling:draft-clipped-score-tv-stability","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# Gaussian-smoothed score approximation is stable in total variation after clipping

Status: proof draft, unaudited. Exact algebraic checks are pending. Input lemma for T411 Target 2.

Let P,Q be Borel probability laws on R^D with TV(P,Q)<=a. For u>0 write P_u=P*N(0,u^2 I), Q_u=Q*N(0,u^2 I), and let s_P,s_Q denote their scores. Suppose E_{P_u}||f-s_P||^2<=e^2. For L>0 let h be f clipped coordinatewise to [-L/u,L/u]. Then

E_{Q_u}||h-s_Q||^2 <=2 e^2 + [12 D exp(-L^2/2)+8 a D(L^2+1)]/u^2.

No moment or smoothness assumption on P,Q is needed. Gaussian convolution gives positive smooth densities, including when the unsmoothed prior has lattice coordinates.

## Proof

For X~P and independent N~N(0,I_D), set Y=X+uN. Differentiating the Gaussian convolution gives s_P(Y)=-E[N|Y]/u. Each fixed Gaussian-kernel derivative is bounded as a function of X, which justifies differentiation against any probability law. Conditional Jensen gives E exp(t u s_{P,j}(Y))<=E exp(-t N_j)=exp(t^2/2). The same holds for Q.

Write Pi for clipping to the box. The two-sided sub-Gaussian tail and Tonelli's theorem give

E_{P_u}||s_P-Pi s_P||^2
 <=(D/u^2) integral_0^infinity 4t exp(-(L+t)^2/2)dt
 <=4D exp(-L^2/2)/u^2=:b.

Here L>=0 and integral_0^infinity t exp(-t^2/2)dt=1. The same bound holds for Q.

Define R_P(g)=E||g(X+uN)+N/u||^2. Conditional expectation is the L2 projection, so R_P(g)=m_P+E_{P_u}||g-s_P||^2, with finite minimum m_P. The minimum restricted to box-valued fields is m_P+b_P, where b_P=E||s_P-Pi s_P||^2<=b. The analogous assertions hold for Q.

Use the common-part coupling X~P,X'~Q with Pr(X!=X')<=a, and take the same fresh N independent of the pair. For any box-valued g the two losses agree on X=X'. Otherwise their absolute difference is at most 4D L^2/u^2+4||N||^2/u^2. The mismatch event is independent of N, so

|R_P(g)-R_Q(g)|<=4aD(L^2+1)/u^2=:k.

The bound is uniform over the restricted class and hence over its two minimum risks. Thus m_P-m_Q<=k+b. Since clipping is a contraction,

E_{P_u}||h-s_P||^2<=2E||Pi f-Pi s_P||^2+2b_P<=2e^2+2b.

Consequently E_{Q_u}||h-s_Q||^2=R_Q(h)-m_Q<=2e^2+3b+2k, proving the bound. Every conditional expectation lies in L2. Independence is used before conditioning, never asserted after observing Y.

Coordinate clipping is a ReLU construction: clip(t,-M,M)=-M+ReLU(t+M)-ReLU(t-M). Polynomial L and polynomial ranges of u preserve polynomial network size and weight bounds. This does not construct exact-score oracles.

Clipping is essential: if P is a point mass at zero and Q=(1-a)P+a delta_M, the unbounded exact P_u score -y/u^2 can have Q_u error of order a M^2/u^4. A small prior TV distance alone gives no bound for that unbounded field.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:7ab9e28c856e2293467a5e36ef14790c8a81e7db0b438eb38951cbab6bdbf181","revision_digest":"sha256:4bb49c4ed56cb42686de979be69dabb934ea4d4c36e6dd11a085171ea1843c0d","source_id":"owner:T411:w740:C005-v1","source_revision":"2026-10-20-v1-unaudited","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

body:
Own-work proof (unaudited), C004 v1, route-failure for T368 Target 2; no novelty or GD nonconvergence claim. Let p>q>=1, tau=(p-q)/(p+q), and a,b>0 satisfy a^2+b^2<=1 and a^2<tau*b^2. Take p signed samples z_i=y_i*x_i=(a,b) and q signed samples (a,-b), with arbitrary labels +/-1 and x_i=y_i*z_i. These data are separated by (1,0) with margin a. Their signed mean mu=(a,tau*b) has negative inner product with the minority samples. Put e=mu/||mu|| and kappa=(tau*b^2-a^2)/||mu||>0. For f(theta,x)=m^-1 sum_j a_j phi(w_j dot x), width m>=1, centered C1 activation phi(0)=0, c=phi'(0)>0 and beta-Lipschitz derivative beta>=0, let P be the orthogonal projection onto the per-neuron spans of (1,e), and Q=I-P. This is the positive expanding eigenspace of simultaneous both-layer logistic-GD linearization at zero for any positive step. Write U=||Ptheta||>0, V=||Qtheta||, R=||theta||. If V<=epsilon*U, epsilon>0, epsilon+epsilon^2/2<=kappa/4, and beta*R*(1+epsilon^2)<=c*kappa/4, then every minority sample has y_i*f(theta,x_i)<=-c*kappa*U^2/(8m)<0. For beta=0 the radius condition is automatic. The cone is nonempty at arbitrarily small radii. The strict data inequalities persist under perturbations when a^2+b^2<1, giving an open family. For general data with nonzero signed mean, that mean separates all samples exactly when all signed Gram row sums sum_l z_i dot z_l are positive; existence of some separator does not imply this. Thus local saddle escape or arbitrarily close expanding alignment alone cannot establish positive margins. This does not control nonlinear trajectories after escape or refute eventual Gaussian burn-in. The exact rational example p=3,q=1,a=3/10,b=4/5 has e=(3/5,4/5), kappa=23/50. The written analytic proof, not its 1722 finite rational assertions, supplies the universal proposition.
Both layers trained, centered C1 activation with positive derivative at zero and Lipschitz derivative.
Explicit separable signed-data family and small-radius cone conditions in statement.
Proof (unaudited), T368-w734-C004 version 1; no novelty claim and no nonlinear-trajectory conclusion.

body: [Lemma le:variation_one_scale of arXiv:2507.15589, 'Tightness of approximations to metrics on non-simple conformal loop ensemble gaskets'] For any $p > d_{\rm SLE}$ there exists $c>0$ such that the following is true. Let $\varphi$ be a conformal transformation from $(D,x,y)$ to $(\mathbf{H},0,\infty)$, and let $\delta = \mathrm{dist}(\varphi^{-1}(i),\partial D)$. Let $\eta$ be a chordal ${\rm SLE}_{\kappa}${} in $(D,x,y)$. For $r,u>0$, let $E$ be the event that for every $s,t$ with $\varphi(\eta[s,t]) \subseteq [-u^{-1},u^{-1}]\times[u,u^{-1}]$ there are $r^{-p}u^{-c}$ times $s = t_1 < t_2 < \cdots < t_{r^{-p}u^{-c}} = t$ such that $\mathrm{diam}(\eta[t_{\ell},t_{\ell+1}]) \le r\delta$ for each $\ell$. Then $\mathbf{P}[E^c] = o^\infty(ru)$ as $ru \searrow 0$.

\begin{enumeratea}
\item  Suppose that $(t_e|t_e>0)$ has the exponential distribution with mean 1.
Then $T_n(1,2) \stackrel{d}{\longrightarrow} \Xi(\mathbf{p}, {\mathrm{Exp}(1)})$ as $n\to\infty$. 
\item 
Suppose that $t_e$ has distribution function $F_{a}(\cdot)$ as in (equation eqn:Fa-def of the paper) for $a>0$. Then $T_n(1,2)\stackrel{d}{\longrightarrow} \Xi(\mathbf{p}, {F_{a}})$  as $n\to\infty$. 
\item  Suppose that $t_e$ has distribution function $G_{b}(\cdot)$ as in (equation eqn:Gb-def of the paper)   for $b> 0$. Then for any $b\in(0,\infty)$ the distribution of $T_n(1,2) \stackrel{d}{\longrightarrow} \Xi(\mathbf{p}, {G_{b}})$ as $n\to\infty$. \end{enumeratea} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
Let (X, B, mu, T) be a measure-preserving system on a Lebesgue space and let P be a countable measurable partition of finite entropy. If P is a GENERATOR - that is, the smallest T-invariant sigma-algebra containing P is B modulo null sets (for invertible T one uses the two-sided join over all integers, for non-invertible T the one-sided join over nonnegative integers) - then the Kolmogorov-Sinai entropy of the system equals the entropy of that one partition: h(T) = h(T, P). There is also an increasing-partitions form: if P_1 is contained in P_2 is contained in ... is an increasing sequence of finite-entropy partitions whose union generates B modulo null sets, then h(T, P_n) increases to h(T).
Finite entropy of the generating partition, and generation modulo null sets.
For an INVERTIBLE T the generator must be two-sided;
using the one-sided join for an invertible map computes a different (in general larger) quantity and is the standard slip.
The Lebesgue-space assumption is the usual standing hypothesis.

				\[\beta \int_0^q \zeta_q([0,u])du=\frac{1}{\sqrt{\mu t}},\]

SOURCE-SCOPE DRAFT, not independently checked: Takanami, Takahashi and Kabashima, Learning Linear Regression with Low-Rank Tasks In-Context, arXiv:2510.04548v2. The work treats a finite base set of task vectors and low-rank task covariance, but Appendix B after equation (26) explicitly sets v21=0 and r21=0; equation (27) then defines a square effective matrix. Section 5.1 compares gradient descent using expected idealized features with finite demonstrations and discusses flat covariance directions. Thus this is relevant finite-pool prior work, but its square reduction does not retain the trained extra feature column needed for the raw augmented K^TQ selector and fixed-M risk question. Its justification of block invariance is an attribution to Zhang et al.; empirical finite-pool symmetry must be checked before importing that statement. This card is a scope distinction, not a theorem about the full model or a declaration of literature novelty.

[Theo 24 of arXiv:2602.14618, 'Finitary coding and Gaussian concentration\\ for random fields'] Let $d\ge2$ and $q\ge2$.

If $\beta<\beta_c(q)$, then the (unique) Gibbs measure
$\nu_{\beta,q}$ satisfies Gaussian concentration.

If $\beta>\beta_c(q)$, then none of the extremal
shift-invariant Gibbs measures
$\nu_{\beta,q}^1,\dots,\nu_{\beta,q}^q$
satisfies Gaussian concentration.

[Corollary 4 of arXiv:2604.10310, 'Weak convergence from projections along a positive-measure set of directions'] Let \((P_n)_{n\ge1}\) and \(P\) be Borel probability measures on
		\(\mathbb R^d\), with \(d\ge2\), and let \(A\subset\mathbb S^{d-1}\) be
		a Borel set with \(\sigma(A)>0\). If \(\pi_u(P_n)\weakto\pi_u(P)\) for
		every \(u\in A\), and each projected law \(\pi_u(P)\), \(u\in A\), has
		finite moments of all orders and is moment-determinate, then
		\(P_n\weakto P\).

\end{equation}

[Theorem 17 of arXiv:2609.03418, 'Sampling and Density Theorems for the Fractional Opdam--Cherednik Transform'] Let $S=[-\Omega,\Omega]$, $\alpha\ge\beta\ge-\frac12$, $\alpha>-\frac12$, and $0<\theta<\pi$. Suppose that
$$ \operatorname{Tr}\bigl(\mathbf{L}_{I,S}^{\theta}-(\mathbf{L}_{I,S}^{\theta})^2\bigr)=o(R), \quad I=[-R,R]. $$

If $\Lambda$ is a separated sampling set for $PW_{\alpha,\beta}^{\theta}(S)$, then
$$ \liminf_{R\to\infty}\frac{n([-R,R])}{R} \ge \frac{2^{1-2\rho}}{\pi}\Omega\csc\theta. $$

If $\Lambda$ is a separated interpolation set, then
$$ \limsup_{R\to\infty}\frac{n([-R,R])}{R} \le \frac{2^{1-2\rho}}{\pi}\Omega\csc\theta. $$

[Proposition 41 of arXiv:2609.02416, '2609.02416'] Assume $q\equiv c>0$ and $a\in C([-L,L])$. For compactly supported $J$, the functions $M$ and $\cH$ are analytic near the origin and $\cH(v)=\sum_{k\ge1}h_{2k}v^{2k}$,
where, writing $D_j=D_j(J)=\int_{\mathbb R}z^jJ(z)\,dz$,
\[
h_2=\frac1{2D_2},\qquad
h_4=-\frac{D_4}{24D_2^4},\qquad
h_6=\frac{D_4^2}{72D_2^7}-\frac{D_6}{720D_2^6}.
\]
For every integer $K\ge1$ and every fixed $1<m<2$,
\[
\Lp(\cA_{\sigma,m,L})
=\sum_{k=1}^{K}h_{2k}c^{2k}\sigma^{(2k-1)m-2k}
-\max a
+O\!\left(\sigma^{(2K+1)m-(2K+2)}\right)+o(1).
\]
More intrinsically, define $N(m)=\max\{k\ge1:(2k-1)m-2k\le0\}$.
Then the expansion through every nonvanishing order is
\[
\Lp(\cA_{\sigma,m,L})
=\sum_{k=1}^{N(m)}h_{2k}c^{2k}\sigma^{(2k-1)m-2k}
-\max a+o(1).
\]
The $k$th correction becomes order one at $m=2k/(2k-1)$; the successive thresholds are $4/3,6/5,8/7,\ldots$.

Let gamma be the standard Gaussian measure on R^n. For every locally Lipschitz f with f and grad f in L^2(gamma), Ent_gamma(f^2) <= 2 E_gamma[ |grad f|^2 ], where Ent(g) = E[g log g] - E[g] log E[g] for g >= 0. The constant 2 is sharp, with near-equality for exponentials f = e^{a . x / 2}. As with the Poincare inequality the constant is DIMENSION-FREE, obtained from the one-dimensional case by tensorization of entropy. Gross's theorem states that this inequality is EQUIVALENT to Nelson's hypercontractivity for the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck semigroup, and it implies the Gaussian Poincare inequality by linearisation. Combined with the Herbst argument it yields Gaussian concentration for Lipschitz functions with the sharp sub-Gaussian variance proxy equal to the square of the Lipschitz constant. Care with normalisation: the inequality is often written as Ent(f) <= 2 E[ |grad sqrt(f)|^2 ] for f >= 0, which is the same statement after substituting f -> f^2, and some sources carry a factor 1/2 from using a different generator normalisation; the version stated here is the one matching the standard Gaussian and the generator L = Laplacian minus x . gradient. [Gross (1975); see Bakry, Gentil and Ledoux, Analysis and Geometry of Markov Diffusion Operators, Chapter 5]
gamma the standard Gaussian measure on R^n
f locally Lipschitz with f and grad f in L^2(gamma)
the generator normalisation L = Laplacian minus x . gradient, which fixes the constant 2

TECHNIQUE CARD. For a mean-zero variable, couple it with a variable having the zero-biased law; the normal law N(0, σ²) is the unique fixed point of the zero-bias transformation, so the distance between the two variables controls the distance from the normal law. Ross, Definition 3.10: for W with E[W] = 0 and Var(W) = σ² < ∞, W^z has the zero-bias distribution with respect to W if E[Wf(W)] = σ² E[f'(W^z)] for all absolutely continuous f with E|Wf(W)| < ∞. Theorem 3.18: let W be a mean zero, variance one random variable and let W^z be defined on the same space as W and have the zero-bias distribution with respect to W; if Z ~ N(0,1), then d_W(W, Z) ≤ 2E|W^z − W|.
E[W] = 0 and Var(W) = 1 (Theorem 3.18)
W^z, with E[Wf(W)] = E[f'(W^z)] for all absolutely continuous f with E|Wf(W)| < ∞, is defined on the same space as W

[Lemma 35 ({\bf Obus--Pries}) of arXiv:2609.03191, 'On lifting representations and actions on curves of the metacyclic groups $C_{p^s}\rtimes '] Suppose that $\underline{z}=(z_0,\ldots,z_{s-1})\in W_s(k((x)))$ is in standard form in the sense of \cite{OP}, Sect.\ 3.2, i.e.,
each non-zero $z_i$ is a polynomial in $x^{-1}$ whose monomial exponents are not
divisible by $p$. For $i\in\llbracket1,s\rrbracket$, let $d_i$ be the pole order of $z_{i-1}$ at $x=0$, with
$d_i:=-\infty$ if $z_{i-1}=0$. If $\wp(\underline{y})=\underline{z}$ defines a cyclic extension of $k((x))$ of degree
$p^s$, then its $i$-th upper jump is
\[
u_i:=\max(p^{i-j}d_j\mid j\in\llbracket1,i\rrbracket).
\]
In particular, $u_1=d_1$ and $u_i=\max(p u_{i-1},d_i)$ for $i\in\llbracket2,s\rrbracket$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: {\bf Obus--Pries}

Given all the GFF values on $\widetilde{\partial}(D_1\cup D_2)$, if they are all non-negative and equal to zero on $[D_j\setminus \mathbf{B}_j]\cup D_{3-j}$, then the conditional probability of $\big\{ D_j \xleftrightarrow{\ge 0} \partial B(N_{3-j})\big\} $ is at most of order $N_j^{d-2}\theta_d(N_{3-j}/4)\mathcal{H}_j$.

body: Lemma 1. A dataset {(pi(g) r_mu, y_mu)}_{g in G, mu in [P]} consisting of P pi-manifolds with labels y_mu is linearly separable if and only if the dataset {(<pi> r_mu, y_mu)}_{mu in [P]} consisting of the P centroids <pi> r_mu with the same labels is linearly separable. Formally, there is a w with y_mu w^T pi(g) r_mu > 0 for all g in G, mu in [P] if and only if there is a w with y_mu w^T <pi> r_mu > 0 for all mu in [P]. Here pi : G -> GL(R^N) is a linear representation of a compact group G and <pi> = <pi(g)>_{g in G} is its average over G with respect to the Haar measure.

[Definition 6 (Exact-shell Microcanonical Ensemble) of arXiv:2607.23526, 'Equivalence of Canonical and Microcanonical Ensembles for Euclidean Lattices'] For $E\in\im(H_N)$ (such an $E$ is referred to as reachable), denote
\[\Gamma_N(E):=\{x\in\Lambda^N:H_N(x)=E\},\quad g_N(E):=\#\Gamma_N(E).\]
Define the exact-shell microcanonical ensemble on $\Gamma_N(E)$ and its entropy by
\[\mu^{\sh}_{N,E}(x):=g_N(E)^{-1}\one_{\Gamma_N(E)}(x),\quad R^{\sh}_{N,E}:=\log g_N(E).\]

body:
[Theorem a10 of arXiv:2411.19926, 'Sparse Pseudospectral Shattering'] Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb C$ be a set such that
\[\inf_{\deg(p)\le k}\sup_{z\in\Omega}\mleft|1-zp(z)\mright|\le C\alpha^k.\]
Let $\varepsilon, \delta \in (0,1)$ and let
$M$ be a matrix such that $\left\|M\right\|\le\poly(n)$ and
$\Lambda_\delta(M)\subset\Omega$. \textnormal{\texttt{shatteredGMRES}} is an algorithm which, in \[k=O\pare{\dfrac{\log(n/\delta)\log(n)+\log(1/\varepsilon)}{\log(1/\alpha)}}\] iterations, outputs $x$ such that
\[(M+\Delta_M)x=(b+\delta_b), \quad \left\|\Delta_M\right\|\le\delta,\quad\left\|\delta_b\right\|\le\varepsilon\]
and uses
\(O\mleft( k\nnz(M)+kn\log^6(n)+k^2n \mright)\)
arithmetic operations.
title: Theorem a10 of arXiv:2411.19926

body:
[Theorem thm:local_analyticity of arXiv:2604.18558, 'Uniform analyticity of local observables in FK-percolation and analyticity of the Ising sp'] Assume that $(d,p,q) \in \mathcal G_{\mathsf{FK}}$. Then, there exists $\delta > 0$ such that:

\begin{enumerate}
\item For any \emph{local} function $F$, for any $z \in \mathbb C$ satisfying $|z|<\delta$, the following limit exists:
\[
\phi_{p + z, q}[F(\omega)] \coloneqq \lim_{N\rightarrow \infty} \phi_{\mathbb T_N, p + z, q}[F(\omega)] \in \mathbb C.
\]
Furthermore, the function 
\[ z \in \mathbb D_\delta(0) \mapsto \phi_{p + z, q}[F(\omega)]\in \mathbb C \]
 is complex analytic.
\item 

There exists a sequence $c_\epsilon$, going to 0 when $\epsilon$ goes to 0, such that for any $|z| < \epsilon < \delta$ and any non-negative \emph{local} function $F$ which is not identically 0, 
\begin{equation}\tag{$\star$}
\left| \frac{\phi_{p + z, q}[F(\omega)]}{\phi_{p, q}[F(\omega)]} \right| \leq 2\exp(c_\epsilon |\mathsf{Supp}_F|),
\end{equation}
where $\mathsf{Supp}_F$ is the support of $F$.

 \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm:local_analyticity of arXiv:2604.18558

body:
[Theorem 1 of arXiv:2607.09246, 'Scaling limit of 1+1 dimensional directed polymer with power-law tail and spatial correlat'] Assume that conditions \textbf{(A)} and \textbf{(B)} hold. Let the tail exponent satisfy $\alpha > \frac{6}{3-2r}$. For a sequence of inverse temperatures $\beta_N$,  the log-partition function $\ln Z_N(\beta_N; \omega)$ exhibits the following two limit behaviors:

\noindent
\textbf{(a)} 
If $\beta_N N^{H/2} \to \beta \in (0, \infty)$ as $N \to \infty$, then the log-partition function centered by its multi-order polynomial drift converges in distribution to the logarithm of the continuous Wiener chaos:
$$
    \ln Z_N(\beta_N; \omega) - N \sum_{j=2}^{\lfloor 2/H \rfloor} \frac{\beta_N^j}{j!} \mathbb{E}_{\mathbb{Q}}[\bar{\xi}^j] \sum_{y=-\infty}^{\infty} \psi_y^j \stackrel{D}{\Longrightarrow} \ln Z_{\sqrt{2}\beta}(1, \cdot),
$$
where $Z_{\sqrt{2}\beta}(t, \cdot)$ is the unique solution to the following stochastic heat equation (SHE)
$$
    \partial_t u = \frac{1}{2} \Delta u + \sqrt{2}\beta u \dot{W}, \quad u(0,x) = \delta_0(x),
$$
driven by a centered Gaussian space-time noise $\dot{W}$ with covariance structure
$$
    \mathbb{E}_{\mathbb{Q}}[\dot{W}(t,x) \dot{W}(s,y)] = H(2H-1)\delta(t-s) |x-y|^{2H-2}.
$$

\noindent
\textbf{(b)} 
Let $\beta_N N^{H/2} \to 0$ as $N \to \infty$, and there exists a constant $a$ with $0 < a < A_{*}(\alpha, H)$, which is defined in \eqref{A_alpha_H}, such that 
\[
\beta_N N^{H/2} \gg N^{-a}.
\]
Then the normalized fluctuation converges to a Gaussian distribution:
$$
    \frac{1}{\beta_N N^{H/2}} \left( \ln Z_N(\beta_N; \omega) - N \sum_{j=2}^{p'} \frac{\beta_N^j}{j!} \mathbb{E}_{\mathbb{Q}}[\bar{\xi}^j] \sum_{y=-\infty}^{\infty} \psi_y^j \right) \stackrel{D}{\longrightarrow} \mathcal{N}(0, \sigma_H^2),
$$
where $p'=\left\lfloor\frac2H\right\rfloor$. \(\text{More generally, \(p'\) can be replaced by any integer }
p\le \lfloor2/H\rfloor
\text{ such that }
\frac{N\beta_N^{p+1}}{\beta_NN^{H/2}}\to0.\) The variance is given by
$$
    \sigma_H^2 = 2H(2H-1) \int_0^1 \int_{\mathbb{R}^2} \rho(t,x)\rho(t,y)|x-y|^{2H-2} \,dx \,dy \,dt,
$$
with $\rho(t,x)$ being the standard heat kernel. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 1 of arXiv:2607.09246

body: [Definition 2 (Limit cycle and basin of attraction) of arXiv:2605.24611, 'Beyond Fixed Points: Superpolynomial Capacity of Asymmetric Hopfield Networks'] A limit cycle of period P ≥1 is a set of distinct states C = {x(0), x(1), . . . , x(P −1)} such that, for the synchronous update map F : {−1, 1}n → {−1, 1}n, we have F(x(i)) = x(i+1) for i = 0, . . . , P −2 and F(x(P −1)) = x(0). The special case P = 1 is a fixed point. The basin of attraction of C is B(C) = {y ∈{−1, +1}n : ∃T ≥ 0 such that F T (y) ∈C}. Clearly, C ⊆B(C); we call C a limit-cycle attractor if C ⊊B(C).
title: Definition 2 (Limit cycle and basin of attraction) of arXiv:2605.24611: Beyond Fixed Points: Superpolynomial Capacity of Asymmetric Hopfield

body: In graph theory, the Robertson–Seymour theorem (also called the graph minors theorem) states that the undirected graphs, partially ordered by the graph minor relationship, form a well-quasi-ordering. Equivalently, every family of graphs that is closed under taking minors can be defined by a finite set of forbidden minors, in the same way that Wagner's theorem characterizes the planar graphs as being the graphs that do not have the complete graph $K_{5}$ or the complete bipartite graph $K_{3,3}$ as minors.
