Let (T(t))_{t ≥ 0} be a C_0-semigroup on a Banach space X with generator A, and let M ≥ 1, ω ∈ ℝ satisfy ‖T(t)‖ ≤ M e^{ωt}. Then: (a) A is densely defined and closed, and A determines T uniquely (two C_0-semigroups with the same generator are equal). (b) For x ∈ D(A) and t ≥ 0, T(t)x ∈ D(A) and d/dt T(t)x = A T(t)x = T(t) A x, the derivative being two-sided for t > 0. (c) For every x ∈ X, ∫_0^t T(s)x ds ∈ D(A) and A ∫_0^t T(s)x ds = T(t)x − x; for x ∈ D(A), T(t)x − x = ∫_0^t T(s)Ax ds. (d) Every λ ∈ ℂ with Re λ > ω belongs to the resolvent set ρ(A), and R(λ, A)x = (λ − A)^{-1}x = ∫_0^∞ e^{-λt}T(t)x dt (an absolutely convergent improper Riemann integral), with ‖R(λ, A)^n‖ ≤ M/(Re λ − ω)^n for all n ≥ 1. (e) The abstract Cauchy problem u'(t) = Au(t), u(0) = x has, for x ∈ D(A), the unique classical solution u(t) = T(t)x. (f) A subspace D ⊂ D(A) which is dense in X and invariant under every T(t) is a core for A.

[Definition 9 (Formal tangent space) of arXiv:2605.30560, 'Projected McKean--Vlasov Dynamics for Entropic Weak Optimal Transport'] The tangent space of the adapted Wasserstein space
$(\mathcal P_2(\mathbb R^{2d}),\mathcal{AW}_2)$ at
$\pi\in\mathcal P_2(\mathbb R^{2d})$ is given by
\[
T_\pi^{\mathrm{ad}}\mathcal P_2(\mathbb R^{2d})
\simeq
\overline{
\left\{
\nabla_\pi^{\mathrm{ad}}\varphi:
\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^{2d}; \R)
\right\}
}^{\,L^2(\pi)}.
\]
It is equipped with the Riemannian-like metric
\[
\|v\|_{T_\pi^{\mathrm{ad}}}^2
:=
\int_{\mathbb R^{2d}} |v(x,y)|^2\,\pi(dx,dy).
\]
title: Formal tangent space

ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Examine whether the moment condition controls the back-and-forth trap time and hence the regeneration-time tail. Result: The quantity 1/(1 - omega(0,e) omega(e,-e)) is the expected number of visits to 0, the first included, during the two-site back-and-forth excursion between 0 and e (a round trip steps from 0 to e and back from e to 0, with probability omega(0,e) omega(e,-e)), so the moment condition bounds the expected holding time in two-site traps but not in larger traps (a trap of k sites in a line has holding time controlled by products of k such ratios, whose expectation is not bounded by the first-moment condition). Proposition 2.21 of the source shows the condition is necessary; sufficiency would need a bound on the expected time spent in traps of every size, i.e. on E[tau_1 | D = infinity]. A natural sufficient strengthening is a moment condition on the exit time from every finite box, which is implied by the two-site condition only under an additional assumption on the transition probabilities to move away. I therefore see the question as open in the sense that the two-site condition is strictly weaker than what the regeneration argument needs, and the Dirichlet case works because of the specific reversal identity of Dirichlet environments (Sabot's exit-time integrability). No new result. Obstruction: Two-site moment condition does not control larger traps; the Dirichlet argument uses a special reversal identity.

body: The Galton–Watson process, also called the Bienaymé-Galton–Watson process or the Galton-Watson branching process, is a branching stochastic process arising from Francis Galton's statistical investigation of the extinction of family names. The process models family names as patrilineal, while offspring are randomly either male or female, and names become extinct if the family name line dies out.
title: Galton–Watson process

 \int_Xd_{g_{i,t}}(p_i,y)^2\,d\nu_t^i(y)\le C_t(-t).

Write g_(k,t)=grad_theta f_k(x_t),P=dim(theta),and F_M=(1/T)*sum_(k,t) g_(k,t)g_(k,t)^T. Let alpha>0 satisfy P/M^2->alpha,and assume explicitly that <g_(k,s),g_(kprime,t)>/M->delta_(k,kprime)*alpha*K_st,where K has diagonal kappa1 and off-diagonal kappa2,with kappa1>=kappa2>=0. All these finitely many limits hold jointly almost surely,or jointly in probability. Then Tr(F_M^2)/P -> C*alpha*((T-1)*kappa2^2/T+kappa1^2/T),in the same convergence mode. In the source closure,kappa1=(1/alpha)*sum_(l=1)^L alpha_(l-1)*qtilde_l*qhat_(l-1),and kappa2=(1/alpha)*sum_(l=1)^L alpha_(l-1)*qtilde_pair_l*qhat_pair_(l-1). Here qhat is the width-normalized inner product of forward activations and qtilde the unnormalized inner product of backward signals,with diagonal or distinct-sample limits respectively. The backward-weight decoupling is Assumption1 of the source;the explicit gradient Gram convergence is an additional hypothesis here. This is a conditional formulation of the leading second-moment formula,not a proof of those convergence premises for tied-weight backpropagation or a proportional-T regime. C,T,L are fixed as M tends to infinity. P is the total number of weights and biases,alpha=sum_(l=1)^(L-1) alpha_l*alpha_(l-1),and P/M^2->alpha>0.

The finite constants satisfy kappa1>=kappa2>=0. Forward and backward same-sample and distinct-sample order parameters entering the source formulas have finite deterministic limits common to each sample or sample pair. These convergence and output-decoupling statements are premises,not consequences proved here from Assumption1.

        p_k=\sum_{n\geq k}\frac{a_n}{n}.

conditionally on \(N=n\), is uniform on \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\), has law

Let R > 0, let f be holomorphic on an open set containing the closed disk |z| ≤ R, with f(0) ≠ 0 and f having no zeros on the circle |z| = R. Let a_1, ..., a_N be the zeros of f in the open disk |z| < R, listed with multiplicity. Then log|f(0)| = Σ_{k=1}^{N} log(|a_k|/R) + (1/2π) ∫_0^{2π} log|f(R e^{iθ})| dθ. Equivalently, (1/2π)∫_0^{2π} log|f(Re^{iθ})| dθ - log|f(0)| = Σ_k log(R/|a_k|) = ∫_0^R n(t) dt/t, where n(t) is the number of zeros of f in |z| ≤ t counted with multiplicity. The formula remains valid if f has zeros on the circle |z| = R, the boundary integral still converging absolutely; if f(0) = 0 of order m one applies the formula to f(z)/z^m and adds m log R. The immediate consequence used constantly: for an entire function of finite order ρ the zero counting function satisfies n(r) = O(r^{ρ+ε}).
f is holomorphic on a neighborhood of the closed disk |z| ≤ R
f(0) ≠ 0 (otherwise divide by z^m)
zeros in the open disk are listed with multiplicity
no zeros on |z| = R in the stated form (the formula extends to that case)

body: In the mathematical field of set theory, a large cardinal property is a certain kind of property of transfinite cardinal numbers. Cardinals with such properties are, as the name suggests, generally very large, such that the cardinal is inaccesible through standard set theory functions, power sets or successors of smaller cardinals.. The proposition that such cardinals exist cannot be proved in the most common axiomatization of set theory, namely ZFC, and such propositions can be viewed as ways of measuring how "much", beyond ZFC, one needs to assume to be able to prove certain desired results. In other words, they can be seen, in Dana Scott's phrase, as quantifying the fact "that if you want more you have to assume more".
title: Large cardinal

body:
[Proposition 31 of arXiv:2608.03497, 'Connective Constants on Nested Fractal Graphs'] Let
\[
  H_m(z)=
  \sum_{\substack{w\text{ is a self-avoiding walk in }F_m\\w(0)=O}}
  z^{L(w)}.
\]
The number of \(n\)-step self-avoiding walks in \(F_m\) starting at
\(O\) is \([z^n]H_m(z)\).  Let \(P_m(z)\) be the sum of \(z^{L(w)}\)
over all self-avoiding paths joining a fixed pair of
diagonally opposite boundary vertices, and define
\(Q_m(z)\) in the same way for a fixed adjacent pair.  Dihedral symmetry
makes these polynomials independent of the
chosen pair.  They satisfy
\begin{equation}
  \begin{aligned}
  P_{m+1}&=P_m^3,\\
  Q_{m+1}&=P_m^2Q_m,\\
  H_{m+1}&=H_m+P_m(1+2Q_m+P_m)(H_m-1),
  \end{aligned}
  
\end{equation}
with
\[
  H_0=1+2z+2z^2+2z^3,\qquad
  P_0=2z^2,\qquad Q_0=z+z^3.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition 22 of arXiv:2609.02850, 'Canonical-row Chern flow on Bott--Samelson towers:\\ realizable-volume models for Schubert'] For a word $\mathbf i=(i_1,\ldots,i_\ell)$ and
$j\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$, declare
\[
 (j,s)\sim(j,t)
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 i_q\ne j\text{ for every }
 \min\{s,t\}<q\le\max\{s,t\}.
\]
Write $\sigma_j(t)=[j,t]$ for the equivalence class.  Its unique
creation-time representative is
\[
 \bigl(j,\tau_j(t)\bigr),\qquad
 \tau_j(t)=\max\bigl(\{0\}\cup\{q\le t:i_q=j\}\bigr).
\]
On the quotient-flag tower constructed in \cref{sec:canonical}, if
$s\le t$ and $(j,s)\sim(j,t)$, then
$F_j^{(t)}$ is canonically the pullback of $F_j^{(s)}$.  Hence the pullback
to the final tower of the bundle represented by $\sigma_j(t)$ is
independent of the representative.

body: [Definition 3 (Colored top-$m$-to-random) of arXiv:2606.29530, 'Cutoff profiles for colored top-\texorpdfstring{$m$}{m}-to-random shuffles with growing bl'] For $1\le m\le n$, one step of $p$-colored top-$m$-to-random is the following shuffle. Remove the top $m$ cards, recolor those $m$ cards by independent uniform elements of $C_p$, apply a uniform random permutation to the removed block, choose an $m$-element set of final positions uniformly among all $\binom nm$ possibilities, and insert the removed cards into those positions. The remaining $n-m$ cards preserve their relative order and color.  Let $Q_{n,p}^{(m)}$ denote the one-step law on $G_{n,p}$.

body:
[Proposition prop:three-causes of arXiv:2607.04620, 'The Exact Ville Identity\\ \large From the Absorbing Case to the General Law\\ with an App'] For a nonnegative supermartingale $(M_n)$ with $M_0=1$ crossing the level $b>1$:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
\item The martingale-versus-supermartingale gap governs $D_b$. If $(M_n)$ is a martingale then $\delta_n\equiv0$ and $D_b=0$; the loss term is nonzero precisely to the extent that the process is a strict supermartingale, that is, sheds predictable mass before crossing.
\item Bounded overshoot governs $O_b$. If the conditional landing value satisfies $\mathbb{E}[M_{T_b}\mid \mathcal{F}_{T_b-1},T_b=n]\le b+\omega$ a.s. for a constant $\omega$, then $O_b\le\omega$ ((sec:overshoot of the paper)); on a lattice that includes $b$, $O_b=0$. The overshoot is nonzero precisely to the extent that the increments can carry the process strictly past the boundary.
\item Wobbling governs $R_b$. If, in the martingale case, conditions (i)--(ii) of (thm:wobbling of the paper) hold (sufficient wobbling and bounded overshoot), then $\mathbb{P}(T_b<\infty)=1$, so the survival event is null and $R_b=0$. The residual is nonzero precisely to the extent that wobbling fails -- that is, to the extent that paths can settle and survive forever without crossing.
\end{enumerate}

body:
[Lemma of arXiv:2607.29020, 'Entropic Symmetrization Resistance'] \label[lemma]{lem:Rd_projection_works}
Let $Y = (Y_1, \dots, Y_d)$ be an independent symmetrizer for $X = (X_1, \dots, X_d)$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$. 
Then, for any nonempty $E \subseteq [d]$, $Y[E]$ is an independent symmetrizer for $X[E]$. 
In particular, for all $i \in [d]$, $Y_i$ is an independent symmetrizer for $X_i$. 
\begin{proof}
Fix $E = \{ i_1, \dots, i_k \} \subsetneq [d]$. 

Clearly, for any $z \in \mathbb{R}^d$
\begin{align*}
f_{X + Y}(z)
&= f_{(X + Y)[E]}(z[E]) f_{(X + Y)[E^c] \mid (X + Y)[E]}(z[E^c] \mid z[E]) .
\intertext{Since $Y$ is an independent symmetrizer of $X$, we have 
$f_{X + Y}(z) = f_{X + Y}(-z)$ and}
f_{(X + Y)[E]}(z[E]) &f_{(X + Y)[E^c] \mid (X + Y)[E]}(u \mid z[E]) \\
&= f_{(X + Y)[E]}(-z[E]) f_{(X + Y)[E^c] \mid (X + Y)[E]}(u \mid -z[E]) .
\intertext{where we have written $u = z[E^c]$. 
Now, write $S = \supp((X + Y)[E^c])$ and sum over $u \in S$:}

 f_{(X + Y)[E]}(z[E]) &\sum_{u \in S} f_{(X + Y)[E^c] \mid (X + Y)[E]}(u \mid z[E]) \\
&= f_{(X + Y)[E]}(-z[E]) \sum_{u \in S} f_{(X + Y)[E^c] \mid (X + Y)[E]}(u \mid -z[E]) .
\end{align*}

Thus
$ f_{(X + Y)[E]}(z[E]) = f_{(X + Y)[E]}(-z[E]) . $
Independence of $X[E]$ and $Y[E]$ is inherited from independence of $X$ and $Y$. 

\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Unnumbered lemma of arXiv:2607.29020, 'Entropic Symmetrization Resistance'

ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Integrator-authored exact special-case argument and failure analysis after checking the incoming source Result: Let f(theta)=g(k*theta). Its Fourier coefficients vanish at lags not divisible by k, so the determinantal kernel is block diagonal on the k residue classes. Determinant factorization proves that these restrictions are independent copies of P_g. If P_g can be represented as F(U_j,...,U_(j+r)) with iid U, define Y_i=F(U_i,U_(i+k),...,U_(i+r*k)). This is a shift-equivariant function of the window U_i,...,U_(i+r*k), so is an (r*k+1)-block factor. The residue-class families use disjoint iid coordinates and have the correct laws. In particular any single-harmonic symbol a+b*cos(k*theta)+c*sin(k*theta) with range in [0,1] inherits the known degree-one construction and is a (k+1)-block factor. Check: For cylinder events on distinct residue classes, all mixed kernel entries vanish and every required inclusion determinant factors. Inclusion-exclusion upgrades those identities to independence of the complete finite-dimensional distributions. The proposed coding depends only on positions at distances k, making its full window length exactly r*k+1. Obstruction: General mixed-harmonic symbols remain untreated. Finite dependence by itself does not imply a block-factor representation.

There is an infinite connected tree of maximum degree three whose rooted self-avoiding-walk counts c_n satisfy liminf c_n^(1/n)=1 and limsup c_n^(1/n)=2. Use successive level-block lengths 2^(2^j), with one child in even blocks and two in odd blocks. Rooted scalar submultiplicativity already fails at c_1=c_2=1,c_3=2. This refutes a generic bounded-degree existence route, but the example is not a stationary iid percolation cluster of Z^2.

At level l, all vertices have b_l children. Partition the levels into successive blocks of lengths L_j=2^(2^j), j=0,1,... . Give one child at every level in even blocks and two children in odd blocks. This is an infinite connected tree with maximum degree three.

Every self-avoiding root walk moves outward, so c_n(o)=product_{l<n} b_l. At the end N_j=sum_{h<=j} L_h, write B_j for the number of two-child levels among those N_j. Then log(c_{N_j}(o))/(N_j*log 2)=B_j/N_j. The earlier blocks have total at most j*L_{j-1}=j*sqrt(L_j), negligible relative to L_j. Along odd block ends this ratio tends to one; along even block ends it tends to zero. Since every ratio lies in [0,1],

    liminf c_n(o)^(1/n)=1,  limsup c_n(o)^(1/n)=2.

The exponential limit therefore does not exist even on an infinite connected bounded-degree graph. On the first three levels, c_1=c_2=1 but c_3=2, directly refuting scalar rooted submultiplicativity c_{n+m}(o)<=c_n(o)*c_m(o). [Thm intro-stable of arXiv:2608.23135, 'Graph distance and effective resistance of the random walk trace in four and five dimensio'] Let \(X_n\) denote either \(D_n\) or \(R_n\).

If \(d=5\), then
\[
    \frac{X_n-\mathbb{E} X_n}{n^{2/3}}
    \ \Longrightarrow\
    Z_{5,X},
\]
where \(Z_{5,X}\) is a non-degenerate stable random variable of index \(3/2\)
with skewness \(-1\). The law of \(Z_{5,X}\) depends on the choice
\(X=D\) or \(X=R\).

If \(d=4\), let \(b_X\) be the constant in the first-order asymptotic
(equation Eq2 of the paper) corresponding to \(X\). Then
\[
    \frac{
        X_n-\mathbb{E} X_n
        -\frac{b_X}{2} n(\log n)^{-3/2}\log\log n
    }{
        n(\log n)^{-3/2}
    }
    \ \Longrightarrow\
    Z_{4,X},
\]
where \(Z_{4,X}\) is a non-degenerate stable random variable of index \(1\)
with skewness \(-1\).  The law of \(Z_{4,X}\) depends on the choice
\(X=D\) or \(X=R\). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Theorem 5 of arXiv:2608.03497, 'Connective Constants on Nested Fractal Graphs'] \phantomsection

\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item If the nested fractal graph is \(h\)-flexible,
then
\begin{equation}
  \lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{c_{n+h}}{c_n}=\mu^h.
  
\end{equation}
In particular, \(1\)-flexibility implies
\[
  \lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{c_{n+1}}{c_n}=\mu.
\]
\item For the regular polygonal \(N\)-gasket with \(N\ge3\) and
\(4\nmid N\), write
\[
  N=4k_N+\ell_N,\qquad
  \ell_N\in\{1,2,3\},\qquad
  s_N=k_N+1,
\]
and put
\[
  h_N
  =
  \gcd\bigl(N-2s_N,\,2s_N-(N-2s_N)\bigr).
\]
Then \(h_N\) is the smallest flexibility step.  In fact, the graph is
\(h_N\)-flexible at scale \(2\), and
\[
  h_N=
  \begin{cases}
    2,&N\equiv2\pmod4,\\
    3,&N\equiv9\pmod{12},\\
    1,&\text{otherwise}.
  \end{cases}
\]
Consequently,
\[
  \lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{c_{n+h_N}}{c_n}=\mu_N^{h_N}.
\]
\item The standard Vicsek graph is not \(h\)-flexible for any
\(h\ge1\).  Its connective constant is
\(\mu=\sqrt2\), but, for every \(k\ge2\),
\begin{equation}
  \begin{aligned}
  c_{3^k-2}&=2^{(3^k+1)/2},\\
  c_{3^k-1}&=3\cdot2^{(3^k-3)/2},\\
  c_{3^k}&=3\cdot2^{(3^k-1)/2}.
  \end{aligned}
  
\end{equation}
Consequently,
\[
  \frac{c_{3^k-1}}{c_{3^k-2}}=\frac34,
  \qquad
  \frac{c_{3^k}}{c_{3^k-1}}=2,
\]
and the successive ratios do not converge.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 5 of arXiv:2608.03497

[Definition Function $K_2^{\mathrm{ad}}$ of arXiv:2607.24528, 'On Feige's conjecture'] For \(x,y\geq 0\), let \(a=\min(x,y)\) and \(b=\max(x,y)\). When \(0\leq a<1<b\), let \(\tau(a,b)\) be the larger root of
\[
t^2-b(1+a)t+ab=0.
\]
Define \(K_2^{\mathrm{ad}}\colon[0,\infty)^2\to[0,1]\) by
\[
K_2^{\mathrm{ad}}(a,b)
=
\begin{cases}
1,
& b\leq 1,\\
\frac{2}{\tau(a,b)}-\frac{1}{\tau(a,b)^2},
& 0\leq a<1<b,\\
\frac{1}{ab},
& 1\leq a.
\end{cases}
\]
title: Function $K_2^{\mathrm{ad}}$

Target 2(b). Status: proof (unaudited), diagnostic. This is not saddle avoidance from the exact isotropic initialization.

Let C be positive semidefinite, P its range projector, N=I-P, T=d[I,0], E=vAB-T, and L=tr(ECE^T)/2. Suppose (A,B,v) is a positive-loss critical point of the C07 flow with v>0 and

BB^T-A^TA=alpha^2 ee^T, v^2=||A||_F^2, BN=alpha N.

Then there is a smooth two-sided curve through the point preserving all three identities exactly, with zero first derivative of loss and strictly negative second derivative.

Proof. Criticality gives A^T EC=0 and EC B^T=0. Choose a unit right singular vector b of EC for a positive singular value sigma, with associated left singular vector l. Let a=-l, so a^T EC b=-sigma. The two criticality identities imply A^T a=0 and Bb=0. Also b lies in range C, so b^T N=0. The proof of C11 gives a unit u in ker A intersect e-perp, and hence B^T u=0.

Define

A(t)=A+t a u^T, B(t)=B+t u b^T, v(t)=sqrt(v^2+t^2).

All square roots are taken positive. Since a,b,u are unit, the quadratic terms in B(t)B(t)^T-A(t)^TA(t) cancel. Its linear terms vanish because Bb=0 and A^Ta=0. Further ||A(t)||^2=||A||^2+t^2, and B(t)N=BN, proving exact preservation. Because Au=0 and u^TB=0,

A(t)B(t)=AB+t^2 a b^T.

At t=0 the first derivative of v(t)AB(t) is zero. Its second derivative is AB/v+2v a b^T. Scalar criticality gives <AB,EC>=0, so

L''(0)=<AB/v+2v a b^T,EC>=-2v sigma<0.

This proves the curve claim without treating the invariant level set as a smooth manifold at a rank-deficient point.

## Why it still does not prove avoidance

Even a descending curve inside an invariant level set does not imply that every trajectory on that set avoids the critical point. A concrete scalar example is f(a,b)=(ab-1)^2/2, with invariant b^2-a^2=0. The curve a=b=t descends from the critical origin. Nevertheless the other branch a=-b has gradient-flow solutions a'=-a(1+a^2) converging to the origin from every nonzero point on that branch. The origin is an ambient strict saddle and a saddle on the invariant set. These starts have loss above the zero predictor, so this example refutes the implication from invariant-set descent alone; it does not satisfy or refute C07's strict initial-loss gap. C11 separately supplies a positive-loss point below that gap but does not prove reachability.

Known background: Bah et al., 1910.05505v5, Theorem 28 printed p.14 gives ambient almost-everywhere avoidance, not avoidance at a specified initialization or on every invariant branch. No new general landscape theorem is claimed.

[Definition 20 of arXiv:2608.25785, 'Proper Actions on Homogeneous Spaces of the Upper Triangular Matrix Group via Coarse Geome'] Let $(S,\mathcal{E})$ and $(T,\mathcal{F})$ be coarse spaces.
A map $f : S \rightarrow T$ is called: 
\begin{enumerate}
    \item \emph{controlled} (cf.~\cite{BunkeEngel2020}) if, for each $E\in \mathcal{E}$, 
    \[
    \Ad_f(E) = \{ (f(x_1),f(x_2)) \mid (x_1,x_2) \in E \} \subset T \times T
    \]
    is an entourage on $T$, 
    \item  \emph{coarsely proper} (cf.~\cite{LeitnerVigolo2023}) if the set $f^\dagger[D]=f^{-1}(D)$ is bounded in $S$ for any bounded subset $D$ of $T$,  
    \item \emph{coarse} (cf.~\cite{Roe2003LectureCoarse}) if it is controlled and coarsely proper,
    \item  \emph{effectively proper} (cf.~\cite{DikranjanZavaCatCoarseGp2020}) if, for any $F\in \mathcal{F}$, the relation 
    \[
    \Ad_{f^\dagger}F = \{ (p,q) \mid (f(p),f(q)) \in F \} \subset S \times S
    \]
    is also an entourage on $S$,
    \item   \emph{a coarse embedding} (cf.~\cite{DikranjanZavaCatCoarseGp2020}) if $f$ is controlled and effectively proper,
    \item  \emph{coarsely surjective} (cf.~\cite{LeitnerVigolo2023}) if there exists $F\in \mathcal{F}$ such that $F[f(S)] = T$,
    \item  \emph{a coarse equivalence} (cf.~\cite{DikranjanZava2017}) if $f$ is controlled and there exists a controlled map $h: T\to S$ such that $h\circ f\sim \id_S$ and $f\circ h\sim \id_T$.
\end{enumerate}

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:56672755211c4fbbd2ae9814363ba78634eb2be478e4e4e12742caac9ee2502e","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/56/56672755211c4fbbd2ae9814363ba78634eb2be478e4e4e12742caac9ee2502e.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:01206d6ebf0d8659f42bf613a2f917d326ca1cbcacd37d248ec55d046cb75c7a","bundle_entry_key":"i0005-c1","bundle_id":"population.i0005-four-dimensional-parking-partials-002","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"interacting particle systems and random-walk potential theory","draft":"w661/bundle_002.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.particle-hole:i0005-c1-draft","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# I0005-C1 v1: the four-dimensional cutoff convolution

Novelty: KNOWN. This is a standard local-central-limit consequence, rederived here to fix the coefficient and the obstruction in Bou-Rabee–Panagiotis (2026), equation (46). Primary reference: Lawler–Limic, *Random Walk: A Modern Introduction*, Chapter 2 (local CLT). No novelty claim is made. Audit status: unaudited.

Let X be discrete-time nearest-neighbor simple random walk on Z^4, with each of the eight steps equally likely. Put p_n(x)=P_0(X_n=x), and

K_N(x)=sum_{n=0}^N (n+1)p_n(x).

There is an absolute constant C such that, for every integer N≥1 and every x in Z^4,

|K_N(x) − (4/π²) log_+(N/(1+|x|_2²))| ≤ C.

In particular, for fixed x, K_N(x)=(4/π²)log N+O_x(1), and the infinite Green convolution is infinite at every separation. The covariance normalization is Cov(X_1)=I/4; replacing it or making the walk lazy changes the coefficient.

## 1. Uniform periodic local CLT, including its error

The characteristic function is φ(θ)=(1/4)sum_{j=1}^4 cos θ_j on the torus [-π,π]^4. Fourier inversion gives

p_n(x)=(2π)^−4 integral e^{−iθ·x} φ(θ)^n dθ.

The only torus points where |φ|=1 are 0 and a=(π,π,π,π), identified periodically at the corners. Choose disjoint small torus neighborhoods of these points. On their complement |φ|≤ρ<1 by compactness. Near zero,

φ(θ)=1−|θ|²/8+O(|θ|⁴),
log φ(θ)=−|θ|²/8+O(|θ|⁴).

The neighborhoods can be chosen so the real quadratic decay dominates the remainder. The inequality |e^u−e^v|≤|u−v|exp(max(u,v)) for real u,v then gives

|φ(θ)^n−exp(−n|θ|²/8)|≤Cn|θ|⁴ exp(−cn|θ|²).

Its integral is at most Cn·n^−4=Cn^−3 (dimension four). Extending the Gaussian integral from the neighborhood to R^4 adds an exponentially small error. The factor e^{−iθ·x} has modulus one, so all errors are uniform in x. The Gaussian Fourier integral is

(2π)^−4 integral_{R^4} e^{−iθ·x}e^{−n|θ|²/8}dθ
= (4/(π² n²))exp(−2|x|²/n).

Under the torus shift θ↦θ+a, φ changes sign and the Fourier phase gains (−1)^{sum_j x_j}. Thus the second neighborhood contributes (−1)^{n+sum_j x_j} times the first. Consequently, for n≥1,

p_n(x)=1_{n≡sum_j x_j mod 2} (8/(π²n²))exp(−2|x|²/n)+O(n^−3),

uniformly in x. The forbidden parity is actually zero, since every step changes the parity of the coordinate sum. Finitely many small n are absorbed into the uniform constant.

## 2. Summation and parity

Writing r²=|x|², the accumulated error from (n+1)O(n^−3) is bounded by an absolute constant. Replacing (n+1)/n² by 1/n costs at most Csum n^−2, also bounded. The n=0 term is at most one. Hence

K_N(x)=(8/π²)sum_{1≤n≤N, n≡sum x_j mod 2} e^{−2r²/n}/n + O(1).

For f(s)=e^{−2r²/s}/s, the difference between either parity sum and half the full sum is uniformly bounded. Indeed, it is half an alternating sum. For r=0, f decreases and the alternating sum is bounded by f(1)=1. For r>0, f increases up to s=2r² and decreases thereafter, with sup f≤1, so its total variation on [1,N] is at most two. Summation by parts with bounded partial sums of (−1)^n bounds the alternating sum by sup f plus total variation. Therefore

K_N(x)=(4/π²)sum_{n=1}^N e^{−2r²/n}/n+O(1).

If r=0, this is the harmonic sum log N+O(1). If r²≥1 and N≥r², the sum below r² is bounded uniformly: sum–integral comparison for a unimodal function reduces it to integral_1^{r²}e^{−2r²/s}ds/s, which is bounded after u=r²/s. Above r², replacing the exponential by one costs at most 2r² sum_{n≥r²}n^−2=O(1). The remaining harmonic sum is log(N/r²)+O(1). Replacing r² by 1+r² changes this by at most log 2. If N<r², the same integral bound and bounded unimodal sum–integral error show the whole sum is O(1), while log_+(N/(1+r²))=0. This proves the asserted uniform formula.

## 3. Relation to equation (46)

Let G(y)=sum_{j≥0}p_j(y), finite in dimension four. By symmetry, Chapman–Kolmogorov and Tonelli,

sum_y G(y)G(y−x)
=sum_{j,k≥0}sum_y p_j(y)p_k(y−x)
=sum_{j,k≥0}p_{j+k}(x)
=sum_{n≥0}(n+1)p_n(x)=∞.

Every interchange is valid for nonnegative terms; the last equality is an equality in [0,∞]. Thus even widely separated targets do not admit the finite infinite-time kernel used in the source's bounded-differences and two-hole proofs. The cutoff formula is a diagnostic, not an extension of that proof: a finite-time or killed-walk replacement would have to be justified separately.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:a717cab0408ba62fa14a8ae11b44e2c6621727ffa391b3ed98fd0857f08973f1","revision_digest":"sha256:4c75fbde3dec791808b1267fc45c59dfdea234297cafb825c4589175a4768e92","source_id":"own-work:w661:I0005-C1:v1","source_revision":"v1; 2026-10-14T05:23:59.4615090+03:00","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

    \begin{proof}
        Note that for a two-card deck, $p_{i,j}=1/2$ for all $i,j$, so any strategy is best. If $n\geq 3$, we notice that $p_{1,1}=p_{1,n}=1/2$ by direct computation or because card $1$ is drawn last, so it must go to the top or the bottom of the shuffled deck. Using Proposition $(doubly stochastic of the paper)$, we have that the column sums of $M$ are $1$. Furthermore, one can verify that there exists an $i\neq 1$ such that $p_{i,1}>0$. Therefore $p_{i,n}>0$ for that same $i$ by Proposition $(guessing strategy symmetry of the paper)$. The pigeonhole principle then implies the result.
    \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem thm:complete-inverse of arXiv:2607.24018, 'Jeu de taquin forests \\ and the inverse infinite RSK correspondence'] Let $T$ be a Plan\-che\-rel-distributed random IYT, and
	let $(z_1,z_2,\ldots) = \RSK^{-1}(T)$ be the associated sequence of i.i.d.
	$U(0,1)$-distributed random variables. Then, almost
	surely, the lifetime map $\tau \mapsto n(\tau)$ is a
	bijection between the set of trees of $\Phi(T)$ and
	the positive integers $\mathbb{N}$, and the numbers $z_n$ are given by
	\[
		z_n = \alpha_\textnormal{asym}(\tau_n) \qquad (n\ge1),
	\]
	where $\tau_n$ denotes the unique tree with lifetime
	$n(\tau_n) = n$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Complete inverse of the RSK map via lifetimes

body:
Let U ⊂ C be a nonempty, open, simply connected set with U ≠ C (equivalently: U is open and connected, its complement in the Riemann sphere is connected, and U is not all of C). Then there exists a biholomorphic map F from U onto the open unit disk D (holomorphic, bijective, with holomorphic inverse). Given any point z0 in U, there is exactly one such F with F(z0) = 0 and F'(z0) > 0. Consequently any two simply connected proper open subsets of C are conformally equivalent. The theorem says nothing about boundary behaviour: for that one needs Carathéodory's theorem (if U is bounded by a Jordan curve, F extends to a homeomorphism of the closures).

Unreviewed finite counterexample, awaiting w542. For 0<h<1, let U,V in {-1,1} have joint law P(U=u,V=v)=(1+h u v)/4. Set A0=B0=U, Ar=V and Br=(V-hU)/(1+h). All are centered and bounded by one. Then E[A0 Ar]=h, E[B0 Br]=0, ||B0-A0||2=0 and ||Br-Ar||2^2=2h^2/(1+h). Thus an unspecified L2 error O(h) does not preserve a positive lower correlation bound of order h. For centered reference observables of L2 norm at most M and both observable errors at most delta, expansion and Cauchy-Schwarz give a correlation error at most 2M delta+delta^2. A sufficiently small explicit relative constant or o(h) can preserve the leading correlation; the example does not challenge such hypotheses. This is a finite transfer obstruction, not a constructed Riesz Gibbs state.

[Proposition 19 of arXiv:2609.01574, 'A linear bound for Fujita's freeness conjecture'] Let $c$ be a positive integer and let $a\geq0$. Let $h_0,h_1,\ldots$ be a finitely supported sequence of nonnegative real numbers such that
$h_k\leq\binom{c+k-1}{k}$, $k\geq0$, and $\sum_{k\geq1}kh_k
 \leq a\sum_{k\geq0}h_k$. Then
$$ \sum_{k\geq0}h_k
 \leq\frac{(a+c)^{a+c}}{a^ac^c}.$$

Method: Moment expansion with a crude operator-norm bound Result: For every finite random graph matrix, E||M|| <= (E||M||_F^2)^(1/2). Expanding each entry as a sum of Rademacher edge monomials, cross terms vanish unless the two monomials use every edge with even combined multiplicity. For a fixed shape the remaining label identifications can be counted to obtain a polynomial upper bound in n. Check: Orthogonality concerns equality of edge monomials, not equality of vertex labelings. Distinct labelings can produce the same edge set and must not be discarded. Obstruction: The Frobenius bound can lose powers of n and cannot decide the sharp operator norm or the existence of one power-log asymptotic form.

[Lemma lem:c4-sparse-overlap of arXiv:2607.05384, 'Well-invertible column subsets of sparse matrices are rare'] Let $G=(I,J,M)$ be $C_4$-free with $|I|=k$, $|J|=n\ge2$, and every right degree between $2$ and $d$. Then
\[
\eta(G)\le 2d\,\frac{k}{n}.
\]

Consequently, if $d$ is fixed and $G^{(k)}$ is a sequence of such graphs with $n_k/k\to\infty$, then $\eta(G^{(k)})=o(1)$.

Then, the following statements hold.\\
{\normalfont(a)} For any $x>0$ and $c\geqslant 0$, we have $(c+\ell_n(xt))/(c+\ell_n(t)) \leqslant 1+\1_{\{x>1\}}\log x$.\\
{\normalfont(b)} We have $(e+t)\ell_n'(t)=\prod_{i=1}^{n-1}(e+\ell_k(t))^{-1}$.\\
{\normalfont(c)} Suppose $\ell(t)=\ell_n(t)^{q_n}\cdots\ell_m(t)^{q_m}$ for some $1\leqslant n\leqslant m$ in $\mathbb{N}$ and either $q_n,\ldots,q_m\geqslant 0$ with $q_n,q_m>0$ or $q_n,\ldots,q_m\leqslant 0$ with $q_n,q_m<0$. Set $\wt\ell(t)\coloneqq (e+t)\ell'(t)$, then we have
\[
\Sigma(x)
\coloneqq
\sup_{t>0,\,y\in [x\wedge 1,x\vee1]}\frac{\wt\ell(yt)}{\wt\ell(t)}
\leqslant\begin{cases}
(1+\log x)^{\sum_{j=n}^m q_j^+},
& x\geqslant 1,\\
(1+|\log x|)^{m+\sum_{j=n}^mq_j^-},

\]

body: Publication record. Y. Shmalo, A Brownian piece in front of a process absolutely continuous with respect to Brownian motion (2026). Burdzy and Scheutzow (Forward Brownian motion, Probab. Theory Related Fields 160 (2014), Problem 7.5) asked whether, for every process X whose law is equivalent to Wiener measure, a random piece of path can be put in front of X so that the new process is a Brownian motion. The paper proves that absolute continuity with respect to Wiener measure is enough: on an extension of the probability space there are a standard Brownian motion B and an almost surely finite random integer N >= 0 with X_t = B_{N+t} - B_N for all t >= 0; N cannot in general be a stopping time for B. More generally, for an invertible measure-preserving map theta of (E, P) and a target law fP, a forward shift theta^N with N built from a P-distributed point and independent uniforms carries P to fP if and only if E[f | I] = 1, I the invariant sigma-field; without the auxiliary uniforms only integer-valued densities can be reached. The construction is Rost's filling scheme (Chacon-Ornstein, Rost 1971) for the unit shift of two-sided Brownian motion. Paper and code: https://github.com/yspennstate/brownian-prefix-filling (commit eb410953a445). Not refereed.
title: A Brownian piece in front of a process absolutely continuous with respect to Brownian motion, answering Burdzy-Scheutzow Problem 7.5 via Rost's filling scheme (Shmalo 2026, repository yspennstate/brownian-prefix-filling)

[Proposition 17 (Phases of the burglars) of arXiv:2609.03968, 'A one-parameter family of local-time conditioned processes : the generalized Brownian burg'] The burglar $X$ behaves in the following way depending on the parameter $\nu$ :

- For $\nu \geq 1 $, $X$ does not hit full local time anywhere else than its target, i.e.\ $L_X(T(X),x)<\lambda_0(x)$ for all $x\in I\setminus\{x_0\}$ almost surely.

- For $\nu \in (0,1)$, for any deterministic $x\in I\setminus\{x_0\}$, $L_X(T(X),x)<\lambda_0(x)$ almost surely, but there almost surely exists exceptional $x\in I\setminus\{x_0\}$ such that $L_X(T(X),x)=\lambda_0(x)$. 

- For $\nu \leq  0$, $X$ is ``local-time-filling", i.e.\ for all $x\in I$, $L_X(T(X),x)=\lambda_0(x)$ almost surely.

body: The Nyquist–Shannon sampling theorem is a theorem in the field of signal processing which serves as a fundamental bridge between continuous-time signals and discrete-time signals. In the case of uniformly spaced (periodic) sampling, it establishes a sufficient condition on the sample rate that permits a discrete sequence of samples to capture all the information from a continuous-time signal of finite bandwidth, such that the original signal can be reconstructed exactly from those samples.
title: Nyquist–Shannon sampling theorem

Let f:R^(d by d)->R be C3, convex and transpose-invariant, and L(U)=f(UU^T)/2 on U in R^(d by r), 1<=r<=d. If U_0 is a second-order stationary point of L, then either rank(U_0)=r or W_0=U_0 U_0^T globally minimizes f over all real positive-semidefinite d-by-d matrices. This is an unconstrained factorized convex-loss result; no matrix sensing RIP or sample-size hypothesis is required.

[Corollary 52 (Parallel tempering converges) of arXiv:2608.03353, '\bfseries A Direct Route to Markov Chain Convergence\\[2mm] \Large via Asymptotic Equivale'] Let $\mathcal{Y},\lambda_{0},K,p_{k},\pi_{k}$ and $\XX,\XXA,\lambda,\pi$ be as above,
let $R_{1},\dots,R_{K}$ satisfy the hypotheses stated there including
\eqref{eq:temperingtheta}, let $\mathcal{S} \ne \emptyset$ and
$\omega \in [0,1)$, and let $T$ be the parallel tempering kernel. Then $\pi$ is the
unique invariant probability measure of $T$ and
\[
  \lim_{n\to\infty}\ \sup_{A \in \XXA}\bigl| (T^{n}\circ\mu)(A) - \pi(A) \bigr| = 0
  \qquad\text{for every } \mu \in \Prob .
\]
More precisely, with $c := (1-\omega)(\theta^{-})^{K} \in (0,1]$,
\[
  \sing\bigl( T^{n}\circ\mu \bigm| \pi\bigr) \;\le\; (1-c)^{n}
  \qquad (\mu \in \Prob,\ n \in \Nz) .
\]

For a uniform-root three-state calibrated observation law invariant under all coordinate permutations, barycentrically split each posterior onto a simplex grid of denominator N divisible by3. Round each whole orbit mass down to a multiple of1/S, S=2^b, and replace removed mass by uniform root revelation. The resulting experiment Blackwell-dominates the original. Applying a physical ferromagnetic edge once, then independently fusing fresh child experiments and upgrading after each binary combination, gives a finite-depth upper experiment on a regular d-child broadcast tree. Its expected squared posterior distance from uniform bounds the canonical signal. Zero-likelihood pairs are excluded before normalization; reused laws denote fresh conditional-root observations.
Uniform prior on three states
Permutation-invariant calibrated posterior laws
Fresh observations independent conditional on root
Exact nonnegative barycentric and orbit-mass arithmetic

Historical source result, superseded as a convergence-rate frontier by arXiv:2606.29593v1 Theorem 3.1. Let M_t be independent symmetric random matrices on a finite-dimensional real Euclidean space, 0<=M_t<=I and E M_t=Q for every t, and let delta_(t+1)=(I-M_t)delta_t, with independent square-integrable initial delta_0. Define N_0=Q and N_(t+1)=N_t(I-2Q)+||N_t||Q. Then E[delta_t^T Q delta_t]<=E[delta_0^T N_t delta_0] for all t>=0. Each N_t is positive semidefinite and commutes with Q. The norm is the spectral norm. This source result does not assert inverse-time convergence for arbitrary Q.

[Defi Def:W-homotopy-Equiv of arXiv:2608.29013, 'Weighted Homology and Cohomology of Weighted Polyhedra'] Let $(X,\lambda)$ and $(X',\lambda')$ be 
    weighted polyhedra of the same type and
       $f, g: (X,\lambda)\rightarrow (X',\lambda')$ be two  
     W-continuous maps. A \emph{W-homotopy} from $f$ to $g$ relative
to $A\subseteq X$ is a W-continuous map
$$H : (X \times [0, 1],\lambda\times \mathbf{1}) \rightarrow (X',\lambda')$$ which satisfies:
 \begin{itemize}
   \item $H(x, 0) =f(x)$ and $H(x,1)=g(x)$ for all $x\in X$;\vskip 0.1cm
   \item $H(a,t)=f(a)=g(a)$ for all $a\in A$ and 
   $t\in [0,1]$.\vskip 0.1cm
   \end{itemize}
   
   Here $([0,1],\mathbf{1})$ is considered as a weighted polyhedron, and $(X\times [0,1],\lambda\times \mathbf{1})$ is the product $(X,\lambda)$ with
   $([0,1],\mathbf{1})$.
   \vskip 0.1cm
   If there exists a W-homotopy from $f$ to $g$,
   we say that $f$ is \emph{W-homotopic to} $g$.
   If moreover $H$ is weight-preserving, we say
   that $f$ is \emph{strongly W-homotopic to} $g$ (a priori $f$ and $g$ must be both weight-preserving).
title: W-Homotopy

[Lemma lem:bound_asymptotics of arXiv:2604.09509, 'An Improved Bipartition Cover Bound for the Multispecies Coalescent Model'] Let $\kappa_{q,k} := \log((k-3)/(1-q))$ and $u(T) := \frac{2-\exp(-T/2)}{1-\exp(-T/2)}$. Then
    
    \[M_o(k,T)  \sim \begin{cases}
    \frac{\kappa_{q,k}}{T}, & T \uparrow \infty, \\
    \frac{2^{k-3}\kappa_{q,k}}{(k-2)! T^{k-3}}, & T = o(k^{-2}), \\
    \frac{\kappa_{q,k}}{-\log(1-s(T))}, & T \text{ fixed}, k \to \infty
\end{cases}\]

    \[M_b(k,T) \lesssim 
        \frac{\kappa_{q,k}}{-\log(1-g_{u(T), 1}(T))}, \qquad T \text{ fixed}, k \to \infty\]

    \noindent Moreover, in the fixed $T$ regime, the improvement factor satisfies
    
    \[
    \liminf_{k\to\infty}\frac{M_o(k,T)}{M_b(k,T)}
    \geqslant \beta_T
    :=\frac{\log(1-g_{u(T),1}(T))}{\log(1-s(T))},
    \qquad
    \beta_T\sim \frac{\pi^2}{2T}
    \quad\text{as }T\downarrow0.
    \] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Bound Asymptotics

body:
[Definition 12 of arXiv:2606.31455, 'Discrete time-multidimensional renewal theory and applications'] Let $U\subseteq\{1,\ldots,d\}$ be a nonempty index set with $|U|=m$ and let
$\pi_U:\mathbb{N}^d\to\mathbb{N}^m$ be the coordinate projection.
Define the projected increments $X_n^{[U]}:=\pi_U(X_n)$.
Then $(X_n^{[U]})_{n\ge 1}$ is an i.i.d.\ sequence on $\mathbb{N}^m$ with pmf

\begin{equation}
f^{[U]}(k_U):=\mathbb{P}(X_1^{[U]}=k_U),
\qquad k_U\in\mathbb{N}^m.
\end{equation}

Assume $f^{[U]}(0_m)<1$ (non-degeneracy in the projected coordinates), and define the
projected renewal chain and counting process by

\begin{equation}
S_0^{[U]}=0_m,
\qquad
S_n^{[U]}=\sum_{i=1}^n X_i^{[U]},
\qquad n\ge 1,
\end{equation}

and

\begin{equation}
N^{[U]}(k_U):=\sup\{n\in\mathbb{N}: S_n^{[U]}\le_m k_U\},
\qquad k_U\in\mathbb{N}^m,
\end{equation}

where $\le_m$ denotes componentwise order in $\mathbb{N}^m$.
Its renewal function is

\begin{equation*}
M^{[U]}(k_U):=\mathbb{E}[N^{[U]}(k_U)].
\end{equation*}

\smallskip
\noindent
In particular, for $U=\{u\}$ one recovers the univariate marginal renewal process
$S_n^{[u]}=\sum_{i=1}^n X_i^{[u]}$ and the marginal counting process

$N^{[u]}(k_u)=\sup\{n:S_n^{[u]}\le k_u\}$.
title: Definition 12 of arXiv:2606.31455

[Cor blowup of arXiv:2608.30847, 'An Almgren-type formula for planar $p$-harmonic functions'] Let $u$, $x_0$, and $\lambda=N_*(x_0,0+)$ be as in Theorem (thm:main of the paper).  If $u$ is not locally constant near $x_0$, then there exists a nonzero homogeneous $p$-harmonic function $P$ of degree $\lambda$ such that
$$
  \frac{u(x_0+r\,\cdot)-u(x_0)}{r^\lambda}
  \longrightarrow P
$$
locally uniformly and in $C^1$ on compact subsets of $\mathbb R^2\setminus\{0\}$ as $r\to0$.

[Lemma lem:volterra of arXiv:2607.20956, 'Sharp moduli of continuity for Gaussian fields and stochastic PDEs via correlation bounds'] Under Assumption (a:kappa of the paper), we have:
\begin{enumerate}[$(i)$]
    \item $\phi(|t-s|) \le \|X(t)-X(s)\|_2 \le \sqrt{2}\, \phi(|t-s|)$ uniformly for all $t,s \in [0\,,T]$; and\smallskip
    \item One-sided SLND:
    \[
        \Var(X(t)|X(t_1),\dots, X(t_n)) \ge \phi^2(t-t_n) \ge \tfrac12 \Var(X(t)-X(t_n))
    \]
    uniformly for all $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and $0 \le t_1 < \cdots < t_n \le t \le T$.
\end{enumerate}
title: Lemma lem:volterra of arXiv:2607.20956

body: [Proposition 3.9 of arXiv:2304.14793, 'Learning Graph Neural Networks using Exact Compression'] There is a single 𝑑-reduct of a graph 𝐺up to isomorphism if and only if 𝑑is greater than or equal to the stable coloring number of 𝐺. A direct consequence of having different non-isomorphic reducts when𝑑is less than the coloring number is that some of these reducts may be smaller than others. In Example 3.7, 𝐺/𝜌1 has 3 nodes and 4 edges while 𝐺/𝜌2 has 3 nodes and only 3 edges.
title: Proposition 3.9 of arXiv:2304.14793: Learning Graph Neural Networks using Exact Compression

body:
[Theorem 25 of arXiv:2609.02878, '2609.02878'] Let \(\xi=(\mu_t)_{t<T}\) be a fixed limiting point of a compact
finite-time K\"ahler--Ricci flow of complex dimension \(n\ge2\), and
let \((Z,d,\cR,g,J,f,\mathfrak m)\) be the time-\((-1)\) model of a
tangent space at \(\xi\).  Thus \(Z\) has
the finite-time tangent-space package of
\cref{sp:prop:limiting-package}: it is the intrinsic completion
of its K\"ahler regular locus, is normal and klt, carries the normalized
shrinker measure and complete soliton flow, and has smooth
metric--complex--density convergence and the local ambient metric lower
bound.  Let \(A\) be the nonnegative
self-adjoint operator associated with the closure of
\[
 \cE_0(\phi,\psi)=
 \int_{\cR}\langle\nabla\phi,\nabla\overline\psi\rangle\,d\mathfrak m,
 \qquad \phi,\psi\in C_c^\infty(\cR).
\]
Then
\begin{equation}
                     \sigma(A)\subset\{0\}\cup[1/2,\infty),
                     \qquad\ker A=\C1.
\end{equation}
If \(u:Z\to\C\) is holomorphic and globally \(d\)-Lipschitz, then
\(u\in L^2(Z,\mathfrak m)\), and
\begin{equation}
 A\left(u-\int_Zu\,d\mathfrak m\right)
 =\frac12\left(u-\int_Zu\,d\mathfrak m\right),

and
\begin{equation}
          \nabla^2\Re u=\nabla^2\Im u=0\qquad\text{on }\cR.
\end{equation}

essential-self-adjointness assertion is made for the minimal operator on
the incomplete regular locus. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 159 (The key top-order integration by parts in $\Lunit$ identity tied to the acoustic geometry) of arXiv:2609.03101, 'The emergence of the Cauchy horizon from the crease for $3D$ compressible Euler flow'] Let $N = \Ntop$, $(\ubar,u) \in [\leftubar,\ubarboot)\times[\moreinterestingu_1,\moreinterestingu_2]$,
	and let $\varphi$ and $\upeta$ be scalar functions on $\characteristicdiamondtwoarg{[\leftubar,\ubar)}{[\moreinterestingu_1,u]}$. Let $ \tander^N \in \mathfrak{P}^{(N)}$, where $\mathfrak{P}^{(N)}$ denotes the set of top-order commutator operators from Def.\,\ref{D:STRINGSOFCOMMUTATIONVECTORFIELDS}.
	Then the following integration by parts identity holds:
	\begin{align}
		\begin{split} 
			&
			\int_{\characteristicdiamondtwoarg{[\leftubar,\ubar)}{[\moreinterestingu_1,u]}}
			 (\muX \varphi) 
			(\Lunit  \tander^N \varphi) 
			\Yvf{A} \upeta \, \weight^{\blowupratetoporderwave} \ReciprocalLunitAppliedtoTimeFunction
			\, \voldiamond 
			\\
			& 
			= 
			\int_{\characteristicdiamondtwoarg{[\leftubar,\ubar)}{[\moreinterestingu_1,u]}}  
			(\muX \varphi) 
			(\Yvf{A} \tander^N \varphi) 
			\Lunit \upeta \, \weight^{\blowupratetoporderwave} \ReciprocalLunitAppliedtoTimeFunction
			\, \voldiamond \\
			& \ \
			- \int_{\ingoingcharacteristicsurfacetwoarg{\ubar}{[\moreinterestingu_1,u]}} 
			( \muX \varphi) \left\{ \frac{1}{\Speed^2} (\gtorus^{-1})^{AB} \gtorusdoublenullCOV_B^C \nullgeop{x^C}\tander^N \varphi \right\} \upeta \, \weight^{\blowupratetoporderwave}
			\, \volingoingnullhypersurface 
			\\
			&  \ \ 
			+ 
			\int_{\ingoingcharacteristicsurfacetwoarg{\leftubar}{[\moreinterestingu_1,u]}} 
			(\muX \varphi) \left\{ \frac{1}{\Speed^2} (\gtorus^{-1})^{AB} \gtorusdoublenullCOV_B^C \nullgeop{x^C} \tander^N  \varphi \right\} \upeta \, \weight^{\blowupratetoporderwave}
			\, \volingoingnullhypersurface 
			\\
			& \ \ 
			+ 
			\int_{\characteristicdiamondtwoarg{[\leftubar,\ubar)}{[\moreinterestingu_1,u]}}
			\left\{ \ErrorIBP_1^{AG;L}[\tander^N \varphi;\upeta;\Yvf{A}]+ \ErrorIBP_2^{AG;L}[\tander^N \varphi;\upeta;\Yvf{A}]  \right\}\ReciprocalLunitAppliedtoTimeFunction
			\, \voldiamond,
		\end{split}
	\end{align} 
	where:  
	\begin{align} 
		\begin{split} 
			\ErrorIBP_1^{AG;L}[\tander^N \varphi;\upeta;\Yvf{A}]
			&  
			\eqdef  \weight^{\blowupratetoporderwave} \Big\{
			(\muX \varphi) 
			([\Lunit, \Yvf{A}] \tander^N \varphi) 
			\upeta  
			\\
			& \ \
			+ 
			(\Lunit \muX \varphi) 
			(\Yvf{A} \tander^N \varphi)
			\upeta 
			- 
			(\Yvf{A} \muX \varphi) 
			(\Lunit \tander^N \varphi)
			\upeta  \\
			& \ \ 
			\left. - \frac{1}{2} (\muX \varphi) (\Lunit \tander^N \varphi)\upeta \mytr_{\gtorus} \, \angdeform{\Yvf{A}} +  (\muX \varphi) (\Yvf{A} \tander^N \varphi )\upeta \mytr_{\gtorus} \upchi \right\} ,
		\end{split} \\
		\begin{split}
			\ErrorIBP_2^{AG;L}[\tander^N \varphi;\upeta;\Yvf{A}] & \eqdef - \blowupratetoporderwave \, \weight^{\blowupratetoporderwave - 1} (\Yvf{A} \weight)(\muX \varphi) (\Lunit \tander^N \varphi) \upeta  \\
			& \ \  +  \blowupratetoporderwave \, \weight^{\blowupratetoporderwave - 1} (\newL  \weight) (\muX \varphi) (\Yvf{A} \tander^N \varphi) \upeta 
		\end{split}
	\end{align}

[Question of arXiv:2605.02226, 'Finitely Dependent Processes on Subshifts'] \begin{enumerate}
\item A $d-$dimensional domino is a $ d$-dimensional box whose one side has length $2$ and all other sides have length 1 with its vertices in $\mathbb{Z}^d$. Does there exist a strongly irreducible subshift contained in the space of domino tilings of $\mathbb{R}^d$ for $d\geq 3$?
    \item In general, is there a natural characterization of the set of boxes $\mathcal{R}$ for which the space of tilings of $\mathbb{R}^d$ by the boxes in $\mathcal{R}$ contains a strongly irreducible subshift?
    
    We know that if the collection $ \mathcal{R}$ satisfies the condition of (thm:eventuallyuniversaltiles of the paper), then there exists a shift-invariant finitely dependent process on the tiling space $X(\mathcal{R})$. However, if $ p_1, p_2, \cdots, p_d$ are prime numbers and $ \mathcal{R} = \{ R_1, R_2, \cdots, R_d\}$ is a collection of bars where $ R_i$ is a bar whose sidelength in $ e_i$ direction is $ p_i$, then does $ X(\mathcal{R})$ contain a strongly irreducible subshift?
    \end{enumerate} (Stated as a question by the paper; open unless the paper says otherwise.)
title: Unnumbered question of arXiv:2605.02226, 'Finitely Dependent Processes on Subshifts'

body:
[Thm DRC of arXiv:2602.06011, 'Excursion decomposition of the XOR-Ising model'] Let $D$ be a Jordan domain and $D_\delta$ be as above. For the (critical) coupling $\mathbb P_\delta$, 
    \begin{equation}
        (h_\delta, \hat\mathbf{n}_\delta, \hat\mathbf{n}_\delta^\dagger, c_\delta, c_\delta^\dagger, \xi_\delta, \xi^\dagger_\delta) \overset{(d)}{\longrightarrow} (\frac{1}{2\sqrt{2}\lambda}\ h, \hat\mathbf{n}, \hat\mathbf{n}^\dagger, c, c^\dagger, \xi, \xi^\dagger),
    \end{equation}
    where
    \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
        \item h is a GFF with zero boundary conditions in $D$, 
        \item The inner boundaries of the boundary cluster of $\hat\mathbf{n}_\delta$ converge to $\mathcal L_{-\sqrt{2}\lambda, \sqrt{2}\lambda}$. The label $c(\ell)$ of an inner boundary $\ell$ is such that the boundary values of $h$ in $\mathcal O(\ell)$ are $c(\ell)\sqrt{2}\lambda$.
        \item The outer boundaries of the outermost clusters of $\hat\mathbf{n}^\dagger_\delta$ converge to $\mathcal L_{-2\lambda, 2\lambda}$. The sign $\xi^\dagger(\gamma)$ of an outer boundary $\gamma$ is such that the boundary values of $h$ in $\mathcal O(\gamma)$ are $\xi^\dagger(\gamma)2\lambda$. Moreover, the inner boundaries of the cluster corresponding to $\gamma$ converge to
        \begin{enumerate}
            \item [(iii.a)] $\mathcal L_{-2\lambda, (2\sqrt{2}-2)\lambda}$ if $\xi^\dagger(\gamma)=+1$,
            \item [(iii.b)] $\mathcal L_{-(2\sqrt{2}-2)\lambda, 2\lambda}$ if $\xi^\dagger(\gamma)=-1$,
            \item [(iii.c)] where the label $c^\dagger(\ell)$ of an inner boundary $\ell$ is such that the boundary values of $h$ in $\mathcal O(\ell)$ are $\xi(\gamma)(c(\ell)+1)\sqrt{2}\lambda$. 
        \end{enumerate}
        \item The structure repeats iteratively by applying the Markov property (MP-free of the paper) of Theorem (thm:master of the paper), which gives the nesting of two-valued sets described in Section (sec:decomp of the paper).
    \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Thm DRC of arXiv:2602.06011

[Theorem 6 (the inverse problem) of arXiv:2608.30138, 'High-frequency wave propagation for the viscoelastic wave equation with singular memory'] Let $0<p<1$. 
For every $\omega\in \S^{n-1}$, let $\chi\in C_0^\infty(\Omega)$ satisfy $\supp\chi\cap\overline{B(0,R)}=\emptyset$. Let $T>0$ be such that every point of $\overline{B(0,R)}$ lies on a ray $z+t\omega$, with $z\in\{\chi\ne0\}$ and $0<t<T$, and every such ray has exited $\overline{B(0,R)}$ by time $T$. Assume that $\Omega$ contains all the relevant incoming and outgoing ray segments up to time $T$. Then the family of corresponding solutions $u$ of \r{1b}, \r{IC1}, restricted to $[0,T]\times(\Omega\setminus B(0,R))$, for a fixed $\lambda$ in \r{lambda} and all $0<h\ll1$, uniquely determines $\sigma_{\mathfrak{m}}$ and the full jet $\{m_k(x)\}_{k\ge0}$ of $m(s,x)$ at $s=0$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: Publication record. Open Problem 7.27 of D. Aldous and J. A. Fill, Reversible Markov Chains and Random Walks on Graphs, is answered by Y. Shmalo, Arc-transitive graphs that mimic the cycle (September 2026): over arc-transitive graphs other than the cycles, the maximal mean commute time need not be O(n log n), the relaxation time need not be O(n), and the ratio of the maximal mean commute time to twice the average hitting time need not tend to one. The paper gives the hitting times, the average hitting time and the relaxation time of the blow-up H[K_r-bar] of any regular graph H (each vertex replaced by r independent copies) in terms of those of H, and shows that every arc-transitive graph is such a blow-up of a twin-free arc-transitive graph, so the question reduces to twin-free graphs. Paper: https://github.com/yspennstate/arc-transitive-graphs-that-mimic-the-cycle (commit 9e30e48c8cf7); ResearchGate record 414324957. Not refereed.
title: Aldous-Fill Open Problem 7.27 answered negatively: arc-transitive graphs need not behave like the cycle in commute, relaxation and hitting times (Shmalo 2026, repository yspennstate/arc-transitive-graphs-that-mimic-the-cycle)

body:
[Proposition prop:variance_explicit of arXiv:2609.01581, 'Concentration of additive functionals of Stratonovich-type'] Consider the empirical density $\overline{\rho}_t(V)$ (Definition~(def:empirical_density of the paper))
and empirical current $\overline J_t(U)$ (Definition~(def:empirical_current of the paper))
and let Assumptions~(ass:dynamics of the paper) hold.
Then for all $t>0$,
\begin{align}
  \mathrm{Var}_\mu(\overline\rho_t)
    &\leq \frac{2\mathrm{Var}_\mu(V)}{\lambda_\mathrm{gap}t},
  \\
  \mathrm{Var}_\mu(\overline J_t)
    &\leq \frac{1}{t}\left(2\E^\mu[Q]
      +\frac{2\mathrm{Var}_\mu(W)}{\lambda_\mathrm{gap}}\right)
      \leq \frac{1}{t}\left(2\|Q\|_{L^\infty(\mu)}
      +\frac{2\mathrm{Var}_\mu(W)}{\lambda_\mathrm{gap}}\right),
  
\end{align}
where $\lambda_\mathrm{gap}$ denotes the spectral gap~(equation eq:gap_variational of the paper) of $\mathcal{L}_S$
and $W=v_{\textrm{s}}\cdot U$ and $Q=U\cdot DU$ as before.
The corresponding asymptotic variances, 
defined by $\sigma_{A,\infty}^2\equiv\lim_{t\to\infty}t\mathrm{Var}_\mu(\overline A_t)$,
are bounded by the same constants, i.e., 
\begin{align}
  \sigma_{\rho,\infty}^2\leq\frac{2\mathrm{Var}_\mu(V)}{\lambda_\mathrm{gap}},
	\quad\quad
  \sigma_{J,\infty}^2\leq 2\E^\mu[Q]+\frac{2\mathrm{Var}_\mu(W)}{\lambda_\mathrm{gap}}
  \leq 2\|Q\|_{L^\infty(\mu)}+\frac{2\mathrm{Var}_\mu(W)}{\lambda_\mathrm{gap}}.
  
\end{align}
title: Finite-time variance upper bounds

[Proposition prop:conformal_rectangles_tight of arXiv:2609.04138, 'The conformally invariant metric on $\CLE_4$ I:\\ subsequential limits of the non-simple C'] We have the following convergences:
	\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
		\item The number $N^\kappa$ of crossings of $A$ by loops in $\Gamma^\kappa_A$ converges in law to the number $N^4$ of crossings of $A$ by loops in $\Gamma^4_A$ as $\kappa \uparrow 4$. More precisely, for all $\kappa_n \uparrow 4$ there exists an ordering of the crossings $\eta_1^n, \ldots, \eta^n_{N^{\kappa_n}}$ of $\Gamma^{\kappa_n}_A$ for which the random vectors $(N^{\kappa_n}, \eta^n_1, \ldots, \eta^n_{N^{\kappa_n}})$ converge in law to $(N^4, \eta_1, \ldots, \eta_{N^4})$, where $\eta_1, \ldots, \eta_{N^4}$ are the crossings of $A$ by loops in $\Gamma^4_A$, for the topology of Hausdorff convergence.
		\item Jointly with the above convergence, the compact sets $\overline{\bigcup_{\SCL \in \Gamma^{\kappa_n, \mathrm{out}}_A} \mathrm{int}(\SCL)}$ and $\overline{\bigcup_{\SCL \in \Gamma^{\kappa_n, \mathrm{in}}_A} \mathrm{int}(\SCL)}$ converge in distribution for the Hausdorff distance to $\overline{\bigcup_{\SCL \in \Gamma^{4, \mathrm{out}}_A} \mathrm{int}(\SCL)}$ and $\overline{\bigcup_{\SCL \in \Gamma^{4, \mathrm{in}}_A} \mathrm{int}(\SCL)}$.
		\item In particular, the conformal rectangles whose left and right sides are given by the crossings of $A$ by loops in $\Gamma^{\kappa_n}_A$ and whose top and bottom sides are respectively included in $\overline{\bigcup_{\SCL \in \Gamma^{\kappa_n, \mathrm{out}}_A} \SCL}$ and $\overline{\bigcup_{\SCL \in \Gamma^{\kappa_n, \mathrm{in}}_A} \SCL}$ converge in distribution as $n \to \infty$ in the Carath\'eodory sense (jointly with their corners) to the conformal rectangles whose left and right sides are given by the crossings of $A$ by loops in $\Gamma^{4}_A$ and whose top and bottom sides are respectively included in $\overline{\bigcup_{\SCL \in \Gamma^{4, \mathrm{out}}_A} \SCL}$ and $\overline{\bigcup_{\SCL \in \Gamma^{4, \mathrm{in}}_A} \SCL}$, and their moduli are tight in $(0,\infty)$.
	\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma Local model convergence of arXiv:2606.23025, 'Spectral-Capacitary Bounds for Homological Recovery from Reflected Brownian Trajectories'] Assume
\(\partial M\) uniformly of class \(C^{1,1}\), and let
\(x_{\varepsilon} \in M\) satisfy
\(\operatorname{dist}\left( x_{\varepsilon},\partial M \right)/\varepsilon \rightarrow a \in \lbrack 0,\infty\rbrack\).
For fixed \(R > 1\) let \(D_{\varepsilon}(R)\) be the
Dirichlet energy of the capacitary potential of
\(B_{M}\left( x_{\varepsilon},\varepsilon \right)\) in
\(B_{M}\left( x_{\varepsilon},R\varepsilon \right)\backslash\overline{B_{M}\left( x_{\varepsilon},\varepsilon \right)}\)
with the Neumann condition on \(\partial M\), and
\(E_{a}(\varepsilon;R)\) the energy of the corresponding model
condenser at radii \((\varepsilon,R\varepsilon)\) --- the free
Euclidean condenser when \(a = \infty\), the reflected half-space
condenser at height \(a\) when \(a < \infty\). Then
\(D_{\varepsilon}(R) = E_{a}(\varepsilon;R)\left( 1 + o(1) \right)\)
as \(\varepsilon \rightarrow 0\) with \(R\) fixed,
uniformly along the sequence.

[Thm 30 of arXiv:2608.13976, 'Boundary Harnack principle for diffusion with jumps on metric measure spaces'] For each ball $B,$ there exists a transient Hunt process $\wh X^{b, B} $ in $B$ such
that $\wh X^{b, B} $ is a strong dual\vadjust{\goodbreak} of $X^{b, B}$ with respect to
the measure $\xi_B$; that is, the density of the semigroup $\{ \wh
P^{b, B}_t\}_{t\geq0}$ of $\wh X^{b, B}$ with respect to $\xi_B(dy)$ is given by
$\wh p^{b, B}(t, x, y):=\overline{p}^{b, B}(t,y,x)$ and thus

\[
\int_B f(x) P^{b, B}_t g(x) \xi_B(dx)=\int_B g(x) \wh P^{b, B}_t f(x) \xi_B(dx)
\qquad\mbox{for all } f, g\in L^2(B, \xi_B).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Corollary 28 of arXiv:2609.04033, 'From configuration spaces to graph complexes via $\mathbf{FA}$-modules'] Let $d$ be even and let $a\geq b\geq 0$ be integers such that $a+b=d$.  Define $t_{(a,b)}$	by
 	$$	t_{(a,b)} = 
 \begin{cases}
 	\left\lfloor\ds\frac{(a-b)}{4} \right\rfloor + 1 -\delta_{a,b}-\delta_{b,0} & \text{ if } a\equiv b \equiv 0 \text{ mod 2} \\ 
 	& \\ 
 	\left\lfloor\ds\frac{(a-b)}{4} \right\rfloor  -\delta_{b,0} & \text{ if } a\equiv b \equiv 1 \text{ mod 2} \\
 	& \\ 
 	0 & \text{ else.}
 \end{cases}	
 $$	
Then
		$$ 
		H^\ast(\mathsf{T}_\Gamma(n)_d)= \bigoplus_{\substack{ a\geq b \\ a+b=d }} \Sigma^{d+1}t_{(a,b)}\Phi[n,(a,b)^\ast]
		$$

[Lemma lem:gen-f-monotone of arXiv:2602.21315, 'The Instability of all Backoff Protocols\thanks{For the purpose of Open Access, the author'] Fix positive integers~$j'$ and~$j$ with $j' \leq j$. Fix  a send sequence~$\overline{p}$ with $p_0=1$, a $\lambda\in (0,1)$, 
a $j$-tuple
$\overline{\Gamma} \in [0,1]^j$
and a $j$-tuple
$\overline{z} \in (\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0})^j$, 
such that 
$z_x \leq \mu_x^{\overline{\Gamma}}$ for all $x\in [j]$.
Then for all $t \ge 1$,     $\sum_{x \in [j']} f^{\overline{\Gamma},\overline{z}}_x(t) \ge \sum_{x \in [j']} f^{\overline{\Gamma},\overline{z}}_x(t-1)$.

[Lemma 6 of arXiv:2604.17732, 'Exact Simulation from Tempered Stable Distributions with Infinite Variation ($\alpha\ge1$)'] Let $a,b,c>0$ and let
$
m= \frac{1}{b}\log\left(\frac{a}{bc}\right).
$
If
$$
L(x) = ax-  ce^{bx}, \ \ x\in\mathbb R,
$$
then, for $x\ge m$,
$$
L(x) \le L(m) - \frac{ab}{2}(x-m)^2 = \frac{a}{b}\left(\log\left(\frac{a}{bc}\right)-1\right) - \frac{ab}{2}(x-m)^2.
$$

body:
[Defn Radial Loewner chain of arXiv:2505.14762, 'Multiple radial SLE($\kappa$) and quantum Calogero-Sutherland system'] Let $g_t$ satisfies the radial Loewner equation

\begin{equation}
\partial_t g_t(z)=g_t(z) \frac{\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{i} \theta_t}+g_t(z)}{\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{i} \theta_t}-g_t(z)}, \quad g_0(z)=z,
\end{equation}

where $t \mapsto \theta_t$ is real continuous and called the driving function. 
Let $K_t$ be the set of points $z$ in $\mathbb{D}$ such that the solution $g_s(z)$ blows up before or at time $t$.  $K_t$ is called the radial SLE hull driven by $\theta_t$.

Radial Loewner chain in arbitrary simply connected domain $\Omega \subsetneq \mathbb{C}$ with a marked interior point $u \in D$, is defined via a conformal map from $\mathbb{D}$ onto $\Omega$ sending 0 to $u$.
title: Radial Loewner chain

[Thm general.bound.Delta of arXiv:2609.02588, 'Ramsey-type results for Maker-Breaker games'] Let $H$ be a graph with at least one edge.
Let $c:V(H)\rightarrow [\chi(H)]$ be a proper vertex colouring,
and let $\Delta_c(H) = \max\{d_H(v):~v\in V(H),~ c(v)=1\}$.
Then 
$$
s^b_{MB}(H) \leq 
\begin{cases}
2\Delta_c(H) - 1 & ~~ \text{if }b=1 \\
b\Delta_c(H) (\ln(\Delta_c(H)) + 2) & ~~ \text{if }b \geq 2 . \\
\end{cases}
$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Thm general.bound.Delta of arXiv:2609.02588

ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Limit of the optimal online random spanning-tree cost structural calculation Result: The Poisson dynamic-programming recursion has exact small-state solutions. For two current components of sizes x,y, F=(xy/2)*F^2 and the positive solution is2/(xy). For three singleton vertices each merged state has cost1, giving F=(3/2)*(F-1)^2. The admissible root exceeding the child cost is(4+sqrt7)/3; the other root is below1 and violates strict monotonicity. Check: The first recursion follows by integrating the accepted-offer surplus over weights below the continuation-cost difference. For n2 the Poisson cost is2 while the combinatorial model must buy its sole Uniform(0,1) edge and has cost1/2, demonstrating why finite-n model identification is invalid. Obstruction: The recursion depends on the entire component-size partition and on n. Standard coagulation hydrodynamic limits assume a prescribed kernel, whereas these acceptance kernels are themselves defined by unknown value functions. A compactness and uniqueness argument for their joint limit is missing.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-p0221-limit-of-the-optimal-online-random-spanning-tree-cost

body:
Under the hypotheses of the cross-cut theorem, let C have m elements. If R is uniform over the 2^m subsets of C, then mu(0, 1) = 2^m E[(-1)^|R| 1{R is spanning}]. If 0 < p < 1 and R_p contains each element of C independently with probability p, then mu(0, 1) = (1 - p)^(-m) E[(-(1 - p)/p)^|R_p| 1{R_p is spanning}]; p = 1/2 gives the uniform form. These are unbiased Monte Carlo estimators of the Moebius number.
L a finite lattice
C a cross-cut
0 < p < 1

[Corollary cor:robust of arXiv:2608.23203, 'Well-posedness of fully coupled McKean--Vlasov\\ FBSDEs with jumps under full-tuple law de'] Let $m=n$, and let the baseline system $(b_0,\sigma_0,h_0,f_0,g)$, with the initial
datum $\xi_0$, satisfy Assumptions~(ass:integ of the paper)--(ass:mono of the paper) with margin
$c_{\mathrm{diss}}>0$ in the unweighted form (equation eq:monomarginu of the paper). Let the perturbations
$p_b,p_\sigma,p_h,p_f$ satisfy the corresponding origin-integrability and diagonal
Lipschitz conditions of Assumptions~(ass:integ of the paper)--(ass:lip of the paper), and, for some
$c_{\mathrm{pert}}\ge0$, for a.e.\ $t\in[0,T]$ and all
$(\Theta,\mu),(\Theta',\mu')\in\mathcal D_t$,
\begin{multline}
\mathbb{E}\!\Big[\inner{\delta p_b}{G^{\!\top}\delta Y}+\inner{\delta p_\sigma}{G^{\!\top}\delta Z}_F
+\inner{-\delta p_f}{G\delta X}+\!\int_E\!\inner{\delta p_h(e)}{G^{\!\top}\delta U(e)}\nu(\mathrm{d} e)\Big]\\
\le c_{\mathrm{pert}}\,\mathbb{E}\big[|\delta X|^2+|\delta Y|^2+|\delta Z|_F^2+\lVert \delta U\rVert_{L^2(\nu)}^2\big]
\end{multline}
If
$c_{\mathrm{pert}}<c_{\mathrm{diss}}$, the perturbed system
\[
(b,\sigma,h,f,g):=(b_0+p_b,\ \sigma_0+p_\sigma,\ h_0+p_h,\ f_0+p_f,\ g)
\]
satisfies, with the same initial datum $\xi_0$, Assumptions~(ass:integ of the paper)--(ass:mono of the paper)
with the same $G,\alpha,\beta_1,\beta_2$ and margin $c_{\mathrm{diss}}-c_{\mathrm{pert}}$. By
Theorems~(thm:stab of the paper), (thm:uniq of the paper) and~(thm:cwp of the paper) it is well-posed.

If, in addition, the perturbations are independent of $\theta$ and $W_2$-Lipschitz,
\begin{equation}
|\delta p_b|+|\delta p_\sigma|_F+\lVert \delta p_h\rVert_{L^2(\nu)}+|\delta p_f|\ \le\ L_p\,W_2(\mu,\mu')
\end{equation}
for a.e.\ $t\in[0,T]$ and all $(\Theta,\mu),(\Theta',\mu')\in\mathcal D_t$, then
(equation eq:pertpair of the paper) holds with
$c_{\mathrm{pert}}=\|G\|L_p$.

[Theorem 4 (Exact \(L^2\) norm and critical boundary) of arXiv:2607.07712, 'Parameter-Space Heat Flow, Gaussian Density Ratios, and Sharp Hermite Truncation Rates'] Assume \(S=S^T\) and \(I+S>0\). Then
\[
K_{u,S}\in L^2(\gamma_d)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\|S\|_{\mathrm{op}}<1.
\]
Moreover, if \(\|S\|_{\mathrm{op}}<1\), then
\begin{equation}
\|K_{u,S}\|_{L^2(\gamma_d)}^2
=
\det(I-S^2)^{-1/2}
\exp\!\left(
u^T(I-S)^{-1}u
\right).

\end{equation}

[Lemma one-step-descent-convex of arXiv:2608.29507, 'Denoising as Projection: Constrained Optimization with Gradient-Guided Diffusion'] Let $\mathcal X\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be nonempty, closed, convex, and bounded, and let
   $ D_{\mathcal X}:=\sup_{u,v\in\mathcal X}\|u-v\|<\infty .$
Suppose that $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ is $\mu$-strongly convex and $L$-smooth on a convex neighborhood containing the iterates and $\mathcal X$. Let
    $x^\star:=\arg\min_{x\in\mathcal X} f(x),~~
    G_\star:=\|\nabla f(x^\star)\|.$
Consider the update in (equation eq:projected-gradient-guidance-relaxed of the paper)
with $\epsilon(1+L\eta)\le 2, \eta\mu<1.$
Assume that, for every $z$, $\widehat\pi_t(z)\in\mathcal X, \|\widehat\pi_t(z)-\pi_{\mathcal X}(z)\|\le E_t.$

Let ~~$ p_t:=\pi_{\mathcal X}(x_t),~n_t:=x_t-p_t,
    ~
    \mathcal V_t:=f(p_t)-f(x^\star)+\frac{1}{2\eta}\|p_t-x^\star\|^2.$
Define
\begin{align*}
    \rho:=1-\epsilon\eta\mu,&
    \quad
    A_{\eta,\epsilon}:=1+\epsilon\eta L,\quad 
    M_\eta:=G_\star+\left(L+\frac{1}{\eta}\right)D_{\mathcal X},
    \quad
    C_\eta:=\frac{L}{2}+\frac{1}{2\eta},\\
   & B_1:=M_\eta A_{\eta,\epsilon},
    \quad
    B_2:=2C_\eta A_{\eta,\epsilon}^2.
\end{align*}
Then
\vspace{-10pt}
\begin{align*}
    \mathcal V_{t-1}
    \le
    \rho\mathcal V_t
    +
    B_1\|n_t\|
    +
    B_2\|n_t\|^2
    +
    \epsilon M_\eta E_t
    +
    2\epsilon^2C_\eta E_t^2.
\end{align*}
Moreover, the normal component satisfies
   $ \|n_{t-1}\|
    \le
    (1-\epsilon)\|n_t\|.$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma one-step-descent-convex of arXiv:2608.29507

body:
Let G be a finite group and p a prime dividing the order |G|. Then G contains an element of order exactly p, hence a subgroup of order p. More precisely (McKay), the number of solutions to x^p = e in G is a multiple of p, and since x = e is one of them, there are at least p - 1 elements of order p; in fact the number of elements of order p is congruent to -1 modulo p. Cauchy's theorem is the p^1 case of Sylow's first theorem (a subgroup of order p^a exists whenever p^a divides |G|) and is the converse of Lagrange's theorem for prime orders; the converse of Lagrange fails in general (A_4 has order 12 and no subgroup of order 6).
G finite, p prime with p dividing |G|

body:
[Theorem thm:vector-valued of arXiv:2608.01279, 'Stochastic heat equation with nondegenerate Hölder diffusion coefficient: uniqueness below'] Let \(d\geq1\), \(\beta\in(2/3,1)\), and let
\[
    G:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^{d\times d}
\]
be a measurable mapping that satisfies the following two conditions:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item For some constant \(c_G>0\),
\[
    G(z)G(z)^{*}\geq c_G^2 I_d,
    \qquad z\in\mathbb R^d,
\]
\item    For some constant \([G]_{C^\beta}<\infty\),
\begin{equation}
    \|G(z)-G(z')\|_{\mathrm{HS}}
       \leq [G]_{C^\beta}\|z-z'\|^\beta,
    \qquad \forall z,z'\in\mathbb R^d.
    
\end{equation}
\end{enumerate}

Consider the following vector-valued stochastic heat equation
$$
    \partial_t U
      =\Delta U+G(U)\dot W,
      \qquad
      U(0)=u_0\in L^2(\mathbb T;\mathbb R^d),
$$
where \(W=(W^1,\ldots,W^d)\) is a \(d\)-dimensional
space--time white noise.

Then weak uniqueness holds for the above equation in
$
    C\bigl([0,T];L^2(\mathbb T;\mathbb R^d)\bigr)
$
for every \(T>0\). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Finite-dimensional vector-field SHEs

body: [Lemma 16 of arXiv:2512.04807, 'Existence and uniqueness of the canonical Brownian motion in non-simple conformal loop ens'] Let $\vertexset$ be a finite set and $w_n\colon \vertexset\times\vertexset \to [0,\infty)$ be a sequence of edge conductances such that each $(\vertexset,w_n)$ is connected. Let $R_n\colon \vertexset\times\vertexset \to [0,\infty)$ be the associated effective resistance metrics. Suppose that $R_n \to R$ for some $R\colon \vertexset\times\vertexset \to [0,\infty)$ with $R(x,y) > 0$ for each $x \neq y$. Then there exists $w\colon \vertexset\times\vertexset \to [0,\infty)$ such that $w_n \to w$ and $R$ is the effective resistance associated with $w$.

body: [Corollary 3.4 (Estimation of wavelet coefficients / $S$) in the first version of arXiv:2512.18592, 'Wavelet Latent Position Exponential Random Graphs'] Assume the conditions of Theorem 3.3. Let $f(x,y):=\log\!\Big(\frac{W(x,y)}{1-W(x,y)}\Big)$ denote the logit of $W$. Under Definition 3.1 we have $\|f\|_{\infty}\leq B$ for a fixed constant $B<\infty$, hence $W$ is uniformly bounded away from $0$ and $1$. Fix a clipping level $\varepsilon\in(0,1/2)$ and let $\widehat{W}_{n}^{\mathrm{clip}}$ be the clipped estimator from Theorem 3.3. Define $\widehat{f}_{n}(x,y):=\log\!\Big(\frac{\widehat{W}_{n}^{\mathrm{clip}}(x,y)}{1-\widehat{W}_{n}^{\mathrm{clip}}(x,y)}\Big).$ Let $\{\Psi_{\lambda}\}_{\lambda\in\Lambda}$ be the tensor-product orthonormal wavelet basis used above and define the coefficient arrays $\beta:=\big(\langle f,\Psi_{\lambda}\rangle\big)_{\lambda\in\Lambda},\qquad\widehat{\beta}_{n}:=\big(\langle\widehat{f}_{n},\Psi_{\lambda}\rangle\big)_{\lambda\in\Lambda}.$ Equip coefficient arrays with the $\ell^{2}(\Lambda)$ (Hilbert–Schmidt) norm $\|T\|_{\mathrm{HS}}^{2}:=\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda}T_{\lambda}^{2}$. Then there exists a constant $C_{1}^{\prime}>0$ (depending only on $s,p,q,M,B$ and $\varepsilon$) such that, with the same exponent $C_{2}$ as in Theorem 3.3, $\sup_{W\in\mathcal{F}^{s}_{p,q}(M)}\mathbb{E}\,\|\widehat{\beta}_{n}-\beta\|_{\mathrm{HS}}^{2}\leq C_{1}^{\prime}\,N_{n}^{-\frac{2s}{2s+2}}(\log N_{n})^{C_{2}}.$

body:
[Corollary 11 (Consistency of FP selection) of arXiv:2608.20998, 'Free-Probability Kernels for Zero-Rollout Hyperparameter Selection in Reservoir Computing'] Assume that the deterministic kernel and the finite reservoir use the
same feature map. Fix finite candidate and ridge grids, with all ridge
parameters strictly positive. For any fixed maximum retained lag $L$,
if the deterministic validation score has a unique minimizer, then
finite-width reservoir selection returns the same minimizer with
probability tending to one as $n\to\infty$.

In the stable regime, a unique complete-history optimum is preserved
by all sufficiently large finite contexts, and selection based on the
complete finite-reservoir trajectory converges to this optimum as
$n\to\infty$.

body:
[Lemma lem:singleton-renewal of arXiv:2608.29403, 'Kac's Walk on Rotation Matrices Mixes in $\boldsymbol{\Theta(n^2)}$ Steps:\\ A Proof Disco'] For a Kac plane $i$, let
\[
 W_i^\circ=\Pi_{\mathcal W}(\mathsf P_i-N^{-1}I_W)
\]
be its pure-Weyl coefficient.  On the common star space, with an arbitrary
passive ancillary Hilbert space $E$, put
\[
 (\mathsf M h)(i,\theta)=(W_i^\circ\otimes I_E)h(i,\theta),
 \qquad \mathsf J=\mathscr E^*\mathscr E,
 \qquad \mathsf Q=I-\mathsf J.
\]
Relative to $\operatorname{ran}\mathsf J\oplus
\operatorname{ran}\mathsf Q$, write
\[
 \mathsf M=
 \begin{pmatrix}0&\mathsf S^-\\ \mathsf S^+&\mathsf V\end{pmatrix}.
\tag{3.2.10n}
\]
We call $0,\mathsf S^-,\mathsf S^+,\mathsf V$ the four
\emph{star statuses} of a passive singleton; a status record chooses one
of these four blocks for every singleton after equal-time fusion.  These
statuses are distinct from the derivative-placement coefficients
$(\alpha,\beta)$ used in the Ricci root calculus.
Then
\[
 \|\mathsf S^-\|=\|\mathsf S^+\|
 \le\sqrt{\frac{n-3}{N(n-1)}}\le N^{-1/2},
 \qquad \|\mathsf V\|\le2,
\tag{3.2.10o}
\]
and the one-sided utilized-step maps factor through the innovation:
\[
 \mathscr E\mathsf M\mathscr T=\mathscr E\mathsf M\mathscr G,
 \qquad
 \mathscr T^*\mathsf M\mathscr E^*
 =\mathscr G^*\mathsf M\mathscr E^*.
\tag{3.2.10p}
\]
Consequently a passive singleton isolated between invariant separators is
zero.  A run of $s\ge2$ passive singletons with $s-1$ prescribed finite
Green gates has norm at most
\[
 \frac{2^{2s-3}}N.
\tag{3.2.10q}
\]
Thus its two endpoints create one $N^{-1}$ resource and every interior
singleton transports that same resource; no additional token is created.
The same conclusion holds when an endpoint is a $\mathscr D$- or
$\mathscr L$-incidence, with the corresponding mixed bound of
(lem:riesz of the paper) and with the already existing root or packet token
transported.

\(e^{\max\{x,y\}}\le e^x+e^y\),
\[
\psi_{n+1}(\theta)
=
\EE{e^{\theta \Svar^{(n+1)}}}
\le
e^\theta\,\EE{e^{\theta \U (\Svar^{(n)})'}+e^{\theta (1-\U)(\Svar^{(n)})''}}.
\]
Conditioning on \(\U\sim \Unif(0,1)\) and using independence of \(\U\), \((\Svar^{(n)})'\), and
\((\Svar^{(n)})''\), we obtain
\[
\psi_{n+1}(\theta)
\le
2e^\theta\int_0^1 \EE{e^{\theta u \Svar^{(n)}}}\,\dd u
=
2e^\theta\int_0^1 \psi_n(\theta u)\,\dd u.
\]
By \Cref{lem:holder-logconvex},
\[
\int_0^1 \psi_n(\theta u)\,\dd u
\le
\int_0^1 \psi_n(\theta)^u\,\dd u
=

body:
[Lemma 43 (Finite-order Cauchy--Dirichlet estimate for scalar-principal systems) of arXiv:2608.30027, 'Under Ricci flow, a 3-torus goes flat'] Fix \(m\geq2\) and \(\sigma\in(0,1)\).  Let
\(Q_i^+=\Omega_i\times[a,a+\theta]\), where
\(\Omega_1\Subset\Omega_2\) are smooth Euclidean domains.  Suppose that a
smooth finite-dimensional vector-valued function \(Z\) satisfies on
\(Q_2^+\)
\[
 \partial_tZ-a^{ij}\partial_i\partial_jZ
 =\mathsf B^i\partial_iZ+\mathsf CZ+G,
\]
where \(a^{ij}=a^{ji}\) is uniformly parabolic and
\(\partial_t-a^{ij}\partial_i\partial_j\) acts componentwise with the same
coefficient matrix on every component; only \(\mathsf B^i\) and
\(\mathsf C\) may couple components.  The coefficients
\(a^{ij},\mathsf B^i,\mathsf C\) have uniformly bounded
\(C^{m-2+\sigma,(m-2+\sigma)/2}\)-norms.  Assume that \(Z=0\) on the initial
face, and that \(Z\) and \(G\) vanish in a fixed spatial collar of
\(\partial\Omega_2\times[a,a+\theta]\).  Then
\[
 \|Z\|_{C^{m+\sigma,(m+\sigma)/2}(Q_1^+)}
 \leq C\left(
   \|G\|_{C^{m-2+\sigma,(m-2+\sigma)/2}(Q_2^+)}
   +\|Z\|_{C^0(Q_2^+)}\right),
\]
where \(C\) depends only on the displayed coefficient and parabolicity bounds,
\(m,\sigma,\theta\), the rank, and the fixed domains \(\Omega_1\Subset
\Omega_2\). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Finite-order Cauchy--Dirichlet estimate for scalar-principal systems

[Theorem 10 (the linear estimate) of arXiv:2609.01093, 'Ideal MHD below the classical well-posedness threshold'] Let $\breg\in(\frac12,1)$, $\varepsilon:=1-\breg$,
$\sreg\ge0$, $\preg\in\Real$ and $0<T\le1$. For every
$f_0\in Y^{\sreg,\preg}$,
$f_1\in Y^{\sreg,\preg-1}$ and
$G\in L^{2}_tY^{\sreg,\preg-1}(\Rst)$ there is
$u$ on $\Rst$ with
\[
 \Box u=G\quad\text{on }[0,T],\qquad
 (u,\partial_tu)|_{t=0}=(f_0,f_1),
\]
satisfying
\begin{equation}
\big\|u\big\|_{H^{\sreg,\preg}_{\breg}}
 \le C_{\rm lin}\Big(
 \big\|f_0\big\|_{Y^{\sreg,\preg}}
 +\big\|f_1\big\|_{Y^{\sreg,\preg-1}}
 +T^{\varepsilon}\big\|G\big\|_{L^{2}_tY^{\sreg,\preg-1}}\Big),
\end{equation}
where $C_{\rm lin}=C(\chi,\breg)$ is independent of $T\le1$, of the
field, of the data and of the indices $\sreg,\preg$. Moreover,
\[
 u\in C([0,T],Y^{\sreg,\preg})
 \cap C^1([0,T],Y^{\sreg,\preg-1}).
\]

Let $\epsilon>0$.	 Then,  there exist constants $c_1,R_0>1$ (depending only on $x,y$,  $\epsilon$,  and $F$) and $c_2>0$ (depending only on $x,y$,  and $F$) such that the following is true for all $R \geq R_0$ and all $z \in F$. Let $t$ (resp.\ $\widetilde{t}$) be the first time that $P$ (resp.\ $\widetilde{P}$) intersects $\overline{B_{2^{-R}}(z)}$.  Then,  the distance between $P|_{[0,t]}$ and $\widetilde{P}|_{[0,\widetilde{t}]}$ with respect to $D_\Gamma$ (equivalently,  since $P$ is a $D_\Gamma$-geodesic,  the quantity $\len(P|_{[t , 1-\widetilde{t}]} ; D_\Gamma)$) is strictly less than $c / R$.

body: [Definition 8 of arXiv:2609.03875, 'Measure theory without infinities'] Let $\mf A$ be an HTM. A map $\mu$ is said to be an $\mf A$-valued $\sigma$-additive function if $\im\mu\subset \mf A$ and $\mu(A) = \sum \mu\circ\mb A$ for every $A\in D_\mu$ and every countable partition $\mb A$ of $A$ into elements of $D_\mu$. A map $\mu$ is called an $\mf A$-valued $\sigma$-content (premeasure)  if $\mu$ is an $\mf A$-valued $\sigma$-additive function and $D_\mu$ is a ring (resp., a $\delta$-ring).

[Corollary 43 of arXiv:2607.21374, 'Local structure at the maximum and sharp persistence asymptotics of rough fractional Brown'] Let
\begin{equation*}
  h_n=2^{-r_n}\downarrow0,
  \qquad
  u_n,L_n\in h_n\mathbb Z_{\geq0},
  \qquad
  u_n\to0,
  \qquad
  L_n\to\infty.
\end{equation*}
Put
\begin{equation*}
  P_{h,u,L}:=(\mathscr M_{u,L})_*Q_{h,u,L},
  \qquad
  P_u:=(\mathscr A_u)_*Q^u\quad(u>0),
\end{equation*}
and let \(P_0\) be the law on \(\mathcal Y\) with zero lifetime, height, and
left arm, and right arm \((G_s)_{s\geq0}\) under \(Q^0\).  Thus
\(K_0=P_0\).  Then
\begin{equation}
\begin{gathered}
  \mathcal L_{Q_{h_n,u_n,L_n}}
    \bigl(W|_{[0,\infty)}\bigr)
  \Longrightarrow Q^0
  \quad\text{in }C_{\mathrm{loc}}([0,\infty)),\\
  P_{h_n,u_n,L_n}\Longrightarrow P_0,
  \qquad
  K_{h_n,u_n,L_n}\Longrightarrow K_0
  \quad\text{in }\mathcal Y.
\end{gathered}
  
\end{equation}
Consequently, the arm-valued map \(u\mapsto P_u\) and the endpoint-tilted map
\(u\mapsto K_u\) are weakly continuous on \([0,\infty)\).

[Definition def: distance and ball of arXiv:2606.13147, 'Scaling limits of the single-curve interface and outermost loops in the planar random fiel'] For any $I\subset \Lambda_M$ and any $x\in I$, recalling that
$\bar{\partial}\Lambda_M=
\partial\Lambda_M
\cup \partial\Lambda_{M/2}(u_i)
\cup \partial\Lambda_{M/4}(u_i),$
define
\[
d_x
=
\min\Big\{
{\operatorname{dist}}(x,\bar{\partial}\Lambda_M),
\min_{y\in I\setminus\{x\}}{\operatorname{dist}}(x,y)
\Big\}.
\]
 When $I=\{x\}$, we use the convention that $\min_{y\in I\setminus\{x\}}{\operatorname{dist}}(x,y)=\infty$.
	In addition, we write
	$$
	\mathrm{Ball}(I):=\bigcup_{x\in I}\Lambda_{d_x/10}(x).
	$$
    Here and throughout, whenever the subscript of $\Lambda$ is not an integer, it is understood to be rounded down to the nearest integer. In particular, $\Lambda_{d_x/10}$ stands for $\Lambda_{\lfloor d_x/10\rfloor}$, and the same convention applies to quantities such as $\Lambda_{d_x/9}$.  Moreover, we adopt the convention that  $\Lambda_{d_x/10}(x)=\{x\}$ whenever $d_x/10<1$.
