body:
[Corollary cor:1-2moment of arXiv:2605.01444, 'From second moments to pairwise negative correlation: \\applications to minimal and unifor'] Let ${\ensuremath{\mathbb P}} $ be either ${\ensuremath{\mathbb P}} _\mathrm{MST}$ or ${\ensuremath{\mathbb P}} _\mathrm{UST}$ on $K_n$, and let ${\ensuremath{\mathbb E}} $ be the corresponding expectation. Let $e$ and $f$ be adjacent edges, and let $e$ and $e'$ be non-adjacent edges. Set
	\[
	p_0 = {\ensuremath{\mathbb P}} [\omega(e)=1],\quad
	p_1 = {\ensuremath{\mathbb P}} [\omega(e)=\omega(f)=1],\quad
	p_2 = {\ensuremath{\mathbb P}} [\omega(e)=\omega(e')=1].
	\]
	Then
	\[
	p_0 = \frac{2}{n},\qquad
	p_1 = \frac{{\ensuremath{\mathbb E}} \big[\sum_{x\in V(K_n)}\deg(x;\omega)^2\big]-2(n-1)}{n(n-1)(n-2)},
	\]
	and
	\[
	p_2 = \frac{4\big[n(n-1)-{\ensuremath{\mathbb E}} \big(\sum_{x\in V(K_n)}\deg(x;\omega)^2\big)\big]}{n(n-1)(n-2)(n-3)}.
	\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Corollary cor:1-2moment of arXiv:2605.01444

body: [Proposition 8 of arXiv:2609.03070, 'Variants of order semicontinuity in Banach lattices'] Assume that $F$ is a vector lattice with PPP and let $Q\subset F_{+}$ and $e\in F$ be such that $e=\bigvee Q$. Then, for every $0\le r<1$ there is a disjoint $D\subset F_{+}$ such that $\bigvee D=re$ and for every $d\in D$ there is $q\in Q$ such that $d\le q$. Moreover, if $Q$ is countable then $D$ can also be chosen to be countable.

[Lemma lem:RR of arXiv:2607.05671, 'Bi-infinite systems of singularly interacting Brownian particles and the KPZ equation'] Fix $\theta \in (0,1)$ and let $T, K_1$ be as above.
For $a_0\in \mathbb{R},  t_0 \ge 0$, $(x,t) \in B(a_0, t_0)$ and $\varepsilon, \delta \in (0,1)$, define $H(x,\varepsilon,\delta):= [x-\sigma\varepsilon^{-1/4}\delta-(\delta \log \delta^{-1})^{1/2}, x-\sigma\varepsilon^{-1/4}\delta+(\delta \log \delta^{-1})^{1/2}]^c$, and
$$
R(x,t, t_0, a_0, \varepsilon, \delta):= \int_{H(x,\varepsilon,\delta)} (\mathcal{G}^{\varepsilon}(t,u)- \mathcal{G}^{\varepsilon}(t_0,a_0)) p_{\delta}(u-x) du.
$$
Then, for each $r\ge 1$, there exists $C \in (0,\infty)$ such that, for all  $\varepsilon, \delta \in (0,1)$ satisfying $\sigma \varepsilon^{-1/4}\delta + c^*\delta \le \frac{1}{4}(\delta \log \delta^{-1})^{1/2}$,
$$\sup_{(a_0, t_0) \in K_1\times [0,T]} \left\|\sup_{(x,t) \in B(a_0, t_0, \theta)} |R(x,t, t_0, a_0, \varepsilon, \delta)|\right\|_r \le C\delta^{1/8}.
$$
title: Lemma lem:RR of arXiv:2607.05671

body:
[Lemma 21 (One-hive marginal of the  quadruply augmented double hive law) of arXiv:2607.04138, 'Hives from deformed GUE minor processes'] \lab{lem:double-one-hive}
Assume \(\bar a,\bar b,\bar d>0\), and assume either \(\bar f>0\), or
\[
\bar f^2<0,
\qquad
\bar a^2+\bar b^2+\bar d^2+\bar f^2<0.
\]
Let \(p_{\mathrm{dbl}}\) be the density on \(\mathbb D^4\) from
Lemma~\ref{lem:double-maxent}.  Put
\[
T=\bar a^2+\bar b^2+\bar d^2+\bar f^2.
\]
Define the geometric side lengths
\[
a^2=\frac{\bar a^2(T-\bar a^2)}{T},\qquad
b^2=\frac{\bar b^2(T-\bar b^2)}{T},
\]
\[
d^2=\frac{\bar d^2(T-\bar d^2)}{T},\qquad
f^2=\frac{\bar f^2(T-\bar f^2)}{T},
\]
and
\[
c_*^2=
\frac{(\bar a^2+\bar b^2)(\bar d^2+\bar f^2)}{T}.
\]
In the second case these quantities are still positive, since
\(\bar d^2+\bar f^2<-(\bar a^2+\bar b^2)\).
Let \(h_1\) denote the first hive, so that
\[
h_1\in H_n(\alpha,\beta;\nu).
\]
Then the marginal law of \(h_1\) is
\[
\mathcal H_n(a,b,c_*).
\]
Similarly, the marginal law of the second hive is
\(\mathcal H_n(d,f,c_*)\); in the case \(\bar f^2<0\), this is understood
using the symmetry of the three boundary components to place the imaginary
raw parameter in the third slot of Theorem~\ref{thm:gaussian1}.  Moreover,
\(c_*\) is the value of the glued side selected by Lemma~\ref{lem:doublehive}:
it maximizes
\[
x\mapsto
\frac{\Delta_{abx}^2}{abx}\frac{\Delta_{xdf}^2}{xdf}.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: One-hive marginal of the  quadruply augmented double hive law

[Lemma lem_decode of arXiv:2608.15344, 'A Harris recurrent continuous-time Markov process without wide-sense regenerative structur'] There exists a Borel measurable function $c:\mathbb{R}\rightarrow\mathcal{V}$ with the following property. Let
\[
p=(p_0,p_1,\dots,p_m),\;\;\;\;q=(q_0,q_1,\dots,q_n)
\]
be two finite simple directed paths (no vertex is visited more than once) with the same initial vertex ($p_0=q_0$) and the same terminal vertex ($p_m=q_n$). If
\[
d=\sum_{i=1}^ml(p_{i-1},p_i)-\sum_{i=1}^nl(q_{i-1},q_i)\neq0,
\]
then $c(d)$ is a non-initial vertex occurring in both $p$ and $q$, i.e., 
\[
c(d)\in\{p_1,\dots,p_m\}\cap\{q_1,\dots,q_n\}.
\]

[Proposition 5 of arXiv:2608.29855, 'Growth of Simple Closed Geodesics in closed Hyperbolic $3$-Manifolds'] For every $0<\varepsilon<1$ there exist a finite set
$S\subset\Gamma^+$, an open spherical disk
$D\subset\partial\hts$, and constants $\alpha,R>0$ such that,
with
$$
U_S\coloneqq \max_{s\in S}d(o,so),
$$
the following hold:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item $s(\overline D)\subset D$ for every $s\in S$, and the sets
$s(\overline D)$ are pairwise disjoint;
\item the positive semigroup on $S$ is free;
\item for every bi-infinite sequence $(s_j)_{j\in\Z}$ with
$s_j\in S$, if $P_0=e$, $P_{j+1}=P_js_{j+1}$, and $x_j=P_jo$, then
\begin{equation}
    \alpha|p-q|
\le
d(x_p,x_q)
\le
U_S|p-q|
\qquad(p,q\in\Z);
\end{equation}
\item every periodic positive $S$-word corresponds to a loxodromic element of $\Gamma^+$ and has a periodic broken geodesic at Hausdorff distance at most $R$ from its axis;
\item
$$
\frac{\log|S|}{U_S}>2-\varepsilon.
$$
\end{enumerate}

[Definition of arXiv:2608.28504, 'Global $\bm\infty$-categories and global Thom spectra'] Let $\textbf{\textup{U}}\subset\ul\CAT_T$ be any full $T$-subcategory. We say that a $T$-$\infty$-category has \emph{$\textbf{\textup{U}}$-colimits} if the $T_{/A}$-$\infty$-category $\textup{fgt}_A^*{\mathcal{C}}$ has ${\mathcal{K}}$-shaped colimits for every $A\in T$ and ${\mathcal{K}}\in\textbf{\textup{U}}(A)\subset\CAT_{T_{/A}}$. If also ${\mathcal{D}}$ has $\textbf{\textup{U}}$-colimits, then we say that a $T$-functor $F\colon{\mathcal{C}}\to{\mathcal{D}}$ is $\textbf{\textup{U}}$-cocontinuous if $\textup{fgt}_A^*F$ preserves ${\mathcal{K}}$-shaped colimits for all $A\in T$ and ${\mathcal{K}}\in\textbf{\textup{U}}(A)$.

    Dually, we define what it means to have \emph{$\textbf{\textup{U}}$-limits} and to be \emph{$\textbf{\textup{U}}$-continuous}.

[Cor 7 of arXiv:2506.12755, '{\bf Stochastic intrinsic gradient flows on the Wasserstein space}\footnote{Supported in p'] Let $n\in\NN_{\geq 3}$. The diffusion $((\mu^{(n)}_t)_{t\geq 0},$ $(\P^{\mu,n})_{\mu\in E_n})$ on $E_n$ 
	which is  associated with $(\EE^{F,n},\D(\EE^{F,n}))$  yields a solution to \eqref{eq:SGF2}, \eqref{eq:DWF} in the following sense:
	
	For $u\in \D(A^{(n)})$,
	\begin{equation*}
		\tilde u(\mu_t^{(n)})-\tilde u(\mu_0)-\int_0^t\Big[A^{(n)}u(\mu_s^{(n)})-\int_{\RR^d}\gamma_{\mu_s^{(n)}}(x)\big\la DW_F(x,\mu_s^{(n)}),Du(x,\mu_s^{(n)})\big\ra\mu_s^{(n)}(\d x)\Big]\d s,\quad t\ge 0,
	\end{equation*}
	is a $\P^{\mu,n}$-martingale for $\EE^{F,n}$-q.e.~$\mu\in E_n$, where  $\tilde u$ denotes an $\EE^{F,n}$-quasi-continuous version.
title: Cor 7 of arXiv:2506.12755

[Theorem thm:SC-concate of arXiv:2608.12415, 'Sharp Phase Transition for Ellipsoid Fitting'] For any linear combination of backbone-dangling shapes \[
K = \sum_{\mathcal{B}(K)} c_\tau \cdot \mathsf{M} _\tau \,,
 \]
	from a ground set $\mathcal{B}(K)$ of size $|\mathcal{B}(K)|$ and each shape has at most $D_V$ vertices. Then, for any $t>0$, we have \[ 
	P^{\mathsf{sc}}_t(K) = \mathsf{P}_t(K) + O( \frac{\operatorname{poly}(t, D_V) }{\sqrt{d}} )
	\]
	Quantitatively, we have \[ 
	P^{\mathsf{sc}}_t(K) = \mathsf{P}_t(K) + \text{SC-Error}(t)
	\]
	for \[
	\|\text{SC-Error}(t)\|_{sp} \leq O(2^{t}) \cdot B_q(\text{non-ideal})	\]
	with $B_q(\text{non-ideal})$ the auxiliary function defined from~(thm:Q-norm of the paper). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition 12 (\cite{xia1996vector}) of arXiv:2608.30589, 'Vector-Valued Wavelet Bases as Hilbert $\mathbb{M}_m(\mathbb{R})$-Module Bases: A Construc'] We say that $\Phi$ is a scaling function for a vector-valued multiresolution analysis $\{V_j\}_{j\in \mathbb{Z}}$ of $L^2(\mathbb{R}^d,\mathbb{R}^m)$ if the sequence $\{V_j\}_{j\in \mathbb{Z}}$ satisfies:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(VMRA\arabic*)}]
\item $V_{j}\subset V_{j+1}$ for all $j\in \mathbb{Z}$.
\item $\bigcap_{j\in\mathbb{Z}} V_j=\{0\}$ and $\bigcup_{j\in \mathbb{Z}} V_j$ is dense in $L^2(\mathbb{R}^d,\mathbb{R}^m)$.
\item $h\in V_j$ if and only if $h(A\cdot)\in V_{j+1}$ for all $j\in\mathbb{Z}$.
\item $h\in V_j$ if and only if $h(\cdot-k)\in V_{j}$ for all $j\in\mathbb{Z}$ and $k\in\mathbb{Z}^d$.
\item The sequence $\{\Phi(\cdot-k)\}_{k\in\mathbb{Z}^d}$ is an orthonormal basis of $V_0$.
\end{enumerate}
title: \cite{xia1996vector}

body:
Let Delta be a real d-by-k matrix of rank r_star>=1, C a positive definite d-by-d matrix and G=C Delta. Let A be d-by-h, B h-by-k with h>=r_star. Consider simultaneous factor GD A_next=A-eta C(AB-Delta)B^T and B_next=B-eta A^T C(AB-Delta), at any finite steps eta, initialized at arbitrary A_0 and B_0=0. Then row(B_t) is contained in row(Delta)=row(G) at every integer t>=0, equivalently B_t(I-P)=0 for the orthogonal projector P onto row(Delta). This inclusion version of the known zero-factor alignment component is the content used from Zhang-Liu-Chen, LoRA-One, arXiv:2502.01235, Theorem 3.1 and Appendix C.1 Theorem C.10 (printed pp.26-27). It does not imply that A_t has aligned, that B_t has full rank, or that the product has fitted Delta. The induction applies to the noiseless quadratic C-metric loss; with additive noise the sample gradient generally has larger rank, so a rank-r_star invariant signal subspace no longer follows.
Real exact-rank-r_star target; positive definite input covariance; h>=r_star
Zero initial output-side factor, arbitrary input-side factor; simultaneous ordinary GD on the noiseless covariance quadratic
Conclusion is a row-space inclusion, not rank equality or residual convergence

[Proposition 18 of arXiv:2608.30589, 'Vector-Valued Wavelet Bases as Hilbert $\mathbb{M}_m(\mathbb{R})$-Module Bases: A Construc'] The family $\{\mathbf{V}_j\}_{j\in\mathbb{Z}}$ is an MRA of $L^2(\mathbb{R}^d)$ with dyadic dilation $2$ and integer
translations. Moreover, for each $j\in\mathbb{Z}$ one has the orthogonal decomposition
\[
\mathbf{V}_{j+1}
=
\mathbf{V}_j\ \oplus\ \bigoplus_{\epsilon\in\{0,1\}^d\setminus\{0\}} \mathbf{W}_j^{(\epsilon)},
\]
where
\[
\mathbf{W}_j^{(\epsilon)}
=
\bigotimes_{\ell=1}^d X_{j}^{(\epsilon_\ell)},
\qquad
X_{j}^{(0)}=V_j,\ \ X_{j}^{(1)}=W_j.
\]
In particular,
\[
L^2(\mathbb{R}^d)
=
\mathbf{V}_0\ \oplus\ \bigoplus_{j\ge 0}\ \bigoplus_{\epsilon\in\{0,1\}^d\setminus\{0\}} \mathbf{W}_j^{(\epsilon)},
\]
and the associated orthonormal wavelet basis consists of the usual $2^d-1$ wavelet types (one for each
$\epsilon\neq 0$), obtained by tensoring the scalar scaling functions and mother wavelets componentwise.

ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Conservation, explicit coupling reduction, exact law comparison or spectral calculation Result: Finite-volume stationarity gives pi_V*K_v,V=pi_V for addition at v. To pass this identity through a local limit, truncate the avalanche at a radius r. If its influence on an observed window leaves that ball with probability at most epsilon_r, uniformly in outer V, then for each bounded local test f the discrepancy between the full and truncated expectations is at most 2*||f||_infinity*epsilon_r. The truncated operator is local and continuous, so subsequential limits inherit addition invariance if epsilon_r tends to zero. Check: Use the same stacks up to the exit from the radius-r ball. On the no-exit event the two evaluations agree, giving the bound directly. This requires a uniform probability estimate; finite-volume almost-sure stabilization alone is not enough. Obstruction: Uniform localization is missing and may fail for critical avalanches. Even inherited addition invariance would still need a uniqueness theorem to identify all subsequential limits.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-p0378-exhaustion-independent-infinite-volume-wired-arw-measure

For the exact critical unshaped tanh variance chain K_(j+1)=n^-1 sum tanh(sqrt(K_j)Z_i)^2 from fixed K0>0, fixed t>0, E[1/(nK_floor(nt))]=exp(2t)-1-(5/6)exp(2t)log(n)/n+O_(K0,t)(1/n) as n tends to infinity. The exact reciprocal expectation is finite for sufficiently large n. The limiting mean is that of dV=(2V+2)dt+sqrt(2)VdW,V0=0. The coefficient of the remaining1/n term is not identified. Assumptions: Zero bias, unshaped tanh, independent standard Gaussian rows and layers, weight variance exactly1/n with no width-dependent normalizer, fixed positive K0 and t. Uses direct finite-chain inverse/positive moment estimates and affine conditional-mean telescoping; C026 entrance convergence is not a premise. Model: K_(j+1)=n^-1 sum_(i=1)^n tanh(sqrt(K_j)Z_(j,i))^2, with independent standard Gaussian rows and layers, K0>0 fixed, no bias, Gaussian weight variance exactly1/n, and no width-dependent normalizer. Write Y_q=tanh(sqrt(q)Z)^2/q, S_(n,q)=n^-1 sum_i Y_q(Z_i), q=K_j, v=1/(nq), V_next=1/(nK_(j+1)). Limit: New proof and dependencies unaudited; literature novelty not asserted. This is one exact raw-mean correction, not Target3 all-order uniform finite-width cumulant remainders.

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:e0edc14525c1efb6185d760262000cfc75cbfcaded470429da5f78c0bd3be9bd","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/e0/e0edc14525c1efb6185d760262000cfc75cbfcaded470429da5f78c0bd3be9bd.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:b6b80062e37a23fca82e641d20dba351ce5b2a9b7c0adb121f8f3309c6a0ca51","bundle_entry_key":"tanh-reciprocal-mean-log-rate","bundle_id":"population.t244-critical-tanh-reciprocal-mean-rate-016","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"probability; random neural networks","draft":"w691/bundle_016.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.randomnetworks:t244-tanh-reciprocal-mean-log-rate","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# C046-C047: critical tanh mesoscopic law and reciprocal-mean correction

Version1, 20 October2026. Target3, kind moved. Proofs (unaudited).
These are direct finite-chain estimates and do not assume C026's functional
entrance limit. They use the independent positive-moment estimates of C027
and the exact inverse moments and drift calculations of C044/C045.
Literature novelty is not asserted.

Let K0>0 be fixed and

    K_(j+1)=n^(-1)sum_(i=1)^n tanh(sqrt(K_j)Z_(j,i))^2,

with independent standard Gaussian rows and layers. This is unshaped,
zero-bias tanh at weight variance1/n. Let V_j=1/(nK_j). These reciprocals
are finite almost surely; for sufficiently large n their required moments
are integrable by C044. No bounded replacement or extinction convention
is needed. Set Q=max(1,K0), so0<K_j<=Q at every layer.

## C046: quantitative mesoscopic variance law

For each finite T there are C_(K0,T),n0 such that for n>=n0,

    E|k K_k-1/2|<=C_(K0,T)[k^(-1/2)+sqrt(k/n)],
                                           1<=k<=floor(Tn).   (1)

Thus k_n K_(k_n)->1/2 in L1 when k_n->infinity and k_n/n->0.

Proof. C027's explicit positive moment bounds give, including k=0,1 by
increasing the constant,

    E K_j^p<=C_(K0,p,T)/(j+1)^p, p=1,2, j<=Tn.                (2)

The coarse reciprocal multiplier estimates C045(5) give

    E V_j<=C_(K0,T)(j+1)/n,
    E V_j^2<=C_(K0,T)(j+1)^2/n^2.                            (3)

Indeed, conditionally on K_j=q and V_j=v,
E V_(j+1)^p <=(1+C/n)v^p+(C/n)v^(p-1) for p=1,2.
Sum first for p=1, then for p=2, starting at V0=1/(nK0). All moments
are finite: conditional inverse sample moments are uniformly finite by
C044 on0<q<=Q, and iteration through finitely many layers preserves this.

Let M_k be the martingale of centered reciprocal increments. C045(5)
and (3) imply

    ||M_k||_2<=C[sqrt(k^3/n^3)+sqrt(k)/n].

The drift estimate C045(6), (2)-(3), and Minkowski give

    ||V_k-V0-2k/n-M_k||_2
        <=C[k(k+1)/n^2+log(k+1)/n+k/n^2
                                      +k(k+1)/n^(5/2)].

This is the C040 martingale argument with K replacing theta and a=2.
It uses no independence between the current state and its conditional
drift; only orthogonality of martingale differences across layers.
Consequently for Z_k=nV_k/k,

    ||Z_k-2||_2<=C[k^(-1/2)+sqrt(k/n)].

Since 1/Z_k=kK_k has a uniformly bounded second moment by (2), inversion
is controlled exactly as in C040: on Z_k>=1 the inverse map is Lipschitz;
on its complement Chebyshev and Cauchy-Schwarz bound the L1 contribution
by C||Z_k-2||_2. This proves(1).

In particular, for fixed t>0 and N=floor(nt),

    sum_(k=1)^(N-1) E K_k=(1/2)log(n)+O_(K0,t)(1),            (4)

because the absolute error term in E K_k is bounded by
C[k^(-3/2)+1/sqrt(nk)], whose sum is bounded through N<=tn.

## C047: a logarithmic bias for the exact reciprocal mean

For every fixed K0>0 and t>0,

    E[1/(nK_floor(nt))]
      = exp(2t)-1 -(5/6)exp(2t)log(n)/n+O_(K0,t)(1/n).        (5)

The limiting mean exp(2t)-1 is the mean of the reciprocal SDE
dV=(2V+2)dt+sqrt(2)VdW,V0=0. This numerical coefficient identifies the
leading logarithmic correction, not the coefficient of the remaining1/n
term. The statement concerns an exact integrable raw reciprocal mean,
unlike the ReLU angle reciprocal.

Proof. Write h=1/n. The exact conditional mean of the limiting linear
diffusion after time h from v is

    L_h(v)=(v+1)exp(2h)-1.

C045(4), subtracting the h^2 coefficient2v+2 of L_h(v)-v, gives on
K=q<=epsilon

    E[V_next | v]-L_h(v)
      =[2v-6-5/(3v)]/n^2+rho_n(v),
    |rho_n(v)|<=C[v/n^(5/2)
                   +(1+v+1/v+1/v^2)/n^3+v exp(-cn)].        (6)

On epsilon<q<=Q, v<=1/(n epsilon). The global inverse sample moment
bound gives E V_next<=C_Q v<=C/n. Both L_h(v)-v and the displayed main
correction in(6) are also O(1/n), since1/v=nq<=nQ. Hence the remaining
defect is bounded by C_Q/n on this large-variance range.

Along the exact chain, the expected number of large-variance visits is
bounded by epsilon^(-2)sum E K_k^2<=C_(K0,T), by (2). On the small range,
use (2)-(3) and1/V_k=nK_k in(6). Summation through N<=Tn yields

    sum_(k=0)^(N-1) E|rho_n(V_k)|<=C_(K0,T)/n.               (7)

For clarity, the inverse-square contribution is at most
n^(-1)sum E K_k^2=O(1/n); the inverse first-power contribution is
O(log(n+1)/n^2); the v/n^(5/2) term sums to O(n^(-3/2)); all remaining
terms are smaller or O(1/n). The large-variance bound was included
separately, so(7) does not apply the small-q Taylor series globally.

Let w_k=exp(2(t_n-(k+1)/n)), t_n=N/n. The affine nature of L_h makes
conditional-mean telescoping exact:

    E V_N - [(V0+1)exp(2t_n)-1]
      =sum_(k=0)^(N-1) w_k E[E(V_(k+1)|V_k)-L_h(V_k)].       (8)

All expectations are legitimate by (3). The weighted sum of the errors
in(7) remains O(1/n). The nonsingular correction2V_k-6 in(6) contributes
O(1/n), using (3). The singular correction contributes

    -(5/(3n)) sum_(k=0)^(N-1) w_k E K_k.

The k=0 term is O_(K0,t)(1/n). For k>=1,
|w_k-exp(2t)|<=C_t(k+1)/n, so (2) bounds the total weighted occupation
error by a constant. Equation(4) therefore gives

    sum_(k=1)^(N-1) w_k E K_k
                        =(exp(2t)/2)log(n)+O_(K0,t)(1).

Insert this into(8), and use V0=1/(nK0), |t_n-t|<=1/n. The initial-state
and fractional-layer effects are O(1/n). This proves(5).

## Scope

C047 is a first finite-width correction for an exactly critical unshaped
tanh scalar observable; it does not prove Target3's all-order uniform
finite-width cumulant expansion. Its proof does not require C026 and
never replaces the model by the shaped tanh model in Li-Nica-Roy.
Independent review is required for C044's inverse-tail deletion, the
coefficient -5/3 in C045, and the global summation of the small-q remainder.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:33310ec7d7ee9992c8f2862dbcd7608afde5016da91276ffa01336685b6b5ff6","revision_digest":"sha256:515fe058a5192e3ef08957c4adfba4362dd6ba75e9ef9800f5baddd34aefb3eb","source_id":"own-work:T244-w691-C047:v1","source_revision":"2026-10-20-v1","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

[Lemma 20 of arXiv:2606.11271, '\LARGE The $K$-th nearest neighbor random walk on a Poisson point process gets trapped'] On $\cE_n$, there exist $m \in \{1,\dots,n-1\}$, $T \in \cT_m$, an embedding $x$ of $T$

		\item $An \le M \sum_{v} (r(v)+1)$.
	\end{enumerate}

[Lemma lem:comXs of arXiv:2510.26724, 'Sharp Fuss-Catalan thresholds in graph bootstrap percolation'] Suppose that $S$ is a 
partial TWG for a given edge $e$, 
with 
\begin{itemize}
\item $\sigma=\sigma(S)$ many vertices not in $e$; and 
\item edge efficiency $\mathcal E=\mathcal E(S)$. 
\end{itemize}
Suppose also that $V$ 
is a vertex set of size $(r-2)k+2$
that contains 
\begin{itemize}
\item all vertices in $S$; 
\item the edge $e$; and 
\item an additional 
$\sigma'=(r-2)k-\sigma$
other vertices.
\end{itemize}
Then the number of $k$-TWGs $T$ for $e$ 
on $V$  
such that $S\subsetneq T$ is at most
\[
k^{c(\mathcal E+1)}\gamma^{\sigma'}\sigma'!,
\]
for some constants $c$ 
depending only on $r$.

body:
Let f be twice continuously differentiable on [a,b]. For the composite trapezoidal rule with n equal subintervals of width h = (b-a)/n and nodes x_k = a + k*h, approximating the integral by T_n = h * ( f(x_0)/2 + f(x_1) + ... + f(x_{n-1}) + f(x_n)/2 ), the error satisfies integral_a^b f(x) dx - T_n = -( (b-a) * h^2 / 12 ) * f''(xi) for some xi in (a,b). In particular, | integral_a^b f(x) dx - T_n | <= ( (b-a) * h^2 / 12 ) * max_{x in [a,b]} |f''(x)|, so the error shrinks quadratically in h (equivalently as 1/n^2) as the number of subintervals grows.

[Corollary 14 (First and second variation equations) of arXiv:2606.15432, 'A Concavity Theorem for the Parisi PDE'] Let \(\gamma\in\Opendenseset_\alpha\) and
\(h,h_1,h_2\in\Hoelder{\alpha/2}([0,1])\). Then
\(V_h^\gamma\in\mathcal X_1\) is the unique solution of
\begin{equation}

\begin{cases}
-\partial_s V_h^\gamma
=
\gamma(s)L_s^\gamma V_h^\gamma
+
\dfrac12h(s)v^\gamma,
& (s,x)\in[0,1)\times\R,
\\[0.6ex]
V_h^\gamma(1,x)=0,
& x\in\R,
\end{cases}
\end{equation}
where \(v^\gamma\) is the quantity fixed in Section~\ref{sec:preliminaries}.
Moreover, \(W_{h_1,h_2}^\gamma\in\mathcal X_1\) is the unique solution of
\begin{equation}

\begin{cases}
\begin{aligned}
-\partial_s W_{h_1,h_2}^\gamma
={}&
\gamma(s)L_s^\gamma W_{h_1,h_2}^\gamma
+
h_1(s)L_s^\gamma V_{h_2}^\gamma
+
h_2(s)L_s^\gamma V_{h_1}^\gamma
\\
&+
\gamma(s)s\,\partial_xV_{h_1}^\gamma\,\partial_xV_{h_2}^\gamma,
\end{aligned}
& (s,x)\in[0,1)\times\R,
\\[0.6ex]
W_{h_1,h_2}^\gamma(1,x)=0,
& x\in\R.
\end{cases}
\end{equation}
The map \(h\mapsto V_h^\gamma\) is linear, and
\((h_1,h_2)\mapsto W_{h_1,h_2}^\gamma\) is symmetric bilinear.

[Lem gen Kac of arXiv:2608.25471, 'Exact Hausdorff measures and fine geometry of collisions of independent Markov processes'] {Kajino_Noda_26_Kac}}]  
  Let $A=(A_{t})_{t \geq 0}$ be a PCAF and let $\nu$ be the associated smooth measure.
  Let $F \colon (0,\infty) \times \Omega \to [0,\infty]$ be 
  $\mathcal{B}((0,\infty)) \otimes \EuScript{F}_{\infty}$-measurable, set
  $F_{t}(\omega) \coloneqq F(t, \omega)$ for $(t, \omega) \in (0,\infty) \times \Omega$,
  and assume that the following conditions are satisfied:
  \begin{enumerate} [label = \textup{(\roman*)}]
    \item  
    there exists a set $\Lambda \in \EuScript{F}_{\infty}$ with $P_x(\Lambda) = 1$ for all $x \in M$ such that
    the function $(0,\infty) \times \Omega \ni (t, \omega) \mapsto 1_{\Lambda}(\omega) F_{t} \circ \theta_{t}(\omega) = 1_{\Lambda}(\omega) F_{t}(\theta_{t}\omega)$ is 
    $\mathcal{B}((0,\infty)) \otimes \EuScript{F}_{\infty}$-measurable;
    \item  
      the function $(0,\infty) \times M \ni (t, x) \mapsto E_{x}[F_{t}]$ is Borel measurable.
  \end{enumerate}
  Then, for any $t \in (0, \infty]$ and $x \in M$,
  \begin{equation} 
    E_{x}\biggl[ \int_{0}^{t} F_s \circ \theta_{s}\, dA_{s} \biggr]
    = 
    \int_{0}^{t} \int_M p_s(x, y) E_y[F_s]\, \nu(dy)\, ds.
  \end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

DRAFT proof (unaudited), T421-W706-005 v1. The common-fixed-point conclusion of Theorem 1 as printed on p.7 of Bock-Weiss arXiv:2210.02070v1 does not follow from its hypotheses. On the closed set X=[0,2], the maps T(t,x)=x/2+2^(-t), t>=0, map X to X, contract uniformly by 1/2, and satisfy |T(t+1,x)-T(t,x)|=2^(-t-1). But their individual fixed points 2^(1-t) are different, so they have no common fixed point. The trajectories do converge to 0, the fixed point of the limiting map; common-fixed-point and limiting-fixed-point statements must be distinguished. This checks the printed statement only, not the validity of the paper as a whole.

[Lemma 10 of arXiv:2604.09248, '\bfseries Limit laws for longest edges in empty region graphs'] Assume that {$S$ is as in \eqref{eq:SetswithoutRot} with a compact and star-shaped set $K\subset\RR^d$} and let $c>0$. Let $x,y,u,v \in \RR^d$ be such that $\lVert x-y \rVert \ge \lVert u-v \rVert$. Then,
\[
\vol(S(x,y)\setminus S(u,v)) \ge {1\over c+1}{\vol(K)\over {\rm diam}(K)} \Big\lVert \frac{x+y}{2} - \frac{u+v}{2} \Big\rVert \lVert x-y \rVert^{d-1},
\]
whenever {$\lVert \frac{x+y}{2} - \frac{u+v}{2} \rVert\leq c\,{\rm diam}(K) \lVert x-y \rVert$.}

Use n=4 stratified inputs x_(s,t)=(1,e s,e^2 t)/sqrt(1+e^2+e^4), s,t in {-1,1}, test law uniform on those same four points, linear single-index teacher g=(s+t)/4, and independent plus/minus 1/2 label noise. Let f=m^(-1/2) sum_j a_j ReLU(w_j^T x), trained in both layers by simultaneous GD of step 1/2 on squared residual norm divided by 8, derivative zero at zero. Initialize hidden weights iid N(0,I_3), and independent readouts a_j=nu epsilon_j with iid centered signs independent of label noise. Risk is clean test MSE averaged over all sixteen training-noise patterns, conditional on network initialization. Assuming the positive limiting risk witness margins proved in the unaudited C007 draft, for every sufficiently small fixed e and confidence tolerance alpha in (0,1), there exists nu>0 FIXED WITH RESPECT TO WIDTH such that every sufficiently large width exhibits the same three strict descent-rise-descent witness differences with probability at least 1-alpha over initialization. A finite-horizon bound controls prediction error by d+F_T nu^2+(G_T nu+J_T)/sqrt(m)+M_T/m+(T/2)Y m^(-1/4), with explicit nonnegative recurrences in the linked proof; its event failure is at most 2/(3m)+48/sqrt(m)+2nu^2/d^2. Choosing variance additionally from a positive finite central-peak gap transfers C007 peak localization along e tending to zero, allowing nu to shrink with e and confidence. This is not an assertion for arbitrary prescribed variance or a peak limit with one variance fixed across scales. No iid Gaussian sampling, nonlinear teacher, high probability over label noise, practical width, novelty, or full Target 1 completion is claimed.

Let (X, Y1, Y2) be jointly Gaussian with S11 = Cov(Y1), S12 = Cov(Y1, Y2), S22 = Cov(Y2), C1 = Cov(X, Y1), C2 = Cov(X, Y2), possibly singular, with Moore-Penrose inverses; let m1 and K1 be the conditional mean and covariance of X given Y1 = y1, T = S22 - S12^T S11^+ S12, D = C2 - C1 S11^+ S12, and w = y2 - mu2 - S12^T S11^+ (y1 - mu1) the innovation of the second observation. Then W = Y2 - mu2 - S12^T S11^+ (Y1 - mu1) is Gaussian, independent of Y1, with covariance T, and Cov(X, W) = D, which is also the conditional cross-covariance of X and Y2 given Y1.

[Theorem BEBT! of arXiv:2412.09290, 'Asymptotics of Harish-Chandra transform and infinitesimal freeness'] Let $A$ be a random Hermitian matrix of size $N$ and assume
  that for every $r \in \mathbb{N}$ one has
  \begin{equation}
    \lim_{N \rightarrow \infty} \log \mathbb{E} [H \text{} C (x_1, \ldots,
    x_r, 0^{N - r} ; \lambda_1 (A), \ldots, \lambda_N (A))] = \sum_{i = 1}^r
    \Psi (x_i), 
  \end{equation}
  where $\Psi$ is a smooth function in a neighborhood of $0$ and the above
  convergence is uniform in a neighborhood of $0^r$. Then for every $k \in
  \mathbb{N}$, the $k$-th moment of the random measure $\sum_{i = 1}^N
  \delta \left( N^{- 1} \lambda_i (A) \right)$ converges as $N \rightarrow \infty$ in
  probability to $\Psi^{(k)} (0) / (k - 1) !$.
title: Theorem BEBT! of arXiv:2412.09290

[Theorem theo:wsobo of arXiv:2411.10235, '\textbf{Smooth transport map via diffusion process}'] For $\phi\in C^2(\mathbb{R}^d)$ satisfying $\phi(x)=a\|x\|^{1+s}$ for $\|x\|\geq K,$ with $ K,a,s>0$, define the measure $\mu$ having a density $d\mu(x) = \exp(-\phi(x))dx$ with respect to the $d$-dimensional Lebesgue measure. Then, for all $k\in \mathbb{N}_{>0}$ and $f:\mathbb{R}^d\rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ with $\|f\|_{L_{\mu}^2}=1$, we have
\begin{align*}
    \int |f(x)|^2|\log(|f(x)|)|^{2sk/(s+1)}d\mu(x)\leq C \sum_{|\alpha|=0}^k\|D^\alpha f\|^2_{L_{\mu}^2}.
\end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Let $K \subset X$ and $L \subset Y$ be compact, geodesically convex sets containing the origin in their respective interiors. Then,

\]

[Definition 3 (Polynomials and their coefficients) of arXiv:2606.19115, 'Finite free perpetuities'] Every polynomial $p\in \tilde\pols_{\leq n}(\C)$ can be written uniquely in the form
\begin{align*}
    p(z) &= \sum_{k=0}^n (-1)^k \binom{n}{k} \coef{k}{n}(p) z^{n-k}.
\end{align*}
In particular, if $p(z) = \prod_{i=1}^n (z-\lambda_i) \in \pols_n(\C)$, then
\[ \coef{k}{n}(p) = \binom{n}{k}^{-1} \sum_{1 \le i_1 < \dots < i_k \le n} \lambda_{i_1} \cdots \lambda_{i_k} \]
for $k\in\{1,\dots,n\}$, while $\coef{0}{n}(p) = 1$.

We say that a polynomial $p\in\tilde\pols_{\leq n}(\C)$ is $d$-monic, $d\in\{0,\ldots,n\}$, if $\coef{d}{n}(p)=1$. In particular, monic polynomials are $0$-monic. More precisely, this notion depends on both \(n\) and \(d\). We suppress the parameter \(n\) when it is clear from the context.
title: Polynomials and their coefficients

[Openproblem op:uniqueness of arXiv:2609.01557, '$L^\infty$ Variational Approximation of the Aubry Set'] Assume
\[
\int_{\mathbb T^n} u_k\,dx=0.
\]
Does the whole sequence \(u_k\) converge uniformly as \(k\to\infty\)?
Equivalently, can two different subsequences converge to different absolute
minimizers? By (cor:lowdim of the paper), when $n\leq 3$, every subsequential limit \(u\) satisfies
\[
D_u=\mathcal A,
\]
but this characterization alone does not determine \(u\) uniquely. (Stated as a problem by the paper; open unless the paper says otherwise.)
title: Uniqueness of the limit

[Proposition 14 (Power sums and the kernel of \(\rho\)) of arXiv:2609.03881, 'Eulerian insertion operators and an Eulerian form of the Pieri rule'] We have
$\rho(p_m)=\delta^mE=\delta^{m-1}\G_1$.
Consequently, if \(\lambda\vdash n\), then
$\rho(p_\lambda)=\delta^nE^{\ell(\lambda)}$.
Moreover, $\ker\rho
  =
  \left\langle
    p_i p_{j+1}-p_{i+1}p_j:\ 1\leq i<j
  \right\rangle$.
In particular, for \(n\geq1\),
\[
  \rho(\Lambda_n)
  =
  \delta^n\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb Q}
  \{E,E^2,\ldots,E^n\},~
  \dim\ker(\rho|_{\Lambda_n})=p(n)-n,
\]
where \(p(n)\) is the number of partitions of \(n\).

[Proposition prop:gauge-link of arXiv:2608.01253, 'The pseudo-quantum representation of \\finite reversible Markov chains'] Let $\mathcal{E}:=\operatorname{diag}\bigl(i^{\,n-k}\bigr)_{k=0}^{n}$, a fixed unitary diagonal
matrix independent of $t$, and let $\lvert \psi_\theta\rangle:=e^{-i\thetaJ_x}\lvert n\rangle$ be
the register coherent state of the imaginary slice. Then

\begin{equation}
\mathcal{E}\,J_x\,\mathcal{E}^{-1}=J_y,\qquad \mathcal{E}\lvert n\rangle=\lvert n\rangle,\qquad
\mathcal{E}\ket{\psi_{\theta}}=e^{-i\thetaJ_y}\lvert n\rangle,

\end{equation}

so $\ket{\sqrt{\pi_t}}=\mathcal{E}\ket{\psi_{\theta(t)}}$ and
$\sigma^{\mathrm{FR}}_t=\mathcal{E}\,\ketbra{\psi_{\theta(t)}}{\psi_{\theta(t)}}\,\mathcal{E}^{*}$.

[Proposition prop-psiconvp-bsdequadr of arXiv:2605.07832, 'A Bismut -Elworthy formula for BSDEs with degenerate noise'] Let $(X,Y,Z)$ be solution of the forward-backward system ((fbsde of the paper)),
and assume that hypotheses (ip_forward of the paper) and (ip-psiphi of the paper) hold
true and let $(Y^n,Z^n)$ be solution of the BSDE in the forward-backward system ((fbsde of the paper))
with generator  $\psi_n$ in the place of $\psi$, where $\psi_n$ is defined in ((infsupconvpsi of the paper)). Namely,
$(Y^n,Z^n)$ solve the following BSDE:
\begin{equation}
    \left\{\begin{array}{l}\displaystyle
 dY^{n,t,x}_\tau=-\psi_n(\tau,X^{t,x}_\tau,Y^{n,t,x}_\tau,Z^{n,t,x}_\tau)\;d\tau+Z^{n,t,x}_\tau\;dW_\tau,
  \\\displaystyle
  Y^{n,t,x}_T=\phi(X_T),
\end{array}\right.
\end{equation}
Then, for all $p\geq 1$, the unique solution of the markovian BSDE in ((fbsde of the paper)) is such that
\[
 \Vert Y-Y^n\Vert _{{\cal S}^p}+\Vert Z-Z^n\Vert_{{\cal M}^p}\rightarrow 0 \qquad \text{as }n\rightarrow \infty.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Test the d = 3 analogue of the Apollonian structure on the simplest candidates (diagonal matrices). Result: Gamma(Z^d) is the set of symmetric matrices A for which there is an integer-valued function on Z^d whose discrete Laplacian is at most the constant ... with quadratic growth A: g(x) = (1/2) x^T A x + (lower order) integer-valued superharmonic. Diagonal A = diag(a_1,...,a_d): g(x) = sum_i (1/2) a_i x_i^2 rounded is integer-valued; the discrete Laplacian of x -> ceil(a x^2 / 2) in one dimension is at most a + 1 ... in one dimension the maximal a with an integer superharmonic quadratic of curvature a is determined by the 1D odometer; for diagonal matrices the problem separates into d one-dimensional problems and the maximal diagonal elements are rational (the 1D maximal curvatures are rational, e.g. the 1D sandpile has only finitely many patterns). This gives rational maximal elements on the diagonal slice, but maximality in Gamma(Z^d) (not just among diagonal matrices) is not implied: a diagonal A might be dominated by a non-diagonal B. In d = 2 the LPS classification shows the maximal elements are dense in the boundary and rational; for d = 3 the analogue of the Apollonian packing would be a packing by spheres of a slab, whose tangency structure has more degrees of freedom (a sphere touching four others is not determined by rational data in general: Descartes-type relations in 3D involve a quadratic form on curvatures with generic irrational solutions unless the initial spheres are chosen integrally). This suggests that rationality may FAIL in d = 3 unless the initial configuration forces integrality via the Soddy-Gosset relation with integer curvatures; the analogue of the band packing in d = 3 has initial curvatures determined by the lattice (integer), and integral Apollonian-type packings in 3D do have all curvatures integral when the initial ones are (Soddy-Gosset gives a quadratic recursion preserving integrality). So rationality is plausible in d = 3 if the correspondence to packings persists, and isolation would be false (packings are dense in the boundary). Recorded as a conjectural picture with the Soddy-Gosset integrality argument as the reason to expect rational entries. Key identity: If the d = 3 maximal elements correspond to a sphere packing generated from integer initial curvatures, Soddy-Gosset integrality gives rational entries. Obstruction: No d = 3 analogue of the LPS correspondence between Gamma(Z^d) and packings.

[Thm 7 of arXiv:2604.11489, '2604.11489'] Let $\{X_n, n\ge 1\}$ be a sequence of independent and identically distributed random variables with common nonuniform distribution $\{p_i, i\ge 1\}$ satisfying $\ee|\ln p(X_1)|^{2+\delta} < \infty$. Assume that there exists an integer valued function $K(n)$ such that, for some $0< \delta<\frac{1}{2}$,
\beq
K(n)\le n^{\frac{1}{2}-\delta},\ \ n^{\frac{1}{2}+\delta}\ln n\sum_{i=K(n)}^{\infty}p_i \leq C
\ \ \text{and}\ \ -n^{\frac{1}{2}+\delta}\sum_{i=K(n)}^{\infty}p_i\ln p_i\leq C.
\deq
If there exists an $\epsilon \in (1/2, 1)$ with
\beq
\sum_{i=1}^{\infty}p_{i}^{1-\epsilon}<\infty,
\deq
then we have
\beq
\sup_x\left|\pp\left(\frac{\sqrt{n}}{\sigma}(\hat H_{JK}-H)\le x\right)-\Phi(x)\right|\le
Cn^{-\frac{\delta}{2}}+Cn^{\frac{1}{4}-\frac{\epsilon}{2}},
\deq
where $\Phi$ denotes the standard normal distribution function and $\sigma^2=Var(\ln p(X_1))$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Thm 7 of arXiv:2604.11489

[Definition def:bs-Ho of arXiv:2412.05142, 'Strong convergence of the Euler scheme for singular kinetic SDEs driven by $\alpha$-stable'] For a function $f:{\mathbb R}^{2d}\to{\mathbb R}$,  the first-order difference operator is defined by
$$
\delta^{(1)}_hf(z):=\delta_hf(z):=f(z+h)-f(z),\ \ z, h\in{\mathbb R}^{2d}.
$$
For $M\in{\mathbb N}$, the $M$-order difference operator  is defined recursively by
$
\delta^{(M+1)}_hf(z)=\delta_h\circ\delta^{(M)}_hf(z).
$

[Lemma lem:conditional-convolution of arXiv:2608.26745, 'Moderate Deviations for the Largest Eigenvalue of a Randomly Deformed Gaussian Unitary Ens'] Let $X_N+Y_N$ be a decomposition with $Y_N$ measurable with respect to a
$\sigma$-algebra $\mathcal F_N$.  Let $a_N\to\infty$, and let $\alpha_N a_N\to\infty$.
Assume the following.

\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.7em]
\item There are events $\mathcal G_N\in\mathcal F_N$ whose complements are
superexponentially small at the speeds
$a_N^{3/2}$, $a_N^3$, and $\alpha_N^2a_N^2$.
\item Uniformly on $\mathcal G_N$ and uniformly for $u$ in compact subsets of
$(0,\infty)$,
\begin{align*}
 \log\mathbb P(X_N>a_Nu\mid\mathcal F_N)
 =-a_N^{3/2}\left(\frac43u^{3/2}+o(1)\right),\\
 \log\mathbb P(X_N\le-a_Nu\mid\mathcal F_N)
 =-a_N^3\left(\frac1{12}u^3+o(1)\right).
\end{align*}
\item The variables $Y_N/a_N$ satisfy an MDP with speed
$\alpha_N^2a_N^2$ and rate $v^2/(2\sigma^2)$.
\end{enumerate}

Here and below, fixed versions of the conditional probabilities are used.
Uniformity on $\mathcal G_N$ means that the displayed deterministic error bounds hold
for almost every outcome in $\mathcal G_N$.

Then the six conclusions of (thm:main of the paper) hold with $Z_N$ replaced by
$X_N+Y_N$.

body: [Definition 1.1 (Connective constants) of arXiv:2604.02746, 'Zero-Freeness of the Hard-Core Model with Bounded Connective Constant'] For a family H of finite graphs, the k-depth connective constant of H for a fixed k, denoted by µk(H), is supG∈H µk(G). The lower connective constant of H, denoted by µinf(H), is infk≥1 µk(H). For an infinite graph G, let HG denote the set of all finite subgraphs of G. We establish the following relationship: for any infinite graph G with connective constant σ(G), µinf(HG) ≤σ(G).

[Cor SSL0 of arXiv:2609.01751, 'Orthogonal polynomials which are eigenfunctions of a partial differential operator'] Let ${\kappa}_1,\ldots, {\kappa}_{d_2-1} > -1$ and ${\kappa}_{d_2} = -1$. The spectral operator ${\mathfrak D}_{{\boldsymbol{\kappa}}}^{{\mathbb S} \rtimes \Sigma} $ can be 
written as 
\begin{align} 
  {\mathfrak D}_{{\boldsymbol{\kappa}}}^{{\mathbb S} \rtimes \Sigma} & = 
   \frac{1}{{\mathsf W}_{{\boldsymbol{\kappa}}}^{{\mathbb S} \rtimes \Sigma} (\bm x, \bm y)}  
       \sum_{i=1}^{d_2-1} (\partial_{y_i} - \partial_{y_{d_2}}) y_i |{\bm y}|^{d_2} {\mathsf W}_{{\boldsymbol{\kappa}}}^{{\mathbb S} \rtimes \Sigma} (\bm x, \bm y)
         (\partial_{y_i} - \partial_{y_d}) \\
   & +  \frac{1}{|\bm y|^{d_1-1}} \frac{1}{{\mathsf W}_{{\boldsymbol{\kappa}}}^{{\mathbb S} \rtimes \Sigma} (\bm x, \bm y)}     
        \partial_{y_d}  \big( |\bm y|^{d_1} {\mathsf W}_{{\boldsymbol{\kappa}}}^{{\mathbb S} \rtimes \Sigma} (\bm x, \bm y) \partial_{y_d} \big)
        + \frac{1}{|\bm y|} \Delta_0^{(\bm x)}. \notag 

 \end{align}
In particular, it follows that 
\begin{align}  
    - &\int_{{\mathbb S}^{d_1-1}\! \rtimes {\mathbb R}_\Sigma^{d_2}}{\mathfrak D}_{{\boldsymbol{\kappa}}}^{{\mathbb S} \rtimes \Sigma} 
    f (\bm x,\bm y) \cdot g(\bm x, \bm y) {\mathsf W}_{{\boldsymbol{\kappa}}}^{{\mathbb S} \rtimes \Sigma} (\bm y) \mathrm{d} \sigma(\bm x, \bm y)  \\ 
  &   =  \int_{{\mathbb S}^{d_1-1}\! \rtimes {\mathbb R}_\Sigma^{d_2}}  \frac{1}{|\bm y|}  \sum_{1 \le i< j \le d_1}  D_{i,j}^{(\bm x)} f(\bm x, \bm y)  D_{i,j}^{(\bm x)} g(\bm x, \bm y) 
  {\mathsf W}_{{\boldsymbol{\kappa}}}^{{\mathbb S} \rtimes \Sigma}(\bm y)  \mathrm{d} \sigma({\bm x}, {\bm y})    \notag \\ 
  & + \int_{{\mathbb S}^{d_1-1}\! \rtimes {\mathbb R}_\Sigma^{d_2}}   \sum_{i=1}^{d_2-1} (\partial_{y_i} - \partial_{y_d}) f(\bm x,\bm y) \cdot 
    (\partial_{y_i} - \partial_{y_d})g(\bm x,\bm y)
  {\mathsf W}_{{\boldsymbol{\kappa}}}^{{\mathbb S} \rtimes \Sigma}(\bm y)  \mathrm{d} \sigma(\bm x, \bm y)    \notag \\
    &  +  \int_{{\mathbb S}^{d_1-1}\! \rtimes {\mathbb R}_\Sigma^{d_2}}  |{\bm y}|^{d_1} \partial_{y_d} f(\bm x,\bm y) \partial_{y_d} g(\bm x,\bm y) 
       |{\bm y}| {\mathsf W}_{{\boldsymbol{\kappa}}}^{{\mathbb S} \rtimes \Sigma}(\bm y)   \mathrm{d} \sigma(\bm x,\bm y).  \notag
 \end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: [Theorem of arXiv:2411.16651, 'On a problem of optimal mixing'] Let $X$ and $Y$ be completely regular topological spaces, let $\mu_1,\dots,\mu_n,\nu$ be Radon measures, let cost function  $c:X\times Y\to [0,+\infty)$ be lower semi-continuous, let $\frac{d\mu_i}{d\mu}$ be continuous $\mu$-a.s., then infimum in ((kantorovich of the paper)) is attained, that is, there is optimal plan $\pi\in\Pi(\overrightarrow{\mu},\nu)$.

body: [Theorem 4.4 of arXiv:2510.05566, 'Domain-Shift-Aware Conformal Prediction for Large Language Models'] shows that the same discrepancy term governing the lower bound also governs possible over-coverage. The only additional term is E[πn+1], which is the expected mass assigned to the point at infinity. This term appears because the empirical score distribution used by DS-CP includes the regularization mass λ, and hence the resulting quantile can be inflated relative to the oracle exchangeable benchmark.
title: Theorem 4.4 of arXiv:2510.05566: Domain-Shift-Aware Conformal Prediction for Large Language Models

body: For an m by n real or complex matrix A with entries a_{ij} and singular values sigma_1 >= ... >= sigma_{min(m,n)} >= 0, the Frobenius norm is ||A||_F = sqrt(sum_{i,j} |a_{ij}|^2) = sqrt(trace(A* A)) = sqrt(sum_i sigma_i^2). The Frobenius norm is the norm induced by the trace inner product <A,B> = trace(A* B) on the space of m by n matrices, and it is submultiplicative: ||AB||_F <= ||A||_F ||B||_F whenever the product is defined. [standard, e.g. Horn and Johnson, Matrix Analysis]
title: Frobenius (Hilbert-Schmidt) Norm of a Matrix

[Definition 48 (Coalescent subtrees) of arXiv:2511.09517, 'From Cannings model to Brownian motion conditioned on local time profile'] For \(0\le j\le h^*\), define the collection of the coalescent subtrees at height \(j\) by
\[
\mathbf{T}_j=\mathbf{T}_j(n,h^*):=\big\{\mathscr{T}^n(v): v\in \cX_j\big\}.
\]
Each element of \(\mathbf{T}_j\) is a subtree rooted at a vertex at height \(j\) that admits at least one descendant at height \(h^*\). Note that \(|\mathbf{T}_j|=|\cX_j|=X_j\).

We then write \(\mathsf{T}_1,\ldots,\mathsf{T}_{|\mathbf{T}_j|}\) for a uniform random ordering of the elements of \(\mathbf{T}_j\). Concretely, conditionally on \(\mathscr{T}^n\), we first list the elements of \(\mathbf{T}_j\) according to the lexicographical order of their roots, denoted by \(\mathbf{T}_j^{(1)},\ldots,\mathbf{T}_j^{(|\mathbf{T}_j|)}\). Then we choose a permutation \(\pi\) uniformly at random from the symmetric group on \(|\mathbf{T}_j|\) elements, and define
\[
(\mathsf{T}_1,\ldots,\mathsf{T}_{|\mathbf{T}_j|})
:= (\mathbf{T}_j^{(\pi(1))},\ldots,\mathbf{T}_j^{(\pi(|\mathbf{T}_j|))}).
\]
Finally, we introduce the labeling map
\begin{align}
    \Lambda_j : \mathbf{T}_j \longrightarrow \{1,\ldots,|\mathbf{T}_j|\}, \qquad
\Lambda_j(\mathsf{T}_i) := i,
\end{align}
which assigns to each coalescent subtree its index in the random ordering.  
The random orderings (and hence the labeling maps \(\Lambda_j\)) are taken independently across different heights~\(j\).
title: Coalescent subtrees

\end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Theorem 2.4 of arXiv:2110.05374, 'When Janson meets McDiarmid: Bounded difference inequalities under graph-dependence'] Let the Ω-valued random vector X be G-dependent and let f : Ω → R be forest-decomposable c-Lipschitz with respect to G. Then for every t > 0, P(f(X) − E[f(X)] ≥ t) ≤ exp(−2t²/D(G, c)), where D(G, c) := min over {(F_k, w_k)}_k ∈ FFC(G) of ( Σ_k w_k √( Σ_{{i,j}∈E(G[F_k])} (c_i + c_j)² + Σ_{T∈T(F_k)} c_{min,k,T}² ) )², with c_{min,k,T} := min{c_i : i ∈ T} for T ∈ T(F_k). By Remark 2.5 of the paper, D(G, c) ≤ χ_f(G)‖c‖₂², the denominator of Janson's inequality (take a fractional independent vertex cover).
c-Lipschitz (Definition 1.1 of the paper): Ω = Ω_1 × ... × Ω_n is a product of Polish spaces, c = (c_1, ..., c_n) ∈ R_+^n, and f : Ω → R is c-Lipschitz when |f(x) − f(x')| ≤ Σ_{i=1}^n c_i 1{x_i ≠ x'_i} for all x, x' ∈ Ω (Lipschitz for the c-weighted Hamming distance).
G-dependent (Definition 1.3 of the paper): X = (X_i)_{i∈V(G)} is G-dependent when for all disjoint S, T ⊂ V(G) with no edge of G between S and T, the families (X_i)_{i∈S} and (X_j)_{j∈T} are independent; this is stronger than pairwise independence of non-adjacent coordinates.
Fractional forest vertex cover: a family {(F_k, w_k)}_k with F_k ⊆ V(G), w_k ∈ [0, 1] and Σ_{k: v∈F_k} w_k = 1 for every v ∈ V(G), such that each F_k induces a forest G[F_k]; T(F_k) is the set of vertex sets of the trees of G[F_k], and FFC(G) is the set of all fractional forest vertex covers of G.
Forest-decomposable c-Lipschitz with respect to G (Section 2.2 of the paper): for every {(F_k, w_k)}_k ∈ FFC(G) there are (c_i)_{i∈F_k}-Lipschitz functions f_k : Ω_{F_k} → R with f(x) = Σ_k w_k f_k(x_{F_k}) for all x ∈ Ω. The paper's sentence puts 'for all x' before 'there exist f_k'; the f_k cannot depend on x, since constant f_k would then make every f decomposable.

body:
[Definition d:derivative of arXiv:2510.13659, 'On the energy image density conjecture of Bouleau and Hirsch'] Suppose $f: X \to \mathbb{R}$ and $\phi=(\phi_1,\ldots,\phi_n): X \to\mathbb{R}^n$ are Lipschitz functions on a metric   space $(X,d)$. Then $f$ is \emph{differentiable with respect to $\phi$ at $x_0 \in X$} if there is a unique $\mathbf{a}=(a_1,\ldots,a_n) \in \mathbb{R}^n$ such that $f$ and the linear combination $a\cdot \phi = \sum_{i=1}^n a_i \phi_i$ agree to first order near $x_0$: 
		\[
		\limsup_{x \to x_0} \frac{\abs{f(x)-f(x_0)-\langle \mathbf{a}, \phi(x)-\phi(x_0) \rangle }}{d(x,x_0)}=0.
		\]
		Equivalently,  $\Lip g(x_0)=0$, where $g(\cdot)= f(\cdot)-\sum_{i=1}^n a_i \phi_i(\cdot)$. The tuple $a \in \mathbb{R}^n$ is the \emph{derivative of $f$ with respect to $\phi$} and will be denoted by $\partial_\phi f(x_0)$.
title: Definition d:derivative of arXiv:2510.13659

[Proposition prop mdp fluc of arXiv:2604.10509, 'Nonequilibrium fluctuations and moderate deviations for the occupation time of the SSEP wi'] The sequence  $\{\mu^n\}_{n \geq 1}$ satisfies the MDP with decay rate $a_n^2 $ and with rate function $\mathcal{Q}_T$. Precisely speaking, for any closed set $C$ and any open set $O$ in $D([0,T], \mathcal{D}^\prime (\mathbb T))$,
	\begin{align*}
		\limsup_{n \rightarrow \infty} \frac{1}{a_n^2} \log \mathbb P^n_{\rho_*} \big( \mu^n \in C\big) \leq - \inf_{\mu \in C} \mathcal{Q}_T (\mu),\\
		\liminf_{n \rightarrow \infty} \frac{1}{a_n^2} \log \mathbb P^n_{\rho_*} \big( \mu^n \in O\big) \geq - \inf_{\mu \in O} \mathcal{Q}_T (\mu).
	\end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Let X = (X_1,...,X_n) have independent real coordinates. (Thm 1.1) If each X_i has density <= K a.e., then for every orthogonal projection P onto a d-dimensional subspace, PX has density <= (CK)^d a.e., C absolute. (Thm 1.2) For d = 1 the optimal constant is sqrt(2): if sum a_j^2 = 1, sum a_jX_j has density <= sqrt(2)K, attained by (X_1+X_2)/sqrt(2) with X_i uniform on [-1/(2K),1/(2K)]. (Cor 1.4) With L(Z,t) = sup_u P(||Z-u||_2 <= t): if L(X_i,t) <= p for all i, then L(PX, t sqrt(d)) <= (Cp)^d. (Thm 1.5) For every m x n matrix A and delta in (0,1), L(AX, t||A||_HS) <= (C_delta p)^{(1-delta) r(A)}, where r(A) = ||A||_HS^2/||A||^2 is the stable rank and C_delta depends only on delta; with densities <= K this reads L(AX, t||A||_HS) <= (C_delta K t)^{(1-delta) r(A)}.

Assumes: independent real coordinates; densities bounded by K a.e. (Thms 1.1-1.2) or L(X_i,t) <= p (Cor 1.4, Thm 1.5); P an orthogonal projection of rank d; A arbitrary in Thm 1.5

Let p be a prime, f a polynomial with coefficients in the p-adic integers Z_p (in particular any polynomial with integer coefficients), and a in Z_p with f(a) congruent to 0 modulo p and f'(a) not congruent to 0 modulo p. Then there is a unique alpha in Z_p with f(alpha) = 0 and alpha congruent to a modulo p. Concretely: a simple root of f modulo p lifts to a unique root modulo p^k for every k, and these lifts converge p-adically to the root alpha. The general form replaces the hypothesis by |f(a)|_p < |f'(a)|_p^2, which allows f'(a) to be divisible by p.

f(a) congruent to 0 mod p
f'(a) a p-adic unit (a SIMPLE root modulo p); the double-root case needs the general form |f(a)|_p < |f'(a)|_p^2

body: The set R of real numbers is uncountable: there is no surjection from N onto R, hence no bijection between N and R. Equivalently, for every sequence x_1, x_2, x_3, ... of real numbers there is a real number different from every x_n.

Let x_1, x_2, ... be any sequence in [0,1]. Choose for each x_n a decimal expansion x_n = 0.d(n,1) d(n,2) d(n,3) ... (each digit d(n,k) in {0, ..., 9}). Define a new number x = 0.b_1 b_2 b_3 ... by the diagonal rule: b_n = 5 if d(n,n) is not 5, and b_n = 6 if d(n,n) = 5. Then x lies in [0,1], and its expansion differs from the chosen expansion of x_n in the n-th digit for every n. Because all digits of x lie in {5, 6}, its expansion contains no infinite tail of 0s or of 9s, and a real number can have two distinct decimal expansions only when one ends in all 9s and the other in all 0s; hence x has exactly one decimal expansion. If x were equal to some x_n as a real number, the chosen expansion of x_n would be a decimal expansion of x differing from x's unique expansion (they differ in digit n), which is impossible. So x differs from every x_n, and no sequence lists all of [0,1]. Since [0,1] is a subset of R, no sequence lists R, so R is uncountable.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:81845b66a64fd9e8baa9830788af1d24ccfa7255e76ef65a7c1032858629b23b","revision_digest":"sha256:5217c7a5ca26073bea088c4a23a842fa0dd29c9f47c16b42b319b5cc59055627","source_id":"wikipedia:Cantor's_diagonal_argument","source_revision":"as-read-2026-08-02","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

[Definition def:decograph of arXiv:2601.20502, 'Optimal matching under size priority'] Let $(G,o,w)$ be a vertex-rooted (resp.\ edge-rooted) weighted graph. Fix $I$ an integer and $(f_i)_{i \in \{1,...,I\}}$ some functions from $\overset{\rightarrow}{E}$ to $\overline{\mathbb{R}}$. We then say that
    $(G,o,w,(f_i)_{i \in \{1,...,I\}})$ is a \emph{decorated} vertex-rooted (resp.\ edge-rooted) weighted graph.  If $f_i$ is symmetrical then we will identify it with a map from $E$ to $\overline{\mathbb{R}}$.
title: Definition def:decograph of arXiv:2601.20502

[Lemma 5 (Double-threat lemma) of arXiv:2609.02283, 'The game chromatic number of generalized Mycielski graphs of paths and cycles'] Suppose that it is Alice's turn in a three-coloring game and that $(t_1,x_1)$ and $(t_2,x_2)$ are threats. Let $U$ be the set of currently uncolored vertices. If
\[
 \bigl(N[x_1]\cap U\bigr)\cap\bigl(N[x_2]\cap U\bigr)=\varnothing,
\]
then Bob has a winning strategy.

body:
[Proposition prop:lindeberg of arXiv:2607.22480, 'Distinguishability threshold for random geometric graphs'] There exist absolute constants $C>c>0$, such that the following holds.

Let $\xi \in \mathbb{R}^m$ be a vector with independent subgaussian coordinates, each with expectation $0$ and variance proxy at most $\sigma^2$.  Also, fix a symmetric zero-diagonal $m\times m$ matrix $M$, and a vector $\boldsymbol{a}\in\mathbb{R}^m$. Let us define
\[\delta_1=\max\big\{\sigma^2\|M\|_{op}, \sigma\|\boldsymbol{a}\|_\infty\big\} \text{  and }\delta_2=\sigma^4\|M\|_{HS}^2+\sigma^2\|\boldsymbol{a}\|_2^2.\]
If $\delta_1\leq c$, then
\begin{align*}
\log\mathbb{E} e^{\xi^TM\xi+\boldsymbol{a}^T\xi}
=\frac{1}{2}\Var(\xi^TM\xi+\boldsymbol{a}^T\xi)+O(e^{C\delta_2} \delta_1\delta_2)
\end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition prop:lindeberg of arXiv:2607.22480

[Definition 14 (Locally bounded function) of arXiv:2605.18198, 'Large deviations of crowding in finite $\beta$-ensembles'] A measurable function $f:\mathbb{R}^2 \to \mathbb{R}$ is said to be a locally bounded function if for every compact set
	$K \subset \mathbb{R}^2$,
		\[
	\|f\|_{L^\infty(K)}
	:=
	\operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{x\in K} |f(x)|
	< \infty .
	\]
	In other words, $f$ is essentially bounded on every compact subset
	of $\mathbb{R}^2$. The space of all locally bounded functions on $\R^2$ is denoted by $L^\infty_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb{R}^2)$.
title: Locally bounded function

body:
[Lemma lem:ricci-removal of arXiv:2608.29403, 'Kac's Walk on Rotation Matrices Mixes in $\boldsymbol{\Theta(n^2)}$ Steps:\\ A Proof Disco'] Let $P_z$ be the rank-one projector onto a unit decomposable bivector and
$C_z=P_z-N^{-1}I_W$.  If $L_z=-2z_{\rm mat}^2$ is the orthogonal
projector onto the plane of $z$, put
\[
 B_z=\frac{L_z-(2/n)I_H}{n-2}.
\tag{2.6.2}
\]
Then the orthogonal curvature decomposition is
\[
 C_z=W_z+X_{B_z},\qquad W_z\in\mathcal W,
 \qquad X_B(u\wedge v)=Bu\wedge v+u\wedge Bv,
\tag{2.6.3}
\]
with no scalar or $\Lambda^4H$ summand, and
\[
 \|B_z\|_\mathrm{op}=\frac1n,\qquad
 \|B_z\|_F^2=\frac{2}{n(n-2)},\qquad
 \|X_B\|_2^2=(n-2)\|B\|_F^2,\qquad
 \|X_B\|_\mathrm{op}\le2\|B\|_\mathrm{op}.
\tag{2.6.4}
\]

In the cumulative moving frame the transported $B_z$ are reverse
martingale differences.  If $\mathfrak B_r$ is their sum, then
\[
 \mathbb E\|\mathfrak B_r\|_F^2=\frac{2r}{n(n-2)},\qquad
 \mathbb E\|\mathfrak B_r\|_F^4
 \le C\frac{r^2}{n^2(n-2)^2},
\tag{2.6.5}
\]
and, for fixed $c$, uniformly over $r\le cN$,
\[
 \max_{r\le cN}\|\mathfrak B_r\|_\mathrm{op}=o_{\mathbb P}(1).
\tag{2.6.6}
\]
More quantitatively, for every fixed $L$ and $1\le p\le L\log n$,
\[
 \left(\mathbb E\max_{r\le cN}\|\mathfrak B_r\|_\mathrm{op}^p\right)^{1/p}
 \le C_{c,L}\left(
 \sqrt{\frac{p+\log n}{n}}+\frac{p+\log n}{n}
 \right)=o(1).
\tag{2.6.6a}
\]
The same martingale satisfies the dimension-free Frobenius estimate
\[
 \left(\mathbb E\max_{r\le cN}\|\mathfrak B_r\|_F^p\right)^{1/p}
 \le C_c\sqrt p,
 \qquad 2\le p\le L\log n.
\tag{2.6.6b}
\]

Finally let $A_i=\operatorname{ad}_{a_i}$.  For traceless symmetric $B$
on $H$ and arbitrary $Z\in\operatorname{End}(W)$, define
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \mathcal R_i(B,Z)&=\{X_B,[A_i,Z]\}a_i,&
 U_i(B,Z)&=\{X_B,Z\}a_i,\\
 E_i(B,Z)&=\{X_{[a_i,B]},Z\}a_i,&
 \bar E(B,Z)&=N^{-1}\sum_iE_i(B,Z).
\end{aligned}
\tag{2.6.7}
\]
Put $\Psi(T)=\sum_jA_jTa_j$ and
$H_B(Z)=-N^{-1}X_B\Psi(Z)$.  Then the exact two-gradient decomposition is
\[
 \boxed{\mathcal R_i=A_iU_i-(E_i-\bar E)
 -\frac1N\sum_jA_jV_j-H_B(Z)},
 \qquad
 \bar E=\frac1N\sum_jA_jV_j+H_B(Z),\qquad V_j=X_BZa_j,
\tag{2.6.8}
\]
and its star-normalized square functions obey
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \frac1N\sum_i\|U_i\|^2
 &\le\frac{4(n-2)}N\|B\|_F^2\|Z\|_\mathrm{op}^2,\\
 \frac1N\sum_j\|V_j\|^2
 &\le\frac{n-2}N\|B\|_F^2\|Z\|_\mathrm{op}^2,\\
 \frac1N\sum_i\|E_i-\bar E\|^2
 &\le\frac{64}{n-1}\|B\|_F^2\|Z\|_\mathrm{op}^2.
\end{aligned}
\tag{2.6.9}
\]
The residue obeys
\[
 \|H_B(Z)\|
 \le\frac{2\sqrt{n-2}}N\|B\|_\mathrm{op}\|Z\|_2.
\tag{2.6.9a}
\]

[Lem 21 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Let $\tilde{F}$ be the function from the statement of Lemma~\ref{l:fp-F-kirszbraun}. We then have
    \[\Big|F^{\ri}(\bG,\bXi,\hat{\by}(\bG,\bXi)) - \E [\tilde{F}(\bXi;\bG) | \bG]
    \Big| \le
    \frac{\epsilon'}{15}\]
with probability at least $1-e^{-cN}$.

\begin{proof}
    By Lemma~\ref{l:fp-gc} and
    \eqref{e:wishart.bound.repeated}, it holds with probability at least $1-e^{-cN}$ that $\bG$ satisifes \eqref{e:fp-F-kirszbraun-bG-event}, $\bXi$ satisfies \eqref{e:fp-F-kirszbraun-bXi-event}, and $\hat{\by} = \ytrunc$.
    On this event, $F^{\ri}(\bG,\bXi,\hat{\by}(\bG,\bXi)) = \tilde{F}(\bXi;\bG)$. It follows by gaussian concentration of measure (Lemma~\ref{l:lip.subgaus}) that
        \[\Big|\tilde{F}(\bXi;\bG) - \E [\tilde{F}(\bXi;\bG)
    \,|\,\bG] \Big| \le \frac{\epsilon'}{15}\]
with probability at least $1-e^{-cN}$, so the claim follows.
\end{proof}

body: [Lemma lem:rn_bound of arXiv:2411.13133, 'Connectivity of the adjacency graph of\\ complementary components of the $\SLE$ Fan'] Fix $\delta_2 > \delta_1 > 0$ and $\epsilon \in (0,\delta_1^2/2)$.  Fix $R > 0$ and suppose that $\rho_1, \rho_2 \in [-R,R]$.  There exists a constant $C > 0$ depending only on $\kappa$,  $\delta_1, \delta_2$, $\epsilon$, and $R$ so that the following is true.  Suppose that $\eta$ is an ${\rm SLE}_\kappa(\rho_1; \rho_2)$ process in $\mathbf{H}$ from $0$ to $\infty$ with force points located at $x_1 = -\delta \in (-\delta_2, -\delta_1)$ and $x_2= 0^+$.  Let $R_\epsilon$, $\sigma_{\epsilon}$ be as in Section~(subsec:single_force_point of the paper).  Then the law of $\eta|_{[0,\sigma_{\epsilon}]}$ is absolutely continuous with respect to that of an ${\rm SLE}_\kappa(\rho_2)$ process stopped at the corresponding time with Radon-Nikodym derivative which is at most $C$.

Own work method record, proof (unaudited), W719-T295-C016 v1; no specialist novelty asserted. Given a conditional Gaussian vector X with predictable mean mu and PSD covariance Sigma, predictable real vectors g,w, v_i=Sigma_ii and ell_i=3mu_i^2+3v_i-g_i^2, S=sum_i w_i(X_i^3-g_i^2 X_i) has conditional mean sum_i w_i[mu_i^3+(3v_i-g_i^2)mu_i] and variance (w*ell)^T Sigma(w*ell)+18(w*mu)^T Sigma^{circ 2}(w*mu)+6w^T Sigma^{circ 3}w. Here * and circ denote entrywise product and power. If Sigma<=sigma^2 I, the variance is at most sigma^2||w*ell||^2+18sigma^4||w*mu||^2+6sigma^6||w||^2. For the C015 phase-retrieval forward law, w=g/m gives centered signal-gradient innovations D_t with conditional mean zero in the post-backward-query filtration. Stop before any predictable budget sigma_t<=s, sum g_i^2/m<=G0, sum g_i^2 mu_(t,i)^2/m<=G1 or sum g_i^2 ell_(t,i)^2/m<=G2 fails. Then N_n=-eta sum_(t<n)1_(t<tau)D_t satisfies P(max_(n<=T)|N_n|>=u)<=T eta^2(s^2G2+18s^4G1+6s^6G0)/(m u^2). With s=K eta, eta=c/log d<=1, m=ceil(alpha*d), T<=C log^2 d and fixed budget constants, max|N_n|=O(1/sqrt(d log d)) with probability at least 1-1/log d. This is stopped unamplified fresh-noise control only; actual-path budgets and positive drift remain unproved. Proof: expand the centered coordinate polynomial as ell_i Z_i+3mu_i(Z_i^2-Sigma_ii)+(Z_i^3-3Sigma_ii Z_i). Gaussian mgf differentiation makes the three degrees orthogonal with covariances Sigma_ij, 2Sigma_ij^2 and 6Sigma_ij^3. Schur-product positivity bounds the entrywise covariance powers. Predictable stopping and conditional mean zero give orthogonal martingale increments; the squared-martingale maximal inequality yields the cumulative bound. No product of conditional characteristic functions or iid stopped Gaussian list is used. No actual-path budget survival, memory-dependent positive drift, amplified-noise bound, overlap growth or convergence follows from this conditional record.

nested chronological post-backward-query filtration; next forward observation unrevealed when its conditional parameters are specified
fixed eta>0, finite deterministic horizon T, predictable stopping before the displayed budgets fail
GD specialization depends on unaudited C015; no probability bound for budget survival or amplified noise is assumed proved

\[
    G_{k+1}^{\nesterov}(j)

    -\rho(1-\eta\lambda_j)G_{k-1}^{\nesterov}(j),
    \qquad
    G_0^{\nesterov}(j)=1,

\[
    e_k^{\mathrm{det}}(j)
    =
    -\frac{(1-\eta\lambda_j-y_{j,-})y_{j,+}^{k}
    -(1-\eta\lambda_j-y_{j,+})y_{j,-}^{k}}
    {y_{j,+}-y_{j,-}}\,\theta_j^* .
\]

body:
[Definition 1 of arXiv:2608.29075, 'The 2-Monoidal Structure of Symmetric Sequences'] Let $\{G_n \; | \; n \in \mathbb{N} \}$ be a set of groups. Denote by $\G$ the totally disconnected groupoid given by $\text{Ob}(\G) = \mathbb{N}$ and $\G(n,n) = G_n \in \text{Ob}(\textbf{Grp})$ for all $n \in \mathbb{N}$, where the groups $G_n$ are such that for all $m,n$ we have a group homomorphism $$\psi_{m,n}:G_m \times G_n \rightarrow G_{mn}$$ that is functorial in $m$ and $n$. 

We define a bifunctor $\nu_{\text{mult}}: \G \times \G \rightarrow \G$ given on objects by $\nu_{\text{mult}}(m,n) = mn$ and on morphisms by the homomorphisms $\psi_{-,-}$.
title: Definition 1 of arXiv:2608.29075

body:
[Definition def:Invariant-subset of arXiv:2609.02213, 'Invariant subspaces for free linearizations of Lipschitz maps'] Let $M$ be a metric space and let $f\in \Lip(M,M)$. A \emph{non-trivial closed invariant subset} for $f$ is a closed subset $A\subset M$ such that $A$ contains at least two points,
		$$
		A\subsetneq M,
		\qquad\text{and}\qquad
		f(A)\subset A.
		$$
title: Definition def:Invariant-subset of arXiv:2609.02213

body: In topology, two continuous functions from one topological space to another are called homotopic if one can be "continuously deformed" into the other, such a deformation being called a homotopy between the two functions. A notable use of homotopy is the definition of homotopy groups and cohomotopy groups, important invariants in algebraic topology.
title: Homotopy

body:
[Definition Ideal gap of arXiv:2604.17170, 'CaTherine wheels from trees and Liouville quantum gravity'] A sequence of proper lines $\eta_i$ in $Z$ which are the convex hulls of 
$\lbrace e_i^L,e_i^R\rbrace$ for a sequence of nested intervals 
$[e_i^L,e_i^R]$ in $\mathcal E$ is said to be {\em end nested}.

A point $p\in Z$ together with an end nested sequence $\eta_i$ as above for which
$\bigcap_i [e_i^L,e_i^R]$ is empty and for which $p \in \bigcap_i \eta_i$ is
called an {\em ideal gap}. We define an equivalence relation on ideal
gaps as follows. Let $S$ and $S'$ be a pair of sequences of nested intervals
in $\mathcal E$ with empty intersection. We say $S$ refines $S'$ if $S'$ is a subsequence
of $S$. The relation of refinement is not an equivalence relation,
but it generates an equivalence relation on sequences of nested intervals
in $\mathcal E$ with empty intersection by
$S {\originalsim} S'$ if there is a finite sequence $S=S_0,S_1,\cdots,S_n=S'$ 
so that for each $i$ either $S_i$ refines $S_{i+1}$ or $S_{i+1}$ refines $S_i$.
Say that two ideal gaps are equivalent if their associated
sequences of nested intervals are related by this equivalence relation.

A point $p$ as above is said to lie in the {\em support} of the 
equivalence class of the given ideal gap.
title: Ideal gap

[Proposition prop_transitive_and_trichotomy of arXiv:2604.04672, 'Connected components and topological ends of stationary planar forests'] The relation $\cdot\in(\cdot,\cdot)_\Gamma$ is \emph{transitive}, that is, for all distinct $\gamma,\sigma',\sigma',\sigma''\in\Gamma$,
        \[\gamma\in(\sigma,\sigma')_\Gamma\setminus(\sigma,\sigma'')_\Gamma\implies\gamma\in (\sigma',\sigma'')_\Gamma.\]
    Furthermore, for all distinct $\sigma,\sigma',\sigma''\in\Gamma$, exactly one of the assertions $\sigma\in(\sigma',\sigma'')_\Gamma$, $\sigma'\in(\sigma,\sigma'')_\Gamma$ and $\sigma''\in(\sigma,\sigma')_\Gamma$ holds.

Let a finite nonempty deterministic path family visit exactly one site in each of finitely many layers t. In layer t there are m_t independent N(0,sigma_t^2) weights, and all layers are independent. For deterministic positive a_p and finite beta, put F=log(sum_p a_p exp(beta sum_t omega(t,p_t))). If A_t is the layer mean and R(t,x)=omega(t,x)-A_t, then Var(F)=beta^2 sum_t sigma_t^2/m_t+Var(F(R)). For M=max_p sum_t omega(t,p_t), Var(M)=sum_t sigma_t^2/m_t+Var(M(R)). In the unrestricted n-vertex up/right model with unit Gaussian weights, this gives Var(M_n)>=H_n; in any n-layer width-W family it gives Var(M)>=n/W.
Finite nonempty deterministic path family
One selected site per layer
Independent centered Gaussian weights with common variance within each layer
Deterministic positive coefficients for F
Finite beta for F

body: In the classical theory of Ambrosio-Gigli-Savaré, metric gradient flows require a rigorous characterization of absolutely continuous curves and metric derivatives. By establishing that every curve in $AC^p(\mathbb{FP}_p)$ can be represented as an adapted flow on a single probability space, Acciaio, Krsek, Pammer, and Rodrigues provide the foundational prerequisite for defining subdifferentials and gradient flows in the space of filtered processes.
title: Foundations for Gradient Flows in Adapted Wasserstein Spaces

[Lemma 9 of arXiv:2608.30554, 'Strong law of large numbers for generalized operator means II'] Let $f$ be an operator monotone function on $(0, \infty)$ such that $f(1) = 0$ and $f'(1) = 1$.
 Let $Y_1, Y_2, \hdots$  be a sequence of i.i.d. random variables with probability law $\mu$ on $\mathbb{P}$ such that
     $$ \int_\mathbb{P} \|f(y)\|\log^{+}\|f(y)\| \: d\mu(y) < \infty.$$

$$
\lim_{\delta\rightarrow 0^+} Z_\upsilon(\Sigma,G) \mathbb{P}_{\operatorname{YM}}^{{\rm free}}\left(\Phi|\mathbf{Hol}_0\in B_\delta(\operatorname{Id}_G)\right)

$$

$$
where $p_t$ is the heat kernel on $G$, $p_{\mathbf{Hol},r}$ is defined in Lemma~(lemm:lawHolcombi of the paper) and $\mathscr{A}_{r}(1)=\int_\Sigma[\blacktriangle(\gamma_r)]\upsilon.$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 15 of arXiv:2609.03750, '\bf Pullback Measure Attractors, Zero-Noise Limits, and Moderate Deviations for 2D Stochas'] Suppose Hypotheses \ref{PEeqAssum-2.2}, \ref{PEeqAssum-2.3}, \ref{PEeqAssum-2.4} and \eqref{PETNs-3.01} hold. For $\tau\in\mathbb R$, set
	\[
	\mathscr M_0(\tau)
	=\mathcal R_1\left(
	1+\int_{-\infty}^{\tau}e^{-\kappa(\tau-s)}|g(s)|^4\,ds
	\right),
	\]
	and
	\[
	\mathscr M_z(\tau)
	=\mathcal R_3\left(
	1+\int_{-\infty}^{\tau}e^{-\kappa(\tau-s)}
	|\partial_zg(s)|^4\,ds
	\right).
	\]
	Define
	\[
	\mathscr K(\tau)
	=
	\left\{
	\mu\in\mathcal P_{4,z}(H):
	\int_H|\zeta|^4\,\mu(d\zeta)\le\mathscr M_0(\tau),\
	\int_H|\partial_z\zeta|^4\,\mu(d\zeta)\le\mathscr M_z(\tau)
	\right\}.
	\]
	Then $\mathscr K=\{\mathscr K(\tau):\tau\in\mathbb R\}$ belongs to $\mathfrak D$ and is a closed $\mathfrak D$-pullback absorbing family for $S_\epsilon$, uniformly for $\epsilon\in(0,\epsilon_0)$.

For n>=81 put t=floor(sqrt(n)), a=t, b=2t+1, m=floor(n/2) and form the Jordan domain D_n from [0,a/n]x[0,1], [b/n,1]x[0,1], and the corridor [a/n,b/n]x[(m-1/2)/n,(m+1/2)/n], taking the interior of their union. Normalize the disk Riemann map f_n by f_n(0)=(1/2,1/2), f_n'(0)>0. Its Jordan boundary extension satisfies |f_n^{-1}(0,1)-f_n^{-1}(0,0)|<=8/n. The boundary arc containing both corners lies behind a height-1/n gate at x=b/n. Brownian motion must hit this gate before exiting on that arc. The half-plane Poisson kernel bounds its harmonic measure by 1/[pi*n*(1/2-b/n)]<=4/(pi*n); the preimage arc has angular length <=8/n. Thus Euclidean corner convergence, even with unmarked kernel and boundary Hausdorff convergence, does not imply marked-prime-end convergence.

[Proposition Capacity-eigenvalue comparison of arXiv:2606.23025, 'Spectral-Capacitary Bounds for Homological Recovery from Reflected Brownian Trajectories'] There
exist constants \(c_{ce},C_{ce} > 0\) and
\(\eta_{ce} > 0\), depending only on the analytic geometry of

Moreover, in the small-capacity regime,
\(\lambda_{A} = \operatorname{Cap}_{N}(A)\left( 1 + O\left( \operatorname{Cap}_{N}(A) \right) \right)\)
after fixing the normalization of capacity consistently with
\(\mu\); this first-order form is proved below. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition 16 of arXiv:2609.02755, 'The Sharp Rate of Probabilistically Strong Convergence to the KPZ Equation'] We recursively define pointed modelled distributions $H_{\tau; \eps, \delta}^{z, g} \in \mcD_2^{\gamma_\tau, \deg_2 \tau; z}$ for $\tau \in \tilde{\mathcal{T}}$, $g \in L^2(\mathbb{R} \times \mathbb{T})$ and a fixed space-time point $z$ by declaring the base cases
	\begin{align*}
		H_{\<b0>; \eps, \delta}^{z, g}(z') =& 0, \qquad H_{\<p0>; \eps, \delta}^{z, g}(z') = 0, \qquad H_{\<s(1)0>; \eps, \delta}^{z, g}(z') = \eps^{-1/2} \partial_x K \ast g_{\eps, \delta}(z'),
		\\
		H_{\<bs(2)0>; \eps, \delta}^{z, g}(z') =& \partial_x K \ast g_\eps(z') \<s(1)0> + \eps^{-1/2} \partial_x K \ast g_{\eps, \delta}(z') \<b1>,
		\\
		H_{\<ps(2)0>; \eps, \delta}^{z, g}(z') =&  \partial_x K \ast g_{\delta}(z') \<s(1)0> + \eps^{-1/2} \partial_x K \ast g_{\eps, \delta}(z') \<p1>,
		\\
		H_{X^k; \eps, \delta}^{z, g}(z') =& 0
	\end{align*}
	alongside the recursive relations
	\begin{align*}
		H_{\tau \bar{\tau}; \eps, \delta}^{z, g}(z') =& H_{\tau; \eps, \delta}^{z, g}(z') \tilde\Gamma_{z'z}^{\eps, \delta} \bar{\tau} + \tilde \Gamma_{z'z}^{\eps, \delta} \tau H_{\bar{\tau}; \eps, \delta}^{z, g}(z'),
		\\

	\end{align*}
	where $\mathcal{K}_{\gamma, \nu, \mathfrak{l}}^{z, 2}$ is the pointed integration operator defined in \cite[Definition 3.16]{HS} associated to the edge type $\mathfrak{l}$.

Check: Each block product is plus/minus1 with mean tanh(beta); its variance is at most1. Chebyshev applied to n blocks proves asymptotic separation without a central limit approximation. Obstruction: Thus finite-range or exponentially decaying local dependence does not justify global total-variation replacement. A renormalization or observable argument controlling crossing geometry is still needed for the actual triangular model.

[Corollary cor:recover-liu-wasserstein-poc of arXiv:2607.00149, '\bf Uniform-in-time Propagation-of-Chaos for\\ Stein Variational Gradient Descent'] Consider the affine Gaussian kernel (equation eq:affine-kernel of the paper) and the
standard Gaussian target on $\mathbb R^d$.  Assume that
\[
        \widetilde\mu_0=N(m_0,\Sigma_0),
        \qquad \Sigma_0>0,
\]
and let $Y_1(0),\ldots,Y_N(0)$ be i.i.d. with law $\widetilde\mu_0$.  Let
$\widetilde\mu_t$ denote the mean-field solution and let
\[
        \widetilde\mu_t^N:=\frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N\delta_{Y_i(t)}
\]
be the empirical measure of the particle system.  Then there is a constant
$C=C(d,m_0,\Sigma_0)<\infty$ such that, for all $N$ sufficiently large,
\begin{equation}
        \mathbb E \left[\sup_{t\ge0}\, W_2^2(\widetilde\mu_t^N,\widetilde\mu_t)\right]
        \le
        C r_d(N),
\end{equation}
where
\[
        r_d(N):=
        \begin{cases}
        N^{-1}\log\log N, & d=1,\\
        N^{-1}(\log N)^2, & d=2,\\
        N^{-2/d}, & d\ge3.
        \end{cases}
\]
Moreover, for fixed \(k\ge1\), writing $\mathcal L(Y_1^N(t),\ldots,Y_k^N(t))$ for the joint law of $Y_1^N(t),\ldots,Y_k^N(t)$,
\begin{equation}
        \sup_{t\ge0}
        W_2^{(k)}\left(\mathcal L(Y_1^N(t),\ldots,Y_k^N(t)),\widetilde\mu_t^{\otimes k}\right)^2
        \le
        C'\left(k r_d(N)+\frac{k^2(k-1)}{N}\right),
\end{equation}
for some constant
$C'=C'(d,m_0,\Sigma_0)<\infty$.

[Corollary 13 (Finite-time Hopf torus trajectories) of arXiv:2609.00501, 'Uniqueness of Finite-Time Varifold Limits for the M\"obius-Invariant Willmore Flow'] Suppose that the MIWF starts from a smooth parametrization \(F_0\) of

for a uniformly conformal bi-Lipschitz parametrization of the limiting
Hopf torus.  In particular, among the alternatives of
Corollary~\ref{cor:four-way}, every such finite-time Hopf trajectory

ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Conservation, explicit coupling reduction, exact law comparison or spectral calculation Result: For a stabilizable stationary system, mass transport preserves the mean particle density: send one unit from every initial particle to its final sleeping site. Thus any local subsequential limit of the bounded occupation indicators has one-site mean zeta_c. This still does not imply almost-sure density. To see the precise gap, fill consecutive blocks of length m with iid Bernoulli(rho) values, constant within a block, and randomize the block origin uniformly. Each resulting process is stationary ergodic with density rho. As m tends to infinity its local law converges to the mixture rho*delta_all_ones+(1-rho)*delta_all_zeros, whose density is random. Check: A fixed window crosses a block boundary with probability at most its diameter/m. Away from a boundary it sees a single Bernoulli variable. Ergodicity of each finite-block process follows by iid block ergodicity and the cyclic action on the random phase. Obstruction: Need control of correlations or ergodic components that is uniform near criticality, together with uniqueness and independence from the initial law. Conservation of mean does not supply any of these.

[Proposition 18 (Nine-component two-point correlation equation) of arXiv:2607.23640, '{\sl Non-equilibrium fluctuations of a two-species exclusion process with slow boundary }'] For every \((x,y)\in V_n\), the nine-component correlation function
	\(\bm\varphi^{n,t}(x,y)\) satisfies
	\begin{equation}
		\partial_t\bm\varphi^{n,t}(x,y)
		=
		\mathcal L_n^\ast\bm\varphi^{n,t}(x,y)
		+
		\bm G^{n,t}(x,y),
	\end{equation}
	where
	\begin{align}
		\mathcal L_n^\ast
		={}&
		n^2\mathscr A_n \mathrm I_9
		+
		n^2\mathbf 1_{\{y=x+1\}}\mathsf P
		+
		\mathbf 1_{\{2\le x\le n-2\}}(Q\otimes \mathrm I_3)
		\nonumber\\
		&+
		\mathbf 1_{\{2\le y\le n-2\}}(\mathrm I_3\otimes Q)
		+
		n\mathbf 1_{\{x=1\}}(R^\alpha\otimes \mathrm I_3)
		+
		n\mathbf 1_{\{y=n-1\}}(\mathrm I_3\otimes R^\beta).
	\end{align}
	The source term \(\bm G^{n,t}\) is supported on the discrete diagonal $ D_n=\{(x,y)\in V_n:\ y=x+1\} $ and for \(a,b\in E\),
	\begin{equation}
		G_{ab}^{n,t}(x,y)
		=
		-n^2
		\left(
		\rho_a^{n,t}(x+1)-\rho_a^{n,t}(x)
		\right)
		\left(
		\rho_b^{n,t}(x+1)-\rho_b^{n,t}(x)
		\right)
		\mathbf 1_{\{y=x+1\}}.
	\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma Spherical curvature approximation of arXiv:2608.27248, 'Optimal Transport and the ABP Method in Higher Codimension'] Let $U$ be a geodesically convex body contained in an open hemisphere of
$\mathbb{S}^3$.  The local spherical Steiner formula uniquely defines a
nonnegative finite Borel measure $M_1(U,\cdot)$ on $\partial U$, called the
first spherical curvature measure.  It has the following properties:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item on every $C^2$ part $W$ of $\partial U$,
\[
 M_1(U,W)=\int_W H_{\mathbb{S}^3}\,\mathrm dA;
\]
\item if $\mathsf d_{\mathrm H}(U_j,U)\to0$, with all bodies contained in a
fixed open hemisphere, then $M_1(U_j,\cdot)$ converges weakly to
$M_1(U,\cdot)$ and $|U_j|\to|U|$.
\end{enumerate}

[Lemma 7 of arXiv:2609.02755, 'The Sharp Rate of Probabilistically Strong Convergence to the KPZ Equation'] Suppose that $(\Hb, \Hp, \bar{\mathcal{W}})$ is a solution of the system
	\begin{align*}
		\Hb &= \mathcal{P}_\gamma \mathbf{1}_+ [(\partial_x \Hb)^2 + \<b0>] + \mathcal{G} \psi
		\\
		\Hp &= \mathcal{P}_\gamma \mathbf{1}_+ [(\partial_x \Hp)^2 + \<p0>] + \mathcal{G} \psi
		\\

	Then if $\mathcal{W} = \bar{\mathcal{W}} + \mathcal{P}_{\tilde{\gamma}} \mathbf{1}_+ \<0t>$, we have that $(\Hb, \Hp, \mathcal{W})$ is a solution of the system of Lemma~\ref{lem:recon_iden}. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Proposition prop:polyroot of arXiv:2602.00988, 'Wealth exchange under ceiling and flooring constraints: a modified Bennati–Dragulescu–Yako'] Given $0 \leq a < \mu < b$ with $a, \mu, b \in \mathbb N$, and define for $x \geq 0$ the polynomial function
\begin{equation}
f(x) =  (b-\mu)\,x^{b+2-a} + (\mu-b-1)\,x^{b+1-a} + (\mu-a+1)\,x + a - \mu.
\end{equation}
Then \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item when $\mu<\frac{a+b}{2}$, $f(x)$ has a unique root within $(0,1)$,
\item when $\mu=\frac{a+b}{2}$, $f(x)$ has a unique root at $x= 1$,
\item when $\mu>\frac{a+b}{2}$, $f(x)$ has a unique root within $(1,\infty)$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition prop:polyroot of arXiv:2602.00988

[Thm Determinant of affine meander matrix of arXiv:2506.01306, 'Asymptotic of Coulomb gas integral, Temperley-Lieb type algebras and pure partition functi'] Let $\widetilde{\mathcal{G}}_n^d$ denote the Gram matrix for the standard module with $n$ nodes and $d = n - 2m$ through-lines. Then:
\[
\begin{aligned}
\det \widetilde{\mathcal{G}}_n^0 &= \prod_{k=1}^{n/2} \left(a^2 - 4 \cos^2\left( \frac{4k\pi}{\kappa} \right) \right) \binom{n}{n/2 - k}, \\
\det \widetilde{\mathcal{G}}_n^d &= \prod_{k=1}^{m} \left(4 - 4 \cos^2\left( \frac{4(k + d/2)\pi}{\kappa} \right) \right) \binom{n}{(n-d)/2 - k}, \quad \text{for } d > 0, \\
\det \widetilde{\mathcal{G}}_n^n &= 1.
\end{aligned}
\]

[Lemma finite-dimensional-Stein-untied of arXiv:2609.03858, 'High-Dimensional Learning Dynamics of \\ Attention-Indexed Models'] Fix a compact set \(\mathfrak D\Subset\mathcal M\times\mathcal Q\) and a constant
\(C_*<\infty\). Let \(J\) be a stopping time such that, on
\(\{n<J\}\), 
\begin{equation}
\left(m_{\mathcal K}^{(n)},q^{(1,n)},q^{(2,n)}\right)\in\mathfrak D,\quad
\max_{1\le l\le K}\left\{\|U_l^{(n)}\|_{\rm op},\|V_l^{(n)}\|_{\rm op}\right\}\le C_*.

\end{equation}
Write \(\mathbb E_n[\cdot]=\mathbb E[\cdot\mid\mathcal F_n]\), and define $b_k^{(n)}:=\sum_{i,j=1}^L\mathcal C_{ij}\,\mathbb E_n\left[\partial_{ijk}\mathcal L(G^{(n)})\right]$.
For \(r=1,2\), set $\mathcal C^{(1)}_{ij,i'j'}:=\mathcal C_{ii'}\mathcal C_{jj'}$ and $\mathcal C^{(2)}_{ij,i'j'}:=\mathcal C_{ij'}\mathcal C_{ji'}$ and define
$a_{kl}^{(r,d,n)}:=\frac12
\sum_{i,j,i',j'=1}^L
\mathcal C^{(r)}_{ij,i'j'}\,\mathbb E_n\left[\partial^2_{(ijk),(i'j'l)}\mathcal L(G^{(n)})\right]$.

Then, uniformly for \(n<J\) and \(k\in\mathcal K\),
\begin{align}
\bar g_{U,k}^{(n)}&=\frac{b_k^{(n)}}{\sqrt d}V_k^{(n)}+\frac{2}{d}\sum_{l=1}^K\sum_{r=1}^2a_{kl}^{(r,d,n)}M_l^{(r,n)}V_k^{(n)}+\mathcal E_{U,k}^{(n)},

\\
\bar g_{V,k}^{(n)}&=\frac{b_k^{(n)}}{\sqrt d}U_k^{(n)}+\frac{2}{d}\sum_{l=1}^K\sum_{r=1}^2a_{kl}^{(r,d,n)}M_l^{(\bar r,n)}U_k^{(n)}+\mathcal E_{V,k}^{(n)}.

\end{align}
Moreover, there exists $C=C(C_*,\mathfrak D,\mathcal C,\mathcal L,K,L)<\infty$
such that $\max_{k,l,r}|a_{kl}^{(r,d,n)}|+\max_k|b_k^{(n)}|\le C$,\\ $\max_{k\in\mathcal K}\left\{\|\mathcal E_{U,k}^{(n)}\|_{\rm op},\|\mathcal E_{V,k}^{(n)}\|_{\rm op}\right\}\le Cd^{-3/2}$ and $\max_{1\le k\le K}
\left|b_k^{(n)}-\frac{\partial\Phi}{\partial m_k}\left(m^{(n)},q^{(1,n)},q^{(2,n)}\right)\right|\le \frac{C}{\sqrt d}$.
