[Definition def:egu of arXiv:2512.21026, 'Minimax Duality in Game-Theoretic Probability\thanks{Work in progress: mistakes are likely'] Let $(\Omega,\mathcal{Z})$ be a gamble space, and $X:\Omega\to\overline{\mathbb{R}}$ a variable.
  Then the \emph{upper game-theoretic expectation of $X$}, with respect to $(\Omega,\mathcal{Z})$, is given by the following equivalent definitions (see Proposition~(prop:egu-equiv-defs of the paper)).
  \begin{align}
    \overline{\textsf{\textbf{E}}} X
    &:= \inf_{Z\in\mathcal{Z}} \sup_{\omega\in\Omega} X(\omega) - Z(\omega)
      
    \\
    &\phantom{:}= \inf\{\alpha\in\mathbb{R} \mid \exists Z\in\mathcal{Z} \text{ s.t. } Z + \alpha > X\}~.
      
  \end{align}
  We define the \emph{lower game-theoretic expectation of $X$}, with respect to $(\Omega,\mathcal{Z})$ by $\underline{\textsf{\textbf{E}}} X := - \overline{\textsf{\textbf{E}}}(-X)$.
  When $\overline{\textsf{\textbf{E}}} X = \underline{\textsf{\textbf{E}}} X$, we write $\textsf{\textbf{E}} X := \overline{\textsf{\textbf{E}}} X = \underline{\textsf{\textbf{E}}} X$.
title: Game-theoretic upper expectation

[Lem 88 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] For any $\mu \in \cP_2(\bbR_{\ge 0})$, the preimage
    \[
        \sym^{-1}(\mu) \equiv \Big\{
            \tilde \mu \in \cP_2(\bbR) : \sym(\tilde\mu) = \mu
        \Big\}
    \]
    is compact with respect to the $\bbW_2$ metric.

\begin{proof}
The set $\sym^{-1}(\mu)$ is clearly closed. Therefore, it suffices to show that any sequence $(\tilde \mu_n)_{n\ge1}$ in $\sym^{-1}(\mu)$ has a $\bbW_2$-convergent subsequence. The collection of measures $\sym^{-1}(\mu)$ is clearly tight, since we have 
	\[
	\tilde{\mu}([-K,K])
	=\mu([0,K]) 
	\stackrel{K\to\infty}{\longrightarrow} 1\,,
	\]
uniformly over all $\tilde{\mu}\in \sym^{-1}(\mu)$. 
    By Prohorov's theorem, any sequence $(\tilde \mu_n)_{n\ge 1}$ in $\sym^{-1}(\mu)$ must have a subsequence $(\tilde \mu_{n_j})_{j\ge 1}$ that converges weakly to some measure $\tilde{\mu}$, which is also clearly in $\sym^{-1}(\mu)$. 
By Skorokhod's theorem, we have can find random variables $X_n,X$ such that $X_n$ is distributed according to $\tilde{\mu}_{n_j}$, $X$ is distributed according to $\tilde{\mu}$, and $X_n$ converges to $X$ almost surely as $n\to\infty$. Then, for any finite $M$, we have
	\[
	\E\Big[
	(X_n-X)^2; \max\{|X_n|,|X|\} \le M
	\Big]
	\le \E\Big[\max\Big\{(X_n-X)^2
	; (2M)^2
	\Big\}
	\Big] \stackrel{n\to\infty}{\longrightarrow} 0
	\]
by the bounded convergence theorem. On the other hand,	since $|X_n|$ and $|X|$ are distributed as samples from $\mu$, we have
	\begin{align*}
	&\E\Big[
	(X_n-X)^2; \max\{|X_n|,|X|\} 
		> M
	\Big]
	\le 2\Big\{
	\E[(X_n)^2;|X_n|>M]
	+\E[X^2;|X|>M]\Big\} \\
	&\qquad= 4 \E[X^2;|X|>M]
	\le o_M(1)\,.
	\end{align*}
By sending $M\to\infty$ we conclude $\tilde \mu_{n_j} \rightarrow \tilde \mu$ in $\bbW_2$, from which the compactness claim follows.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition 7 of arXiv:2604.07478, 'Mixing Times and Cutoff for the Rook's Walk'] Define a {\bf Rook's Walk Birth-Death} (denoted RWBD) Markov chain over the state space $\Omega_* = \{0,\dots , d\}$ with a transition from $X_t \in \Omega_*$ to $X_{t+1}\in \Omega_*$ governed by parameter $n\in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 3}$ as follows:
  \[X_{t+1}=\begin{cases}
   X_t, \quad&\text{w.p. } \mathbb{P}[Y_1 \in H_{X_t} \mid Y_0\in H_{X_t}] \\
   X_t-1, \quad&\text{w.p. } \mathbb{P}[Y_1 \in H_{X_t-1} \mid Y_0\in H_{X_t}]\\
   X_t+1, \quad&\text{w.p. } \mathbb{P}[Y_1 \in H_{X_t+1} \mid Y_0\in H_{X_t}] \\
  \end{cases}\]
  where $Y_1\in \Omega$ follows from $Y_0\in \Omega$ according to the Rook's Walk with parameters $n,d$ where $\Omega$ is the state space of said Rook's Walk.

body:
Kolossov-Montanari-Tandon unbiased selection influence objective. Let X have a specified probability law. For fixed p>=1, let H be a deterministic symmetric positive-definite p-by-p matrix, Q a deterministic symmetric positive-semidefinite p-by-p matrix, and G(X) a measurable positive-semidefinite p-by-p matrix. Define Z(X)=Tr(G(X) H^(-1) Q H^(-1)), and assume E Z(X)<infinity. A nonnegative randomized selection weight S is unbiased when E[S|X]=1 almost surely. Its retention probability is pi(X)=P(S>0|X), and a fixed mean retention budget is E pi(X)=gamma. Define the influence objective J(S)=E[S^2 Z(X)], allowing infinity. An inverse-probability scheme draws I conditional on X as Bernoulli(pi(X)), and sets S=I/pi(X), for measurable pi(X)>0; then it is unbiased and J(S)=E[Z(X)/pi(X)]. In the source statistical application, G is the conditional score outer-product matrix and H is the population risk Hessian. Identifying J with an estimator asymptotic error requires the separate regularity hypotheses of source Proposition4.1; no estimator limit or exponential pruning law is asserted by this definition.
Fixed finite-dimensional positive-definite H, positive-semidefinite Q and measurable positive-semidefinite G; finite mean score.

Sharp two-quantile variance lower bound

Let X be a real square-integrable random variable. Suppose a < b, p,q > 0, P(X <= a) >= p, and P(X >= b) >= q. Necessarily p+q <= 1. Then

    Var(X) >= [pq/(p+q)] (b-a)^2.

Proof. Write mu=E X. If mu lies in [a,b], the two disjoint events give
Var(X) >= p(mu-a)^2 + q(b-mu)^2. Completing the square gives the claimed lower bound. If mu<a, the right event alone gives Var(X) >= q(b-mu)^2 >= q(b-a)^2, which is at least the claimed expression. The case mu>b is symmetric. Equality is attained by masses p at a, q at b, and 1-p-q at (pa+qb)/(p+q). The mean of this three-atom law is that middle location, so the computed variance is exactly the lower bound. This proves sharpness. No claim about independence of lattice events is used.

[Lemma 16 of arXiv:2607.18862, 'Tamed Euler Schemes for Singular SDEs with Multiplicative L\'{e}vy Noise'] \begin{enumerate}
		\item[(i)]	Let $\eta\in (0,2]$, and $y^{(\eta)}:=y\textbf{1}_{\eta\in[1,2]}$. For any $p\in (d/\eta\vee 1,\infty]$, there is a constant $C=C(p,d,\eta)>0$ such that for all $f\in \mH_{\eta,p}(\mR^d)$,
		\begin{equation}
			\| \sup_{y\neq 0}|y|^{-\eta}|f(\cdot+y)-f(\cdot)-y^{(\eta)}\cdot \nabla f(\cdot) \|_p\leq C\| f\|_{\mH_{\eta,p}(\mR^d)},
		\end{equation}
		where we adopt the convention $\nabla f =0$ when $\eta\in (0,1)$.
		\item[(ii)] For any $p\in (d,\infty]$, there is a constant $C=C(p,d)>0$ such that for all $f\in \mH_{1,p}(\mR^d)$,
		\be
		\| \sup_{y\neq 0}|y|^{-1}|f(\cdot+y)-f(\cdot)|\|_p\leq C\| f\|_{\mH_{1,p}(\mR^d)}.
		\ee 
		\item[(iii)] For any $\delta,\gamma\in (0,1]$ and $p\in (d/\delta\vee d/\gamma,\infty]$, there is a constant $C=C(p,d,\delta,\gamma)>0$ such that for all $f\in \mH_{\delta+\gamma,p}(\mR^d)$,
		\be 
		\|\sup_{z,w\neq 0}|w|^{-\delta}|z|^{-\gamma}|(f(\cdot+z+w)-f(\cdot+z))-(f(\cdot+w)-f(\cdot))|\|_p\leq C\| f\|_{\mH_{\delta+\gamma,p}(\mR^d)}.
		\ee
	\end{enumerate}

body: Burnside's lemma, sometimes also called Burnside's counting theorem, the Cauchy–Frobenius lemma, or the orbit-counting theorem, is a result in group theory that is often useful in taking account of symmetry when counting mathematical objects. It was discovered by Augustin Louis Cauchy and Ferdinand Georg Frobenius, and became well known after William Burnside quoted it. The result enumerates orbits of a symmetry group acting on some objects: that is, it counts distinct objects, considering objects symmetric to each other as the same; or counting distinct objects up to a symmetry equivalence relation; or counting only objects in canonical form. For example, in describing possible organic compounds of certain type, one considers them up to spatial rotation symmetry: different rotated drawings of a given molecule are chemically identical.
title: Burnside's lemma

body: [Proposition 3.3 of arXiv:2304.14793, 'Learning Graph Neural Networks using Exact Compression'] Let 𝐿be a GNN composed of𝑑∈N layers,𝑑≥1. If cr𝑑(𝐺)(𝑣) = cr𝑑(𝐻)(𝑤) then 𝐿(𝐺)(𝑣) = 𝐿(𝐻)(𝑤). As a consequence, if S is a hypothesis space consisting of GNNs of at most 𝑑layers and cr𝑑(𝐺)(𝑣) = cr𝑑(𝐻)(𝑤) then (𝐺, 𝑣) ∼S (𝐻,𝑤). In other words, 𝑑-layer GNNs cannot distinguish nodes that are assigned the same color by 𝑑steps of color refinement.

[Corollary prop:actionclassification_perfectfits of arXiv:2608.30973, 'Pseudo-Anosov flow and dynamics on guts'] Let \(M\) be a closed, orientable 3-manifold and \(\varphi\) be an almost pseudo-Anosov flow without perfect fits and not conjugate to suspension Anosov flow.
Let \(g\in \pi_{1}(M)\) act on \(P_{\varphi}\) by deck transformation.
Then, exactly one of the following holds:
\begin{enumerate}
\item \(g\) fix a regular point in \(P_{\varphi}\)
\item \(g\) fix a singular point \(p\) in \(P_{\varphi^{\natural}}\) and hence all the vertices of blown-up tree associated to \(p\) in \(P_{\varphi}\).
\item \(g\) acts hyperbolically on \(\partial P_{\varphi}\) with one fixed point attracting and the other repelling.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Corollary prop:actionclassification_perfectfits of arXiv:2608.30973

[Prop weighted-tree-small-smin of arXiv:2607.05384, 'Well-invertible column subsets of sparse matrices are rare'] Let $G=(I,J,M)$ be a real weighted bipartite graph. Suppose $G$ contains a
\hyperref[def:weight-compatible-rooted-matching-tree]{\textcolor{PineGreen}{\emph{weight-compatible $m$-matching rooted tree}}}, witnessed by a root $j_\star$ and sets
$\mathcal K_i$, $i\in I_\star=N_G(j_\star)$. 
Define the third left layer
\[
\mathcal L_{\rm out}:=
\bigcup_{i\in I_\star}
\bigcup_{j\in\mathcal K_i}
\left(N_G(j)\setminus I_\star\right),
\]
and define its maximum weight by
\[
A_{\rm out}:=
\max\left\{
|M_{\ell,j}|:
i\in I_\star,\ j\in\mathcal K_i,\ \ell\in N_G(j)\setminus I_\star
\right\},
\]
with the convention $A_{\rm out}=0$ if the set is empty. Then
\[
s_{\min}(M)\le
\frac{A_{\rm out}}{m}\sqrt{|\mathcal L_{\rm out}|}.
\]

Weak-* convergence of bounded lattice height functions to a constant does not by itself imply convergence of each height frequency. Alternating arrays equal to 1 everywhere, or to a fine checkerboard of heights 0 and 2, both converge weak-* to 1, while the height-1 frequencies are respectively 1 and 0. body:
[Proposition 8 of arXiv:2605.14206, 'The clumsy coupon collector's problem'] The language $H$ admits a well-defined decomposition into primitive languages:
\begin{align*}
  H = \Big[\Big(\C_1^{\geqslant 0} \circ \D_1^{\geqslant 0}\Big).\C_1\Big]
  \circ \cdots \circ
  \Big[
    \Big(\C_m^{\geqslant 0} \circ \D_m^{\geqslant 0}\Big).\C_m
  \Big].
\end{align*}
Its exponential generating function is hence
\[
  \hat\phi_H(z) = \left(1-p\right)^m \left(e^{z/m} - 1\right)^m.
\]
\begin{proof}
It holds for all $i$ that
\[
  \hat\phi_{\C_i^{\geqslant 0}}(z) = 
  e^{z(1-p)/m} \quad \text{and} \quad
  \hat\phi_{\D_i^{\geqslant 0}}(z) = 
  e^{zp/m} \quad \text{and} \quad 
  \phi_{\C_i}(z) = \frac{\left(1-p\right)z}{m}.
\]
Apply Proposition \ref{thm:shuffling} to find
\[
  \hat\phi_{{\C_i^{\geqslant 0}} \circ {\D_i^{\geqslant 0}}}(z)
  = \hat\phi_{\C_i^{\geqslant 0}}(z) \,
    \hat\phi_{\D_i^{\geqslant 0}}(z)
  = e^{z/m},
\]
then take the Laplace--Borel transform:
\[
  \phi_{{\C_i^{\geqslant 0}} \circ {\D_i^{\geqslant 0}}}(x)
  = \int_0^\infty e^{xt/m}\, e^{-t} \, dt
  = \int_0^\infty e^{-\left(1-x/m\right)t} \, dt
  = \frac{1}{1-x/m}, \quad 0 < x < 1.
\]
Therefore
\[
  \phi_{\left({\C_i^{\geqslant0}} \circ {\D_i^{\geqslant0}}\right).\C_i}(z)
    = \frac{\left(1-p\right)z}{m} \cdot \frac{1}{1-z/m}
  = \frac{\left(1-p\right)z}{m} \sum_{n=0}^\infty \left(\frac{z}{m}\right)^n
  = (1-p) \sum_{n=1}^\infty \left(\frac{z}{m}\right)^n,
\]
so by introducing the $n!$ terms,
\[
  \hat\phi_{\left(\C_i^{\geqslant0} \circ \D_i^{\geqslant0}\right).\C_i}(z)
  = (1-p)\sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{(z/m)^n}{n!}
  = (1-p)\left(e^{z/m} - 1\right).
\]
We find $\hat\phi_H(z) = \prod_i 
\hat\phi_{\left(\C_i^{\geqslant0} \circ \D_i^{\geqslant0}\right).\C_i}(z)
= (1-p)^m\left(e^{z/m} - 1\right)^m$.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition 8 of arXiv:2605.14206

[Lemma 16 (Finite-free quotient) of arXiv:2608.29585, '2608.29585'] Let $\cO$ be a complete DVR with uniformizer $\pi$, let $m\ge1$, let
$u_1,\ldots,u_m\in\pi\cO$, and put
\[
 g(U)=\prod_{i=1}^{m}(U-u_i)\in\cO[U].
\]
For every $F(U)\in\cO[[U]]$, there is a unique polynomial
$P(U)\in\cO[U]$ of degree $<m$ whose class in
$B=\cO[U]/(g)$ is the convergent value of the series $F(U)$.  Moreover,
\begin{equation}
 P(u_i)=F(u_i)\qquad(1\le i\le m).
\end{equation}

$\widehat m_\gamma(Y_\gamma)=\E[X_0\mid Y_\gamma]$ and
$\widehat m_\gamma^R(Y_\gamma,R)=\E[X_0\mid Y_\gamma,R]$.  Then, for
$\gamma>0$ (and by right differentiation at $\gamma=0$),
\begin{equation}

\frac{\dd}{\dd\gamma}\mathcal M_\gamma
=
\frac12\E\big\|
\widehat m_\gamma^R(Y_\gamma,R)-\widehat m_\gamma(Y_\gamma)
\big\|^2.

Consequently,
\begin{equation}

\mathcal M_\gamma
=
\frac12\int_0^\gamma
\E\big\|
\widehat m_u^R(Y_u,R)-\widehat m_u(Y_u)
\big\|^2\,\dd u.
\end{equation}
At $\gamma_t=a_t^2/\Delta_t$,
\begin{equation}

\E\|g_t(X_t,R)\|^2
=
\left.
\frac{2a_t^2}{\Delta_t^2}
\frac{\dd}{\dd\gamma}\mathcal M_\gamma

body:
[Defn Slices of arXiv:2608.30031, 'Ziggurats, taut foliations, and contact structures'] Let $A \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ and $\bm{t} \in \mathbb{R}^{n-k}$ for $0 \leq k \leq n-1$. 
    \begin{itemize}
        \item The \textbf{(right) $\bm{t}$-slice of $A$} is defined as
    $$Sl_{\vert \bm{t}}A \coloneqq \left(\mathbb{R}^{k} \times \{\bm{t}\}\right) \cap A.$$
    It can be naturally identified with a subset of $\mathbb{R}^k$.
        \item The set of \textbf{transversally interior points} in the (right) $\bm{t}$-slice $Sl_{\vert \bm{t}}A$, denoted by $Sl^\circ_{\vert\bm{t}} A$, is the set of $\bm s \in Sl_{\vert \bm{t}}A$ such that there exists $\varepsilon > 0$ satisfying 
        $$\{\bm{s}\} \times (\bm{t}-\bm{\varepsilon}, \bm{t} +\bm{\varepsilon}) \subset A.$$
    \end{itemize}

body: In combinatorics, the inclusion–exclusion principle is a counting technique which generalizes the familiar method of obtaining the number of elements in the union of two finite sets; symbolically expressed as where A and B are two finite sets and |S| indicates the cardinality of a set S. The formula expresses the fact that the sum of the sizes of the two sets may be too large since some elements may be counted twice. The double-counted elements are those in the intersection of the two sets and the count is corrected by subtracting the size of the intersection.
title: Inclusion–exclusion principle

[Corollary 4 of arXiv:2607.19873, 'Local limit theorem for the operator norm of products of random matrices'] Let $B$ be a compact metric space and let $\pi: E \to B$ be a 
Lipschitz vector bundle of dimension $d$ over $B$. 
Let $G$ be a locally compact group acting on $E$ by an isometric Lipschitz bundle action
and let $\mu$ be a Borel probability measure on $G$. 
Assume that there exists a constant $\alpha >0$ such that $\bb E ({\rm Lip}_E(g_1)^{\alpha} ) < \infty$ 
and that the pair $(G, \mu)$ satisfies the contraction property \eqref{contraction-property-on-B} on $B$. 
Then, for each $b \in B$, there exists a continuous linear map $\zeta_b: \bf \Gamma^{0}(E) \to \pi^{-1} (b)$
such that, for any section $s \in \bf \Gamma^{0}(E)$, we have  
\begin{align*}
\frac{1}{n} \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} P_{\mu}^k s(b)  \xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}  \zeta_b(s). 
\end{align*}
Moreover, this convergence holds uniformly over $b \in B$.
title: Corollary 4 of arXiv:2607.19873

body:
[Theo 15 of arXiv:2605.23292, 'Second-order Poincaré inequalities and localization on the Poisson space'] (normal approximation for sums of localizing score functions in hyperbolic space)
    Denote by $\mathcal{H}^d$ the $d$-dimensional hyperbolic space of curvature $-1$ and $\nu$ its standard Riemannian measure. For any $\lambda\geq 1$, let $W_\la \subseteq X_\la \subseteq \mathcal{H}^d$ with either $W_\la=X_\la$ or $W_\la=B(p,\la)$ for a fixed point $p\in \hyp$ and arbitrary $X_\la \subseteq \hyp$ containing $W_\la$. Let $\mathcal{P}_\la$ be a Poisson measure on $X_\la$ of intensity $\nu$ and $\hat{\mathcal{P}}_\la$ its marked version. Let $\xi:(X_\la \times \MM) \times \mathbf{N}_{X_\la \times \MM} \rightarrow \R$ be a score function on the marked space domain $X_\la \times \MM$ and define
    \[
    H_\la=\sum_{z \in \P_\la \cap W_\la} \xi((z,M_z),\hat{\P}_\la).
    \]
    Assume that the score $\xi$ satisfies $BL(\tfrac{1}{240})$-localization in space uniformly over $\la \geq 1$ such that 
    \begin{enumerate}[(i)]
        \item the function $\psi$ can be written as $\psi(r)=\min(2,\exp(-\tau(r)))$, where $\tau:\R \rightarrow \R$ is such that
        \begin{equation}
        \liminf_{r \rightarrow \infty} \frac{\tau(r)}{240(d-1)r} > 1.
        \end{equation}
        \item the moments $M_{5,X_\la}^\xi$ satisfy
        \[
        \sup_{\la \geq 1} M_{5,X_\la}^\xi < \infty.
        \]
    \end{enumerate}
    Then there is a constant $C>0$ such that for any $\la \geq 1$
    \begin{equation}
    \mathbf{d}_K\left( \frac{H_\la - \E H_\la}{\sqrt{\Var H_\la}},N\right) \leq C \frac{\nu(W_\la)^{1/2}}{\Var H_\la}
    \end{equation}
    and
    \begin{equation}
    \mathbf{d}_W \left( \frac{H_\la - \E H_\la}{\sqrt{\Var H_\la}},N\right) \leq C \frac{\nu(W_\la)^{1/2}}{\Var H_\la} + C \frac{\nu(W_\la)}{\Var H_\la^{3/2}}.
    \end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition prop:matrix-decomp of arXiv:2507.12502, 'Quantitative Edge Eigenvector Universality for Random Regular Graphs: Berry-Esseen Bounds '] At time $t_* = N^{-1/3+\varepsilon}$, the evolved matrix admits the decomposition
\[
\tilde{H}_{t_*} = e^{-t_*/2}\tilde{H}_0 + \sqrt{1-e^{-t_*}}W = \tilde{H}_0 - \frac{t_*}{2}\tilde{H}_0 + \sqrt{t_*}W + R
\]
where $W$ is a constrained GOE matrix satisfying $W\mathbf{e} = 0$ (defined in Section  (sec:transfer of the paper)), and the remainder $R$ satisfies
\[
\|R\| \leq \frac{Ct_*^{3/2}}{(1-e^{-t_*})^{3/2}} \cdot \|\tilde{H}_0\|^3 \leq CN^{-1/2+3\varepsilon/2}
\]
with probability at least $1 - N^{-D}$ for any $D > 0$.

[Lemma lem:lbm-abstract-direction-interface of arXiv:2608.02459, 'Response Calculus for Spectral Simplicity\\ and Joint Eigenvalue Densities'] The space $\mathcal Q_D$ has the following three properties.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textnormal{(\roman*)},leftmargin=*,itemsep=0pt,topsep=0.35em,parsep=0pt,partopsep=0pt]
\item $\mathcal Q_D$ is a nonzero countable rational vector space contained in
$C_c^\infty(D)=H_{\mathrm{reg}}$.
\item It is dense in the Cameron--Martin space:
\[
 \overline{\mathcal Q_D}^{\,H_0^1(D)}=H_0^1(D).
\]
\item Its annihilator among finite signed measures is trivial:
\begin{equation}
 \int_Dq\,d\sigma=0\quad(q\in\mathcal Q_D)
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \sigma=0,
 \qquad \sigma\in\mathcal M_{\rm fin}(D).
 
\end{equation}
\end{enumerate}

title: FPP chi=1/3 campaign, 2026-08-15 fire 8: rerouting FATTENS the per-block conditional fourth moment - the campaign's first positive measurement, pre-registered. THE DESIGN IS THE RESULT. Raw kappa4 cannot discriminate for (L2'): a sum of L iid centred uniforms has kurtosis exactly 3 - (6/5)/L, which CONVERGES to 3 as occupation grows, and (L2') holding also predicts a bounded kurtosis near 3 - null and alternative converge on the same number, so enlarging the blocks makes the experiment WEAKER, not stronger. The fix is PAIRING: each resample yields both Delta (rerouting allowed) and Delta_0 (no-reroute, summed over the ORIGINAL geodesic's edges inside the block) on the SAME weights with the SAME occupation, so Delta_0 is an EXACT empirical null and EXCESS := kappa4(Delta) - kappa4(Delta_0), bootstrapped by resampling PAIRS, cancels the occupation confound by construction. GENERAL FORM: when null and alternative converge on the same summary statistic, do not enlarge the experiment - find a statistic on which they diverge. MEASURED, reps sized from a measured first-pass CI half-width: at N=24, 106134 conditional samples, occupation 6.04, reroute fraction 0.383, kappa4 3.048 vs 2.992, excess +0.0557 with 95% CI [0.0263, 0.0843]; at N=40, 45345 samples, occupation 10.09, reroute 0.605, kappa4 3.106 vs 2.920, excess +0.1855 with CI [0.1290, 0.2403]. Both clear of zero and the excess more than triples. NOT A REVERSAL of the underpowered first pass - the N=40 estimate was +0.137 there with half-width 0.18 against +0.186 here with 0.056. HALF-EXPLAINED and flagged at the claim: the excess grows because kappa4(Delta) rises (+0.058) AND the null FALLS (-0.072), the latter against what the fixed-L formula predicts; the plausible cause is occupation VARIANCE differing by size, unmeasured. WHAT IT DOES NOT SAY: (L2') asks whether kappa4 stays BOUNDED, and kappa4 itself is 3.048 and 3.106 - bounded, near Gaussian, moving six hundredths over the whole range. Two points cannot establish a rate. NEXT: 3-4 more occupation points at matched sample counts plus a direct read of occupation variance per size; if the excess keeps climbing with the null controlled, that is the first real evidence AGAINST (L2'), which would take the 9.5 reduction with it. chi = 1/3 UNMOVED.

[Definition of arXiv:2609.00233, 'A survey on mapping class groups of 3-manifolds'] We set up some more terminology.
\begin{enumerate}
    \item     A compact, orientable \(3\)-manifold \(M\) is \emph{Seifert fibred} if it admits a Seifert fibration.
    \item The inverse image of a point $x \in B$ is called a \emph{fibre}.
    \item  The \emph{multiplicity} of an interior fibre is the number $a$ associated to that fibre in the local model from (defn:SFS-defn of the paper). The multiplicity of a boundary fibre is $1$.
    \item  A fibre is \emph{exceptional} or \emph{singular} if $p \neq \pm 1$, and is \emph{regular} otherwise.
\item       Let $g \in \mathbb Z$ be the genus of $B$ for $B$ an orientable surface, and let $ g:= -\beta_1(B)$ for  $B$ nonorientable.
\item  Let $c \in \mathbb Z_{\geq 0}$ be the number of boundary components of $B$.
\end{enumerate}
title: Unnumbered definition of arXiv:2609.00233, 'A survey on mapping class groups of 3-manifolds'

body: Bayesian inference is a method of statistical inference in which Bayes' theorem is used to calculate a probability of a hypothesis, given prior evidence, and update it as more information becomes available. Fundamentally, Bayesian inference uses a prior distribution to estimate posterior probabilities. Bayesian inference is an important technique in statistics, and especially in mathematical statistics. Bayesian updating is particularly important in the dynamic analysis of a sequence of data. Bayesian inference has found application in a wide range of activities, including science, engineering, philosophy, medicine, sport, psychology, and law. In the philosophy of decision theory, Bayesian inference is closely related to subjective probability, often called "Bayesian probability".

body:
Let P be a finite partially ordered set. The largest size of an antichain in P (a set of pairwise incomparable elements) equals the smallest number of chains (totally ordered subsets) whose union is P. The statement extends to infinite posets of finite width w: such a poset is a union of w chains. The dual statement (Mirsky's theorem) exchanges chains and antichains: the largest chain has size equal to the least number of antichains covering P.
P finite, or of finite width
metadata_json: {"artifact_digest":"sha256:d0e65d09c3e9a4fc01716db8ed5d468323bffcbf052370a2e41bfa21dc3b2eee","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/d0/d0e65d09c3e9a4fc01716db8ed5d468323bffcbf052370a2e41bfa21dc3b2eee.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:ea2cfa959096aae6f626bc9e9e4d79f94927404c371e6029f9e06d73562f05ba","bundle_entry_key":"stmt-wiki-dilworth-s-theorem","bundle_id":"population.wikipedia-leads-to-statements-001","claim_kind":"theorem","conditions":[],"domain":"order theory / combinatorics","draft":"claude-loop-mathbrain-b3b708/bundle_001.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:harvest.wikipedia:wiki-dilworth-s-theorem","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"The easy direction: an antichain meets each chain in at most one element, so any chain partition has at least as many chains as the largest antichain. For the converse argue by induction on |P|. Let a be a maximal element and apply induction to P' = P minus a: it is a union of k chains C_1, ..., C_k where k is the width of P'. If the width of P is k + 1 the chains together with the chain {a} do the job. Otherwise every maximal antichain of P' has size k and meets each C_i; let x_i be the largest element of C_i lying in some size-k antichain of P'. The set A = {x_1, ..., x_k} is an antichain: if x_i < x_j, take a size-k antichain A_j of P' containing x_j; it meets C_i in some element y, and y <= x_i by the choice of x_i, so y <= x_i < x_j with both y and x_j in A_j, contradicting that A_j is an antichain. If a were incomparable to every element of A then A together with a would be an antichain of size k + 1, against the width assumption; since a is maximal, a > x_i for some i. Let K be the chain {a} together with the elements of C_i at or below x_i. Every size-k antichain of P minus K would be a size-k antichain of P' avoiding the part of C_i below x_i, hence meeting C_i above x_i, contradicting the choice of x_i; so P minus K has width k - 1, induction partitions it into k - 1 chains, and K makes k. Mirsky's dual: give each element the length of the longest chain ending at it; elements of equal height are pairwise incomparable, so the height classes are antichains, and their number equals the length of the longest chain, which no antichain cover can beat since a chain meets each antichain at most once. Infinite posets of finite width w: every finite subposet is a union of w chains by the finite theorem, and a compactness argument (Tychonoff's theorem applied to the product of the finite sets of chain-labellings, or Rado's selection lemma) yields a single labelling of the whole poset into w chains consistent on every finite subposet.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:7b09312016e49880ce80485d30f216c41aada6801fe2cca944c4c57a2fc6f66b","revision_digest":"sha256:5e9b8e3afe63779218251401d655d8a837643e742443f1fe815ef508c3319b46","source_id":"wikipedia:Dilworth's theorem","source_revision":"statement authored 2026-08-29 replacing the lead read 2026-08-02","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":["claim_190531fba801b402364fe8b4d051674a16470545997d258174bb03488b4fdeed"],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

Let X_1, ..., X_n be independent centered random variables such that each X_i is sub-exponential with parameters (sigma_i^2, b). Let v = sum_{i=1}^n sigma_i^2. Then for any t >= 0, P(sum_{i=1}^n X_i >= t) <= exp(- t^2 / (2 * (v + b * t))).
X_1, ..., X_n are independent and centered
Each X_i is sub-exponential with parameter (sigma_i^2, b)
t >= 0

[Lemma 18 (Linear dissipative estimate) of arXiv:2605.03057, 'Uniform-in-time quantitative fluctuations of large scale interacting particle systems'] Fix $ p \ge 2 $, $ \kappa > 0 $, $ M \ge 0 $, and let $ 0 \le s \le u $. Let
$ \left( W_r \right)_{r \in [s,u]} $ be an $ m $-dimensional Brownian motion. Let
$ Y $ be an adapted continuous $ \R^d $-valued process satisfying
\begin{equation*}
Y_r
=
Y_s
+
\int_s^r
\left(
A_\ell Y_\ell + f_\ell
\right)
d\ell
+
\int_s^r
\left(
C_\ell\left[ Y_\ell \right] + g_\ell
\right)
dW_\ell,
\qquad
r \in [s,u],
\end{equation*}
where, for almost every $\ell \in [s,u] $, $ A_\ell$ is an $ \R^{d
  \times d}$-valued progressively measurable process, $ C_\ell $ is progressively measurable with values in the space of linear maps from
$ \R^d $ into $ \R^{d \times m} $, $ f_\ell $ is an $ \R^d $-valued
progressively measurable process, and $ g_\ell $ is an $ \R^{d \times
  m} $-valued progressively measurable process. Assume that, for all $ h \in \R^d $,
\begin{equation}

2 \left\langle h, A_\ell h \right\rangle
+
\left( p-1 \right)
\norm{C_\ell\left[ h \right]}^2
\le
-\kappa \abs{h}^2\quad\mbox{and}\quad
\norm{C_\ell\left[ h \right]}
\le
M \abs{h}.
\end{equation}
Assume also that
\begin{equation*}
\E\left( \abs{Y_s}^p \right)
+
\int_s^u
\E\left(
\abs{f_\ell}^p + \norm{g_\ell}^p
\right)
d\ell
<
\infty.
\end{equation*}
Then, it holds that
\begin{align}

\E\left(
\abs{Y_u}^p
\right)^{1/p}
\le
e^{-\kappa \left( u-s \right)/4}
\E\left(
\abs{Y_s}^p
\right)^{1/p}
+
\Lambda_{p,\kappa,M}
\left(
\int_s^u
e^{-p \kappa \left( u-r \right)/4}
\E\left(
\abs{f_r}^p + \norm{g_r}^p
\right)
dr
\right)^{1/p},
\end{align}
where $\Lambda_{p,\kappa,M}$ and $\Xi_{p,\kappa}$ are the quantities
defined in Assumption \ref{ass:first-malliavin-uniform}.

[Lemma 22 of arXiv:2506.11707, 'Fluctuations of two-dimensional determinantal processes associated with Berezin--Toeplitz '] Let $B$ be a self-adjoint operator and let $\Pi$ be an orthogonal
projector on a separable Hilbert space so that $\|\Pi B(1-\Pi)\|_{\tr} \le {\rm C}$.
One has, for $t\ge 0$,
\[
\|\Pi\mathcal U_t(B)\|_{\rm tr} \le {\rm C} t.
\]
Moreover, if $\Delta$ is a bounded operator such that 
\begin{equation} 
\| \Pi B(1-\Pi)\Delta\Pi\| \vee  \| \Pi \Delta (1-\Pi)B\Pi\| \vee \|[\Delta, B]\| \le \varepsilon  \, , \qquad 
\|\Pi\Delta \Pi B(1-\Pi)\|_{\tr} \le \varepsilon , 
\end{equation}
then for $t\ge 0$,
\[
\|\Pi\Delta\Pi\mathcal U_t(B) \|_{\tr}   \le \varepsilon (1+\tfrac 32
{\rm C}t).
\]
title: Lemma 22 of arXiv:2506.11707

Established criterion stated by Ruodu Wang in arXiv:1411.6190v3 Section 2.2(e), equation (7), p.9, attributing Wang-Wang Joint Mixability (doi:10.1287/moor.2015.0755): Let n>=2, and let F_i all have increasing densities on finite essential intervals [a_i,b_i], or all have decreasing densities there, with means mu_i. The tuple is jointly mixable if and only if sum a_i+max_i(b_i-a_i)<=sum mu_i<=sum b_i-max_i(b_i-a_i). Increasing/decreasing is nonstrict and includes step densities and uniform laws. Joint mixability here means a coupling with marginals F_i and sum equal to sum mu_i almost surely. This card records the exact author-survey statement; it does not claim the original long proof has been independently checked. Publisher access to the original theorem was blocked in this round.
All densities monotone in the same direction on their finite essential intervals
n>=2
a_i<b_i finite
title: Source note: Wang-Wang joint monotone-density mixability criterion

[Lemma G-CW-Hausdorff of arXiv:2608.28504, 'Global $\bm\infty$-categories and global Thom spectra'] Let $G$ be a compact Lie group and let ${\mathcal{F}}$ be any collection of closed subgroups of $G$ closed under conjugation. Then any ${\mathcal{F}}$-cofibrant $G$-space $X$ is Hausdorff, and every isotropy group of $X$ is contained in ${\mathcal{F}}$.
    \begin{proof}
        By Lemma~(lemma:restr-equiv-lQ of the paper), the underlying non-equivariant space of $X$ is cofibrant, hence Hausdorff. For the second statement, note that the collection of all spaces with isotropy groups contained in ${\mathcal{F}}$ is closed under coproduct, pushout and transfinite composition along closed embeddings, as well as under passage to subspaces. As moreover the source and target of any generating cofibration for the ${\mathcal{F}}$-model structure have isotropy groups contained in ${\mathcal{F}}$ (here we use the closure under conjugation), the lemma follows.
    \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma G-CW-Hausdorff of arXiv:2608.28504

[Lemma 33 (KL bound using regularized large gaps) of arXiv:2607.04138, 'Hives from deformed GUE minor processes'] \lab{lem:KLhive}
Let \(h_n\in H_n(\lambda_n,M_n;N_n)\) be the hive obtained, via
Proposition~\ref{gt-rem}(iv), from the large-gap construction applied to the
deformed GUE minor process for \(X_n\).
 Conditionally on \(h_n\), attach three
independent uniform Gelfand--Tsetlin patterns with top rows
\[
\lambda_n,\qquad M_n,\qquad N_n.
\]
Let \(q_n\) be the resulting density on the triply augmented hive space
\(\mathbb A^3\).

Let \(p_n\) be the maximum-entropy triply augmented hive density from
Theorem~\ref{thm:gaussian1}, with the same expected quadratic boundary
moments as \(q_n\):
\[
\mathbb E_{p_n}|\lambda|^2=\mathbb E_{q_n}|\lambda|^2,\qquad
\mathbb E_{p_n}|\mu|^2=\mathbb E_{q_n}|\mu|^2,\qquad
\mathbb E_{p_n}|\nu|^2=\mathbb E_{q_n}|\nu|^2.
\]
Then
\[
D_{\mathrm{KL}}(q_n\Vert p_n)=O(n\log n).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: KL bound using regularized large gaps

[Definition of arXiv:2605.15066, 'The critical activation density in graph bootstrap percolation'] Let $S\subset F$ be graphs and suppose that 
$V(F)$ is ordered. 
Let $S'\subset F'\subseteq G$ be some other graphs, where $V(G)$ is ordered.  
Then we call $F'$ an {\it $(S,F)$-extension}
of $S'$ in $G$ if  there is an isomorphism of the graphs $F\setminus E(S)$
and $F'\setminus E(S')$ such that 
the $i$th largest vertex in $S$ is mapped to the $i$th 
largest vertex in $S'$, for each $1\leqslant i\leqslant v(S)$.

[Theorem th:mlsi of arXiv:2608.19358, 'An optimal Poincaré inequality\\for the complex Ginibre log-gas'] For every symmetric $f\in\mathcal{C}^1(\mathbb{C}^n,\mathbb{R})$ such that
  $\Phi_f(G)=f(\lambda_1(G),\ldots,\lambda_n(G))\in
  H^1(\gamma_n^{\mathrm{mat}})$, we have
  \begin{equation}
    \operatorname{Var}_{\mu_n}(f)
    \leq
    \frac{2}{n}
    \mathbb{E}\left[
      a_f(G_n)^*\mathcal{O}(G_n)a_f(G_n)
    \right]
    \text{ and }
    \operatorname{Ent}_{\mu_n}(f^2)
    \leq
    \frac{4}{n}
    \mathbb{E}\left[
      a_f(G_n)^*\mathcal{O}(G_n)a_f(G_n)
    \right]
  \end{equation}
  where $a_f(G)$ is the random vector of $\mathbb{C}^n$ given by
  $(a_f(G))_j=\partial_{z_j}f(\lambda_1(G),\ldots,\lambda_n(G))$. Moreover the
  quadratic form on the right-hand sides is independent of the labeling of the
  eigenvalues. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 18 (Hypoelliptic propagation control from a non-characteristic boundary layer) of arXiv:2607.19752, 'Weak Equilibrium Measures and Capacity--Hitting Identities\\ for the Hypoelliptic Third-Or'] Let $\lambda\in(0,1/2)$.  For $\alpha>0$, define
\[
    C_{\alpha,\lambda}
    :=
    \left\{z\in\calD\setminus\calC:
        \dist(z,\calC)\le \alpha^\lambda,\quad
        |r|\ge \alpha^{\lambda/4}
      \right\}.
\]
Then
\[
    \sup_{z\in C_{\alpha,\lambda}}
    \Pbb_z\left(\tau_\calC>\alpha^\lambda\right)\to0
    \qquad\text{as }\alpha\downarrow0,
\]
and
\[
    \sup_{z\in C_{\alpha,\lambda}}
    \Pbb_z^\alpha\left(\tau_\calC^\alpha>\alpha^\lambda\right)
    \longrightarrow0
    \qquad\text{as }\alpha\downarrow0 .
\]
The same estimates hold for the adjoint processes.

Every pair is independent, exactly as for three iid fair bits, but the supermodular function phi(x)=x1*x2*x3 has expectations0 and1/8 respectively. The odd-parity law has the same pairwise distributions and expectation1/4. Thus identical pairwise data permits opposite comparisons for a legitimate supermodular test. Enumerating the four parity configurations verifies every pair marginal and the three distinct product expectations. Obstruction: These are static diagnostic laws, not a CTMC counterexample. A necessary-and-sufficient Markov generator condition must control the entire sequence of transition kernels at all lags and all supermodular test functions. [Thm operator_bdd of arXiv:2604.10446, 'Least singular values of shifted sparse random combinatorial matrices'] There are absolute positive constants $C_1$ and $C_2$ 
such that the following holds. 
Let $1\leq m\leq n$, $\gamma\geq 4$, $\beta \geq 1$, and let $d$ be an integer satisfying $1\le d \le n$.  
Let $M$ be an $m \times n$ random matrix with entries in $\{0, 1\}$, where each row is independently and uniformly 
sampled from the set of all vectors in $\{0, 1\}^n$ containing exactly $d$ ones. Let 
$$N= \max\big\{ 9 \min\{d,n-d\}, 2\gamma\log m \big\}.$$
Then, with probability 
    at least $1-n\cdot m^{-\gamma} -2n^{-\beta}$, one has 
    \[
     \|M-\mathbb{E}M\| \leq \frac{2 \min \{d,n-d\}}{\sqrt{N}} + C_1 \beta \sqrt{N}
     \leq C_2 \beta \left( \sqrt{\min\{d,n-d\}+ \gamma \log m} \right).
    \]
In particular, taking $m=n$, $\gamma=4$, $\beta =2$, and $\log n \leq d \leq n- \log n$, we have 
\[
 \|M-\mathbb{E}M\| =\|M^{T}-\mathbb{E}M^{T}\|\leq C_{(thm: operator_bdd of the paper)}\sqrt{d}.
\]
with probability at least $1 -3 n^{-1}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: In mathematics, the Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture describes the set of rational solutions to equations defining an elliptic curve. It is an open problem in the field of number theory and is widely recognized as one of the most challenging mathematical problems. It is named after mathematicians Bryan John Birch and Sir Peter Swinnerton-Dyer, who formulated the conjecture in the 1960s with the help of machine computation. Only special cases of the conjecture have been proven.
title: Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture

[Lem Varadhan of arXiv:2604.23751, 'Large deviation principles for pattern-avoiding permutations, and limit shapes for constra'] For any $n\ge 1,$ let $\mu_n$ denote the distribution of $X_n$ and assume that $(X_n)$ satisfies an LDP at speed $a_n$ with good rate function $I.$ Let $F:E \rightarrow \mathbb R$ be a bounded continuous function. Let the distribution $\nu_n$  be defined as follows:
 \[ \mathrm{d}\nu_n(x) := \frac{1}{Z_n} \textup{e}^{a_nF(x)} \mathrm{d}\mu_n(x),\]
 where $Z_n$ is a normalizing constant such that $\nu_n$ is a probability measure.
 Then we have
	\[ \lim_{n \rightarrow \infty} \frac{1}{a_n} \log Z_n = -  \inf_{y\in E} (I(y)- F(y)). \]
	Moreover, if we let $Y_n$ have distribution $\nu_n$,
the sequence $(Y_n)$ satisfies an LDP at speed $a_n$ with good rate function $J$
 given by
 \[ \forall x\in E, \quad J(x) = I(x) - F(x) - \inf_{y\in E} (I(y)- F(y)).\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lem Varadhan of arXiv:2604.23751

[Lemma of arXiv:2607.29020, 'Entropic Symmetrization Resistance'] \label[lemma]{lem:Zp_symmetrizer_space}
For $f \in_R \mathbb{Z}_{2q+1}$ ($q \ge 1$),
\[ \Sym(f) = 
    \{ g \in_R \mathbb{Z}_{2q+1}
    \mid \forall x \in [q] \quad
    \sum_{i=-q}^q (f(x-i) - f(-x-i)) g(i) = 0 \}.
    \]
In particular, $\dim(\Sym(f)) \ge q$. 
\begin{proof}
We identify the elements of $\mathbb{Z}_{2q+1}$ with $[-q,q] \cap \mathbb{Z}$ so that inverses are obvious. 
By direct computation, $\Sym(f)$ is the set of random vectors $g  \in \mathbb{Z}_{2q+1}$  such that for all integers $x \in [-q,q]$, $(f * g)(x) = (f * g)(-x)$, i.e.
\[    \sum_{i=-q}^q (f(x-i) - f(-x-i)) g(i) = 0 \}.    \]
But the condition corresponding to $x=0$ is vacuous, and for all $x \in [q]$ the conditions produced by $x$ and $-x$ are identical. 

To see the dimension, note that the simplex of probability measures on $\mathbb{Z}_{2q+1}$ has dimension $2q$, and we have imposed $q$ linear constraints. 
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition 8 (Minimal set) of arXiv:2607.20838, 'Long-memory Markov chains with power-law intensities'] An invariant set $M$ is called a minimal set if it contains no proper closed invariant subsets. 
	That is, for any closed invariant set $E \subseteq M$, we have $E = M$.
title: Minimal set

[Propo oo of arXiv:2412.01673, 'Spatial SIR epidemic model with varying infectivity without movement of individuals'] The system of equations (equation sy of the paper) admits a unique solution  $\left\{\left(\overline{\mu}^S_t,\overline{\mu}_t^{\mathfrak{F}},\overline{\mu}_t^{I},\overline{\mu}_t^{R}\right),\ t\ge0\right\}$   which is absolutely continuous with respect to the Lebesgue measure, with the densities\\ $\left\{\left(\overline{\mu}^S(t,.), \overline{\mu}^{\mathfrak{F}}(t,.), \overline{\mu}^{I}(t,.) ,\overline{\mu}^{R}(t,.)\right),\ t\ge0\right\}$ satisfying for all $(t,x)\in \mathbb{R}_+\times D$
	\begin{equation}
	
	\left\lbrace
	\begin{aligned}
	\overline{\mu}^{S}(t,x)&= \overline{\mu}^{S}(0,x)- \int_0^t\overline{\mu}^S(s,x)\int_DM(x,y)\overline{\mu}^{\mathfrak{F}}(s,y)dyds,\\
	\overline{\mu}^{\mathfrak{F}}(t,x) &=\overline{\lambda}^0(t)\mu^I(0,x)+\int_0^t\overline{\lambda}(t-s)\overline{\mu}^S(s,x)\int_DM(x,y)\overline{\mu}^{\mathfrak{F}}(s,y)dyds,\\
	\overline{\mu}^{I}(t,x)&= \mu^I(0,x)F_0^c(t)+\int_0^t F^c(t-s)\overline{\mu}^S(s,x)\int_DM(x,y)\overline{\mu}^{\mathfrak{F}}(s,y)dyds,\\
	\overline{\mu}^{R}(t,x)&= \overline{\mu}^R(0,x)+\overline{\mu}^I(0,x)F_0(t)+\int_0^tF(t-s) \overline{\mu}^S(s,x)\int_DM(x,y)\overline{\mu}^{\mathfrak{F}}(s,y)dyds,\\
	\overline{\mu}^{S}(0,x)&= \overline{S}(0)\pi_S(x),\ \overline{\mu}^{I}(0,x)= \overline{I}(0)\pi_I(x),\ \overline{\mu}^{R}(0,x)= \overline{R}(0)\pi_R(x),
	\\ \overline{\mu}(x)&=\overline{\mu}^S(t,x)+\overline{\mu}^{I}(t,x)+\overline{\mu}^{R}(t,x),\ \forall t\ge0.
	\end{aligned}
	\right.
	\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Propo oo of arXiv:2412.01673

body: Theorem (campaign status: proved): For five-sign support with repeated planar types $A,A,B$, let $G$ be the graph on the five supported columns with $ij\in E$ when $u_i+u_j=2T$, $T\in\{\pm B,\pm2A\pm B\}$. Each edge contributes at most two solutions, so a total of at least fourteen implies $|E(G)|\ge7$; Mantel gives a triangle, and a disconnected graph on five vertices has at most six edges, so $G$ is connected. Relabelling a triangle $0,1,2$ with edge labels $a,b,c$ determines $u_0=a+b-c$, $u_1=a+c-b$, $u_2=b+c-a$ uniquely; a spanning tree to vertices $3,4$ has exactly two forms, giving the count $6^3\bigl((3\cdot6)^2+3\cdot6\cdot6\bigr)=93{,}312$. Notes: VERIFIED: $216\cdot(324+108)=216\cdot432=93312$. There is no remaining continuous parameter -- the triangle determines $u_0,u_1,u_2$ and every attachment equation determines the next $u_i$. Sorting the five $u_i$ quotients only by an allowed $S_5$-symmetry, so the reduction to $2{,}934$ multisets is LOSSLESS. This is the argument that upgrades a finite enumeration into a complete classification.

body:
[Definition 38 of arXiv:2608.29157, 'Dilator-based analysis of $\KP$'] A sentence in the language of $\RS$ is \emph{axiomatic} if it is one of the following: 
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item Extensionality:
        \begin{equation*}
        \forall x\in \ttL(u)_\ttOmega\,
        \forall y\in \ttL(u)_\ttOmega
        \left[
          \neg\left(
            \forall z\in x\, z\in y
            \wedge
            \forall z\in y\, z\in x
          \right)
          \vee x=y
        \right].
        \end{equation*}
        
        \item Pairing:
        \begin{equation*}
        \forall x\in \ttL(u)_\ttOmega\,
        \forall y\in \ttL(u)_\ttOmega\,
        \exists z\in \ttL(u)_\ttOmega
        \left(
          x\in z\wedge y\in z
        \right).
        \end{equation*}
        
        \item Union:
        \begin{equation*}
        \forall x\in \ttL(u)_\ttOmega\,
        \exists y\in \ttL(u)_\ttOmega\,
        \forall z\in x\,
        \forall w\in z\,
        w\in y.
        \end{equation*}
        
        \item Set Induction:
        \begin{equation*}
        \neg
        \forall x\in \ttL(u)_\ttOmega
        \left(
          \neg\forall y\in x\,A(y)\vee A(x)
        \right)
        \vee
        \forall x\in \ttL(u)_\ttOmega A(x).
        \end{equation*}
        
        \item Infinity:
        \begin{equation*}
        \exists x\in \ttL(u)_\ttOmega
        \left[
          \exists y\in x\, y\in x
          \wedge
          \forall y\in x\,\exists z\in x\,y\in z
        \right].
        \end{equation*}
        
        \item $\Delta_0$-Separation:
        For every $\Delta_0$-formula $A(x,\vec a)$,
        \begin{equation*}
        \forall b\in \ttL(u)_\ttOmega\,
        \forall \vec a\in \ttL(u)_\ttOmega\,
        \exists c\in \ttL(u)_\ttOmega\,
        \forall x\in \ttL(u)_\ttOmega
        \left[
          \left(x\notin c\vee
            \left(x\in b\wedge A(x,\vec a)\right)
          \right)
          \wedge
          \left(
            \neg\left(x\in b\wedge A(x,\vec a)\right)
            \vee x\in c
          \right)
        \right].
        \end{equation*}
        
        \item $\Delta_0$-Collection:
        For every $\Delta_0$-formula $A(x,y,\vec a)$,
        \begin{equation*}
        \forall b\in \ttL(u)_\ttOmega\,
        \forall \vec a\in \ttL(u)_\ttOmega
        \left[
          \neg\forall x\in b\,\exists y\in \ttL(u)_\ttOmega A(x,y,\vec a)
          \vee
          \exists c\in \ttL(u)_\ttOmega
          \forall x\in b\,\exists y\in c\,A(x,y,\vec a)
        \right].
        \end{equation*}
    \end{enumerate}

    A sequent $\Gamma$ in the language of $\RS$ is \emph{axiomatic} if $\Gamma$ contains one of the following subsequent:
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item An axiomatic sentence.
        \item $A,\lnot A$ for some formula $A$.
        \item $s\notin s$ for some set term $s$.
        \item $s\subseteq s$ for some set term $s$.
        \item $s\neq t, \lnot A(s),A(t)$ for some set term $s$, $t$, and some formula $A$.
    \end{enumerate}

[Theorem 22 of arXiv:2608.01516, 'Nondegeneracy and regularity of polynomial pushforwards'] Let $n,d,k\in\mathbb N$ and assume that $n\ge k$. There exist two functions
\[
\alpha_{n,d,k}\colon(0,\infty)\to(0,\infty)
\quad\text{and}\quad
\beta_{n,d,k}\colon(0,\infty)\to(0,\infty),
\]
with the following property.

Let $\mu$ be an isotropic log-concave measure on $\mathbb R^n$,
and let
$f=(f_1,\ldots,f_k)\in \mathcal P_d(\mathbb R^n;\mathbb R^k)$
be such that
\[
\operatorname{Var}_\mu(f_j)>0,
\quad
\forall j\in\{1,\ldots,k\}.
\]
Then, for every $a>0$,
\[
\int_{\mathbb{R}^n} \Delta_{\hat{f}}\,d\mu\ge a
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\det \Sigma_\mu^d(f)\ge \beta_{n,d,k}(a),
\]
and, for every $b>0$,
\[
\det \Sigma_\mu^d(f)\ge b
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\int_{\mathbb{R}^n} \Delta_{\hat{f}}\,d\mu\ge \alpha_{n,d,k}(b).
\]

body:
[Corollary corr:covariances of arXiv:2411.07878, 'Bernstein-type and Bennett-type inequalities for unbounded matrix martingales'] Let $X_1, \dots, X_n \in \mathbb{R}(d)$ be independent random vectors, such that $U_i \coloneqq \norm*{\norm{X_i}}_{\psi_{\alpha}} < \infty$ for some $\alpha \ge 2$. Denote 
    \[
    \boldsymbol{\Sigma} \coloneqq \sum_{i=1}^n \E X_i X^T_i, \quad
    \sigma^2 \coloneqq \norm*{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}}, 
    \quad
    U^2 \coloneqq \sum_{i=1}^n U_i^2, \quad
    K \coloneqq \max_{i \in [n]} U_i ,\quad
    z \coloneqq z\lr{U, \sigma; \frac{\alpha}{2}}.
    \]
    Then, with probability at least $1 - d e^{-\mathrm{x}}$, it holds
    \[
    \lambda_{\max}\lr{\sum^n_{i=1} X_i X^T_i - \boldsymbol{\Sigma}} \le 2 \sigma K z \sqrt{\mathrm{x}} + \frac{4 K^2 z}{\min\lrc{2 \alpha z^{\alpha}, \hspace{0.2em}\underline{\log}\hspace{0.2em} \lr{\lr{ \frac{K }{\sqrt{2}\sigma }}^2 \mathrm{x}} }} \mathrm{x} .
    \]

[Def pi-realizable of arXiv:2607.19511, 'A Conditional Probability Hierarchy for Stochastic Choice\footnote{We thank Samson Abramsk'] A stochastic choice rule $G \mapsto c_G(\cdot)$ is \textbf{realizable as a $\Pi$-based probability mixture} if there is a finitely additive probability measure $Q$ on $(\Pi, {\cal D}_\Pi)$ such that for all $E \in \cal F$ and $G \in \cal G$:
\begin{equation}~
c_G(E) = Q([E, G]_\Pi).
\end{equation}
title: Def pi-realizable of arXiv:2607.19511

[Proposition prop:VDC_conseq of arXiv:2609.04045, 'Heat content and spectrum for subordinated sub-Laplacians'] Suppose that $\Omega$ is an open set in $\mathbb{G}$.
    \begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=*]
    \item If $\Omega$ satisfies the volume density condition then $\operatorname{Vol}(\partial\Omega)=0$.
    \item If $\Omega$ satisfies the intrinsic exterior cone condition and $\overline{\Omega}$ has finite volume, then it also satisfies the volume density condition. In particular, if $\Omega$ is open, bounded with $C^1$ boundary having no characteristic points, it satisfies the volume density condition.
    \end{enumerate}
title: Proposition prop:VDC_conseq of arXiv:2609.04045

[Definition of arXiv:2607.29020, 'Entropic Symmetrization Resistance'] A probability measure $\mu\in \mathcal{P}(G)$ is {\em $\Phi$-symmetrization resistant relative to $\mathcal{P}$ with constant $c>0$} if  
$$
A_{\Phi, \mathcal{P}}(\mu) \geq c\Phi(\mu) .
$$
If this holds with $c=1$, we simply say that $\mu$ is {\it $\Phi$-symmetrization resistant} in $\mathcal{P}$.
title: Unnumbered definition of arXiv:2607.29020, 'Entropic Symmetrization Resistance'

body: [Definition defn_tarp_parll of arXiv:2609.02491, 'Generalised Random Parking for Trapeziums on a Strip'] Define $\mathcal{T}_x$ as the unique trapezium of height $1$, and bases of length $x+(a-b)/2$ and $x-(a-b)/2$, where the longer base is on the lower side. Similarly, we define $\mathcal{P}_x$ as the unique parallelogram with two (parallel) sides of length $x$, height $1$ between those two sides, and acute angle $\vartheta=\arctan(2/(a-b))$ whenever $a>b$, and $\vartheta=\pi/2$ if $a=b$, where the left-most point is on the upper line.
title: Definition defn_tarp_parll of arXiv:2609.02491

[Theorem 14 (Frequency-envelope variant) of arXiv:2606.16662, '2606.16662'] Fix \(0<T\le T_0\) and a finite family \(\mathcal M\) of mixed labels.
Assume the Fourier-diagonal covariance model \eqref{eq:conv-cov} together with the envelope coefficient bounds \eqref{eq:env-K}--\eqref{eq:env-A-increment}.  Let \((\beta_\tau,\zeta_\tau,\sigma)\) be such that, for every \(\tau\in\mathcal M\), the two quantities \(\mathfrak S_{\tau,H}^{\eps}(\beta_\tau,\sigma)\) and \(\mathfrak S_{\tau,B}^{\eps}(\zeta_\tau,\sigma)\) in \eqref{eq:env-SH}--\eqref{eq:env-SB} are finite, with \(\eps>0\) leaving room for the time-lift absorption \eqref{eq:time-lift-absorb}.  Then, for every finite \(p\ge2\), the centered cutoff operators satisfy
\begin{equation}
        B_\Lambda^\tau\longrightarrow B^\tau
        \quad\hbox{in}\quad
        L^p\bigl(\Omega;\mathcal L(X_T^\sigma,Y_T^{\beta_\tau,\zeta_\tau})\bigr)
\end{equation}
and almost surely in the corresponding operator norm.  If, in addition, a deterministic diagonal resolution has been chosen so that the retained branches satisfy \eqref{eq:env-retained-bound}, the localized source-tail bound \eqref{eq:env-X-localized}, and fixed-block convergence in \(Y_T^{\beta_\tau,\zeta_\tau}\), then
\begin{equation}
        T_\Lambda^{\tau,\mathfrak P}=T_\Lambda^\tau-\Ctr^\tau_\Lambda
        \longrightarrow \Ret^\tau+B^\tau
        \quad\hbox{in}\quad
        \mathcal L(X_T^\sigma\cap\mathcal X_T,Y_T^{\beta_\tau,\zeta_\tau})
\end{equation}
almost surely and in \(L^p(\Omega)\).  Fully Wick-subtracted branches are obtained by setting \(\Ret^\tau_\Lambda=0\). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Frequency-envelope variant

[Lemma 4 of arXiv:2606.06193, 'Peng's Maximum Principle for McKean-Vlasov Stochastic Differential Equations with Common N'] If Assumption \ref{Assumption:C^{2,1}} holds, then, for any $k \geq 1$,
    \begin{align}
        &\mathbb{E}\left[\sup _{t \in[0, T]}\left\|\Delta X_t\right\|^{2 k}\right] \in O(\epsilon^k), \\
        &\mathbb{E}\left[\sup _{t \in[0, T]}\left\|Y_t\right\|^{2 k}\right] \in O(\epsilon^k), \\
        &\mathbb{E}\left[\sup _{t \in[0, T]}\left\|Z_t\right\|^{2 k}\right] \in O(\epsilon^{2k}),  \\
        &\mathbb{E}\left[\sup _{t \in[0, T]}\left\|\Delta X_t-Y_t\right\|^{2 k}\right] \in O(\epsilon^{2k}). 
    \end{align}

[Theorem 7 of arXiv:2604.19924, 'Fluctuation theory for spectrally negative Lévy processes killed by additive functionals'] Let $q \geq 0$, $x \in (c,b)$, and let $f:\R \to \R$ be a bounded, non-negative measurable function. Then
	\begin{align}
		\E_x\left[\int_0^{\tau_b^+\wedge\tau_c^-} e^{-qt-A_t} f(X_t)\,dt\right]
		= \int_c^b f(y)\left(
		\frac{W_{{\mathbf{T}}(\nu_A)}^{(q)}(x,c)}{W_{{\mathbf{T}}(\nu_A)}^{(q)}(b,c)}
		W_{{\mathbf{T}}(\nu_A)}^{(q)}(b,y)
		- W_{{\mathbf{T}}(\nu_A)}^{(q)}(x,y)
		\right)dy.
	\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Proposition 22 of arXiv:2609.02416, '2609.02416'] The exponential criteria used to close the simplicity argument are the following.

\textup{(i)} Assume the hypotheses of Lemma~\ref{thm:growth}. Let $\lambda_p=\Lp(\R)$ and choose $\beta>\gamma_H$. If
\[
\limsup_{|x|\to\infty}\left[a(x)+\lambda_p+d\big(M_J(\beta)-1\big)+q_1\beta\right]<0,
\]
where $M_J(\beta)=\int_\R J(z)e^{\beta|z|}\,dz$, then $W(x)=e^{\beta\sqrt{1+x^2}}$ satisfies $(\cA_\R+\lambda_p)W\le-\delta W$
outside a compact interval for some $\delta>0$. Every positive eigenfunction associated with $\lambda_p$ is $o(W)$. Consequently $\lambda_p$ is simple in the positive cone.

\textup{(ii)} Let $\lambda_p=\Lp(\R)$. Assume that every positive principal eigenfunction satisfies the exponential Harnack bound of Lemma~\ref{thm:growth} with exponent $\gamma_H$. Suppose there exist $\beta_+,\beta_->\gamma_H$ such that
\[
\limsup_{x\to+\infty}\left[a(x)+\lambda_p+d(M(\beta_+)-1)+q(x)\beta_+\right]<0
\]
and
\[
\limsup_{x\to-\infty}\left[a(x)+\lambda_p+d(M(\beta_-)-1)-q(x)\beta_-\right]<0,
\]
where $M(\beta)=\int_\R J(z)e^{\beta z}\,dz$; symmetry makes $M$ even. Then $\lambda_p$ is simple in the positive cone.

body: [SYNTHESIS 09-08 09:5x] Bernoulli 2/3: the three obstructions found separately - the CRT free window at 0.369m, the automaton floor of log 2, and the two-entropies gap log 3 versus log(3/2) - are ONE arithmetic deficit. Everything is a function of (A_m, x_m); the bit is A_m mod 2 and the depth-k history is fixed by A_m mod 3^k, so the coupling is governed by whether A_m equidistributes mod 2x3^k - and A_m ranges over only about (3/2)^m consecutive integers. Hence the free window is exactly k < m log(3/2)/log 3 = 0.36907m (where 3^k still fits), and the full history needs 3^m residues against (3/2)^m available, a shortfall of 2^m = log 2 per step. Same number three ways, and log 2/log(4/3) = 2.4094 is the same 2.41 reported independently. ONE WALL, not three: the integer A_m is too small a register for the information the phase history carries. It bounds only arguments that DECOUPLE bit from history; an argument estimating the actual correlation (measured defect 0.048, far below log 2) is untouched

body: Lemma (campaign status: audited-pass): Let E_1,...,E_k be the selected witness rows in deletion order; choose one pivot coordinate p_s from each witness pair. The pivots are distinct and E_s contains no later pivot p_t (t>s), so the matrix (h_s(p_t))_{s,t=1..k} is triangular with nonzero diagonal. Consequently {h_1,...,h_k} united with {e_i : i not in {p_1,...,p_k}} is a coordinate basis, and k <= ell/log2(4/3). All selected dense witnesses can be inserted simultaneously after O(ell) exchanges. If an old selector used a removed pivot Q_{p_s}, select the witness Y_s and add the discrepancy e_s = Q_{p_s} - Y_s: at most one new direction per exchange. Under bounded congestion the exchanged-basis quotient rank remains linear. Notes: ell = entropy defect ell(A). What fails is the stronger hope that ALL remaining rows are paid solely by the number of selected witnesses - ruled out by the Walsh crosspolytope (p.43).

[Lemma lem:loc_t of arXiv:2609.00978, 'Towards Categorical K\"ahler Geometry'] The quotient category $\cE=\cD/F(\cC)$ coincides with the localization along the components of the natural transformation $\tau\colon 1_{\cD}\to S$. Furthermore, any morphism $f\in\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{h}\cE}(X,Y)$ can be represented by a cospan in $\mathrm h\cD$ of the form
\[
X \xrightarrow{g} S^nY\xleftarrow{\tau^n_Y}Y, \qquad \tau^n_Y\coloneqq  \tau_{S^{n-1}Y}\cdots\tau_{SY}\tau_Y
\]
for some $n\geq 0$, in the sense that $f=(\tau_Y^n)^{-1}g$ in $\mathrm{h}\cE$.

[Theorem 1 (Descent--Hochster decomposition; informal form) of arXiv:2609.01882, '\textbf{Coxeter Descents and Parabolic Homotopy Colimits}\\[2mm] \large A Hochster-type de'] For every finite Coxeter system $(W,S)$ and every simplicial complex $\mathcal K\subseteq 2^S$ there is a based chain decomposition
\[
  \BK_{\mathcal K}(W)
  \cong
  \bigoplus_{w\in W}
  \Sigma^{2\ell(w)} C_*(A_{\mathcal K},L_{\mathcal K,\DesR(w)};\Z),
\]
and each relative summand admits an explicit unit Morse reduction
\[
  C_*(A_{\mathcal K},L_{\mathcal K,D};\Z)
  \simeq
  \Sigma\wtC_*(\sd\mathcal K_D;\Z).
\]
Consequently
\[
  H_n(\BK_{\mathcal K}(W);\Z)
  \cong
  \bigoplus_{w\in W}
  \wtH_{n-2\ell(w)-1}(\mathcal K_{\DesR(w)};\Z).
\]
For Weyl groups, $\BK_{\mathcal K}(W)$ is the cellular chain complex of $\XK(G)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Descent--Hochster decomposition; informal form

For every integer N >= 2 let X be uniform on H_N = {x in {-1,1}^N : x_1 x_2 ... x_N = 1}. Then every family of at most N - 1 coordinates of X is mutually independent, each coordinate an unbiased sign: P(X_i = s_i for i in I) = 2^(-|I|) for every proper subset I of {1, ..., N} and all signs s_i. The whole family is not independent: X_1 X_2 ... X_N = 1 almost surely, whereas for N independent unbiased signs the product is itself an unbiased sign. In bits b_i = (1 - X_i)/2 this is the uniform law on the words of even parity; N = 3 gives the classical three pairwise independent but not mutually independent events.
N is an integer, N >= 2
X is uniform on the sign vectors whose product is 1

[Defn of arXiv:2507.09120, 'Chemical distance in graphs of polynomial growth'] Let $0 \le \Delta < \infty$. A graph $G = (V,E)$ is called \emph{$\Delta$-simply connected}
   if for any edge cycle $C \subset E$, there exist edge cycles $C_1,...,C_N$ with each $\mathrm{diam} C_i \le \Delta$
   such that $C = C_1 \oplus \cdots \oplus C_N$,
   where $A \oplus B$ denotes the symmetric difference of sets $(A \setminus B) \sqcup (B \setminus A)$.
   That is, every cycle of $G$ is generated (under symmetric difference) by cycles of diameter at most $\Delta$.
   If $G$ is $\Delta$-simply connected for some $\Delta < \infty$, then we call $G$ \emph{coarsely simply connected}.
title: Unnumbered defn of arXiv:2507.09120, 'Chemical distance in graphs of polynomial growth'

[Defstar def:boundary of arXiv:2605.06488, 'Continuous-state branching processes with L\'evy-Khintchine drift-interaction: Laplace dua'] Let $\Delta \in \{0,\infty\}$.

\begin{enumerate}[(a)]
	\item
	$\Delta$ is \textbf{instantaneous} if
	\[
	\mathbb{P}_{\Delta}(T_\Delta=0)=1,
	\qquad 
	T_\Delta:=\inf\{t>0: X_t\neq \Delta\}.
	\]
	Equivalently,
	\[
	\mathbb{P}_{\Delta}\big(\forall t>0,\ \exists s\in(0,t): X_s\neq \Delta\big)=1.
	\]

\item   
$\Delta$ is \textbf{continuous} if, under $\mathbb{P}_\Delta$, the process is either identically equal to $\Delta$ (absorbing case) or leaves $\Delta$ without a jump, that is, the jump measure of the process vanishes at~$\Delta$.

Equivalently, in the non-absorbing case, if one denotes by $G$ the set of strictly positive left-end points of excursion intervals away from $\Delta$, then
\[\mathbb{P}_{\Delta}\left( \forall s\in G, \ X_s=\Delta \right)=1.\]
\item  $\Delta$ is \textbf{non-sticky} if
\begin{equation}
\mathbb{P}_x(X_t=\Delta)=0,\ \forall t\in (0,\infty), \ x\in [0,\infty].\end{equation}
Equivalently, the Lebesgue measure of the $\Delta$-level set $\{t\geq 0: X_t\in \Delta\}$ is zero. 
\item $\Delta$ is \textbf{regular-for-itself} if 
\begin{equation}\mathbb{P}_{\Delta}(R^{\Delta}=0)=1, \text{ with } R^\Delta:=\inf\{t>0: X_{t-}=\Delta \text{ or } X_t=\Delta\}.
\end{equation}
In words, the process started from $\Delta$, returns immediately to $\Delta$. 
\end{enumerate}
title: Defstar def:boundary of arXiv:2605.06488

[Proposition 4 (LDP for $R_n$) of arXiv:2605.22445, 'Generalized specific entropy on Wiener space with application to Martingale Optimal Transp'] Under the $1$-dimensional Wiener measure $\mathbb P$, the sequence $(R_n)_{n\ge1}$ satisfies a large deviation principle on $\mathcal M_1(D([0,1],\mathbb R^d))$ with speed $n$ and good rate function $I$, i.e. 
\begin{itemize}
\item[{\rm (i)}] For every open set $G \subset \mathcal M_1(D([0,1],\mathbb R^d))$, $$ \liminf_{n \to \infty} \frac{1}{n} \log \mathbb W ( R_n \in G)  \geq - \inf_{P \in G} I(P).$$
\item[{\rm (ii)}] For every closed set $F \subset \mathcal M_1(D([0,1],\mathbb R^d))$, $$ \limsup_{n \to \infty} \frac{1}{n} \log \mathbb W ( R_n \in F)  \leq - \inf_{P \in F} I(P).$$
\item[{\rm (iii)}] For any $k \in \mathbb R_+$, $\{P \in \mathcal M_1(D([0,1],\mathbb R^d)): \, I(P) \leq k\}$ is compact in weak topology. 
\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: LDP for $R_n$

[Definition D:prelandscapes of arXiv:2604.10020, 'The directed landscape in half-space'] A random function $\mathcal{M}^\rho: \mathbb{Q}^4 \cap \mathbb{H}^2_\uparrow \to \mathbb{R}$ is a \textbf{(half-space) pre-landscape} with parameter $\rho \in \mathbb{R} \cup \{-\infty\}$ if the following three conditions hold:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item (Triangle inequality) For any $o = (x, s)$, $p = (y, r)$, $q = (z, t) \in \mathbb{Q}_{\ge 0} \times \mathbb{Q}$ with $s<r<t$, we have
				$\mathcal{M}^\rho(o; p) + \mathcal{M}^\rho(p; q) \le \mathcal{M}^\rho(o; q)$.
				\item (Independent increments) For any $s_1<s_2<\cdots<s_k \in \mathbb{Q}$, the increments $\mathcal{M}^\rho(\cdot, s_i; \cdot, s_{i+1}):\mathbb{Q}_{\ge 0}^2 \to \mathbb{R}, i\in\llbracket1, k-1 \rrbracket$ are independent.
                \item (KPZ fixed point marginals) Recall that $\NW_{+}$ is the set of all $f \in \operatorname{UC}_+$ such that $\text{supp}(f) = \{x : f(x) > -\infty\}$ is finite. Consider any function $f \in \NW_{+}$ with $\text{supp}(f) \subset \mathbb{Q}_{\ge 0}$ and $f(\mathbb{R})\subset\mathbb{Q}\cup\{-\infty\}$.  Then for any $t, s \in \mathbb{Q}$, $s > 0$ and any finite set $Y \subset \mathbb{Q}_{\ge 0}$ we have that
				\[
				 (f \diamond \mathcal{M}^\rho(\cdot, t; y, t + s) : y \in Y)
				\stackrel{d}{=} (\mathfrak{h}^\rho (t, y; f) : y \in Y).
				\]
                Here the right-hand side above is given by Theorem (T:half-space-fixed-point of the paper).
\end{enumerate}
Moving forward, we will use the notation $\mathcal{M}^\rho_{s, t}(\cdot, \cdot) = \mathcal{M}^\rho(\cdot, s; \cdot, t)$ for the increment in a pre-landscape from time $s$ to time $t$, and the notation $\mathfrak{h}^\rho_t f = \mathfrak{h}^\rho (t, \cdot; f)$, which will help emphasize the semigroup structure under metric composition.
title: Definition D:prelandscapes of arXiv:2604.10020

[Lem 38 of arXiv:2510.22783, 'Universality of Cutoff for Riffle Shuffling'] With all assumptions in Proposition \ref{prop:new-firstmoment}, we have for all $y\in \tal,z\in \tar$ and $x \in A_{y,z}^{\stable}$, the following holds.
        \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
            \item 
            
            If $c_L(x)\geq 2\delta$, we have
        \begin{equation}
            \sum_{i=1}^{N-1}\mathbb P[(i,i+1)\in E(G_{B_x})]^2\leq C N^{4 c_L(x)- c_F(x)+2c_E( x)+O(\delta)} + e^{-\Omega(N^{\delta-o(1)})}.
        \end{equation}
            \item
             
            If $ c_L(x)< 2\delta$, $ c_F\geq\delta-(\log N)^{-1/2}$ and $A_{y,z}^{\stable}\neq\{y\vee z\}$, we have
              \begin{equation}
                  \sum_{i=1}^{N-1}\mathbb P[(i,i+1)\in E(G_{B_x})]^2\leq C N^{- c_F(x)+2c_E( x)+O(\delta)} + e^{-\Omega(N^{\delta-o(1)})}.
              \end{equation}
            \item 
            
            If $c_L(x)<2\delta$ and $ c_F(x)<\delta-(\log N)^{-1/2}$, then $x=y\vee z$ and $A_{y,z}^{\stable}=\{y\vee z\}$.
            \item 
            
            If $A_{y,z}^{\stable}=\{y \vee z\}$ and $c_L(y \vee z)<2\delta$, 
            we have $x=y\vee z$ and
            \begin{equation}
                \sum_{i=1}^{N-1}\mathbb P[(i,i+1)\in E(G_{B_{x}})]^2\leq C N^{2c_L(x)+2c_E(x)+O(\delta)} + e^{-\Omega(N^{\delta-o(1)})}.
            \end{equation}
        \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lem 38 of arXiv:2510.22783

body:
[Proposition SI_subshift_cocycle of arXiv:2605.02226, 'Finitely Dependent Processes on Subshifts'] Let $ X \subset \mathcal{A}^{\mathbb{Z}^d}$ be a strongly irreducible subshift for $ d \geq 2$. Let $G$ be a finitely generated group and $c:X\times \mathbb{Z}^d\to G$ be a continuous cocycle. For all $x\in X$, consider the map $c_x:\mathbb{Z}^d\to G$ given by $c_x(v)=c(x,v)$. Then there exists a constant $K$ such that
    \begin{enumerate}
            \item For all $x,y\in X$ and $u\in \mathbb{Z}^d$, there are group elements $g_1, g_2\in G$ such that $|g_1|, |g_2|<K$ and $c_x(u)=g_1c_y(u)g_2$.
        \item For all $x\in X$ and $v,w\in \mathbb{Z}^d$, there are group elements $g_1, g_2\in G$ such that $|g_1|, |g_2|<K$ such that $c_x(v+w)=c_x(v)g_1c_x(w)g_2$.
    \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition SI_subshift_cocycle of arXiv:2605.02226

[Theorem Thm.StrongUniqueness of arXiv:2411.15485, '\bf\Large Stochastic Volterra Equations for Local Times of Spectrally Positive L\'evy Proc'] If $\bar{\bar{\nu}}(0+)<\infty$, the stochastic Volterra equation (equation MainThm.SVE of the paper) has a unique strong solution. Moreover, the solution is a semimartingale with the following representation
 	\begin{eqnarray}
 	\left\{ \begin{split}
 	X_\zeta(t) 
 	&= \zeta \cdot c\cdot W'(t)  
 	+  \int_0^\zeta\int_0^\infty \big( W(t) -W(t-y)\big) \, N_0(dz, dy) \cr
 	&\quad + \int_0^t \Big( W''(0+) \cdot M(s) +  \int_0^s W'''(s-r)M(r)\,dr \Big) \, ds + \frac{1}{c}\cdot M(t),\cr
 	M(t) &= \int_0^t   \int_0^r \int_0^{X_\zeta(s)} \int_{r-s}^\infty    \widetilde{N}_\nu(ds,dz,dy)\,dr + \int_0^t \int_0^{X_\zeta(s)} \, B_c(ds,dz).
 	\end{split}
 	\right.
 	\end{eqnarray} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem Thm.StrongUniqueness of arXiv:2411.15485

[Lemma lem:threshold of arXiv:2609.03264, 'Certified Spherical MUSIC for 3D Localization under Adversarial Subspace Perturbations'] Suppose that $f\colon B_1(0)\to [0,\infty)$ is an $L$-Lipschitz threshold-admissible  landscape for $\{\bm{x}_\ell\}_{\ell=1}^s$ with parameters $(\varepsilon,\rho,\tau_0,\tau_1)$. Let $G\subset B_1(\bm{0})$ be a finite set satisfying
		\[
		{\rm mesh}_{B_1}(G)
	<
		\min\left\{
		\rho-\varepsilon,\,
		\frac{\tau_1-\tau_0}{L}
		\right\}.
		\]
		Define the thresholded set
		\begin{eqnarray}
		G_{\tau_1}
		:=
		\{\boldsymbol\omega\in G:f(\boldsymbol\omega)<\tau_1\}.
		\end{eqnarray}
		By (equation eq:2.2 of the paper), 	
		$$	
		G_{\tau_1}
		\subseteq
		\bigcup_{\ell=1}^s B_\rho(\bm{x}_\ell).
		$$
In addition,
		\[
		B_\rho(\bm{x}_\ell)\cap G_{\tau_1} \neq \emptyset,\quad  \forall \ell\in\{1,\dots,s\}. 
		\]

[Proposition 27 of arXiv:2609.03191, 'On lifting representations and actions on curves of the metacyclic groups $C_{p^s}\rtimes '] Suppose that $X\rightarrow X/G$ is an HKG cover. Let
$$l_1<\cdots<l_s$$
be the lower jumps of the wild cyclic subgroup $H=C_{p^s}$ at the wild branch point. Then the following properties hold.

\medskip
\smallskip
{\bf (1) (Bleher--Chinburg--Kontogeorgis)} For each $b\in\llbracket0,p^s-1\rrbracket$, with the notation of Proposition \ref{P3}(4), we have
\begin{equation}
d_b=\left\lfloor \frac{N_{s,b}}{p^s}\right\rfloor=\left\lfloor \frac{\sum_{i=1}^s p^{s-i}[p-1+(p-1-\delta_{i,b})l_i]}{p^s}\right\rfloor.
\end{equation}

{\bf (2)} The set $\{x^idx|i\in\llbracket0,d_b-2\rrbracket\}$ is a $k$-basis of $H^0\bigl(\mathbb P_k^1,\Omega_{\mathbb P_k^1}(D_b)\bigr)$. In particular, if $d_b\le 1$, then this $k$-vector space is $\{0\}$.

\smallskip
{\bf (3)} For $b\in\llbracket0,p^s-1\rrbracket$, we have $d_b=0$ if and only if $b=p^s-1$.

\smallskip
{\bf (4)} The sequence $(d_b)_{b\in\llbracket0,p^s\rrbracket}$ is non-increasing.

[Proposition of arXiv:2601.07808, 'Supercritical long-range percolation on graphs of polynomial growth: the truncated one-arm'] \label[proposition]{prop:giant_concentration}
    Let $G$ be a transitive graph of polynomial growth with $d \geq 1$, and suppose that $J : V \times V \to \mathbf{R}_+$ is a transitive kernel with $J(x,y) = \Omega(d_G(x,y)^{-d \alpha})$ with $\alpha > 1$. 
    
    Let $\beta > \beta_c$ be sufficiently large.
    
    Then there exist $\rho = \rho(\beta,G,J) > 0$ and $c = c(\beta, G,J) > 0$ such that for all $r$ sufficiently large,
    
    \begin{equation}
        \mathbf{P}_{\beta}
        \left(
            \# 
            K
            (r)
            \geq 
            \rho
            \# B(r) 
        \right)
        \geq 
        \exp
        \left(
            - c  
            \# S(r)
        \right).
    \end{equation}

[Theorem label_multiple_vertices_conditional_degrees of arXiv:2606.09386, 'High-degree vertices in uniform recursive directed acyclic graphs with freezing'] Fix $m,k\in\mathbb{N}$ and $(b_v)_{v\in [k]}\in[0,m+1)^k$. Let $V_1,\ldots,V_k\in\mathbb{A}_n$ be distinct active vertices selected uniformly at random. Let $(d_v(n))_{v\in[k]}$ be $k$ integer-valued sequences diverging to infinity such that, for all $v\in[k]$, $\lim_{n\to\infty}d_v(n)/h_n^+ = b_v$. Fix a choice sequence $\mathbf x$ such that Assumption~$\hyperref[ass:A]{\mathbf{x}}$(item:geq1 of the paper) and~$\hyperref[ass:A]{\mathbf{x}}$(item:lb of the paper) are satisfied  with $I_{\hyperref[ass:A]{\mathbf{x}}}=\mathcal{O}((h_n^+)^{\gamma_0(1/2-\delta)})$, where $\gamma_0\in(1,\min\{(1/2+\delta)^{-1},(1-2\delta)^{-1}\})$ and $\delta$ is as in Part~(item:lb of the paper).
Let $(M_i)_{i\in[k]}$ and $(N_i)_{i\in[k]}$ be i.i.d.\ standard normal random variables. Then, conditionally on the event $\{\deg_n(V_v)\geq d_v\text{ for all }v\in[k]\}$,
\begin{equation} \begin{aligned} 
\bigg({}&\frac{u_n(V_v)-(mh_n^+-\frac{m}{m+1}d_v)}{\sqrt{mh_n^+-\frac{m}{(m+1)^2}d_v}}, \frac{h_{V_v}^+-(h_n^+-\frac{1}{m+1}d_v)}{\sqrt{\frac{1}{(m+1)^2}d_v}}\bigg)_{v\in [k]}\\
&\buildrel {\mathrm{d}}\over{\longrightarrow} \bigg(M_i\sqrt{\frac{mb_v}{(m+1)^2-b_v}}+N_i\sqrt{1-\frac{mb_v}{(m+1)^2-b_v}},M_i\bigg)_{i\in[k]}.
\end{aligned} \end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition prop:tropp_bound of arXiv:2411.07878, 'Bernstein-type and Bennett-type inequalities for unbounded matrix martingales'] Let $\mathbf{X}_1, \dots, \mathbf{X}_n \in \mathbb{H}(d)$ be a sequence adapted to a filtration $\mathscr{F}_1 \subset \mathscr{F}_2 \subset \dots \subset \mathscr{F}_n $. 
    Let $\mathbf{X}_k$ satisfy for all $k = 1, \dots, n$
    \[
    \E[\mathbf{X}_k | \mathscr{F}_{k-1}] = 0, 
    \quad
    \lambda_{\max}(\mathbf{X}_k) \le K~\text{a.s.}
    \]
    Set for all $k = 1, \dots, n$
    \[
    \mathbf{S}_k  \coloneqq \sum^k_{i=1} \mathbf{X}_i, 
    \quad
    \boldsymbol{\Sigma}_k \coloneqq \sum^k_{i=1}  \E\left[\mathbf{X}^2_i \middle| \mathscr{F}_{i-1}\right].
    \]
    Then, for all $t \ge 0$ and $\sigma^2 > 0$,
    \[
    \mathbb{P} \lr{\exists k \ge 0: \lambda_{\max}(\mathbf{S}_k) \ge t~~\text{and}~~ \norm{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_k} \le \sigma^2} \le d \elr{-\frac{\sigma^2}{K^2} h\left(\frac{K t}{\sigma^2} \right)}.
    \] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 3.1, \cite{tropp2011freedman}

[Lemma meanfieldspectralgap of arXiv:2606.01937, 'Stationary fluctuations for an exclusion process with mass and energy conservation'] For $\alpha\in [0,1]$, define the binomial product measure $\varpi_\alpha = \mathrm{Bin}(\kappa ,\alpha )^{\otimes\mathbb{Z}}$. There exists a universal constant $C_{11}=C_{11}(\kappa )>0$ such that for any local function $f:\Omega\longrightarrow\mathbb{R}$ supported in $\{0,\hdots ,\ell -1\}$ for some $\ell\ge 1$, and such that~$\varpi_\alpha(f)=0$ for any $\alpha\in [0,1]$, we have
    \begin{equation}
        \mathrm{Var}_{\varpi_\alpha}(f) \le \frac{C_{11}}{\ell}\sum_{x,y=0}^{\ell -1}\int_{\Omega}\eta_x(\kappa -\eta_y)\big[ f(\eta^{x\to y})-f(\eta )\big]^2\,\mathrm{d}\varpi_\alpha(\eta ).
    \end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Mean-field spectral gap estimate

[Lemma 8 (Talagrand's inequality) of arXiv:2608.18557, 'Randomly Permuted Orthogonal Products and Fast Dimension Reduction'] Let \(\xi\in\{-1,1\}^d\) be a Rademacher vector, and let

	\right\}
	\le
	4\exp\left(
	-\frac{t^2}{8L^2}
	\right) \qquad \text{for } t\geq0.
	\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Every smooth manifold M of dimension n > 0 that is Hausdorff and second-countable admits a smooth embedding into R^{2n}: there is a smooth map i: M -> R^{2n} that is an injective immersion and a homeomorphism onto its image with the subspace topology.

[Definition def:discrete_process of arXiv:2411.13964, 'Long-time analysis of a pair of on-lattice and continuous run-and-tumble particles with ja'] Let $L$ be a positive integer,
  $y^L_0 \in \{ 1, \ldots, L \}$  and
  $\sigma^1_0, \sigma^2_0 \in \{-1, 1\}$ (resp.
  $\sigma^1_0, \sigma^2_0 \in \{-1, 0, 1\}$) . Let $\sigma^1$ and $\sigma^2$ be two
  independent Markov jump processes with the transition rates of
  figure (fig:single_speed_transition_rates_slowman_2016 of the paper)
  (resp. (fig:single_speed_transition_rates_slowman_2017 of the paper)) and respective initial states \( \sigma^1_0 \) and \( \sigma^2_0 \). Further let
  $N_1$ and $N_2$ be two independent Poisson clocks with rate $\gamma$
  independent of the $\sigma^i$. Recursively define $y^L(t)$ by $y^L(0) = y^L_0$ and,
\begin{itemize}
\item when $N_1$ rings at time $t$, $y^L(t)=\max(1,\min(L, y^L(t-) - \sigma^1(t-)))$.
\item when $N_2$ rings at time $t$, $y^L(t)=\max(1,\min(L, y^L(t-) + \sigma^2(t-)))$
\end{itemize}

[Lmm lmm1.4ext of arXiv:2609.02682, 'LDP for tensor forms'] Let  $G_{W_\infty, \phi}$  be as in (def:g2 of the paper).
For an arbitrary function $\phi:[c]^v\to \mathbb{R}$, a probability measure $\mu$ on $[c]$, and $\beta\in \mathbb{R}$, let $Z(\beta,\mu)$ be as in
  
  
  
 the RHS of (equation eq:potts_unconstrained_opt2 of the paper). Also, let $\mathscr{F}_{\beta, \mu}\subseteq \mathcal{F}_c$  be the set of maximizers in (equation eq:potts_unconstrained_opt2 of the paper).
    \\
    \begin{itemize}
        \item[(i)]     If $\big\{ G_{W_{\infty},\phi}(\boldsymbol f): {\boldsymbol f} \in \mathscr{F}_{\beta, \mu}\big\}$ has cardinality one for some $\left(\beta, \mu\right)$, and $Z(., \mu)$ is differentiable at $\beta$, then
 $Z^\prime\left(\beta, \mu\right)= G_{W_{\infty},\phi}({\boldsymbol f}^*)$ for ${\boldsymbol f}^* \in \mathscr{F}_{\beta, \mu}$.
 \item[(ii)] Moreover, if for the same $\left(\beta, \mu\right)$ as above we also have $ Z^\prime\left(\beta, \mu\right)=t$, then $$\underset{\substack{\boldsymbol f \in \mathcal{F}_c \\ { G_{W_{\infty},\phi}(\boldsymbol f)= t}}}{\arginf} \int_0^1\sum_{r=1}^c f_{r}(u)\log \frac{f_{r}(u)}{\mu_r}du=\mathscr{F}_{\beta, \mu}. $$
 \end{itemize}

Measured 2026-09-05 on the EMIT and OCO-2 stacking pools (70 cells, split B, full calibration, paired). The two-vertex blend of the transductive covariance penalty keeps the simplex's gain on EMIT and closes three quarters of its deficit to the pool's hand-tuned heuristic on OCO-2 (-0.27 there); the heuristic is itself label-free, so it was added as a third vertex with barycentric weights chosen by the same criterion. P26 (a) REFUTED: on OCO-2 the three-vertex blend reads -0.09 vs the pool best and +0.18 vs the two-vertex blend; (b) HELD: on EMIT it reads +4.78 vs the pool best and +0.05 vs the two-vertex blend; (c) HELD: mean weights (simplex, least squares, pool) are (0.09, 0.44, 0.47) on OCO-2 and (0.59, 0.24, 0.17) on EMIT; falsifier (three-vertex worse than two-vertex by more than 0.5 on either corpus) not triggered. Fresh-split replication (P27, split C, pre-registered before the split-B result was read): P27 (a) HELD: on split C OCO-2 the three-vertex blend reads -0.12 vs the pool best and +0.20 vs the two-vertex blend; (b) HELD: on EMIT +4.83 vs the pool best and +0.18 vs the two-vertex blend; (c) HELD: mean weights (simplex, least squares, pool) (0.11, 0.42, 0.48) on OCO-2 and (0.57, 0.26, 0.17) on EMIT; falsifier (three-vertex worse than two-vertex by more than 0.5 on either corpus) not triggered. A fourth vertex (P33, the CV-shrunk long-only stack that the calibration-only selector picks on most EMIT cells): P33 (a) REFUTED: on EMIT the four-vertex blend reads +0.06 vs the three-vertex blend and +4.84 vs the pool best (candidate B alone +5.23, the three-vertex blend +4.78); (b) HELD: on OCO-2 +0.00 vs the three-vertex blend (-0.09 vs the pool best); (c) REFUTED: mean weights (simplex, least squares, pool, B) are (0.48, 0.26, 0.14, 0.12) on EMIT and (0.01, 0.48, 0.40, 0.11) on OCO-2; falsifier (four-vertex worse than three-vertex by more than 0.3 on either corpus) not triggered. P42: the held-out split D (P42): P42 (a) HELD: on split D OCO-2 the three-vertex blend reads +0.06 (registered) / +0.10 (R_1) vs the pool's heuristic, its best vertex there (within 0.3); (b) HELD: on split D EMIT +4.31 / +5.33 vs the pool's heuristic (at least +4.0; P26 / P27 read +4.78 / +4.83) - on this split the simplex is the best single vertex and the blends read +0.13 / +1.27 against it; (c) REFUTED: R_1 vs the registered blend +1.08 on EMIT, +0.04 on OCO-2 (within 0.2); (d) HELD: the prediction-norm variant of the registered criterion vs the registered blend +0.00 / +0.00 (within 0.1); (e) HELD: the same for R_1 -0.05 / +0.00; falsifier (EMIT gain over the pool's heuristic below +3.0 or OCO-2 worse than it by more than 0.5, either criterion) not triggered; the (d)/(e) falsifier (a difference beyond 0.3) not triggered.

[Thm 4 of arXiv:2606.24584, '2606.24584'] Let $(D_\ell)_{\ell\geq 1}$ be a sequence of doubly stochastic matrices in $\Omega_n$. If
\[
\sum_{\ell=1}^\infty \big(1-\sigma_2(D_\ell)\big) = +\infty,
\]
where $\sigma_2(D_\ell)$ denotes the second largest singular value of $D_\ell$, then
\[
\lim_{m\to\infty} D_1D_2\cdots D_m = J_n.
\]
title: Thm 4 of arXiv:2606.24584

[Cor cor;non of arXiv:2411.00663, 'Ergodicity and Mixing of invariant capacities and applications'] Let $(\Omega,\mathcal{F},P)$ be a probability space, and $T:\Omega\to\Omega$ be a measurable transformation. If there exists an upper probability $V$ on $(\Omega,\mathcal{F})$ such that $V$ is ergodic with respect to $T$, and $P\in\operatorname{core}(V)$, then there exists a unique ergodic probability $Q\in\mathcal{ M}^e(T)\cap \operatorname{core}(V)$ on $(\Omega,\mathcal{F})$ such that  for any $f\in L^1(\Omega,\mathcal{F},Q)$,
	$$
	\lim _{n \rightarrow \infty} \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=0}^{n-1} f(T^{i} \omega)=\int f dQ,\text{ for }P\text{-a.s. }\omega\in\Omega.
	$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Cor cor;non of arXiv:2411.00663

body:
[Corollary cor:multiplicative-type-diversity of arXiv:2609.01690, 'Iterated-sumset spectra: The complete exponent law and its rank geometry'] For fixed $k\geq3$ and $0\leq r\leq k-2$, as $h\to\infty$, the number of weak
$h$-multiplication-table types of rank $r$ is
\[
 \Theta_{k,r}\!\left(h^{(k-1)r}\right).
\]
The total number of weak multiplication types, the total number of ordered
multiplication types, and the total number of generic multiplication types
are all
\begin{equation}
 \Theta_k\!\left(h^{(k-1)(k-2)}\right).
\end{equation}
