PRIVATE REDUCTION, author-recorded. Under (IID)+(UE) transience in direction l gives the Sznitman-Zerner regeneration structure with tau_1 < infinity a.s.; ballisticity is E[tau_1 | D = infinity] < infinity (Drewitz-Ramirez Open Question 2.20). Under (UE) a trap of diameter r holds the walk at most exponentially long in r, so sub-ballistic behaviour needs polynomially rare traps of logarithmic size along the path, which i.i.d. environments do allow; the question is whether the tail P(tau_1 > n) can be as heavy as n^{-1+eps}. Open Question 3.20 (does positive velocity imply (P)_M for M > 15d + 5) asks at least as much as whether a finite first moment of tau_1 self-improves to higher moments: (P)_M for M >= 15d + 5 implies (T') and with it finite moments of tau_1 of every order, so a yes to 3.20 gives the self-improvement. The converse, (P)_M from a moment of tau_1 of order about M/d, is not established, so reading 3.20 as equivalent to moment self-improvement is a conjecture, not a reduction. The Guerra-Ramirez theorem (T) <=> (T') (2018) settles Open Question 3.28 but neither of these. Recorded as a one-directional moment-self-improvement reformulation.

[Lem spectralradius of arXiv:2608.13084, '\bf Branching random walk in random environment'] If $A$ is finite and connected subset in ${\mathbb Z}^d$ with $\#A\ge 2$, then we have
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\rho_A\in (0,1)$.
\item for any $x\in A$, the limits 
\[
\lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{{\bf Q}_x(\tau_A>2n)}{\rho_A^{2n}} \textrm{ and } \lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{{\bf Q}_x(\tau_A> 2n +1)}{\rho_A^{2n+1}},
\]
exist and belong to $(0,\infty)$. In general, these two limits are different.
\item 
For every sequence of
finite connected sets $(A_k)$ with $R_{A_k}\to\infty$, we have
$\rho_{A_k}\to1$,
where $R_A$ denotes the radius of the largest $\ell^1$-ball contained in $A$, i.e., 
\[
R_A:= \max\{ R\in {\mathbb N} \vert \exists y\in A \textrm{ such that } \{z\in {\mathbb Z}^d: |z-y|_1\le R\}\subset A\}.
\]
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lem spectralradius of arXiv:2608.13084

Let U ⊂ C be open and connected, let f_n be holomorphic on U, and assume the family {f_n} is uniformly bounded on every compact subset of U. Assume also that the limit of f_n(z) exists in C for every z in a set E ⊂ U that has at least one accumulation point inside U. Then f_n converges uniformly on every compact subset of U, and the limit is holomorphic on U. (This is the complex-analytic Vitali convergence theorem; it is unrelated to the measure-theoretic theorem of the same family of names.)

[Theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] We have the following formula, valid for any $a,b>0$,
$$\int_0^1x^{a-1}(1-x)^{b-1}dx=\frac{\Gamma(a)\Gamma(b)}{\Gamma(a+b)}$$
generalizing our previous computation for $a,b\in\mathbb N$, which was as follows:
$$\int_0^1x^{a-1}(1-x)^{b-1}dx=\frac{(a-1)!(b-1)!}{(a+b-1)!}$$
The above quantity is denoted $B(a,b)$, and called beta function.

  Any weighted simplicial complex $(K,\mu)$ determines
  a map $\lambda_{\mu}: |K| \rightarrow \mathbb Z_+$ by:
      \begin{equation} 
         \lambda_{\mu} (x) = \mu(\mathrm{Car}_K(x)), \ \forall  x\in |K|,
    \end{equation}
   where $\mathrm{Car}_K(x)$ is the unique simplex of $K$
   such that $|\mathrm{Car}_K(x)|$ contains $x$ in the relative interior.  
     We call $(|K|,\lambda_{\mu})$ the \emph{geometric realization} of $(K,\mu)$.

Let nu be a real signed Borel measure on R such that every polynomial is absolutely integrable with respect to its total variation. Suppose q_0,...,q_(N+1), for an integer N>=0, are monic orthogonal polynomials for nu with deg(q_j)=j. Fix 0<=i<=N and r in R such that q_i(r)!=0. Assume that (t-r)dnu(t) has a unique monic polynomial of degree i orthogonal to all polynomials of degree<i. Then that polynomial is [q_(i+1)(t)+alpha_i q_i(t)]/(t-r), where alpha_i=-q_(i+1)(r)/q_i(r). The numerator vanishes at r, so the quotient is a polynomial. The existence and uniqueness assumption for the modified signed measure is essential; positivity of nu is not assumed. This is Cohn-Kumar Lemma3.3.

monic orthogonal family through degree N+1

[Lemma fix-rec-UB of arXiv:2608.19050, 'Online Permutation Embedding: \\ Optimal Stopping and Scaling Laws'] Let $\pi$ be a non-empty permutation of $[k]$. Let $\tau$ be any stopping time defined on the collection of variables $X_0,X_1,\ldots$ with $\EE\,\tau<\infty$, and let
\[
    \mathcal{A}_L=(\tau_j^L)_{j=1}^{\pi(1)-1},
    \qquad
    \mathcal{A}_R=(\tau_j^R)_{j=1}^{k-\pi(1)}
\]
be randomized online embedding algorithms for $L(\pi)$ and $R(\pi)$, respectively, with finite expected runtime. There is a randomized online embedding algorithm $\mathcal{A}=(\tau_j)_{j=1}^k$ for $\pi$ such that
\[
    \EE\tau_k
    =
    \EE\,\tau
    +
    \EE\,\Big(\frac{1}{X_\tau}\Big)\EE\,T_{\mathcal{A}_L}
    +
    \EE\,\Big(\frac{1}{1-X_\tau}\Big)\EE\,T_{\mathcal{A}_R}.
\]
If one of $L(\pi)$ and $R(\pi)$ is empty, the corresponding algorithm and term are omitted. In particular, for every subtree $S$ of $\mathcal{T}_\pi$, there is a recursive interval algorithm $\mathcal{A}_S^*$ with
\[
    \E{T_{\mathcal{A}_S^*}}=b(S).
\]
Consequently, $\beta(\pi)\le b(\mathcal{T}_\pi)$ for every permutation $\pi$.

body:
[Theorem 7 of arXiv:2607.13273, 'Asymptotics of transition densities for L\'evy processes with stochastic resetting'] Let $\beta\in(0,1)$ and $Y_t$ be a $\beta$ -- stable subordinator, i.e., real-valued L\'evy process with non-decreasing sample paths, such that 
	\[
          \mE e^{-s Y_t} = 
          e^{-t s^\beta},\quad s,t>0, 
	\]
        and $\mP(Y_t<0)=0$ for all $t>0.$ Then, for all $\lambda>0, t>0,$ and $x\in\R,$ the density $p_\lambda(t,x,\cdot)$ of
        the corresponding process with resetting exists and satisfies
        \begin{equation}
		   p_\lambda(t,x,u)\sim_{t,u}\,\, \frac{\beta}{\lambda\Gamma(1-\beta)}u^{-1-\beta}.
	\end{equation}

body:
[Theorem 7 of arXiv:2512.04807, 'Existence and uniqueness of the canonical Brownian motion in non-simple conformal loop ens'] Consider the setup described just above. There exists a unique (up to a deterministic factor) collection of measurable functions $\Gamma^D \mapsto \rform{\cdot}{\cdot}{\Gamma^D}$ for each simply connected domain $D \subseteq \C$ where each $\rform{\cdot}{\cdot}{\Gamma^D} = ((\rformres{k}{\cdot}{\cdot}{\Gamma^D}, \rfdomainres{\Upsilon_k}{\Gamma^D}))_{k \in \N}$ is a collection of resistance forms with the following properties. There is a further collection of resistance forms $((\rformres{V}{\cdot}{\cdot}{\Gamma^D}, \rfdomainres{V}{\Gamma^D}))_{V \in \metregions}$ such that the following hold.
\begin{enumerate}[I.]
 \item For each $k \in \N$ we have that $(\rformres{k}{\cdot}{\cdot}{\Gamma^D}, \rfdomainres{\Upsilon_k}{\Gamma^D})$ is a local, regular resistance form on $\Upsilon_k$. Its associated resistance metric $\rmetres{k}{\cdot}{\cdot}{\Gamma^D}$ is topologically equivalent to $\dpathY[\Upsilon_k]$.
 \item Let $V_1,\ldots,V_n \in \metregions[k]$, $n \in \N$, such that $V_i \cap V_j = \emptyset$ for $i \neq j$ and $\bigcup_i \ol{V_i} \cap \Upsilon_k = \Upsilon_k$. Then
 \begin{align*}
  \rfdomainres{\Upsilon_k}{\Gamma^D} &= \{ f : f|_{\ol{V_i} \cap \Upsilon_k} \in \rfdomainres{V_i}{\Gamma^D} \text{ for each } i \} ,\\
  \text{and}\quad
  \rformres{k}{f}{f}{\Gamma^D} &= \sum_i \rformres{V_i}{f|_{\ol{V_i} \cap \Upsilon_k}}{f|_{\ol{V_i} \cap \Upsilon_k}}{\Gamma^D} .
 \end{align*}
\item If $V,V' \in \metregions[k]$, $V \subseteq V'$, and $f\colon \ol{V'} \cap \Upsilon_k \to \R$ is a continuous function that is constant on each $\dpathY$-connected component of $\ol{V'} \cap \Upsilon_k \setminus \ol{V}$, then
\begin{align*}
 & f \in \rfdomainres{V'}{\Gamma^D} \text{ if and only if } f|_{\ol{V} \cap \Upsilon_k} \in \rfdomainres{V}{\Gamma^D} \\
 \text{and}\quad & \rformres{V'}{f}{f}{\Gamma^D} = \rformres{V}{f}{f}{\Gamma^D} .
\end{align*}
 \item For each open set $U \subseteq \C$, the collection of forms $(\rformres{V}{\cdot}{\cdot}{\Gamma^D})_{V \in \metregions[U]}$ is a.s.\ a measurable function of $\Gamma^D|_U$ that does not depend on the choice of $D$.
\item For each simply connected domain $D \subseteq \C$ and $z \in \C$, we have
\[ \rform{\cdot}{\cdot}{\Gamma^D} = \rform{T_{z}\cdot}{T_{z}\cdot}{\Gamma^D+z} \quad\text{a.s.,} \]
where $T_{z} f = f(\cdot -z)$ denotes translation by $z$.
\item There exists a constant $\resexp > 0$ so that the following holds. For each simply connected domain $D \subseteq \C$ and $\lambda > 0$, we have
\[ \rform{\cdot}{\cdot}{\Gamma^D} = \lambda^{\resexp}\rform{S_{\lambda}\cdot}{S_{\lambda}\cdot}{\lambda\Gamma^D} \quad\text{a.s.,} \]
where $S_{\lambda} f = f(\lambda^{-1}\cdot)$.
\end{enumerate}
The analogous statement holds for the \clekp{} Brownian motion. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Let (X,Sigma,mu) be a probability space (more generally a finite measure space) and T: X -> X a measurable, measure-preserving transformation (mu(T^{-1}A)=mu(A) for all A in Sigma). Then for every measurable A with mu(A)>0, mu-almost every x in A returns to A infinitely often: for a.e. x in A there are infinitely many n>=1 with T^n(x) in A.
(X,Sigma,mu) is a finite (e.g. probability) measure space
T is measurable and measure-preserving

Let N take values in {0, 1, ..., m} on a probability space, mu = E[N] > 0 and beta = E[binom(N, 2)] = E[N(N-1)/2]; put x = 2 beta / mu and r = 1 + floor(x). Then 1 <= r <= m and P(N > 0) >= D := 2 mu/(r+1) - 2 beta/(r(r+1)); writing theta = x - (r - 1) in [0, 1), D = mu[(1 - theta)/r + theta/(r+1)]. This r maximizes the bound of the linear family over integers r >= 1: when x is a positive integer, r = x and r = x + 1 tie and r is the latter; when x = 0, r = 1 is the unique maximizer. Integer values are needed: for X = 3/2 surely, with beta read as E[X(X-1)/2], mu = 3/2, beta = 3/8, r = 1 and the formula gives 9/8 > 1 = P(X > 0).
N is integer valued with 0 <= N <= m
mu = E[N] > 0

Then the conclusions of Theorem (t:multcltmarkedpp of the paper) hold.

[Thm A. thm: convergence in hatC of arXiv:2412.08236, 'Aging and sub-aging for Bouchaud trap models on resistance metric spaces'] [{Convergence in $\widehat{C}_{c}(M, \Xi)$}]  
  Let $f, f_{1}, f_{2}, \ldots$ be elements of $\widehat{C}_{c}(M, \Xi)$.
  The following conditions are equivalent.
  \begin{enumerate} [label = (\roman*)]
    \item  
      The functions $f_{n}$ converge to $f$ in the compact-convergence topology with variable domains.
    \item 
        The sets $\dom(f_{n})$ converge to $\dom(f)$ in the Hausdorff topology in $M$,
        and there exist functions $g_{n}, g \in C(M, \Xi)$ such that $g_{n}|_{\dom(f_{n})} = f_{n}$, $g|_{\dom(f)} = f$
        and $g_{n} \to g$ in the compact-convergence topology.
    \item 
      The sets $\dom(f_{n})$ converge to $\dom(f)$ in the Hausdorff topology in $M$,
      and, for any $x_{n} \in \dom(f_{n})$ and $x \in \dom(f)$ with $x_{n} \to x$,
      it holds that $f_{n}(x_{n}) \to f(x)$.
  \end{enumerate}

[Definition of arXiv:2608.27904, 'Instantons, indefinite 4-manifolds, and Dehn surgery'] A \textit{stratified-smooth manifold} $(P,\Delta)$ (or simply $P$) of dimension $n$ is the following data: 
	\begin{itemize}
		\item a partially ordered set $\Delta$ equipped with a dimension function $d: \Delta \to \mathbb N$ with maximum value $n$, 
		\item a compact topological space $P$ equipped with a partition into locally-closed subsets $P_\sigma$ for $\sigma \in \Delta$, satisfying $\overline P_\sigma = \bigcup_{\tau \le \sigma} P_\tau$, 
		\item the structure on each stratum $P_\sigma$ of a smooth manifold of dimension $d(\sigma)$.
	\end{itemize}
	We demand that the following {\it locally standard} hypothesis holds: for each $p \in P_\sigma$, there exists an isomorphism of posets $\bar \phi: \Delta_{\ge \sigma} \cong \{0,1\}^k$ for some integer $k$. This isomorphism may be chosen so that for an appropriate neighborhood $p \in U \subset P$, there exists a homeomorphism $\phi: U \to [0,\infty)^k \times \mathbb R^{n-k}$ so that $\phi$ sends the stratum $P_\tau$ onto the stratum corresponding to $\bar \phi(\tau)$. Finally, we demand that $\phi$ is a diffeomorphism on each stratum.
	
	A \textit{stratified-smooth $SO(3)$-manifold} is a stratified-smooth manifold $P$ equipped with a continuous $SO(3)$-action, for which each $P_\sigma$ is $SO(3)$-invariant, and the action is smooth on each stratum.

	A \textit{diffeomorphism} of stratified-smooth manifolds $(\phi,\bar \phi): (P,\Delta)\to (P',\Delta')$  is the pair of an isomorphism of partially-ordered sets 
	$\bar \phi:\Delta \to \Delta'$ and a homeomorphism $\phi:P\to P'$ that restricts to a diffeomorphism from $P_\sigma$ to $P'_{\bar \phi(\sigma)}$ for each 
	$\sigma\in \Delta$.

[Lem 19 of arXiv:2605.05986, '\bf Convergence rate of the occupation measure of { classes of ergodic processes toward th'] Let $p>0$,  $\b\!\in (0, 1/2]$. Let $t>0$ be fixed and let $L: (0, +\infty)\to \R_+$ be defined by 
\[
L_t(u):=\sum_{\ell\ge 0} 2^{-p\ell} \min\Big(u^{\frac{1}{2\b}}, \big(u/t)^{\frac 12}2^{d\ell(1-\b)}\Big).
\]

The function $L$ satisfies the following upper-bounds depending on $p$, $\b$ and the dimension $d$ where $C_{p,\b,d}>0$ denotes    a positive constant only depending on $p$, $\b$, $d$ that may vary from line to line.
\begin{itemize}
\item If $p>d(1-\b)$, then 
\[
L_t(u) \le C_{p, \b,d} \min\Big( u^{\frac{1}{2\b}}, \Big( \frac{u}{t}\Big)^{\frac 12}\Big).
\]

\item  If $p=d(1-\b)$ then
	\begin{align}
	 L_t(u) &\le C_{p,\b,d}
	
	 \Big(u^{\frac{1}{2\b}} \mbox{\bf 1}_{\{u\,t^{\frac{\b}{1-\b}}  \le 1\}}+ \Big(\frac ut\big)^{\frac 12} \big(1+\log(u\,t^{\frac{\b}{1-\b}})\big) \mbox{\bf 1}_{\{ut^{\frac{\b}{1-\b}}  \ge 1\}}\Big)\\
		 & \le C_{p,\b,d}
	
	\Big(\frac ut\Big)^{\frac 12} \big(1+\big(\log(u\,t^{\frac{\b}{1-\b}})\big)^+\big) 
	\end{align}
	

\item If $p < d(1-\b)$, then
$$
L(u) \le C_{p,\b,d} u^{\frac{1}{2\b}}\min\Big( 1,\big(ut^{\frac{\b}{1-\b}}\big)^{-\frac{p}{2\b d}}\Big).
$$
\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: Load-bearing hypothesis: in ∂_t u + Σ_j A_j ∂_j u = 0 the estimate ‖u(t)‖_{L²} ≤ e^{Kt}‖u(0)‖_{L²} comes from the Hermitian symmetry of the A_j (which makes u* A_j ∂_j u an exact divergence up to lower order). Real eigenvalues alone (weak hyperbolicity) are not enough. Concrete counterexample in n = 1, m = 2: take A = [[0,1],[0,0]], a Jordan block whose only eigenvalue is 0 (real, so the system is weakly hyperbolic) but which is not symmetrizable. The system ∂_t u1 + ∂_x u2 = 0, ∂_t u2 = 0 with data (f,g) has the solution u2(t,x) = g(x), u1(t,x) = f(x) − t g'(x). So ‖u(t)‖_{L²} ≥ t‖g'‖_{L²} − ‖f‖_{L²}, which is not bounded by any function of t times ‖(f,g)‖_{L²}: one derivative is lost per unit time, and the Cauchy problem is ill-posed in L² (and in every H^s). Consequences for auditing: (i) hyperbolicity claims must say symmetric, symmetrizable or strictly hyperbolic, never merely 'real eigenvalues'; (ii) the constant K in the energy estimate depends on sup|Σ_j ∂_j A_j| and sup|B|, so the argument needs the coefficients to be differentiable in x with bounded derivative — Lipschitz in x is enough (the derivative then exists a.e. and is bounded), but mere continuity is not, and for merely continuous, non-Lipschitz coefficients well-posedness can genuinely fail with a loss of derivatives; (iii) after an approximate symmetrization, the estimate holds with the symmetrizer's constants, not with 1.

$\Omega$, and let $\Psi:\Delta(\Omega)\to\R$ be concave. Suppose that
$U$--$Y$--$Z$ is a Markov chain; equivalently, $U$ and $Z$ are conditionally
independent given $Y$. Then
\[
  \mathsf I_\Psi(U;Y)
  \geq \mathsf I_\Psi(U;Z)
  \geq 0.
\]

[Theorem 5 (Subcritical rigidity) of arXiv:2609.03339, 'Exterior Serrin Rigidity for the Homogeneous \texorpdfstring{$k$}{k}-Hessian Equation\\'] Let $2\le k<\frac{n}{2}$ and let $\Omega\Subset\R^n$ be smooth,
		bounded, strictly star-shaped, and strictly $(k-1)$-convex.  Suppose that
		$u\in C^{1,1}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\overline E)$ is a k-admissible solution of
		\begin{equation}
		  \begin{cases}
		  		\sigma_k(D^2u)=0&\text{in }~\R^n\setminus\overline\Omega,\\
		  	u=-1& \text{on}~\partial\Omega,\\
		  	u(x)\to0\ &\text{as }|x|\to\infty.
		  \end{cases}
		\end{equation}	
	
	
	
	
	
		If $|Du|=c>0$ on $\partial\Omega$, then for some $x_0\in\R^n$,
		\[
		\Omega=B_R(x_0),\qquad
		R=\frac{n-2k}{kc},\qquad
		u(x)=-\left(\frac{R}{|x-x_0|}\right)^{\frac{n-2k}{k}}.
		\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Subcritical rigidity

[Prop intro of arXiv:2509.08659, 'Gap metrics for stationary point processes and quantitative convexity of the free energy'] Let $1<p<2$ and $\varphi(x)=|x|^{-s}$. Then, $(X^a_p,\mathscr W_{gap,p})$ is a complete geodesic metric space. The free energy $\mathcal F_\beta$ is weakly $\lambda$-geodesically convex on $(X^a_p,\mathscr W_{gap,p})$ with $\lambda=\beta a^{-\frac{2-p}{p}}>0$, i.e.\ for $\mathsf{P}_0,\mathsf{P}_1\in X^a_p$ there is a constant speed geodesic $(\mathsf{P}_t)_{t\in[0,1]}$ such that for any $0\leq t \leq 1$
    \begin{align*}
        \mathcal F_\beta(\mathsf{P}_t)\leq (1-t) \mathcal F_\beta(\mathsf{P}_0)+t \mathcal F_\beta(\mathsf{P}_1)-\lambda \frac{t(1-t)}{2} \mathscr W_p^2(\mathsf{P}_0,\mathsf{P}_1).
    \end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Prop intro of arXiv:2509.08659

[Definition 21 (Property~\ref{prop:mono}: Monotonicity) of arXiv:2603.28734, 'Free energy analyticity of the disordered XY model and Debye screening in the 2D Coulomb g'] Suppose that $S$ is a partially ordered set.
    Then we call a Glauber dynamic $R$ \emph{monotone} if for any $u\in V$ and $\iota\in\Sigma$,
    the map $R_{u,\iota}:S^V\to S^V$ preserves the partial order at the spin $u$.
    This means that
    $R_{u,\iota}(\alpha)_u\preceq R_{u,\iota}(\alpha')_u$ for any $\alpha,\alpha'\in S^V$ such that $\alpha_v\preceq\alpha'_v$ for all $v\in V$.
title: Property~\ref{prop:mono}: Monotonicity

[Theorem of arXiv:2508.12951, '\textbf{On the central limit question for strictly stationary, reversible Markov chains}'] {\rm (Merlev\`ede and Peligrad)}.    
\label {thm4.2}
Suppose $X := (X_k, k \in \mathbb Z)$ is a 
(not necessarily Markovian)
strictly stationary sequence of random variables such that
the following three conditions (a), (b), (c) hold: \hfil\break
(a) $P(|X_0| \leq C) = 1$ for some 
positive constant $C$, and $E[X_0] = 0$; \hfil\break 
(b) $\liminf_{n \to \infty} n^{-1} 
\textrm{\rm Var}(\, \sum_{k=1}^n X_k) > 0$; and \hfil\break
(c) $\alpha_X(n) = o(n^{-1})$ as $n \to \infty$. \hfil\break
Then letting $b_n := (\pi/2)^{1/2} E|\sum_{k=1}^nX_k|$
for each $n \in \mathbb N$, one has that 
$b_n \to \infty$ as $n \to \infty$, and   
$(1/b_n) \sum_{k=1}^n X_k$ converges in distribution to
$N(0,1)$ as $n \to \infty$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem thm:finiteness of arXiv:2607.04620, 'The Exact Ville Identity\\ \large From the Absorbing Case to the General Law\\ with an App'] Let $(Z_n)$ be any sequence of random variables such that $|Z_n|$ is a submartingale with respect to a suitable filtration, and let $T$ be any associated extended-valued stopping time. Then
\[
  \mathbb{E}|Z_T|\mathbf{1}(T<\infty)<\infty
  \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
  \lim_{n\to\infty}\mathbb{E}|Z_T|\mathbf{1}(n\le T<\infty)=0.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Defn Chordal link pattern of arXiv:2506.01306, 'Asymptotic of Coulomb gas integral, Temperley-Lieb type algebras and pure partition functi'] Given $\boldsymbol{x}=\{x_1,x_2,...,x_n\}$ on the real line, a link pattern is a homotopically equivalent class of non-intersecting curves connecting pair of boundary points (links) or connecting boundary points and the infinity (rays). The link patterns with $n$ boundary points and $m$ links are called $(n,m)$-links, denoted by ${\rm LP}(n,m)$.

The number of chordal $(n,m)$-links is given by $|{\rm LP}(n,m)|=C_{n}^{m+1}-C_{n}^{m}$.

[Corollary 15 (Second-order convergence of the locally reconstructed helical direction) of arXiv:2609.00673, '2609.00673'] Assume the hypotheses of Proposition~\ref{prop:smooth-consistency} and, in addition, that $\gamma$ is a smooth general helix on $J$. Orient its smooth helical direction $U$ so that $T\cdot U>0$, and write
\[
\rho=\frac{\kappa}{\tau},
\qquad
W=T+\rho B=\sec\alpha\,U,
\]
where $\rho$ is constant on $J$. For sufficiently small $h$, define the local binormal coefficient
\[
\widehat y_i^h
=
\frac{x_{i+1}^h+x_i^h\cos\phi_i^h}{\sin\phi_i^h}
\]
and the local reconstructed vector
\[
\widehat Q_i^h
=
T_i^h-x_i^hN_i^h+\widehat y_i^hB_i^h.
\]
Then, uniformly on compact cells contained in $J$,
\[
\widehat Q_i^h=W+O(h^2).
\]
Thus, with
\[
\widehat U_i^h=\frac{\widehat Q_i^h}{\|\widehat Q_i^h\|},
\qquad
\cos\widehat\alpha_i^h=\frac1{\|\widehat Q_i^h\|},
\]
one has
\[
\boxed{\ \|\widehat U_i^h-U\|=O(h^2),\qquad
\cos\widehat\alpha_i^h-\cos\alpha=O(h^2).\ }
\]
Moreover, the finite-step defect of Proposition~\ref{prop:smooth-consistency} satisfies $D_i^h=O(h^3)$ for a smooth general helix.

body: Theorem (campaign status: proved): (S14 (23)-(26).) Z_u = 1{L_u != 0}; after conditioning on the root sign A this is the occupancy indicator of u in the corresponding stable set. Match every u_j to the FIRST vertex m_j of its following gap; the matched vertices are distinct and lie outside U. Fix an activation pattern z contained in U: the d signs on U are fixed and every active u in z forces its matched neighbour to be unoccupied. Hence, FOR EVERY fixed root value and every additional ancestor boundary value w, |(A_n)_{W=w, Z=z}| <= 2^{n-d-|z|}. Incompatible patterns give an empty cell; exactly, on the full rooted cycle the cell count is the number of independent sets of C_n[V \ (U u N(z))]. Summing, |supp(B_1,...,B_n | W=w)| <= 2^n (3/4)^d. Notes: TARGET-UNIFORM is the operative strengthening over S12 (2): the bound holds for every boundary value w, not just on the root marginal. So (14) is not merely a selector basis but a target-uniform CONDITIONAL activation-cell certificate.

[Lemma 9 of arXiv:2605.28801, 'Microscopic Weak Selection Principle for the Logistic Branching Brownian Motion with selec'] Let $(\boldsymbol{X}^c(t))_{t\geq 0}$ denote the Log-BBM($1,c$) process. Given $\varepsilon_1 \sim$ Exp$(1)$, define the times 
	\[
	T_1 := \inf \{t\geq 0: N^c_t = 1\} \quad \text{ and } \quad
	T_2 := \inf \{ t \geq T_1 + \varepsilon_1: N_t^c = 1 \},
	\]
	which are the hitting time of one and the first return time to one of the process $N_t^c$, respectively. Set $T:=T_2 - T_1$, and we define 
	\begin{equation*}
		\gamma := \max\limits_{t \in [0,T]}\Big|\max\limits_{u \in \mathcal{N}^c_t} X^c_u(t) \Big|.
	\end{equation*}
	Then $\mathbb{E}_{(0)}(\gamma)<\infty$, where $\mathbb{E}_{(0)}$ denote expectation under the law of the process starting from one particle at position zero. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma 9 of arXiv:2605.28801

body: In mathematics, a Sobolev space is a vector space of functions equipped with a norm that is a combination of Lp-norms of the function together with its derivatives up to a given order. The derivatives are understood in a suitable weak sense to make the space complete, i.e. a Banach space. Intuitively, a Sobolev space is a space of functions possessing sufficiently many derivatives for some application domain, such as partial differential equations, and equipped with a norm that measures both the size and regularity of a function.
title: Sobolev space

Suppose F=E_p(mu,Sigma,Psi), with Sigma positive semidefinite, and Psi is a valid characteristic generator for a p x n matrix-variate elliptically contoured distribution as required by the source. Then F is n-completely mixable with constant sum n*mu. The matrix-generator extension is an explicit additional hypothesis; being an arbitrary p-dimensional elliptical law does not by itself verify it. Source: Chuancun Yin, Joint mixability of elliptical distributions and related families, arXiv:1706.05499, Theorem 4.1 p.14 and Corollary 4.1 p.15.
p>=1 and n>=2 integers
Sigma positive semidefinite
Psi extends as a valid generator to the required p x n matrix-variate elliptical family

body: In probability theory, Lindeberg's condition is a sufficient condition for the central limit theorem (CLT) to hold for a sequence of independent random variables. Unlike the classical CLT, which requires that the random variables in question have finite variance and be both independent and identically distributed, Lindeberg's CLT only requires that they have finite variance, satisfy Lindeberg's condition, and be independent. It is named after the Finnish mathematician Jarl Waldemar Lindeberg.
title: Lindeberg's condition

[Definition 15 ($(m,n)$-good) of arXiv:2506.09609, 'Schramm-Loewner evolution contains a topological Sierpi\'nski carpet when $\kappa$ is clos'] We define the \textbf{$(m,n)$-good} property for points in $V_n$ and integers $m \geq 0$. If a point is not $(m,n)$-good, we say that it is \textbf{$(m,n)$-bad}.
    The definition is given inductively on $m$. For $m = 0$ and $n \geq 0$, we say $x \in V_n$ is \textbf{$(0,n)$-good} if and only if $x$ is $n$-good.

    For $m \geq 1$, given the definition of $(j,n)$-good for $0 \leq j \leq m-1$, we define the $(m,n)$-good property for $x \in V_n$ as follows. Let $J_x$ be the set of points in $B(x,\epsilon^n) \cap V_{n+1}$ that are either $(m-1,n+1)$-bad or $(0, n+1)$-bad. Consider the collection of closed boxes $\{ \overline{B(w, \epsilon^{n+1})} \}_{w \in J_x}$ and the connected components formed by their union on $\mathbb{C}$, where two boxes that share exactly one point are also viewed as connected. We say that $x$ is \textbf{$(m,n)$-good} if all these components have $|\cdot|_\infty$-diameter at most $\frac{1}{4} \epsilon^n$.
title: $(m,n)$-good

PRIVATE OBSERVATION, author-recorded, used to reduce Heydenreich-van der Hofstad Open Problem 15.1. If random probability measures mu_n on R^d have r-point (moment) measures converging weakly to those of a random probability measure mu whose moment measures satisfy a Carleman-type determinacy condition (total masses of order r! K^r), then mu_n converges in distribution to mu: the law of a random probability measure is determined by its moment measures under such a condition, and tightness is automatic on the compact scaling window. Integrated super-Brownian excursion satisfies the condition. Consequently, for spread-out critical percolation in d > 6, Hara-Slade's convergence of the r-point functions conditioned on cluster size n (with the n^{-1/4} spatial scaling at fixed Fourier variable) implies the conditional-measure convergence to ISE asked in Open Problem 15.1, provided the r-point convergence gives weak convergence of the r-point measures (characteristic-function convergence at every bounded Fourier variable suffices). The nearest-neighbour case is not covered (no r-point expansion in d >= 11).
Random probability measures on R^d
Carleman-type moment determinacy of the limit (holds for ISE)
Hara-Slade r-point convergence, not re-verified here
title: For a moment-determinate limit such as ISE, convergence of all r-point functions of a random probability measure gives convergence in distribution of the measure

[Definition of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] A linear map $f:\mathbb R^N\to\mathbb R^N$ is called diagonalizable if there is a basis  $v_1,\ldots,v_N\in\mathbb R^N$ such that $f$ multiplies by $\lambda_i$ in the direction $v_i$:
$$f(v_i)=\lambda_iv_i$$
In terms of the writing $f(x)=Ax$, we say that the corresponding matrix $A\in M_N(\mathbb R)$ is diagonalizable, with eingenvectors $v_i$ and eigenvalues $\lambda_i$.
title: Unnumbered definition of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'

[Proposition 14 of arXiv:2609.02808, 'Minimizers of Laplace eigenvalues under a lower curvature bound'] For $(M,g)\in\Cc$, the following are equivalent.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] $\la_k(M,g)\ge\la_k(\Sph^2)$ for every $k\ge1$.
\item[(ii)] $\la_{\ell^2}(M,g)\ge\ell(\ell+1)$ for every $\ell\ge1$.
\end{enumerate}
Consequently the round sphere minimizes $f_k$ on $\Cc$ for every $k$ if and only if it
minimizes $f_{\ell^2}$ on $\Cc$ for every $\ell$.

[Thrm main result of arXiv:2607.27612, '\Large \bf Small value probabilities of additive and derivative martingales in supercritic'] (i) Let $\lambda \in (0, \sqrt{2\beta(m-1)}]$. Assume either Condition (cond1 of the paper) or Condition (cond2 of the paper) holds. Then
\[
\lim_{\varepsilon \to 0+} \varepsilon^{-\rho} \, \mathbb{P}\bigl( M_\infty(\lambda) \in (0, \varepsilon) \bigr) \quad \text{exists and lies in } (0, \infty),
\]
where
\[
\rho := \frac{1}{\lambda} \left( \sqrt{ \left( \frac{\lambda}{2} + \frac{\beta(m-1)}{\lambda} \right)^2 + 2\beta \bigl(1 - f'(q_c)\bigr) } - \left( \frac{\lambda}{2} + \frac{\beta(m-1)}{\lambda} \right) \right).
\]

(ii) Let $\lambda \in (0, \sqrt{2\alpha}]$. Assume Condition (cond2.5 of the paper) holds and either Condition (cond3 of the paper) or Condition (cond4 of the paper) holds. Then
\[
\lim_{\varepsilon \to 0+} \varepsilon^{-\rho^X} \, \mathbb{P}\bigl( M_\infty^X(\lambda) \in (0, \varepsilon) \bigr) \quad \text{exists and lies in } (0, \infty),
\]
where
\[
\rho^X := \frac{1}{\lambda} \left( \sqrt{ \left( \frac{\lambda}{2} + \frac{\alpha}{\lambda} \right)^2 + 2 \psi'(\lambda^*) } - \left( \frac{\lambda}{2} + \frac{\alpha}{\lambda} \right) \right).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Thrm main result of arXiv:2607.27612

[Defn 2 of arXiv:2605.25762, 'Brownian Convergence of Planar Domains and Stability of the Planar Skorokhod Embedding Pro'] Let $U$ be planar domain and let $(U_{n})_{n}$ be
a sequence of planar domains, all containing a common point, say the
origin. For each $n$, let $(Z^{[n]}_{t})_{t\geq0}$ be a planar Brownian
motion started at $0$ and denote by $\tau_{n}$ its exit time from
$U_{n}$. Similarly, let $(Z_{t})_{t\geq0}$ be a planar Brownian
motion started at $0$ and denote by $\tau$ its exit time from $U$.
We say that $(U_{n})_{n}$ converges to a domain $U$ in the \textbf{$p$-Brownian
sense} if there exists a coupling of the laws of $(Z^{[n]}_{\tau_{n}},\tau_{n})$
and $(Z_{\tau},\tau)$ on a common probability space such that 
\[
\mathscr{C}_{1}:\begin{alignedat}{1}\mathbf{E}\left(\big|Z^{[n]}_{\tau_{n}}-Z_{\tau}\big|^{p}\right) & \underset{n\to+\infty}{\longrightarrow}0\end{alignedat}
\]
and 
\[
\mathscr{C}_{2}:\begin{alignedat}{1}\mathbf{E}\left(\big|\tau_{n}-\tau\big|^{\frac{p}{2}}\right) & \underset{n\to+\infty}{\longrightarrow}0\end{alignedat}
.
\]

This definition captures the geometric proximity of the domains in
terms of Brownian trajectories. More discussion of the \emph{$p$-Brownian
convergence }is presented in the last section. The main result of
this work is\emph{ }
title: Definition 2 of arXiv:2605.25762

[Lemma 16 of arXiv:2607.02434, 'A Topological Formula for \\ Potts Lattice Gauge Theory Correlations'] Let $P$ be an $i$-dimensional percolation subcomplex of $\Lambda\subset \Z^d$ let $\sigma$ be an $i$-cell that is not contained in $P.$ If $q$ is prime, $i=1,$ or $i=d-1,$ then either
$$\beta_{i-1}\paren{P\cup \sigma}=\beta_{i-1}\paren{P}-1, \beta_i\paren{P\cup \sigma}=\beta_i\paren{P}, P\notin V_{\sigma}$$
or
$$\beta_{i-1}\paren{P\cup \sigma}=\beta_{i-1}\paren{P}, \beta_i\paren{P\cup \sigma},\beta_i\paren{P\cup \sigma}=\beta_i\paren{P}+1, P\in V_{\sigma}\,.$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem 8 (Absorption for convex hulls of walks: Combinatorial version) of arXiv:2608.16752, 'Absorption Probabilities for Random Convex Hulls: Distribution-Freeness via the Wall-Cross'] Let $d\geq 1$ and $n \ge d+1$.
Let $x_1,\dots, x_{n}\in \R^d$ be vectors such that   $X= (x_1\, |\, \dots\,| \, x_n)$  is regular. Then,
$$
|\mathcal M(X)| = 2\sum_{q\geq 0}
\stirlingb{n}{d-1-2q},
$$
where $\stirlingb{n}{k}$ are the $B$-Stirling numbers defined in Theorem~\ref{thm:1}.
In particular, $|\mathcal M(X)|$ is the same for all $X\in \R^{d\times n}\setminus \mathcal D$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Absorption for convex hulls of walks: Combinatorial version

[Theorem 28 (Wick formula) of arXiv:2604.05234, 'Quantitative propagation of chaos and universality for asymmetric Langevin spin glass dyna'] Fix $p, n \in \bbN$. Let $Y_1, \ldots, Y_p$ be independent standard Gaussian random variables and consider $X_1, \ldots, X_n \in \{Y_1, \ldots, Y_p\}$. Let $\scrP_2(n)$ denote the set of pairings of $n$ elements. Then we have
\[ \bbE[X_1 \cdots X_n] = \sum_{\pi \in \scrP_2(n)} \prod_{i = 1}^n \bbE[x_ix_{\pi_i}].\]
title: Wick formula

[Lem lm:connected of arXiv:2412.00610, 'Joint Poisson Convergence of Monochromatic Hyperedges in Multiplex Hypergraphs'] Fix $k \geq 1$ and suppose $S = (\bm e_1, \bm e_2, \ldots, \bm e_k)$ be a collection of hyperedges (not necessarily distinct) of size $r \geq 2$ such that the hypergraph formed the union of the edges in $S$ is connected and $|\bigcup_{j=1}^k \bm e_j| <  b r-b+1$, where $b$ is the number of distinct hyperedges in $S$. Then there exists an ordering (permutation) $\sigma: [k] \rightarrow [k] $ such that the following hold: 
\begin{itemize}
\item for every $i \in [2, k]$, $t_i(\sigma)  \geq 1$, and  

\item for some $i \in [2, k]$, $t_i(\sigma) \in [2, r-1] $, 
\end{itemize} 
where 
$$t_i(\sigma) = \left|\bm e_{\sigma(i)} \bigcap \left(\bigcup_{j = 1}^{i-1}\bm e_{\sigma(j)}\right) \right| , $$ 
for $i \in [2, r]$.
title: Lem lm:connected of arXiv:2412.00610

[Lemma 17 of arXiv:2606.23099, 'Path-dependent Affine Processes'] For each $n \in \N$, let $X^n$ be a weak solution of
    \begin{equation*}
        X^n(t) = X^n(0) + \int_0^t \overline{b}^n(s,X^n) \, ds + \int_0^t \overline{\sigma}^n(s,X^n) \, dW^n(s), \quad t\in[0,T],

    where $\overline{b}^n : [0,T] \times C([0,T],\R^d) \to \R^d $ and $\overline{\sigma}^n : [0,T] \times C([0,T],\R^d) \to \R^{d\times m}$ are continuous non-anticipative functionals satisfying the linear growth Assumption~\ref{LG-Condition} with a common constant $C_{LG}$.
    Suppose further that $\overline{b}^n \to \overline{b}$, $\overline{\sigma}^n \to \overline{\sigma}$,
    locally uniformly on $[0,T]\times C([0,T],\R^d)$, where $\overline{b}$ and $\overline{\sigma}$ are the lifted coefficients defined above, and that $X^n \Rightarrow X$ for some continuous process $X$.
    Then $X$ is a weak solution of \eqref{path_dependent_sde_existence}.

[Lem 6. lem: distance between original and trace of arXiv:2412.08236, 'Aging and sub-aging for Bouchaud trap models on resistance metric spaces'] Fix $(F, R, \rho, \nu) \in \mathbb{F}$.
  Assume that, for some $\lambda > 1$, $r>0$, and $\delta > 0$,
  \begin{equation}
    R(\rho, B_{R}(\rho, r)^{c}) \geq \lambda, 
    \quad 
    \nu(B_{R}(\rho, 1)) \geq \delta.
  \end{equation}
  Write $(X^{\nu}, (P^{\nu}_{x})_{x \in F})$ (resp.\  $(X^{\nu^{(r)}}, (P^{\nu^{(r)}}_{x})_{x \in F^{(r)}})$)
  for the process associated with $(F,\allowbreak R,\allowbreak \nu)$ (resp.\ $(F^{(r)},\allowbreak R^{(r)},\allowbreak \rho^{(r)})$).
  It then holds that, for any $T > 0$,
  \begin{equation}
    d_{P}^{D(\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}, F)}
    \bigl(
      P_{\rho}^{\nu}(X^{\nu} \in \cdot), P_{\rho}^{\nu^{(r)}}(X^{\nu^{(r)}} \in \cdot)
    \bigr)
    \leq 
    e^{-T} + \frac{4}{\lambda} + \frac{4T}{\delta(\lambda - 1)},
  \end{equation}
  where we recall that $d_{P}^{D(\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}, F)}$ is the Prohorov metric on $\mathcal{P}(D(\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}, F))$
  induced by the Skorohod metric $d_{J_{1}}$ on $D(\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}, F)$ defined as (equation 3. eq: dfn of J_1 metric of the paper).

body: In mathematics, and in particular linear algebra, the Moore–Penrose inverse $A^{+}$ of a matrix $A$, often called the pseudoinverse, is the most widely known generalization of the inverse matrix. It was independently described by E. H. Moore in 1920, Arne Bjerhammar in 1951, and Roger Penrose in 1955. Earlier, Erik Ivar Fredholm had introduced the concept of a pseudoinverse of integral operators in 1903. The terms pseudoinverse and generalized inverse are sometimes used as synonyms for the Moore–Penrose inverse of a matrix, but sometimes applied to other elements of algebraic structures which share some but not all properties expected for an inverse element.

body:
The Fejer kernel is K_N(t) = (1/(N+1)) sum_{n=0}^{N} D_n(t) = (1/(N+1)) ( sin((N+1)t/2) / sin(t/2) )^2 for t not a multiple of 2pi, with K_N(0) = N+1. It satisfies: (i) K_N(t) >= 0 for all t; (ii) (1/2pi) integral over [-pi,pi] of K_N = 1; (iii) for every delta in (0,pi), the supremum of K_N over delta <= |t| <= pi tends to 0 as N tends to infinity. These three properties are precisely the definition of a nonnegative approximate identity, and they are what drive Fejer's theorem. By contrast the Dirichlet kernel D_N has L^1 norms growing like log N and changes sign, which is why partial sums behave worse than Cesaro means.
Stated on the circle with the normalised measure dt/2pi.

[Proposition 27 of arXiv:2608.30549, '\vspace{-1cm}Maximally Spread Out Measures and Implications\\{} for Phase Transitions in A'] Let $(\SC,\metr)$ and $(\SC',\metr')$ be two non-empty quasi-metric spaces. 
 Let $\mu$ be a Borel probability measure on $\SC$ that satisfies the small-ball condition
 with parameter $s>0$ on $\SC$.
 Let $\Phi \colon \SC \to \SC'$ be a Borel-measurable map that satisfies
 the following sub-H{\"o}lder condition:
 there exist $c>0$ and $\beta>0$ such that
 \begin{equation}
     
     \metr'\bigl( \Phi(x_1), \Phi(x_2) \bigr) \ge c \cdot \metr( x_1,x_2)^{\beta} \quad \text{for all $x_1,x_2\in \SC$.}
 \end{equation}
 Then the measure $\Phi_{\#}\mu$ is a Borel probability measure on $\SC'$
 that satisfies the small-ball condition with parameter $\frac{s}{\beta}$ on $\SC'$.

body:
[Lemma 58 (Mixtures with a low-degree curve component) of arXiv:2608.27372, 'Universality and sharp thresholds for ellipsoid fitting'] For each $d$, let $V_d\subset\R^d$ be an affine algebraic curve whose
		irreducible complex projective closure has degree $D_d$, and suppose
		$V_d$ is not contained in any centered ellipsoid.  Let $\nu_{V,d}$ be a
		non-atomic probability measure supported on $V_d$, let $\nu_{0,d}$ be any
		probability measure on $\R^d$, and set
		$\mu_d=(1-p_d)\nu_{0,d}+p_d\nu_{V,d}$ for $0<p_d\le1$.  If
		$x_1,\ldots,x_n$ are iid from $\mu_d$, then
		\begin{equation}
			
			\Pp\left\{\begin{array}{c}
				\text{there exist }R\succ0\text{ and }\rho>0\text{ such that}\\[-1mm]
				x_i^\top R x_i=\rho\quad\text{for every }i\le n
			\end{array}\right\}
			\le \Pp\{\operatorname{Binomial}(n,p_d)\le 2D_d\}.
		\end{equation}
		Consequently, for every fixed $\delta\in(0,1)$,
		\begin{equation}
			
			2D_d\le(1-\delta)np_d
			\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
			\Pp\{\text{an exact fit exists}\}
			\le \exp\left(-\frac{\delta^2}{2}np_d\right).
		\end{equation}
		In particular, exact fitting fails with high probability whenever
		$np_d\to\infty$ and $D_d=o(np_d)$.  If
		$n/d^2\to\alpha\in(0,\infty)$ and $\liminf_d p_d>0$, this includes every
		$D_d=o(d^2)$; more generally, the same conclusion holds whenever
			\[
			\limsup_{d\to\infty}\frac{2D_d}{d^2}
			<\alpha\liminf_{d\to\infty}p_d.
			\]

body:
Setting: $N$ is a compact interval or the circle $S^1$, and $f: N \to N$ is a $C^2$ map. Write $\mathrm{Crit}(f) = \{x : Df(x) = 0\}$ for the critical set. A periodic point $p$ of period $k$ is hyperbolic repelling if $|Df^k(p)| > 1$.

Theorem (Mañé, 1985). Let $\Lambda \subset N$ be a compact set which is forward invariant ($f(\Lambda) \subset \Lambda$) and such that
  (i) $\Lambda$ contains no critical point of $f$, and
  (ii) every periodic point of $f$ lying in $\Lambda$ is hyperbolic repelling (so $\Lambda$ contains no attracting and no neutral / indifferent periodic point);
  (iii) if $N = S^1$, assume in addition that $f$ has at least one periodic point in $N$. (This excludes in particular every circle homeomorphism of irrational rotation number, for which the conclusion is false; the literature states the caveat as 'f is not a homeomorphism without periodic points', and the hypothesis given here is the safe, slightly stronger form. Interval maps always have a fixed point, so (iii) is automatic on an interval.)
Then $\Lambda$ is uniformly expanding (a hyperbolic repelling set): there exist constants $C > 0$ and $\lambda > 1$, depending only on $f$ and $\Lambda$, such that
  $|Df^n(x)| \ge C \lambda^n$ for every $x \in \Lambda$ and every $n \ge 0$.

Standard corollary (the form usually quoted as the uniform expansion criterion). Suppose every periodic orbit of $f$ is hyperbolic repelling (and, on the circle, $f$ has a periodic point). Let $U$ be any open neighbourhood of $\mathrm{Crit}(f)$ and let $\Lambda(U) = \{x \in N : f^n(x) \notin U \text{ for all } n \ge 0\}$ be the set of points whose forward orbit never enters $U$. Then $\Lambda(U)$ is compact, forward invariant, disjoint from the critical set, and hence uniformly expanding: $|Df^n(x)| \ge C_U \lambda_U^n$ on $\Lambda(U)$. In words: 'all periodic orbits repelling' forces uniform expansion on any piece of the phase space that stays a fixed distance away from the critical points. Consequently every point either accumulates on the critical set or is uniformly expanded.

Where it FAILS if a hypothesis is dropped. (a) Without (i) the conclusion is false trivially: $Df = 0$ at a critical point. (b) Without (ii): an attracting or neutral periodic point in $\Lambda$ has $|Df^{nk}(p)| \le 1$. Attracting periodic orbits may exist elsewhere in $N$; the theorem only asks that none lies in $\Lambda$. (c) Without (iii): an irrational rotation, or any $C^2$ circle diffeomorphism with irrational rotation number, has $\Lambda = S^1$, no critical points and no periodic points at all (so (ii) holds vacuously), yet the derivatives $|Df^n|$ do not grow exponentially (each $f^n$ is a diffeomorphism of a circle of length 1, so $\min_x |Df^n(x)| \le 1$ for all $n$). (d) Smoothness: the proof uses $C^2$ (bounded distortion of iterates away from critical points); do not quote it for maps that are merely $C^1$. (e) Only one-dimensional: this is a theorem about interval and circle maps; there is no analogue for higher-dimensional maps or for holomorphic maps without further hypotheses. Note also that the theorem does NOT assume non-flat critical points and does NOT need to assume the absence of wandering intervals: both are handled inside the proof, and in particular no wandering interval can lie in a set $\Lambda$ satisfying (i)-(iii).
N is a compact interval or the circle S^1 and f: N -> N is C^2 (not merely C^1)
Lambda is compact and forward invariant, f(Lambda) contained in Lambda
Lambda contains no critical point of f
every periodic point of f that lies in Lambda is hyperbolic repelling (no attracting or neutral periodic point in Lambda)
if N is the circle, f has at least one periodic point (excludes homeomorphisms of irrational rotation number, where the conclusion fails)

Let (X, d) be a nonempty complete metric space and let T from X to X be a contraction: there exists a constant q with 0 <= q < 1 such that d(T(x), T(y)) <= q d(x, y) for all x, y in X. Then T has exactly one fixed point x* in X (a point with T(x*) = x*). Moreover, for any starting point x_0 in X the iterates x_(n+1) = T(x_n) converge to x*, with the a priori error bound d(x_n, x*) <= q^n d(x_1, x_0) / (1 - q).

By induction d(x_(n+1), x_n) <= q^n d(x_1, x_0). For m > n, the triangle inequality and the geometric series give d(x_m, x_n) <= (q^n + q^(n+1) + ... + q^(m-1)) d(x_1, x_0) <= q^n d(x_1, x_0) / (1 - q), which tends to 0 as n grows; hence (x_n) is Cauchy and, by completeness, converges to some x* in X. A contraction is Lipschitz, hence continuous, so T(x*) = lim T(x_n) = lim x_(n+1) = x*, and x* is a fixed point. Uniqueness: if x and y are both fixed points then d(x, y) = d(T(x), T(y)) <= q d(x, y), and since q < 1 this forces d(x, y) = 0, that is, x = y. Letting m tend to infinity in the displayed bound for d(x_m, x_n) yields d(x*, x_n) <= q^n d(x_1, x_0) / (1 - q).","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:81845b66a64fd9e8baa9830788af1d24ccfa7255e76ef65a7c1032858629b23b","revision_digest":"sha256:626f847ce40a84768e019fa3cdadd10e8d0b827e51626996fee08499fcf8c844","source_id":"wikipedia:Banach_fixed-point_theorem","source_revision":"as-read-2026-08-02","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

body:
[Proposition prop:quadric of arXiv:2608.01253, 'The pseudo-quantum representation of \\finite reversible Markov chains'] The real and imaginary parts of $\Phi=x+iy\in\mathcal{Q}$ satisfy
$|x|^{2}-|y|^{2}=1$ and $x\cdot y=0$, so $\mathcal{Q}$ is the set of pairs $(x,y)$ with
$x$ on a sphere of radius $|x|\ge1$ and $y$ tangent to it. After rescaling,
$\mathcal{Q}$ is the tangent bundle $TS^{N-1}$. On this quadric the imaginary slice
$W_{i\theta}$ acts as a real rotation of the base sphere, and the real slice
$W_s$ acts as a boost along the fibres, growing $|x|$ and $|y|$ without bound
while preserving $|x|^{2}-|y|^{2}=1$.

body:
[Lemme 39 of arXiv:2604.00635, 'Large deviations of the periodic Toda chain'] Let  $\eta, \kappa, M_0, M_1, M_2,  M_3> 0$, and assume that  $\kappa < \frac{1}{2}$.
Fixing the notation $\mathbf{M}=(M_0,\dots, M_3)$, define the continuous and bounded function

$$f_{\kappa, \mathbf{M}}(x,y) \overset{\mathrm{def}}{=}

\max\Big\{   \ln_{M_0} |x - y| - \frac{\ell \kappa}{4M_1} V(x)  - \frac{\ell \kappa}{4M_1} V(y),

- M_{2} \Big\}  \, .$$

Next, given $\bs{\mf{r}} \, = \, (\eta, \kappa,\mathbf{M})$

define the functional $J_{\bs{\mf{r}}} : \mathcal{M}_1(\mathbb{R}) \longrightarrow \mathbb{R}$

\beqa

J_{\bs{\mf{r}}}[\mu]  &\overset{\mathrm{def}}{=} & \Int{\mathbb{R}}{}\ln_{M_1}\Big( 1+ \frac{2}{\ell}

\Int{\mathbb{R}}{} f_{\kappa, \mathbf{M}}(x,y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu (y)+ \eta \Big) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(x) \nonumber \\

 && \qquad + \Int{\mathbb{R}}{}\max\Big\{  -(1-\kappa) V(x)  + W(x),  - M_3\Big\} \,  \mathrm{d}\mu(x) \, .

\eeqa

Then $J_{\bs{\mf{r}}}$ is continuous with respect to the weak topology.

Let (X,d) be a compact metric space of diameter at most one, with covering numbers N(X,epsilon)<=epsilon^(-d_x) for 0<epsilon<=1, where d_x>0. Let P be a Borel probability measure, and W:X x X->[0,cmax] a measurable symmetric kernel with 0<cmin<=d_P(x)=integral W(x,y)dP(y) and cmax<=1. Assume there is ONE partition X=X_1 union ... union X_q into q>=1 measurable pieces such that |W(x,y)-W(xprime,y)|<=cLip d(x,xprime) for every y and every x,xprime in the same piece. Let x_1,...,x_n be independent samples from P, and fix 0<rho<=1/2. Define d_X(x)=n^(-1)sum_i W(x,x_i) and D_X(rho)=cmin^(-1)[cLip sqrt(d_x)+(cmax+cLip)sqrt(log(q/rho))]. For a universal sufficiently large C, n>=C D_X(rho)^2 implies P(inf_x d_X(x)>=cmin/2)>=1-rho. This is a common-partition restricted version of the source degree lemma; it is not a lower bound on the random Bernoulli graph degrees themselves.

[Lemma Nevanlinna of arXiv:2608.18320, 'Asymptotics for Beta-Splitting Trees via Homogeneous Fragmentations and Meromorphic Potent'] Let $f$ be a nonconstant complete Bernstein function which admits a
    meromorphic extension to $\mathbb C$. Then there exist $\gamma,\alpha\ge0$, a
    finite or infinite strictly increasing sequence
    \[
            0<b_1<b_2<\cdots,
    \]
    with $b_n\to\infty$ in the infinite case,
    and coefficients $B_n>0$ satisfying
    $\sum_n B_n/b_n^2<\infty$, such that
    \begin{equation}
            f(z)
            =
            \gamma+\alpha z
            +\sum_{n\ge1}B_n
            \left(
            \frac1{b_n}-\frac1{z+b_n}
            \right)
            =
            \gamma+\alpha z
            +\sum_{n\ge1}B_n
            \frac{z}{b_n(z+b_n)}.
    \end{equation}
    The series converges locally uniformly on
    $\mathbb C\setminus\{-b_n:n\ge1\}$. The poles of $f$ are real and simple. All zeros of $f$ are real and
    simple, and the zeros interlace with the poles.

[Lemma of arXiv:2609.00436, 'A counterexample to the stable forking conjecture'] Let $i \in I ( \mathbb  M) $ and $j \in J( \mathbb  M)$. Let $U_i:= \operatorname{span}_{Q_{\Gamma( \mathbb  M) }} ( u_i , t_i )$ and $W_j = \operatorname{span}_{Q_{\Gamma( \mathbb  M) }} ( w_j , z_j )$. When $\neg E(i,j)$ holds, $U_i \cap W_j = \{ 0 \}$. When $E(i,j)$ holds, we have that $U_i \cap W_j = \operatorname{span}_{Q_{\Gamma( \mathbb  M) }} ( u_i + X_jt_i ).$ 

    It follows that if one takes $\alpha_i = ( u_i , t_i )$ and $\beta _j = ( w_j , z_j )$ then $\alpha_ i \mathop{\mathpalette\setbox0=\hbox{$x$}\kern\wd0\hbox to 0pt{\hss$\mid$\hss} \lower.9\ht0\hbox to 0pt{\hss$\smile$\hss}\kern\wd0{}} \beta _j $ if and only if $\neg E(i,j)$.

ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Explicit model calculation or source-specific limiting obstruction Result: In a location-family submodel Y=m(X)+Z with known noise law and a reference matching Z, the conditional transport map is T_x(u)=m(x)+u. Thus estimating the map under integrated squared error is at least as hard as estimating the regression function m: the map difference is exactly the shift-estimation error for every reference point u. Check: Integrating |T_hat_x(u)-T_x(u)|^2 in the shift submodel over a unit-mass reference measure gives |m_hat(x)-m(x)|^2. For an arbitrary map estimator, averaging T_hat_x(u)-u over the reference law produces an estimator of m(x), whose squared error is bounded by the map loss by Jensen. Thus a uniformly faster map estimator would imply an equally faster regression estimator on that submodel. Obstruction: This reduction supplies a lower-bound route but no sharp rate for the general conditional map. One must combine covariate localization with the response-dimensional transport difficulty and prove a matching estimator under precisely specified regularity assumptions.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-p0338-minimax-rates-for-conditional-optimal-transport-maps
No independent review

body:
[Conj 93 of arXiv:2509.01797, 'Relation between Wick powers and excursion clusters of the 2D GFF'] Fix $c\in (0,1)$.
The hypothetical fractional powers $:\fld_{c} \Theta_{\LL^{c}_{D}}^{n-1}:$ admit restriction to clusters of 
$\LL^{c}_{D}$.
That is to say, given a cluster $\clus$ of $\LL^{c}_{D}$, the field
\begin{displaymath}
\ind_{d(z,\clus)<\delta}\, :\fld_{c} \Theta_{\LL^{c}_{D}}^{n-1}:
\end{displaymath}
converges as $\delta\to 0$, in an appropriate sense (conditional $L^2$), towards a well defined generalized function
supported of $\overline{\clus}$,
which we will denote by $:\fld_{c} \Theta_{\LL^{c}_{D}}^{n-1}:_{\vert \overline{\clus}}$.
By contrast, the renormalized intersection local times $:\Theta_{\LL^{c}_{D}}^{n}:$
do not admit restrictions to clusters.
More precisely the integral
\begin{displaymath}
\int_{d(z,\clus)<\delta}:\Theta_{\LL^{c}_{D}}^{n}:
\end{displaymath}
converges in probability,
as $\delta\to 0$, to $\sigma(\clus)(-1)^{n-1}\infty$.

The $\varepsilon$-neighborhood of a cluster $\clus$ of $\LL^{c}_{D}$,
both for the Euclidean distance and conformal radius,
admits an asymptotic expansion in the $L^2$ sense, as $\varepsilon\to 0$,
into the powers $(\vert \log\varepsilon\vert^{-(n-c/2)})_{n\geq 1}$
of $\vert \log\varepsilon\vert$.
The coefficient of $\vert \log\varepsilon\vert^{-(n-c/2)}$
is a linear combination of fields
$\sigma(\clus):\fld_{c} \Theta_{\LL^{c}_{D}}^{k-1}:_{\vert \overline{\clus}}$
for $k\in\{1,\dots, n\}$.
By contrast, the renormalized intersection local times $:\Theta_{\LL^{c}_{D}}^{n}:$
do not appear in the expansion.
The expansion for the Euclidean distance and that for the conformal radius are related
through the expectations
\begin{displaymath}
\hat{\mu}^{\rm loop}_{\text{SLE}_{\kappa}}
\Big(
\log\Big(
\dfrac{\CR(0,\inter(\Gamma))}{d(0,\Gamma)}
\Big)^{k}
\Big)
\end{displaymath}
w.r.t. the MKS measure $\hat{\mu}^{\rm loop}_{\text{SLE}_{\kappa}}$,
where $\kappa$ and $c$ are related by \eqref{Eq rel kappa c}. (Stated as a conjecture by the paper; open unless the paper says otherwise.)
title: Conjecture 93 of arXiv:2509.01797

body:
[Thm matsutomo_yor of arXiv:2412.06701, 'Matsumoto-Yor processes on Jordan algebras'] The process $Z=(Z_t \ ; \ t\ge 0)$ defined by
$$Z_t := \exp( b_t^{(\nu)} )\int_{0}^{t} \exp\left( -2 b_s^{(\nu)} \right) ds \ , \ t\ge 0,$$
is a Markov process, whose natural filtration is strictly contained in that of $b$, i.e. for all $t > 0$, ${\mathcal F}_t^Z \varsubsetneq {\mathcal F}_t^b$.

Furthermore, we have the conditional distribution
$$
   {\mathbb P}\left( \exp\left( b^{(\nu)} \right) \in dx \ | \ {\mathcal F}_t^Z, \ Z_t = z \right) 
   = \mathrm{GIG}_{{\mathbb R}_+^*}\left( \nu ; \frac1z , \frac1z \right)(dx) \ .
$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Matsumoto--Yor \cite{matsumoto2000analogue}

[Corollary 5 (The Functional Sine-Santal\'o inequality) of arXiv:2609.01460, 'On cost-induced Santal\'o-type inequalities \\ in Polish measure spaces'] Let $n \geq 2$. For any non-negative measurable functions $f, g: \R^n \to \R_+$ and any non-increasing measurable function $\Omega: (0, \infty) \to (0, \infty)$ satisfying the pointwise bound:
    $$f(x)g(y) \leq \Omega^2([x,y]) \quad \text{for all } x, y \in \R^n \text{ with } [x,y] > 0,$$
one has the inequality:
    $$\left(\int_{\R^n} f(x) dx \right) \left(\int_{\R^n} g(y) dy \right) \leq \left(\int_{\R^n} \Omega(|z|^2) dz \right)^2.$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: The Functional Sine-Santal\'o inequality

[Lem 25 of arXiv:2608.05185, '\large\bf ON THE HEAT FLOW CONJECTURE FOR RANDOM MATRICES'] Let \(N\geq1\), let \(\mathbf{A}\) be a fixed \(N\times N\) complex
matrix, and regard \(z\) and the entries \(Z_{ij}\) of \(\mathbf{Z}\) as
algebraically independent variables.  For
\[
 P(z,\mathbf{Z})
 =\det\!\left(z\mathbf{I}_N-\mathbf{A}-\mathbf{Z}\right),
\]
one has the following identity in the polynomial ring
\(\C[z,(Z_{ij})_{1\leq i,j\leq N}]\):
\begin{equation}
 \sum_{i,j=1}^{N}
 \frac{\partial^2P}{\partial Z_{ij}\partial Z_{ji}}
 =-\partial_z^2P.
\end{equation}
All derivatives are formal polynomial derivatives.

[Lemma 5 (\cite{VER2020}) of arXiv:2607.21392, 'Gaussian Convexity Principles for Sharp Moderate Deviations of Gaussian Maxima and Critica'] For every $u\ge 0$,
\[
\mathbb P\bigl(|\max_{1\le i\le N}X_i-m_N|\ge u\bigr)\le 2e^{-u^2/2}.
\]
Consequently,
\begin{equation}
    | \E \max_{1\le i\le N} X_i-m_N|
\le \E|\max_{1\le i\le N}X_i-m_N|
\le \int_0^\infty 2e^{-u^2/2}\,du
=\sqrt{2\pi}=C_{\mathrm{med}}.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: \cite{VER2020}

[Cor 10 of arXiv:2606.24584, '2606.24584'] If $m \geq 1$ and $X\in\Omega_n$, then
\[
X^m=J_n
\]
if and only if  $X=J_n+N\geq 0$ (entrywise), where $N$ is a matrix whose rows and columns sum to 0 and for which $N^m=0$.

body:
[Definition 28 of arXiv:2604.01978, 'Homogenized Transformers'] Let $B\in C^{1}((\S^{d-1})^{n};\mathsf{T}(\S^{d-1})^{n})$ and
$G:(\S^{d-1})^n\times\Uptheta\to \mathsf{T}(\S^{d-1})^n$ be such that for ${\uprho_*}$-a.e.\ $\theta$,
the map $X\mapsto G(X,\theta)$ is $C^2$.
A continuous $(\S^{d-1})^{n}$-valued adapted process $(X(t))_{t\ge 0}$ with $X(0)=x$ is called a solution to the Itô SDE 
    \begin{equation} 
        \de X(t)=B(X(t))\de t+\int_{\Uptheta}G(X(t),\bm{\theta})\mathsf{W}(\de \bm{\theta},\de t),
    \end{equation}
if for all $g\in C^{\infty}((\S^{d-1})^{n})$, we have
\begin{align*}
g(X(t))
= g(x)
&+ \int_{0}^{t} (Bg)(X(s))\,\de s \\
&+ \frac{1}{2}\int_{0}^{t}\int_{\Uptheta} \Hess g(X(s))[G(X(s),\theta), G(X(s),\theta)]\,{\uprho_*}(\de \theta)\,\de s \\
&+ \int_{0}^{t}\int_{\Uptheta} (G(\cdot,\theta)g)(X(s))\,\mathsf{W}(\de \theta,\de s),
\end{align*}
where $Bg=\langle \grad g,B\rangle$, $G(\cdot,\theta)g=\langle \grad g, G(\cdot,\theta)\rangle$.
title: Definition 28 of arXiv:2604.01978

Let (X, mu) be a measure space and 0 < p < infinity. Let (f_n) be a sequence in L^p(mu) that is bounded in L^p norm and converges mu-almost everywhere to a function f. Then f is in L^p and lim_n ( ||f_n||_p^p - ||f_n - f||_p^p ) = ||f||_p^p. Equivalently the L^p norm splits asymptotically into the norm of the limit plus the norm of the vanishing part - a refinement of Fatou's lemma, which alone gives only ||f||_p <= liminf ||f_n||_p.
Uniform L^p boundedness AND almost-everywhere convergence.
Without the norm bound the conclusion fails;
no convergence in norm is assumed or concluded.

body: [Proposition 12 of arXiv:2608.13358, 'Extreme points of sets of probability measures and $\phi$-divergences'] Let $(\Omega_i,\cF_i,p_i)_{i=1,\ldots, n}$ be a family of probability spaces,  $\cM:=\Pi(p_1,\ldots,p_n)$ be the set of multi-marginal couplings of $p_1,\ldots,p_n$, and $p\in\cM$ be concentrated on a marginal uniqueness set $S\in\cF$.\ Then $p$ is $\ll$-minimal in $\cM$.\ In particular, $p$ is an extreme point of $\cM$, and the blow-up \eqref{eq:blowup} of Theorem~\ref{thm:minimal:divergence} holds for every $p'\in\cM\setminus\{p\}$, every $q\in\cM$ with $p,p'\ll q$, and every convex function $\varphi$ satisfying \eqref{eq:phi:blowup}.

body:
[Theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] The ``normal'' law $g_t$, having as Fourier transform 
$$F(x)=e^{-tx^2/2}$$
must have all odd moments zero, and its even moments must be the numbers
$$M_k(g_t)=t^{k/2}\times k!!$$
where $k!!=(k-1)(k-3)(k-5)\ldots\,$, as usual.

[Lem 11 of arXiv:2606.18877, 'Ergodic Properties of Non-Linear Density-Dependent Perturbations of the Ornstein--Uhlenbec'] Let \(Q:=J\times O\) be a bounded cylinder in \(\R_+\times\R^d\), where \(J\subset\mathbb R_+\) is a bounded open interval
and \(O\subset\mathbb R^d\) is a ball. Suppose that
\[
u_t-\Delta u=\operatorname{div}G+H
\]
in \(Q\) in the sense of distributions, with \(G\in C^{\beta/2,\beta}(Q)\) for some \(\beta\in(0,1)\) and \(H\in L^\infty(Q)\). 
Then the gradient of \(u\) exists in a classical sense and satisfies
\[
\nabla_x u\in C^{\beta/2,\beta}_{\mathrm{loc}}(Q).
\]

[Lem paley-zygmund of arXiv:2607.05097, 'Asymptotics of Lyapunov Exponents and Phase Transitions for Fluids with Degenerate Forcing'] Given $K \in \mathbb{N}_0$ and a sequence of elements $g_k \in \mathcal{H}^{\otimes_s k}$, let
    $X = \sum_{k=0}^K \tilde I_k(g_k)$.

    $$\mathbb{P}\Big(|X| > \Big[\frac{K!}{2}\Big]^{1/2}\delta\Big) \geq \frac{3^{-2K}}{4} \,.$$

body:
ONE VARIABLE. Let $a, b: (t_0, t_1) \to \mathbb{R}$ be $C^1$ and let $F(x, t)$ and $\partial_t F(x, t)$ be continuous on an open set of $\mathbb{R}^2$ containing $\{(x,t) : t \in (t_0,t_1),\ x \text{ between } a(t) \text{ and } b(t)\}$. Then for $t \in (t_0, t_1)$
$$\frac{d}{dt} \int_{a(t)}^{b(t)} F(x,t)\,dx = \int_{a(t)}^{b(t)} \partial_t F(x,t)\,dx + F(b(t),t)\, b'(t) - F(a(t),t)\, a'(t).$$

SEVERAL VARIABLES. Let $v(x,t)$ be a $C^1$ velocity field on an open set $U \subset \mathbb{R}^n$, $t \in (t_0, t_1)$, with flow $\varphi_t$ (so $\partial_t \varphi_t(y) = v(\varphi_t(y), t)$, $\varphi_{0} = \mathrm{id}$), and let $\Omega(t) = \varphi_t(\Omega_0)$ where $\Omega_0$ is a bounded open set with Lipschitz (e.g. piecewise $C^1$) boundary whose closure stays in $U$. Let $F(x,t)$ be $C^1$ on $U \times (t_0, t_1)$. Then
$$\frac{d}{dt} \int_{\Omega(t)} F\,dx = \int_{\Omega(t)} \partial_t F\,dx + \int_{\partial \Omega(t)} F\,(v \cdot \nu)\,dS = \int_{\Omega(t)} \big(\partial_t F + \nabla\cdot(F v)\big)\,dx,$$
where $\nu$ is the outward unit normal and $v \cdot \nu$ is the outward normal velocity of the boundary. Only the NORMAL component of the boundary velocity enters: two motions of the domain whose boundaries sweep the same sets (differing by a tangential reparametrisation) give the same derivative, so the formula can be stated with any $C^1$ boundary velocity having the correct normal component. The one-variable formula is the case $n = 1$, $\nu = \pm 1$ at $b$ and $a$.

WHERE IT FAILS OR NEEDS CARE. (1) $F$ must be continuous up to the moving boundary from inside; if $F$ jumps across $\partial\Omega(t)$ the boundary integrand is the one-sided limit from inside $\Omega(t)$. (2) $\partial_t F$ must be integrable over $\Omega(t)$ (continuity on a compact closure suffices); without domination, differentiation under the integral sign can fail. (3) The bounded-domain / Lipschitz-boundary hypothesis is what licenses the divergence theorem in the second equality; the first equality (Lagrangian form) needs only the change of variables. (4) If the domain is not transported by a $C^1$ flow but its boundary merely moves with a prescribed normal speed $w$, the same formula holds with $v \cdot \nu$ replaced by $w$, but the proof must build a flow with that normal speed.
F and its time derivative are continuous (F is C^1) on a neighbourhood of the closures of the moving domains
the domain is transported by a C^1 velocity field (one variable: the endpoints are C^1 functions of t)
the domain is bounded with Lipschitz boundary so that the divergence theorem applies
only the outward normal component of the boundary velocity enters the boundary term

Let G be a finite undirected loopless multigraph on n vertices with positive edge weights w_e, L its weighted Laplacian, and t > 0. A spanning rooted forest is a spanning forest with one chosen root in each tree; its weight is t^|E(F)| prod_{e in F} w_e (so an unrooted forest with trees T_1, ..., T_k counts prod |T_i| times). Z(t) is the total weight of spanning rooted forests, and Q_t = (I + tL)^-1. As t -> infinity, Q_t converges to the orthogonal projector onto ker L, which equals sum over the connected components C of G of 1_C 1_C^T / |C|.

body:
For a finite undirected graph with labeled terminal vertices and a random open-edge configuration, its terminal partition puts two terminals in the same block exactly when an open path joins them inside the graph. The boundary-partition law is the probability distribution on these terminal partitions. When the graph attaches to an exterior only through those terminals, ordinary open-path connectivity in the union is determined by this partition and the exterior connectivity.
The gadget meets the exterior only at the named terminal vertices.
Connectivity uses open paths.
title: Boundary partition law of a finite percolation gadget

Let A,Phi be real symmetric n-by-n matrices with Phi positive semidefinite. Fix z with Im(z)>0,nonzero alpha with Im(alpha)<=0,and gamma>0. For s in the open upper half-plane let S(s)=(A+s^(-1)*Phi-zI)^(-1),f_n(s)=alpha^(-1)+gamma*tr(S(s)Phi),and tr=Tr/n. Then Im f_n(s)>=gamma*Im(z)*tr(S Phi S*)>=0. More precisely,Im f_n(s)=Im(alpha^(-1))+gamma*Im(s)/|s|^2*tr(S Phi S* Phi)+gamma*Im(z)*tr(S Phi S*). For s1,s2 in the upper half-plane,write S_j=S(s_j) and d_j=(Im f_n(s_j)-gamma*Im(z)*tr(S_j Phi S_j*))/Im(s_j)>=0. Then |f_n(s1)-f_n(s2)|<=|s1-s2|*sqrt(d_1*d_2). These are normalized-trace identities and inequalities for finite matrices;no simultaneous diagonalization of A and Phi is assumed. Draft,independent review pending.

body: The continuous (topological) dual X* of a normed space X is the space of bounded linear functionals f : X -> scalars, itself a Banach space under the operator norm ||f|| = sup_{||x||<=1} |f(x)|. The Hahn-Banach theorem guarantees X* is rich (functionals extend and separate points); the natural map X -> X** is an isometric embedding, and X is reflexive when it is onto.
title: Dual Space

For \(\alpha>0\), a real random variable \(\xi\) has Weibull tails of index \(\alpha\) if there is \(c_\xi\in(0,\infty)\) such that
\[
 \lim_{t\to\infty}t^{-\alpha}\log\mathbb P(\abs\xi>t)=-c_\xi.
\]

body:
[Proposition 13 (\cref{sec:end-analysis}) of arXiv:2608.31008, 'Stability of gravitational instantons with a bounded Killing vector field'] Let $(M^4,g)$ be a complete Ricci-flat ALF manifold satisfying
\eqref{eq:intro-end}, and let $K$ be a nonzero bounded Killing field.
After multiplying $K$ by a nonzero constant, for every
$0<\varepsilon<\frac12$ one has, on the end,
\[
 |\nabla_b^j(K-T)|_b+|\nabla_b^j(V-1)|_b
   =\mathcal O(r^{-1-j}),\qquad \text{ and }\qquad
 |\nabla_b^jF|_b=\mathcal O(r^{-2-j}),\qquad \text{for }j\geqslant0.
\]
There are global functions $u$ and $\chi$ respectively satisfying 
 $\Delta u=V+2$ and $d\chi=\iota_K(*F)$ and for every $j\geqslant0$,
\[
 |\nabla_b^j(u+r^2/2)|_b=\mathcal O(r^{1+\varepsilon-j}),
 \qquad
 |\nabla_b^j\chi|_b=\mathcal O(r^{-1+\varepsilon-j}).
\]
The symmetric $2$-tensor
 $k_K=\nabla^2u-\kappa\otimes\kappa+\frac{V+1}{2}g$ satisfies
 $$|\nabla^jk_K|=\mathcal O(r^{-1+\varepsilon-j})\qquad \text{ for }0\leqslant j\leqslant2.$$ In particular, all of the integrals used below converge: for $M_R=\{r<R\}$, we have as $R\to+\infty$
\begin{equation}
\begin{split}
 &\int_{\partial M_R}|k_K|\,|\nabla k_K|\,dA\longrightarrow0,\\
 &\int_{\partial M_R}
   |(F^+\circ F^-)(\nabla u,\nu)|\,dA\longrightarrow0,\\
 &\int_{\partial M_R}|1-V\pm\chi|\,
   |\partial_\nu(V\pm\chi)|\,dA\longrightarrow0.
\end{split}
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Thm 1 of arXiv:2605.07369, '2605.07369'] {\bf (Exponential inequality)}
Let $(X_n)_{n\ge 0}$ be a stochastic process taking values in $\rr$ and satisfying the stochastic approximation algorithm  (\ref{sa-0}). Assume that the conditions (\ref{sa-2}) and (\ref{g}) hold.
Then, for any $\varepsilon>0$, there exist a constant $\delta\in (0,1)$ such that, for all sufficiently large $n$, we have
$$
\pp\left(\left|X_{n+1}-x^*\right|\ge \varepsilon\right)\le 2 \exp\left(- \frac{C \varepsilon^2\delta n}{1-\delta}\right)\left(1+\frac{1}{1-\exp\left(- \frac{C \varepsilon^2  }{1-\delta}\right)}\right).
$$
Here $\delta$ can be chosen to satisfy
$$
0<\delta<\exp\left(-\frac{2(F+\varepsilon)}{b K_1 \varepsilon}\right),
$$
where $F=F\left(b, K_1, K_u\right)$ is a positive constant. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 23 of arXiv:2605.05864, 'Classification and Metrization of Classes of Smooth measures'] Let $\mu_n, \mu$ be Radon measures on $E$. If $\mu_n$ converges vaguely to $\mu$, then the inequality
\[\int_E f \,d\mu \leq \varliminf_n \int_E f \,d\mu_n\]
        holds for any non-negative lower semi-continuous function $f$ on $E$.

[Theorem thm:main-critical-level-percolation of arXiv:2609.02829, 'Quantitative explosion and percolation of the divisible sandpile'] Let $d\geq2$ and let $\nu_{0}>0$, $\theta_{0}>0$, and $K_{0}<\infty$. There are $c=c(d,\nu_{0},\theta_{0},K_{0})>0$ and $t_0=t_0(d,\nu_{0},\theta_{0},K_{0})<\infty$ such that the following holds. Suppose $(\sigma(x))_{x\in\mathbb{Z}^d}$ is an i.i.d.\ field with mean $\mathbb{E}\sigma(0)=1$, $\Var(\sigma(0))\geq\nu_{0}^2$, and $\mathbb{E} e^{\theta_{0}|\sigma(0)-1|}\leq K_{0}$. Then, for every integer $t\geq t_0$, the level set
\[
    \{x\in\mathbb{Z}^d:u_t(x)>c \, h(t)\}\, ,
    \qquad\text{where}\quad
    h(t)=
    \begin{cases}
    t^{(4-d)/4} & \text{if } d\in\{2,3\}\, ,\\
    \log t & \text{if } d=4\, ,\\
    (\log t)^{2/d} & \text{if } d\geq5\, ,
    \end{cases}
\]
contains an infinite nearest-neighbor component almost surely.

body:
[Corollary cor:augment_stable of arXiv:2411.03609, 'Asymptotically optimal Wasserstein couplings for the small-time stable domain of attractio'] Assume that $\bm{X}$ is an augmented $\alpha$-stable process and $\bm{Z}$ is an $\alpha$-stable process with $\alpha\in(0,2)\setminus\{1\}$ and fix any $q\in(0,1]\cap(0,\alpha)$ with $\mathds{E}[|\bm{X}_1|^q]<\infty$.
\begin{description}[leftmargin=0em, nosep]
\item[(a)]

Assume $|\mathcal{Q}(x,\bm{v})-c_\alpha| \leqslant K(1\wedge x)$ for  some $K>0$ and all $x>0$, $\bm{v}\in \mathbb{S}^{d-1}$. Then, for $\bm{X}^t\coloneqq(\bm{X}_{st}/t^{1/\alpha})_{s\in[0,1]}$,  
\begin{equation*}
c_1 t^{1-q/\alpha}
\leqslant\mathcal{W}_q\big(\bm{X}^t_1,\bm{Z}_1\big)
\leqslant\mathcal{W}_q\big(\bm{X}^t,\bm{Z}\big)\leqslant
c_2\big(t^{1-q/\alpha}\1_{\{\alpha<1\}} + t^{q(1-1/\alpha)}\1_{\{\alpha>1\}}\big),
\end{equation*}
for some $c_1,c_2>0$ and all sufficiently small $t>0$.

\item[(b)] Assume $\mathcal{Q}(x,\bm{v})\!=\! c_\alpha H(x)^\alpha$ for $x>0$, $\bm{v}\in \mathbb{S}^{d-1}$ and some monotone $H\in\mbox{SV}_0\cap C^1$. Set $\varrho(x)\!\coloneqq \!\int_x^\infty H(y)^\alpha y^{-\alpha-1}\mathrm{d} y$ and let $\varrho^{\leftarrow}$ be its right-continuous inverse. Suppose $G(x)\coloneqq H(\varrho^{\leftarrow}(1/x))$ satisfies Assumption~(\nameref{asm:S}) for some function $G_2\in\mbox{SV}_0$. Then, for $g(t)\coloneqq t^{1/\alpha}G(t)$, $a(t)\coloneqq G(2t)/G(t)$ and $\bm{X}^t\coloneqq(\bm{X}_{st}/g(t))_{s\in[0,1]}$, we have
\[
\mathcal{W}_q(\bm{X}^t,\bm{Z})=\mathcal{O} ( G_2(t)^q),
\quad\text{as }t \downarrow 0,\quad\text{and}\quad
\max\big\{\mathcal{W}_q(\bm{X}^t_1,\bm{Z}_1)
,\mathcal{W}_q(\bm{X}^{2t}_1,\bm{Z}_1)\big\}
\geqslant |1-a(t)^q|\mathds{E}\big[|\bm{Z}_1|^q\big]/3,
\]
for sufficiently small $t >0$. The function $t\mapsto|1-a(t)^q|$ is not upper bounded by any non-decreasing function $\phi$ with $\int_0^1\phi(t)t^{-1}\mathrm{d} t<\infty$, $G$ is $C^1$ with $t\mapsto t|G'(t)|\in\mbox{SV}_0$ and there exists some $\phi\in\mbox{SV}_0\cap\mbox{SV}_\infty$ satisfying the inequality $\phi(x)\geqslant\sup_{t>0,y\in[x\wedge 1,x\vee1]}yG'(yt)/G'(t)$ for all $x>0$. Moreover, defining  $L(t)\coloneqq t|G'(t)|/G(t)$, there exist constants $c_1,c_2>0$ such that for all sufficiently small $t>0$, we have
\[
c_2L(t)
\leqslant\max\{\mathcal{W}_q(\bm{X}^t_1,\bm{Z}_1)
,\mathcal{W}_q(\bm{X}^{2t}_1,\bm{Z}_1)\}
\quad\text{and}\quad
\mathcal{W}_q(\bm{X}^t,\bm{Z})
\leqslant c_1L(t)^q.
\]

\end{description}
title: Corollary cor:augment_stable of arXiv:2411.03609

Let mu(dx) be proportional to exp(-V(x))dx with smooth convex V and a finite second moment. Let G~N(0,I) be independent of X~mu and t>0. For Y=X+sqrt(t)G, the posterior mu_y has density proportional to exp(-V(x)-|x-y|^2/(2t)). For smooth bounded f, grad_y E[f(X)|Y=y]=Cov_mu_y(f,X)/t. The strong-log-concavity Poincare bound gives C_P(mu_y)<=t and 0<=Cov(mu_y)<=tI. These assertions also hold for nonsmooth convex potentials by log-concave approximation; they do not assert C_P(mu)<=t.

body: In probability theory, the central limit theorem (CLT) states that, under appropriate conditions, the distribution of a normalized version of the sample mean converges to a standard normal distribution. This holds even if the original variables themselves are not normally distributed. There are several versions of the CLT, each applying in the context of different conditions.
title: Central limit theorem

body: A topological space X is connected if it cannot be written as the union of two disjoint nonempty open sets. Equivalently: the only subsets of X that are simultaneously open and closed are the empty set and X itself. A subset of a topological space is called connected if it is connected in the subspace topology. A pair (U, V) of disjoint nonempty open sets whose union is X is called a separation of X. The real interval [0,1] with its standard topology is connected (a consequence of the least-upper-bound property of the reals).
title: Connected space

body:
[Thm reg_existence of arXiv:2506.01746, '\bf Optimal Bregman quantization: existence and uniqueness of optimal quantizers revisited'] Let $r>0$ and let $\|\cdot\|$ denote any norm on  $\mathbb{R}^d$.  Assume $\int_{\mathbb{R}^d}\|\xi\|^{r}\mathbb{P}(\mathrm{d}\xi)< + \infty$.

\smallskip
\noindent $(a)$ For every $n\ge 1$, there exists at least one $L^r$-optimal quantizer $\Gamma^{(r,n)}$ of size at most $n$, solution to the minimization problem
\[
\inf_{\Gamma: |\Gamma|\leq n}  e_r(\Gamma,P,\|.\|)
\]
i.e. such that 
\[
e_r(\Gamma^{(r,n)},P,\|.\|)=  e_{r,n}(P,\|.\|).  
\]

\smallskip
\noindent $(b)$ If ${\rm card}\big({\rm supp}(P)\big) \ge n$, then any $L^r$-optimal quantizer $ \Gamma^{(r,n)}$ has full size $n$ and for every $a\!\in  \Gamma^{(r,n)}$, $P(C_a( \Gamma^{(r,n)}))>0$. Moreover, 

\smallskip
 $(i)$ if the norm $\|\cdot\|$ is smooth~(\footnote{that $\|\cdot\|$ is differentiable on $\mathbb{R}^d\setminus\{0\}$, like Euclidean norms or $\ell^p$-norms, $1<p<+\infty$.}) and strictly convex then {\em the boundary of the Voronoi partition is $P$-negligible}: for every $a\!\in \Gamma^{(r,n)}$, $P\big(\partial C_a(\Gamma^{(r,n)})\big)=0$

\smallskip
  $(ii)$ if   $r\ge 2$ and the norm $\|\cdot\|=|\cdot|_e$ is Euclidean then these quantizers are {\em $L^r$-stationarity}: for every $a\!\in \Gamma^{(r,n)}$,
\[
a = \frac{\int_{C_a(\Gamma^{(r,n)})}\xi|\xi-a|^{r-2}P(\mathrm{d}\xi)}{\int_{C_a(\Gamma^{(r,n)})}|\xi-a|^{r-2}P(\mathrm{d}\xi)}.
\]
\
\noindent $(c)$ When $d=1$  and $P=U([0,1])$, then for every $r>0$, the $L^r$-optimal quantizer is unique and 
\[
\Gamma^{(r,n)} = \Big\{\frac{2k-1}{2n},\; k=0,\ldots,n\Big\}.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition prop-well-posedness-approx of arXiv:2507.09922, 'A scaling limit for Vlasov equations with electrostatic fluctuations'] Assume that $f^\delta_0\in C_c^\infty (\mathbb{T}^3\times \mathbb{R}^3, \mathbb{R}_+)$. Then for any $\delta>0$, the approximate equation (equation stoch-Vlasov-approx of the paper) admits a unique probabilistically strong solution $f^\delta$, represented as
  $$f^\delta_t(x,v)= f^\delta_0 \big(\Phi^{\delta,-1}_t(x,v) \big), $$
where $\big\{\Phi^{\delta,-1}_t \big\}_{t\ge 0}$ is the inverse flow associated to the stochastic equations
  \begin{equation}
  \left\{ \aligned
  d X^\delta_t &= V^\delta_t\, dt, \\
  d V^\delta_t &= \big[E_{\rho^\delta_t}\big(X^\delta_t \big) + B V^\delta_t\times \bm{e}_3 \big]\, dt + \sum_k \sigma_k\big(X^\delta_t \big)\circ dW^k_t
  \endaligned \right.
  \end{equation}
with initial condition $\big(X^\delta_0, V^\delta_0 \big)= (x,v)\in \mathbb{T}^3\times \mathbb{R}^3$. Moreover, $\|f^\delta_t \|_{L^p_{x,v}} = \|f^\delta_0 \|_{L^p_{x,v}}$ for any $p\ge 1$.

[Prop of arXiv:2507.09120, 'Chemical distance in graphs of polynomial growth'] (Russo's Formula; see e.g. [grimmett1999percolation])
   Let $f : 2^E \to \mathbb{R}$ be a decreasing function, in the sense that $\omega \subset \omega'$ implies
   $f(\omega) \ge f(\omega')$. Suppose further that $f$ only depends on a finite set of edges
   (that is, there exists $F \subset E$ finite such that $f(\omega) = f(\omega \cap F)$ for all $\omega \in 2^E$).
   Then $\mathbb{E}[f(G_p)]$ is differentiable in $p$, and its derivative is given by
   \[ 
      \frac{d}{dp} \mathbb{E}[f(G_p)] = - \sum_{e \in E} \mathbb{E}[ \Delta_e f (G_p) ],
   \]
   where for $\omega \in 2^E$ and $e \in E$ we define 
   $ \Delta_e f(\omega) := f(\omega \setminus \{e\}) - f(\omega \cup \{e\})$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Unnumbered prop of arXiv:2507.09120, 'Chemical distance in graphs of polynomial growth'

A sequence is Cauchy if for every epsilon > 0 there is N with |a_m - a_n| < epsilon for all m, n >= N. In R (and any complete metric space) a sequence converges if and only if it is Cauchy. The forward direction holds in any metric space; the converse is exactly completeness. This lets one prove convergence without knowing the limit.

body:
[Definition of arXiv:2602.00853, 'Mixing times for the stochastic $p$-Laplace equation'] Let $p\in (1,2)$. We say that $\{X_t\}_{t\in [0,T]}$ is a \emph{stochastic variational inequality (SVI) solution} to (equation eq:pLaplace of the paper) for initial data $x_0\in L^2(U)$ if
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item $X\in L^2([0,T]\times\Omega;L^2(U))$ such that
\[\operatorname{ess\,sup}\displaylimits_{t\in [0,T]}\mathbb{E}\int_0^T\int_U|\nabla X_s|^p\,\mathrm{d} z\,\mathrm{d} s<\infty,\]
\item for any $z_0\in L^2(U)$, every $Z\in L^2([0,T]\times\Omega;H^1_0(U))$, and every progressively measurable $G\in L^2([0,T]\times\Omega;L^2(U))$ such that
\[Z_t=z_0+\int_0^t G_s\,\mathrm{d} s+B\,W_t,\]
we have that for a.e. $t\in [0,T]$
\begin{align*}&\mathbb{E}\left[\|X_t-Z_t\|^2_{L^2(U)}\right]+\frac{2}{p}\mathbb{E}\int_0^t\int_U|\nabla X_s|^p\,\mathrm{d} z\,\mathrm{d} s\\
\le &\mathbb{E}\left[\|x_0-z_0\|^2_{L^2(U)}\right]+\frac{2}{p}\mathbb{E}\int_0^t\int_U|\nabla Z_s|^p\,\mathrm{d} z\,\mathrm{d} s-2\mathbb{E}\int_0^t\int_U G_s(X_s-Z_s)\,\mathrm{d} z\,\mathrm{d} s.\end{align*}
\end{enumerate}

body:
[Definition 11 of arXiv:2609.02878, '2609.02878'] For \(p=[w]\in\PP^N\), define the ambient chord-square barrier
\begin{equation}
 \widehat\rho_p([z])
 :=1-\frac{|\langle z,w\rangle|^2}{|z|^2|w|^2}.
\end{equation}
It is a smooth nonnegative function, vanishes precisely at \(p\), and
the family \(\{\widehat\rho_p\}_{p\in\PP^N}\) has uniform first- and
second-derivative bounds.  Moreover, for uniform \(0<c<C<\infty\),
\begin{equation}
 c\,d_{\rm FS}(y,p)^2\le\widehat\rho_p(y)
 \le C\,d_{\rm FS}(y,p)^2,
 \qquad y,p\in\PP^N.
\end{equation}
Indeed, in the standard normalization
\(\widehat\rho_p=\sin^2d_{\rm FS}(\,\cdot\,,p)\), and the
Fubini--Study diameter is finite.

Now let \(q\in U_0\Subset U_1\Subset Y^{\rm rv}\).  Compose
\(\widehat\rho_{\iota(q)}|_Y\) with a smooth nondecreasing function
that is the identity near zero and is constant once its argument leaves
a sufficiently small sublevel set contained in \(U_1\).  The resulting
function \(\rho_q\) is called a \emph{localized squared-distance
barrier at \(q\)}.  It is the restriction of a smooth ambient function,
has zero set \(\{q\}\), is uniformly comparable to
\(d_\eta(\,\cdot\,,q)^2\) near \(q\), is bounded below on
\(Y\setminus U_0\), and has its first two derivatives supported in
\(U_1\).

[Theorem 5 of arXiv:2605.23222, 'On global solutions to the semidiscrete stochastic heat equation'] If $\beta$ is sufficiently small, the following holds: Let $\Omega' \in \Fc$ such that $Q(\Omega') = 1$ and $\theta_t(\Omega') = \Omega'$ for all $t \in \R$. Let $Z: \Z^d \times \R \times \Omega' \to (0, \infty)$ be a global stationary solution to~\eqref{eq:sSHE} such that for every $\omega \in \Omega'$ there is $\epsilon \in (0,1)$ with 
$$
\lim_{\|y\| \to \infty} \frac{\lvert \ln(Z(y,0,\omega)) \rvert}{\|y\|^{1-\epsilon}} = 0. 
$$
Then, $Q$-almost surely, for all $(y,t) \in \Z^d \times \R$, 
$$
Z(y,t,\omega) = Z_{-\infty}^{y,t}(\omega) \cdot \frac{Z(0,0,\omega)}{Z_{-\infty}^{0,0}(\omega)}. 
$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lem thm:bobkov of arXiv:2602.22342, 'Sum of Gaussian vectors and large sets'] Let $C\geq 1$ and let $\mu$ be a probability measure on $\R$ with piecewise continuous density 
$$C^{-1}\varphi(x)\leq \frac{d\mu (x)}{dx} \leq  C \varphi(x).$$
Then $\mu = F_*(\gamma_1)$ for a Lipschitz map $F:\R\to \R$ with Lipschitz constant at most $C^2$.
