[Prop P:properties-elpp of arXiv:2604.10020, 'The directed landscape in half-space'] Fix $\rho \in \mathbb{R} \cup \{-\infty\}$, and let $\mathcal{Q}^\rho$ be a subsequential limit in law of $\mathcal{Q}_n^{\rho_n}$ along a sequence $\rho_n \to \rho$. Then $\mathcal{Q}^\rho$ satisfies the following properties. In what follows, $c> 0$ are universal constants, and we define
		$\mathcal{G}^\rho(x, s; y, t) = \mathcal{Q}^\rho(x, s; y, t) + \frac{(x-y)^2}{(t-s)}$ for any $(x,s;y,t)\in \mathbb{H}^2_\uparrow$.
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item \textup{(Independent increments)} For any disjoint collection of time intervals $(s_i, t_i), i\in\llbracket1, k \rrbracket$, the increments
		$\mathcal{Q}^\rho(\cdot, s_i; \cdot, t_i)$
		are independent.
		\item \textup{(Metric composition)} For any fixed $r < s < t$ and $x, y \ge 0$, we have
		$$
		\mathcal{Q}^\rho(x, s; y, t) = \max_{z \ge 0} \mathcal{Q}^\rho(x, s; z, r) + \mathcal{Q}^\rho(z, r; y, t).
		$$
		\item \textup{(KPZ scaling)} Fix $q > 0$, and consider the rescaled field
		$$
		\mathcal{Q}^{\rho, q}(x, s; y, t) := q^{-1} \mathcal{Q}^\rho(q^2x, q^3 s; q^2 y, q^3 t).
		$$
		Then $\mathcal{Q}^{\rho, q}$ is a subsequential limit of the sequence $\mathcal{Q}^{q \rho_n}_n$.
		\item \textup{(One-point tail bounds)} For $u = (x, s; y, s + t) \in \mathbb{H}^2_\uparrow$, and all $a > 0$,
		\begin{align*}
			\mathbb{P}( \mathcal{G}^\rho(u)< - a t^{1/3}) &\le 2\exp(-c a^3), \\
			\mathbb{P}( \mathcal{G}^\rho(u) > a t^{1/3} + t (\rho\vee 0)^2) &\le 2\exp\left(-c a^{3/2} \left(1 \wedge \frac{\sqrt{a}}{(\rho \vee 0) t^{1/3}}\right)\right).
		\end{align*}
		Furthermore, for $u = (0, s; 0, s + t)$ on the diagonal, we have the following Gaussian lower bound: for all $0 < a < t (\rho\vee 0)^2$,
		\begin{align*}
			\mathbb{P}( \mathcal{G}^\rho(u) < -a + t (\rho\vee 0)^2) &\le 2\exp\left(- \frac{ca^2}{(\rho\vee 0)t}\right).
		\end{align*}
		\item \textup{(Two-point spatial tail bound)} 
        There is a universal constant $C_0>0$, such that for any $u = (x, s; y, s+t), u' = (x, s; y + z, s+t)  \in \mathbb H^2_\uparrow$, and 
        $a>C_0\max(z^{3/2}/t, \sqrt{z}|x-y|/t, \sqrt{z} (\rho\vee 0))$,
        we have:
		\begin{equation}
			
\mathbb{P}(|\mathcal{G}^\rho(u) - \mathcal{G}^\rho(u')| \ge a\sqrt{z}) \le 2 \exp(- c a^2).
		\end{equation}
		\item \textup{(Two-point temporal tail bound)} There is a universal constant $C_0>0$, such that for any $u = (x, s; y, s + t), u' = (x, s; y', s+t + r)  \in \mathbb H^2_\uparrow$, where $0<r<t$ and $(x, s), (y, s+t), (y', s + t + r)$ are all collinear, and $a > C_0\max(r^{2/3}(x-y)^2/t^2, r^{2/3}(\rho\vee 0)^2)$, we have:
		\begin{equation*}
			\mathbb{P}(|\mathcal{G}^\rho(u) - \mathcal{G}^\rho(u')| \ge a r^{1/3}) \le 2 \exp(- c a^{3/2}).
		\end{equation*}
		\item \textup{(Basic parabolic shape estimate)} For any $(x, s; y, s + t) \in \mathbb{H}^2_\uparrow$ and $a, \delta > 0$ we have:
		\begin{equation*}
            \begin{split}
                \mathbb{P}(\mathcal{G}^\rho(x, s; y + z, s+ t) &\le t(\rho\vee 0)^2  + a t^{1/3} + \delta z^2 \text{ for all } z \in [-y, \infty)) \\
                &\ge 1 - 2\exp\left(-c_\delta a^{3/2} \left(1\wedge \frac{\sqrt{a}}{(\rho\vee 0) t^{1/3}}\right)\right),
            \end{split}
		\end{equation*}
        where $c_\delta$ is a constant depending on $\delta$.
		\item \textup{(Time stationarity and reversal)} For any $r \in \mathbb{R}$, we have
        $$
\mathcal{Q}^\rho(x, s; y, t) \stackrel{d}{=} \mathcal{Q}^\rho(x, s + r; y, t + r) \stackrel{d}{=} \mathcal{Q}^\rho(y, -t; x, -s),
        $$
        where the equality in law is as continuous functions on $\mathbb H^2_\uparrow$. 

        \item \textup{(Quadrangle inequality)} For any $s < t$, and  $x_1 \le x_2$ and $y_1 \le y_2$, we have
        $$
       \mathcal{Q}^\rho(x_1, 0;  y_1, t) + \mathcal{Q}^\rho(x_2, 0;  y_2, t) - \mathcal{Q}^\rho(x_1, 0;  y_2, t) - \mathcal{Q}^\rho(x_2, 0;  y_1, t) \ge 0.
        $$

[Corollary cor:sharp of arXiv:2608.25279, 'Provable Non-Acceleration of Standard Strang\\ Splittings of Kinetic Langevin Dynamics'] \begin{enumerate}
\item[\rm(i)] For the tuning
\begin{equation*}
 h=\frac1{4\sqrt\kappa},
 \qquad
 \gamma=4\sqrt\kappa,
 \qquad
 Q=Q_{1/(4\sqrt\kappa),\,4\sqrt\kappa}^{U},
\end{equation*}
there is a universal
constant $C_1<\infty$ such that, for every $\kappa>1$, $d\ge1$,
$U\in\mathcal U_\kappa^d$, every initial state $z$, and every
$\varepsilon\in(0,1)$,
\begin{equation*}
 t_{\mathrm{mix}}(z,\varepsilon;Q,\pi)
 \le C_1\kappa\log\!\left(\frac{C_1\kappa(1+W_2(\delta_z,\pi))}{\varepsilon}\right),
\end{equation*}
where $\pi$ is the unique invariant law of $Q$.
\item[\rm(ii)] Let $\mathfrak t$
be any numerically
stable fixed-parameter OBABO tuning rule, let $C,c>0$ and $a,b\ge0$
be constants, let $\tau:(1,\infty)\to(0,\infty)$ satisfy
$\tau(\kappa)=o(\kappa)$ as $\kappa\to\infty$, and let
$\kappa_0>1$. Then there exist $\kappa\ge\kappa_0$ and
$U\in\mathcal U_\kappa^2$ such that $Q_{h_\kappa,\gamma_\kappa}^U$ has a
unique invariant law $\pi$, and there are $z\in\mathbb R^4$ and
$n\in\mathbb N$ for which
\begin{equation}
 \norm{\delta_z(Q_{h_\kappa,\gamma_\kappa}^U)^n-\pi}_{\mathrm{TV}}
 >C\kappa^a\bigl(1+W_2(\delta_z,\pi)\bigr)^b
   \exp\!\left(-\frac{cn}{\tau(\kappa)}\right).
\end{equation}
In particular, no such bound holds with $\tau(\kappa)=\kappa^\alpha$
for any $\alpha<1$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Sharpness of the diffusive scale

[Definition def:scaleFunction of arXiv:2412.05030, 'Characterization of Subordinate Symmetric Markov Processes'] For constants $0 < \alpha_1 \le \alpha_2$, 
  we say a continuous function $\psi : [0,\infty) \to [0,\infty)$ satisfies $LU(\alpha_1,\alpha_2)$
  if $\psi$ is strictly increasing, $\psi(0) = 0$, $\psi(1) = 1$  and 
  there exists constants $C \ge 1$ such that
  \begin{align}
    C^{-1} \left(\frac{R}{r}\right)^{\alpha_1} \le \frac{\psi(R)}{\psi(r)} \le C \left(\frac{R}{r}\right)^{\alpha_2}, \qquad 0 < r \le R.
  \end{align}
  We call such function $\psi$ a scale function.

        s^{2\alpha}D_{0^+}^{\alpha}(s^{-\alpha}f_s)

body:
[Theorem 22 (Two-parameter rough integral on rectangular domains) of arXiv:2605.08844, 'Signature Kernel and Schwinger-Dyson Kernel Equations as Two-Parameter Rough Differential '] Let 
\[
Z \in \mathcal{D}^{p, q}_{\mathbf{X}, \mathbf{Y}}\big([a, b] \times [c,d], \mathrm{Hom}(V \boxtimes W, F)\big).
\] 
Then the limit
\[
\int_{[a,b] \times [c,d]} Z_{s, u} \, d(\mathbf{X}, \mathbf{Y})  
   :=  \lim_{\left|\mathcal{P} \times \mathcal{D}\right| \to 0} 
   \sum_{\mathcal{P}\times \mathcal{D}} \Omega^Z
\]
exists and satisfies the estimate
\begin{align*}
\Bigg|
\int_{[a,b]\times[c,d]} Z_{s,u}\, d(\mathbf{X}_s,\mathbf{Y}_u)
- \Omega^Z\begin{pmatrix} a, b \\ c, d \end{pmatrix}
\Bigg|
&\le C_{p,q,T}\Big[
      A(\theta,T,\mathbf{R})\,
      \omega_{\mathbf{X}}(a,b)^{\theta}\,
      \omega_{\mathbf{Y}}(c,d)^{\theta} \\
&\qquad
      + B_X(c,d)\,\omega_{\mathbf{X}}(a,b)^{\theta}
      + B_Y(a,b)\,\omega_{\mathbf{Y}}(c,d)^{\theta}
\Big].
\end{align*}

where $\theta = \min(\frac{\floor{p} + 1}{p}, \frac{\floor{q} + 1}{q})$ and 
\begin{align*}
&A(p, q, \mathbf{R}) 
= \left( \sup_{j \in [0:\kappa)} \| \mathbf{X}^{(j+1)} \|_{p_j} \right)
  \left( \sup_{k \in  [0:\lambda)} \| \tilde{\mathbf{X}}^{(k+1)} \|_{\tilde{p}_k} \right)
  \left( \sup_{(j,k)\in [0:\kappa) \times [0:\lambda)} \| \mathbf{R}^{(j,k)} \|_{(q_j,\tilde{q}_k)} \right),\\
&B_{X}(c,d)
= 
\sup_{(j,k)\in [0:\kappa) \times [0:\lambda)}\left[ 
  \|\mathbf{X}^{(j+1)}\|_{\frac{p}{j+1}}\,
  \|\mathbf{Y}^{(k+1)}\|_{\frac{q}{k+1}}\,
  \big\| R^{1, (j,k)}
       \big\|_{\frac{p}{\kappa - j}}\,
  \omega_{\mathbf{Y}}(c,d)^{\frac{k+1}{q}}
\right],\\
&B_{Y}(a,b)
= \sup_{(j,k)\in [0:\kappa) \times [0:\lambda)}
\left[
   \|\mathbf{X}^{(j+1)}\|_{\frac{p}{j+1}}\,
  \|\mathbf{Y}^{(k+1)}\|_{\frac{q}{k+1}}\,
  \big\| R^{2,(j,k)}\!
       \big\|_{\frac{q}{\lambda - k}}\,
  \omega_{\mathbf{X}}(a,b)^{\frac{j+1}{p}}
\right].
\end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Two-parameter rough integral on rectangular domains

body:
[Lemma 13 of arXiv:2604.25470, 'A mathematical analysis of hierarchical Hopfield models'] Fix $\alpha$ and suppose that $\mathcal G_\alpha(\delta,\rho)$ holds.
	Then 
	\[
	\mathrm{score}^{\mathrm{pen}}_\alpha(x)
	\ge
	a(1-\delta)L_\alpha-bL_\alpha,
	\]
	and for every $\beta\neq\alpha$,
	\[
	\mathrm{score}^{\mathrm{pen}}_\beta(x)
	\le
	a\bigl(|S_\alpha\cap S_\beta|+\rho\bigr)-bL_\beta.
	\]
	
	Consequently,
	\[
	\mathrm{score}^{\mathrm{pen}}_\alpha(x)
	-
	\mathrm{score}^{\mathrm{pen}}_\beta(x)
	\ge
	a\bigl(
	(1-\delta)L_\alpha
	-
	|S_\alpha\cap S_\beta|
	-
	\rho	
	\bigr)
	-
	b(L_\alpha-L_\beta).
	\]
	
	In particular, if
	\[
	|S_\alpha\cap S_\beta|
	<
	(1-\delta)L_\alpha-\rho-\frac{b}{a}(L_\alpha-L_\beta),
	\]
	then
	\[
	\mathrm{score}^{\mathrm{pen}}_\alpha(x)
	>
	\mathrm{score}^{\mathrm{pen}}_\beta(x).
	\]

[Theorem 2 of arXiv:2608.20613, 'Random walks on wreath products \\and spectral gaps for coloured interchange processes'] Let $\Lambda=(\lambda^\gamma)_{\gamma\in\Gamma}$ be a $G$-multipartition of $n$.  Then
\[
\dim V_\Lambda^{\Sn_n}
=
\prod_{\gamma\in\Gamma}
\dim \Schur_{\lambda^\gamma}(\C^{d_\gamma}).
\]
Moreover, $V_\Lambda$ occurs in $\mathcal P_n(G)$ if and only if $\len(\lambda^\gamma)\leqslant d_\gamma$ for every $\gamma\in\Gamma$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem RoughInt of arXiv:2411.06089, '{\Large \bf Averaging principle for semilinear slow-fast rough partial differential equati'] \emph{([GH19])}
For any $T>0$, let $\mathbf X=(X,X^2)\in \mathscr{C}^\gamma([0,T]; \mathbb R^d)$ for some $\gamma\in(1/3,1/2]$ and let
$(Y,Y^{\prime})\in\mathscr{D}_{S,\mathbf X}^{2\gamma}([0,T];\mathcal{H}_\alpha^d)$.
Then one has that the rough integral
$$\int_{s}^{t}S_{t-u}Y_{u}d \mathbf X_u:=\lim_{|\mathcal{P}|\to 0}\sum_{[u,v]\in\mathcal{P}}S_{t-u}(Y_u \delta X_{v,u}+Y_{u}^{\prime} X^2_{v,u})$$
exists in $\hat{C}^\gamma([0,T];\mathcal{H}_\alpha)$,
where the limit is taken along any partitions $\mathcal P$ of $[s,t]$ such that mesh $|\mathcal P| \rightarrow 0$.
Furthermore, for any $0\leq\beta<3\gamma$ one has the bound
\begin{align} 
& \Big \|\int_{s}^{t}S_{t-u}Y_{u}d \mathbf X_{u}-S_{t-s}Y_{s} \delta X_{t,s}-S_{t-s}Y_{s}^{\prime} X^2_{t,s} \Big\|_{\mathcal{H}_{\alpha+\beta}} \nonumber\\
 \lesssim &   \big(|R^{Y}|_{2\gamma,\alpha}|X|_{\gamma}+\|Y'\|_{\gamma,\alpha}|X^2|_{2\gamma}\big)|t-s|^{3\gamma-\beta},
\end{align}
and the map
$$(Y,Y')\rightarrow (U,U'):=\Big(\int_0^\cdot S_{\cdot-u}Y_u d \mathbf X_u,Y \Big)$$
is continuous from $\mathscr D_{S,\mathbf X}^{2\gamma} ([0,T]; \mathcal{H}_\alpha^d )$ to $\mathscr D_{S,\mathbf X}^{2\gamma} ([0,T]; \mathcal{H}_\alpha )$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition def:wall of arXiv:2609.00970, 'The unique predual problem for Lipschitz spaces, revisited'] A non-empty closed subset $W\subset M$ is a \emph{geodesic wall} in $M$ if there exist two sets $A,B\subset M$ such that
\begin{enumerate}[label={\upshape{(\alph*)}}]
\item $M$ equals the disjoint union $A\cup W\cup B$,
\item $W\subset\overline{A}\cap\overline{B}$,
\item $A,B$ are open and connected, and
\item for any $a\in A$, $b\in B$ there exists $w\in W$ such that $d(a,w)+d(w,b)=d(a,b)$.
\end{enumerate}
title: Definition def:wall of arXiv:2609.00970

[Cor prop.tga of arXiv:2412.00822, '\textsc{Ideal Poisson--Voronoi tessellations \\ beyond hyperbolic spaces}'] For any isometry $g=(g_{1},g_{2})\in {\rm Isom}_{1}$, the action on a corona point $(\theta,\phi,r)\in \widetilde{\partial \mathcal{M}}$ defined in the product of disks model
$$
g(\theta,\phi,r) \coloneqq \left(g_{1}(\theta), g_{2}(\phi),\frac{r}{K(g_{1}^{-1}\left(\mathbf{o}),\theta\right) \cdot K(g_{2}^{-1}\left(\mathbf{o}),\phi\right)}\right)
$$
is a transitive group action that leaves the corona measure $\mu$ in (equation eq.cormes of the paper) invariant. Consequently, the law of ${\rm IPVT}(\mathcal{M})$ is invariant under ${\rm Isom}_{1}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Thm 4 of arXiv:2608.13208, 'Universality in dimension $1$ of kinetically constrained lattice gases'] KCLGs in one dimension divide in three universality
classes:
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $c(-1,0,\bone_{(-\infty,-1]})\neq0$ and $c(-1,0,\bone_{[0,\infty]})\neq0$,
then $q_{c}=0$. In this case the model is \emph{noncooperative} (see
\cite{Shapira2024Noncooperative} and Section \ref{subsec:noncooperative}
below).
\item If $c(-1,0,\bone_{(-\infty,-1]})=0$ and $c(-1,0,\bone_{[0,\infty)})=0$,
then $q_{c}=1$. We say in this case that the model is \emph{blocked}.
\item If $c(-1,0,\bone_{(-\infty,-1]})\neq0$ and $c(-1,0,\bone_{[0,\infty)})=0$
or vice versa, then $q_{c}\in(0,1)$. We call such models \emph{one-sided}.
\end{enumerate}
By $\bone_{(-\infty,-1]}$ (respectively $\bone_{[0,\infty)}$) we
mean the configuration filled in $(-\infty,-1]$ (respectively $[0,\infty)$)
and empty elsewhere. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Thm 4 of arXiv:2608.13208

[Lemma 40 of arXiv:2606.24887, '2606.24887'] Let $d$ satisfy \cref{eq:regimedlog2}.

body:
[Lemma 24 of arXiv:2608.18557, 'Randomly Permuted Orthogonal Products and Fast Dimension Reduction'] There exist couplings of an ORA walk \(Q_T^{\mathrm O}\) and an
	S-ORA walk \(Q_T^{\mathrm S}\), both of length \(T\), such that,
	possibly under different couplings,
	\[
	Q_T^{\mathrm S}
	=
	G_T^{\mathrm L}Q_T^{\mathrm O},
	\qquad 
	Q_T^{\mathrm S}
	=
	Q_T^{\mathrm O}G_T^{\mathrm R},
	\]
	where \(G_T^{\mathrm L}\), \(G_T^{\mathrm R} \in \mathcal H_d\) are signed
	permutation matrices. Consequently, for every $I\subseteq [d]$ and every $X\subseteq \mathbb{S}^{d-1}$, we have
	\[
	\norm{Q_T^{\mathrm S}}_\infty
	\stackrel{\mathrm d}=
	\norm{Q_T^{\mathrm O}}_\infty,
	\qquad
	\kappa_I(Q_T^{\mathrm S})
	\stackrel{\mathrm d}=
	\kappa_I(Q_T^{\mathrm O}),
	\qquad
	\Theta_{Q_T^{\mathrm S}}(X)
	\stackrel{\mathrm d}=
	\Theta_{Q_T^{\mathrm O}}(X).
	\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma 24 of arXiv:2608.18557

[Thm eq:RootDecomp of arXiv:2506.18207, 'Cartan's Path Development, the Logarithmic Signature and a Conjecture of Lyons-Sidorova'] Let $\Delta$ be the set of
all nonzero roots with respect to a given Cartan subalgebra $\mathfrak{h}.$
Then $\mathfrak{g}$ can be written as the direct sum 
\begin{equation}
\mathfrak{g}=\mathfrak{h}+\sum_{\alpha\in\Delta}\mathfrak{g}^{\alpha}.
\end{equation}
In this decomposition, one has $\dim\mathfrak{g}^{\alpha}=1$ for
each $\alpha\in\Delta$. Moreover, if $\alpha,\beta,\alpha+\beta\in\Delta$
then $[\mathfrak{g}^{\alpha},\mathfrak{g}^{\beta}]=\mathfrak{g}^{\alpha+\beta}.$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Root Space Decomposition

[Lemma Bony of arXiv:2604.07497, 'The Three-Dimensional Stochastic EMHD System: Local Well-Posedness and Maximal Pathwise So'] (Bony's paraproduct formula)
Let $u$ and $v$ be tempered distributions. Then
\begin{equation*}
u\cdot v
=\sum_{l = -1}^\infty \big({\mathcal S}_{l-2} u\cdot  \Delta_l v\big)
+\sum_{l = -1}^\infty \big(\Delta_l u \cdot {\mathcal S}_{l-2} v \big)
+\sum_{l=-1}^\infty \big(\Delta_l u \cdot \widetilde{\Delta}_l v\big).
\end{equation*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma Bony of arXiv:2604.07497

body:
[Lem VEV of arXiv:2609.02409, 'Membranes and Maps'] [OP06:GW-H]
    The connected vacuum expectation value $\langle \mathcal{E}_{k_1}(z_1) \cdots \mathcal{E}_{k_n}(z_n) \rangle^{\circ}$ vanishes for $n>1$ whenever $k_1\leq 0$, $k_n\geq 0$, or $\sum_j k_j\neq 0$. If $k_1 > 0$, it satisfies the recursion
    \begin{equation}
        \left\langle \mathcal{E}_{k_1}(z_1) \cdots \mathcal{E}_{k_n}(z_n) \right\rangle^{\circ}
        =
        \sum_{i=2}^n
        \varsigma\Bigl(
            \det\begin{psmallmatrix} k_1 & k_i \\ z_1 & z_i \end{psmallmatrix}
        \Bigr)
        \left\langle
            \mathcal{E}_{k_2}(z_2) \cdots
            \mathcal{E}_{k_i+k_1}(z_i+z_1) \cdots
            \mathcal{E}_{k_n}(z_n)
        \right\rangle^{\circ} \,,
    \end{equation}
    with initial condition $\langle \mathcal{E}_{k}(z) \rangle^{\circ} = \frac{\delta_{k,0}}{\varsigma(z)}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
Let a<b be finite, f in C-infinity([a,b]), t_1,...,t_m distinct nodes in [a,b], m>=1, and k_1,...,k_m positive integers. Put D=sum_i k_i and g(t)=product_i(t-t_i)^(k_i). There is a unique polynomial p of degree<D with p^(j)(t_i)=f^(j)(t_i) for 0<=j<k_i. For t in [a,b] outside the nodes, there exists xi strictly between min(t,t_1,...,t_m) and max(t,t_1,...,t_m) such that f(t)-p(t)=f^(D)(xi)g(t)/D!. At a node the error is zero; no strict-interior witness is asserted for a collapsed interval. In particular, if every k_i is even and f^(D)>=0 on [a,b], then p(t)<=f(t) throughout [a,b]. Derivatives at endpoints are understood one-sided.
a<b finite; f smooth on the closed interval
distinct real nodes inside [a,b]; all multiplicities positive integers
the strict-interior remainder assertion is for nonnodes

[Proposition 209 (The main below-top-order a priori estimates for the transport variables and the modified fluid variables) of arXiv:2609.03101, 'The emergence of the Cauchy horizon from the crease for $3D$ compressible Euler flow'] Let $N = \Ntop$ and let $\fluxcontrolVort_N(\ubar,u),  \dots, \bulkcontrolDivGradEnt_N(\ubar,u)$ be the $L^2$-transport-controlling quantities as defined in Def.\,\ref{D:FUNDAMENTALTRANSPORTL2CONTROLLINGQUANTITIES}. 
	Under the parameter size-assumptions of Sect.\,\ref{SS:PARAMETERSIZEASSUMPTIONS}, the data-assumptions of Sects.\,\ref{S:ASSUMPTIONSONTHEDATA}, 
	and the bootstrap assumptions of Sect.\,\ref{S:BOOTSTRAPEVERYTHINGEXCEPTENERGIES},
	there exists a constant $C > 0$
	such that the following estimates hold for 
	$(\ubar,u) \in [\leftubar,\ubarboot) \times [\moreinterestingu_1,\moreinterestingu_2]$: 
\begin{subequations} 
	\begin{align}
		\fluxcontrolVort_{\le N} (\ubar,u) + \bulkcontrolVort_{\le N} (\ubar,u)
		& \leq C \initialsmalldoublenull^2,  \\
		\fluxcontrolGradEnt_{\le N} (\ubar,u) + \bulkcontrolGradEnt_{\le N} (\ubar,u)& \leq C \initialsmalldoublenull^2,  \\
		\fluxcontrolVortVort_{\le N-1} (\ubar,u) + \bulkcontrolVortVort_{\le N-1} (\ubar,u) & \leq C \initialsmalldoublenull^2,  \\	
		\fluxcontrolDivGradEnt_{\le N-1} (\ubar,u) + \bulkcontrolDivGradEnt_{\le N-1} (\ubar,u) & \leq C \initialsmalldoublenull^2.  
	\end{align}
\end{subequations}	
In addition, let $\toricontrolVort,\toricontrolGradEnt,\toricontrolVortVort, \toricontrolDivGradEnt$ denote the $L^2$-controlling quantities on the double-null tori  defined in Def.\,\ref{D:FUNDAMENTALTRANSPORTL2CONTROLLINGQUANTITIES}. Then, the following a priori estimates hold:
\begin{subequations}
		\begin{align}
			\toricontrolVort_{\le N - 1}(\ubar,u), 
			\,
			\toricontrolGradEnt_{\le N - 1} 
			& 
			\leq C \initialsmall^2, 
			 \\
			\toricontrolVortVort_{\le N - 2}(\ubar,u),
			\,
			\toricontrolDivGradEnt_{\le N - 2}(\ubar,u)
			& \leq C \initialsmall^2.
			
	\end{align}
\end{subequations} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Controlled generators, exact finite-state diagnostic, coupling, renewal reward or capacity comparison Result: A two-job calculation isolates the value of probing. Job A has size 0.01 with probability 0.9 and 100 with probability 0.1; job B has known size 2. SERPT initially selects B because E[A]=10.009. Completing B before A gives expected sum of completion times 14.009. Serving A for 0.01, then serving B if A survives, gives 0.9*(0.01+2.01)+0.1*(102+2.01)=12.219. The Gittins stopping ratio at probe duration 0.01 is 0.01/0.9, smaller than B rank 2. Any approximation proof based only on expected residual size loses this probing advantage. Check: In the long-A branch, total A completion time is 102 after the intervening two units for B; omitting those two units would give a false larger improvement. Both strategies are enumerated by the two possible A sizes. Obstruction: This finite instance does not establish a stationary approximation factor, nor distinguish the full worst-case ratios of SERPT and M-SERPT.

body:
[Pro LowerBound of arXiv:2606.19583, 'Power-law hypothesis and (un)fairness of PageRank on undirected multi-type PAMs'] The following holds true:
\begin{enumerate}[(a)]
    \item The sequence $(R^{1,\textup{dirTr}}_{\phi_n}(\vec{G}_n))_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ converges in distribution to
\[R^{1,\textup{dirTr}}_\phi(\mathcal{T}_X(\tau)):=c(1-c)\sum_{u \rightarrow \phi}\frac{1}{m_{X_u}+d_u^-}.\]
\item Fix $k \in S$. Conditionally on $X_{\phi_n}=k$, the sequence $(R^{1,\textup{dirTr}}_{\phi_n}(\vec{G}_n))_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ converges in distribution to
\[R^{1,\textup{dirTr}}_\phi(\mathcal{T}_k(\tau)):=c(1-c)\sum_{u \rightarrow \phi}\frac{1}{m_{X_u}+d_u^-},\]
where the r.h.s. refers to the process $\mathcal{T}_X(\tau)$ conditioned on $X=k$.
\item For $k \in S$, there exists some finite $\beta$ such that, as $r \rightarrow \infty$,
\[\mathbb{P}(R^{1,\textup{dirTr}}_\phi(\mathcal{T}_X(\tau))>r \mid X_\phi=k) \geq  (1+o(1)) \;\mathbb{P}(d_{\phi}^->\beta r \mid X_\phi=k).\]
\end{enumerate}
In particular, conditionally on $X_\phi=k$, the random variable $R^{1,\textup{dirTr}}_\phi(\mathcal{T}_X(\tau))$ satisfies a power law with the same $k$-dependent exponent as the (in-)degree.

Let X, Y, Z be Banach spaces, T in B(X,Y) and S in B(Y,Z) both Fredholm. Then S T in B(X,Z) is Fredholm and ind(S T) = ind S + ind T. In particular, composing with an invertible operator does not change the index, and if S T is a compact perturbation of the identity then ind S = -ind T.
X, Y, Z are Banach spaces
T in B(X,Y) and S in B(Y,Z) are both Fredholm

[Theorem 2 of arXiv:2609.02732, 'Conservation of mass for solutions of Leibenson's equation on Riemannian Manifolds'] Assume that, for some $x_0\in M$ and all large enough $r>0$, \begin{equation}V(x_0, r)\leq Cr^{N},\end{equation} where $C, N$ are positive constants.

body:
[Theorem theo.generalcluster of arXiv:2411.19145, 'On the intersection of critical percolation clusters and other tree-like random graphs'] Assume that $\mathcal G$ satisfies the BK inequality and (equation Halpha of the paper), for some $\alpha\in (d/2,d)$. Let $(\mathcal C_0^i)_{i\ge 1}$ be independent copies of the connected component of $0$ in $\mathcal G$. 
\begin{itemize}
\item[$(i)$] If $\alpha \in (\frac{(k+1)d}{2k},\frac{kd}{2(k-1)})$, for some $k\ge 2$, then there exists $\kappa>0$, such that  
$$\mathbb E\left[\exp\left(\kappa \cdot |\mathcal C_0^1 \cap \dots\cap \mathcal C_0^k|^{\frac{2\alpha}{d}-1}\right)\right]<\infty.  $$
\item[$(ii)$] If $\alpha = \tfrac{kd}{2(k-1)}$, for some $k\ge 3$, then there exists $\kappa>0$, such that for any $t>e$, 
$$\mathbb P(|\mathcal C_0^1 \cap \dots\cap \mathcal C_0^k|>t)\le \exp\Big(-\kappa (\frac t{\log t})^{\frac {2\alpha}d-1}\Big).$$
\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem theo.generalcluster of arXiv:2411.19145

body:
Let Gamma be a C^2 embedded (D-M)-dimensional manifold of local minima of a C^3 function L on R^D, with rank(Hess L(x))=M for every x in Gamma. Let U be an open neighborhood of Gamma such that gradient flow from each point in U exists for all t>=0 and converges to an endpoint Phi(x) in Gamma. Assume Phi:U->Gamma is C^2. Then for x in Gamma, D Phi(x) is the Euclidean orthogonal projection onto T_x Gamma. In particular, ker(Hess L(x))=T_x Gamma, range(Hess L(x)) is its normal space, D Phi(x) is identity on tangent vectors, and it vanishes on normal vectors. This derivative assertion is at x in Gamma; it does not say Phi agrees with the nearest-point projection away from Gamma. Source: Li, Wang and Arora, Lemma 4.3, PDF p7, proof PDF pp29--30.
Gamma is a C^2 embedded manifold of local minima of L in Euclidean R^D
L is C^3 and Hess L has constant rank equal to codimension M on Gamma
U is an open neighborhood of Gamma with globally existing convergent gradient flow
The endpoint map Phi:U->Gamma is C^2

body: Let U subset R^n be open. A function u: U -> R is harmonic if it is twice continuously differentiable on U (u in C^2(U)) and satisfies Laplace's equation Delta u = sum_{i=1}^n partial^2 u/partial x_i^2 = 0 at every point of U.
title: Harmonic Function

[Theorem intro:1-d continuum T>0:FRSB of arXiv:2605.05631, 'Wandering Exponents and the Free Energy of the High-Dimensional Elastic Polymer'] Let us assume that $(B''(x))^{-1/3}$ is strictly concave and fix $\beta,t>0$. If ((eqn:Larkin equation of the paper)) has a solution and $\mu<\mu_{Lar}(\beta;t)$ then the model is FRSB. Otherwise the model is RS. Moreover, when the model is FRSB, the Parisi pair is given by 
		\[
		\zeta_c([0,s])=\begin{cases}
			\beta^{-1}\left(\frac{4}{t}\right)^{1/3}\frac{-B'''(2(q_c-s))}{3\left(B''(2(q_c-s))\right)^{4/3}};\quad s\in [q_0,q_*)\\
			1;\quad s\in [q_*,q_c]\\
			0;\quad s\in [0,q_0)
		\end{cases},
		\]
		where $(q_0,q_*,q_c)$ is the unique triple with $0\le q_0<q_*<q_c$ which satisfies:
		\[q_c-q_*=\frac{1}{\beta\sqrt{\mu_{Lar}(\beta;t)t}},\;\;\; 2B''(2(q_c-q_0))=\sqrt{\mu^3t},\;\; -B'(2(q_c-q_0))=\frac{q_0}{\mu^3t}. \] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem intro:1-d continuum T>0:FRSB of arXiv:2605.05631

Own-work draft; proof (unaudited). CLASSICAL METHOD, own presentation; proof (unaudited), not a novelty claim. Let B be an invertible real dxd matrix,K=B*(c+closed Euclidean ball of radius r),r>=0,contained in an open differentiability domain. Let F_theta be C1 there for every admissible parameter theta. Suppose Z encloses every B^-1 F_theta(Bc),an exact new center c_new has distance at most e from every point of Z,and ||B^-1 DF_theta(y)B||2<=q for all y in K and all admissible theta. Then every x in K satisfies ||B^-1 F_theta(x)-c_new||2<=q*r+e. For a real matrix C,one may certify its Euclidean operator norm by ||C||2^2<=max_i sum_j |(C^T C)_ij|. Outward-rounded interval bounds on the derivative and central image therefore give r_next=up(q*r+e),including midpoint rounding. The domain test and invertibility must be verified; a floating-point center alone gives no error bound.

[Proposition prop:5 of arXiv:2510.13572, 'Coalescence in Markov chains'] We have $\mathbb{Q}(\mathcal{P}(\mathcal G))=0$ in the following two cases.
\begin{letlist}
\item
Let $i,j\in S$ and $\mathcal G=\mathcal G_{i,j} =\{f\in \mathcal{F}_S:f(i)\ne j\}$.

\item
Let $i_1, i_2, j_1,j_2\in S$ satisfy $i_1\ne i_2$, and let $\mathcal G$ be the set of all $f\in\mathcal F_S$ such that 
\[
f(i_1)=j_1 \quad\text{if and only if}\quad f(i_2)=j_2.
\]
\end{letlist} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition prop:5 of arXiv:2510.13572

body: A space is a Baire space if every countable intersection of dense open sets is dense. Baire category theorem: every complete (pseudo)metric space - hence every Banach space - is a Baire space, and so is every locally compact Hausdorff space. It underlies the uniform boundedness principle, the open mapping theorem, and the closed graph theorem.
title: Baire category theorem

ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Brown-measure universality beyond complex entry densities structural calculation Result: Every one-matrix holomorphic polynomial is already reducible to the circular law. If X_N has a circular-law limit and P is a fixed complex polynomial, spectral mapping gives mu_(P(X_N))=P_pushforward(mu_(X_N)) exactly, including algebraic multiplicities. The continuous mapping theorem therefore yields the pushforward of the circular law. The Brown measure of P(c) is the same pushforward, by factorizing P(z)-lambda and using multiplicativity of the Fuglede-Kadison determinant. Check: For each test function h bounded and continuous, h composed with P is bounded and continuous, so weak convergence passes through P. At the logarithmic-potential level, P(c)-lambda factors into commuting(c-root_j) terms, and determinant multiplicativity gives the same transformed Brown measure. Existing real-Gaussian and Bernoulli circular laws supply the initial one-matrix convergence. Obstruction: For several noncommuting input matrices there is no joint eigenvalue spectral mapping. Arithmetic and structural dependence in least-singular-value estimates remain unresolved here.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-p0192-brown-measure-universality-beyond-complex-entry-densities

[Lemma lem:FinalLB-underbackoff of arXiv:2602.21315, 'The Instability of all Backoff Protocols\thanks{For the purpose of Open Access, the author'] Fix $\lambda \in (0,1/3)$. Let $\overline{p}$ be a send sequence with $p_0=1$ such that, for all positive integers~$x$, $W_x \le (6/\lambda)^x$. 
Let $i$ be a sufficiently large integer and suppose that bin~$i$ is a bottleneck. 
Let $U = (U^A,U^B,U^C)$ be the under-backoff process with birth rate~$3\lambda$ and send sequence~$\overline{p}$.
Let $T = i \lceil  \exp((\log i)^{2/3} ) \rceil$.
Then 
with probability at least 
$W_i^{-1/3}  $,
for all $t\in [T]$, 
$\mathbf{s}^{U^A}(t)$ and $\mathbf{s}^{U^B}(t)$ are both non-empty.

\]

[Lemma G-Top*-tensored of arXiv:2608.28504, 'Global $\bm\infty$-categories and global Thom spectra'] The levelwise smash product $\textbf{\textup{$\bm G$-Top}}_*\times\cat{$\bm G$-$\textbf{\textup{L}}$-Top}_*\to \cat{$\bm G$-$\textbf{\textup{L}}$-Top}_*$ is a left Quillen bifunctor for the $\mathchoice{\hbox{\hfuzz=20pt\hbox{$\mathcal A\kern-.3pt$}\setbox0=\hbox{$\ell\kern-.75pt\ell$}\hbox to 0pt{\hfuzz=8pt\kern-.075pt\unhcopy0}\hbox to 0pt{\hfuzz=8pt\kern.075pt\unhcopy0}\box0\kern.05pt}}{\hbox{\hfuzz=20pt\hbox{$\mathcal A\kern-.3pt$}\setbox0=\hbox{$\ell\kern-.75pt\ell$}\hbox to 0pt{\hfuzz=8pt\kern-.075pt\unhcopy0}\hbox to 0pt{\hfuzz=8pt\kern.075pt\unhcopy0}\box0\kern.05pt}}{{\mathcal{A}}\kern-.3pt\ell\kern-.6pt\ell}{{\mathcal{A}}\kern-.3pt\ell\kern-.6pt\ell}$-model structure on $\textbf{\textup{$\bm G$-Top}}_*$ and the $G$-global model structure on $\cat{$\bm G$-$\textbf{\textup{L}}$-Top}_*$.
    \begin{proof}
        Adjoining over, we may equivalently show that the cotensoring over $\textbf{\textup{$\bm G$-Top}}$ is a right Quillen bifunctor, which can be checked after forgetting the basepoint. Adjoining back, it therefore suffices to prove that the cartesian product $\textbf{\textup{$\bm G$-Top}}\times\cat{$\bm G$-$\textbf{\textup{L}}$-Top}\to \cat{$\bm G$-$\textbf{\textup{L}}$-Top}$ is a left Quillen bifunctor. 
        
        For the pushout-product axiom for cofibrations, it then suffices to treat the case of the generating cofibrations, which by the same reasoning as before reduces to showing that $X\coloneqq G/K\times\textbf{\textup{L}}(V,-)\times_\varphi G$ is a cofibrant orthogonal $G$-space for every closed subgroup $K\subset G$, any homomorphism $\varphi\colon H\to G$, and any faithful $H$-representation $V$. However, if we write $i\colon K\to G$ for the inclusion, then $X$ is isomorphic to $i_!i^*(\textbf{\textup{L}}(V,-)\times_\varphi G)$, so the claim follows as both $i_!$ and $i^*$ are left Quillen by Lemmas~(lemma:restr-inj-left-Quillen of the paper) and~(lemma:restr-right-Quillen of the paper). With this established, the pushout product for acyclic cofibrations is then an instance of [barrero2021]*{Corollary~A.10}.
    \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition 20 of arXiv:2608.17449, 'Spectral Simplicity and Joint Eigenvalue Densities\\ for a Non-Gaussian Brownian Time Chan'] Let $f_1,\ldots,f_N\in\mathcal T$ and
\[
 d\mu_t=e^{\gamma\sum_{j=1}^Nt_jf_j}\,d\mu,
 \qquad t\in\R^N.
\]
Write $\mathbf e_j$ for the $j$th coordinate vector of $\R^N$.  Then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textnormal{(\roman*)}]
\item For every $n\ge1$,
\[
 \R^N\ni t\longmapsto\Lambda_n^{\mu_t}
\]
is continuous.
\item For $t_0\in\R^N$, let $\Lambda$ be an eigenvalue of
$A_{\mu_{t_0}}$ of multiplicity $r$.  For each $1\le j\le N$, there are
real-analytic branches $\lambda_1^{(j)},\ldots,\lambda_r^{(j)}$ of
$A_{\mu_{t_0+s\mathbf e_j}}$ through $\Lambda$ such that
\begin{equation*}
 \lambda_a^{(j)}(0)=\Lambda,
 \qquad 1\le a\le r.
\end{equation*}
The $r$ numbers $(\lambda_a^{(j)})'(0)$ are precisely the eigenvalues of
$B_{f_j}^\Lambda(\mu_{t_0})$, each repeated according to its multiplicity.
If
$\phi_1,\ldots,\phi_r$ is a real $L^2(\mu_{t_0})$-orthonormal basis of
$E_{\mu_{t_0}}(\Lambda)$, then
\begin{equation}
 \left\langle
 B_{f_j}^\Lambda(\mu_{t_0})\phi_a,\phi_c
 \right\rangle_{L^2(\mu_{t_0})}
 =-\gamma\Lambda\int_D f_j\phi_a\phi_c\,d\mu_{t_0},
 \qquad 1\le a,c\le r.
 
\end{equation}
\end{enumerate}

[Lemma 18 (Tail flow from general initial data) of arXiv:2608.10992, '2608.10992'] Let $\mu$ be a probability law on $\N$. There exists a unique family
$q^\mu=(q_k^\mu)_{k\geq1}$ such that $q_1^\mu\equiv1$,
$q_k^\mu\in C^1([0,\infty))$ for $k\geq2$,
$q_k^\mu(0)=\mu([k,\infty))$, and
\begin{equation}

        (q_k^\mu)'
        =
        \sum_{u=1}^{k-1}q_u^\mu
        (q_{k-u}^\mu-q_k^\mu)
        +q_k^\mu(1-q_k^\mu),
        \qquad k\geq2.
\end{equation}
For every $t\geq0$,
\[
        1=q_1^\mu(t)\geq q_2^\mu(t)\geq\cdots\geq0,
\]
and each $q_k^\mu$ is non-decreasing in $t$. Consequently,
$q^\mu(t)$ is the tail of a unique probability law $\mu_t$ on
$\N\cup\{\infty\}$, with
\[
        \mu_t(\{\infty\})
        =
        q_\infty^\mu(t)
        :=
        \lim_{k\to\infty}q_k^\mu(t),
\]
and $(\mu_t)_{t\geq0}$ is non-decreasing in stochastic order.

Cards are drawn from the bottom of the deck and placed on a shelf uniformly at random. body:
[Lemma lem:riesz of arXiv:2608.29403, 'Kac's Walk on Rotation Matrices Mixes in $\boldsymbol{\Theta(n^2)}$ Steps:\\ A Proof Disco'] The following statements hold not only for the right regular action on
$\mathcal H$ but for every finite-dimensional unitary
$\mathrm{SO}(n)$-module: in that formulation $P_i$ is the orthogonal
average of the circle $\pi(R_i(\theta))$, and the definitions above use
$N^{-1/2}\pi(R_i(\theta))$ in place of $\mathscr T$.
On the orthogonal complement of the $\mathcal K$-invariant functions,
with $(I-\mathcal K)^\dagger$ denoting the Moore--Penrose inverse,
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \|\mathscr D(I-\mathcal K)^\dagger\mathscr D^*\|&\le1,\\
 \|\mathscr G(I-\mathcal K)^\dagger\mathscr G^*\|&\le2.
\end{aligned}
\tag{3.2.3}
\]
On functions of circle Fourier degree at most $d$,
\[
 \|\mathscr L(I-\mathcal K)^\dagger\mathscr L^*\|\le d^2.
\tag{3.2.4}
\]
The mixed blocks satisfy
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \|\mathscr D(I-\mathcal K)^\dagger\mathscr G^*\|&\le\sqrt2,
 &\|\mathscr G(I-\mathcal K)^\dagger\mathscr D^*\|&\le\sqrt2,\\
 \|\mathscr L(I-\mathcal K)^\dagger\mathscr D^*\|&\le d,
 &\|\mathscr D(I-\mathcal K)^\dagger\mathscr L^*\|&\le d,\\
 \|\mathscr L(I-\mathcal K)^\dagger\mathscr G^*\|&\le\sqrt2\,d,
 &\|\mathscr G(I-\mathcal K)^\dagger\mathscr L^*\|&\le\sqrt2\,d.
\end{aligned}
\tag{3.2.4a}
\]
All these bounds remain true after tensoring by $I_V$.  They also hold,
with the same constants, when $(I-\mathcal K)^\dagger$ is replaced
everywhere by a finite Green kernel
$R_s=\sum_{\ell=0}^s\mathcal K^\ell$ acting between centered channels.

A second independent reading (a Codex model) was still in progress on 14 October. Not refereed.

body: [Definition def:standard complex of arXiv:2608.29986, 'Khovanov-Rozansky homology over $\F[U,V]$'] Let $n \in 2\ensuremath{\mathbb{N}} _0$ and let $a_1, \dots, a_n$ be a sequence of nonzero integers. The \emph{standard complex} $C(a_1, \dots, a_n)$ is a free chain complex over $\mathcal{R}_1$ with a distinguished basis $B=\{x_{0}, \dots, x_n\}$ and a differential $\partial$ defined as follows. For each odd $i$, there is a horizontal arrow of length $|a_i|$ connecting $x_i$ and $x_{i-1}$. For each even $i$, there is a vertical arrow of length $|a_i|$ connecting $x_i$ and $x_{i-1}$. The direction of the arrow is determined by the sign of $a_i$, as follows. If $a_i > 0$, then the arrow goes from $x_i$ to $x_{i-1}$, and if $a_i < 0$, then the arrow goes from $x_{i-1}$ to $x_i$. The $\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}} \oplus\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}} \oplus\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}} $ grading on $C(a_1, \dots, a_n)$ is uniquely determined by the condition $\mathrm{gr}(x_0)=(0, 0, 0)$ and that $\mathrm{gr}(\partial) = (-1, -1, -2)$.
title: Definition def:standard complex of arXiv:2608.29986

[Theorem thm:mfl-decay-centered-moment of arXiv:2605.20697, 'Uniform-in-time propagation of chaos for \\ Second-Order Consensus-Based Optimization'] Let \(p\geqslant2\). Suppose that \(f\) satisfies (assumption:bounded of the paper) and that
\(\overline\rho_0\in\mathcal P_p(\mathbf R^{2d})\). Assume
(assump:admissibility,assump:centered-decay of the paper) for this value of \(p\). Then there
exists a finite constant \(C_p>0\), independent of \(t\), such that
\begin{equation}
    \mathbf{E}\left[
        |\overline X_t-m_{\overline X}(\overline\rho_t)|^p
        +
        |\overline V_t-m_{\overline V}(\overline\rho_t)|^p
    \right]
    \leqslant
    C_p e^{-\lambda_{p}t}
    \mathbf{E}\left[
        |\overline X_0-m_{\overline X}(\overline\rho_0)|^p
        +
        |\overline V_0-m_{\overline V}(\overline\rho_0)|^p
    \right].
\end{equation}

body:
[Corollary cor:conjugacy-poc-transfer of arXiv:2607.00149, '\bf Uniform-in-time Propagation-of-Chaos for\\ Stein Variational Gradient Descent'] Let $(\widetilde\pi,\widetilde K)$ be a finite-rank base pair with Stein
feature vector $\widetilde F$, and let $(\pi_H,K_H)$ be any conjugate pair
constructed from a diffeomorphism $H$ as in (equation eq:potential-transform of the paper)
and (equation eq:kernel-transform of the paper).  Denote its Stein feature vector by $F_H$.

Fix an initial law $\widetilde\mu_0$ for the base system, and define the conjugate initial law \( \mu_0^H := H_{\#}\widetilde\mu_0 . \) Let $(\widetilde\mu_t)_{t\ge0}$ be the base mean-field solution started from $\widetilde\mu_0$, and let $(\mu_t^H)_{t\ge0}$ be the transformed mean-field solution started from $\mu_0^H$. Let \( \widetilde X_1(0),\ldots,\widetilde X_N(0) \quad\text{be i.i.d. with law }\widetilde\mu_0, \) and define the transformed initial particles by \( X_i^H(0):=H(\widetilde X_i(0)), \, i=1,\ldots,N. \) Let $\widetilde\mu_t^N$ and $\mu_t^{H,N}$ denote the corresponding empirical particle solutions.

Then, for every $t\ge0$,
\begin{equation}
        d_{F_H}(\mu_t^{H,N},\mu_t^H)
        =
        d_{\widetilde F}(\widetilde\mu_t^N,\widetilde\mu_t).
\end{equation}
Consequently, any propagation-of-chaos estimate for the base pair in the
restricted feature metric transfers to every conjugate pair with the same rate
and the same constant.  In particular, if for some rate $\varepsilon_N\to0$,
\[   
        \mathbb E\left[\sup_{t\ge0}\, d_{\widetilde F}^2(\widetilde\mu_t^N,\widetilde\mu_t)\right]
        \le C\varepsilon_N,
\]
then
\begin{equation}
        \mathbb E\left[\sup_{t\ge0}\, d_{F_H}^2(\mu_t^{H,N},\mu_t^H)\right]
        \le C\varepsilon_N .
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Transfer of feature-level POC rates within a conjugacy class

body:
[Lemma 7 (Wedge expansion) of arXiv:2609.03466, 'Least-Favorable Location for Binomial Top-$t$ Selection'] At $p=\pc$, the wedge rate and its derivative are given by
\begin{gather}
 \Kn:=I_H(\pc)
 =-3\log\left(\frac{\taud}{1-\taud+\taud^2}\right),
 \\
 \kappa_\delta:=I_H'(\pc)
 =\frac{(1-\taud)^3(1+\taud)(1-\taud+\taud^2)}{\taud^3}>0.
 
\end{gather}
On some neighborhood $U$ of $\pc$, the high-centered wedge probability has the strong expansion
\begin{equation}
 H_n(p)=n^{-1}e^{-nI_H(p)}\{A_2(p)+o_{C^2(U)}(1)\}.
 
\end{equation}
Here $A_2(p)$ is smooth and positive. In particular,
\begin{align}
 H_n(\pc)
 &=A_{2,\delta}n^{-1}e^{-n\Kn}\{1+o(1)\},
 \notag\\
 H_n'(\pc)
 &=-\kappa_\delta A_{2,\delta}e^{-n\Kn}\{1+o(1)\},
 \\
 L_n(\pc)&=H_n(\pc),
 \qquad
 L_n'(\pc)=-H_n'(\pc),
 
\end{align}
where
\begin{equation*}
 A_{2,\delta}:=A_2(\pc)
 =\frac{1+\taud^2+\taud^4}
 {6\pi\sqrt3\,\taud(1-\taud)^2}.
\end{equation*}
Moreover, uniformly for $|p-\pc|\le n^{-1}$,
\begin{equation}
 |H_n''(p)|+|L_n''(p)|=O(ne^{-n\Kn}).
 
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Wedge expansion

         \item After time step $m$, the weighted sum of squares of the differences in the number of nodes connecting to $A_{K_j}^{i}(m)$ in each of the two trees satisfies the bound
        \[
        \frac{1}{\ell + 1} \sum_{j=0}^{\ell} \frac{1}{K_j} \bbbclr{  \sum_{k=m+1}^{n} \mathbbm{1}_{ \left\{ X_k^{1} \in A_{K_j}^{1}(m) \right\} }  - \sum_{k=m+1}^{n} \mathbbm{1}_{ \left\{ X_k^{2} \in A_{K_j}^{2}(m) \right\} } }^2 < C\log(n),
       \]
       for some fixed  $C>0$.
    \end{enumerate}
    Then
    \ba{
        \frac{1}{(\ell + 1)\log(n)} \sum_{j=0}^{\ell} \frac{1}{K_j} &\bbbclr{ \sum_{x \in A_{K_j}^{1}(n)} \deg_{T_n^{1}}(x) -  \sum_{x \in A_{K_j}^{2}(n)} \deg_{T_n^{2}}(x)  }^2 \\
         &< C  + \frac{1}{(\ell + 1)\log(n)} \sum_{j=0}^{\ell} \frac{2(m+1) \log(n)^{2/3} + (m+1)^2}{K_j}. 
    } (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Let H = (L, R, E) be a finite bipartite graph and take the network with a source s, a sink t, arcs s->u of capacity 1 for u in L, arcs u->v for each edge uv, and arcs v->t of capacity 1 for v in R, every middle arc u->v of capacity M = |L| + 1. For a minimum s-t cut with source side S, put X = S n L and Y = S n R; then Y = N(X) and the cut has capacity |L| - |X| + |N(X)|. Conversely, for every X in L of maximal deficiency |X| - |N(X)|, the set {s} u X u N(X) is a minimum cut. So the minimum cut value is |L| - max over X in L of (|X| - |N(X)|). The strict inequality M > |L| is needed: with one edge and M = |L| = 1, the cut {s, u} is minimum and crosses the middle edge.

Author-derived obstruction pending w539: for finite N>=2 and s>0, a Riesz pair energy plus a C^2 external/background term near an interior point has a transverse second derivative -s epsilon^(-s-2)+O(1) when one pair approaches distance epsilon and other particles stay a positive distance away. It is negative for small epsilon, so no positive pointwise global Hessian lower bound holds on the full finite-particle configuration space. This does not analyze a renormalized infinite-volume Hessian or the Hessian restricted near a fixed crystal. A controlled-region/complement argument or a nonconvex inequality is required instead.
Finite N>=2
s>0
Interior near-collision pair
Other particles a fixed positive distance away
External/background potential C^2 with bounded Hessian nearby

$$P=[v_1,\ldots,v_N]\quad,\quad

and respectively called passage matrix, and diagonal form of $A$.

\begin{enumerate}[(i)]	
\item
The admissible endpoint for $q_g$ is
	\[
	\bar c=\frac{r+1}{r+2x}.
	\]

\item
The coefficients of $q_g$ satisfy 
	\[
	\alpha(g)=(r+2x)m(g)T_{33}(U_g),
	\qquad
	\beta(g)=-2m(g)B(g),
	\qquad
	\gamma(g)=V_{32}(U_g),
	\]
	where
	\[
	\begin{aligned}
		B(g)={}&-(r^2+rx-r-2x)\\
		&+g\bigl(yr^2+yrx-2yr-3yx-y-r^2-rx+x\bigr).
	\end{aligned}
	\]
	
\item	
	The vertex-location expression satisfies
	\[
	2\alpha(g)\bar c+\beta(g)
	=2m(g)\bigl(T_{31}(U_g)+1\bigr).
	\]
	
	
\item	
The reduced discriminant factor from
	Lemma~\ref{lem:Frydman-discriminant-factorization} is
	\[
	\widetilde H_{23}(U_g)=4\Theta(g),
	\]
	where
	\[
	\Theta(g)=h_2g^2+h_1g+x^2(r-2).
	\]
	Here
	\[
	h_2=-(r+2x)T_{21}(U)>0,
	\]
	and the explicit formula for $h_1$, together with the remaining
	polynomial identities used below, is recorded in
	Appendix~\ref{app:X23-Frydman-formulas}.
\end{enumerate}

Let S be a separable metric space, and let \mu_n, \mu be Borel probability measures on S such that \mu_n \Rightarrow \mu weakly. Then there exists a single probability space (\Omega, \mathcal{F}, \mathbb{P}) and S-valued random variables X_n, X defined on \Omega such that the law of X_n is \mu_n for all n, the law of X is \mu, and X_n(\omega) \to X(\omega) as n \to \infty for \mathbb{P}-almost every \omega \in \Omega.

body:
[Defi 13 of arXiv:2608.28148, 'Flows and homotopies of Banach Lie algebroids'] An \emph{almost Lie bracket} on an anchored bundle $\left(A,\pi, M,\rho\right)$ is a sheaf of antisymmetric bilinear maps
\[
\LB_{A_U} \colon \Gamma\left( A_{U}\right)  \times\Gamma\left(  A_{U}\right)
\to\Gamma\left(  A_U\right), U\subseteq M \text{open}
\]
which satisfies the following properties
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\textbf{AL \arabic*})]
\item  the Leibniz identity:
\[
\forall\left(   \mathfrak{u}_{1}, \mathfrak{u}_{2}\right)  \in \Gamma \left(A_{U} \right)  ^{2}, \forall f \in C^{\infty}(U)
,\ \LB[\mathfrak{u}_{1},f \mathfrak{u}_{2}]_{A_{U}}=f.\LB[\mathfrak{u}_{1}, \mathfrak{u}_{2}]_{A_{U}}+df(\rho( \mathfrak{u}_{1})). \mathfrak{u}_{2}.
\]
\item For any  open set $U\subseteq M$ and any $(\mathfrak{u}_1,\mathfrak{u}_2) \in \Gamma(A_{U})^2$, the maps
\[
\mathfrak{u}_1,\mapsto \LB[\mathfrak{u}_1,\mathfrak{u}_2]_{A_{U}} \textrm{ and } \mathfrak{u}_2,\mapsto \LB[\mathfrak{u}_1,\mathfrak{u}_2]_{A_{U}}
\]
only depend on the $1$-jets of $\mathfrak{u}_1$ and $\mathfrak{u}_2$, respectively.
\end{enumerate}
By abuse of notation, such a sheaf of almost Lie brackets will be denoted $\LB_A$. The quintuple $(A,\pi, M,\rho,\LB_A)$ is called an \emph{almost algebroid}.
title: Definition 13 of arXiv:2608.28148

body:
At the regular 24-cell (vertices the 24 permutations of (+-1,+-1,0,0); facets a.x = 1 with a = +-e_i or a = (+-1/2,+-1/2,+-1/2,+-1/2)), the 144 vertex-facet incidence equations a_j.v_i = 1 in the 192 coordinates of the 24 vertices and 24 facet normals have rank 140: four of them are dependent at this point. The Zariski tangent space of the realization space therefore has dimension 52, against the expected dimension 48 (28 against 24 after quotienting by the 24-dimensional projective group), so a first-order count cannot certify the local dimension. This is why Brysiewicz and Sinn (arXiv:2609.02818) use a second-order (quadratic obstruction) test; the local dimension they certify is the expected one, 48, so the regular 24-cell is not locally projectively rigid.

Assumes: realization space in vertex and facet-normal coordinates, facets normalised as a.x = 1 (the origin is interior)

[Def frame bundle of arXiv:2609.04023, 'Characterizing Contractions and Weighted Blowdowns'] Let $\mathcal{Y} \to \mathcal{Z}$ be a degree $d$ finite \'etale morphism of smooth separated Deligne--Mumford stacks. 
Then, the {\em frame bundle} $\underline{\mathrm{Isom}}_{\mathcal{Z}}(\mathcal{Z}^{\sqcup \, d}, \mathcal{Y}) \to \mathcal{Z}$ defined as follows: suppose $T \to \mathcal{Z}$ is an \'etale morphism where $T$ is a complex scheme, then
\[
\underline{\mathrm{Isom}}_{\mathcal{Z}}(\mathcal{Z}^{\sqcup \, d}, \mathcal{Y})(T) := \underline{\mathrm{Isom}}_T(T^{\sqcup \, d}, \mathcal{Y} \times_{\mathcal{Z}} T)
\]
where $\underline{\mathrm{Isom}}_T(T^{\sqcup \, d}, \mathcal{Y} \times_{\mathcal{Z}} T)$ is the usual Isom scheme (see [SGA2]).
The frame bundle naturally defines a principal $S_d$-bundle induced by the canonical left action of $S_d$ on $\mathcal{Z}^{\sqcup \, d}.$

body: [Definition of arXiv:2609.03988, 'A $p$-summability approach to the weak maximizing property'] Let $1 \leq p < \infty$. A pair of Banach spaces $(X, Y)$ is said to have the \textbf{weakly $p$-singular maximizing property} ($\mathrm{SMP}_p$, for short) if every bounded linear operator $T: X \to Y$ which admits a weakly $p$-singular maximizing sequence is norm-attaining.

body:
[Proposition nest of arXiv:2608.07236, 'Negative association of Busemann functions \\in exponential last-passage percolation'] Fix $k<m<n$.
For any vertices $\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{y}$ above or along level $n$, we have 
\begin{align} 
G^{\textup{S}}_{m, \mathbf{x}}(h) - G^{\textup{S}}_{m, \mathbf{y}}(h) = G^{\textup{S}}_{n, \mathbf{x}}(\sigma^{n-1}\cdots\sigma^m h) - G^{\textup{S}}_{n, \mathbf{y}}(\sigma^{n-1}\cdots\sigma^m h).
\end{align}
Similarly, for any vertices $\mathbf{a}, \mathbf{b}$ below or along level $k$, we have 
$$G^{\textup{N}}_{\mathbf{a}, m}(h) - G^{\textup{N}}_{\mathbf{b}, m}(h) = G^{\textup{N}}_{\mathbf{a}, k}(\sigma_{k}\cdots\sigma_{m-1} h) - G^{\textup{N}}_{\mathbf{b}, k}(\sigma_{k}\cdots\sigma_{m-1} h).$$
title: Nested LPP property

$.

        \item The operator $D$ is self-adjoint and is positive in the Hilbert space sense.

        \item Both $H_{\mathrm{even}}$ and $H_{\mathrm{odd}}$ reduce $D$, and one has $Dq_n = nq_n$ for all $n \in \mathbb{N}$.
    \end{enumerate}

Own-work draft; proof (unaudited). Uniform-origin stationarization of iid fixed-length finite-alphabet blocks is either iid (the block law is a product of identical marginals) or has rho(n)=1 for every lag. Random-length, dependent-block and hierarchical encodings not excluded. Concatenate a bi-infinite iid family of blocks with law P on S^L at fixed boundaries, then translate by an independent uniform phase in {0,...,L-1}. Distinct translated laws are separated by some finite-cylinder probability; its two directional length-L sampled empirical frequencies yield a shared tail statistic. The statement does not cover random-length or dependent blocks.

body:
[Definition 6 of arXiv:2609.00702, 'On the Set-Valued Katugampola Fractional Integral: Properties and Regular Selections'] Let $F$ be a compact set-valued function such that $F:I\rightrightarrows \mathbb{R}$ and for each $u\in [a,b]$, $F(u)$ is compact. For any partition $\mathcal{T}=\{t_0,t_1,t_2,\ldots t_n\}\subset I= [a,b]$ and $n\in \mathbb{N},$ the total Jordan variation of $ F$ is
    \[ V_a^b(F)=\sup_{\mathcal{T}} \sum_{i=1}^nH_d(F(t_i),F(t_{i-1})), \]
    with the supremum over all partitions $\mathcal{T}$ of $I.$ If $V_a^b(F)< \infty,$ then we say that $F$ is of bounded variation on $I.$ 

 \begin{definition}
     A set valued map $F:I\to \mathbb{R}$ is said to be Lipschitz on $I$ with respect to $H_d$ if there exists a constant $C_F>0$ such that 
     \[ H_d(F(t_1),F(t_2)) \le C_F|t_1-t_2| \text{ for all } t_1,t_2 \in I \] 
     and such a constant $C_F$ is called the Lipschitz constant of $F.$

body:
[Corollary 10 (Positive definiteness of the Mellin quotient) of arXiv:2606.18458, 'Stable size-biasing and the positive scale-mixture order of generalized Gaussian laws'] For $p,q>0$, the function
\[
\Phi_{p,q}(t)=\frac{2^{it/p}\Gamma((1+it)/p)\Gamma(1/q)}{2^{it/q}\Gamma((1+it)/q)\Gamma(1/p)}
\]
is a characteristic function if and only if $p\le q$. If $p<q$, then $\Phi_{p,q}$ is the characteristic function of
\[
\log V_{p,q}=\left(\frac{1}{p}-\frac{1}{q}\right)\log 2+\log W,
\qquad
W=\left(S_{p/q}^{-1/q}\right)^*,
\]
where the star denotes ordinary size-biasing of the positive random variable $S_{p/q}^{-1/q}$. If $p=q$, then $\Phi_{p,p}\equiv1$.

\end{align}

[Lemma 14 (Consistency and rate for \textup{($ii$)}) of arXiv:2608.29465, 'Deciding When to Decide:\\Testing Operational Suboptimality Under Distributional Shift'] Suppose the assumptions of Lemma~\ref{lem:termI_consistency} hold, specifically that the envelope $F(X)$ and the Lipschitz modulus $L(X)$ are square-integrable under the target distribution $\mathbb{P}_1$.
\begin{equation}

|\textup{($ii$)}|
=\Big|
\min_{z\in\mathcal Z}
\rho^{\mathbb P_1}\!\big(f(z;X,\hat\theta)\big)
-
\rho^{\mathbb P_1}\!\big(f(\hat z_1;X,\hat\theta)\big)
\Big| \leq 2\,\sup_{\theta\in\Theta}\sup_{z\in\mathcal Z}\big|\rho^{\widehat{\mathbb P}_1'}\!\big(f(z;X,\theta)\big) - \rho^{\mathbb P_1}\!\big(f(z;X,\theta)\big)\big|
=O_p(\varepsilon_{m'}).
\end{equation}
In particular, if $\varepsilon_{m'}\to 0$ then $\textup{($ii$)}\xrightarrow{p}0$, and if $\varepsilon_{m'}\asymp (m')^{-1/2}$ then $|\textup{($ii$)}|=O_p((m')^{-1/2})$.
title: Consistency and rate for \textup{($ii$)}

body:
[Lemma 35 (Double-hive KL bound using a shared large-gap side) of arXiv:2607.04138, 'Hives from deformed GUE minor processes'] \lab{lem:doubleKLhive}
Let \(w,w'>0\) and \(u,u'\geq 0\). Let \(G_n,\widetilde G_n,G'_n,\widetilde G'_n\) be independent GUE
matrices, and set
\[
D_n=\operatorname{diag}(\operatorname{spec}(\widetilde G_n)),
\qquad
D'_n=\operatorname{diag}(\operatorname{spec}(\widetilde G'_n)).
\]
Let
\[
X_n=\sqrt n\,(wG_n+uD_n),
\qquad
Y_n=\sqrt n\,(w'G'_n+u'D'_n),
\]
and put
\[
a^2=w^2+u^2,\qquad b^2=(w')^2+(u')^2.
\]
Assume
\[
\frac{u}{w^2}=\frac{u'}{(w')^2}.
\]
Let
\[
\lambda_n=\operatorname{spec}(X_n),
\qquad
\mu_n=\operatorname{spec}(Y_n).
\]
Let \(L_n\) be the corrected regularized large-gap side from
\eqref{eq:corrected-large-gap}, and set
\[
N_n=L_n+\operatorname{diag}(X_n),
\qquad
P_n=L_n - \operatorname{diag}(Y_n).
\]
Let
\[
h_n^{(1)}\in H_n(\lambda_n,L_n;N_n),
\qquad
h_n^{(2)}\in H_n(\mu_n,L_n;P_n)
\]
be the two hives obtained, via Proposition~\ref{gt-rem}(iv), from the
large-gap construction applied to the two deformed minor processes arising from
$X_n$ and $Y_n$ respectively.  Paste them along the common side \(L_n\), with
the exterior sides in clockwise cyclic order
\[
\lambda_n,\qquad \mu_n,\qquad P_n,\qquad N_n.
\]
\begin{center}
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.9, every node/.style={font=\small}]
  \coordinate (L) at (0,0);
  \coordinate (T) at (2,2);
  \coordinate (R) at (4,0);
  \coordinate (B) at (2,-2);
  \draw[thick] (L) -- (T) -- (R) -- (B) -- cycle;
  \draw[thick] (L) -- (R);
  \node[below left] at (1,-1) {\(\lambda_n\)};
  \node[above left] at (1,1) {\(\mu_n\)};
  \node[above right] at (3,1) {\(P_n\)};
  \node[below right] at (3,-1) {\(N_n\)};
  \node[above] at (2,0) {\(L_n\)};
\end{tikzpicture}
\end{center}
Decorate these four exterior sides, with
independent uniform Gelfand--Tsetlin patterns.  Let \(q_n^{\mathrm{dbl}}\)
be the resulting density on the four-boundary double-hive cone \(\mathbb D^4\).

Let \(p_n^{\mathrm{dbl}}\) be the maximum-entropy density on \(\mathbb D^4\)
whose four exterior sides, in clockwise cyclic order, have the same expected
quadratic moments as
\[
\lambda_n,\qquad \mu_n,\qquad P_n,\qquad N_n .
\]
Then
\[
D_{\mathrm{KL}}\!\left(q_n^{\mathrm{dbl}}\Vert p_n^{\mathrm{dbl}}\right)
=O(n\log n).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Double-hive KL bound using a shared large-gap side

body:
Let A be the infinitesimal generator of a strongly continuous (C_0) semigroup on a Banach space. Then the semigroup is UNIQUELY determined by A: if (S(t)) and (T(t)) are C_0-semigroups with the same generator then S(t) = T(t) for every t >= 0. Equivalently, the Laplace transform of the semigroup is the resolvent of A, and the resolvent determines the semigroup. The Hille-Yosida theorem says which operators are generators: A is the generator of a contraction semigroup exactly when A is densely defined and closed and every lambda > 0 lies in the resolvent set with ||(lambda I - A)^{-1}|| <= 1/lambda.
Both semigroups strongly continuous with the SAME generator including the same domain - two operators that agree on a common core but have different domains can generate different semigroups, which is precisely the non-uniqueness phenomenon for symmetric operators with several self-adjoint extensions.

[Proposition prop:gf-existence-bub of arXiv:2603.28161, 'Boundary four-point connectivities of conformal loop ensembles'] For $x_1,...,x_n\in\mathbbm{R}$, the limit
\[
\widehat{G}^\mathrm{Bub}_0(x_1,...,x_n)=\lim_{r_i\to0}\prod_{i=1}^nr_i^{-h}\cdot \mu^\mathrm{Bub}_0[\gamma\cap B(x_i,r_i)\neq\emptyset,1\le i\le n]
\]
exists and is continuous of $x_1,...,x_n$. Furthermore, for any disjoint $S_1,..,S_n\subset\mathbbm{R}$,
    \begin{equation}
        \int_{S_1\times...\times S_n}\widehat{G}^\mathrm{Bub}_0(x_1,...,x_n)\prod_{i=1}^ndx_i=C^n\mu^\mathrm{Bub}_0\left[\prod_{i=1}^n\nu_{\gamma\cap\mathbbm{R}}(S_i)\right].
    \end{equation}
Hence, $\widehat{G}^\mathrm{Bub}_0(x_1,...,x_n)=C^n G^\mathrm{Bub}_0(x_1,...,x_n)$ where $G^\mathrm{Bub}_0(x_1,...,x_n)$ is defined in~(equation eq:def-gf-bub of the paper) and $C$ is the same constant as in Proposition~(prop:equivalence of the paper). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition prop:gf-existence-bub of arXiv:2603.28161

body:
[Proposition prop: distance of arXiv:2609.00257, 'Stability estimates for the initial-to-final-state inverse problem'] Let $n\geq 2$ and $V_1, \, V_2 \in L^1((0, T); L^\infty(\mathbb{R}^n))$ with $\| V_j \|_w < \infty$, for $j\in\{1, 2\}$ and weight $w:\mathbb{R}^n \to (0, 1)$. The quantity defined in (equation eq: distance of the paper) is a distance. 

In particular, fix $R_0>0$ and for $V \in L^1((0, T); L^\infty(\mathbb{R}^n))$ with $\| V \|_w < \infty$ and $\| \mathop\mathrm{Im} {V} \|_w\leq \frac{1}{4T}$ set 

\[
\mathcal {T}_V := \{\widetilde{ V} \in  L^1((0, T); L^\infty(\mathbb{R}^n)) : \,\, \| \widetilde{V} \|_w<\infty, \, \| \mathop\mathrm{Im} \widetilde{V} \|_w \leq \frac{1}{4T} \,\,

\text{and such that} \,\, 

\| V - \widetilde{V} \|_w \leq \frac{R_0}{2} \}.
\]

Then, if $\mathcal J$ is the set of the initial-to-final-state maps corresponding to potentials in $ \mathcal T_V$, the quantity (equation eq: distance of the paper) becomes a quasi-metric on the set $\mathcal J$.

body: [Definition definition strong on of arXiv:2607.18531, 'Doubly reflected BSDEs driven by Inhomogeneous simple Lévy processes: Applications to gene'] Let $\beta >0$, $Y \in \mathcal{S}^2_{\beta}$, and $\sigma,\tau \in \mathcal{T}_{0}^T$ such that $\sigma \leq \tau$ a.s. The process $Y$ is said to be a strong $\mathcal{E}^f$-supermartingale (resp. $\mathcal{E}^f$-submartingale) on $[\sigma,\tau]$, if for all $\sigma^{\star}, \tau^{\star} \in \mathcal{T}_{0}^T$ such that $\sigma \leq \sigma^{\star} \leq \tau^{\star} \leq \tau$ a.s., we have $\mathcal{E}^f_{\sigma^{\ast},\tau^{\ast}}(Y_{\eta^{\ast}}) \leq Y_{\sigma^{\ast}}$ (resp. $\mathcal{E}^f_{\sigma^{\ast},\tau^{\ast}}(Y_{\tau^{\ast}}) \geq Y_{\sigma^{\ast}}$) a.s. Finally, the process $Y$ is said to be a strong $\mathcal{E}^f$-martingale on $[\sigma,\tau]$, if it is both a strong $\mathcal{E}^f$-supermartingale and a strong $\mathcal{E}^f$-submartingale on $[\sigma,\tau]$.
title: Strong $\mathcal{E}^f$-(sub,super)martingale

Suppose $H$ is a Hadamard matrix of order $n$ with first row $h_1=\one^\transpose$, and let $\bL$ be a family of $m$ MALS of order $n-1$.

\[

 1\leqslant r\leqslant n-1\}.

Then $\mathcal C_1,\dots,\mathcal C_n$ partition the vertex set of
$\Gamma(H;\bL)$ into cliques of size $m(n-1)$, each regular with nexus
$(n-2)+(m-1)(n/2-1)$.

    \item If $\gamma\prec\gamma_1$,
        $\gamma\prec\gamma_2$, and
        $\{\gamma,\gamma_{1},\gamma_{2}\}$ are a
        compatible set of contours, then either
        $\gamma_{1}\prec\gamma_{2}$ or $\gamma_{2}\prec\gamma_{1}$.

body:
Load-bearing hypothesis in the stability theorem: the approximating functions must be VISCOSITY sub/supersolutions and the convergence must be LOCALLY UNIFORM. Neither can be dropped. (1) Almost-everywhere solutions are not closed under uniform convergence: let u_k(x) := dist(x, (1/k)Z) on R. Then |u_k'| = 1 at every point of differentiability, 0 ≤ u_k ≤ 1/(2k), so u_k → 0 uniformly, yet the limit u ≡ 0 satisfies |u'| = 0 and solves the eikonal equation nowhere. The u_k are not viscosity solutions of |u'| - 1 = 0 (at each of their convex kinks, on (1/k)Z, the supersolution test with the touching slope p = 0 fails), which is exactly why the stability theorem does not apply. (2) The convergence hypothesis cannot be weakened to pointwise or weak-* convergence. What goes wrong in the a.e. setting is already visible in (1): Du_k = ±1 a.e. while Du_k ⇀ 0 weakly-*, and the nonlinear expression H(Du_k) does not pass to weak limits. For genuine viscosity sub/supersolutions the proof of the stability theorem uses LOCALLY UNIFORM convergence to move maximum points of u_k - φ to a maximum point of u - φ; for a family that is merely locally uniformly bounded the correct substitutes are the half-relaxed limits limsup* u_k and liminf* u_k (Barles-Perthame), which are respectively a subsolution and a supersolution but in general differ from a pointwise limit. (If the u_k are locally equi-Lipschitz, pointwise convergence already forces locally uniform convergence, so the gap between the two modes of convergence bites only in the absence of equicontinuity.) Auditor's check: any passage to the limit in a nonlinear first-order PDE that is justified only by 'u_k → u and each u_k solves the equation a.e.' is invalid.
Counterexample: sawtooth functions u_k = dist(·, (1/k)Z) for the eikonal equation |u'| = 1 on R
Viscosity stability requires locally uniform convergence of the solutions (convergence of the equations must also be locally uniform)
Half-relaxed limit techniques replace uniform convergence only when combined with semicontinuous envelopes, not with a.e. solutions
title: Pitfall: Stability under Uniform Limits Needs Viscosity Solutions, Not a.e. Solutions

[Proposition DriverSenguptaDiscrete of arXiv:2602.08591, 'The Yang--Mills measure on compact surfaces as a \\ universal scaling limit of lattice gau'] Let $M$ be a family of random variables, one for each horizontal edges with joint law
\[
\mathrm{d} \mathbb{M}_N\left(\left(M_{\theta\xrightarrow{r}\theta_+ }\right)_{\substack{\theta\in\Theta^N_-\\r\in R^N}}\right)
\coloneq \frac{1}{Z_N}\prod_{\substack{\theta\in \Theta^N_-\\r\in R^N_-}}\rho_{\sigma\left(\square\left(r,r_+,\theta,\theta_+\right)\right)}\left(M_{\theta\xrightarrow{r}\theta_+}^{-1}M_{\theta\xrightarrow{r_+}\theta_+}\right)\mathrm{d} M.
\]
Let $(U_i)_{1\le i\le 2g}$ be independent, uniformly distributed random variables in $G$, independent of $M$. 
Then $H(M,U)$ generates the same lattice gauge theory as the Driver--Sengupta measure.

[Theorem 16 of arXiv:2607.08242, 'Convergence of random sums in non-commutative probability'] Let $\{a_n\}$ be self-adjoint identically distributed  variables in an NCP $(\mathcal{A}, \varphi)$ with $\varphi(a_1)=0$ and $\varphi(a_1^2)=1$, and $\sup_{n}|\varphi(a_n^k)|<\infty$ for each $k\in\mathbb{N}$. Set $\mathcal{S}_k=a_1+\dots+a_k$, $k\in\mathbb{N}$. Let $\{N_n\}$ be positive integer-valued rvs, independent of $\{a_n\}$, such that $N_n/n\stackrel{\mathbb{P}}{\to}K>0$, a constant, as $n\rightarrow\infty$.\vskip5pt
    
    \noindent (i) If $\{a_i\}$ are free then 
    $\frac{\mathcal{S}_{N_n}}{\sqrt{N_n}}
    
    \stackrel{*}{\to} s$.

\vskip 3pt
    \noindent (ii) If $\{a_i\}$ are independent then $\frac{\mathcal{S}_{N_n}}{\sqrt{N_n}}\stackrel{*}{\to} z$. 
    \vskip3pt
    \noindent (iii) If $\{a_i\}$ are half independent then $\frac{\mathcal{S}_{N_n}}{\sqrt{N_n}}\stackrel{*}{\to} r_S$. 

   If $a_1$ has a probability measure, then the probability measures of $\frac{\mathcal{S}_{N_n}}{\sqrt{N_n}}$ in (i), (ii) and (iii) exist, and converge weakly to the probability measure of the standard 
    semi-circle, standard Gaussian and standard symmetric Rayleigh measures, respectively.

Let $x\in\mbb R^2$ and $t>0$ be fixed,

\begin{enumerate}[(1)]

\[\be_{[a,b]\times[c,d]}(Z)=\lim_{\eps\to0}\be^\eps_{[a,b]\times[c,d]}(Z)

\item If $0\leq a<b\leq t$, then

\qquad\text{in probability.}\]

body: Let (S, A) be a measurable space and mu a sigma-finite measure on it, the intensity measure. A Poisson point process with intensity mu is a random counting measure N on S (N(A) is a random element of {0, 1, 2, ...} union {infinity} for each A in A, and N is a measure for each outcome) such that (i) for every A with mu(A) < infinity, N(A) has the Poisson distribution with mean mu(A), and (ii) for pairwise disjoint A_1, ..., A_k the counts N(A_1), ..., N(A_k) are independent. Such a process exists for every sigma-finite mu (construct it on each piece of finite measure by throwing a Poisson(mu(A)) number of independent points with law mu restricted to A and normalised, then superpose the pieces). When mu has no atoms the points are almost surely distinct; when mu is a multiple of Lebesgue measure on R^d the process is homogeneous with rate equal to that multiple. Basic calculus: the mapping theorem (the image of a Poisson process under a measurable map is Poisson with the image intensity), superposition (independent Poisson processes add to a Poisson process with the summed intensity), thinning (keeping each point independently with probability p(x) gives a Poisson process with intensity p mu), and Campbell's formula E sum_{x in N} f(x) = integral f d mu.

body: [Theorem of arXiv:2606.00325, 'Ergodicity for a class of stochastic Hasegawa-Mima equations with dissipation'] Let $G : \mathbb{X} \rightarrow R$ be collection of functions which determines measures. Assume that there exists a measurable $\mathbb{X}_0 \subset \mathbb{X}$ such that for any $(u_0,v_0) \in \mathbb{X}_0 \times  \mathbb{X}_0 $ and any $\phi \in G$ there exists a $\Gamma= \Gamma(u_0, v_0, \phi) \in \tilde C(\delta_{u_0}P^\mathbb{N}, \delta_{v_0}P^\mathbb{N})$ such that $\Gamma( D_\phi)>0$. Then there exist at most one ergodic invariant measure $\mu$ for $P$ with $\mu(\mathbb{X}_0) > 0$. In particular if $\mathbb{X}_0 = \mathbb{X}$, then there exists at most one, and hence ergodic, invariant measure. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: [Definition Type path descendants of arXiv:2607.16911, 'Multipartite random graphs with given degrees: local limit, revisiting the giant, distance'] Consider any directed edge $e=(p(v),v)$ in $\mathbb T$ where $v\neq \varnothing$, with type $T(e)=(T_{p(v)},T_v)$. Let $s_0=T_{p(v)}$ and $s_1=T_v$, and for a type path $\pi=(s_0\rightarrow s_0s_1 \rightarrow \dots \rightarrow s_0s_1\dots s_k)$ in $\mathscr T(T_{p(v)})$, we inductively define a set $C(e;\pi)$ of descendants of $v$ as follows. If $k=2$ then $C(e;\pi)=\mathbf c_\mathbb T(v;s_2)$, while if $k>2$, then $$C(e;\pi)=\cup_{u\in \mathbf c_\mathbb T(v;s_2)}C((v,u);\pi^{(1)}),$$ where recall $\pi^{(1)}$ from (equation eq:def_pi_uppercut of the paper).

[Theorem 2 of arXiv:2607.29495, 'Fast Mixing for Low-Temperature Potts Models via Poisson Trees'] Let $\theta>1$ and $\kappa,K>0$ be arbitrary reals.  Then, for all large enough real $d$,  for  all integer $q\geq d^{\theta}$, for all real $\beta > (1+\frac{1.01}{\theta})\frac{\log q}{d}$, the following holds for all large~enough~$n$.

    
      Let $T$ be a Poisson tree with parameter $d$,  truncated at level~$h=\lfloor K\log_d n\rfloor$. Then, with probability $\geq 1 -n^{-\kappa}$ over  $T$,  the Glauber dynamics for the Potts distribution $\mu^{\pl}_{T^h;q,\beta}$ with monochromatic boundary condition has mixing time $\leq |V(T)|n^{o(1)}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 2 of arXiv:2607.29495

body:
Random variables X_n converge in distribution to X if and only if their characteristic functions converge pointwise, phi_{X_n}(t) -> phi_X(t) for every t. More usefully: if phi_{X_n}(t) -> psi(t) pointwise and psi is continuous at t = 0, then psi is the characteristic function of some random variable X and X_n -> X in distribution. This is the engine that turns the characteristic-function computation in the Central Limit Theorem into convergence in distribution.

Here the random variables are real-valued and phi_X(t)=E[exp(i t X)]. In the forward direction X_n converging in distribution to X implies the stronger conclusion that, for every T<infinity, sup_{|t|<=T}|phi_{X_n}(t)-phi_X(t)| tends to zero. Equivalently, for probability measures mu_n on R, weak convergence to mu gives convergence of their characteristic functions uniformly on every compact subset of R; the pointwise-convergence converse still requires continuity of the limit at 0.
for the converse, the limit function is continuous at 0

Let H and B be jointly translation-invariant disjoint binary fields on Z^d, marking holes and active sites. Use graph distance, put h=E H(0)>0, S=sum_{0<|x|<=2R}E[H(0)H(x)], T=sum_{|x|<=2R}E[H(0)B(x)], and let B_R be the graph ball of integer radius R>=1. The probability that the origin is strictly nearer a hole than an active site is at least |B_R|(h-T)_+^2/(h+S). Consequently in d=4, if h_t tends to zero, R_t=floor(b h_t^(-1/4)) for fixed b>0, S_t<=C h_t and T_t<=theta h_t eventually with C finite and theta<1, the closer-hole probability has positive liminf. {"artifact_digest":"sha256:e14d6f9533aba8111cd4fb6f84e823b67a7db654c6592746fbad34ebbd519242","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/e1/e14d6f9533aba8111cd4fb6f84e823b67a7db654c6592746fbad34ebbd519242.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:a31d174696b39217c23e18b76d86886c8a46b0b980c4086414d1bd398b3b5ce2","bundle_entry_key":"i0005-c7","bundle_id":"population.i0005-palm-reductions-and-comparisons-004","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"interacting particle systems and comparison fields","draft":"w661/bundle_004.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.particle-hole:stationary-hole-active-mixed-second-moment-covering-draft","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# I0005-C7 v1: an overlap criterion using mixed hole–active moments

Novelty: UNCHECKED. A direct first/second-moment geometric reduction, compared against the source's isolation argument and own C2. No earlier separate source found in the limited I0005 search. This does not prove its required moment estimates in the fixed-law d4 process.

Fix d≥1. Let H(x),B(x) be jointly translation-invariant binary fields on Z^d indicating holes and active sites, with H(x)B(x)=0 and h=EH(0)>0. Distances are graph distances. For an integer R≥1, put V_R=|B_R(0)| and

S_{2R}=sum_{0<|z|_1≤2R}E[H(0)H(z)],
T_{2R}=sum_{|z|_1≤2R}E[H(0)B(z)].

The z=0 term in T is zero by disjointness. If F is the event that the origin is strictly closer to some hole than to every active site, then

P(F)≥V_R (h−T_{2R})_+²/(h+S_{2R}).

Thus a time-indexed d4 configuration with h_t→0 has positive closer-hole liminf if, for some fixed b>0,C<∞,θ<1 and R_t=floor(bh_t^−1/4),

S_{2R_t}≤C h_t and T_{2R_t}≤θ h_t

eventually. The resulting lower limit is at least (2^4/4!)b^4(1−θ)²/(1+C). Unlike C2, this criterion allows an arbitrarily large fixed finite conditional expected number of neighboring holes; it requires a separate hole–active bound instead.

## Proof

Define G(x)=H(x)1_{there is no active site within distance 2R of x}. Its intensity g satisfies g≥h−T_{2R}, by applying the union bound to H(0) together with the active-site events. Since G≥0, g≥(h−T_{2R})_+.

If G(x)=1 and w is within distance R of x, then any active site y satisfies |y−x|_1>2R. Consequently

|w−y|_1≥|y−x|_1−|w−x|_1>2R−R≥|w−x|_1.

Thus every site within radius R of a G-center is strictly nearer a hole than every active site. If the active set is empty the same conclusion holds, with its nearest distance interpreted as infinity.

Let M=sum_{x∈B_R(0)}G(x). Then {M>0}⊂F and EM=V_R g by translation invariance. Since G≤H and H is binary,

EM²≤sum_{x∈B_R}EH(x)+sum_{x,y∈B_R,x≠y}E[H(x)H(y)]
≤V_R h+V_R sum_{0<|z|_1≤2R}E[H(0)H(z)]
=V_R(h+S_{2R}).

The second inequality follows by fixing x and enlarging the possible differences y−x to B_{2R}\{0}; all terms are nonnegative. Cauchy–Schwarz gives (EM)²≤P(M>0)EM². Hence

P(F)≥P(M>0)≥V_R g²/(h+S_{2R})≥V_R(h−T_{2R})_+²/(h+S_{2R}).

The denominator is positive since h>0. If EM=0 the asserted bound is zero, so no division by a vanishing EM occurs. All sums are finite and require no independence.

Finally, V_R=(2^d/d!)R^d+O_d(R^{d−1}+1). For d4 and the stipulated R_t, h_tV_{R_t}→(2^4/4!)b^4. Substituting the moment bounds and taking lower limits proves the stated sufficient condition and constant.

## The missing input changes, rather than disappears

In the sparse particle–hole model one can bound B by active multiplicities A. Therefore it is sufficient to prove the same T-bound with E[H(0)A(z)]. The source's two-hole estimate supplies no such mixed bound in d4. A product FKG argument conditioned on initial randomness alone is not enough after averaging the walk instructions; no negative association of the full dynamics is assumed here.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:1c3dcea0c0d9581690e0b39d8bdb7899bedd14af1bcebf941ddc1ef05029982c","revision_digest":"sha256:688bd96428f9a3df4c2ae0cc3ed5e78ffcc21b789685add6b2ee28f2fdb1b8bf","source_id":"own-work:w661:I0005-C7:v1","source_revision":"v1; 2026-10-14T06:00:17.3108952+03:00","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

body:
Let X be a real random variable with E[X^2] < infinity, G a sub-sigma-field, and Var(X | G) = E[(X - E[X | G])^2 | G]. Then Var(X) = E[Var(X | G)] + Var(E[X | G]), both terms on the right are finite and nonnegative, and so Var(E[X | G]) <= Var(X), with equality if and only if X = E[X | G] almost surely, that is, X is almost surely equal to a G-measurable variable.
(Omega, F, P) is a probability space and G is a sub-sigma-field of F

[Thm Existence-r of arXiv:2506.01746, '\bf Optimal Bregman quantization: existence and uniqueness of optimal quantizers revisited'] Let $r\!\in [2, +\infty)$. Assume that  the distribution $P$ of $X$ satisfies the  moment assumption~(equation eq:Integrabilite of the paper), that  

$F$ is $C^2$ on $U$ with $\nabla^2F(x)$ (symmetric) positive definite for  every $x\!\in U$.
Assume that at every $\bar x \!\in\hat\partial U =  \partial   U$, 

\noindent either
\begin{equation} 
\nabla^2F \mbox{ can  be continuously extended at } \bar x \mbox{ and } \nabla^2F(\bar x) \mbox{ is (symmetric) positive definite}
\end{equation}
or \\
\indent the l.s.c. extensions $\phi_{_F}(\xi, \cdot)$  on $ \bar U^{\widehat{\mathbb{R}^d}}$ satisfy at $\bar x$ 
\begin{equation}

 \forall\, \xi \!\in U, \qquad \phi_{_F}(\xi, \bar x) =\displaystyle  \sup_{x\in U}\phi_{_F}(\xi,x).
\end{equation}
Finally,  if $U$ is unbounded, assume that $\bar x = \infty$ satisfies the above condition~(equation eq:Cond-rb2 of the paper).

\medskip
\noindent $(a)$ Then for every $n\ge1$ there exists an $n$-tuple $x^{(r,n)}= \big(x^{(r,n)}_1, \ldots, x^{(r,n)}_n\big) \!\in U^n$ which minimizes $G_{r,n}$ over $U^n$. Moreover, if  the support (in $U$) of the distribution $P$ has at least $n$ points then $x^{(r,n)}$ has pairwise distinct components and $P\big(\mathring C_i(x^{(r,n)})\big)>0$ for every $i\!\in \{1,\ldots,n\}$.

\smallskip
\noindent $(b)$ The distribution  $P$ assigns no mass to the   boundary of  any $\phi_{_F}$-Bregman--Voronoi partitions of $x^{(n)}$ i.e.
\[
P\left (\bigcup_{i=1}^n\partial C_i\big( x^{(r,n)})\right) = 0
\]
and $x^{(r,n)}$ satisfies the $(r,\phi_{_F})$-stationary (or $(r,\phi_{_F})$-master) equation
\begin{equation}
 x^{(r,n)}_i = \frac{ \int_{C_i(x^{(r,n)})}\xi \phi_{_F}( \xi,x^{(r,n)}_i )^{\frac r2-1}P(\mathrm{d}\xi)}{\int_{C_i(x^{(r,n)})}\phi_{_F}( \xi,x^{(r,n)}_i )^{\frac r2-1}P(\mathrm{d}\xi) } , \quad  i=1,\ldots,n.
\end{equation}
 
\noindent $(c)$ The sequence $\displaystyle G_{r,n}\big( x^{(r,n)}\big) = \min_{U^n} G_{r,n}$ decreases as long as it is not $0$ and converges to $0$ as $n$ goes to infinity. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 19 of arXiv:2606.17859, 'Full $\Gamma-$expansion for the level-two large deviation rate functionals of non-reversib'] Fix $\lambda>0$, $1\leq p\leq \widehat{\mf q}$ and a bounded function
$g\colon \mc S_p \to \bb R$. Let $\phi_{p,\epsilon}$ be the solution of
\eqref{smooth_resolvent_eq}. Then, for every
$x\in \bb T\setminus \mc M_p$,
\begin{align*}

&\Big| \,\phi_{p,\epsilon}(x) \,-\, \phi_{p,\epsilon}(m_p^-(x))
\, \bb P_x^\epsilon \big[\, \tau(m_p^-(x))<\tau(m_p^+(x)) \,\big]
\,-\,\phi_{p,\epsilon}(m_p^+(x))\, 
\bb P_x^\epsilon \big[\, \tau(m_p^+(x))<\tau(m_p^-(x)) \,\big] \,\Big|
\notag\\
&\quad \leq 2\, \Vert G_g\Vert_\infty \,\bb E_x^\epsilon
\Big[\tau(m_p^-(x),m_p^+(x))\,/\,\theta^{(p)}_\epsilon\Big]\,. 
\end{align*}
In particular, 
\begin{equation*}
\liminf_{\epsilon\to 0}\inf_{x\in \bb T}\phi_{p,\epsilon}(x)
\,\ge \, \min_{\mc M\in \mc S_p}f_p(\mc M) \,.
\end{equation*}

[Theorem 9 of arXiv:2606.15843, 'Long-time behaviour of DLRA for SDEs'] Given any invariant probability measure $\pi^*$ of Eqn.~\eqref{eq:DO}  whose second marginal $$\mu^*(A):=\int_{V_r(\bb R^d)}\pi^*(\rrm du, A), \quad\text{for any }A\in \scr B(\bb R^r),$$
    satisfies $\rrm{det}(C_{\mu^*}) \neq 0$, there exists another invariant probability measure $\widetilde\pi^*\in\scr P_2(V_r(\bb R^d)\times\bb R^r)$ that is $O(r)$-invariant. Moreover, define $$\widetilde\mu^*(A)=\int_{V_r(\bb R^d)}\widetilde\pi^*(\rrm du, A), \quad\text{for any }A\in \scr B(\bb R^r).$$
    Then we have $\rrm{det}(C_{\widetilde\mu^*}) \neq 0$.

body:
[Lemma of arXiv:2608.28504, 'Global $\bm\infty$-categories and global Thom spectra'] Any automorphism of ${\textup{O}}(2)$ is an inner automorphism.
    \begin{proof}
        As ${\textup{SO}}(2)$ is the identity component of ${\textup{O}}(2)$, $f$ restricts to an automorphism of ${\textup{SO}}(2)$. By [broecker-tom-dieck]*{Proposition~II.8.1}, we therefore need to have $f(A)=A$ or $f(A)=A^{-1}$ for all $A\in{\textup{SO}}(2)$. As $A$ and $A^{-1}$ become conjugate in ${\textup{O}}(2)$ via the reflection $R\coloneqq\begin{psmallmatrix}-1&0\\0&1\end{psmallmatrix}$, we see that $f\colon{\textup{O}}(2)\to{\textup{O}}(2)$ preserves conjugacy classes of elements in ${\textup{SO}}(2)$. 
        
        On the other hand, any matrix in ${\textup{O}}(2)\smallsetminus{\textup{SO}}(2)$ has $-1$ and $1$ as eigenvalues and hence is conjugate to $R$. As $f$ also has to preserve ${\textup{O}}(2)\smallsetminus{\textup{SO}}(2)$, we conclude that $f$ preserves also the conjugacy class of elements in ${\textup{O}}(2)\smallsetminus{\textup{SO}}(2)$, so that it is conjugate to the identity by Lemma~(lemma:conjugate-to-On of the paper).
    \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 26 of arXiv:2605.13512, '2605.13512'] For any fixed $(x,t)$ and $h >0$ we can find functions $d(h) \le 2e(h)=o(h)$ and a path ${\bf w} \in \mathcal H^{v_0}_{x,t- e(h)}$ such that: 
\begin{enumerate}
\item ${\bf w}(0) = (w_1(0), -v_0(w_1(0)))$ and ${\bf w}(t-e(h)) = (x, -v(x,t)),$
\item there exists a constant $C_{\max}(x,t) \in (0,\infty)$ and a $\xi_h \in [-C_{\max}(x,t), C_{\max}(x,t)]$ so that $${\bf w}(t-h-d(h)) := (x_h, y_h) = (x - h\xi_h, g^{z_0}(x_h-z_0, t-h)-v_0(z_0)),$$
where $-v(x,t) = g^{z_0}(x-z_0, t)-v_0(z_0)$,
\item we have the following equality
\be
v(x,t) \le v(x_h, t-h-d(h)) - \int_{t-h-d(h)}^{t-e(h)}\tilde c({\bf w}(s))\psi \left( \frac{w_1'(s)}{\tilde c({\bf w}(s))} \right)\,ds.
\ee
\item and 
\be 
        \sup_{s\in[t-h-d(h),\,t-e(h)]}
        \left|
        {\bf w}(s)-(x,-v(x,t))
        \right|
        \longrightarrow 0
        \qquad\text{as }h\downarrow0.
\ee
\end{enumerate}
