[Proposition 24 (Heisenberg representation facts) of arXiv:2605.27212, '2605.27212'] Let \(\Heis=W\times\Fp\) be the group in \eqref{eq:heis-law}, with
\(\dim W=2m\).  For \(\xi\in W^*\), define
\[
    \chi_\xi(v,z)=\psi(\xi(v)).
\]
The following facts hold.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}, leftmargin=*]
    \item The functions \(\chi_\xi\), \(\xi\in W^*\), are exactly the
    irreducible complex representations of \(\Heis\) on which the center
    \(\{0\}\times\Fp\) acts trivially.
    \item For each \(\lambda\in\Fp^\times\), there is an irreducible unitary
    representation \(\rho_\lambda\) of \(\Heis\), of dimension \(p^m\), such
    that
    \[
        \rho_\lambda(0,z)=\psi(\lambda z)I,\qquad z\in\Fp.
    \]
    \item If \(\sigma\) is any irreducible complex representation of \(\Heis\)
    on which the center does not act trivially, then there is a unique
    \(\lambda\in\Fp^\times\) such that
    \[
        \sigma(0,z)=\psi(\lambda z)I,\qquad z\in\Fp.
    \]
    For this \(\lambda\), there is a unitary map \(U\) from the representation
    space of \(\sigma\) to that of \(\rho_\lambda\) such that
    \[
        U\sigma(g)U^{-1}=\rho_\lambda(g),\qquad g\in\Heis.
    \]
\end{enumerate}
Moreover, if \(g=(v,z)\), \(g'=(w,t)\), and \(\lambda\in\Fp^\times\), then
\begin{equation}
    \rho_\lambda(g)\rho_\lambda(g')
    =
    \psi(\lambda\omega(v,w))\rho_\lambda(g')\rho_\lambda(g).
\end{equation}

[Lemma lem:positive-finite-energy-potential of arXiv:2608.02459, 'Response Calculus for Spectral Simplicity\\ and Joint Eigenvalue Densities'] For every finite positive Radon measure $\mu$ with $I_D(\mu)<\infty$, there is
a unique potential $U_D\mu\inH$ characterized by
\[
 \mathcal E(U_D\mu,v)=\int_D\widetilde v\,d\mu,
 \qquad v\inH.
\]
Moreover,
\[
 \mathcal E(U_D\mu,U_D\mu)=I_D(\mu),
\]
and its quasi-continuous representative is given by
\begin{equation}
 \widetilde{U_D\mu}(z)
 =\int_DG_D(z,w)\,\mu(dw)
 \qquad\text{for $\mathcal E$-q.e. }z\in D.
 
\end{equation}

[Theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] At half-integer parameters, $a,b\in\mathbb N/2$, we still have the formula
$$P(s)=\frac{\binom{s+a-1}{s}\binom{n-s+b-1}{n-s}}{\binom{n+a+b-1}{n}}$$
with the following convention for the quantities in brackets,
$$\binom{n}{k}=\frac{(2n+1)!!}{(2k+1)!!(2n-2k+1)!!}$$
where $M!!=(M-1)(M-3)\ldots$ for any integer $M\in\mathbb N$, as usual.

[Theorem bhp of arXiv:2411.14921, 'A boundary Harnack principle and its application to analyticity of 3D Brownian intersectio'] Let $U$ be a domain in $\mathbb{R}^3$ and $K$ a compact set such that $K\subseteq U$. For $\mathbb{P}_{\vec x}$-almost every $\mathcal{W}$, there exists $C(U,K,\mathcal{W})\in (0,\infty)$ such that for all closed subset $\mathcal{A}\subseteq\mathcal{W}$, if $u$ and $v$ are bounded positive harmonic functions in $U\setminus \mathcal{A}$ that vanish continuously on regular points of $\mathcal{A}\cap U$, then
    \begin{equation}
        u(x_1)\,v(x_2)\leq C\,u(x_2)\,v(x_1) \quad \text{for all $x_1,x_2\in K\setminus \mathcal{A}$}.
    \end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: [Lem proofthm3ii of arXiv:2605.06488, 'Continuous-state branching processes with L\'evy-Khintchine drift-interaction: Laplace dua'] Assume $\underline{\theta}_{\,\scriptscriptstyle\Phi,\hat{\Sigma}}>1$. There exist no continuous Fellerian extension of $X^{\mathrm{m}}$ with $\infty$ non-absorbing. In particular, the extended process $X^{\mathrm{e}\infty}$, in Theorem~(thm2infty of the paper), is absorbed at $\infty$.

body: Both hypotheses are used, and each failure has a clean counterexample on the unit disk D. (1) The set E where pointwise convergence is assumed must have an accumulation point in the open set U, not merely on its boundary. Take a_k = 1 - 1/k^2, so that the sum of (1 - a_k) converges, and let B be the Blaschke product with simple zeros exactly at the a_k; B is holomorphic on D with |B| < 1 and B is not identically zero (B(0) = product of the a_k, nonzero). The sequence f_n = (-1)^n B is uniformly bounded by 1 and converges (to 0) at every point of E = {a_k}, a set whose only accumulation point is the boundary point 1, yet f_n diverges at every point where B ≠ 0, for instance at 0. (2) Local uniform boundedness cannot be dropped: on U = D(0,2) the functions f_n(z) = z^n converge pointwise on E = D (a set with plenty of interior accumulation points) but diverge for |z| > 1; the family is not bounded on compact subsets of U. (3) Connectedness of U matters in the same way as for the identity theorem: if U has several components, the hypothesis must be met on each component separately, since the identity theorem step is applied there. When auditing an argument that upgrades pointwise convergence of holomorphic functions to locally uniform convergence, check exactly these three things, and check that the pointwise limits are finite complex numbers rather than ∞.
title: Pitfall: Vitali–Porter needs the convergence set to accumulate inside the domain, and local boundedness

[Definition def:densities of arXiv:2411.12149, 'Airy limit for $\beta$-additions through Dunkl operators'] For $x>0$, $h,g> 0$, we define 
    \[\mathbf{F}(x;h,g)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi x}}\left(\exp\left(-\frac{(g-h)^{2}}{2x}\right)-\exp\left(-\frac{(g+h)^{2}}{2x}\right)\right).\]
    Note that (by reflection principle) $\mathbf{F}(x;h,g)$ is the transition density of a Brownian bridge from $g$ to $h$, conditioned on staying nonnegative.

    Let \[\mathbf{F}_{0}(x,h)=\frac{2h}{\sqrt{2\pi x^{3}}}\exp\left(-\frac{h^{2}}{2x}\right),\]
and let \[\mathbf{F}_{0,0}(x)=\frac{2}{\sqrt{2\pi x^{3}}}.\]

[Lemma 5 of arXiv:2609.02779, '2609.02779'] There exist $\rho_0,\mu,C,\lambda_0,e_0>0$ such that the following holds for
$0<\rho\le\rho_0$ and every real interval $[a,b]$.

\begin{enumerate}[label=\textnormal{(\roman*)}]
\item If $0<\lambda\le\lambda_0$ and
$Z_\lambda:[a,b]\to T^*M$ is the lift of a $u_\lambda$-calibrated curve with
\[
 d_{T^*M}(Z_\lambda(s),\Gamma)<2\rho
 \qquad\text{for every }a\le s\le b,
\]
then
\begin{equation}
 d_{T^*M}(Z_\lambda(s),\Gamma)
 \le C\rho\bigl(e^{-\mu(s-a)}+e^{-\mu(b-s)}\bigr)+C\lambda
 \qquad\text{for every }a\le s\le b.
\end{equation}

\item If $Z^0:[a,b]\to T^*M$ is a conservative orbit satisfying
\[
 \dot Z^0=X_H(Z^0),
 \qquad
 H(Z^0(s))\equiv c+e,
 \qquad |e|\le e_0,
\]
and
\[
 d_{T^*M}(Z^0(s),\Gamma)<2\rho
 \qquad\text{for every }a\le s\le b,
\]
then
\begin{equation}
 d_{T^*M}(Z^0(s),\Gamma)
 \le C\rho\bigl(e^{-\mu(s-a)}+e^{-\mu(b-s)}\bigr)+C|e|
 \quad\text{for every }a\le s\le b.
\end{equation}
\end{enumerate}

body:
[Defn rational SLE of arXiv:2505.14762, 'Multiple radial SLE($\kappa$) and quantum Calogero-Sutherland system'] In the unit disk $\mathbb{D}$, let $e^{i\theta} \in \partial\mathbb{D}$ be the growth point, and let $u_1 = e^{i\theta_1}, u_2 = e^{i\theta_2}, \dots, u_k = e^{i\theta_k} \in \overline{\mathbb{D}}$ be marked points. A symmetric double divisor $(\boldsymbol{\sigma}^+, \boldsymbol{\sigma}^-)$ assigns a charge distribution on $e^{i\theta}$ and $\{u_1, \dots, u_k\}$, where
\[
\boldsymbol{\sigma}^+ = a \cdot e^{i\theta} + \sum_{j=1}^{k} \sigma_j \cdot u_j,
\quad \text{and} \quad
\boldsymbol{\sigma}^- = \overline{\boldsymbol{\sigma}^+}|_{\mathbb{D}},
\]
and the total charge satisfies the neutrality condition $(\mathrm{NC}_b)$.

We define the rational $\mathrm{SLE}_\kappa[\boldsymbol{\sigma}]$ as a random normalized conformal map $g_t(z)$, with initial condition $g_0(z) = z$ and normalization $g_t'(0) = e^{-t}$. It evolves according to the radial Loewner equation:
\[
\partial_t g_t(z) = g_t(z) \frac{e^{i\theta(t)} + g_t(z)}{e^{i\theta(t)} - g_t(z)}, \quad g_0(z) = z.
\]

Let $h_t(z)$ be the covering map of $g_t(z)$, defined via
\[
e^{i h_t(z)} = g_t(e^{i z}),
\]
so that $h_0(z) = z$, and
\[
\partial_t h_t(z) = \cot\left( \frac{h_t(z) - \theta(t)}{2} \right).
\]

The driving function $\theta(t)$ evolves as
\[
d\theta(t) = \frac{\partial \log \mathcal{Z}(\theta)}{\partial \theta} \, dt + \sqrt{\kappa} \, dB_t,
\]
where the Coulomb gas partition function is
\begin{equation} 
\mathcal{Z}(\boldsymbol{\theta}) = \prod_{j < k} \sin\left( \frac{\theta_j - \theta_k}{2} \right)^{\sigma_j \sigma_k} 
\cdot \prod_j e^{\frac{i}{2} \sigma_j (\sigma_0 - \sigma_\infty)\theta_j}.
\end{equation}

The flow map $g_t$ is well-defined up to the first time $\tau$ when $\zeta(t) = g_t(w)$ for some $w$ in the support of $\boldsymbol{\sigma}$. For any $z \in \mathbb{D}$, the process $t \mapsto g_t(z)$ is defined up to time $\tau_z \wedge \tau$, where $\tau_z$ is the first time such that $g_t(z) = e^{i\theta(t)}$. Define the associated hull by
\[
K_t = \left\{ z \in \overline{\mathbb{D}} : \tau_z \le t \right\}.
\]

Furthermore, the law of the rational $\mathrm{SLE}_\kappa[\boldsymbol{\sigma}]$ Loewner chain is invariant under Möbius transformations $\mathrm{Aut}(\mathbb{D})$, up to a time change, due to the conformal covariance of the Coulomb gas correlation functions. Thus, we define rational $\mathrm{SLE}_\kappa[\boldsymbol{\sigma}]$ in a general simply connected domain $\Omega$ via a conformal map $\phi: \Omega \to \mathbb{D}$ by pulling back the flow.
title: Rational SLE

[Proposition 15 of arXiv:2609.02416, '2609.02416'] Let $\Omega=(\alpha,\beta)$ be bounded and assume $q\in C^1(\overline \Omega)$. Let $\phi_\Omega$ be the positive principal eigenfunction associated with $\Lp(\Omega)$. Then the formal adjoint
\[
\cA_\Omega^*v=d\left(\int_\Omega J(x-y)v(y)\,dy-v(x)\right)-(qv)'(x)+a(x)v(x)
\]
has a positive eigenfunction $\phi_\Omega^*\in C^1(\Omega)\cap C(\overline \Omega)$ satisfying
\[
\cA_\Omega^*\phi_\Omega^*+\Lp(\Omega)\phi_\Omega^*=0\ \hbox{in }\Omega,\quad \phi_\Omega^*(\alpha)=0,\quad \phi_\Omega^*>0\ \hbox{in }\Omega.
\]
If $v\in C^1(\Omega)\cap C(\overline \Omega)$ satisfies $v>0$ in $\Omega$, $v(\beta)=0$ and $\cA_\Omega v+\mu v\ge0$ in $\Omega$, then $\Lp(\Omega)\le\mu$. If equality holds and $v$ is an eigenfunction, then $v$ is proportional to $\phi_\Omega$.

body: [Lemma lem:VHStheorem of arXiv:2411.00663, 'Ergodicity and Mixing of invariant capacities and applications'] Let $(\Omega, \mathcal{F})$ be a measurable space, and $\{P_n\}_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence  of probabilities. Suppose that  for any $A\in \mathcal{F}$ the  limits exist $\lim _{n \rightarrow \infty} P_n(A)=Q(A)$. Then $Q$ is a probability. If we further suppose that each $P_n$ is absolutely continuous with respect to the probability $Q$, then the absolute continuity of the $P_n$ with respect to $Q$ is uniform in $n\in\mathbb{N}$, that is, for any $\epsilon>0$ there exists $\delta>0$ such that for  any $A\in\mathcal{F}$, if  $Q(A)<\delta$ then $ P_n(A)<\epsilon$ for all $n\in\mathbb{N}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Owner draft: independently checked proof (C015 v1). Suppose a d-dimensional body is decomposed up to null sets into finitely many nondegenerate d-simplices with disjoint interiors and volume fractions q_j/D, where q_j are positive integers and D=sum q_j. Then its uniform law is n-CM at n=kD whenever every k*q_j>=d+1. Take a complete mix of k*q_j uniform points in each simplex, concatenate the groups, and randomly permute all output positions. Deterministic volume-matched counts give the full uniform marginal and total n times the whole-body centroid despite differing piece centers. Rational-coordinate convex polytopes have such a rational-volume triangulation, so admit arbitrarily large commensurate-order mixes. This does not prove critical order for a multi-piece decomposition or all nonmultiple orders, and variable-order approximation cannot be passed to a fixed-order mix. Novelty UNKNOWN.

For f, g in L^1(R^n) the convolution (f * g)(x) = integral over R^n of f(x - y) g(y) dy is defined for almost every x, belongs to L^1(R^n) with ||f * g||_1 <= ||f||_1 ||g||_1, and its Fourier transform is the product of the transforms: (f * g)^(xi) = f^(xi) g^(xi) for every xi, with f^(xi) = integral f(x) exp(-2 pi i x . xi) dx (with another normalisation of the transform a constant factor appears). Dually, for f, g in L^2(R^n) (or in L^1 with transforms in L^1) the transform of the pointwise product is the convolution of the transforms: (f g)^ = f^ * g^. The same identity holds for the Fourier series of 2 pi-periodic functions (the convolution on the circle, coefficients multiply), for the discrete Fourier transform of finite sequences with cyclic convolution (the basis of fast convolution by FFT, O(N log N) instead of O(N^2)), and for the Laplace transform with the convolution on [0, infinity). Consequences: L^1(R^n) with convolution is a commutative Banach algebra without unit whose Gelfand transform is the Fourier transform; convolution with an approximate identity converges to the function (the transforms tend to 1 pointwise); a convolution operator f -> k * f is diagonalised by the Fourier transform, with symbol k^, which is how constant-coefficient linear PDE and filters are analysed.

\]
converges to $\mathbf L_\beta(\vec\mathbf k,\vec\boldsymbol{\tau})$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem 7 of arXiv:2606.14812, 'Joint convergence in Wiener chaos via transport hierarchy and Malliavin covariances'] Let $(X_N = I_p(f_N), N\geq 1)$ with $p\geq 2$ satisfying \eqref{c1}. 
	Let us consider a sequence $(\mathbb{Y}_N=(Y_{1,N},\ldots,Y_{d,N}), N\geq 1)$ 
	of $d$-dimensional random vectors, with components in the $p$th Wiener 
	chaos, which converges in distribution to $\mathbb{Y}=(Y_1,\ldots,Y_d)$. 
	Assume
	\begin{equation}
		\mathbf{E}\!\left[X_N Y_{j,N}\right] \to_{N\to\infty} \rho_j, 
		\quad\text{for every } j=1,\ldots,d.
	\end{equation}
	Let $\rho=(\rho_1,\ldots,\rho_d)\in\mathbb{R}^d$. Then
	\begin{equation}
		(X_N,\mathbb{Y}_N) \xrightarrow[N\to\infty]{(d)} (Z,\mathbb{Y}),
	\end{equation}
	where $Z\sim N(0,\sigma^2)$ and the characteristic function of 
	$(Z,\mathbb{Y})$ is given by, for every $u\in\mathbb{R}$, 
	$v\in\mathbb{R}^d$,
	\begin{equation}
		\varphi_{(Z,\mathbb{Y})}(u,v) 
		= \mathbf{E}\!\left[e^{i\langle v,\mathbb{Y}\rangle}\right]
		e^{-\frac{\sigma^2 u^2}{2} - u\langle\rho,v\rangle}.
	\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Defini 12 of arXiv:2608.27934, 'An example of biquandle and an invariant of long virtual knots defined through it'] (Index of a crossing)\\
Let $G(D)$ be the pointed Gauss diagram of a long virtual knot diagram $D$. 
For each dashed arrow in $G(D)$, we assign symbols $+$ and $-$ to the endpoints of the dashed arrow so that the symbol assigned to the tail is the same as that of the dashed arrow and that the symbol assigned to the head is the opposite to that of the dashed arrow. 
For each classical crossing $c$ of $D$, corresponding dashed arrow in $G(D)$ cuts unique interval without the specified point $p$ from the circle. 
The signed sum of symbols on the interior of the interval is denoted by $\alpha(c)$ and called {\it the index of }$c$.
title: Definition 12 of arXiv:2608.27934

[Lemma lemma-M_N martingale of arXiv:2505.24043, 'Weak solutions of Navier-Stokes Equation with purely discontinuous L\'evy Noise'] For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the process ${{M}}_{n}$ is a square integrable $\mathbb{F}$-martingale and 
\begin{align}

\sup_{n \in \mathbb{N}}\mathbb{E} \left[ \sup_{t\in [0,T]}\bigl\vert  {{M}}_{n} (t) \bigr\vert_{H}^2 \right]
&\leq C_2 \sup_{n \in \mathbb{N}}
\mathbb{E} \Bigl[   \int_0^{T} \int_{Y} \rvert P_n F(s, u_n(s),y)\vert_{H}^2 \, \nu(\mathrm{d} y) \, \mathrm{d}s
\Bigr]
\\
&\leq C_2 \sup_{n \in \mathbb{N}} \left( 1+ \mathbb{E} \left[ \int_0^T  \lvert u_n (t) \rvert^2_H \, \mathrm{d}t \right] \right) < \infty. 

\end{align}
Moreover, if Assumption F.(assum-F5 of the paper)  is satisfied,  then for every $p\in [2, 4+\gamma] $ and for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the process ${{M}}_{n}$ is a $p$-integrable $\mathbb{F}$-martingale
\begin{align}
\sup_{n \in \mathbb{N}}\mathbb{E} \left[ \sup_{t\in [0,T]}\bigl\vert  {{M}}_{n} (t) \bigr\vert_{H}^p \right]
&\leq C_p \; \sup_{n \in \mathbb{N}}
\mathbb{E} \Bigl[   \Bigl( \int_0^{T} \int_{Y} \rvert P_n F(s, u_n(s),y)\vert_H^2 \, \nu(\mathrm{d} y) \, \mathrm{d}s \Bigr)^\frac{p}2
\\
\nonumber
&\hspace{2truecm}+\int_0^{T} \int_{Y} \rvert P_n F(s, u_n(s),y)\vert_H^p \, \nu(\mathrm{d} y) \, \mathrm{d}s
\Bigr]
\\

&\leq C_p \sup_{n \in \mathbb{N}} \left( 1+ \mathbb{E} \left[ \int_0^T  \lvert u_n (t) \rvert^p_H \, \mathrm{d}t \right] \right) < \infty .
\end{align}
The constants $C_2$, $C_p$ are generic positive constants which can change from line to line but which do not depend on $n$.

[Cor of arXiv:2608.28504, 'Global $\bm\infty$-categories and global Thom spectra'] Let ${\mathcal{C}}$ be globally presentable and representation stable. Then $\ev_{\mathbb S}\colon{\textup{Fun}}^\textup{L}({\mathpalette\ulhelper{\mathfrak d\kern-.25pt}}\hbox{\rule[-2pt]{0pt}{0pt}}{\mathfrak S\kern-.5pt\mathfrak p}_\textup{gl},{\mathcal{C}})\to{\mathcal{C}}(1)$ is the left adjoint in a Bousfield localization.
    \begin{proof}
        As a consequence of the previous proposition, $\ev_{\mathbb S}$ has a right adjoint given by the composite
        \[
            {\mathcal{C}}(1)\xrightarrow{\;\mathbb S_*\;}{\textup{Fun}}'({\mathpalette\ulhelper{{\mathfrak d\kern-.25pt}{\mathfrak S\kern-.5pt\mathfrak p}}}\hbox{\rule[-2pt]{0pt}{0pt}}_\textup{lvl},{\mathcal{C}})\xrightarrow{\;\smash{\raisebox{-0.25ex}{\ensuremath{\scriptstyle\sim}}}\;}{\textup{Fun}}^\text{L}({\mathpalette\ulhelper{\mathfrak d\kern-.25pt}}\hbox{\rule[-2pt]{0pt}{0pt}}{\mathfrak S\kern-.5pt\mathfrak p}_\textup{gl},{\mathcal{C}}),
        \]
        where ${\textup{Fun}}'({\mathpalette\ulhelper{{\mathfrak d\kern-.25pt}{\mathfrak S\kern-.5pt\mathfrak p}}}\hbox{\rule[-2pt]{0pt}{0pt}}_\textup{lvl},{\mathcal{C}})$ denotes the full subcategory of left adjoints factoring through the localization $L\colon{\mathpalette\ulhelper{{\mathfrak d\kern-.25pt}{\mathfrak S\kern-.5pt\mathfrak p}}}\hbox{\rule[-2pt]{0pt}{0pt}}_\textup{lvl}\to{\mathpalette\ulhelper{\mathfrak d\kern-.25pt}}\hbox{\rule[-2pt]{0pt}{0pt}}{\mathfrak S\kern-.5pt\mathfrak p}_\textup{gl}$ and the unnamed equivalence is given by precomposing with a right adjoint to $L$. As $\mathbb S_*$ is fully faithful by Proposition~(prop:Sigma-oo-lev-ff of the paper), the claim follows.
    \end{proof}

$\tau_1\geq\cdots\geq\tau_m$.  With $b=\theta^{-1}-1$, the series
$\mathbf L_b[\boldsymbol k;\boldsymbol\tau]$ converges absolutely, and
\begin{align*}
 \lim_{N\to\infty}\mathbb E\left[
   \prod_{p=1}^m
   N\int
   \left(\frac{x}{\mu_{p,N}}\right)^{K_p}
   \mathrm d\mu_{\mathrm{PP}}[\lambda^{(N)}(s_{p,N})](x)
   \right]
   \notag=(1+\mu_+)^m
   \mathbf L_b[\boldsymbol k;\boldsymbol\tau].
\end{align*}
The convergence is locally uniform in the ordered time vector
$\boldsymbol\tau$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: Let W_t be a standard Brownian motion and let X_t solve the Ito stochastic differential equation dX_t = mu_t dt + sigma_t dW_t for adapted, sufficiently integrable processes mu_t, sigma_t. If f(t,x) is continuously differentiable once in t and twice in x, then Y_t = f(t,X_t) satisfies dY_t = [f_t + mu_t f_x + (1/2) sigma_t^2 f_xx] dt + sigma_t f_x dW_t, all partial derivatives evaluated at (t,X_t). Equivalently df = f_t dt + f_x dX_t + (1/2) f_xx d[X]_t, using the Ito rule (dW_t)^2 = dt. The stochastic-calculus chain rule; due to Kiyoshi Ito.

body:
[Definition def:propagation-of-chaos of arXiv:2606.29557, 'Propagation of chaos for Belavkin equations beyond pure states'] Let $\rho_0^N\in\mathcal S(\mathcal H_N)$ and $\gamma_0\in\mathcal S(\mathcal H)$.  Propagation of chaos is said to hold if, for every
fixed $n\ge1$ and $T>0$,
\begin{equation}
  \sup_{0\le t\le T}
  \mathbb E\left[
    \left\|
      \rho_t^{N:n}-\Gamma_t^n
    \right\|_1
  \right]
  \longrightarrow0
  \qquad
  \text{as }N\longrightarrow \infty.
  
\end{equation}
title: Propagation of chaos

body:
[Lem tree-power-residual of arXiv:2609.03856, 'Consensus time for asynchronous $\ell^p$ relaxation: graph dependence'] Let $x_0,x_1,\ldots,x_k\ge0$, let $\sigma_i\in\{-1,1\}$, and put
\[
 \rho=\left|\sum_{i=0}^k\sigma_i x_i^a\right|.
\]
If $\alpha_i>0$ and $\sum_{i=1}^k\alpha_i=1$, then, for
$0<\varepsilon\le1$,
\begin{equation}
 x_0^p\le(1+\varepsilon)
 \sum_{i=1}^k\alpha_i^{-1/a}x_i^p
 +C_p\varepsilon^{-1/a}\rho^q.
\end{equation}

[Lemma lem:rigidity of arXiv:2607.05226, 'The Exact Worst-Case Tail Probability under Bounded Kurtosis'] Let $t>0$ and let $\mu$ have mean $0$ and variance $1$. If $\mu([t,\infty))=1/(1+t^2)$, then
$\mu=\mu_C=\tfrac1{1+t^2}\delta_t+\tfrac{t^2}{1+t^2}\delta_{-1/t}$; in particular
$\mathbb{E}_\mu X^4=\kappa_{\mathrm{c}}(t)$.

body: [Cor fineET of arXiv:2608.30031, 'Ziggurats, taut foliations, and contact structures'] Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a cooriented $C^0$-foliation on $M$ transverse to $\partial M$ without compact planar leaves nor $\mathbb{T}^2$-type planar minimal sets. Then $\mathcal{F}$ can be $C^0$ approximated by positive and negative contact structures which dominate some foliation $\mathcal{G}$ on $\partial M$ which is isotopic to $\partial \mathcal{F}$, via a $C^0$-small isotopy. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Cor fineET of arXiv:2608.30031

[Definition 1 of arXiv:2607.12384, '2607.12384'] Let $(\Omega, \mathcal{F}, \{\mathcal{F}_t\}_{t\geq 0}, \mathbb{P})$ be a filtered probability space satisfying the usual conditions, and let $W(ds, dy)$ be a space-time white noise defined on this space.  An adapted and jointly measurable random field
	\[
	\{u(t,x):(t,x)\in[0,T]\times\mathbb R\}
	\]
	is called a mild solution to \eqref{eq:main equation} if
	\[
	\sup_{(t,x)\in[0,T]\times\mathbb R}
	\mathbb E|u(t,x)|^2<\infty,
	\]
	and, for every
	\((t,x)\in[0,T]\times\mathbb R\),
	\[
	\int_0^t\int_{\mathbb R}
	G_{t-s}(x-y)^2
	\mathbb E\left[|\sigma(u(s,y))|^2\right]\,dy\,ds
	<\infty,
	\]
	so that the Walsh integral below is well defined in \(L^2(\Omega)\). Moreover,
	for every \((t,x)\in[0,T]\times\mathbb R\),
	\begin{equation}
		u(t,x)
		=
		1+
		\int_0^t\int_{\mathbb R}
		G_{t-s}(x-y)\sigma(u(s,y))\,W(ds,dy)
	\end{equation}
	holds in \(L^2(\Omega)\).
title: Definition 1 of arXiv:2607.12384

[Corollary 25 of arXiv:2607.10486, 'Weak martingale solutions to stochastic Navier-Stokes-Cahn-Hilliard system with transport '] Let the assumptions of Proposition \ref{prop-First-propo} be satisfied. 
There exists a positive constant $C= C(\domO)>0$ such that  for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and every  $p \geq 2$,  the 
 solution $\bX_n$  to \eqref{eqn-Compact-Galerkin-Modified-stochastic-CHNSEs-n}, satisfies, 
 $\mathbb{P}$-a.s. $\omega \in \Omega$, the following inequalities: 
\begin{align}
\Vert \phi_n \Vert_{C([0,T];L^2(\domO))}^p &\leq C\, e^{\frac{p}{2} T} \lvert \phi_0 \rvert_{\newone{H}}^p,
\\

\int_0^T \lvert \phi_n(s) \rvert_{L^2}^{p-2} \lvert \Atwo \phi_n(s) \rvert_{L^2}^2\,\d s 
&\leq C\, e^{\frac{p}{2} T} \lvert \phi_0 \rvert_{\newone{H}}^p,
\\

\int_0^T \lvert \phi_n \rvert_{L^2}^{p-2} \Vert \phi_n \Vert_{H^2}^2 \, \d s 
&\leq C\, e^{p T} \lvert \phi_0 \rvert_{\newone{H}}^p.
\end{align}
title: Corollary 25 of arXiv:2607.10486

[campaign result 2026-09-14, author checked] This is the supporting identity used in the campaign partial answer to Problem 3.11 of Takahiro Hasebe and Yuki Ueda's Large time unimodality for classical and free Brownian motions with initial distributions, ALEA 15 (2018), 353-374, DOI:10.30757/ALEA.v15-15 (arXiv:1710.08240). A probability measure is unimodal if, for some mode m, it is an atom at m plus an absolutely continuous measure whose density is nondecreasing to the left of m and nonincreasing to the right. Write boxplus for additive free convolution, the distribution of a sum of freely independent self-adjoint variables with the indicated laws, and * for classical convolution of independent real variables. For t>0 let C_t have density t/[pi(t^2+x^2)] on the real line. For every probability measure mu on R, mu boxplus C_t = mu * C_t. In transform notation, G_mu(z)=integral_R (z-x)^(-1) mu(dx) for Im(z)>0, and G_{mu boxplus C_t}(z)=G_mu(z+i t), where i^2=-1. The record explicitly treats the identity as classical rather than claiming novelty for it. This is an unrefereed campaign result.
t>0 and mu is any probability measure on R.

The whole point is an identity that is special to the Cauchy family. Its Cauchy transform is
$G_{C_t}(z) = 1/(z+it)$ on the upper half plane, so $K_{C_t}(w) = 1/w - it$ and the $R$-transform is the
constant $R_{C_t}(w) = -it$. Free convolution adds $R$-transforms, so for any $\mu$,
$$K_{\mu\boxplus C_t}(w) = K_\mu(w) - it \quad\Longrightarrow\quad G_{\mu\boxplus C_t}(z) = G_\mu(z+it).$$
On the other side, the density of $\mu * C_t$ at $x$ is the Poisson integral
$\tfrac1\pi\int t\,d\mu(y)/((x-y)^2+t^2) = -\tfrac1\pi\operatorname{Im}G_\mu(x+it)$, so
$G_{\mu*C_t}(z) = G_\mu(z+it)$ as well. Hence
$$\mu \boxplus C_t \ = \ \mu * C_t \qquad\text{for every } \mu \text{ and every } t>0,$$
the free and classical convolutions with a Cauchy law coinciding.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:41d53089fc9154dfc68427cb689fc659cab94c6fae196dceb869ccf188d76c60","revision_digest":"sha256:692d5257f04848621ef0a15c85ace5ae808ba7700ca47e9f5495cb8d32102dac","source_id":"doi:10.30757/ALEA.v15-15","source_revision":"problem source: ALEA 15 (2018), 353-374; own campaign record: 2026-09-14","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

[Lem 6 (Lemma 3.4, Yao, Chen, and Guo \cite{YCG11}) of arXiv:2605.31568, 'Lipschitz continuity of the time constant for continuum percolation'] Suppose that $\lam_0 > \lam_c$. 
Then there exist constants $\rho_1=\rho_1(d,\lam_0) > 0$ and $c=c(d,\lam_0) > 0$  such that, for all $x \in \R^d$, all $t \ge \rho_1 \|x\|$, and all $\lam \ge \lam_0$ we have
\begin{equation}
    \P_{0,x}^\lam(0 \xleftrightarrow{G_\lam} x, d_{G_\lam} (0,x) \ge t) \le \exp(-ct).
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma 3.4, Yao, Chen, and Guo \cite{YCG11}

[Lemma eq:shifted-r-derivative of arXiv:2607.27613, 'Regularized Bulk Universality versus Bounded-Disorder Nonuniversality\\for Annealed Comple'] \label[lemma]{lem:conditional-aggregate-remainder}
Assume (equation eq:array-assumptions of the paper), and write \(r=m+1\).  Fix
\(O\in\mathcal O_{N,L}\), \(t\in[0,1]\), \(I\in[N]^p\), and
\(z_{-I}\in\mathbb R^{[N]^p\setminus\{I\}}\).  Define
\[
 \phi_I(s)=F_O(z_{-I},s),\qquad
 a_I^0=\abs{\partial_I\Psi_O(z_{-I},0)},\qquad
 B_I=\int\phi_I(s)\mu_{I,t}(\,\mathrm d s),
\]
and
\[
 \Delta_I(z_{-I})
 =\int\phi_I(s)\gamma(\,\mathrm d s)
  -\int\phi_I(s)\mu_I(\,\mathrm d s).
\]
Then, for all sufficiently large \(N\), the following estimates hold
uniformly in \(O,t,I,z_{-I}\):
\begin{align}
 \abs{\phi_I^{(r)}(s)}
 &\le C\phi_I(s)
 \left\{(a_I^0+\mathfrak d_I\left\lverts\right\rvert)^r
       +\mathfrak d_Iq_N^{r-2}\right\},
 \\
 c\phi_I(0)\le B_I&\le C\phi_I(0),\qquad
 \int\left\lverts\right\rvert^k\phi_I(s)\mu_{I,t}(\,\mathrm d s)
 \le C_kB_I,\quad 1\le k\le2r,
 \\
 \abs{\Delta_I(z_{-I})}
 &\le CB_I
 \left\{(a_I^0)^r+\mathfrak d_Iq_N^{r-2}\right\}.
 
\end{align}
Moreover,
\begin{equation}
 \sum_{I\in[N]^p}
 \int\abs{\Delta_I(z_{-I})}\lambda_{t,-I}(\,\mathrm d z_{-I})
 \le CNq_N^{r-2}A_O(t).
\end{equation}

body: Hilbert's tenth problem is the tenth on the list of mathematical problems that the German mathematician David Hilbert posed in 1900. It is the challenge to provide a general algorithm that, for any given Diophantine equation, can decide whether the equation has a solution with all unknowns taking integer values.
title: Hilbert's tenth problem

[Lemma lem:finite-elliptic-comparison of arXiv:2608.11931, '\texorpdfstring{Nonlinear parabolic characterizations of stochastic completeness at infini'] {KLW21}}]
Let $\Omega\subseteq X$ be finite.  Let $f,g\colon \Omega\to\mathbb R$ and let
$\xi,\eta \colon X\setminus\Omega\to\mathbb R$ be
$(\operatorname{id},\Omega)$-admissible exterior data.  Suppose that
$\xi\le\eta$ on $\partial_e\Omega$.  If
\[
    \Delta_\Omega^\xi f\leq\Delta_\Omega^\eta g
    \qquad\text{on }\Omega,
\]
then $f\le g$ on $\Omega$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 55 of arXiv:2608.07239, 'Unified framework for asymptotically uniform iterative construction of generalised random '] We have the sum estimates
		\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
			\item $\begin{aligned}[t]
				\sum_{r=0}^{\alpha-k-1}\frac{q_r^2}{n_{\alpha-r}-K}=P+O(M\log\alpha/\alpha^2),
			\end{aligned}$
			\item $\begin{aligned}[t]
				\sum_{r=0}^{\alpha-k-1}\frac{q_r^2p_r}{n_{\alpha-r}-K}=\frac12P+O(M\log\alpha/\alpha^2),
			\end{aligned}$
			\item $\begin{aligned}[t]
				\sum_{r=0}^{\alpha-k-1}\frac{q_r}{n_{\alpha-r}-n_k}=O(\log\alpha/\alpha),
			\end{aligned}$
			\item $\begin{aligned}[t]
				\sum_{r=0}^{\alpha-k-1}\frac1{n_{\alpha-r}-n_k}=O(\tfrac1{k+1}(\log(k+1)+1))=O(1).
			\end{aligned}$
		\end{enumerate}

body: [Theo existprod of arXiv:2608.25865, 'Instability of Böhm's Einstein metrics'] For all $(k,l)\in \mathbb{N}^2$ such that $k,l\geqslant 2$ and $k+l\leqslant 8$, there exists a sequence of pairwise non-isometric Einstein metrics $(g_i)$ on $S^{k+1}\times S^l$ with Einstein constant $\Lambda=k+l$. Moreover, the sequence of initial conditions $(\bar h_i)$ is decreasing and converges to 0. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Existence of Einstein metrics on $S^{k+1}\times S^l$, Theorem 3.4 \cite{bohm}

[Lemma circular_order of arXiv:2604.17170, 'CaTherine wheels from trees and Liouville quantum gravity'] Let $f:S^1 \to S^2$ be a CaTherine wheel with zipper $Z^\pm$.
For $i=0,1,2$ let $p_i \in S^2$ be three distinct points with unique preimages 
$e_i \in S^1$ under $f$. Let $r_i$ be equivalence classes of
proper rays in $Z^+$ that land at $p_i$. Then the circular order on the $e_i$ in
$S^1$ agrees with the circular order on the ends of the $r_i$ in $Z^+$.

ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Explicit calculation or obstruction with source-specific scope Result: The circle contour calculation shows why simply integrating the constant mode over a real period imposes neutrality. For an integer screening expansion, the integral of exp(i*k*beta*c) over a full period vanishes unless k=0. A noncompact complex Hankel-type contour can avoid that selection rule, but requires a large-argument estimate for the complex GMC Laplace transform along its two infinite legs. Finite exponential moments only ensure finiteness for each fixed argument, not decay along those legs. Check: For a deterministic complex random variable M=-1, every exponential moment is finite but E exp(-z*M)=exp(z) grows on the positive real ray. Thus existence of all moments cannot provide the needed contour decay. This diagnostic does not assert that the actual imaginary GMC has this behavior. [Theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] When rolling a die $n$ times, the distribution of the sum is
$$P(s)=\frac{1}{6^n}\sum_{k=0}^{[\frac{s-n}{6}]}(-1)^k\binom{n}{k}\binom{s-6k-1}{n-1}$$
with this coming from independence, and the binomial formula for negative exponents.

[Theorem thm:power-law-caseII of arXiv:2604.25108, 'Terminal Defects, Growing Multiplicity, and Variance Extremality\\in the Double Dixie Cup '] Fix $m\ge1$ and $\alpha>0$.  Let
\[
        A_N=\sum_{j=1}^N j^{-\alpha},
        \qquad
        p_{N,j}=\frac{j^{-\alpha}}{A_N}.
\]
Put
\[
        C_N=A_NN^\alpha,
        \qquad
        \rho_N=\log\frac{N}{\alpha},
\]
and
\[
        B_N=C_N\left[\rho_N+(m-2)\log\rho_N-\log((m-1)!)\right].
\]
Then
\[
        \frac{T_m(N)-B_N}{C_N}\Rightarrow G,
\]
where $G$ is standard Gumbel.

[Theorem Lebesgue of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] There is a unique regular, translation-invariant measure on $\mathbb R^N$, normalized as for the volume of the unit cube to be $1$. This measure is called Lebesgue measure, and appears alternatively as the measure on the Borel sets 
$$E\subset\mathbb R$$
whose corresponding integration theory extends the usual Riemann integral, as constructed in Proposition 5.29, or equivalently, as in multivariable calculus.

Method: Union small-ball lower bound and one-normal upper bound Result: For a standard M-by-M real Gaussian matrix A, sigma_min(A)<=t implies that some column has distance at most sqrt(M)t from the span of the other columns: project a minimizing unit vector equation using a coordinate of magnitude at least 1/sqrt(M). Each such distance has the law |N(0,1)|, so P(sigma_min<=t)<=sqrt(2/pi) M^(3/2)t. There are at most 4^M M-row submatrices of a (2M-1)-by-M frame. Therefore its minimum omega exceeds exp(-(log 4+epsilon)M) with probability tending to one. Conversely fix M-1 rows and a unit normal u. The M remaining row projections are independent N(0,1), and omega is at most their minimum absolute value, giving omega<=C log(M)/M with probability tending to one for sufficiently large C. Check: Full spark holds almost surely. Adding rows increases the Gram matrix, so the minimum relevant frame bound is attained among M-row subsets. Both bounds use union/inclusion inequalities and never assume independence among overlapping minors. Obstruction: The exponential lower bound and polynomial upper bound are far apart. Sharp extremes of the strongly dependent minors remain uncontrolled.

body:
[Dfn smooth of arXiv:2608.25471, 'Exact Hausdorff measures and fine geometry of collisions of independent Markov processes'] [{Smooth measures}] 
  A Borel measure $\nu$ on $M$ is said to be a \textit{smooth measure} if it satisfies the following conditions:
  \begin{enumerate} [label = (\roman*)]
    \item 
      $\nu$ charges no semipolar sets, i.e., 
      $\nu(E) = 0$ for any semipolar $E \in \mathcal{B}(M)$;
    \item 
      there exists an increasing sequence $(E_{n})_{n \geq 1}$ of Borel subsets 
      such that $M = \bigcup_{n \geq 1} E_n$, $\nu(E_{n}) < \infty$ for each $n$, 
      $\int_{E_n} r_1(x,y)\, \nu(dy)$ is bounded in $x$ for each $n$,
      and $P_x( \lim_{n \to \infty} \tau_{E_n} \geq \zeta) = 1$ for all $x \in M$,
      where $\tau_{E_n} \coloneqq \inf\{t > 0 \mid X_t \notin E_n\}$.
  \end{enumerate}
title: Dfn smooth of arXiv:2608.25471

[Corollary cor:spectral0 of arXiv:2606.01937, 'Stationary fluctuations for an exclusion process with mass and energy conservation'] Let $(f_i)_{i\ge 1}$ be a sequence of local functions from $\Omega$ to $\mathbb{R}$ that have disjoint supports, and assume that the support of the function $f_i$ has cardinality $\ell_i$ for any $i\ge 1$. Assume that $\psi_{f_i}(\rho ,\mathcal{E})=0$ for any $\rho\in [0,1]$, any $\mathcal{E}\in [\rho ,\kappa\rho ]$ and any $i\ge 1$. Finally, assume that the series $\sum_{i=1}^\infty \mathrm{Var}_{\rho ,\mathcal{E}}(f_i)$ converges. Then, we have
    \begin{equation}
        \left\|\sum_{i=1}^\infty f_i\right\|_{-1}^2 \le C_6\sum_{i=1}^\infty \ell_i^2 \mathrm{Var}_{\rho ,\mathcal{E}}(f_i).
    \end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Corollary cor:spectral0 of arXiv:2606.01937

\]

 x=\frac{\delta u}{1-u},

AUTHOR-CHECKED GRAPH CALCULATION; CANDIDATE NEGATIVE ANSWER TO THE HISTORICAL QUESTION, NOVELTY UNVERIFIED. For odd m>=5, the degree-four arc-transitive graph C_m[empty K_2] has n=2m vertices, relaxation time 1/(1-cos(2*pi/m)), maximal commute time 2*floor(m^2/4)+2*m and stationary-average hitting time (m^2-1)/6+m. These violate proposed O(n) relaxation and O(n log n) commute bounds; the commute/ twice-average-hitting ratio tends to3/2. The source has a variable-assignment typo in its arc-transitivity definition; the proof uses the standard intended definition. Thirteen exact rational finite controls agree, but do not supply independent review.

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:9ea5b85517036020530e7b15f2ed4969895ef72e4547a77140109f9419efb64b","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/9e/9ea5b85517036020530e7b15f2ed4969895ef72e4547a77140109f9419efb64b.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:782e3ef5bbb0faf01a685eb529732c0d77bfa3843ab0c5c3cb1c854a588ec117","bundle_entry_key":"wreath-graph-counter","bundle_id":"population.probability-candidate-obstructions-and-spatial-lemmas-005","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"probability theory","draft":"codex-probability-1000-20h-20260906/bundle_005.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.markov:candidate-arc-transitive-wreath-graph-hitting-relaxation-obstruction","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# P0208: the wreath graph and Aldous–Fill Problem 7.27

Status: complete counterexample candidate, checked by the author through hitting-time and spectral calculations. No independent review or novelty certificate. The graph itself is an established construction, not an invention here. This is a response to a historically sourced question; present-day open status remains unverified.

Primary question: Aldous and Fill, *Reversible Markov Chains and Random Walks on Graphs*, 2002 unfinished monograph, 2014 recompilation, Open Problem 7.27, PDF p.259, https://www.stat.berkeley.edu/~aldous/RWG/book.pdf . Section 7.2 is internally dated January 31, 1994. It asks, for arc-transitive graphs other than cycles on n vertices, whether maximal mean commute time is O(n log n), relaxation time is O(n), and the ratio of maximal commute time to twice stationary-average hitting time tends to one. The three assertions are counted as one related question.

## Source scope and a printed definition error

Page 254 prints an inconsistent variable assignment in the definition of arc-transitivity: the images of two possible identical starting vertices would be allowed to be distinct. Read literally, that formula excludes any graph with a vertex having two neighbors. The surrounding discussion, examples of tori and Cayley graphs, and Lemma 7.19 unmistakably use the usual definition: the automorphism group is transitive on ordered adjacent pairs. Our result concerns that intended standard definition, and does not silently claim to satisfy the misprinted formula.

Conder's 2013 Rogla summer-school notes, p.8, independently describe the same established wreath/necklace graph and its arc-transitivity: https://www.famnit.upr.si/sl/resources/files/konference/rogla2013/conderlecturenotes.pdf . This is evidence that the construction is prior art. It does not establish when the probability question was answered.

## Construction and symmetry

Let m be an odd integer at least five, and put

\[
 V_m=(\mathbb Z/m\mathbb Z)\times\{0,1\},\qquad
 (i,b)\sim(i+1,c),\ (i,b)\sim(i-1,c)\quad(c=0,1).
\]

This is the lexicographic product of a cycle with an edgeless two-vertex graph. It is connected, simple, 4-regular, and has n=2m vertices, so it is not an n-cycle. Dihedral symmetries act on the first coordinate. Independently swapping the two vertices in any fiber preserves every edge. Given two directed edges, a dihedral symmetry sends their ordered base edges to each other, after which independent swaps in the two distinct endpoint fibers match both second coordinates. Thus the graph is arc-transitive.

Use discrete-time simple random walk, or its rate-one continuization. The book states on p.115 that the parameters at issue are unchanged by this continuization. The first-coordinate projection is simple random walk on the m-cycle, and the second coordinate is replaced at each step by a fresh fair bit independent of the base step.

## Exact hitting times

Write h(v,w) for the mean first hitting time, with h(w,w)=0. From a base position at cyclic distance j in {1,...,m-1}, the mean first arrival at base fiber zero is

\[
 H_j=j(m-j).
\]

Indeed H_0=H_m=0 and H_j=1+(H_{j-1}+H_{j+1})/2. At the first fiber arrival, the fair bit hits a specified vertex with probability one half.

Let h be the mean hitting time from its twin to the specified vertex. Starting in that fiber, the first positive return of the base walk has mean m. The arrival bit succeeds with probability one half; on failure the same twin state recurs. Hence h=m+h/2, giving h=2m. Therefore

\[
 h((j,b),(0,0))=j(m-j)+m\quad(j\ne0),\qquad
 h((0,1),(0,0))=2m.
\]

The formula is symmetric in source and target and gives 2m-1=n-1 for neighboring vertices, exactly as Lemma 7.19 requires. Its maximum is floor(m²/4)+m for m at least five. Thus

\[
 \tau^*=2\lfloor m^2/4\rfloor+2m.
\]

The stationary law is uniform. Summing the same hitting-time formula gives

\[
 \tau_0=\frac1{2m}\left[2m+2\sum_{j=1}^{m-1}
          \{j(m-j)+m\}\right]
       =\frac{m^2-1}{6}+m.
\]

On a vertex-transitive graph the stationary mean to a fixed target equals the source's stationary-average target parameter, so either equivalent convention yields this value.

## Independent spectral route

For functions constant on each two-vertex fiber, the transition operator is the cycle operator, with eigenvalues cos(2πk/m), k=0,...,m-1. For functions antisymmetric within every fiber it is zero. These orthogonal invariant subspaces both have dimension m and exhaust the state space. Consequently

\[
 \tau_2=\frac1{1-\cos(2\pi/m)}\sim\frac{m^2}{2\pi^2}.
\]

The fundamental-matrix trace is

\[
 \sum_{k=1}^{m-1}\frac1{1-\cos(2\pi k/m)}+m
 =\frac{m^2-1}{6}+m,
\]

which agrees with the direct hitting-time sum. The trigonometric sum can also be recovered from the already derived cycle hitting-time formula by stationary averaging; it is not needed as an unproved numerical identity for the counterexample.

## Consequences and limitations

Since n=2m, both τ* and τ2 are of order n². They violate the proposed n log n and n upper bounds. Moreover

\[
 \frac{\tau^*}{2\tau_0}
 =\frac{\lfloor m^2/4\rfloor+m}{(m^2-1)/6+m}
 \longrightarrow\frac32,
\]

which violates the third assertion. These are exact formulas, not simulation estimates.

The strongest reasons for caution are the old unfinished source, its definition typo, and the fact that wreath graphs have long been standard. Focused searches on September 6, 2026 located the original question and primary graph-theory descriptions but no verified later disposition of Problem 7.27. Absence from that search is not evidence of novelty. A future reviewer should check the intended arc-transitivity convention, rate-one normalization, and prior probability literature before any promotion.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:556c6b1fcc6b4db785822e5b4cae963c5ea31477c78e3e04ba1fa72416f504a4","revision_digest":"sha256:6953ca17d9e261b9f17c422ee3d80a50d1c860e65bbcef06c9e4366bd4afe678","source_id":"owner-original-probability-research-20260906:wreath-graph-counter","source_revision":"author-checked-20260906-v1","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

[Theorem 2 of arXiv:2605.18198, 'Large deviations of crowding in finite $\beta$-ensembles'] Let $U\subset \mathbb F$ which satisfies Assumption \ref{ass:U}, and $n^{-1}\mathcal X_{n,\beta}^{\mathbb F}(U) $ be as defined in \eqref{eqn:defncrowding}.    Then the sequence of laws of $\{n^{-1}\mathcal X_{n,\beta}^{\mathbb F}(U) \}$ satisfies the following large deviation type bounds with speed $n^2$ and good rate  $\gamma$ as  defined in \eqref{eqn:defgamma}.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] For any open set $O \subseteq [0,1]$,
\[
\liminf_{n \to \infty} \frac{1}{n^2} \log \P^{\mathbb F}_{n,\beta} (n^{-1}\mathcal X_{n,\beta}^{\mathbb F}(U)  \in O) \geq -\inf_{x\in O} \gamma(x),
\]
\item[(ii)] For $\mathbb F= \mathbb{R}$ and any closed set $F \subseteq [0,1]$,
\[
\limsup_{n \to \infty} \frac{1}{n^2} \log \P^{\mathbb R}_{n,\beta}(n^{-1}\mathcal X_{n,\beta}^{\mathbb R}(U)  \in F) \leq -\inf_{x\in F} \gamma(x).
\]
However, for $\mathbb F=\mathbb C$, the last inequality holds if $F$ satisfies
\begin{align}
\P_{n,\beta}^{\mathbb{C}}(L_n\in \mathcal S_F\cap M_1^*(\mathbb C)^c)\le e^{n^\alpha}\P_{n,\beta}^{\mathbb{C}}(L_n\in \mathcal S_F\cap M_1^*(\mathbb C)),
\end{align}
for some $0\le \alpha<2$ and for large $n$, where $\mathcal S_F=\{\mu\in M_1(\C)\suchthat \mu(U)\in F\}$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] The probability for $A$ to happen, knowing that $B$ happens, is
$$P(A|B)=\frac{P(A\cap B)}{P(B)}$$
with this being called conditional probability.

[Lemma lem:weighted-exp-conc of arXiv:2609.02829, 'Quantitative explosion and percolation of the divisible sandpile'] Let $\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_N$ be independent real-valued random variables, and let $F=F(\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_N)$ be real-valued and measurable. Let $\xi_i'$ be an independent copy of $\xi_i$, independent of all coordinates, and let $\xi^{(i)}$ be obtained from $\xi=(\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_N)$ by replacing only $\xi_i$ with $\xi_i'$. Assume that, for deterministic numbers $\ell_i\geq0$, not all zero, for every $1\leq i\leq N$,
		\[
			|F(\xi)-F(\xi^{(i)})|\leq \ell_i|\xi_i-\xi_i'|\, .
		\]
		Write
		\[
			\|\ell\|_{\ell^2}\coloneqq\left(\sum_{i=1}^N\ell_i^2\right)^{1/2}\, ,
			\qquad
			\|\ell\|_{\ell^\infty}\coloneqq\max_{1\leq i\leq N}\ell_i\, .
		\]
		\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}]
			\item If $p\geq2$ and $\mathbb{E}|\xi_i|^p<\infty$ for every $i$, then there is
			$C=C(p)$ such that
			\[
				\bigl(\mathbb{E}|F-\mathbb{E} F|^p\bigr)^{1/p}
				\leq
				C
				\left[
				\left(\sum_{i=1}^N \ell_i^2\bigl(\mathbb{E}|\xi_i-\xi_i'|^p\bigr)^{2/p}\right)^{1/2}
				+
				\left(\sum_{i=1}^N \ell_i^p \mathbb{E}|\xi_i-\xi_i'|^p\right)^{1/p}
				\right]\, .
			\]

			\item If the $\xi_i$ are i.i.d.\ and
			$\mathbb{E} e^{\theta_0|\xi_1|}\leq K_0$, then there are $c>0$ and $C<\infty$, depending
			only on $\theta_0$ and $K_0$, such that, for all $r\geq0$,
			\[
				\mathbb{P}(|F-\mathbb{E} F|\geq r)
				\leq
				C\exp\left\{
				-c\min\left(
				\frac{r^2}{\|\ell\|_{\ell^2}^2}\, , 
					\frac{r}{\|\ell\|_{\ell^\infty}}
				\right)
				\right\}\, .
			\]

				\item If the $\xi_i$ are i.i.d.\ with $\mathbb{E}\xi_1=0$ and
				$\mathbb{E} e^{\theta_0|\xi_1|}\leq K_0$, then there are $c>0$ and
				$C<\infty$, depending only on $\theta_0$ and $K_0$, such that,
				for every $\lambda\in\mathbb{R}$ with
				$|\lambda|\,\|\ell\|_{\ell^\infty}\leq c$,
				\[
					\log\mathbb{E}\exp\Bigl\{\lambda\sum_{i=1}^N\ell_i\xi_i\Bigr\}
					\leq
					C\lambda^2\|\ell\|_{\ell^2}^2\, .
				\]

			\item Under the assumptions of part~\textup{(b)}, if
				$|\lambda|\|\ell\|_{\ell^\infty}<\theta_0$, then
				\[
					\mathbb{E} e^{\lambda(F-\mathbb{E} F)}
					\leq
					\exp\{C\lambda^2\|\ell\|_{\ell^2}^2\}\, ,
				\]
				where $C$ depends only on $\theta_0$, $K_0$, and
				$\theta_0-|\lambda|\|\ell\|_{\ell^\infty}$.
		\end{enumerate}

[Lemma 16 of arXiv:2609.00690, 'Boundary behavior and optimal pointwise H\"older exponent of the total local time of $(1+\'] Let $\{K_t : t \in [0,T]\}$ be a c\`adl\`ag stochastic process. Suppose there are constants $a > 1$, $b > 0$, and $C > 0$ such that for all $s,t \in [0,T]$,
	\[
	\mathbb{E}|K_t - K_s|^a \le C |t-s|^{1+b}.
	\]
	Fix $\gamma \in (0, b/a)$. Define
	\[
	\bar\rho_\gamma := \sup\{ r\in[0,T] : \forall s,t \in [0,T],\ |t-s| \leq r \Rightarrow |K_t - K_s| \leq |t-s|^\gamma \},
	\qquad \rho_\gamma:=\frac12\bar\rho_\gamma.
	\]
	Then 
	\begin{itemize}
		\item[{\rm(1)}] $|K_t - K_s| \leq |t-s|^\gamma$ whenever $|t-s| \leq\rho_\gamma$,\ $s,t \in [0,T]$;
		\item[{\rm(2)}] $\mathbb P(\rho_\gamma > 0) = 1$;
		\item[{\rm(3)}] for all $0 < h < h_{\gamma}/2$,
		\[
		\mathbb P(\rho_\gamma < h) \le C' h^{b - a\gamma_0},
		\]
		where $\gamma_0 =(\gamma+b/a)/2$, $h_\gamma= [2^{-\gamma_0}(1 - 2^{-\gamma_0})/3]^{1/(\gamma_0 - \gamma)}$ and 
		\[
		C' := \frac{CT(T\vee 1/T)2^{2b - 2a\gamma_0+1}}{1 - 2^{-(b - a\gamma_0)}}.
		\]
	\end{itemize}

critical point of $E_{u_0}$. If
$\mu\in T_Y\mathcal T(\Sigma)$ is represented by a harmonic Beltrami
differential, then
\begin{equation}
  \operatorname{Hess}_Y E_{u_0}(\mu,\mu)
  =
  4\|\mu\|_{\mathrm{WP}}^2,
  \qquad
  \|\mu\|_{\mathrm{WP}}^2
  :=
  \int_Y|\mu|^2\,dA_Y.
  
\end{equation}

body:
[Lemma 19 of arXiv:2604.27242, 'Statistical Inference for Homogenization Limits Driven by Wiener or Hermite Processes'] For \(m>1\) and \(H^*(m)<1/2\), and any \(1\leq r\leq m-1\), with \(r_I, r_S\) as in \eqref{eq: rI rS def}, the diagonal and off-diagonal contributions in \eqref{eq: second moment of chaos term} satisfy
\[
E_{2m-2r}^{\mathrm{Diag}} \lesssim 4\Bigl(\int_0^{\infty}\rho(s)^m\,ds\Bigr)^2 \delta\,\varepsilon^{2},
\]
and
\[
E_{2m-2r}^{\mathrm{Off}} \lesssim
\begin{cases}
\delta^{3}(\varepsilon/\delta)^{2m(2-2H)}, & r< r_I\wedge r_S,\\[0.3em]
\varepsilon^{2(m-r)(2-2H)+2}, & r> r_I\vee r_S,\\[0.3em]
\delta^{2+2(m-r)(2H-2)}(\varepsilon/\delta)^{2m(2-2H)}, & r_S< r < r_I,\\[0.3em]
\delta\,\varepsilon^{2}(\varepsilon/\delta)^{2(m-r)(2-2H)}, & r_I< r < r_S,
\end{cases}
\]
with implicit constants depending only on \(H, m\) and \(r\).
title: Lemma 19 of arXiv:2604.27242

body:
[Proposition 52 of arXiv:2609.02878, '2609.02878'] Let \(\xi\) be a fixed limiting point based at
\(q=q_\pi(\xi)\in Y^{\rm prod}\).  After forgetting the distinguished
conjugate heat measures, the underlying K\"ahler metric flow of every
tangent space at \(\xi\) is the shrinking cylinder
\[
 \left(\C^m\times\PP^1,
 g_{\rm E}+(-s)g_{S^2}\right)_{s<0},
 \qquad \Rc(g_{S^2})=\tfrac12g_{S^2}.
\]
More precisely, let \(\tau_i\searrow0\) realize such a tangent space and
let \(p_i\) be \(H_{2m+2}\)-centres of
\(\mu_{i,-1}=\mu_{1-\tau_i}\) with respect to
\(g_i(-1)=\tau_i^{-1}g(1-\tau_i)\) at backward scale one.
After passing to a further subsequence that still realizes the same
tangent space, there is \(D<\infty\) such that, for all sufficiently
large \(i\),
\[
 F_q\subset
 B_{\tau_i^{-1}g(1-\tau_i)}(p_i,D),
\]
and, for every finite \(A\ge0\), there is \(C_A<\infty\) such that
\[
 \sup_{B_{\tau_i^{-1}g(1-\tau_i)}(p_i,D+A)}
 |\Rm_{\tau_i^{-1}g(1-\tau_i)}|_{\tau_i^{-1}g(1-\tau_i)}
 \le C_A.
\]

[Lemma lem:interp of arXiv:2608.30254, 'Exact Recovery Thresholds for Weighted Data Selection\\ in Vector-Valued Linear Regression'] For $t_i\ne t_j$ let
$B_{ij}=\Bigl(\frac{t_iz_j-t_jz_i}{t_i-t_j},\ \frac{z_i-z_j}{t_i-t_j}\Bigr)
\in\mathbb{C}^2$ (the coefficients of the affine function of $t$ through the two
points) and $d_{ij}=|t_i-t_j|^2$. Then for every admissible $q$,
\[
  D(q):=1-|\mu|^2=\sum_{i<j}q_iq_jd_{ij},
  \qquad
  (a,b)=\sum_{\substack{i<j\\ t_i\ne t_j}}
  \frac{q_iq_jd_{ij}}{D(q)}\;B_{ij} .
\]
In particular $(a,b)$ is a convex combination of the pairwise interpolation
coefficients; the conditioning factor $(1-|\mu|^2)^{-1}$ is absorbed
entirely.

DRAFT author reduction with standard switching inputs; C0052 remains unresolved. In the zero-field unit-coupling nearest-neighbor Ising model on Z^3 at beta<beta_c, let G(x)=E[sigma_0 sigma_x], chi=sum_x G(x), xi=[lim_n -(1/n)log G(ne1)]^(-1), U4 the fourth joint cumulant, and lambda=-sum_{x,y,z}U4(0,x,y,z)/(chi^2 xi^3). Let independent X,W have law mu(x)=G(x)/chi. Given X,W, sample independent ORIGINAL currents with sources {0} symmetric-difference {X} and {y} symmetric-difference {y+W}; retain tagged vertices when endpoints coincide. Let Q_y be the averaged probability that 0 and y are connected in their union. Then lambda=2 xi^(-3)sum_y Q_y. For xi>=1 and B={y:||y||infinity<=floor xi}, with Q_B=|B|^(-1)sum_{y in B}Q_y, lambda>=2|B|xi^(-3)Q_B>=2Q_B. The original source target is lambda not tending to zero; no limit existence is assumed.
Translation-invariant subcritical free Gibbs state on Z^3
chi finite; xi is the exponential coordinate correlation length

[Theorem 64 (Rank-uniform Newton element) of arXiv:2608.29585, '2608.29585'] For every zero-framed knot $K$, the series
\begin{equation}
 \mathscr H_K(X,A,q)=
 \sum_{k=0}^{\infty}
 B_k(X;A,q)\mathsf H_k(K;A,q)
\end{equation}
converges in $\widehat{\mathscr C}_{A,q}$ and has the following
properties.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.8em]
\item For every $r\ge0$,
\begin{equation}
 \mathscr H_K(X_r(A,q),A,q)=\HH_r(K;A,q).
\end{equation}
\item For every $n\ge2$, the specialization $A=q^n$ gives the
fixed-rank Newton series with coefficients $H_k^{(n)}$.  After the
substitution $X=q^nx^2+q^{-n}x^{-2}$, it is the colored lift
$\mathscr J_K^{(n)}(x,q)$ of
\eqref{eq:colored-lift}.
\item For every $n\ge2$, $r\ge0$, and complex root of unity $\zeta$,
there is a canonical finite evaluation
\begin{equation}
 \operatorname{ev}_{n,r,\zeta}(\mathscr H_K)
 =J_r^{SU(n)}(K;\zeta),
\end{equation}
where the right side means evaluation of the generic Laurent polynomial,
and $\operatorname{ev}_{n,r,\zeta}$ means first specializing $A=q^n$,
then $X=X_r(q^n,q)$, and finally $q=\zeta$.
\item The Newton coefficients in
\eqref{eq:two-variable-unified-element} are unique, and the full
family of color evaluations determines the element.
\end{enumerate}

[Proposition prop:gap of arXiv:2609.03448, 'Prime-power Diophantine tuples'] Assume that $N>2^{2^{117}}$. After the lower-bound reduction of
Lemma~(lem:lower of the paper), the ordered elements
$a_1<a_2<\cdots<a_m$ of a positive reduced $D(\varepsilon N)$-tuple satisfy
\begin{equation}
 a_{i+\ell}>N^\gamma a_i
 \qquad(1\le i\le m-\ell),
\end{equation}
where $\ell<2^{35}$ and $\gamma>2^{-26}$.

body: In algebraic geometry, Bézout's theorem is a statement concerning the number of common zeros of n polynomials in n indeterminates. In its original form the theorem states that in general the number of common zeros equals the product of the degrees of the polynomials. It is named after Étienne Bézout.
title: Bézout's theorem

[Prop asymptotic_densities_separable of arXiv:2512.20338, 'Up-down chains and scaling limits: \\ application to permuton- and graphon-valued diffusio'] Let $\pi$ be a pattern.
	Then as $ t \to \infty $, we have the estimate
	$$
		 \mathbb E [ d ^o_\pi(  F (t))]
			=
				\begin{cases}
					 \mathbb E [ d ^o_\pi(  \bm\mu^{\text{\tiny rec}}_p ) ] + O(e^{-2t}),
						&	
							\qquad
							\pi \text{ is separable},
						\\
        			O\left( 
        					e^{ - t \, j(j-1) } 
        			\right),
						&	
							\qquad
							\pi \text{ is nonseparable}
						,
				\end{cases}
	$$

	\noindent
	where $j$ is the size of the nonseparable core of $\pi$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Prop asymptotic_densities_separable of arXiv:2512.20338

[M,M]_{t} = \sum_{s\leq t} \vert \Delta M(s) \vert^2, \;\;\mathbb{P}\mbox{-a.s.}.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Cor 8 of arXiv:2609.03777, '2609.03777'] Let $k_1\geq3$ and $k_2,\dots,k_r\geq2$, and put $k=k_1+\cdots+k_r$.  Then, locally uniformly for $\tau\in\HH$,
\begin{align}
\tau_N^k
G_{k_1,\dots,k_r}\left(\tau_N\right)
\longrightarrow

Own work draft; proof (unaudited), no novelty established. Let d>=2 and let an equal-weight identity-covariance three-Gaussian teacher have planar means (a,0),(-a/2,3sqrt(3)a/2),(-a/2,-3sqrt(3)a/2), a>0. For an equal-weight identity-covariance mixture-score student with planar means (s,0),(t,v),(t,-v), three reduced population DDPM excess-risk stationary equations imply full unrestricted criticality. For risk F=E||score_student-score_teacher||^2, define planar responsibilities w, posterior mean r, discrepancy h=r-r_teacher and J=[w_j(u_j-r)] over the two-dimensional teacher mixture. The full mean Hessian splits into a planar six-by-six block and d-2 identical perpendicular blocks K=2E[ww^T+J^T J-w h^T J-J^T h w^T]. Reflection decomposes the planar block into even/odd three-by-three blocks and K into a two-by-two block and a scalar. Thus for d>=3 positivity of blocks of sizes 3,3,2,1 is equivalent to positive definiteness of the full Hessian; for d=2 only the planar blocks occur. This is an exact finite-noise certificate reduction for arbitrary finite a,s,t,v, not a root enclosure, stability verdict, bifurcation location, new general symmetry theorem or resolution of Target 2.

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:db304008efaf035d6a786c20db55eb6f0952fedbef4efe02440c187e6c5c25fb","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/db/db304008efaf035d6a786c20db55eb6f0952fedbef4efe02440c187e6c5c25fb.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:dcaefeed7c723b4b285a26af04710d4c81b4dad4c4a6d10d8f5fc62ca1f5597e","bundle_entry_key":"t309-c21","bundle_id":"population.t309-finite-noise-stability-reduction-draft","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"Gaussian mixture learning and diffusion objectives","draft":"w721/bundle_014.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.learning:gaussian-mixture-ddpm-finite-noise-reflection-perpendicular-hessian","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"Own work draft; T309-w721-C21 v1; proof (unaudited); Target 2 route 12 auxiliary certificate reduction.

# Exact finite-noise stability blocks for reflection-symmetric planar DDPM students

This supplies an exact reduction for the finite-noise stability step left by C20. It does not certify stability at any new amplitude or locate a bifurcation. No novelty finding or general-target move is asserted. The proof uses differentiated finite-mixture formulas and Gaussian integration, not a high-noise asymptotic expansion.

## 1. Setup and statement

Let d>=2 and fix a plane identified with R^2. The teacher is the equal-weight spherical mixture whose planar means are

    (a,0), (-a/2,3 sqrt(3)a/2), (-a/2,-3 sqrt(3)a/2), a>0,

and whose component covariance is I_d. Embed the student means in that plane, with

    u_0=(s,0), u_+=(t,v), u_-=(t,-v).

The student also has equal weights and covariance I_d. For general planar student means u_j, define

    w_j(y)=exp(y.u_j-||u_j||^2/2)/sum_l exp(y.u_l-||u_l||^2/2),
    r(y)=sum_j w_j u_j, h(y)=r(y)-r_*(y),
    J(y)=[w_0(u_0-r), w_+(u_+-r), w_-(u_--r)].       (1)

Here r_* is the teacher posterior mean and expectation E_y below is under its two-dimensional noisy mixture q_2. The population excess DDPM risk is F=E||score_student-score_teacher||^2, with no factor 1/2. At planar means it equals E_y||h(y)||^2 exactly.

The three equations partial_s F=partial_t F=partial_v F=0 imply full unrestricted mean criticality, including every ambient direction. At such a point the full mean Hessian is the direct sum of a six-dimensional planar block and d-2 identical perpendicular blocks

    K=2 E_y[ww^T+J^T J-w h^T J-J^T h w^T].          (2)

The planar block further splits into two explicit three-dimensional reflection blocks. The perpendicular block splits into a two-dimensional label-symmetric block and a one-dimensional label-antisymmetric block. Thus, for d>=3, positive definiteness of four matrices of sizes 3,3,2,1 is sufficient and necessary for positive definiteness of the full Hessian. For d=2 only the two planar blocks occur. This certifies a nondegenerate strict local minimum when the reduced gradient is zero; it does not characterize degenerate minima.

All expressions are exact two-dimensional expectations for arbitrary finite a,s,t,v. No noncollinearity is needed for the identities. Noncollinearity can be imposed separately when continuing the C06 branch.

## 2. Exact planar derivatives

For any planar direction p=(p_0,p_+,p_-), set

    L_j=(y-u_j).p_j, Lbar=sum_j w_j L_j,
    A_p=sum_j w_j p_j+sum_j w_j(u_j-r)L_j,
    B_p=2 Cov_w(p,L)+Cov_w(u,(L-Lbar)^2-||p||^2).

Cov_w(f,g)=sum_j w_j(f_j-E_w f)(g_j-E_w g), interpreted as a vector when f is vector valued. Direct differentiation of the softmax weights, including the second derivative -||p_j||^2 of each logit, gives

    D_p r=A_p, D_p^2 r=B_p,
    D_p^2 F=2 E_y[||A_p||^2+h.B_p].                 (3)

Polarization supplies the six-by-six planar Hessian. Equivalently the planar gradient for component j is

    grad_{u_j} F=2 E_y w_j[h+(y-u_j)((u_j-r).h)].    (4)

This form computes all reduced derivatives without differentiating a high-dimensional integral. At any fixed finite means, the score difference is bounded by the student and teacher mean norms. Parameter derivatives introduce polynomial factors in y with bounded softmax weights. Local Gaussian-mixture domination therefore justifies differentiation and polarization under the expectation to the finite orders used here.

## 3. The perpendicular Hessian and the essential logit bias

Perturb one perpendicular coordinate by mean components tau z_j, with z=(z_0,z_+,z_-). Let X denote the standard normal observation in that coordinate; it is independent of y under the teacher. At tau=0 define

    mu=w^T z, B=Jz, V=E_w z^2-mu^2.

The logit increments are tau X z_j-tau^2 z_j^2/2. Hence

    w'_j=w_j X(z_j-mu),
    w''_j=w_j[X^2((z_j-mu)^2-V)-(z_j^2-E_w z^2)]. (5)

The planar posterior derivative is X B and the perpendicular posterior derivative is mu. Averaging the planar second derivative over X, using E X^2=1, gives

    E_X r_planar''=-2 mu B.                       (6)

Indeed the average coefficient in (5) is -2 mu w_j(z_j-mu). The teacher has zero perpendicular posterior mean, so no perpendicular second derivative contributes to its inner product with the base score difference. Differentiating the squared error therefore yields

    D_z^2 F=2 E_y[mu^2+||B||^2-2 mu h.B]=z^T K z,

which proves (2).

The negative quadratic norm term in each logit is essential. Dropping it leaves a spurious Cov_w(u,z^2) contribution in (6), and generally changes the Hessian. As a simple consistency check, z=(1,1,1) gives mu=1 and B=0, so z^T K z=2: translating every mean equally in a normal direction changes the risk by exactly tau^2.

For multiple perpendicular coordinates, each first planar derivative contains its own independent standard Gaussian X_i. Cross products average to zero for distinct i, and the mean-norm logit has no mixed second derivative between distinct orthogonal axes. The normal posterior derivatives also occupy orthogonal coordinates. Consequently the perpendicular Hessian is I_{d-2} tensor K. Mixed planar/perpendicular Hessian blocks vanish by oddness in X_i. All perpendicular first derivatives vanish for the same reason.

## 4. Reflection blocks and full criticality

Order planar coordinates as (x_0,y_0,x_+,y_+,x_-,y_-). Reflection of the physical second coordinate together with exchanging labels + and - acts by

    T(x_0,y_0,x_+,y_+,x_-,y_-)
      =(x_0,-y_0,x_-,-y_-,x_+,-y_+).

The teacher and risk are invariant under this orthogonal involution. The proposed student lies in its fixed space. Thus its gradient has no T-odd component. The map (s,t,v) spans the fixed space with full rank, so the three reduced stationary equations force its entire planar gradient to vanish. Section 3 supplies the remaining ambient criticality.

Let e_i be the six standard basis vectors. Orthogonal bases for the T-even and T-odd spaces are

    Q_even=[e_1,(e_3+e_5)/sqrt(2),(e_4-e_6)/sqrt(2)],
    Q_odd =[e_2,(e_3-e_5)/sqrt(2),(e_4+e_6)/sqrt(2)].

At a reflection-fixed point, the planar Hessian H commutes with T, by differentiating the invariance twice. Therefore Q_even^T H Q_odd=0. Its two blocks are H_even=Q_even^T H Q_even and H_odd=Q_odd^T H Q_odd, both of size three. This splitting holds even before imposing stationarity.

On each perpendicular coordinate the same physical reflection leaves the perpendicular axis unchanged and swaps student labels +,-. Consequently K commutes with S(z_0,z_+,z_-)=(z_0,z_-,z_+). With three-dimensional standard basis f_j, set

    P_even=[f_1,(f_2+f_3)/sqrt(2)],
    P_odd=(f_2-f_3)/sqrt(2).

Then K_even=P_even^T K P_even has size two, K_odd=P_odd^T K P_odd is scalar, and the off-block term vanishes. Together with Section 3 this proves the stated fixed-size Hessian test in every ambient dimension.

For underlying locations nu with noisy means M=a nu, gradients and Hessians at fixed a acquire factors a and a^2 respectively. Therefore stationary points and Hessian signs are unchanged by that fixed-a parameter conversion. A changing-noise algorithm still needs C20's explicit learning-rate conversion.

## Scope and next unpaid certificate

This is an exact certificate reduction, not a finite-noise stability verdict. To establish continuation beyond the small-amplitude regime one must connect enclosed zeros of the three reduced equations to the C06 bad branch, for example by overlapping uniqueness boxes, and prove positivity of all applicable blocks over the relevant parameter/noise boxes. A positive excess-risk bound must separately certify nonglobality; enclosing some stationary point could instead locate the teacher's global minimum. Alternatively one may exhibit and certify a loss of positivity on the continued branch. Any computer-assisted implementation must use outward-rounded integration or exact bounds, with Gaussian tails controlled. Floating-point roots or sampled Hessian eigenvalues would be numerical evidence only.

The finite rational script checks (5)--(6), the common-normal-translation value, a wrong-logit-bias control and the reflection eigenspaces. It does not independently certify analytic differentiation, root existence or block positivity. body:
[Corollary cor:geometry of arXiv:2608.28330, 'Realising atomless laws as distance distributions on metric measure spaces'] Let $\Theta$ be an atomless Borel probability measure on $\mathbb R_+$ such
	that $0\in\operatorname{supp}\Theta$.  For every $L>1$, there is a realisation
	$(S,d,\mu)$ of $\Theta$ such that $\operatorname{supp}\mu=S$ and $d$ is
	$L$-bi-Lipschitz equivalent to an ultrametric $u$ on $S$.  In fact,
	\[
	u(x,y)\leq d(x,y)\leq Lu(x,y),
	\qquad x,y\in S.
	\]
	If $\Theta$ has bounded support, then $S$ may be chosen compact and
	homeomorphic to the Cantor space.  In this case,
	\[
	\{d(x,y):x,y\in S\}=\operatorname{supp}\Theta,
	\qquad
	\operatorname{diam} S=\max\operatorname{supp}\Theta.
	\]
	If $\Theta$ has unbounded support, then $S$ may be chosen proper and
	homeomorphic to a countable disjoint union of Cantor spaces.

[Definition 12 of arXiv:2608.25785, 'Proper Actions on Homogeneous Spaces of the Upper Triangular Matrix Group via Coarse Geome'] Let $S$ be a set.
    A family $\mathcal{B}\subset \mathcal{P}(S)$ of subsets of $S$ is called a \emph{bornology} on $S$ if it satisfies the following three conditions. 
    \begin{enumerate} 
        \item $\mathcal{B}$ is a cover of $S$ (i.e.~ $\bigcup_{B\in \mathcal{B}}B=S$).
        \item $B_1 ,B_2\in \mathcal{B}$ implies $B_1\cup B_2\in \mathcal{B}$. 
        \item $B\in \mathcal{B}$ and $B'\subset B$ imply $B'\in \mathcal{B}$. 
    \end{enumerate}
    The pair $(S,\mathcal{B})$ is called a \emph{bornological space}.

[Lem def:yosida of arXiv:2601.19145, 'Stochastic Persistence in Infinite Dimensions'] Consider the notation and assumptions from (general-mild-existence of the paper). For each $n \geq 1$ define
    $$
    R_n \coloneqq n(n - A)^{-1} = \int_0^\infty ne^{-nt}S(t)dt 
    $$
    
    and $F_n \coloneqq R_nF$,  $G_n \coloneqq R_nG$. 
    Then, there is a unique strong solution $x_n(t)$ (called Yosida approximations of (equation eq:gefx of the paper))
    of the problem
    \begin{equation}
    dx_n(t) = [Ax_n(t) + F_n(x_n(t))]dt + G_n(x_n(t))dW_t \,, \quad x_n(0) = R_n x_0 \,.
    \end{equation}
    Furthermore, $(x_n)_{n \geq 1}$ converge as $n \to \infty$ to the mild solution $x$
    of (equation eq:gefx of the paper) in $L^p(\Omega; C([0,T];B))$ for all $p,T > 0$.

body:
[Lemm 10 of arXiv:2608.30357, 'Mean convergence for Banach space-valued random elements indexed in measure spaces'] Let $X, Y$ be $\cX$-valued random elements.
\begin{enumerate}[\rm (i)]
\item If $X$ and $Y$ are independent, then they are diagonally negatively dependent.

\item $X, Y$ are diagonally negatively dependent if and only if $Y, X$ are. Moreover, \eqref{def:PDND} holds for a set $A \in \cB(\cX)$ if and only if it holds for $A^c$.

\item Let $(\cY, \|\cdot\|_\cY)$ be a separable Banach space and let $f \colon \cX \to \cY$ be $\cB(\cX)/\cB(\cY)$-measurable. If $X, Y$ are diagonally negatively dependent, then so are $f(X), f(Y)$.
\end{enumerate}
title: Lemm 10 of arXiv:2608.30357

[Proposition prop_T_c_convexity_GHS of arXiv:2503.24372, 'A criterion on the free energy for log-Sobolev inequalities in mean-field particle systems'] Suppose Assumption~(ass_doublewell of the paper) applies. 
Then $T_c = \var_{\alpha_V}(x)$ and 
\begin{equation}

 \inf_{\varphi}\partial^2_\varphi V_T(\varphi) = 
\frac{T - T_c}{T^2}.
\end{equation}

As a consequence, $V_T$ is uniformly convex  for $T>T_c$ and 
the first part of Corollary~(cor: double well of the paper) follows by applying Proposition~(prop_LSI_quadratic_W of the paper).

[Proposition 5 of arXiv:2512.08745, 'Variance strikes back: sub-game--perfect Nash equilibria in time‑inconsistent $N$‑player g'] Let {\rm\Cref{assumpDPP_NplayerGame}} and {\rm\Cref{assumption:regularityForNecessity}} hold, and let $\hat\balpha^N \in \mathcal{N}\!\mathcal{A}_{s,N}$ be a sub-game--perfect Nash equilibrium. Then, one can construct a tuple 
\[
(\Y^N,\Z^N,\M^{\star,N},\N^{\star,N},\Z^{m,\star,N},\Z^{n,\star,N}) \coloneqq (Y^{i,N}, \Z^{i,N}, M^{i,\star,N}, N^{i,\star,N}, \Z^{i,m,\star,N},\Z^{i,n,\star,N})_{i\in\{1,\ldots,N\}},
\]
that satisfies the system \eqref{BSDE_NplayerGame} and, for some $p \geq 1$, the integrability condition
\begin{align*}
&\sup_{\balpha \in \cA^\smalltext{N}_\smalltext{N}} \E^{\P^{\smalltext{\balpha}}} \Bigg[ \sup_{t \in [0,T]} \big|Y^{i,N}_t\big|^p + \bigg(\int_0^T \sum_{\ell =1}^N \big\|{Z}_t^{i,\ell,N}\big\|^2 \d t\bigg)^\frac{p}{2} \Bigg] \\
&+\esssup_{\balpha \in \cA^\smalltext{N}_\smalltext{N}} \Bigg\{\sup_{t \in [0,T]} \Big\{ \big| M^{i,\star,N}_t\big| + \big| N^{i,\star,N}_t \big| \Big\} + \sup_{\tau \in \cT_{0,T}} \E^{\P^{\smalltext{\balpha}\smalltext{,}\smalltext{N}\smalltext{,}\smalltext{\tau}}_{\smalltext{\cdot}}} \Bigg[ \int_\tau^T \sum_{\ell =1}^N \Big( \big\|Z^{i,m,\ell,\star,N}_t\big\|^2 + \big\|Z^{i,n,\ell,\star,N}_t\big\|^2 \Big) \d t \Bigg] \Bigg\} < +\infty.
\end{align*}
It holds that $V^{i,N}_t = Y^{i,N}_t$, $\P\text{\rm--a.s.}$, for every $t \in [0,T]$. Moreover,
\begin{align}
\hat\balpha^N_t \in \cO_{N}\big(t, \X^N_{\cdot \land t}, \Z^N_t, \M^{\star,N}_t, \N^{\star,N}_t, \Z^{m,\star,N}_t, \Z^{n,\star,N}_t\big), \; \text{\rm for}\; \d t \otimes \d \P\text{\rm--a.e.} \; (t,\omega) \in [0,T] \times \Omega.
\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition 5 of arXiv:2512.08745

[Cor stabilization-exists of arXiv:2608.28504, 'Global $\bm\infty$-categories and global Thom spectra'] Let ${\mathcal R}\subset\smash{\ul\Spc_{S\triangleright T,*}}$ small. Then $\smash{\CAT_T^{S\textup{-cc},\textup{${\mathcal R}$-ex}}}\hookrightarrow\CAT_T^\textup{$S$-cc}$ admits a left adjoint restricting to $\textup{Pr}^S_T\to\textup{Pr}^{S,\textup{${\mathcal R}$-ex}}_T$, and both of these adjunctions are smashing localizations. In particular, there exists for any pointed $S$-presentable ${\mathcal{C}}$ an \emph{$\bm{\mathcal R}$-stabilization}, i.e.\ an $S$-cocontinuous $\Sigma^\infty\colon{\mathcal{C}}\to\ul\Sp^{\mathcal R}_{S\triangleright T}({\mathcal{C}})$ to an $S$-presentable ${\mathcal R}$-stable $T$-$\infty$-category, such that for any $S$-cocomplete ${\mathcal R}$-stable ${\mathcal{D}}$
    \[
        \ul{\textup{Fun}}^\textup{$S$-cc}(\Sigma^\infty,{\mathcal{D}})\colon\ul{\textup{Fun}}^\textup{$S$-cc}(\ul\Sp^{\mathcal R}_{S\triangleright T}({\mathcal{C}}),{\mathcal{D}})\xrightarrow{\;\smash{\raisebox{-0.25ex}{\ensuremath{\scriptstyle\sim}}}\;}\ul{\textup{Fun}}^\textup{$S$-cc}({\mathcal{C}},{\mathcal{D}}).
    \]
    \begin{proof}
        Note that if $X,Y\in{\mathcal R}(A)$ act invertibly, then so does $X\otimes Y$. We may therefore assume that ${\mathcal R}$ is a symmetric monoidal subcategory, and the first claim follows by applying Theorem~(thm:sym-mon-localization-for-modes of the paper) to $\core{\mathcal R}\hookrightarrow\ul\Spc_{S\triangleright T,*}$. The second claim is then an instance of Lemma~(lemma:smash-module-internal-hom of the paper).
    \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Cor stabilization-exists of arXiv:2608.28504

Let U ⊂ C be open and let f_n be holomorphic on U with f_n → f uniformly on every compact subset of U. Then f is holomorphic on U, and for every k ≥ 1 the derivatives f_n^(k) converge to f^(k) uniformly on every compact subset of U. Quantitatively, if the closed disk of radius 2r about a lies in U and g is holomorphic on U, then sup over |z - a| ≤ r of |g^(k)(z)| ≤ k! r^{-k} sup over |z - a| ≤ 2r of |g(z)|. The same holds for series: a series of holomorphic functions converging locally uniformly may be differentiated term by term any number of times. The convergence of derivatives is locally uniform, not uniform on all of U.
U ⊂ C is open
each f_n is holomorphic on U
f_n → f uniformly on each compact subset of U

[Proposition 14 of arXiv:2608.19744, 'Conditioned Brownian motion and local equivalence of path ensembles'] For every $z$ with $\Re z>0$, the form $\mathfrak h_z$ is
densely defined, closed, and sectorial on the common domain $\mathcal D$.
Its associated operator, denoted by $H_z$, is the weak realization of
\[
       -\frac12\Delta+zQ.
\]
More precisely,
\[
 \mathcal D(H_z)
 =\left\{f\in\mathcal D:
 -\frac12\Delta f+zQf\in L^2(\mathbb R^d)
 \text{ in the sense of distributions}\right\}.
\]
Furthermore,  $H_z $ has compact resolvent and $H_z^*=H_{\overline z}$.

[Lemma lem:1* of arXiv:2512.09219, 'Strong confluence of geodesics in Liouville quantum gravity'] Fix $q\in (0,1/5)$ and $\Phi\in (0,1/10)$. 
   Then for all $b \in (0,1)$ sufficiently small (depending only on $q,\Phi$), the following is true. For all $z\in \mathbb{C},r>0$, there exist deterministic (depending only on $z,r,q,\Phi,b$) points $u_+,u_-,v_+,v_-$ satisfying $u_+,u_-\in B_{\Phi r}(z-r)$ and $v_+,v_-\in B_{\Phi  r}(z+r)$ such that the balls of Euclidean radius $2br$ around $u_+,u_-,v_+,v_-,u,v$ are all pairwise disjoint and the intersection of the following events, which we call $G_r(z)$, occurs with probability at least $q$.
   \begin{enumerate}
   \item  $\mathscr{X}_{u_-,v_-}^{u_+,v_+}$
   \item  $\Gamma_{u_+,u}\cup \Gamma_{u_-,u}\subseteq B_{\Phi r}(z-r)$ and $\Gamma_{v,v_+}\cup \Gamma_{v,v_-}\subseteq B_{\Phi r}(z+r)$.
   \item  $\mathrm{dist}(\Gamma_{u,v_+}\cup \Gamma_{u,v_-}, \{u_+,u_-\})\geq 2br$ and $\mathrm{dist}(\Gamma_{u_+,v}\cup \Gamma_{u_-,v}, \{v_+,v_-\})\geq 2br$

   \item $\mathrm{dist}(\Gamma_{u_-,u}\cup \Gamma_{u_+,u}, \Gamma_{v,v_-}\cup \Gamma_{v,v_+})\geq 2br$
   \end{enumerate}
   Further, the points $u_+,u_-,v_+,v_-$ can be chosen such that the family of events $\{G_r(z)\}_{z\in \mathbb{C}, r>0}$ is translation and scale invariant.

Let (S,g) be a compact, oriented, boundaryless smooth Riemannian 2-manifold (surface) with Gaussian curvature K. Then the integral of K over S with respect to the Riemannian area element dA equals 2*pi times the Euler characteristic of S: integral_S K dA = 2 pi chi(S). More generally, if S has piecewise smooth boundary, integral_S K dA + integral_{boundary S} k_g ds + sum of exterior angles at corners = 2 pi chi(S), where k_g is the geodesic curvature of the boundary.
S is compact, oriented, and without boundary
g is a smooth Riemannian metric on S

[Definition 11 (Compatibility conditions) of arXiv:2608.30138, 'High-frequency wave propagation for the viscoelastic wave equation with singular memory'] Fix $k\geq1$. Assume $ u_0\in H^{k+1}(\Omega)$, $v_0\in H^k(\Omega)$, 
and
\begin{equation}
\partial_t^\ell u_-
\in
C_{\mathrm b}\bigl((-\infty,0];
H^{k+1-\ell}(\Omega)\bigr),
\qquad 0\leq\ell\leq k.
\end{equation}
Assume also that
\begin{equation}
\partial_t^\ell f
\in
C\bigl([0,T];H^{k-\ell}(\Omega)\bigr),
\qquad 0\leq\ell\leq k.
\end{equation}
In particular, $\partial_t^k f\in C([0,T];L^2(\Omega))$. 

We say that $(u_0,v_0,u_-,f)$ satisfies the compatibility conditions of
order $k$ if the following two conditions hold.

(i) The forward jets agree with the corresponding prehistory jets:
\begin{equation}
\partial_t^j u_-(0-,\cdot)=U_j
\quad\text{in }H^{k+1-j}(\Omega),
\qquad 0\leq j\leq k.
\end{equation}

(ii) The forward jets satisfy the Dirichlet boundary condition:
\begin{equation}
U_j\in H^{k+1-j}(\Omega)\cap H_0^1(\Omega),
\qquad 0\leq j\leq k.
\end{equation}
 
For $0\leq j\leq k$, define the concrete differentiated initial history
by
\begin{equation}
\widehat\eta_j^{\,0}(s,\cdot)
:=
U_j-\partial_t^j u_-(-s,\cdot),
\qquad s\geq0.
\end{equation}
Then \eqref{eq:corner-compatibility} is equivalently
\[
\widehat\eta_j^{\,0}(0,\cdot)=0
\quad\text{in }H^{k+1-j}(\Omega),
\qquad 0\leq j\leq k.
\]
Here $\widehat\eta_j^{\,0}$ denotes the concrete history function. If
$\eta_j^0\in\mathcal M$ denotes the corresponding abstract history
element, no pointwise value $\eta_j^0(0)$ is being asserted.

[Theorem 19 (Linearity \citep{malinovskii2025higgs}) of arXiv:2608.25188, 'Transforms for LLM Quantization:\\ The Great Inversion and Format Co-Design'] To leading order in the per-layer quantization perturbations (the first-order
term vanishing at the trained optimum), the increase in the
model's perplexity decomposes as a sum of per-layer
contributions, each a layer-specific constant times that layer's relative
squared weight error $\|\Delta W_l\|_F^2/\|W_l\|_F^2$. Minimizing each per-layer
error is therefore aligned, in the small-perturbation regime, with minimizing
end-to-end degradation.

[Proposition 8 of arXiv:2608.20252, '2608.20252'] A set $A$ belonging to $C([0,T], \Omega)$ or $\mathcal{D}([0,T],\Omega)$ is compact exactly when
\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] $\{\pi_t: \pi\in A\}$ is relatively compact in $\Omega$ for each $t\in[0,T]$.
\item[(b)] $\lim_{\gamma\downarrow 0} \sup_{\pi\in A} \bar{w}_\pi(\gamma)  =  0$
where $\bar{w}_\pi = w_\pi$ on $C([0,T], \Omega)$ and $\bar{w}_\pi = w'_\pi$ on $\mathcal{D}([0,T], \Omega)$.
\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
Let S be a smooth surface in R^3 with its induced Riemannian metric (first fundamental form), and let K denote its Gaussian curvature (the product of the two principal curvatures). Then K at each point is an intrinsic invariant: it can be computed entirely from the first fundamental form and its derivatives, without reference to how S is embedded in R^3. Consequently, if f: S -> S' is a local isometry between two surfaces in R^3 (a diffeomorphism preserving the induced metric), then K_S(p) = K_{S'}(f(p)) for every p in S.
S is a smooth surface immersed in Euclidean R^3
f is a diffeomorphism between surfaces preserving the induced first fundamental form

Assume~(equation eq:epsexp2 of the paper). For $\delta>0$, let $E_\delta$ be the event that there exist $x,y\in \eta[0,\infty] \cap \eta^R$ such that if $U_{x,y}$ denotes the region bounded between the segments of $\eta[0,\infty]$ and $\eta^R$ from $x$ to $y$, then
\begin{itemize}
\item $U_{x,y} \subseteq B(0,1)$,
\item $\mathrm{diam}(U_{x,y}) \le \delta$,
\item $\mathrm{dist}(U_{x,y},\eta[-\infty,0]) \ge \delta^\zeta$, and
\item $\sup_{u,v \in \partial U_{x,y} \cap \eta} \median{\epsilon}^{-1} \metapproxacres{\epsilon}{U_{x,y}}{u}{v}{\Gamma} \ge L\delta^\zeta+\epsilon^{a_0}$.
\end{itemize}
Then $\mathbf{P}[E_\delta] = o^\infty(L^{-1}\delta)$.
