Own work draft; proof (unaudited), no novelty established. For the equal-weight teacher q_a=(1/3)sum_j N(a E u_j,I_d), where d>=2, E^T E=I_2 and u_j are the unit equilateral vertices, unrestricted physical unit-step population DDPM mean GD admits a fast centroid/slow shape decomposition. Write M=a b 1^T+a sqrt(3/2) Z V^T, V=sqrt(2/3)U^T, P=EE^T, gamma=2a^2/3. On ||b||<=11, ||Z||<=5, b_+=(I/3+(2a^2/3)ZZ^T)b+O(a^4) and Z_+=Z+gamma[(P-ZZ^T)Z+2bb^T Z+O(a^2)]. For ||b_0||<=10 the centroid impulse in shape is O(a^2); the covariance-flow comparison error through rescaled time S is at most C a^2(1+||b_0||^2)exp(76(S+1)). Set sigma_0=1/(80 sqrt(d)), S=10 log(100/(sigma_0 rho)), and choose a^2<=c rho exp(-76(S+1)) with c and rho sufficiently small absolute constants. At N=ceil(3S/(2a^2)), the unrestricted trajectory enters a fixed equilateral tube, with normalized centroid O(a^4). For iid mean initialization N(0,3a^2/(2d)), entry with surrogate angle away from the three unstable sectors has probability at least 553/1600. In that tube the full normal error contracts by 1-kappa a^2 per step and the tangent perturbation is quadratic in the normal error. This is a dynamic lemma; an empirical learning guarantee is not asserted here.
equal weights 1/3; known common covariance I_d; centered equilateral teacher
canonical mixture-score DDPM population objective at one fixed noise time
unrestricted mean parameters; physical Euclidean unit GD step
d>=2, sufficiently small fixed tube radius rho and absolute constant c
a at the stated inverse-polynomial scale; real arithmetic
C06 v1, C07 v2, C08 v2 dependencies remain unaudited

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:6d39032b1739aca3943b901fde292ae0b0b1d25d12d0379c33b897387d9da88f","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/6d/6d39032b1739aca3943b901fde292ae0b0b1d25d12d0379c33b897387d9da88f.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:673f95530dab2b490a9c4f0489c157cf47df9ca849c157d7423e598879b06cc7","bundle_entry_key":"t309-c10","bundle_id":"population.t309-free-centroid-ddpm-entry-normal-tracking-draft","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"Gaussian mixture learning and diffusion objectives","draft":"w721/bundle_006.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.learning:equilateral-gaussian-mixture-ddpm-free-centroid-entry-normal-tracking","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"Own work draft; T309-w721-C10 v2, proof (unaudited), Target 2.

# Fast centroid relaxation releases the centering constraint in the equilateral DDPM route

This is a dynamic lemma toward the named random-initialization target. It builds on C06's free-centroid expansion and C07--C09's equilateral centered route, rather than rechecking those results. All these claims remain unaudited. The present lemma treats a centered true equilateral teacher but imposes no centroid constraint on the learned means or their initialization.

## 1. Coordinates and exact GD metric

Use the notation of C07: U is the 2-by-3 unit equilateral vertex matrix, E^T E=I_2, P=EE^T, V=sqrt(2/3)U^T and c=sqrt(3/2). Every unrestricted mean matrix has a unique decomposition

    M=a b 1^T+a c Z V^T,
    b=M1/(3a), Z=MV/(ac).

The squared Euclidean metric on means is

    ||dM||_F^2=3a^2||db||^2+c^2 a^2||dZ||_F^2.

For the exact population DDPM excess risk F_a(b,Z), physical unit-step mean GD is therefore exactly

    b_+=b-(1/(3a^2)) partial_b F_a,
    Z_+=Z-(2/(3a^2)) grad_Z F_a.                     (1)

Taking a unit step directly in b coordinates would describe a different algorithm and would miss the fast centroid rate.

## 2. Fast centroid and its impulse during covariance entry

C06 Section 5 gives, after substituting C_V=ZZ^T/2,

    F_a(b,Z)=a^2||b||^2
       +a^4[||ZZ^T-P||_F^2/4-b^T ZZ^T b]+a^6 H_a(b,Z). (2)

On ||b||<=11, ||Z||_F<=5, the remainder and any fixed finite number of parameter derivatives are bounded by absolute constants independent of d. The reason is the same finite-span Gaussian/softmax differentiation bound used in C05--C07; increasing the fixed b bound to 11 changes constants only. No analyticity assumption is needed, only the smooth Taylor remainder. We use (2) as settled input from C06, with its metric now included dynamically.

Set gamma=2a^2/3 and f(Z)=(P-ZZ^T)Z. Equation (1) becomes

    b_+=(I/3+(2a^2/3)ZZ^T)b-(a^4/3)partial_b H_a,
    Z_+=Z+gamma[f(Z)+2bb^T Z-a^2 grad_Z H_a].       (3)

For a sufficiently small absolute a and ||Z||<=5,

    ||b_+||<=||b||/2+C a^4,
    ||b_k||<=2^(-k)||b_0||+2C a^4.                 (4)

In particular initial ||b_0||<=10 keeps ||b||<11, conditional only on the shape ball. The dependence of H on b does not invalidate (4), since its b derivative is uniformly bounded throughout this ball.

Compare the Z iterates with the covariance flow of C07, on its stopped radius-5 ball. The extra forcing is bounded by C||b_k||^2+C a^2. Let e_k be the factor error and retain C07's L=76 for the leading flow. Its Euler defect is Cgamma^2. Then

    e_{k+1}<=(1+Lgamma)e_k
                    +Cgamma a^2+Cgamma||b_k||^2+Cgamma^2. (5)

The transient centroid term has total impulse

    gamma sum_{k>=0} 2*4^(-k)||b_0||^2
       =(8/3)gamma||b_0||^2=O(a^2||b_0||^2).       (6)

The constant floor in ||b_k||^2 is O(a^8). Its contribution to the geometric-series bound in (5) is O(a^8 exp(Lk gamma)), not a factor exponential in a^(-2). Thus

    e_k<=C a^2(1+||b_0||^2)exp(Lk gamma).           (7)

The usual constant-forcing geometric series also absorbs the O(a^2) remainder and Euler defect. Choosing the absolute constant in C07's bound a^2<=c rho exp(-76(S+1)) smaller accommodates ||b_0||<=10 and makes (7)<=rho/4 through N=ceil(3S/(2a^2)). The stopped bound closes induction: the exact flow has norm at most 4 and the error is less than 1, so no Z exit occurs. Together with (4), neither coordinate leaves its assumed ball.

At N, b_N=O(a^4); indeed 10*2^(-N)<=C a^4 for the specified small a and S>=1. Consequently the unrestricted means enter the same equilateral tube as C07, with an additional normalized centroid error O(a^4). The fast centroid transient changes the entry estimate by an absolute constant, not a dimension-dependent exponent or a long-time instability factor.

## 3. Gaussian initialization and its entry angle

Initialize all 3d mean entries independently as N(0,3a^2/(2d)). Orthogonal right projection onto span(1) and its complement gives Z_0 with iid N(0,1/d) entries and b_0~N(0,I_d/(2d)). In particular E||b_0||^2=1/2, so

    P(||b_0||>10)<=1/200.

Combining with C07's good centered-factor event G, of probability at least 2/5, by a union bound gives

    P(G and ||b_0||<=10)>=79/200.                  (8)

Independence follows as well from orthogonal Gaussian projections, but is not needed for this probability bound. The joint event is invariant under rotations in the teacher plane, acting simultaneously on b_0 and Z_0. The surrogate factor flow is rotation-equivariant and its planar polar factor exists on G. Thus the argument of C08 gives a uniform surrogate entry angle conditional on this joint event, in either determinant branch. Excluding delta=pi/24 neighborhoods of its three unstable angles removes exactly fraction 1/8. Hence the simultaneous entry-and-angle event has probability at least

    (79/200)*(7/8)=553/1600.                       (9)

Actual unrestricted GD inherits the small angular error via (7); its own objective has no assumed continuous rotational symmetry. The extra b_N term is normal to the equilateral subspace and does not change the projected angle.

## 4. Normal contraction for unrestricted mean parameters

Use normalized Euclidean coordinates J=M/a and the same two-dimensional equilateral linear subspace L as C08, now inside all d-by-3 mean matrices. Exact population GD preserves L. The simultaneous teacher rotation, cyclic label permutation and perpendicular reflection used in C02 still have L as their fixed space even when free means are allowed. In particular the family has zero centroid without requiring the optimization to enforce one.

Write J=v+w, v in L, w perpendicular to L. In a small fixed tube, v has radius r in [0.9,1.1] and ||w||<=rho_0. Decompose w into its centroid and centered-shape parts, using orthonormal coordinates u=sqrt(3)b and Y=cZ for the whole normalized mean space. The physical mean Hessian restricted to normal directions has blocks

    H_cc=(2/3)I+O(a^2),
    H_ss=a^2 A+O(a^2||w||+a^2||b||^2+a^4),
    H_cs=O(a^2||b||+a^4),                           (10)

where A has a dimension-independent positive lower bound and finite upper bound by C05's centered normal Hessian estimate. The centroid block follows from a^2||b||^2 in (2) and the factor 3 of the metric. The b-dependent quartic term contributes O(a^2||b||^2) to the physical shape block and O(a^2||b||) to the cross block. The sixth-order remainder contributes O(a^4). These estimates hold along normal segments within the tube.

Choose rho_0 small and then a small. Completing the square in the centroid block, whose inverse is uniformly bounded, shows that the cross-block Schur correction is O(a^4||b||^2+a^8), smaller than the positive order-a^2 shape block. Consequently, for absolute kappa>0,

    kappa a^2 I <= H_normal <= (9/10)I.             (11)

For the upper bound, the leading centroid eigenvalue is 2/3, all shape eigenvalues are O(a^2), and all remaining blocks vanish as a decreases. Bounds are in physical Euclidean mean coordinates; a single crude global Lipschitz-square estimate is not used to select the step.

Since normal gradient vanishes on L, its value at v+w equals the integral of the normal Hessian applied to w along v+t w. In physical coordinates the unrestricted unit-step normal update is therefore (I-Hbar_normal)w, with the integral block Hbar satisfying (11). Rescaling to J preserves the inequality. Hence

    ||w_+||<=(1-kappa a^2)||w||                     (12)

as long as the radial annulus and tube are retained. The unit physical step is admissible because the largest normal eigenvalue is below 1, despite the unequal centroid and shape time scales.

## 5. Tangent forcing remains quadratic

In J coordinates, use rescaled step a^2 and vector field g_a=-a^(-4)grad_J F_a. It contains a large linear centroid term of order a^(-2), so its full derivative is not uniformly bounded as a->0. However that term is entirely normal: its tangent projection onto L is identically zero. The tangent part and its first two derivatives are uniformly bounded. This follows from (2): after projection and division by a^4, the divergent centroid quadratic disappears, the quartic polynomial has bounded derivatives, and the remainder is O(a^2) with its derivatives.

Invariance of L and self-adjointness of the gradient Hessian imply Pi_L Dg_a(v)w=0 for normal w, just as in C08. Taylor's theorem applied to the tangent projection therefore gives

    ||Pi_L g_a(v+w)-g_a(v)||<=C||w||^2.             (13)

Equations (12),(13) are precisely the normal-decay and summable-tangent-forcing inputs to C08, after replacing its fixed coordinate constants by the J metric constants. They close radial confinement by the same inward leading field (1-r^2)r. Their accumulated angular impulse is O(||w_0||^2), since a^2 sum_k (1-kappa a^2)^(2k) is bounded. An a^(-2) loss from the fast centroid is not present in (13).

## Scope and audit priorities

This lemma establishes entry, entry-angle probability and full normal tracking for unrestricted means in the equilateral population case. A learning corollary is recorded separately to keep this dynamic statement distinct from its empirical concentration extension. The centered teacher, known radius, equal weights, identity covariance and equilateral geometry remain assumptions. No extension to the anisotropic trap C06 or general triangles is implied.

The least trusted steps are uniform remainder derivatives for bounded free centroid, the metric and accumulated transient in (3)--(7), and the physical-coordinate Hessian bounds (10)--(13). Exact polynomial checks can test their finite algebra only; no independent PASS or novelty finding is recorded.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:c2890e8a61a7647f868d72341f59eff40df43d81cc19a057eadc961fc48b3af5","revision_digest":"sha256:6ce3ef4a977b35e41518277aab29962778f98dab10b5309ce032bf407965eaca","source_id":"own-work:T309-w721-C10-v2","source_revision":"2026-10-20-v2-unaudited","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

body: In computational complexity, problems that are in the complexity class NP but are neither in the class P nor NP-complete are called NP-intermediate, and the class of such problems is called NPI. Ladner's theorem, shown in 1975 by Richard E. Ladner, is a result asserting that, if P ≠ NP, then NPI is not empty; that is, NP contains problems that are neither in P nor NP-complete. Since it is also true that if NPI problems exist, then P ≠ NP, it follows that P = NP if and only if NPI is empty.
title: NP-intermediate

[Proposition 55 (Optimality of the $\ell^1$ convolution bound) of arXiv:2602.14618, 'Finitary coding and Gaussian concentration\\ for random fields'] Let $b=(b_m)_{m\in\mathbb Z^d}$ be a nonnegative, absolutely summable kernel
on $\mathbb Z^d$, with
\[
\|b\|_1 := \sum_{m\in\mathbb Z^d} b_m < \infty.
\]
For any finitely supported vector $\delta=(\delta_k)_{k\in\mathbb Z^d}$,
define the quadratic form
\[
Q(\delta) := \sum_{k,\ell\in\mathbb Z^d} \delta_k\,\delta_\ell\, b_{\ell-k}.
\]
Then
\[
\sup_{\delta\neq 0} \frac{Q(\delta)}{\|\delta\|_2^2} = \|b\|_1.
\]
Moreover, this supremum is asymptotically attained by block indicators:
if $\delta^{(L)}_k := \1_{\{k\in\Lambda_L\}}$ with
$\Lambda_L := [-L,L]^d\cap\mathbb Z^d$, then
\[
\lim_{L\to\infty}
\frac{Q(\delta^{(L)})}{\|\delta^{(L)}\|_2^2}
=
\|b\|_1.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Optimality of the $\ell^1$ convolution bound

body: Record of outside readings, 14 October 2026, of Y. Shmalo, A nonergodic flow rule with Galton-Watson stationary measure (repository yspennstate/nonergodic-galton-watson-flow-rule, commit 837dd0c8da7d), which answers Lyons-Peres Question 17.18 negatively. Two readers working from fresh clones without seeing each other, one a Claude model and one a Codex model, both found the argument correct, with no fatal or major finding. They agree on the question's wording and location (Probability on Trees and Networks, 2016 hardback p. 572; Question 3 of Section 10 of Lyons, Pemantle and Peres 1995), that a flow rule may send zero flow to a child (strict positivity is the extra hypothesis of Proposition 17.17), on d_1 = 5/16 and d_2 = 1849/8192, and that GW(.|C = 0) and GW(.|C = 1) are the two ergodic components; one reader also checked stationarity on all Borel sets, the other simulated 333,300 finite trees to depth 15 with no bias after the flow step (a biased control was detected). Minor findings: 'stationary' should allow sigma-finite measures; the step from Borel coordinates to a Borel flow needs one sentence; the repository's check script reports failures but exits with status 0. The n-ray example of Exercise 17.22 gives only absolute continuity, so it does not already answer the question, and a web and arXiv search found no earlier answer (Rousselin 2017/2018 assumes strictly positive child masses). Not refereed.
title: Outside readings of the nonergodic Galton-Watson flow rule (Lyons-Peres Question 17.18), 14 October 2026: two independent readings find it correct

Let X be a real random variable with characteristic function f(t) = E exp(itX) and Q(X; l) = sup_x P(x <= X <= x + l). For all l > 0 and a > 0: Q(X; l) <= (96/95)^2 max(l, 1/a) int_{|t|<a} |f(t)| dt. With a = 1/l: Q(X; l) <= (96/95)^2 l int_{|t|<1/l} |f(t)| dt. Consequently, if int |f| < infinity, X has a density bounded by (96/95)^2 int |f| (Fourier inversion gives the better constant 1/(2 pi)).

Assumes: any real random variable; l > 0, a > 0

body:
[Theo 14 of arXiv:2605.23292, 'Second-order Poincaré inequalities and localization on the Poisson space'] (normal approximation of local U-statistics on metric measure spaces)
Let $(X,d,\nu)$ be a  metric measure space with $\sigma$-finite measure $\nu$ and metric $d$. 
Fix $\delta>0$ and a function $f_\delta:X^k \times \MM \rightarrow \R$ such that $f_\delta((x_1,m_{x_1}),\hdots,(x_k,m_{x_k}))=0$ whenever $\max(d(x_i,x_j): i,j \in \{1,\hdots,k\})\geq\delta$.  Let $W \subset X$ with $\nu(W)<\infty$.
We put
\[
c_\delta := \sup_{x \in X} \nu(B_{2\delta}(x)).
\]
and assume that $c_\delta < \infty$.
Let $(\MM,\QQ)$ be a space of marks and $\hat{\P}$ a Poisson measure of intensity $\nu \otimes \QQ$
on $X \times \MM$.
For $x\in W$ and $m_x \in \MM$, we define
\[
\xi((x,M_x), \tP) := 
\sum_{(x_1,...,x_{k-1}) \in (\P \setminus \{x\})^{k-1}_{\neq}} f_{\delta}((x, M_x),(x_1,M_{x_1}),\hdots,(x_{k-1}, M_{x_{k-1}})),
\]
where $(\P \setminus \{x\})^{k-1}_{\neq}$ denotes the set of $(k-1)$-tuples of distinct points in $\P\setminus \{x\}$.
We define the \textit{local U-statistic}
\[
H := \sum_{x \in \P \cap W} \xi((x,M_x),\hat{\P}),
\]
where $M_x$ is the independent mark associated to $x \in \P$. Then $H$ satisfies the bounds
\[
\mathbf{d}_K \left(\frac{H - \E H}{\smash{\sqrt{\Var H}}}, N \right) \leq c (M^\xi_{5})^{2/5} \max(1,c_\delta)^3 \frac{(\nu(W)+\nu(W_\delta))^{1/2}}{\Var H}
\]
and
\begin{multline*}
\mathbf{d}_W \left(\frac{H - \E H}{\smash{\sqrt{\Var H}}}, N \right) \leq c (M^\xi_{5})^{2/5} \max(1,c_\delta)^3 \frac{(\nu(W)
+\nu(W_\delta))^{1/2}}{\Var H} \\
+ c (M^\xi_{5})^{3/5} \max(1,c_\delta)^3 \frac{\nu(W)+\nu(W_\delta)}{(\Var H)^{3/2}},
\end{multline*}
where $W_\delta = \{x \in X \setminus W: d(x,W)<\delta\}$ and
\[
M_5^\xi := \max(1,\sup_{\substack{z \in X \\ \mathcal{A} \subset X, |\mathcal{A}|\leq 6}} \E |\xi((z,M_z),\hat{\mathcal{P}} \cup \hat{\mathcal{A}})|^5).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theo 14 of arXiv:2605.23292

The transportation-information method, pioneered by Katalin Marton and developed by Michel Talagrand, Cédric Villani, and Felix Otto, establishes concentration inequalities by relating optimal transportation metrics (Wasserstein distances W_1 and W_2) to relative entropy (Kullback-Leibler divergence). By Kantorovich duality, transportation-entropy inequalities immediately imply exponential tail bounds for Lipschitz functions.

[Lemma l:chi.square.lower.tail of arXiv:2607.02013, 'Resolution of the Detection Threshold Conjecture for Random Geometric Graphs in the $d>n$ '] If $X\sim\chi^2(d)$, then it holds for all $x\ge0$ that
    \[
    \mathbb{P}(X \le d-x) \le 
    \mathop{\rm exp}\bigg(-\frac{x^2}{4d}\bigg)\,.
    \]
\begin{proof}
From the moment-generating function of the chi-square distribution, for any $t<0$ we can bound
    \[
    \mathbb{P}(X \le d-x) 
    \le \frac{\mathbb{E}[e^{tX}]}{\mathop{\rm exp}(t(d-x))}
    = \frac{(1-2t)^{-d/2}}{\mathop{\rm exp}(t(d-x))}
    \le \mathop{\rm exp}(tx + dt^2)\,.
    \]
Optimizing over $t<0$ gives the claimed bound.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma l:chi.square.lower.tail of arXiv:2607.02013

[Definition 40 (Tight cores) of arXiv:2606.14564, 'Upper tails for irregular graphs \\ beyond the mean-field regime'] We say that a graph $C\subseteq K_n$ is a \emph{tight core} if there exists a sequence of graphs $\emptyset = C_0 \subseteq C_1 \subseteq \dotsb \subseteq C_\ell=C$ such that, for every $i \in \br{\ell}$, either
  \begin{enumerate}[label=\textbf{(C\arabic*)}]
  \item
    
    $C_i = C_{i-1} \cup K$ for some $K \in \cJ^*(H,C)$ such that $K\cap C_{i-1} \notin \cJ_\emptyset^*$ or
  \item
    
    $C_i = C_{i-1} \cup K_1 \cup K_2$ for some $K_1,K_2\in \cJ^*(H,C)$ such that $K_1 \cap C_{i-1} \in \cJ_\emptyset^*$ but $K_2\cap (C_{i-1} \cup K_1) \notin \cJ_\emptyset^*$;
  \end{enumerate}
  we call $(C_0, C_1, \dotsc, C_\ell)$ a \emph{witness sequence} of $C$.
  Finally, we denote by $\cC$ the set of all tight cores, and by $\cC_m$ the set of all tight cores with at most $m$ edges.
title: Tight cores

[Proposition 102 of arXiv:2609.03875, 'Measure theory without infinities'] Let $\mf A$ be a monoid, $K$ be a finite set, $f(k)\in \mf A$ for all $k\in K$, and $x = \finsum_{k\in K}f(k)$.
  \begin{enumerate}
  \item[(i)] Let $\tau\colon J\to K$ be a bijection. Then $x = \finsum_{j\in J}f(\tau(j))$.
  \item[(ii)] Let $g(k)\in \mf A$ for all $k\in K$. Then $\finsum_{k\in K}(f(k) + g(k)) = x + \finsum_{k\in K}g(k)$.
  \item[(iii)] Let $\mf B$ be a monoid and $\varphi\colon\mf A\to\mf B$ be a monoid homomorphism. Then $\finsum_{k\in K} \varphi(f(k)) = \varphi(x)$.  
  \item[(iv)] Let $K = I\cup J$, where $I\cap J = \varnothing$. Then $x = \finsum_{k\in I}f(k) + \finsum_{k\in J}f(k)$.
  \item[(v)] Let $f(k) = 0$ for all $k\in K$. Then $x = 0$.
  \end{enumerate}

Own-work draft: proof (unaudited); no independent C010 PASS. For every fixed integer n>=2 and q in (0,2), put a=1-q, W_n=sum_{0<=i<j<n}(a^i-a^j)^2 and J_n=q^2*W_n/(2*(n-1)*(1-a^(2n))). Then J_n=[n*q/(2-q)-(1-a^n)/(1+a^n)]/(2*(n-1)) and J_n derivative equals n*(1-a^(n-1))*(1-a^(n+1))/((n-1)*(1+a)^2*(1+a^n)^2)>0. Under the independently checked C004 hypotheses this makes kappa_T*min P_T -> s2*J_n(c/2) and every optimal kappa_T*eta_T -> c/2.
n integer >=2; 0<q<2. Corollary: fixed n, deterministic fixed x0!=0,y0, fixed zero-sum linear terms b_i,c_i with mean squares s1>=0,s2>0; common-Hessian f_i=x^2/2+kappa_T*y^2/2+b_i*x+c_i*y; fresh independent uniform epoch permutations; T=nK; kappa_T*log(T)/T->c in (0,4).

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:a195ea190c4f4c90821eeb752d856ee0283beb1d7574178d86fc9042d1e1bc52","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/a1/a195ea190c4f4c90821eeb752d856ee0283beb1d7574178d86fc9042d1e1bc52.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:6420d090cdf3d68b6b61adfb2f091ae99e6b3e1fb6362dfd941f8db2582541f2","bundle_entry_key":"stationary-variance-strict-monotonicity-common-hessian","bundle_id":"population.t362-jn-monotonicity-009","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"optimization; random reshuffling; geometric sums; stationary variance monotonicity","draft":"w732/bundle_011.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:optimization.randomreshuffling:common-hessian-random-reshuffling-jn-strict-monotonicity","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# C010 v1: strict monotonicity of J_n and the explicit C004 limit

Kind: lemma. Target: 1, requested by the reviewer after PASS of C004.
Status: proof (unaudited). No novelty or general-RR claim.

For every fixed integer n>=2 and q in (0,2), define a=1-q and

    W_n(q)=sum_{0<=i<j<n}(a^i-a^j)^2,
    J_n(q)=q^2*W_n(q)/(2*(n-1)*(1-a^(2n))).

Then J_n is differentiable and strictly increasing on (0,2), with

    J_n(q) = [n*q/(2-q)-(1-a^n)/(1+a^n)]/[2*(n-1)],       (1)

    J_n'(q) = n*(1-a^(n-1))*(1-a^(n+1))
                /[(n-1)*(1+a)^2*(1+a^n)^2] > 0.          (2)

Consequently, in the exact hypotheses of independently checked C004 v1
(fixed n, common diagonal Hessian, x0!=0, s2>0, and
kappa_T*log(T)/T->c in (0,4)),

    kappa_T*min_eta P_T(eta) -> s2*J_n(c/2),
    kappa_T*eta_T -> c/2

for every global minimizing sequence. No claim is made about approaching
c/2 from a particular side at finite T.

## Proof

1. Since -1<a<1, both a!=1 and a!=-1, and 1-a^n and 1+a^n
are strictly positive. Every denominator below is nonzero. The finite
pairwise-square identity gives W_n=n*S2-S1^2, where

    S1=sum_{i=0}^{n-1}a^i=(1-a^n)/(1-a),
    S2=sum_{i=0}^{n-1}a^(2i)=(1-a^(2n))/(1-a^2).

These sums have n terms. Multiplying by q^2=(1-a)^2 and dividing
by 1-a^(2n) yields

    q^2*W_n/(1-a^(2n))
      = n*(1-a)/(1+a) - (1-a^n)/(1+a^n).

Here the last cancellation uses 1-a^(2n)=(1-a^n)*(1+a^n)
and 1-a^n>0. Division by 2*(n-1)>0 proves (1).

2. Differentiate (1) with respect to q, remembering da/dq=-1:

    d[q/(2-q)]/dq=2/(2-q)^2=2/(1+a)^2,
    d[(1-a^n)/(1+a^n)]/dq=2*n*a^(n-1)/(1+a^n)^2.

Thus

    J_n'=n/(n-1)*[1/(1+a)^2-a^(n-1)/(1+a^n)^2].

The numerator on a common positive denominator is

    (1+a^n)^2-a^(n-1)*(1+a)^2
      = 1-a^(n-1)-a^(n+1)+a^(2n)
      = (1-a^(n-1))*(1-a^(n+1)).

All exponents n-1 and n+1 are positive integers. Since |a|<1,
|a^k|<1 for either exponent; hence both factors are strictly positive.
This covers odd and even n, negative a, and a=0 without a parity split.
Equation (2) and the mean value theorem give strict increase on (0,2).

3. C004 v1 already proves convergence to the minimum of J_n over
[c/2,2) and convergence in distance to its argmin. By (2), that minimum
is uniquely attained at c/2. Substitution in the two independently
checked conclusions of C004 gives the displayed explicit limit and
optimizer convergence. Its boundary recovery, not an assumed finite-T
constraint q>=c/2, makes this use legitimate.

## Scope and checks

The n>=2 condition makes n-1 positive and n-1 a positive exponent.
The open q interval is needed for the geometric cancellations and positive
denominators. Endpoints q=0 and q=2 are not included in (1)-(2) as written.
The C004 corollary retains its positive stiff-noise and slow-initialization
hypotheses; this lemma does not remove them. Growing n remains out of scope
for the asymptotic corollary, even though the finite algebra holds for each n.

Finite exact checks, if completed, certify only their listed rational inputs.
Any formal check of the numerator identity concerns that algebraic identity,
not the derivative, positivity, mean-value argument or asymptotic corollary.
The exact factorization and the C004 substitution await independent audit.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:e8169642cf544470d8e437ba5ab4344377483951617d36d5008c19da19731a49","revision_digest":"sha256:6d1664a1ec55993d9eaff8bc449838dcf1f338184ec16d555666d2fa5de69914","source_id":"own-work:w732:T362:C010:v1","source_revision":"C010-v1-proof-unaudited; depends on approved C004 v1 for optimizer corollary","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

[Lemma lem:saddle of arXiv:2512.17808, 'Zeros of polynomial powers under the heat flow'] For each $t>0$,  $z \in \mathcal D_t$, there exists a unique saddle point $u_t^*(z)$ such that:
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item There exists a path $\gamma=(-i\infty, -i C]\cup\gamma_C\cup [+iC, +i\infty)$ from $-i\infty$ to $+i\infty$, for some $C>0$ and some simple curve $\gamma_C$ from $-iC$ to $+iC$, that contains $u_t^*(z)$ and avoids the singularities $\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_d$.
		\item For all points $u\in\gamma\setminus \{u_t^*(z)\}$, we have $G(z,u_t^*(z))>G(z,u)$.
		\item 
		The choice $u_t^*(z)$ is the unique saddle point $u_t^j(z)$ such that for each $\varepsilon>0$ there exists no path in $\Sigma(G(z,u_t^j(z))-\varepsilon)$ connecting $-i\infty$ and $+i\infty$, whereas there exists such a path in $\Sigma(G(z,u_t^j(z))+\varepsilon)$.

[Definition def:F-function of arXiv:2608.12415, 'Sharp Phase Transition for Ellipsoid Fitting'] Let \(\mu_{\mathrm{sc}}\) be the semicircle distribution on \([-2,2]\), with density
\(
    f_{\mathrm{sc}}(x)
    =
    \frac{\sqrt{4-x^2}}{2\pi}.
\)
Define

\[F(x)=\textup{max}(2x,0)=\begin{cases}
        2x, & x>0,\\
        0,  & x\leq 0.
    \end{cases}\]
Let
\(
    P_j(x):=U_j\left(\frac{x}{2}\right),
\)
where \(U_j\) is the \(j\)-th Chebyshev polynomial of the second kind. Then
\(\{P_j\}_{j\ge0}\) is an orthonormal basis for
\(L^2([-2,2],\mu_{\mathrm{sc}})\), with \(P_0=1\) and \(P_1=x\).

We write
\[
    F(x)
    =
    C_F+x+\sum_{j\ge2} b_j P_j(x),
\]
where
\(
    C_F
    =
    \mathbb E_{x\sim\mu_{\mathrm{sc}}}[F(x)]
    =
    \frac{8}{3\pi},
    \mathbb E_{x\sim\mu_{\mathrm{sc}}}[F(x)P_1(x)]=1,
\)
and, for \(j\ge2\),
\(
    b_j\coloneqq
    \mathbb{E}_{x\sim\mu_{\mathrm{sc}}}[F(x)P_j(x)].
\)

[Lemma l:invertibly-independence-dirstructure of arXiv:2510.13659, 'On the energy image density conjecture of Bouleau and Hirsch'] Let  $(X,\mathcal{X}, \mu,\mathcal{F},\mathcal{E})$ be a Dirichlet structure (in the sense of Definition (d:dirstructure of the paper)) with carr\'e du champ $\gamma:\mathcal{F} \times \mathcal{F} \to L^1(\mu)$. Consider this also as a $2$-Dirichlet structure  $(X,\mathcal{X}, \mu,\mathcal{E}_2, \mathcal{F}_2, \Gamma_2)$  in the sense of Definition (d:p-dir-structure of the paper) as given by Lemma (lem:dirichlet of the paper).
		Let $n \in \mathbb{N}$,     $\bphi=(\phi_1,\ldots,\phi_n) \in \mathcal{F}_2^n$ and let $\gamma(\bphi)$ denote the associated carr\'e du champ matrix as defined in (equation e:def-cdc-matrix of the paper).  Then the following are equivalent:
		\begin{enumerate}[(a)]
			\item $\det(\gamma(\bphi))>0$ for $\mathds{1}_{\{\Tr (\gamma(\bphi))>0\}}\cdot \mu$-a.e.~$A$.
			\item $\bphi$ is $2$-linearly independent on $A$.
		\end{enumerate}
		Furthermore, $\bphi$ is $2$-linearly independent on the set $I_{\bphi}:=\{x \in X \vert \det(\gamma(\bphi)(x))>0\}$ and the measures
		$\mathds{1}_{I_{\bphi}} \cdot \nu$ and $\mathds{1}_{I_{\bphi}} \cdot \Lambda_{\bphi}$ are mutually absolutely continuous. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition prop:variance-canonical of arXiv:2608.19050, 'Online Permutation Embedding: \\ Optimal Stopping and Scaling Laws'] There is a finite universal constant $C$ such that the following holds. Fix any $k <\infty$, let $S$ be a fringe subtree of $\mathcal{T}_\pi$ for some $k$-permutation $\pi$, and let $\mathcal{A}_S^*$ be the canonical recursive algorithm for embedding $S$. Then,
\[
\EE T_{\mathcal{A}_S^*}=\beta(S)
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\pVar{T_{\mathcal{A}_S^*}}\le C\,\beta(S)^{3/2}.
\]
Consequently,
\[
\PP[\mathcal{S}]{\ba{T_{\mathcal{A}_S^*}-\beta(S)} > y\,\beta(S)^{3/4}} \le \frac{C}{y^2},
\qquad y\ge 1.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Variance bound for the canonical algorithm

[Dfn 11 ({\cite[p.\ 1) of arXiv:2605.27974, 'Discrete approximation of semi-Dirichlet forms with non-symmetric perturbations of resista'] {oshima2013semi}}] 
$(\mathcal{A},\mathcal{F})$ is called a closed form on $\mathscr{H}$ if the following hold: 
\begin{enumerate}
    \item[$\mathrm{(SD1)}$]
    There exists $\lambda \geq 0$ such that $\mathcal{A}_{\lambda}(u) \geq 0$ 
    for any $u \in  \mathcal{F}$.
    \item[$\mathrm{(SD2)}$]
    $\mathcal{A}_{\lambda+1}(\cdot)^{1/2}$ is a complete norm on $\mathcal{F}$.
    \item[$\mathrm{(SD3)}$]
    There exists $K \geq 1$ such that
    \begin{equation}
    \abs{\mathcal{A}(u,v)}
    \leq
    K\mathcal{A}_{\lambda}(u)^{1/2}\mathcal{A}_{\lambda}(v)^{1/2}, 
    \quad u,v \in  \mathcal{F}.
    \end{equation}
\end{enumerate}
When $\mathscr{H} = L^2(X,\mu)$ with a measure space $(X,\mu)$, 
a closed form $(\mathcal{A},\mathcal{F})$ on $L^2(X,\mu)$ is called a semi-Dirichlet form 
on $L^2(X,\mu)$ if the following holds in addition:
\begin{enumerate}[resume]
\item[$\mathrm{(SD4)}$]
For any $f \in \mathcal{F}$ and $a \geq 0$, we have $f \wedge a \in \mathcal{F}$ 
and $\mathcal{A}(f \wedge a,f-f \wedge a) \geq 0$.
\end{enumerate}
Condition $\mathrm{(SD4)}$ is called the Markov property. 

Also, a semi-Dirichlet form $(\mathcal{A},\mathcal{F})$ on $L^2(X,\mu)$ is called 
a Dirichlet form on $L^2(X,\mu)$ if $\mathcal{A}$ is symmetric and 
we can take $0$ as the constant $\lambda$ in $\mathrm{(SD1)}$.

[Definition 13 of arXiv:2607.27786, 'Gaussian free field in annulus: \\BPZ equations and crossing probabilities for level lines'] Fix $\kappa\in (0,4]$ and $n\ge 1$ and $\ell\in\Z$. 
Fix $\bs{\alpha}, \bs{\beta}\in\LX_n$. 
For $1\le j\le n$, let $\gamma^j$ be annulus $\SLE_{\kappa}(\LFcro{1}^{(\kappa;\ell)})$ in $(\A_r;\ee^{\ii \alpha_j};\ee^{\ii \beta_j})$. 
Let $\Pind{n}^{(\kappa;\ell)}$ be the probability measure on $\bs{\gamma}=(\gamma^{1}, \ldots, \gamma^{n})$ under which the curves are independent.
As $\LFcro{n}^{(\kappa; \ell)}$ satisfies annulus BPZ equations~\eqref{eqn::annulus_BPZ_alpha} with $F(r)=F_n(r)$ given by~\eqref{eqn::F(r)inBPZ}, 
the process $M_{\bs{t}}(\LFcro{1}^{(\kappa;\ell)}; \LFcro{n}^{(\kappa;\ell)})$ is $n$-time local martingale under $\Pind{n}^{(\kappa;\ell)}$ due to Proposition~\ref{prop::multitime_mart_annulus}. 
We define $n$-annulus $\SLE_{\kappa}(\LFcro{n}^{(\kappa;\ell)})$ in $(\A_r; \ee^{\ii\bs{\alpha}}, \ee^{\ii\bs{\beta}-r})$ as the probability measure obtained by tilting $\Pind{n}^{(\kappa;\ell)}$ by the $n$-time local martingale $M_{\bs{t}}(\LFcro{1}^{(\kappa;\ell)}; \LFcro{n}^{(\kappa;\ell)})$. 
We denote by $\Pcro{n}^{(\kappa; \ell)}=\Pcro{n}^{(\kappa; \ell)}(\A_r; \ee^{\ii\bs{\alpha}}, \ee^{\ii\bs{\beta}})$ the law of $n$-annulus $\SLE_{\kappa}(\LFcro{n}^{(\kappa;\ell)})$.

Own-work research draft; status proof (unaudited), independent review pending. Fix a feedforward ReLU architecture with L>=1 affine layers and affine output in R^D. Each affine coefficient is fixed or one of W>=1 scalar parameter slots, possibly shared. All coefficients have magnitude <=R>0. F is the maximum number of incoming weighted edges per neuron, counting repeated uses of a shared slot. The latent law is fixed and supported on [-1,1]^d; graph and fixed coefficients are target-independent. Set K=max(1,R(F+1)) and Cnet=sqrt(D)*L*(F+1)*K^(L-1). The output laws have a W1 t-cover with at most [1+ceil(2R*Cnet/t)]^W elements for every t>0, by rounding the parameters within t/Cnet in maximum norm. For a target class whose error against every <=2^S output family is at least c(S+1)^(-alpha), the bounded-real-weight minimax error E_R is at least c[W*log2(1+ceil(2R*Cnet/t))+1]^(-alpha)-t. In particular E_R<=epsilon requires W*log2(1+ceil(2R*Cnet/epsilon))+1 >=[c/(2epsilon)]^(1/alpha). The saved density-slack manifold packing uses alpha=1/k; the fixed-volume uniform-manifold packing uses alpha=2/k, each under its own stated compatibility conditions. No novelty or unrestricted-real-weight lower rate is asserted; unbounded magnitude, changing latent law or uncounted architecture choices are excluded.
Fixed architecture and latent law; bounded cube latent support; all coefficients bounded by R; F counts edges, W counts variable slots; hidden coordinate ReLU and affine output.
title: Draft: deep ReLU bounded-real-weight Wasserstein cover with shared parameters

Let (X, Sigma, mu) be a finite measure space and let F be a subset of L^1(mu). Then F is uniformly integrable if and only if there exists a nondecreasing convex function Phi on [0, infinity) with Phi(0) = 0 and Phi(t)/t tending to infinity as t tends to infinity, such that sup over f in F of integral Phi(|f|) dmu is finite. The 'if' direction is the one used in practice: a uniform bound on a superlinear moment forces uniform integrability.
mu finite.
Phi must be convex, nondecreasing and superlinear (Phi(t)/t to infinity);
mere growth of Phi is not enough.

Let $\mathscr{X} $ be a topological space such that there exists a sequence $\{ {f}_{m}\} $ of continuous functions ${f}_{m}\colon \mathscr{X}  \to \mathbb{R} $ that separates points of $\mathscr{X} $. Let us denote by $\mathcal{S} $ the $\sigma $-algebra generated by the maps $\{ {f}_{m}\} $.
Then

and ${\xi }_{k}$ converges to $\xi $ on $\Omega $.
Moreover, the law of $\xi $ is a Radon measure.

[Lemma 2 of arXiv:2606.23383, 'Near-Lipschitz stability of the Kim--Milman flow map'] Let $X_0 \sim \mu$ and $Z \sim \gamma$ be independent, and write $X_t = e^{-t}\,X_0 + \sqrt{1-e^{-2t}}\,Z$.
    Then, for all $t > 0$,
    \begin{align}
        \nabla \log \frac{q_t^\mu}{\gamma}(x_t)
        &= -\frac{e^{-t}}{1-e^{-2t}}\, \E[e^{-t} X_t - X_0 \mid X_t = x_t]\,, \\[0.25em]
        \nabla^2 \log \frac{q_t^{\mu}}{\gamma}(x_t)
        &= -\frac{e^{-2t}}{1-e^{-2t}}\,I + \frac{e^{-2t}}{(1-e^{-2t})^2} \Cov(X_0 \mid X_t=x_t)\,.
    \end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma 2 of arXiv:2606.23383

[Thmx 2 (Lower soft edge limit, $\liminf a_n/n>0$, \cite{RRV}) of arXiv:2607.08536, 'Soft edge limit of the Laguerre beta-ensemble at the lower edge'] Assume $\liminf\limits_{n\to \infty} \frac{a_n}{n}>0$, and let $\Lambda_{n}\sim \mathrm{Laguerre}_{n,\beta,a_n}$. Then as $n\to \infty$, we have
 \begin{align*}
     \frac{((n+a_n) n)^{1/6}}{(\sqrt{n+a_n}-\sqrt{n})^{4/3}}(\Lambda_n-(\sqrt{n+a_n}-\sqrt{n})^2)\Rightarrow \Airyb. 
 \end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
Consider the Hamilton-Jacobi initial value problem u_t + H(Du) = 0 in R^n times (0, infinity) with u = g at time 0, where H is convex and superlinear (H(p)/|p| tends to infinity) and g is Lipschitz. Then the function u(x,t) = min over y in R^n of ( t L( (x - y)/t ) + g(y) ), with L the Legendre transform of H, is Lipschitz, solves the equation almost everywhere, attains the initial data continuously, and is the unique viscosity solution. In particular, for H(p) = |p| the formula gives the distance-like representation u(x,t) = min over |x - y| <= t of g(y), and for g the indicator-style data of a set the solution is the signed distance function, which is why the Hopf-Lax representation is the control-theoretic tool for distance functions.
H convex AND superlinear, g Lipschitz (or merely continuous with growth conditions, with care).
Without convexity of H the formula is not the viscosity solution;
uniqueness holds in the viscosity class, not among almost-everywhere solutions, of which there are many.

[Lemma of arXiv:2608.25065, 'Detection of first homology via random geometric graphs in the thermodynamic regime'] \label[lemma]{good cover exists}
    For any $\epsilon >0$,
    there exists $r_0(\epsilon,M)$
    such that the following holds
    for all
    $0 < r \le r_0$.
    Taking $\Delta = \lfloor e^{2d\epsilon} 13^d \rfloor $,
    $K=4 Q \rho r |\log r|$
    and $L = (\Delta + 1)K + 2r$,
    there exists a finite open cover
    $\mathcal{O}$
    of $M$
    such that
    for each $x \in M$
    there exists $U$ in $\mathcal{O}$
    such that
    $\bar{B}(x,L) \subseteq U$,
    and we have
    \[
        \sup_{x \in M}
        \#
        \{U \in \mathcal{O}:B(x,(\Delta+1)K) \cap U \ne \emptyset \}
        \le 
        \Delta.
    \]
    Moreover, for each $U \in \mathcal{O}$,
    we have
    $\mathrm{diam}(U) \le 
    (\Delta + 1)16 Q \rho r |\log r| + 8r$.

body: Let K(x,y) be a measurable kernel on (Omega_1 x Omega_2, mu_1 x mu_2), and suppose there exist a measurable function p > 0 and constants C_1, C_2 > 0 such that integral over y of |K(x,y)| p(y) d mu_2(y) <= C_1 p(x) for mu_1-almost every x, and integral over x of |K(x,y)| p(x) d mu_1(x) <= C_2 p(y) for mu_2-almost every y. Then the integral operator (Tf)(x) = integral over y of K(x,y) f(y) d mu_2(y) defines a bounded linear operator from L^2(mu_2) to L^2(mu_1) with operator norm at most sqrt(C_1 C_2). [standard, e.g. Halmos and Sunder, Bounded Integral Operators on L2 Spaces]

[Definition of arXiv:2608.30848, '\huge \bf Limit Laws of the Iterated Logarithm Under Sub-linear Expectations'] \begin{itemize}
\item[(i)](Identical distribution) Let $\bm{X}_1$ and $\bm{X}_2$ be two $n$-dimensional random vectors defined on sub-linear expectation spaces $(\Omega_1,\mathscr{H}_1,\widehat{\mathbb E}_1)$ and $(\Omega_2,\mathscr{H}_2,\widehat{\mathbb E}_2)$, respectively. If for any $\varphi\in C_{b,Lip}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ we have
$$ \widehat{\mathbb E}_1[\varphi(\bm{X}_1)]=\widehat{\mathbb E}_2[\varphi(\bm{X}_2)], $$
then they are said to be identically distributed, denoted by $\bm{X}_1\overset{d}{=}\bm{X}_2$. If $X_i\overset{d}{=}X_1$ for each $i\geq 1$, then the sequence of random variables $\{X_n;n\geq 1\}$ is said to be identically distributed.
 \item[(ii)](Independence) In a sub-linear expectation space $(\Omega,\mathscr{H},\widehat{\mathbb E})$, a random vector $\bm{Y}=(Y_1,\cdots,Y_n)$, $Y_i\in\mathscr{H}$ is said to be independent of another random vector $\bm{X}=(X_1,\cdots,X_m)$, $X_i\in\mathscr{H}$ under $\widehat{\mathbb E}$, if for every test function $\varphi\in C_{b,Lip}(\mathbb{R}^m\times\mathbb{R}^n)$ we have
     $$\widehat{\mathbb E} [\varphi(\bm{X},\bm{Y})]=\widehat{\mathbb E} [\widehat{\mathbb E} [\varphi(\bm{x},\bm{Y})]\vert_{\bm{x}=\bm{X}}].$$

  If for each $i\geq 1$, $X_{i+1}$ is independent of $(X_1,\cdots,X_i)$, then the sequence of random variables $\{X_n;n\geq 1\}$ is said to be independent.
\end{itemize}

[Lemm l:I-given-B of arXiv:2607.18194, 'Temperature chaos in directed polymers'] Fix any Borel set $B\in\mathcal{B}(\mathbb{R}^2)$ and any square-integrable random variable $X\in L^2(\Xi,\mathcal{F},\mathbb{P})$, and denote its chaos expansion by 
    $X = \sum_{n=0}^\infty I_n(f_n)$ (see (p:chaos-expansion of the paper)).
    Then we have
    \begin{align*}
        \mathbb{E}[X|\mathcal{F}_B]
        = \sum_{n=0}^\infty I_n(f_n \1_{B}^{\otimes n})
        \qquad\text{in $L^2(\Xi,\mathcal{F},\mathbb{P})$,}
    \end{align*}
    where for $n=0$, the $0\textsuperscript{th}$ tensor power of any function is identically $1$.
    Note that for $n\geqslant 1$, we have $\1_B^{\otimes n} = \1_{B^n}$, where $B^n\coloneqq B\times\cdots\times B$ is the $n$-fold Cartesian product.

    It follows by (equation e:parseval of the paper) that for any $X,Y\in L^2(\Xi,\mathcal{F},\mathbb{P})$ with chaos expansions $X=\sum_{n=0}^\infty I_n(f_n)$ and $Y=\sum_{n=0}^\infty I_n(g_n)$, we have
    \begin{align}
        \mathbb{E}\Bigl[
            \mathbb{E}[X|\mathcal{F}_B]\cdot\mathbb{E}[Y|\mathcal{F}_B]
        \Bigr]
        &=
        \sum_{n=0}^\infty \mathbb{E}\left[
            I_n(f_n\1_B^{\otimes n})
            I_n(g_n\1_B^{\otimes n})
        \right].
    \end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Conditional expectations of chaos expansions

[Theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] We can talk about scalar products and lengths in $\mathbb C^N$,
$$<x,y>=\sum_ix_i\bar{y}_i\qquad,\qquad ||x||=\sqrt{\sum_i|x_i|^2}$$
which are related by the following conversion formulae,
$$||x||=\sqrt{<x,x>}\quad,\quad <x,y>
=\frac{||x+y||^2-||x-y||^2+i||x+iy||^2-i||x-iy||^2}{4}$$
and the following happen:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $<\lambda x,y>=<x,\bar{\lambda}y>=\lambda<x,y>$.

\item $<x+y,z>=<x,z>+<y,z>$.

\item $<x,y+z>=<x,z>+<y,z>$. 

\item $<x,y>=\overline{<y,x>}$.

\item $||\lambda x||=|\lambda|\cdot||x||$.

\item $|<x,y>|\leq||x||\cdot||y||$.

\item $||x+y||\leq||x||+||y||$.

\item $x\perp y\iff<x,y>=0$, by definition.
\end{enumerate}
title: Unnumbered theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'

[Lemma lem.logconcdomination of arXiv:2603.11043, 'An asymptotically optimal bound for the concentration function of a sum of independent int'] Let $\epsilon > 0$. Let $X$ be a log-concave integer random variable,
     
    and let $Y$ be any integer random variable.

For n>=3 put p=n^(-1/6), a=n^(1/3), b=sqrt(n*log n). Let R have masses (1-p)/2 at +/-a and p/2 at +/-b, and X_n=n+R. Then X_n>0, E X_n=n, and (X_n-n)/n^(1/3) converges in total variation to a symmetric sign, but Var(X_n)=(1-p)*n^(2/3)+n^(5/6)*log n, with log Var(X_n)/(2 log n)->5/12. For every lambda>=0, P(|X_n-E X_n|>=lambda*sqrt(n/log n))<=exp(1/3)*exp(-lambda/6). This is an abstract random-variable counterexample, not an iid lattice FPP construction.

Let R_n have masses (1-p_n)/2 at each of +/-a_n and p_n/2 at each of +/-b_n. Set X_n=n+R_n.     log Var(X_n)/(2 log n) -> 5/12,

[Dfn 97 (occupation measures) of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] In the setting described above,
let $\rho_{\vY}$ be the occupation measure of the $\vY$ process, so that
	\[\int_{t,y} 
	f(t,y)\,\rho_{\vY}(dt\,dy)
	= \bE
	\int_0^1 f(t,\vY(t))\,dt\,.
	\]
Let $\rho_{D^i}$ and $\rho_{Q^{ij}}$
be the occupation measures of the drift and quadratic variation processes, so that
	\begin{align*}
	\int_{t,y}
	f(t,y) \rho_{D^i}(dt\,dy) 
	&= \bE
	\int_0^1 f(t,\vY(t))\,dD^i(t)\,,\\
	\int_{t,y} f(t,y) 
	\rho_{Q^{ij}}(dt\,dy) 
	&= \bE
	\int_0^1 f(t,\vY(t))\,dQ^{ij}(t)\,.
	\end{align*}
for any continuous bounded function $f$.

[Cor co:spectral-dimension of arXiv:2604.14122, 'The scaling limit of random walk and\\ the intrinsic metric on planar critical percolation'] Let $\beta$ be the scaling exponent of the CLE$_6$ resistance metric defined in~[my2025diffusion]. Let $\mathrm{P}_0$ denote the law of the simple random walk on the IIC starting at $0$, let $\mathrm{p}_{2t}(0,0)$ denote its return probability after $2t$ steps, and let $\tau_n$ denote its hitting time of $\partial B(0,n)$. Under $\mathbf{P}_{\mathrm{IIC}}$, almost surely,
    \begin{align*}
    \mathrm{p}_{2t}(0,0) &= t^{-\frac{91/48}{91/48+\beta}+o(1)} \quad\text{as } t\to\infty ,\\
    \quad \mathrm{E}_0 \tau_n &= n^{91/48+\beta+o(1)} \quad\text{as } n\to\infty .
    \end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Lem 181 (annealed second moment bounds for $\bar{D}^{\Ising}$ and $\bar{D}^{\frozen,\Ising}$) of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] For $\bar{D}^{\Ising}$ as in \eqref{e:drift.error.Ising}, we have
	\[\E\Big[\Delta\bar{D}^{\Ising}(q_d)^2\Big]
	\le\frac{ L^{O(1)}\BUCKETS\delta}
		{N}
	 \]
for all $0\le d\le \dmax-1$, with $\BUCKETS$ as in 
\eqref{e:buckets.scB}. The same bound holds with $\bar{D}^{\frozen,\Ising}$ in place of $\bar{D}^\Ising$.
	
\begin{proof} Recalling the notation from \eqref{e:normalized.vectors.y}, we can rewrite \eqref{e:drift.error.Ising} as
	\[
	\frac{\Delta \bar{D}^{\Ising}(q_d)}{(\delta_d)^{1/2}}
	=\frac{1}{|B|^{1/2}}
	\bigg(\sum_{i\in B}
	\frac{\be_i}{|B|^{1/2}},
	\by(q_{d+1})\bigg)
	\equiv \frac{(\be_B,\by(q_{d+1}))}{|B|^{1/2}}\,,
	\]
where we abbreviate $B\equiv B^\Ising$.
The vector $\be_B$ is measurable with respect to $\cG(q_d)$. It follows by applying 
Lemma~\ref{l:y.subgaus} that
	\[
	\frac{\E[\Delta \bar{D}^{\Ising}(q_d)^2]}{\delta_d}
	= \frac{1}{N}\E\bigg[
	\sum_{B\in\mathcal{B}^{\Ising}(q_d)}
	(\be_B,\by)^2\bigg]
	\le \frac{L^{O(1)}\BUCKETS}{N}\,.
	\]
This proves the claim for $\bar{D}^{\Ising}$, and the claim for
$\bar{D}^{\frozen,\Ising}$ follows by using \eqref{e:barD.vs.plus}.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: annealed second moment bounds for $\bar{D}^{\Ising}$ and $\bar{D}^{\frozen,\Ising}$

[Lem 93 of arXiv:2605.23308, 'Convergence rate estimates for semigroups and heat kernels associated with resistance form'] Suppose that $\mu$ satisfies $\rm{(A1)}$ and
take $x\in F$ and $B(x_0,r)\neq F$. Then the following hold.
\begin{itemize}

[Prop Feynman-Kac of arXiv:2411.05441, 'Sticky diffusions on star graphs : characterization and It\^o formula'] Let $T > 0$ and $u \in C^{1,2}_b((0,T) \times \Gamma) \cap C_b([0,T] \times \Gamma)$  be a solution to
 \begin{equation}
  \begin{cases}
   -\partial_t u(t,\mathsf{x}) - L u(t,\mathsf{x}) = f(t,\mathsf{x}) \quad & \textnormal{for all } t \in (0,T), \, \mathsf{x} \neq \mathsf{v}, \\
   u_i(t,0) = u_j(t,0) \quad & \textnormal{for all } 1 \leq i, j \leq N, \, t \in (0,T), \\
   -\eta \partial_t u(t,\mathsf{v}) - \sum_{i=1}^N \rho_i \partial_x u_i(t,0) = \eta \theta(t) \quad &  \textnormal{for all } t \in (0,T), \\
   u(T, \cdot) = u_T,
  \end{cases}
 \end{equation}
 with $f \in C([0,T], PC(\Gamma))$, $u_T \in C_b(\Gamma)$ and $\theta \in C([0,T])$. Then
 \[
  u(t,\mathsf{x}) = \mathbf E \left[u_T(X(T)) + \int_t^T f(s,X(s)) \mathbf 1_{\{X(s) \neq \mathsf{v} \}} + \theta(s) \mathbf 1_{\{X(s) = \mathsf{v} \}} ds \big \vert X(t) = \mathsf{x} \right ],
 \]
 where $X$ is the sticky diffusion generated by $L$ with stickiness $\eta$.

For both lattice trees and lattice animals on $\mathbb{T}_r^d$,
there are constants $c,C>0$ such that
for all $p \in [p_c - \delta_L, p_c)$ and all $x\in \mathbb{T}_r^d$,
\begin{align}

G_p ^{ \mathbb{T} } (x)
	&\le G_p(x) + \frac{C}{m(p)^2 r^d},
	\\

G_p ^{ \mathbb{T} }(x)
	&\ge \bigg(1- \frac{C}{m(p)^8r^d} \biggr)
	\biggl( G_p(x) + \frac {c} {m(p)^2 r^d} \bigg)
\qquad (p_c - p \le c r^{-4}).
\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lem bootstrap-inductive-step of arXiv:2601.19145, 'Stochastic Persistence in Infinite Dimensions'] Define $\eta = 1/2 + \beta > 0$, where $\beta$ is as in  (SPDE-G-lem of the paper) and recall that $N$ is the dimension of domain $D$. For all $T > 0$, $p > 1$, $q \in (2,\infty]$ we have

    $$\frac{1}{r} = \Big(\frac{\eta \wedge p^{-1}}{N} + \frac{1}{q}\Big) \wedge \frac{1}{2} \,.$$

body:
[Theorem 24 (Sign theorem at the starting sites) of arXiv:2608.15805, 'Spectral duality structures and the Fisher--Rao geometry of reset distributions'] Let $(\Delta_{m-1},C)$ be a spectral duality structure satisfying
the vertex condition \textup{(V)}. Then:
\begin{itemize}
\item[\textup{(i)}] at every neutral site,
      $C(e_{z_0},\cdot)\equiv C^\ast$ \textup{(}no hypothesis
      needed\textup{)};
\item[\textup{(ii)}] at every site $z$ of an active orbit $O$, the
      map $\gamma\mapsto C(e_z,\gamma)$ is strictly monotone on
      $(0,1)$, with
      \[
      \operatorname{sgn}\partial_\gamma C(e_z,\gamma)
      =\varepsilon\cdot\operatorname{sgn}[\mathbf d_O]_z
      \qquad\text{for all }\gamma;
      \]
\item[\textup{(iii)}] the two members of each orbit respond in
      opposite directions,
      \[
      \operatorname{sgn}\partial_\gamma C(e_z,\gamma)
      =-\operatorname{sgn}\partial_\gamma C(e_{\sigma(z)},\gamma),
      \]
      so one starting site of the pair is strictly ascending and
      the other strictly descending; the site involution $\sigma$,
      which permutes the vertices, exchanges the two classes.
\end{itemize}

[Definition def:admissible of arXiv:2609.03264, 'Certified Spherical MUSIC for 3D Localization under Adversarial Subspace Perturbations'] Let $f\colon B_1(0)\to [0,\infty)$, let
		\[
		X=\{\bm{x}_1,\dots,\bm{x}_s\}\subset B_1(0),
		\]
		and let $\varepsilon,\rho,\tau_0,\tau_1$ satisfy
		\[
			0\leq\varepsilon<\rho,
			\qquad
			0\le \tau_0<\tau_1.
		\]
		We say that $f$ is a threshold-admissible optimization landscape for $X$,
		with parameters
		$(\varepsilon,\rho,\tau_0,\tau_1)$, if:
		\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
			\item for every $j=1,\dots,s$, the function $f$ has a 
			local minimum
			$\widetilde{\bm{x}}_j\in
			\overline{B_\varepsilon(\bm{x}_j)}$;
			\item the relevant minima are uniformly shallow and all points
			outside the certified neighborhoods are uniformly higher:
			\begin{eqnarray}
			\max_{1\le j\le s} f(\widetilde{\bm{x}}_j)&\le& \tau_0,\\
			f(\bm{z})&\ge &\tau_1, 
			\quad
			\forall
			\bm{z}\in B_1(0)\setminus
			\bigcup_{j=1}^s B_\rho(\bm{x}_j).
			\end{eqnarray}
		\end{enumerate}
title: Threshold-admissible landscape

body:
Let X_n, X be random variables or vectors with X_n -> X in distribution as n -> infinity, and let Y_n -> c in probability for a constant c. Then X_n + Y_n -> X + c in distribution, X_n Y_n -> c X in distribution, and, provided c is not 0, X_n / Y_n -> X / c in distribution. More generally, if g(x,y) is continuous at every point (x,c), then g(X_n,Y_n) -> g(X,c) in distribution. Slutsky's theorem lets one combine a distributional limit with a probability limit as though the latter were a genuine constant. Due to Eugen Slutsky.
For the scalar arithmetic conclusions, X_n, X, and Y_n are real-valued random variables and c is a deterministic real constant.
X_n converges in distribution to X.
Y_n converges in probability to c.
For division, c is nonzero.
For a vector or general mapping formulation, explicitly choose separable metric state spaces S, T, and U; take X_n and X to be measurable S-valued random elements, Y_n to be measurable T-valued random elements, and c in T deterministic.
For the general mapping conclusion, g:S x T -> U is measurable and continuous at every point (x,c) with x in S; a weaker almost-sure continuity formulation would require a separately revised statement.
Any named vector addition, multiplication, or division operation must be explicitly defined and continuous on the selected state spaces; scalar multiplication cX is distinct from an unspecified vector product.

body: [Definition defi:fiberwise-colims of arXiv:2608.28504, 'Global $\bm\infty$-categories and global Thom spectra'] We say that a $T$-$\infty$-category ${\mathcal{C}}$ is \emph{fiberwise cocomplete} if it has $(\textup{const}\,K)$-shaped colimits for all small $\infty$-categories $K$, i.e.\ if it factors through the non-full subcategory $\CAT_\infty^\text{cc}\subset\CAT_\infty$. Analogously, we say that $F\colon{\mathcal{C}}\to{\mathcal{D}}$ is \emph{fiberwise cocontinuous} if and only if it preserves $\textup{const}\,K$-colimits for all $K\in\Cat_\infty$.
title: Definition defi:fiberwise-colims of arXiv:2608.28504

body:
[Proposition prop:pseudo-bloch of arXiv:2608.01253, 'The pseudo-quantum representation of \\finite reversible Markov chains'] Let $N=2M$ and let $\{\Sigma_a\}_{a=1}^{d}$, with $d=\tfrac{N(N+1)}2-1$, be a
trace-orthonormal basis of the traceless complex-symmetric matrices, so that
$\operatorname{Tr}(\Sigma_a\Sigma_b)=\delta_{ab}$, $\operatorname{Tr}\Sigma_a=0$, and
$\Sigma_a^{T}=\Sigma_a$. Orthonormality here is meant for the bilinear trace form
$\operatorname{Tr}(\Sigma_a\Sigma_b)$, with no complex conjugation, and such a basis exists
because that form is nondegenerate on the complex-symmetric matrices, for instance
the symmetrised units $(E_{ij}+E_{ji})/\sqrt2$ for $i<j$ together with an
orthonormal set of $N-1$ real traceless diagonal matrices work. The
$\Sigma_a$ are complex symmetric, not Hermitian, so they are the bilinear analogue
of the Gell-Mann matrices rather than the matrices themselves. Write

\[
\rho_z=\frac{\operatorname{Tr}\rho_z}{N}\,\mathrm{I}+\sum_{a=1}^{d}r_a(z)\,\Sigma_a,\qquad
r_a(z)=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_z\Sigma_a).
\]

Then the coordinate vector obeys the linear flow

\[
\dot r_a(z)=\sum_{b}\Omega_{ab}\,r_b(z),\qquad
\Omega_{ab}=\operatorname{Tr}\bigl(\Sigma_a[K,\Sigma_b]\bigr),\qquad \Omega^{T}=-\Omega.
\]

Hence the flow lies in $\OO(d,\mathbb{C})$ and preserves the bilinear quantity
$\sum_a r_a^{2}$.

[Theorem thm:geounicont of arXiv:2604.10020, 'The directed landscape in half-space'] Fix $\rho \in \mathbb{R} \cup \{-\infty\}$.
	\begin{enumerate}[nosep, label=\arabic*.]
		\item Almost surely, for all $(p; q) \in \mathbb H^2_\uparrow$, there exists at least one geodesic in $\mathcal{L}^\rho$ from $p$ to $q$.
		\item Almost surely, all geodesics in $\mathcal{L}^\rho$ are H\"older-$(2/3-\epsilon)$ continuous for all $\epsilon > 0$.
		\item For any fixed $(p; q) \in \mathbb H^2_\uparrow$, almost surely there is a unique geodesic in $\mathcal{L}^\rho$ from $p$ to $q$.
	\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Fix training data D of size n>=1, a prior probability pi, model likelihood p(D|theta), and a test-observation distribution nu on pairs s=(y,x). For lambda in a positive open interval containing1, assume Z(lambda)=integral p(D|theta)^lambda pi(dtheta) is finite and positive, and define q_lambda(dtheta)=p(D|theta)^lambda pi(dtheta)/Z(lambda). This is likelihood-only tempering; the prior is not raised to lambda. Temperature T=1/lambda is cold when lambda>1. For a posterior rho let m_rho(y|x)=E_rho p(y|x,theta), B(rho)=E_nu[-log m_rho(y|x)], J(rho)=E_rho[-log p(D|theta)], and Ghat(rho,D)=J(rho)/n. Assume the losses used are finite and lambda->B(q_lambda) is differentiable at1. Definition1 calls the local CPE present exactly when Bprime(1)<0. This definition concerns infinitesimal cooling at1; Bprime(1)=0 alone does not imply a minimum or rule out improvement at another temperature. The authors call q_1 underfitting if some posterior rho has simultaneously B(rho)<B(q_1) and Ghat(rho,D)<Ghat(q_1,D).

[Definition DefSGP of arXiv:2410.23899, 'Tightness for interlacing geometric random walk bridges'] Fix a set $\Sigma = \llbracket 1, N \rrbracket$ with $N \in \mathbb{N}$ or $N = \infty$ and $T_0, T_1\in \mathbb{Z}$ with $T_0 \leq T_1$. A $\Sigma$-indexed geometric line ensemble $\mathfrak{L} : \Sigma \times \llbracket T_0, T_1 \rrbracket \rightarrow \mathbb{Z}$ is said to satisfy the {\em interlacing Gibbs property} if it is interlacing, meaning that 
$$ L_i(j-1) \geq L_{i+1}(j) \mbox{ for all $i \in \llbracket 1, N - 1 \rrbracket$ and $j \in \llbracket T_0 + 1, T_1 \rrbracket$},$$
and for any finite $K = \llbracket k_1, k_2 \rrbracket \subseteq \llbracket 1, N - 1 \rrbracket$ and $a,b \in \llbracket T_0, T_1 \rrbracket$ with $a < b$ the following holds.  Suppose that $f, g$ are two increasing paths drawn in $\{ (r,z) \in \mathbb{Z}^2 : a \leq r \leq b\}$ and $\vec{x}, \vec{y} \in \mathfrak{W}_k$ with $k=k_2-k_1+1$ altogether satisfy that $\mathbb{P}(A) > 0$ where $A$ denotes the event $$A =\{ \vec{x} = ({L}_{k_1}(a), \dots, {L}_{k_2}(a)), \vec{y} = ({L}_{k_1}(b), \dots, {L}_{k_2}(b)), L_{k_1-1} \llbracket a,b \rrbracket = f, L_{k_2+1} \llbracket a,b \rrbracket = g \},$$
where if $k_1 = 1$ we adopt the convention $f = \infty = L_0$. Then, we have for any $\{ B_i \in \Omega(a, b, x_i , y_i) \}_{i = 1}^k$ that
\begin{equation}
\mathbb{P}\left( L_{i + k_1-1}\llbracket a,b \rrbracket = B_{i} \mbox{ for $i \in \llbracket 1, k \rrbracket$} \, \vert  A \, \right) = \mathbb{P}_{\mathsf{Inter}, \operatorname{Geom}}^{a,b, \vec{x}, \vec{y}, f, g} \left( \cap_{i = 1}^k\{ Q_i = B_i \} \right).
\end{equation}
title: Definition DefSGP of arXiv:2410.23899

body:
Fix 0<alpha<log(2)/2 and rho in [0,1/2) with 2alpha<I(1-2rho), where I(t)=((1+t)log(1+t)+(1-t)log(1-t))/2 and I(1)=log(2). For integers N with rho N integral, let M=floor(exp(alpha N))+1 and let xi^1,...,xi^M be iid uniform patterns in {-1,+1}^N (all bits mutually independent). Conditional on the stored patterns, draw one input sigma^nu independently and uniformly on the Hamming sphere of radius rho N about xi^nu, for every nu. Set T_i(sigma)=sign(sum_mu [exp(xi_i^mu+sum_{j!=i}xi_j^mu sigma_j)-exp(-xi_i^mu+sum_{j!=i}xi_j^mu sigma_j)]). Equivalently T_i(sigma)=sign(sum_mu xi_i^mu exp(sum_{j!=i}xi_j^mu sigma_j)), since the omitted common factor is 2sinh(1)>0. Then P(exists nu exists i: T_i(sigma^nu)!=xi_i^nu) tends to zero as N tends to infinity. The sign at zero may be arbitrary. In particular rho=0 gives simultaneous fixed-point stability of every stored pattern whenever alpha<log(2)/2. This is one random corrupted input per pattern and coordinate evaluation on that initial input, not uniform correction of all Hamming-ball inputs and not a claim about an adaptively changing asynchronous trajectory. Source: Demircigil--Heusel--Lowe--Upgang--Vermet, Theorem 1.3 and Remark 1.4, arXiv:1702.01929v2, PDF p4; model equation (1), PDF p2. Integer rounding of the paper's M=exp(alpha N)+1 is immaterial.

Union over all M(M-1)N directed target/competitor/coordinate triples bounds the global truncation-bad probability by M(M-1)N exp(-nI(q)), which tends to zero. For a fixed target nu and coordinate i, define Z_mu=xi_i^nu xi_i^mu exp(S_mu)1{S_mu<=qn}. Under conditioning only on this target and input, the competitor variables Z_mu are independent and centered: the competitor's i-th bit is an independent uniform sign and is absent from S_mu and its cutoff. They obey |Z_mu|<=b=exp(qn). The point-mass bound P(S_n=s)<=exp(-nI(s/n)), obtained by optimizing cosh(t)^n and using symmetry for s<0, shows E[exp(2S_n)1{S_n<=qn}]<=(n+1)exp(nJ(q)), where J(q)=sup_{-1<=u<=q}(2u-I(u)) equals 2q-I(q) for q<=tanh(2) and log(cosh(2)) otherwise. The endpoints s=+/-n have exact mass 2^{-n}. Thus sum_mu E Z_mu^2<=v=(M-1)(n+1)exp(nJ(q)). Apply Bernstein's bounded-variable inequality to the independent centered Z_mu and -Z_mu: P(|sum Z_mu|>=h)<=2exp(-h^2/[2(v+bh/3)]), with h=exp(mN-1), a lower bound on the signed self-pattern signal. Every denominator is strictly positive. There is a strict variance gap alpha+J(q)<2m. For q<=tanh(2), use I(q)>2alpha and q<m. Otherwise use alpha<log(2)/2 and log(cosh(2))+log(2)/2<2tanh(2)<2q<2m. The strict elementary middle inequality follows by putting r=exp(-4)<1/16: 2tanh(2)-log(cosh(2))-log(2)/2=log(2)/2-log(1+r)-4r/(1+r)>1/3-5r>1/48; here log(2)>2/3 follows by integrating the strict tangent bound 1/x>=4/3-4x/9 on [1,2], and exp(1)>2 follows from its series. Hence h^2/v>=exp((2m-alpha-J(q))N+J(q)-2)/N and h/b=exp((m-q)N+q-1); the Bernstein exponent grows at least exp(cN) for some fixed c>0. On the global truncation-good event the original competitor field equals this truncated field pointwise. A union bound over MN coordinates therefore bounds total failure by M(M-1)N exp(-nI(q))+2MN exp(-h^2/[2(v+bh/3)]), tending to zero. Crucially Bernstein is never conditioned on the global truncation-good event; its complement is added afterward. No independence between different target/coordinate error events is needed. Exact finite checks of update identity, truncation centering and self-signal cover 917 cases for N=2,...,8 in check_repair_finite.py; the asymptotic argument is analytic, not numerical. [Lemm l:L2-norm-occupation-measure of arXiv:2607.18194, 'Temperature chaos in directed polymers'] Let $\{\mathrm{e}_i\}_{i\geqslant 1}\subset C_c(\mathbb{R}^2)$ be an orthonormal basis of $L^2(\mathbb{R}^2)$ as in Lemma (l:nice-L2-basis of the paper).
    Let $\mu$ be a Radon measure on $\mathbb{R}^2$, and for $i\geqslant 1$ let $\mu_i\coloneqq  \int_{\mathbb{R}^2} \mathrm{e}_i\,d\mu$ (the integral exists because $\mathrm{e}_i$ is continuous and compactly supported).
    If $\sum_{i=1}^\infty \mu_i^2 < \infty$, then $\mu$ is absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure.

    Thus, since for any $X\in C([s,t])$ the occupation measure $\gamma^X$ in (equation e:occupation-measure of the paper) is singular with respect to Lebesgue measure,  we have
    \begin{align*}
        \lim_{n\to\infty} \VarXi\left(\sum_{i=1}^n \xi_i \gamma_i^X\right)
        =
        \sum_{i=1}^\infty (\gamma_i^X)^2
        =\infty.
    \end{align*}

[Proposition 4 (Order properties) of arXiv:2607.29560, 'Tractable Relaxations of Multivariate Stochastic Dominance via Optimal Transport and CVaR'] For fixed $\gamma\in[0,1]$, CSD is a preorder, is preserved under
common-weight mixtures. In addition CSD is nested in $\gamma$, i.e., $P\preceq_{s,\lambda,\gamma}^{\rm CSD}Q$ implies $
P\preceq_{s,\lambda,\gamma'}^{\rm CSD}Q$  whenever $0\le\gamma\le\gamma'\le1$ and if $\gamma<1$, then
$ 
P\preceq_{s,\lambda,\gamma}^{\rm CSD}Q
\quad\text{and}\quad
Q\preceq_{s,\lambda,\gamma}^{\rm CSD}P
$ 
hold if and only if $W_s(P,Q)=0$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma lem:entropy-decomp of arXiv:2606.09221, 'Log-Sobolev under random monotone censoring'] For every $0\le s \le n$ and $f:\, H_s\to \mathbb{R}$, we have
$$     
\operatorname{Ent}_{\pi_s}(f^2) =\operatorname{Ent}_{p}(\bar{f}^2)+\sum_{k= s}^{n-1}p_{k}\operatorname{Ent}_{\nu_k}(f^2),
$$
where $\bar{f}:\, \{s,\ldots,n\}\to \mathbb{R}$ is defined by $\bar{f}(k)= (\mathbb{E}_{\nu_k}f^2)^{\frac12}=\Vert f(X_k)\Vert_{L^2}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Entropy decomposition

[Lemma lem:haar-passive-zero of arXiv:2608.29403, 'Kac's Walk on Rotation Matrices Mixes in $\boldsymbol{\Theta(n^2)}$ Steps:\\ A Proof Disco'] Let $V_-$ and $V_+$ be orthogonal $\mathrm{SO}(n)$-modules.  On their
star dilations write $\mathscr T_\pm,\mathscr E_\pm,\mathsf Q_\pm$ and
$\mathscr G_\pm=\mathsf Q_\pm\mathscr T_\pm$ for the maps in (eq:3.2.2 of the paper).
Let $\mathsf M:(V_-)_\star\to(V_+)_\star$ be a typed passive singleton,
so that
\[
 (\mathsf Mh)(i,\theta)=M_i h(i,\theta),\qquad
 \rho_+(R_i(\theta))^*M_i\rho_-(R_i(\theta))=M_i,
 \qquad \sum_iM_i=0.
\tag{3.2.10s$_1$}
\]
Put $\mathsf S^+_{+,-}=\mathsf Q_+\mathsf M\mathscr E_-^*$.
If $\Pi_-$ is the projection onto $V_-^{\mathrm{SO}(n)}$, then
\[
 \boxed{\mathscr G_+^*\mathsf S^+_{+,-}\Pi_-=0.}
\tag{3.2.10s$_2$}
\]
Writing
$\mathsf S^-_{-,+}=\mathscr E_-\mathsf M^*\mathsf Q_+$, applying the
same statement to $\mathsf M^*$ gives the oppositely oriented identity
$\Pi_-\mathsf S^-_{-,+}\mathscr G_+=0$.
Consequently every maximal residual temporal component made only of
passive singleton supernodes is identically zero, term by term in its
weak order and finite residual gaps.  This includes either end component
under the common auxiliary Haar projection of
(lem:haar-residual of the paper).

body:
[Lemma lem:finite-rank-lower-cluster of arXiv:2606.21006, 'Law of the Iterated Logarithm for Weighted Sums of Functionals of Long-Memory Gaussian Seq'] Let \(\mathfrak H\) be a real separable Hilbert space, and let \(W_n\), \(n\ge3\), be
isonormal Gaussian processes over \(\mathfrak H\). Let \(E\subset\mathfrak H\) be a
finite-dimensional subspace with orthonormal basis \(e_1,\ldots,e_N\).

Assume that for some \(\xi\in E\) with \(\|\xi\|_{\mathfrak H}\le1\), there exists a subsequence
\(n_k\to\infty\) such that
\[
    \frac{W_{n_k}(e_i)}{(2\log\log n_k)^{1/2}}
    \longrightarrow
    \langle e_i,\xi\rangle_{\mathfrak H},
    \qquad i=1,\ldots,N .
\]
Fix \(T<\infty\). Let \(Q_t\in E^{\odot m}\), \(0\le t\le T\), be a continuous finite-rank kernel family. Then
\[
    \frac{I_m(Q_t;W_{n_k})}{(2\log\log n_k)^{m/2}}
    \longrightarrow
    \langle Q_t,\xi^{\otimes m}\rangle_{\mathfrak H^{\otimes m}}
\]
uniformly in \(t\in[0,T]\).

[Lem W1 lower-principle of arXiv:2411.15724, 'Wasserstein Convergence Rates for Empirical Measures of Random Subsequence of $\{nα\}$'] Let $\alpha$ be an irrational number, and let $q \in \mathbb N$ such that  $\| q \alpha \| \leq C q^{-\gamma}$ holds for some constants $\gamma \ge 1$ and $C > 0$.
For simplicity, we set $K(q) = \lfloor q^\gamma / (3C) \rfloor$. Then for any $\nu \in \mathscr{P}(\mathbb{T})$ such that $\text{supp} (\nu) \subset \big\{ \{ j \alpha \} \, ; \, |j| \leq K(q) \big\}$, we have
$$
\mathbb W_1(\nu, \mu) \geq \frac{1}{36q}.
$$

body: Let (X, Sigma, mu) be a measure space and let p, q in [1, infinity] be conjugate exponents, meaning 1/p + 1/q = 1 (with 1/infinity read as 0). If f is in L^p(mu) and g is in L^q(mu), then fg is in L^1(mu) and integral of |fg| dmu <= ||f||_p ||g||_q, where ||f||_p = (integral |f|^p dmu)^(1/p) for p < infinity and the essential supremum of |f| for p = infinity. The discrete form is sum |x_i y_i| <= (sum |x_i|^p)^(1/p) (sum |y_i|^q)^(1/q). For 1 < p < infinity, equality holds iff |f|^p and |g|^q are proportional a.e.
title: Holder's inequality

[Lemma 27 (Matsuda, Lemma 3.4 and Remark 3.5) of arXiv:2507.06186, '2507.06186']

Let $t>0$ be fixed.
\begin{enumerate}[(1)]
\item If $0\leq a<b\leq t$, then
as $\eps\to0$, one has
\[\mbf E\big[\be^\eps_{[a,b]^2_\leq}(B^{0,0}_t)\big]
=\frac{b-a}{2\pi}\big(\log(1/\eps)+\log t\big)+\frac1{2\pi}\int_0^{b-a}\log r-\log(t-r)\d r+o(1)\]
and
\[\mbf E\big[\be^\eps_{[a,b]^2_{\leq}}(B^0)\big]
=\tfrac{b-a}{2\pi}\big(\log(1/\eps)+\log(b-a)-1\big)+o(1).\]
\item If $0\leq a<b\leq c<d\leq t$, then as $\eps\to0$, one has
\[\mbf E\big[\be^\eps_{[a,b]\times[c,d]}(B^{0,0}_t)\big]=\frac1{2\pi}\int_{c-a}^{d-a}\log r-\log(t-r)\d r
-\frac1{2\pi}\int_{c-b}^{d-b}\log r-\log(t-r)\d r+o(1).\]
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem 3 of arXiv:2605.06953, 'Asymptotic Results for Uniform Group Drawing in the Coupon Collector's Problem'] Let $t\ge 2$ be an integer. \newline\newline
    (a) If $s = n -\lambda\cdot n^{\frac{t-1}{t}}$, where $\lambda >0$, then $$\lim_{n \to \infty} \E[Y] = te^{-\lambda^t}+(t+1)(1-e^{-\lambda^t}).$$ Moreover, $Y \xrightarrow[n\to \infty]{\mathcal{D}} Z$, where $Z$ is a random variable with the distribution $$\PP[Z=i] = 
    \begin{cases}
            e^{-\lambda^t}, &i=t, \\
            1-e^{-\lambda^t}, &i=t+1.
        \end{cases}$$
    (b) If $s = n-o(n^{t/(t+1)})$ and $s = n-\omega(n^{(t-1)/t})$ then 
    $$ \lim_{n \to \infty} \E[Y] = t+1.$$
    Moreover, $Y \xrightarrow[n\to \infty]{\mathcal{P}} t+1$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Defn of arXiv:2609.01458, 'Confluence relations for $q$-analogues of multiple zeta values'] Define $\pi\colon\mathbb{Q}\mathcal{C}\to\mathbb{Q}\langle\mathcal{B}\rangle^{0}$
and $\pi_{z}\colon\mathbb{Q}\mathcal{C}^{0}_{z}\to\mathbb{Q}\langle\mathcal{B}\rangle$
by
\begin{align*}
\pi(\mathbb{L}_{k_{1},\dots,k_{d}}(q^{n_{1}},\dots,q^{n_{d}})) & \coloneqq\pi_{z}(\mathbb{L}_{k_{1},\dots,k_{d}}(q^{n_{1}},\dots,q^{n_{d-1}},q^{n_{d}}z))\\
 & \coloneqq F(k_{1},\dots,k_{d};n_{1},\dots,n_{d})
\end{align*}
and
\[
\pi(\mathbb{L}(\emptyset))\coloneqq\pi_{z}(\mathbb{L}(\emptyset))\coloneqq1.
\]

[Proposition 18 of arXiv:2604.05138, 'Convergence rate of $H$-property for step-graphons'] The following two items hold:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item If $W$ does not satisfy Condition $B'$, then there exist positive constants $c$ and $\lambda$ such that
    $$
    P_n(W) \leq c \, e^{-\lambda n}. 
    $$
    \item If $W$ satisfies Conditions $A$ and $B$, then there exist positive constants $c$ and $\lambda$ such that
    $$
    1 - P_n(W) \leq c \, e^{-\lambda n}.
    $$
\end{enumerate}
title: Proposition 18 of arXiv:2604.05138

[Cor 3 of arXiv:2512.03884, '2512.03884'] Under assumption \eqref{psicondition}, for any $1 \le p\le \infty$, we have the limit laws
\[ \sqrt{N} W_{I,p}(\mu_N,\lambda) \overset{d}{\to} \| Y \|_{L^p ([0,1])} \quad \textrm{and} \quad \sqrt{N} W_{\mathbb{T},p}(\mu_N,\lambda) \overset{d}{\to} \inf_{c \in \mathbb{R}} \| Y -c \|_{L^p ([0,1])}, \]
and the laws of the iterated logarithm
\[ \begin{split} \limsup_{N \to \infty} \frac{\sqrt{N}W_{I,p} (\mu_N, \lambda)}{\sqrt{2 \log \log N}} &= \sup_{f \in B(\Gamma)} \| f \|_{L^p ([0,1])} \quad \textrm{a.s.}, \\ \limsup_{N \to \infty} \frac{\sqrt{N}W_{\mathbb{T},p} (\mu_N, \lambda)}{\sqrt{2 \log \log N}} &= \sup_{f \in B(\Gamma)} \inf_{c \in \mathbb{R}} \| f -c \|_{L^p ([0,1])} \quad \textrm{a.s.} \end{split} \] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

in the sense of [Jacod_Shiryaev], of the right-continuous filtration $\bigl(\mathscr{H}_{n,t}^{+}\bigr)_{t\geq 0}$ and 
the following equality holds 
\begin{equation}
 {\overline{\mathscr{F} }}_{n,t} = \bigcap_{s>t}  \sigma\bigl(  \mathscr{H}_{n,s} \cup \mathscr{N}\bigr).
\end{equation}
In particular,  the filtration ${\overline{\mathbb{F}}_n}$ is the usual augmentation of filtration $\mathbb{H}_n$ and satisfies the usual hypothesis, see   [Jacod_Shiryaev].

Suppose there is a homeomorphism \(h: A \to B\) such that for every Borel \(E \subset A\) we have \(\lambda^0(E) = 0 \iff \lambda^0(h(E)) = 0 \). Own-work draft, claim w733-T363-023 v1; proof (unaudited), no novelty claim. On x1=(1,1/4),x2=(-1,1/4), labels+1, train both layers of f(x)=sum_j v_j ReLU(w_j.x), with no biases, by gradient flow of summed exponential or logistic loss, ReLU derivative zero at zero. Initially require exactly one positive-output both-active neuron C, at least one positive-output x1-only neuron A, no x2-only neuron, and all remaining neurons strictly dead with arbitrary output. There is no initial restriction on C tilt, output-to-hidden norm ratio, initialization scale, or prediction imbalance. A global absolutely continuous flow exists; every such flow creates a positive x2-only B seed at finite time and then attains global normalized margin sqrt17/16, with normalization by total parameter squared norm. Reflection exchanges the two points. This is an entire activation-pattern family, extending the prior tilted balanced subcone. A C-to-A exit is impossible because the incoming C normal velocity at that boundary is positive. Under hypothetical absence of B, y and v diverge, homogeneity gives v>=3y/4 eventually, and a late E=f1-f2 barrier becomes invariant. The weighted variable s=v+(w.x1)/a then obeys s<=s(base)exp(aI1-bI2), a=sqrt17/4,b=15/(8sqrt17)-1/3>0, I_i=integral[-ell_prime(fi)]dt; the clock contradiction forces B creation. For iid Gaussian hidden/output coordinates N(0,sigma^2), sigma>0, p=atan(1/4)/pi, the exact probability of this family and its disjoint reflection is J_m=m*p[(1/4+p/2)^(m-1)-p^(m-1)]. It adds70 proposed global signed permutation orbits at widths2..6:2,6,12,20,30. With the prior two-initial-seed family this gives196 proposed global orbits and2643 unclassified. These are sufficient-family masses and unaudited labels, not total basin probabilities or a solution of the general max-margin question. Do not add the full prior subcone mass P_m to H_m+J_m: its single-C contribution is already contained in J_m. Only k>=2 subcone terms are disjoint extras. Multiple C neurons and negative-output live neurons remain outside this theorem.
