[Defn d:ssm-pp of arXiv:2605.28430, 'Limit theory for Lipschitz-localized statistics in random geometric models'] The Gibbs spin model~(equation eqn:gibbs of the paper) satisfies {\em averaged weak spatial mixing} on the graph $\Psi = \Psi(\cdot)$ with respect to the input process $\mathcal{P}$ if
the following conditions hold: 
\begin{enumerate}[wide,label=(\roman*),labelindent=0pt]

\item  for any finite subset ${\cal X } \subset \mathbb{R}^d$, there exists a spatial mixing function 
$\mathcal{A}_{\Psi({\cal X })}: 2^{\cal X } \times 2^{\cal X } \to [0, \infty)$ 
such that   
\begin{equation} 
d_{\textnormal{TV}} \big( \mathcal{L}(V_{{\cal X }''} \mid V_{\partial {\cal X }'} = \v_{\partial {\cal X }'}),  
\mathcal{L}(V_{{\cal X }''} \mid V_{\partial {\cal X }'} = {z}_{\partial {\cal X }'}) \big)  
\leq \mathcal{A}_{\Psi({\cal X })}({\cal X }'', \partial {\cal X }'),
\end{equation}  
for all subsets ${\cal X }'' \subset {\cal X }' \subset {\cal X }$ and boundary conditions $\v_{\partial {\cal X }'}, {z}_{\partial {\cal X }'}\in \mathbb{K}^{\partial {\cal X }'}$, and 
\vskip.2cm
\item   
for all $p \in \mathbb{N}$ the functions 

\begin{equation} 
\mathfrak{a}_p(k):=\sup_{B \in {\cal B}_b} \sup_{x_1,\ldots, x_p\in B}  
\mathbb {E} _{\bk x1p} \big[\mathcal{A}_{\Psi(\mathcal{P} \cap B)} (\bk x1p, \partial \mathfrak{B}_k(\bk x1p))\big],  \ \  k \in \mathbb{N},
\end{equation}  

are fast decreasing as \( k \to \infty \).  
Here, \(\mathfrak{B}_k(\bk x1p) = \bigcup_{i=1}^p \mathfrak{B}_k(x_i)\) and the boundary $\partial$ of \(\mathfrak{B}_k(\bk x1p)\) is again with respect to~\(\Psi(\mathcal{P} \cap B)\);
${\cal B}_b$ are the bounded Borel subsets of $\mathbb{R}^d$. 
We  assume that the mapping $((\mathbb{R}^d)^p,\hat\mathcal{N}_{\mathbb{R}^d\times\mathcal{N}_{\mathbb{R}^d}})\owns(\bk x1p,\tilde\mu)=(\bk x1p,\Psi(\mu)) \mapsto \mathcal{A}_{\Psi}(\bk x1p,\partial^\Psi\mathfrak{B}_k(\bk x1p))\in\mathbb{R}$ is measurable for all $k\in\mathbb{N}$. Without loss of generality, we assume that $\mathfrak{a}_p$ are increasing in $p$.
\end{enumerate}
title: Averaged weak spatial mixing of the Gibbs spin model on a random spatial  graph

body:
[Theorem 3 of arXiv:2512.05340, 'The rate of convergence of the critical mean-field $O(N)$ magnetization via multivariate n'] Suppose $V$ satisfies Assumption \ref{assumption: assumptions on V}, and let $\mu$ have Lebesgue density proportional to
  $e^{-V}$.
  Let $W,W'$ be identically distributed $\RR^d$-valued random variables, defined on the same probability space, such that if $\delta:=W'-W$ then
  $W$ and $\delta\delta^\transpose$ are both integrable. 
  Let $\sF\supseteq\sigma(W)$ be a $\sigma$-algebra, let $\lambda>0$, and define $R_1$ and $R_2$ so that
    \begin{equation}
      \mathbb{E}[\delta|\mathcal{F}] = \lambda(-\grad V(W) + R_{1}),
      
    \end{equation}
    and
    \begin{equation}
      \mathbb{E}\left[\delta\,\delta^{\transpose}\big|\mathcal{F}\right] = 2\lambda(\id + R_{2}).
      
    \end{equation}
    Then there exists a constant $C\in(0,\infty)$ such that
    \begin{equation}
      d(\sL(W),\mu)
      \leq C\left\lbrace \frac{1}{\lambda}\mathbb{E} [|\delta|^{3}(|\log|\delta|| \vee 1)] + \mathbb{E}|R_{1}|
      + \sqrt{d}\,\mathbb{E}\,\|R_{2}\| \right\rbrace. 
    \end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma lem:root_declumping of arXiv:2607.22291, 'Rare subtree patterns in size-conditioned Bienaymé trees: Poisson approximation and declum'] Set $\pi_n=\P(G_{k_n}(\mathcal T)=1)$ and
$\widehat{\pi}_n=\P(\widehat{G}_{k_n}(\mathcal T)=1)$.
Set
$$
b_B=\P\bigl(k_\varnothing(\mathcal T)\in B,\
k_\varnothing(\mathcal T)\ge1\bigr)>0.
$$
Then $\widehat\pi_n\ge b_B\pi_n$ for every $n \geq 1$. In addition:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)]  If $(n\pi_n)$ is bounded, then $
n\widehat{\pi}_n-c_B n\pi_n\to0$.
\item[(ii)] If $n\pi_n\to\infty$, then $n\widehat{\pi}_n\to\infty$.
\item[(iii)] Finally, if $(G_k)$ satisfies Assumption (hyp:S of the paper) along $(k_n)$ with
respect to $(M_n)$, then $(\widehat G_k)$ satisfies Assumption (hyp:M of the paper)
along $(k_n)$ with respect to the same cutoff.
\end{enumerate}

[Corollary 3 of arXiv:2607.26254, 'A Simple Model of Sea Spray'] Suppose, $\mathcal{F}(dr)=\mathcal{F}(r) dr$ and $ \mathcal{F}(r)$ is strictly positive on a finite interval $[r_{min},r_{max}]$ and equal to zero otherwise. Suppose $r\to\zeta(r)$ is continuous on $[r_{min},r_{max}]$ and $(t,r)\to (r_t,z_t(r))$ is continuous on,  

$$
A=\{\,(t,r)\mid0\leq t\leq \zeta(r),\,\,  r_{min}\leq r\leq r_{max},\,\}.
$$

\mpar
Finally, suppose $m$ is a continuous function of $z.$ Then,
$$
z_{100}=\max_{(r,t)\in A} z_t(r).
$$
\begin{proof}
Let $z^{**}=\max_{(t,r)\in A} z_t(r).$ Note that  $z_{100}\leq z^{**}$ since no droplet ever exceeds this height. Suppose, on the other hand, that $w< z^{**}.$ Since $z$ is a continuous function and $A$ is a closed set, $z$ attains its maximum value, hence  $z_t(r)>w$  for all $(t,r)$ in an open subset of $A.$ In particular, there is an interval $[a,b]\subset [r_{min}, r_{max}]$ such that,
$$
\int_0^\infty r_t^31_{(0,w]}(z_t(r))dt  < \int_0^\infty r^3_t1_{(0,z_{100}]}(z_t(r))dt
$$
for all $r\in [a,b]$. Thus,
\begin{align*}
m(w) & = \tfrac{4}{3}\pi\rho   \int_0^\infty \negthickspace \int_0^\infty r^3_s\, 1_{(0,w]}(z_s(r))\mathcal{F}(dr) ds\\
& <\tfrac{4}{3}\pi\rho   \int_0^\infty \negthickspace \int_0^\infty r^3_s\, 1_{(0,z_{100}]}(z_s(r))\mathcal{F}(dr) ds\\
& = m(z_{100}),
\end{align*}
since $\mathcal{F}(r)$ is strictly positive on $[a,b].$ By continuity this implies,
$$
m(z^{**})=\lim_{z\to z^{**}}m(z)\leq m(z_{100}),
$$
and because $m$ is non-decreasing, we have $z^{**}\leq z_{100}$ which proves the result.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Let a_j be independent N(0,I_n), fix a deterministic unit signal x_*, put y_j=(a_j^T x_*)^2 and f(x)=(1/(4m)) sum_j ((a_j^T x)^2-y_j)^2. Fix a sufficiently small absolute constant C1>0 and sufficiently large absolute constants C2,c0. If m>=c0 n log n, then on a simultaneous event of probability at least 1-O(m n^(-10)), every point x with ||x-x_*||<=2C1 and max_j |a_j^T(x-x_*)|<=C2 sqrt(log n) satisfies ||x-eta grad f(x)-x_*||<=(1-eta/2)||x-x_*|| whenever 0<eta<=1/[5C2(10+C2)log n]. The event is uniform in x, so the point may depend on the samples. This is an absolute projection bound for unit signal, not the relative-error bound C2 sqrt(log n)||x-x_*||. The cited statement does not replace n log n samples by alpha n or by itself preserve the region along a trajectory.

body:
[Ppn 138 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] If $\psi:\bbR^{d_1}\to\bbR^{d_2}$ is Lipschitz, then $\psi$ preserves $\bbW_2$ convergence.
If $d_1=2,d_2=1$ and $\psi(X,Y)=XY$, then $\psi$ preserves $\bbW_2$ convergence for sequences on which $X$ is uniformly bounded.

\begin{proof}
The first statement follows because $L$-Lipschitz maps increase $\bbW_2$ distances by at most a factor of $L$.
For the second statement, suppose 
$X_N\to X$ and $Y_N\to Y$ in $L^2$, with $|X_N|\leq C$ almost surely for all $N$. 
We will argue that this implies $X_NY_N\to XY$ in $L^2$, and the assertion then follows. First,
the uniform bound on $X_N$ gives
  \[
  \E\Big[(X_NY_N-X_NY)^2\Big]
  \le C^2 \E\Big[(Y_N-Y)^2\Big]
  = o_N(1)\,,
  \]
so $X_NY_N$ and $X_NY$ are close in $L^2$. For $T$ growing sufficiently slowly with $N$, we then bound
  \[
  \E\Big[ (X_NY-XY)^2\Big]
  \le T^2\E\Big[ (X_N-X)^2\Big]
  + 4C^2\E\Big[Y^2; |Y| \ge T\Big]
  \le T^2 o_N(1) + o_T(1)\,,
  \]
where the last term is because $Y^2\in L^1$. Therefore $X_NY$ converges to $XY$ in $L^2$, and the claim follows.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Ppn 138 of arXiv:2608.29416

[Proposition 2 of arXiv:2606.31455, 'Discrete time-multidimensional renewal theory and applications'] Let $\mathcal{R}:=\mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{N}^d}$ be the set of all real-valued sequences on $\mathbb{N}^d$.
Equipped with pointwise addition $+$ and the convolution product $*$ in \eqref{eq:conv}, $(\mathcal{R},+,*)$ is a commutative ring
with unity. The identity element (unit) is the sequence $\ez$ defined by

\[
\ez(k)=
\begin{cases}
1, & k=0_d,\\
0, & \text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\]

If there exists $b:\mathbb{N}^d\to\mathbb{R}$ such that $a*b=b*a=\ez$, then $a$ is \emph{convolutionally invertible} and $b$ is called
its \emph{convolutional inverse}, denoted by $a^{(-1)}$.

Moreover, the map $\Phi:\mathcal{R}\to \mathbb{R}[[x_1,\ldots,x_d]]$ defined by $\Phi(a)=P_a$ is a ring isomorphism. In particular,
for all $a,b\in\mathcal{R}$,
\[
P_{a+b}(x_{1:d})=P_a(x_{1:d})+P_b(x_{1:d}),\ \
P_{a*b}(x_{1:d})=P_a(x_{1:d})\,P_b(x_{1:d}),\ \
P_{\ez}(x_{1:d})=1.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition 2 of arXiv:2606.31455

body: [Theorem 9.1 of arXiv:2503.23159, 'Hall's marriage theorem'] A sufficient condition for a family A of hypergraphs to have an SDR is that, for every subfamily B of A, there is a matching M in S B which cannot be pinned by fewer than |B| disjoint edges from S B. If each edge in each hypergraph is a singleton, the hypothesis reduces to that of Hall’s theorem (each hypergraph can be represented as a set, the union of its singleton edges), and the conclusion is the same as Hall’s.
title: Theorem 9.1 of arXiv:2503.23159: Hall's marriage theorem

[Theorem thm:main of arXiv:2608.30166, 'Square Functions and Rectifiability\\ under Monotone Transformations of the Density'] Let $\mu$ be an $n$-AD-regular measure in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with constant $c_0$ and
$\mu(\mathbb{R}^d)=\infty$. Let $F\colon(0,\infty)\to\mathbb{R}$ be a Borel function and
bi-Lipschitz on $J_0$ with constant $\lambda$. Then $\mu$ is uniformly $n$-rectifiable if and only if
there exists a constant $c$ such that, for any ball $B(x_0,R)$ centered at $\operatorname{supp}(\mu)$,
\begin{equation}
\int_0^R\!\!\int_{x\in B(x_0,R)} |\Delta^F_\mu(x,r)|^2\, d\mu(x)\,\frac{dr}{r}
\;\le\; c\,R^n.
\end{equation}
Quantitatively: if (equation eq:carleson of the paper) holds with constant $c'$ then
(equation eq:carlesonF of the paper) holds with constant $\lambda^2 c'$, and if (equation eq:carlesonF of the paper)
holds with constant $c$ then (equation eq:carleson of the paper) holds with constant $\lambda^2 c$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm:main of arXiv:2608.30166

body: Load-bearing hypothesis: H^s(R^n) embeds into L^∞(R^n) ∩ C^0 only for s > n/2, strictly; the borderline s = n/2 is excluded. Concrete counterexample, n = 2 (s = 1): u(x) = log log(1/|x|) for 0 < |x| < e^{−1}, extended by 0. Then ∫|∇u|² = 2π ∫_0^{e^{−1}} dr / ( r log²(1/r) ) = 2π < ∞ and ∫ u² < ∞, so u ∈ H¹(R²), yet u is unbounded at the origin. General n: choose f with f̂(ξ) = (1+|ξ|)^{−n} (log(2+|ξ|))^{−1} ≥ 0; then ∫ (1+|ξ|²)^{n/2}|f̂|² dξ < ∞ (radially, ∫ dρ/(ρ log²ρ) converges) so f ∈ H^{n/2}(R^n), while ∫ f̂ dξ = ∞ (∫ dρ/(ρ log ρ) diverges); since f̂ ≥ 0, an L^∞ bound on f would force ∫ f̂ < ∞ (test against a Gaussian approximate identity with positive Fourier transform and use monotone convergence), so f ∉ L^∞. Consequences: an energy-critical argument may not conclude a pointwise bound from the energy norm; ‖u‖_{L^q_t L^∞_x} estimates at the critical regularity generally require Besov spaces, since Ḃ^{n/2}_{2,1} embeds into L^∞ while H^{n/2} does not. This is the same phenomenon that makes the Lebesgue-space wave Strichartz estimates carry the restriction r < ∞ (the Littlewood–Paley summation of the dyadic blocks needs r < ∞, and at r = ∞ one lands in Besov spaces). The failure of the endpoints (q,r) = (2,∞) — Schrödinger in n = 2, wave in n = 3 — is a separate matter, proved by explicit counterexamples of Montgomery-Smith and of Klainerman–Machedon, not a corollary of this embedding failure.
title: Pitfall: H^{n/2} Does Not Embed in L^∞ (the Critical Sobolev Endpoint Fails)

[Lemma ex:finite-perturbation of arXiv:2604.13968, 'Divisible sandpiles via random walks in random scenery'] Let $G=(V,E)$ be an infinite, locally finite, and connected graph, and fix $o\in V$. For $m>0$ consider the configuration $\sigma(v)=1+m\,\mathbf{1}_{\{v=o\}}$.
		Then for every $x\in V$ and $n\geq 0$, we have $u_n(x)=m g_n(x,o)$, and hence $u_\infty(x)=m\,g(x,o)\in[0,\infty]$. In particular, $\sigma$ stabilizes if and only if the random walk on $G$ is transient. If the walk is recurrent, then $\sigma$ explodes.

body:
[Theorem 8 (Random regular graphs: pointwise version) of arXiv:2604.20514, 'Macroscopic loops in the random loop model on sparse random graphs'] Fix \(d\ge 3\), \(u\in[0,1]\), and \(\theta\in\mathbb N\) with \(\theta>1\). Let \(G_n\) be the random \(d\)-regular graph on \(n\) vertices, with law \(p_{d,n}\). Assume
\[
d>2c_{\theta,u}
=
2\bigl(1+\theta\max\{u,1-u\}\bigr).
\]
Then for every \(\delta>0\) there exist \(\eta>0\) and \(c>0\) such that for every
\[
t\ge T_{\theta,u}(d)+\delta,
\]
one has
\[
p_{d,n}\!\left(
\Pbb^{G_n}_{\theta,t,u}(A_\eta)\ge c
\right)\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}1.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Random regular graphs: pointwise version

body:
[Defn 5 of arXiv:2606.04636, 'A Thomson-type variational principle for diffusion coefficients'] $V_{0}$ is the space of admissible flows with vanishing
divergence, that we write formally as
\begin{equation}
V_{0}=\left\{ \phi\in\cH_{2}:\left\langle \div\phi,\div\phi\right\rangle =0\right\} .
\end{equation}
For $\phi\in\cH_{2}$, $\left\langle \div\phi,\div\phi\right\rangle =0$
should be understood by the completion under $\left\langle \cdot,\cdot\right\rangle $.
That is, there exists a sequence $(\phi_{n})_{n\in\N}$ of flows with
well defined divergence that converge in $\cH_{2}$ to $\phi$, such
that $\left\langle \div\phi_{n},\div\phi_{n}\right\rangle \xrightarrow{n\to\infty}0$.
title: Definition 5 of arXiv:2606.04636

body:
[Prop 33 (Change of uniformizer) of arXiv:2609.00723, 'An integral Hyodo--Kato isomorphism'] Let $\pi$ and $\pi'$ be two uniformizers of $\sO_K$, and let $m\geq0$
satisfy $e\leq p^m$. Then there is a canonical natural equivalence
\[
T_{\pi,\pi'}^{(m)}\colon
R\Gamma_{\rm crys}
\bigl(
 \sX_{\OK^\pi}^{(m)} 
/\sO_K^\pi\bigr)
\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
R\Gamma_{\rm crys}
\bigl(
 \sX_{\OK^{\pi'}}^{(m)} 
/\sO_K^{\pi'}\bigr)
\]
such that
\[
\rho_{\pi',m}^{\rm int}
\simeq
T_{\pi,\pi'}^{(m)}\circ\rho_{\pi,m}^{\rm int}.
\]
These equivalences satisfy
\[
T_{\pi,\pi}^{(m)}=\id,
\qquad
T_{\pi',\pi''}^{(m)}\circ T_{\pi,\pi'}^{(m)}
\simeq
T_{\pi,\pi''}^{(m)}.
\]

body:
Measured 2026-09-05 on the EMIT and OCO-2 stacking pools (70 cells, the pool protocol, full calibration, paired). Given that the long-only gain is the estimation variance the constraint removes at the rows the stack is scored on, the amount of constraint was chosen with the evaluation inputs: a blend w(t) between the simplex and least-squares stacks with t minimising the cross-validated calibration error plus the excess bootstrap variance of the blend at the evaluation rows over the calibration rows, and a per-row version t_i = 1/(1 + kappa v_i/median v) that leans to the simplex where least squares is uncertain. P24 (a) HELD: on EMIT the per-cell blend reads +0.08 vs the simplex and beats least squares on 39 of 40 cells; (b) HELD: on OCO-2 t* is at or above 0.5 on 30 of 30 cells and the blend reads +0.66 vs least squares; (c) REFUTED: the per-row blend vs the per-cell blend is +0.70 on Y2 and -0.14 on EMIT overall; falsifier (blend worse than the simplex by more than 1 on EMIT, or than least squares by more than 0.3 on OCO-2) not triggered. Fresh-split replication (P25, split C, SPLIT_SEED 11, the criterion uses no evaluation targets): P25 (a) HELD: on split C the EMIT blend reads +0.63 vs the simplex and beats least squares on 35 of 40 cells; (b) HELD: on OCO-2 the blend reads +0.84 vs the simplex (wins 30 of 30) and +0.65 vs least squares; (c) HELD: t* averages 0.34 on EMIT and 0.67 on OCO-2; falsifier (blend worse than the simplex by more than 1 on EMIT, or than least squares by more than 0.3 on OCO-2) not triggered. Bootstrap-size stability (P28, B = 16 against B = 8 on split B): P28 (a) HELD: t*(16) equals t*(8) on 86 pct of the 70 cells and is within 0.2 on 100 pct; (b) HELD: the blend's mean gain against the simplex moves from +0.08 to +0.06 on EMIT and from +0.83 to +0.83 on OCO-2, and the both-endpoints win count on OCO-2 is 30 of 30 at B = 16; falsifier (agreement below 50 pct or a gain moving by more than 0.5) not triggered. Break test: a fixed midpoint t = 0.5 matches the criterion on OCO-2 (+0.96 / +1.01 against +0.83 / +0.84 on the two splits) but loses 1.6 and 4.4 pct on EMIT where the criterion stays at +0.08 and +0.63 - the criterion's value is knowing, without labels, when not to leave the simplex; the EMIT shortfall against the hindsight-best t is the bias-shift term of the risk identity. Scarce calibration (P30, 240 of the calibration rows per cell, split B): P30 (a) HELD: at n = 240 the simplex beats least squares by +14.10 on EMIT (full calibration +8.83); (b) REFUTED: t* averages 0.22 on EMIT and the blend reads -2.61 vs the simplex; (c) HELD: on OCO-2 the blend beats both endpoints on 30 of 30 cells and the simplex reads +2.27 vs least squares (full calibration -0.18); falsifier (blend worse than the simplex by more than 1 on EMIT) TRIGGERED. The observable part of the bias shift (P31): adding t^2 (D_ev - D_cal), the shift in the two bases' mean squared disagreement between the evaluation and calibration rows, to the criterion - P31 (a) REFUTED: the R'-blend reads -0.71 vs the simplex on EMIT split B (R-blend +0.08) and +0.71 on split C (R-blend +0.63); (b) HELD: on OCO-2 the R'-blend is -0.11 vs the R-blend on split B and -0.12 on split C; (c) REFUTED: mean t** 0.39 against t* 0.33 on EMIT, share of the hindsight optimum 0.07 -> -0.62; falsifier (R'-blend worse than the R-blend by more than 0.3 on any corpus or split) TRIGGERED. Per-output mixing weights (P34, the criterion decoupled across outputs): P34 (a) REFUTED: the per-output blend reads -0.41 vs the per-cell blend on EMIT split B and -0.53 on split C; (b) HELD: on OCO-2 -0.02 and -0.08 on split C; (c) REFUTED: on Y2 the share of outputs at t_d = 0 is 0.20 and at t_d >= 0.5 is 0.34; falsifier (per-output worse than per-cell by more than 0.3 anywhere) TRIGGERED.
the members' predictions on the rows to be scored are available (transductive setting); their targets are not
the blend w(t) = (1 - t) w_simplex + t w_leastsquares is linear in t, so the cross-validated and bootstrap predictions of every t come from the two base estimators' predictions; the criterion is the 5-fold cross-validated squared relative error on the calibration rows plus the excess pairs-bootstrap variance (B = 8) of the blend at the evaluation rows over the calibration rows

[Cor GHProps of arXiv:2411.18563, 'Lower tails for triangles inside the critical window'] Under Condition~(ConditionThm1 of the paper), the following events hold wvhp with respect to $G \sim \mu_{\lambda,\zeta}$. Setting $\overline \Delta:=\mathbb{E}_{\lambda,\zeta} \Delta(G)$,
\begin{enumerate}
\item  $\delta(G) = (1+o(1))\Delta(G) =(1+o(1))\overline\Delta$,
\item $\alpha_{G_v,\lambda,\zeta}=(1+o(1))\alpha(\overline\Delta,\lambda,\zeta)$ for all $v\in V(G)$,
\item $\rho_{G_v,\lambda,\zeta}=(1+o(1))\rho(\overline\Delta,\lambda,\zeta)$ for all $v\in V(G)$.
\end{enumerate}
In particular, $\mathbb{E}_{\lambda,\zeta}(\alpha_{G_v,\lambda,\zeta})=(1+o(1))\alpha(\overline\Delta,\lambda,\zeta)$ and $\mathbb{E}_{\lambda,\zeta}(\rho_{G_v,\lambda,\zeta})=(1+o(1))\rho(\overline\Delta,\lambda,\zeta)$ for all $v\in V(G)$.
title: Cor GHProps of arXiv:2411.18563

[Prp 12 of arXiv:2608.13976, 'Boundary Harnack principle for diffusion with jumps on metric measure spaces'] Suppose assumptions (A1) and (A2)-(A4) hold for some $R_0>0$.
 Let $D$ be an  open subset of $\sX$. For each
 $B=B(z_0, R)$ with $z_0\in \partial D$ and  $R\in (0, R_0/8)$ so that $\overline {B}\subsetneq \sX,$
there exists $C=C(z_0, R)>0$ depending on the constants in (A2)-(A4) for the ball $B(z_0, R)$
such that for any
$x_k\in D\cap B(z_0,  R/64)$ with $k=1,2$ and $y\in D\cap  A(z_0, 3R/8, R/2), $
\begin{equation}\begin{aligned}
&C^{-1}G^B_{D\cap B(z_0, R/2)}(x_2, y) \dfrac{\E_{x_1} \left[ \tau_{D\cap B(z_0, R/32)} \right]}{\E_{x_2} \left[ \tau_{D\cap B(z_0, R/32)}  \right]}\leq G^B_{D\cap B(z_0, R/2)}(x_1, y)\\
&\qquad  \leq C \dfrac{\E_{x_1} \left[ \tau_{D\cap B(z_0, R/32)} \right]}{\E_{x_2} \left[ \tau_{D\cap B(z_0, R/32)}  \right]}G^B_{D\cap B(z_0, R/2)}(x_2, y).
\end{aligned}\end{equation}
 If we further assume  (A2')-(A4') and (A5) hold,  then the constant in \eqref{e:3.2'} depends only on $R.$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma lem:break_loops of arXiv:2507.15589, 'Tightness of approximations to metrics on non-simple conformal loop ensemble gaskets'] {amy-cle-resampling}}]

Suppose that $\Gamma$ is a nested ${\rm CLE}_{\kappa}${} in a simply connected domain $D$. For each $a\in(0,1)$, $b>0$ there exists $p > 0$ such that the following holds. 

Let $z\in D$ and $j_0\in\mathbf{Z}$ be such that $B(z,2^{-j_0})\subseteq D$. There exists a resampling $\Gamma^{\mathrm{res}}_{z,j}$ of $\Gamma$ within $A(z,2^{-j},2^{-j+1})$ for each $j>j_0$ with the following property. Let $G^{\mathrm{res}}_{z,j}$ be the event that
\begin{itemize}
 \item no loop in $\Gamma^{\mathrm{res}}_{z,j}$ crosses the annulus $A(z,2^{-j},2^{-j+1})$,
 \item denoting $\mathcal {C}$ the loops in $\Gamma$ that cross $A(z,2^{-j},2^{-j+1})$, the collection of loops of $\Gamma$ and $\Gamma^{\mathrm{res}}_{z,j}$ remain the same in each connected component of $\mathbf{C} \setminus \bigcup\mathcal {C}$ that is not surrounded by a loop in $\mathcal {C}$ and intersects $B(z,2^{-j})$, and the gasket of $\Gamma$ in these components is contained in the gasket of $\Gamma^{\mathrm{res}}_{z,j}$.
\end{itemize}
For $k\in\mathbf{N}$, let $\widetilde G_{z,j_0,k}$ be the event that the number of $j=j_0+1,\ldots,j_0+k$ so that
\[ \mathbf{P}[ G^{\mathrm{res}}_{z,j} \,|\, \Gamma ] \geq p\]
is at least $(1-a)k$.  Then
\[ \mathbf{P}[(\widetilde G_{z,j_0,k})^c] = O(e^{-b k}) \]
where the implicit constant does not depend on $z,j_0,k$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Prop brw+killing of arXiv:2608.13084, '\bf Branching random walk in random environment'] If $A$ is finite and connected subset in ${\mathbb Z}^d$ with $\#A\ge 2$, then for the branching random walk absorbed outside $A$, we have
\[
{\mathbb P}^{(A)}_x(Z_n \ge 1, \forall n\ge 0)>0, \forall x\in A,
\]
if and only if 
\begin{equation}
\left(\sum_k kp_k \right) \times \rho_A >1.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Prop consistency of arXiv:2412.04918, 'On one dimensional weighted Poincar\'e inequalities for Global Sensitivity Analysis'] Given $i \in \{ 1,\ldots, d \}$ and a finite interval $[a_i,b_i]$, we assume that $\mu_i \in \mathcal{P}(a_i,b_i)$ and that the main effect $f_i \in \mathscr{C}^{1,2}_{*}(a_i,b_i)$ satisfies $f'_i(a)\neq 0$ and  $f'_i(b)\neq 0$. Moreover we assume that $\frac{\partial f }{\partial x_i}(X)\in L^2 $. \\
Let $(X_1,\ldots, X^{(n)})$ be an i.i.d. sample generated from $X$ and consider an estimator $\widehat{f_i}$ constructed with respect to this sample. We assume the following (almost sure) hypothesis:
\begin{itemize}
\item[(i)] $\widehat{f_i}$ is centered with respect to $\mu_i$. 
\item[(ii)] $\widehat{f_i} \in \mathscr{C}^{1,2}_{*}(a_i,b_i)$ satisfies $\widehat{f_i} '(a)\neq 0$ and  $\widehat{f_i} '(b)\neq 0$. 
\item[(iii)] $\widehat{f_i}$ converges uniformly to $f_i $ on $[a_i,b_i]$ as $n\rightarrow \infty$.
\item[(iv)] $\widehat{f_i}'$ converges uniformly to $f_i '$ on $[a_i,b_i]$ as $n\rightarrow \infty$.
\end{itemize}
Then almost surely, the data-driven weight $\widehat{w_{i}}=w_{\widehat{f_i}}$ converges uniformly to $w_{f_i}$ on $[a_i,b_i]$ as $n\rightarrow \infty$. Moreover, the Monte-Carlo estimator 
\[
\widehat{\nu_{i}}=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{k=1}^n \widehat{w_{i}}(X_i^{(k)})\abs{\frac{\partial f}{\partial x_i}(X^{(k)})}^2\]
converges almost surely to $\nu_{i,w_{f_i}}$ as $n\rightarrow \infty$.

[Lemma 66 of arXiv:2603.24616, 'Pinning in non-critical half-space geometric last passage percolation'] Assume the same notation as in Definition \ref{Def.LETop}. Then, $L^N_1, L^N_2$ are a.s. increasing paths on $\llbracket 0, M \rrbracket$. Fix $b \in \llbracket 1, M \rrbracket$, $A, B \in \mathbb{Z}$, and an increasing path $g$ on $\llbracket 0, b \rrbracket$, such that $\mathbb{P}_N(E(A,B,g)) > 0$, where
$$E(A,B,g) = \{ L_1^N(0) = A, \hspace{2mm} L_1^N(b) = B, \hspace{2mm} L^N_2 = g \}.$$
Then, for any $E \subseteq \Omega(0,b,A,B)$, we have 
\begin{equation}
\mathbb{P}_N(L^N_1 \in E \vert E(A,B,g)) = \frac{\mathbb{P}_{\mathrm{Geom}}^{0,b, A, B}(\{Q \in E\} \cap \{Q \succeq g\} )}{\mathbb{P}_{\mathrm{Geom}}^{0,b, A, B}(Q \succeq g)},
\end{equation}
where $Q$ has law $\mathbb{P}_{\mathrm{Geom}}^{0,b, A, B}$.

Conditional reduction, independent review pending: let W be a continuous adapted real chordal Loewner driver, W_0=0, with dg_t(z)=2/(g_t(z)-W_t)dt in one usual filtration. For three real marks 0<a<b<c put X=g_t(a)-W_t and Y_i=g_t(b_i)-W_t, b_1=b,b_2=c. On each stopped compact localization with 0<X<Y_1<Y_2 and positive separations, assume BOTH C(X/Y_i) are local martingales, where C(u)=B(1/3,1/3)^(-1) integral_0^u [v(1-v)]^(-2/3)dv. Smooth inversion of the first makes W a semimartingale; the two Ito signed-measure equations force zero finite variation part and local martingale bracket 6dt. If the assumption holds for a countable mark/localization family covering every finite time, W/sqrt(6) is Brownian motion. The square-lattice martingale approximation needed to apply this reduction is unproved in this draft.

[Definition 5 (Bessel Space) of arXiv:2608.07365, 'A pathwise Ito formula \\for weakly differentiable functions'] For $p\in [1, \infty]$ and $\alpha> 0$ the Bessel space $\mathcal{L}^p_{\alpha}(\Rr^d)$ is defined by
\[
\mathcal{L}^p_{\alpha}(\Rr^d):=\{\, g_{\alpha}\star f\colon\, f\in L^p(\Rr^d) \,\},
\]
where $g_0:= \delta_0$, so that $g_{0}\star f =f$.  The space $\mathcal{L}^p_{\alpha}(\Rr^d)$ is endowed with the norm
\[
\|F\|_{\mathcal{L}^p_{\alpha}(\Rr^d)} :=\|f\|_{L^p(\Rr^d)}
\]
where $f\in L^p(\Rr^d)$ such that $F=g_{\alpha}\star f$.
title: Bessel Space

body:
[Lemma lem:ht.graph-laws of arXiv:2607.12459, 'Renormalisation of Inhomogeneous Random Graphs'] Let $\hat G^{(\ell)}[\hat X]$ be the inhomogeneous random graph on $[N_{L-\ell}]$ with edge densities
\[
b_\ell^{\neq}(I,J) = B\hat X_I^{(\ell)}\hat X_J^{(\ell)}, \qquad I\neq J,
\]
and self-loop densities
\[
\tfrac12 [b_\ell^{\neq}(I,I)+b_\ell^{=}(I)]
= \tfrac12\big[B\big(\hat X_I^{(\ell)}\big)^2+C\hat X_I^{(\ell)}\big].
\]
Let $\hat G_{\ell,\gamma,\delta,\eta}[\hat Y]$ be the inhomogeneous stable-law random graph on $[N_{L-\ell}]$ with edge densities
\[
c_\ell^{\neq}(I,J) = \delta \hat Y_I\hat Y_J, \qquad I\neq J,
\]
and self-loop densities
\[
\tfrac12\big[c_\ell^{\neq}(I,I)+c_\ell^{=}(I)\big] = \tfrac12\big[\delta(\hat Y_I)^2+\eta\hat Y_I\big].
\]
Then, for every measurable set $\mathcal A$ of graphs on $[N_{L-\ell}]$,
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb{E}_U\big[P\big(\hat G^{(\ell)}[\hat X]\in\mathcal A\mid U\big)\big]
&= P\big(\hat G^{(\ell)}[\hat X]\in\mathcal A\big),\\
\mathbb{E}_U\big[P\big(\hat G_{\ell,\gamma,\delta,\eta}[\hat Y]\in\mathcal A\mid U\big)\big]
&= P\big(G_{\ell,\gamma,\delta,\eta}[Y]\in\mathcal A\big).
\end{aligned}
\]
In the first line, the law on the right-hand side is the annealed graph law obtained by first sampling an i.i.d.\ family of block variables with the same law as $\hat X_I^{(\ell)}$ and then sampling edges and self-loops conditionally independently. In the second line, the law on the right-hand side is the annealed stable-law graph law.

ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Design the algorithm and check whether the exploration frontier remains Markov. Result: For bond percolation the peeling frontier is a two-colour boundary (free/blocked edges) and the algorithm peels the edge at the colour change, keeping the unexplored region a Boltzmann map with a boundary of the same type. For site percolation the colour lives on vertices and after peeling a face the newly exposed boundary vertices are uncoloured; the natural algorithm peels the edge whose left endpoint is black and right endpoint is uncoloured, colouring the new vertices as they appear. The unexplored region is then a Boltzmann map with a boundary condition that is a word in {black, white, uncoloured}, and the difficulty is that the length of the black segment is no longer a Markov chain by itself: the future depends on the positions of uncoloured vertices along the boundary. The frontier becomes Markov if one records the boundary word, which is an infinite-dimensional state. On triangulations the problem was solved (Angel-Curien) because degree-3 faces expose at most one new vertex per step, keeping the state finite; for general Boltzmann maps with large faces a peeled face exposes many uncoloured vertices at once. So a Markov site-percolation peeling exists exactly when faces expose boundedly many vertices, i.e. for bounded face degrees, and the general Boltzmann case requires a state space of boundary words; whether the threshold can still be computed from a word-valued Markov chain is the open part. Obstruction: Unbounded face degrees expose many uncoloured boundary vertices at once; the frontier state is a word, not an integer.

[Lem 6 of arXiv:2605.07369, '2605.07369'] Let $(X_n)_{n\ge 0}$ be a stochastic process taking values in $\rr$ and satisfying the stochastic approximation algorithm  (\ref{sa-0}).
Assume that  the conditions (\ref{sa-2}) and (\ref{g}) hold.
Then, for any $\varepsilon>0$ and $F>0$, there exists a positive constant $\delta\in(0,1)$ such that for all sufficiently large $n$, we have
\begin{align*}
\pp\left(\left|X_{n+1}-x^*\right|\ge \varepsilon\right)&\le \pp\Big(\left|X_{[\delta n]}-x^*\right|>F\Big)+
\pp\left(b \left|\sum_{i=[\delta n]}^n \frac{U_{i+1}}{i+1}\right|\ge 2\varepsilon\right)\\
&\ \ \   +\sum_{k=[\delta n]}^n\pp\left(b \left|\sum_{i=k+1}^n \frac{U_{i+1}}{i+1}\right|\ge \frac{\varepsilon}{4}\right).
\end{align*}
Here, $[\delta n]$ denotes the integer part of $\delta n$. The constant $\delta$ can be chosen to satisfy
$$
0<\delta<\exp\left(-\frac{2(F+\varepsilon)}{b K_1 \varepsilon}\right),
$$

[Theorem of arXiv:2604.09509, 'An Improved Bipartition Cover Bound for the Multispecies Coalescent Model'] If $m = \arg \min_{i=1,...,k} \lambda_i$, then the CDFs have asymptotics
        
        \[\begin{cases}
            1-F_k(T)  \sim   C_{m,k}\exp(-\lambda_m T), & T \uparrow \infty \text{ and k fixed,}\\
            F_k(T)  \sim \frac{\prod_{i=1}^k \lambda_i}{k!} T^{k}, &  T = o((s_{k}/k)^{-1}),\\
        \end{cases}\]
        \noindent where $T = o((s_k/k)^{-1})$ denotes any sequence of pairs $(T_n, k_n)$ so that $\lim_{n \to \infty} s_{k_n}T_n/k_n = 0$. More generally, in the same $T = o((s_k/k)^{-1})$ regime and for any finite $m \geqslant 0$
        \[\frac{F_k(T) - \sum_{r=0}^{m} a_{r,k}}{a_{m, k}} \to 0, \qquad a_{r,k} := (-1)^r \frac{h_{r}(\lambda_1,..., \lambda_k)\prod_{i=1}^k \lambda_i }{(k+r)!} T^{k+r}.\]

body: A set A of positive integers is sum-distinct if its 2^|A| subset sums are pairwise different. Exhaustive enumeration shows there are exactly two sum-distinct 5-element subsets of {1,...,13}, namely {3,6,11,12,13} and {6,9,11,12,13}, and none of the C(12,5) = 792 five-element subsets of {1,...,12} is sum-distinct, so the least such N is exactly 13. The 32 subset sums of {3,6,11,12,13} are 0, 3, 6, 9, 11 to 34, 36, 39, 42, 45. In Lean 4 (the formal-conjectures statement Erdos1.erdos_1.variants.least_N_5) the kernel decides the witness half, and the 792-set lower bound compiles in 425 s once maxRecDepth is raised. The corresponding statement for n = 9 (least N = 161) does not reduce to a finite witness check of the same size.

body:
[Lemma l:W.is.subgaussian of arXiv:2607.02013, 'Resolution of the Detection Threshold Conjecture for Random Geometric Graphs in the $d>n$ '] Let
\begin{equation}
{\mathcal{H}} =  \{\|I_n+W\|_{\operatorname{op}}\le 4 \}.
    
\end{equation}
If $d \ge (1+\epsilon) n$ for some arbitrarily small constant $\epsilon>0$, then there exists a constant $c>0$ only depending on $\epsilon$ such that 
$\mathbb{P}_0(W \in {\mathcal{H}}^c) \leq \mathop{\rm exp}(-cn)$ 
and,
for any zero-diagonal symmetric matrix $U$,
\[
\mathbb{E}_{X\sim \mathbb{P}_{0}}[\mathop{\rm exp}( \langle U,W\mathbf{1}_{\mathcal H}\rangle)]\le \mathop{\rm exp}\left(\frac{2 \|U\|^2}{d}\right)+1\le 2\mathop{\rm exp}\left(\frac{2\|U\|^2}{d}\right).
\]

\begin{proof}

Recall that $W=XX^\top -I_n$, so 

${\mathcal{H}}$ is implied by the event
$\{\|X\|_{\rm op} \le 2\}$.
Let $Z$ be an $n\times d$ matrix with i.i.d.\ standard gaussian entries, and let $D$ be the $n\times n$ diagonal matrix with diagonal entries $\|z_1\|,\ldots,\|z_n\|$. Then $X$ is equidistributed as $D^{-1}Z$, so we can bound
    \[\|X\|_{\rm op} \le 
    \frac{\|Z\|_{\rm op}}
        {\min_i \|z_i\|}\,.\]
By the standard concentration inequality for Gaussian matrices~[vershynin2010introduction], we have
\[\|Z\|_{\rm op}
\le\sqrt{d} + \sqrt{n}
+t\]
with probability at least $1-2\mathop{\rm exp}(-t^2/2)$. By the standard concentration bound for chi-squared random variables (Lemma~(l:chi.square.lower.tail of the paper)), we have
    \[
    \min\Big\{ \|z_i\|
    : 1\le i\le n\Big\}
    \ge d-(2d)^{1/2} t
    \]
with probability at least $1-n\mathop{\rm exp}(-t^2/2)$.  Taking $t=cn^{1/2}$, we conclude that with probability at least $1-3n\mathop{\rm exp}(-c^2 n/2)$, we have
\[\|X\|_{\rm op} \le \frac{1+(1+c)/\sqrt{1+\epsilon}}{[1-\sqrt{2}c/\sqrt{1+\epsilon}]^{1/2}} \le 2\,,\]
where the last inequality holds by choosing $c$ to be a sufficiently small constant  depending on $\epsilon$. 

Next, let $W_m$ denote the principal submatrix of $W$ formed by the first $m$ rows and columns. We will truncate on the event
$\mathcal H_m= \{\| I_m+W_m\|_{\operatorname{op}}\le 4 \}$.
Note that ${\mathcal{H}}_{m+1} \subset {\mathcal{H}}_{m}$ for all $1 \le m \le n-1$ and $\mathcal{H} = \mathcal{H}_n$. Abbreviating $u_n$ for the last column of $U$, we can bound
\begin{align*}
     &\ \mathbb{E}_{X\sim \mathbb{P}_{0}}\Big[\mathop{\rm exp}( \langle U,W\mathbf{1}_{\mathcal H}\rangle)\Big]\\
   \le &\ \mathbb{E}_{x_1,\dots,x_n}
   \bigg[\mathop{\rm exp}\bigg( \sum_{i<j}u_{ij}\langle x_i,x_j\rangle\bigg)
   \mathbf{1}\{W_n \in \mathcal H_n\}\bigg]+1\\
   \le&\ \mathbb{E}_{x_1,\dots,x_{n-1}}\bigg[\mathop{\rm exp}\bigg(
   \sum_{i<j<n}u_{ij}\langle x_i,x_j\rangle\bigg)\mathbf{1}\{ W_{n-1} \in \mathcal H_{n-1}\} \mathbb{E}_{x_n}\bigg[\mathop{\rm exp}\bigg(
   \bigg\langle \sum_{i<n} u_{in}x_i,x_n
   \bigg\rangle
   \bigg)\bigg]\bigg]+1\\
    \le&\ \mathbb{E}_{x_1,\dots,x_{n-1}}\bigg[\mathop{\rm exp}\bigg(\sum_{i<j<n}u_{ij}\langle x_i,x_j\rangle\bigg)\mathbf{1}\{W_{n-1}\in \mathcal H_{n-1}\}\cdot \mathop{\rm exp}\bigg(\frac{ (u_n)^\top (I_{n-1}+ W_{n-1}) u_n}{2d}\bigg)\bigg]+1\\
    \le&\ \mathbb{E}_{x_1,\dots,x_{n-1}}\bigg[\mathop{\rm exp}\bigg(\sum_{i<j<n}u_{ij}\langle x_i,x_j\rangle\bigg)\mathbf{1}\{W_{n-1} \in \mathcal H_{n-1}\}\bigg]\cdot \mathop{\rm exp}\left(\frac{2 \|u_n\|^2
    }{d}\right)+1\,,
\end{align*}
where the second-to-last inequality is by Lemma~(lem:beta.mgf of the paper), and the
 last inequality holds because we have $\|I_{n-1}+W_{n-1}\|_{\operatorname{op} }
\le 4$ on the event ${\mathcal{H}}_{n-1}$.
Iterating the above gives the claimed bound.
\end{proof}

body: [Corollary 3.4 of arXiv:2603.27659, 'Operator Norm Bounds for Multi-leg Matrix Tensors and Applications to Random Matrix Theory'] For $m,N\in\mathbb{N}$, for any permutations $\sigma_{1},\sigma_{2}\in\mathcal{P}([m])$, we have $\displaystyle\max_{\|A_{1}\|,\ldots,\|A_{m}\|\leq 1}\left|\left(\mathrm{Tr}_{\sigma_{1}}\otimes\mathrm{Tr}_{\sigma_{2}}\right)\left(A_{1},\ldots,A_{m}\right)\right|\leq N^{R(\sigma_{1})+R(\sigma_{2})}.$

Let X be a centered finite Gaussian with PSD covariance C, and P a finite nonempty family of nonempty positively weighted paths. Let D_xi=min_p sum_{v in p} a_pv exp(xi X_v) and F_beta(y)=-(1/beta)log sum_p exp[-beta log(sum_{v in p} a_pv exp(y_v))]. For 0<=a<b, E log D_b-E log D_a=lim_{beta->infinity} integral_a^b xi E tr[C Hess F_beta(xi X)] dxi. Each endpoint has soft-min error at most log|P|/beta. This assertion does not exchange the beta limit with a derivative.
V finite
X centered Gaussian with PSD covariance C, singular covariance allowed
Finite nonempty family P of nonempty paths
Positive deterministic weights on each path support
xi>=0; beta>0
0<=a<b<infinity

[Thm weak_convergence of arXiv:2605.29073, 'Volterra clocks and their pure-jump limits: \\hitting times of curved boundaries'] Let $\left(W^n\,, X^n\right)_{n \geq 0}$ be a sequence of weak solutions to (equation eq:Volterra_clock of the paper) on $[0\,,T]\,$, for the sequence of inputs $(G_0^n\,, K^n\,, f^n\,, \lambda^n\,, \nu^n)_{n \geq 0}\,$, where $\lambda^n\,, \nu^n \geq 0\,$, $f^n$ satisfies Assumption (assumption:f of the paper), $K^n \in L^1_{loc}(\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}_+\,, \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}_+)$ and $G_0^n : \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}_+ \to \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}_+$ is non-decreasing with $G_0^n(0) = 0\,$, for each $n \geq 0\,$. Suppose that:
    \begin{itemize}
        \item $K^n(t)\,dt \Rightarrow \delta_0(dt)$ weakly on $[0\,,T]\,$.
        \item $G_0^n \to G_0$ pointwise on $[0\,,T]\,$, where $G_0$ is continuous.
        \item $f^n \to_{l.u.} f$ on $\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}_+$, with $\sup_{n \geq 0} \sup_{x \geq 0} f^n(x) / (1 + x^2) < + \infty\,$.
        \item $\lambda^n \to \lambda$ and $\nu^n \to \nu\,$.
    \end{itemize}
    Then, we have the weak convergence of processes 
    $$
    \left(W^n\,, X^n \right) \overset{n \to \infty}{\implies} \left(W^*\,, X^*\right)
    $$
    on $D^{\circ}[0\,,T]\,$, where $W^*$ is a standard Brownian motion and 
    $$
    X^*_t = \inf\{s \geq 0\,:\, (1+ \lambda)s - \nu\,W^*_{f(s)} > G_0(t)\}\,, \quad t \leq T\,.
    $$

[Proposition 37 (Combined high-tail comparison and constant) of arXiv:2605.14511, 'Clumsy and Careless:\\ Stationary-Entry Flux in Non-monotone Coupon Collectors'] Fix $\alpha\in[0,1)$ and $\beta\in(0,1)$, and put $Q=1-\alpha$ and $S=1-\beta$.  Let $\nu_n^{\alpha,\beta}$ be the stationary law of the combined count chain \eqref{eq:combined-transition}, and let $w_{n,k}^{\alpha,\beta}$ be defined by \eqref{eq:combined-lucky-scale}.  There are constants $0<c<C<\infty$ and an integer $M<\infty$, depending only on $\alpha,\beta$, such that, for all sufficiently large $n$ and all $M\le k\le n$,
\[
        c w_{n,k}^{\alpha,\beta}
        \le \nu_n^{\alpha,\beta}(k)
        \le C w_{n,k}^{\alpha,\beta}.
\]
Moreover,
\[
        \nu_n^{\alpha,\beta}(n)
        \sim
        \frac{1}{(S;S)_\infty}
        \frac{n!}{n^n}Q^nS^{n(n+1)/2}.
\]

[Lemma 20 of arXiv:2606.01742, 'Large deviation principles for SPDEs with locally Lipschitz coefficients'] (\cite[Lemma A.1]{BMS} and \cite[Lemma A.4]{LWYZ17})
Let $K$ be a compact set in $\mathbb R$ and let $\{V^\varepsilon(t,x):(t,x)\in[0,T]\times K\}$ be a family of real-valued functions. Assume that
\begin{itemize}
  \item[(A1).] for any $(t,x)\in[0,T]\times K$,
     $$\lim_{\varepsilon\rightarrow 0}|V^{\varepsilon}(t,x)|=0;$$
  \item[(A2).] there exist $\beta_1,\beta_2>0$ satisfied that for any $(t,x),(t',x')\in[0,T]\times K$,
$$
|V^\varepsilon(t,x)-V^\varepsilon(t',x')|\le C_{6,4}(|t-t'|^{\beta_1}+|x-x'|^{\beta_2}),
$$
where $C_{6,4}$ is a constant independent of $\varepsilon$.
\end{itemize}
Then for any $\theta\in(0,1)$, we have
$$\lim_{\varepsilon\to 0}\|V^\varepsilon\|_{\theta\beta_1,\theta\beta_2}=0. $$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma 20 of arXiv:2606.01742

body: Mordell-Weil theorem: Let A be an abelian variety over a number field K. Then A(K), the group of K-rational points of A, is a finitely generated abelian group, called the Mordell-Weil group; equivalently A(K) is isomorphic to Z^r x T, where r >= 0 is the rank and T is the finite torsion subgroup. The special case in which A = E is an elliptic curve and K = Q is Mordell's theorem, which answers a question apparently posed by Henri Poincare around 1901 and was proved by Louis Mordell in 1922; the general case is due to Andre Weil (1928). It is a foundational theorem of Diophantine geometry and of the arithmetic of abelian varieties.
title: Mordell–Weil theorem

[Df reachability of arXiv:2605.14910, 'Sharp Phase Transition for the Formation of Infinite Tubes'] For two vertices $\Delta$ and $\Delta'$ in the associated directed graph $G_w$, we say that $\Delta'$ is \emph{reachable} from $\Delta$ in $G_w$, and write $\Delta\rightsquigarrow_w\Delta'$, if there exists a directed path from $\Delta$ to $\Delta'$; that is, a finite sequence $(\Delta_0,\Delta_1,\ldots,\Delta_I)$ of vertices in $G_w$ such that $\Delta_0=\Delta$, $\Delta_I=\Delta'$, and $(\Delta_{i-1},\Delta_i)\in E_w$ for all $i=1,2,\ldots,I$.
  Furthermore, we say $\Delta$ \emph{reaches infinity} in $G_w$, and write $\Delta\rightsquigarrow_w\infty$, if there exists an infinite self-avoiding directed path from $\Delta$; that is, a sequence $(\Delta_0,\Delta_1,\ldots)$ of distinct vertices such that $\Delta_0=\Delta$ and $(\Delta_{i-1},\Delta_i)\in E_w$ for all $i\in\mathbb{N}$.
title: Reachability

[Thm stargrp_NS-NStability of arXiv:2606.29829, ''] Let $\lambda\vdash n$, and $\mathscr{B}_{\lambda}$ be the orthonormal basis of $V^{\lambda}$ containing the normalized GT-vectors. Also, for every $n\geq 1$, let $\mathfrak{f}_n:S_n\longrightarrow\{0,1\}$ be a Boolean function. Then,
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item The sequence of $\{\mathfrak{f}_n\}_n$ is noise sensitive with respect to the interchange process on $\ST$ if and only if for all positive integer $k>0$
		\[	\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\;\sum_{\lambda\vdash n} \frac{f^{\lambda}}{n!^2}\sum_{\substack{T\in\std(\lambda)\\n-1-k<c(b_T(n))\leq n-2}}\sum_{S\in\std(\lambda)}\left|\text{The }(S,T)\text{th entry of the matrix }\Big[\widehat{\mathfrak{f}_n}(\lambda)\Big]_{\mathscr{B}_{\lambda}}\right|^2=0.\]
		\item The sequence of $\{\mathfrak{f}_n\}_n$ is noise stable with respect to the interchange process on $\ST$ if and only if for all $\delta>0$ there exists a positive integer $k$ such that
		\[\sup_n\;\sum_{\lambda\vdash n}\frac{f^{\lambda}}{n!^2}\sum_{\substack{T\in\std(\lambda)\\c(b_T(n))\leq n-1-k}} \sum_{S\in\std(\lambda)}\left|\text{The }(S,T)\text{th entry of the matrix }\Big[\widehat{\mathfrak{f}_n}(\lambda)\Big]_{\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}}\right|^2<\delta.\]
	\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Thm stargrp_NS-NStability of arXiv:2606.29829

TECHNIQUE CARD (drafted from a spec by a helper model, every card read and seven corrected by the Fable agent on 2026-09-07; canonical statements only, no original claim). A Nash inequality on a graph with Dirichlet form E and reference measure mu has the form ||f||_2^{2+4/d} <= C E(f,f) ||f||_1^{4/d} for all f in the domain of the form, where d is an effective dimension parameter. Such an inequality is classically equivalent, by results of Nash and later Carlen-Kusuoka-Stroock, to an on-diagonal heat-kernel upper bound p_t(x,x) <= C' t^{-d/2} for the associated Markov semigroup, and combining it with matching volume-growth and effective-resistance-growth estimates, within the general framework relating resistance growth to heat-kernel decay used for fractal-like and random graphs, yields two-sided sub-Gaussian or Gaussian heat-kernel bounds. On graphs where effective resistance to the complement of a ball of radius n grows like n^zeta and volume grows like n^alpha, this gives sub-Gaussian heat-kernel estimates with off-diagonal decay governed by the exponent alpha+zeta, a technique central to analysis on fractals and on random graphs such as critical percolation clusters or random walk among random conductances. The technique does not give the resistance or volume exponents themselves, which are separate geometric inputs, and a full two-sided heat-kernel estimate typically requires both the Nash-type inequality, giving the upper bound, and a separate lower-bound argument, often via a chaining construction or an elliptic Harnack inequality. Typical failure: Assuming ordinary Euclidean Gaussian heat-kernel scaling, of the t^{-d/2} exp(-|x-y|^2/4t) form, transfers automatically to a random or fractal-like graph without re-deriving the resistance exponent zeta; on structures such as the incipient infinite cluster of critical percolation, or random conductance models with heavy-tailed conductances, the correct scaling is sub-Gaussian with zeta != 1, and using the Euclidean exponent silently mis-states both the walk dimension and the tail behavior of the heat kernel. Canonical reference: Nash, 1958, American Journal of Mathematics; Carlen, Kusuoka and Stroock, 1987, Annales de l'Institut Henri Poincare; Barlow, 2004, Annals of Probability; Kumagai, Random Walks on Disordered Media and their Scaling Limits, 2014, Springer.
a well-defined Dirichlet form and reversible Markov chain with a reference measure mu
a valid Nash-type functional inequality with a specified effective dimension d
for two-sided estimates: matching volume-growth and effective-resistance-growth bounds on balls
typically also an elliptic Harnack inequality, or comparable regularity, to establish the matching lower heat-kernel bound
title: Technique: Nash Inequality and Heat-Kernel Bounds via Resistance

body: Standard Brownian motion (the Wiener process) is a stochastic process W with W_0 = 0, independent increments, W_t - W_s distributed N(0, t - s) for s < t, and continuous paths. It exists (Wiener), is a martingale, is nowhere differentiable almost surely, has quadratic variation [W]_t = t, and is the scaling limit of random walks (Donsker).
title: Brownian Motion

body:
[Lemma 21 of arXiv:2608.19744, 'Conditioned Brownian motion and local equivalence of path ensembles'] Let $(\mu_{T,x})_{T\geq1,x\in\mathbb R^d}$ be probability measures on $\mathbb R$, with
characteristic functions $\chi_{T,x}$.  Suppose that, for every compact
$K\subset\mathbb R^d$, the following hold for some $\sigma^2>0$.
\begin{enumerate}
 \item Locally uniformly in $(x,v)$, 
       \[
       \chi_{T,x}(v/\sqrt T)\longrightarrow \mathrm e^{-\sigma^2v^2/2}.
       \]
 \item There are $\varepsilon,c,C,\gamma>0$ such that for $T$ large enough
       \[
       \sup_{x\in K}|\chi_{T,x}(u)|
       \leq C\bigl(\mathrm e^{-cTu^2}+ \mathrm e^{-\gamma T}\bigr),
       \qquad |u|\leq\varepsilon.
       \]
 \item For every $0<\delta<R<\infty$, there are $C_{K,\delta,R},\eta>0$
       such that for $T$ large enough
       \[
       \sup_{\substack{x\in K\\\delta\leq|u|\leq R}}
       |\chi_{T,x}(u)|
       \leq C_{K,\delta,R}\mathrm e^{-\eta T}.
       \]
\end{enumerate}
Then, for every directly Riemann-integrable $h$ and every $M<\infty$,
\begin{equation}
 \sup_{\substack{x\in K\\|a|\leq M}}
 \left|
  \sqrt T\int_\R \mu_{T,x}(\de y) \, h(y-a)
  -\frac1{\sqrt{2\pi\sigma^2}}
   \int_\R \de y \, h(y)
 \right|
 \longrightarrow0.
 
\end{equation}
title: Lemma 21 of arXiv:2608.19744

[Introcor 6 (Convergence of ergodic averages) of arXiv:2608.03353, '\bfseries A Direct Route to Markov Chain Convergence\\[2mm] \Large via Asymptotic Equivale'] In each of Theorems \ref{thm:crit}, \ref{thm:posdens}, \ref{thm:mhintro}, \ref{thm:eventual} and \ref{thm:gibbsintro}, let
$(X_{k})_{k \in \Nz}$ be the Markov chain with kernel $T$ started in an arbitrary
initial distribution $\mu$, and let $\Prb_{\mu}$ denote its law on the space of
trajectories. Then for every measurable map $f : \XX \to \R$ with
$\int_{\XX} |f| \dd\pi < \infty$,
\[
  \frac{1}{n}\sum_{k=0}^{n-1} f(X_{k}) \longrightarrow \int_{\XX} f \dd\pi
  \qquad (n \to \infty), \quad \Prb_{\mu}\text{-almost surely.}
\]
If $f$ is bounded, the convergence holds in addition in $L^{r}(\Prb_{\mu})$ for every
number $r \in [1,\infty)$. If $\mu \le M\pi$ for some number $M \in [1,\infty)$ ---
for instance if $\mu = \pi$ --- then, for every number $r \in [1,\infty)$, the
convergence holds in $L^{r}(\Prb_{\mu})$ for every $f$ with
$\int_{\XX} |f|^{r} \dd\pi < \infty$.

In Theorems \ref{thm:posdens}--\ref{thm:gibbsintro}, where $\pi$ is presented by a
density $p$ with respect to a reference measure $\lambda$, the integrals against $\pi$
read $\int_{\XX} f(x)\,p(x)\dd\lambda(x)$ and the condition $\mu \le M\pi$ says that
$\mu$ has a $\lambda$-density bounded by $Mp$. Theorem \ref{thm:crit} names no
reference measure, and the statement is the one displayed above. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Convergence of ergodic averages

[Definition 2 of arXiv:2607.20838, 'Long-memory Markov chains with power-law intensities'] The latent processes $\mathbf{X}_n = \{(X_n, c_n)\}$ evolve according to 
	\begin{equation}
		\mathbf{X}_n = \Psi(\mathbf{X}_{n-1}, \tau_n) = (\Psi_x(x, c, t), \Psi_c(x, c, t)).
		
	\end{equation}
	where
	\begin{align}
		\Psi_x(x, c, t) &= x \left(1 + \frac{t}{c}\right)^{-p} + \xi,  \\
		\Psi_c(x, c, t) &= \frac{\Psi_x(x, c, t)}{\,\frac{x}{c} \left(1 + \tfrac{t}{c}\right)^{-p-1} + \tfrac{\xi}{\gamma}}, 
	\end{align}
	with parameters $\mu> 0, \gamma> 0, \xi > 0$ and $p>1$.
	Equivalently, the update equations can be written as
	\begin{align*}
		&X_n = X_{n-1} \left(1  + \frac{\tau_n}{c_{n-1}} \right)^{-p} + \xi \\
		&\frac{X_n}{c_n} =  \frac{X_{n-1}}{c_{n-1}} \left(1  + \frac{\tau_n}{c_{n-1}} \right)^{-p-1} + \frac{\xi}{\gamma}.
	\end{align*}
	Define $\Phi(t, x, c)$ as
	\begin{align}
		\Phi(t, x, c) & = \int_0^t  \lambda_{n-1}(s; x, c) \D s= \int_0^t \left( \mu + \frac{x c^p}{(c+s)^p} \right)\, \D s \\
		& = \mu t + \dfrac{x c}{p-1}\left( 1 - \bigg(1+\dfrac{t}{c}\bigg)^{-p+1}  \right). 
	\end{align}
	The inter-arrival time $\tau_n$ is generated via the inverse transform
	\[
	\tau_n = \Phi^{-1}(\varepsilon_n,  X_{n-1}, c_{n-1}),
	\]
	where the inverse is taken with respect to $t$ for fixed $x$ and $c$,
	and $\{\varepsilon_n\}$ is an i.i.d. sequence drawn from $F_\varepsilon$
	satisfying $F_\varepsilon(0) = 0$ (so that $\varepsilon_n \ge 0$ a.s.), $\mu_{\varepsilon} = \mathbb{E}[\varepsilon] < \infty$,
	and $\mathbb{E}[\varepsilon^2] < \infty$.

[Definition stoch_domination of arXiv:2504.00512, 'Localization-delocalization transition for a random block matrix model at the edge'] {\rm{(i)}} Let
	\[\xi=\left(\xi^{(N)}(u):N\in\mathbb N, u\in U^{(N)}\right),\hskip 10pt \zeta=\left(\zeta^{(N)}(u):N\in\mathbb N, u\in U^{(N)}\right),\]
	be two families of non-negative random variables, where $U^{(N)}$ is a possibly $N$-dependent parameter set. We say $\xi$ is stochastically dominated by $\zeta$, uniformly in $u$, if for any fixed (small) $\tau>0$ and (large) $D>0$, 
	\[\mathbb P\bigg(\bigcup_{u\in U^{(N)}}\left\{\xi^{(N)}(u)>N^\tau\zeta^{(N)}(u)\right\}\bigg)\le N^{-D}\]
	for large enough $N\ge N_0(\tau, D)$, and we will use the notation $\xi\prec\zeta$. 
	
	If for some complex family $\xi$ we have $|\xi|\prec\zeta$, then we will also write $\xi \prec \zeta$ or $\xi=\mathrm{O}_\prec(\zeta)$. 
	
	\vspace{5pt}
	\noindent {\rm{(ii)}} As a convention, for two deterministic quantities $\xi$ and $\zeta$, we will write $\xi\prec\zeta$ if and only if $|\xi|\le N^\tau |\zeta|$ for any constant $\tau>0$. 

 \vspace{5pt}
	\noindent {\rm{(iii)}} Let $A$ be a family of random matrices and $\zeta$ be a family of non-negative random variables. Then, we use $A=\mathrm{O}_\prec(\zeta)$ to mean that $\|A\|\prec \zeta$, where $\|\cdot\|$ denotes the operator norm. 
	
	\vspace{5pt}
	\noindent {\rm{(iv)}} We say an event $\Xi$ holds with high probability (w.h.p.) if for any constant $D>0$, $\mathbb P(\Xi)\ge 1- N^{-D}$ for large enough $N$. More generally, we say an event $\Omega$ holds $w.h.p.$ in $\Xi$ if for any constant $D>0$,
	$\mathbb{P}( \Xi\setminus \Omega)\le N^{-D}$ for large enough $N$.
title: Stochastic domination and high probability event

body: In mathematics, the term homology, originally introduced in algebraic topology, has three primary, closely related usages. First, there is the homology of a chain complex, a sequence of abelian groups, called homology groups, which are regarded as fundamental invariants of the chain complex. Secondly, when one can associate a chain complex to a different mathematical object, one can also associate its homology to that object. Distinct procedures of associating chain complexes to a given object are grouped into homology theories. Finally, homology is important in the study of topological spaces. Under nice conditions in which distinct homology theories for a single topological space produce the same homology groups, one can define a single homology of a topological space. This last notion of homology is closely related to topological ideas frequently discussed in popular mathematics such as the holes of a surface or the cycles of a graph. There is also a related notion of the cohomology of a cochain complex, giving rise to various cohomology theories, in addition to the notion of the cohomology of a topological space.
title: Homology (mathematics)

[Definition def:circuit-primitives of arXiv:2608.29403, 'Kac's Walk on Rotation Matrices Mixes in $\boldsymbol{\Theta(n^2)}$ Steps:\\ A Proof Disco'] For an ordered finite set $S$ of oriented carrier labels, write
$\mathscr H_S=\bigotimes_{u\in S}H_u$, with every factor equipped with
the Euclidean Hilbert norm.  A \emph{normalized Brauer primitive} is a
signed carrier permutation, a wedge reversal, full transpose, a share
turn, a through string, the orthogonal antisymmetrizer, or a cup/cap
normalized so that its operator norm is one.  A share turn is the fixed
signed boundary permutation, possibly followed by full transpose,
induced when a principal pivot reverses one of the two ordered boundary
intervals.  The two coefficient primitives are
\[
 \widehat C_{uv}=\iota_{uv}C\pi_{uv}:H_u\otimes H_v\to H_u\otimes H_v,
\]
where $\pi_{uv}$ is the normalized orthogonal projection and
identification onto $\Lambda^2H$, and $\iota_{uv}=\pi_{uv}^*$; hence
$\widehat C_{uv}$ is zero on $\operatorname{Sym}^2H$ and has norm $K$.
The other coefficient primitive is the restriction/re-expression of
(eq:2.1.3 of the paper) as the Bianchi transfer
\[
 (\Phi_CY)_{ik}=\sum_{m,n}C_{in,mk}Y_{mn},
 \qquad Y\in\Lambda^2H.
\]
The first Bianchi identity identifies the latter with the physical action
of $C$.  A \emph{safe gate} is a typed composite of these primitives,
including the $AA$ words and correctly oriented $AB$ words used below.
Its degree is the number of coefficient primitives.  Thus a degree-$d$
safe gate $G:\mathscr H_S\to\mathscr H_T$ satisfies
$\|G\|_{\rm op}\le K^d$; untouched factors are ancillary identities.

A coefficient box has four darts
$L_{i,0},L_{i,1},R_{i,0},R_{i,1}$.  For a column pairing $q$, a
\emph{packet} is a connected component of the box-incidence graph whose
edges are the $q$-pairs joining different boxes.  A $q$-pair joining the
two darts of one wedge is forbidden and gives zero.  An allowed
\emph{smoothing} chooses at each box either
\[
 h_i^{\parallel}=\{L_{i,0}R_{i,0},L_{i,1}R_{i,1}\},\qquad
 h_i^{\times}=\{L_{i,0}R_{i,1},L_{i,1}R_{i,0}\}.
\]
The alternating circuits of $q\vee h$ are the \emph{smoothing
carriers}; adjoining one carrier means adjoining one identity factor
$I_H$.  The smoothing support $\operatorname{supp}_h(i)$ of a box is the
one- or two-element set of $q\vee h$ carriers containing its two
$h$-passages.  A \emph{ported pair comb} on two chosen carriers consists of all
boxes whose smoothing support is that pair, together with every singleton-support box
assigned to it exactly once; removing all other support groups leaves
their boundary darts as linearly ordered typed ports.  These definitions
fix the domains and codomains of every safe word, fold, comb, and
attachment below.

An \emph{ambient rooted ribbon record} $\Gamma$ consists of a common
finite dart set, its coefficient boxes and local wedge signs, a row
pairing $p$, a column pairing $q$, a rooted trace pairing $r$, and the
declared boundary/root data.  Thus $p\vee r$ is the disjoint union of the
original trace circuits in that record; its components, not temporary
proof cuts, receive the normalization bases below.  The more detailed
Weingarten data carried by $\Gamma$ are specified in
(def:ribbon-record of the paper).
title: Typed circuit primitives

[Theorem th44 of arXiv:2604.24914, 'SPDEs with time-independent\\ L\'evy colored noise'] a) If $\kappa =H_{d,\alpha/2}$ for some $\alpha>0$, then
\[
J_p(t) \leq C \int_{\mathbb{R}^d}|\mathcal{F} G_t(\xi)|^2 e^{-\frac{\alpha|\xi|^2}{2}}d\xi \quad \mbox{for any $p>0$}.
\]
b) If $\kappa=R_{d,\alpha/2}$ for some $\alpha \in (0,d)$, then
\[
J_p(t) \leq C \|G_t\|_{L^q(\mathbb{R}^d)}^2 \quad \mbox{for any} \quad p>\frac{2d}{2d-\alpha},
\]
provided that $G_t \in L^q(\mathbb{R}^d)$, where $\frac{1}{q}=\frac{1}{p}+\frac{\alpha}{2d}$.\\
c) If $\kappa \in L^1(\mathbb{R}^d)$ (in particular if $\kappa=B_{d,\alpha/2}$ for some $\alpha>0$), then
\[
J_p(t) \leq C \|G_t\|_{L^p(\mathbb{R}^d)}^2 \quad \mbox{for any}  \quad p\geq 1,
\]
provided that $G_t \in L^p(\mathbb{R}^d)$. (Here $C>0$ is a constant which depends on $(d,\alpha,p)$.) (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition 3 (Riemannian complex) of arXiv:2609.00183, '2609.00183'] A {\bf Riemannian complex} is a cell complex $Y$ equipped with a collection of metrics $G=\{G^S\}$ such that 
\begin{enumerate}
    \item each cell $S$ of $Y$ is endowed with a smooth metric $G^S.$ 
    \item the metric $G^S$ is smooth in the interior of $S$ and extends smoothly to $\partial S.$
\end{enumerate}
Moreover, if $F$ is a face of $S$, then
\[
G^S|_{F}=G^{F}.
\]
title: Riemannian complex

[Proposition 15 of arXiv:2608.30549, '\vspace{-1cm}Maximally Spread Out Measures and Implications\\{} for Phase Transitions in A'] Let $d \in \N$, $p \in [1,\infty]$, $m \in \N_0$ and $\alpha \in (0,1]$ and set $r := m + \alpha$.
  We say that $f : [0,1]^d \to \R$ belongs to $C^{m,\alpha}([0,1]^d)$
  if $f$ is $m$ times continuously differentiable with
  \[
    \| f \|_{C^{m,\alpha}}
    := \max
       \Bigl\{ 
         \| f \|_{L^\infty},
         \quad
         \max_{\beta \in \N_0^d, |\beta| = m} \,\,
           \sup_{x,y \in [0,1]^d, x \neq y} \,\,
             \frac{|\partial^\beta f (x) - \partial^\beta f(y)|}{\norm{x-y}^\alpha}
       \Bigr\}
    < \infty
    .
  \]
  Then, as a subset of $\XX = L^p ([0,1]^d)$, the set
  \[
    \SC
    := \bigl\{ f \in C^{m,\alpha}([0,1]^d) \,\,:\,\, \| f \|_{C^{m,\alpha}} \leq 1 \bigr\}
  \]
  satisfies $\md(\SC) = \frac{d}{r}$,
  there exists a Borel probability measure on $\XX = L^p ([0,1]^d)$
  that is critical for $\SC$,
  and the family of neural networks
  \(
    (\CalA_n)_{n \in \N} = \bigl(\CalNN_n (3,\R^d)\bigr)_{n \in \N}
  \)
  defined in \Cref{prop:NNApproximationOfControlledComplexity} (with $g = 3$)
  is optimal for $\SC$ in the class of families of controlled complexity in $L^p([0,1]^d)$.
  In particular, a phase transition as in
  \Cref{thm:PhaseTransitionForFamiliesWithControlledComplexity} occurs.
title: Proposition 15 of arXiv:2608.30549

[Definition def:trap-family of arXiv:2604.13968, 'Divisible sandpiles via random walks in random scenery'] For a finite set $C\subset V$ and $y\in V$, the \textbf{inverse-degree exit time} from~$C$ starting at~$y$ is
		\[
		\Theta_C(y)\coloneqq\sum_{v\in C}g_C(y,v)=\mathbb{E}_y\Bigl[\sum_{k=0}^{\tau_C-1}\frac{1}{\deg(X_k)}\Bigr]\,.
		\]
		We say that $G$ admits a \textbf{uniform local trap condition} if for every $L>0$ there exist $r_L$ and $M_L$, and for each $y\in V$ a finite connected set $C_L(y)$, such that
		\[
		y\in C_L(y)\subseteq B(y,r_L),\qquad |C_L(y)|\leq M_L,\qquad\Theta_{C_L(y)}(y)\geq L\,.
		\]

body:
[Corollary 41 (The Metropolis--Hastings algorithm converges; Theorem \ref{thm:mhintro}) of arXiv:2608.03353, '\bfseries A Direct Route to Markov Chain Convergence\\[2mm] \Large via Asymptotic Equivale'] Let $(\XX,\XXA)$ be a measurable space, $\lambda$ a $\sigma$-finite measure on it,
and let the target be $\pi(A) = \int_{A} p \dd\lambda$ for a measurable map
$p : \XX \to (0,\infty)$ with $\int_{\XX} p \dd\lambda = 1$. Let the proposal be the
Markov kernel $Q(A \mid x) = \int_{A} q(y \mid x)\,\lambda(\dd y)$, given by an
$\XXA\otimes\XXA$-measurable map $q : \XX\times\XX \to [0,\infty)$ with
$\int_{\XX} q(y \mid x)\,\lambda(\dd y) = 1$ for every $x \in \XX$, define the
acceptance probability
\[
  a : \XX\times\XX \to [0,1], \qquad
  a(y \mid x) := \min\Bigl\{ 1,\ \frac{p(y)\,q(x \mid y)}{p(x)\,q(y \mid x)} \Bigr\}
  \quad\bigl(:= 1 \text{ when } q(y \mid x) = 0\bigr),
\]
and let $T$ be the Metropolis--Hastings kernel
\[
  T(A \mid x) := \int_{A} a(y \mid x)\,q(y \mid x)\,\lambda(\dd y) + r(x)\,\ind_{A}(x),
  \qquad
  r(x) := 1 - \int_{\XX} a(y \mid x)\,q(y \mid x)\,\lambda(\dd y) .
\]
Assume
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep,topsep=3pt]
  \item $q(y \mid x) > 0$ for $(\lambda\otimes\lambda)$-almost every $(x,y) \in \XX\times\XX$;
  \item for every $x \in \XX$ the set $\{ y \in \XX : q(y \mid x) > 0 \text{ and } q(x \mid y) > 0 \} \in \XXA$ has positive $\lambda$-measure.
\end{enumerate}
Then $\pi$ is the unique invariant probability measure of $T$, and
$\tv{T^{n}\circ\mu - \pi} \to 0$ for every initial distribution $\mu \in \Prob$.

Both hypotheses hold in either of the following two cases, which are the ones met in
practice and which give Theorem \ref{thm:mhintro}:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*),nosep,topsep=3pt]
  \item $q(y \mid x) > 0$ for every $(x,y) \in \XX\times\XX$;
  \item $q$ is symmetric, $q(y \mid x) = q(x \mid y)$ for all $(x,y)$, and
        $q(y \mid x) > 0$ for $(\lambda\otimes\lambda)$-almost every $(x,y)$.
\end{enumerate}

[Cor lem:1block of arXiv:2601.10568, 'Hydrodynamic Limit with a Weierstrass-type result'] Fix $L\in\mathbb{N}_+$, $w\in\mathbb{T}_N$ and $y\notin B_{L}(w)$. For each $x\in\mathbb{T}_N$, let $\varphi_{x}:[0,T]\times \mathcal{D}_{\Omega_N}[0,T]\to\mathbb{R}$ be independent of the occupation-values in $\{x+w+r,x+y\}_{r\in B_{L}}$, and such that $\text{c}_{t,\varphi}:=\int_0^t\sup_{x\in\mathbb{T}_N,\eta\in\Omega_N}|\varphi_x(\cdot,s)|\mathrm{d} s<\infty $.

For every $t\in [0,T]$ it holds that
    \begin{align}
        \mathbb{E}_{\mu_N}
        \bigg[
        \bigg|
        \int_{0}^t
        \frac{1}{N}\sum_{x\in\mathbb{T}_N}
        \varphi_{x}(s,\eta_{N^2s})
        \big(
        \inner{\tau^{x+w}\eta_{N^2s}}_{L}
        -\eta_{N^2s}(x+y)
        \big)
        \mathrm{d} s
        \bigg|
        \bigg]
\\        \leq 
        \frac{4\sqrt{2\text{c}_\alpha}c_{T,\varphi}}{\sqrt{\min\{\mathbf{r}_{\beta,\ell_N}\}TN^2}}
        \bigg(
        \mathrm{d}(w,y)+\frac1L\sum_{r\in B_L}\mathrm{d}(r,y)
        \bigg)
.
    \end{align}
title: One-block estimate

DRAFT; independent referee pending. For a unit-rate Poisson process N, M^n_t=1-t+nN_{t/n}, 0<=t<=1, is a nonnegative true martingale in its own natural filtration. Its paths eventually equal 1-t on the entire interval almost surely, because the first Poisson jump time is positive. Thus it converges uniformly almost surely to a continuous deterministic non-martingale. Uniform integrability is absent: E[M^n_t]=1 but E[1-t]=1-t. Joint path convergence alone cannot pass a renormalized observable's conditional martingale identity to the limit.

body:
[Definition 2 (Admissible deterministic diagonal resolution) of arXiv:2606.16662, '2606.16662'] A deterministic diagonal resolution for a finite family \(\cM\) assigns to
each label \(\tau\in\cM\) deterministic diagonal Volterra operators
\(\Ret^\tau_\Lambda\) and \(\Ctr^\tau_\Lambda\) such that
\begin{equation}
        D^\tau_\Lambda=\Ret^\tau_\Lambda+\Ctr^\tau_\Lambda .
\end{equation}
The first term is retained and the second is subtracted from the raw mixed
block.  The resolution is dyadically admissible if, for each label with
\(\Ret^\tau_\Lambda\ne0\), there exists \(\delta_\tau>0\) such that
\begin{equation}
        \|\Ret^\tau_{\Lambda,N,Q}P_Qw\|_{C_TL^2}
        \le C_{\mathfrak P}N^{-\delta_\tau}
        \bigl(\|P_Qw\|_{L_T^\infty L^2}
        +\|P_Q\partial_tw\|_{L_T^\infty L^2}\bigr)
\end{equation}
for \(0<T\le T_0\) and \(Q\le c_{\rm ap}N\), uniformly in \(\Lambda\).
For every fixed \((N,Q)\), the corresponding two-time scalar kernels are
also required to converge in
\(C_{t,s}\cL(\ell_q^2,\ell_q^2)\).

The retained term may be any prescribed finite linear combination of scalar
diagonal branches, provided the combined kernel satisfies
\eqref{eq:retained-block-bound} and fixed-block convergence.  The raw
resolution is \(\Ret^\tau_\Lambda=D^\tau_\Lambda\), while the fully
Wick-subtracted resolution is \(\Ret^\tau_\Lambda=0\).
title: Admissible deterministic diagonal resolution

with continuous embeddings and a measure $\mu_{\operatorname{YM}}$ of total mass $Z_{\operatorname{YM}}$ on $\mathcal{H}$ endowed with the Borel $\sigma$-algebra such that the following holds
\begin{enumerate}

 \mu_{\operatorname{YM}}\left(\left\{(\langle A,\psi_1\rangle,\ldots,\langle A,\psi_p\rangle)\in B\right\}\right)=\mathbb{M}_{\operatorname{YM}}\left(\left\{(\langle A(\xi,\mathrm{b}),\psi_1\rangle,\ldots,\langle A(\xi,\mathrm{b}),\psi_p\rangle)\in B\right\}\right);
 $$
 \item for every $\kappa>0$ and for $\mu_{\operatorname{YM}}$ almost every $A$, $A\in H_{\operatorname{loc}}^{-1-\kappa}\left(\Sigma\setminus\{a_{2g+2}\},T^*\Sigma\otimes\mathfrak{g}\right).$

body:
Let S={4^k:k>=1}, sigma_n=min(sqrt(n)/4,1+dist(n,S)/4) for n>=0, and let epsilon be one fair random sign. On the ray with edges j-1 to j assign tau_j=1+(sigma_j-sigma_(j-1)) epsilon. These weights lie in [3/4,5/4], and their unique minimizing path to n has T_n=n+sigma_n epsilon. Its mean is n, variance is sigma_n^2, and E exp(alpha |T_n-E T_n|/sqrt(Var T_n))=exp(alpha) for every alpha>0. Define a as the upper uniform concentration threshold: inf q for which some alpha>0 makes sup_(n>=1) E exp(alpha |T_n-E T_n|/n^q) finite. Define b as the lower uniform variance threshold: sup q for which some N has inf_(n>N) Var T_n/n^(2q)>0. Then a=1/2 and b=0. The weights share epsilon and are nonstationary; this is not an iid undirected Z^2 law.
A ray graph
Dependent nonstationary edge weights driven by a common fair sign

[Lemma l:localized_energy_inequality of arXiv:2607.15140, 'On the absence of blow-up in the 3D Navier-Stokes equations with transport noise'] In the setting of Proposition (prop:local_energy of the paper), for all $\phi\in C^{\infty}_{{\rm c}}(B)$ with $\int_B \phi^2=1$ and $\psi\in C^{\infty}_{{\rm c}}((t_0-\varrho^2,t_0])$, it holds that
\begin{align}
\nonumber
\psi^2(t)\int_{B}  \phi^2 |\widetilde{v}_\phi(t)|^2 
&\leq
  \int_{t_0-\varrho^2}^t\partial_t (\psi^2)\int_{B} \phi^2 |\widetilde{v}_\phi|^2 \\
  \nonumber
&+ 2\int_{t_0-\varrho^2}^t \psi^2\int_B \pi \nabla\cdot (\phi^2 \widetilde{v}_\phi)-\nu \nabla \widetilde{v}_\phi : \nabla (\phi^2  \widetilde{v}_\phi) - F: \nabla (\phi^2 \widetilde{v}_\phi)\\
\nonumber
& + \sum_{n}\int_{t_0-\varrho^2}^t\psi^2\int_B\nabla \widetilde{\pi}_n \cdot (\zeta_n\cdot \nabla) (\phi^2 \widetilde{v}_\phi)\\ 
\nonumber
&+\sum_{n}\int_{t_0-\varrho^2}^t\psi^2 \int_B\phi^2 |-\nabla \widetilde{\pi}_n + (\zeta_n\cdot \nabla) \widetilde{v}_\phi + G_n|^2\\
&+2 \sum_n \int_{t_0-\varrho^2}^t\psi^2 \Big(\int_B [-\nabla\widetilde{\pi}_n + (\zeta_n \cdot \nabla) \widetilde{v}_\phi+G_n ]\cdot( \phi^2 \widetilde{v}_\phi)\Big)\,\mathrm{d} W^n,

\end{align} 
 a.s.\ for all $t\in I=(t_0-\varrho^2,t_0)$.

[Lemma lem:measurable-operator-field-calculus of arXiv:2608.02459, 'Response Calculus for Spectral Simplicity\\ and Joint Eigenvalue Densities'] From the preceding definitions we obtain the following three properties.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textnormal{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.1em,itemsep=2pt,topsep=3pt]
 \item If $S$ and $T$ are measurable, then
 \[
  S^*,\ ST\quad\text{are measurable operator fields}.
 \]
 Consequently, measurable bounded operator fields are closed under adjoints,
 products, and polynomials.

 \item Let $(T^{(\ell)})_{\ell\ge1}$ be measurable bounded operator fields.  If
 \begin{equation*}
  T_\mu^{(\ell)}\xrightarrow[\ell\to\infty]{\rm s}T_\mu
  \qquad\text{for every }\mu,
 \end{equation*}
 then $T=(T_\mu)_\mu$ is measurable.

 \item Suppose $T$ is measurable and every $T_\mu$ is positive,
 self-adjoint, and compact.  Then, for every $F\in C_b([0,\infty))$, every
 open interval $I\subset(0,\infty)$, and every $n\ge1$,
 \begin{equation}
  \begin{gathered}
   F(T),\ \mathbf 1_I(T)\quad\text{are measurable operator fields},\\
   \mu\longmapsto\lambda_n(T_\mu)
   \quad\text{is measurable}.
  \end{gathered}
 \end{equation}
\end{enumerate}

[Theorem thm:terminal-lift of arXiv:2608.16119, 'Fully nonlinear parabolic equations under a fixed reference diffusion: weighted \texorpdfs'] Assume Assumptions~(ass:reference-diffusion of the paper) and
(ass:drift-multiplier of the paper).  For every
regular weight $w$, every interval $I=(r_0,r_1)$, and
$
 F\in H_{x,w}^1(I),\, \eta\in H^1(\mu_{r_1}),
$
one has
\begin{equation}
 D_x\mathcal U_I(F,\eta)
 =\mathcal P_{1,I}^{-1}(D_xF,D_x\eta)
 \in H_{x,w}^1(I;\mathbb R^d).
 
\end{equation}
In particular, for $\psi\in H^1(\mu_T)$, recall
$v^\psi=\mathcal U(0,\psi)$ and set
\begin{equation*}
p^\psi:=\mathcal P_1^{-1}(0,D_x\psi).
\end{equation*}
The terminal identities are
\begin{equation}
 p^\psi=D_xv^\psi,\qquad D_xp^\psi=D_x^2v^\psi,\qquad
 \operatorname{Tr}_T^Xp^\psi=D_x\psi(X_T).
 
\end{equation}
Consequently, for every $\alpha\geq0$, $v^\psi$ is the unique
order-$\alpha$ occupation Sobolev solution with data $(0,\psi)$, and
there exists a constant $C=C(T,\lambda,\Lambda,M_1(a),\Lambda_b)>0$ such that
\begin{equation}
 \left\lVert v^\psi\right\rVert_0^2+\left\lVert D_xv^\psi\right\rVert_0^2
 +\left\lVert D_x^2v^\psi\right\rVert_0^2
 \leq C\norm\psi_{H^1(\mu_T)}^2.
 
\end{equation}

Let \(u=u_n\in\bR\) satisfy \(\dist(u,\supp\mu)\geq\varepsilon\), and assume
\begin{equation}
\sup_{z\in B(u+\ri\eta,\eta/2)}
\bigl|m_{Y_n}(z)-m_{\mu}(z)\bigr|
\leq \frac{\delta_n}{n\eta}.
\end{equation}
Then, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
\lambda_i^{(n)}\notin[u-\eta,u+\eta],
\qquad 1\leq i\leq n.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Lem 191 (annealed first moment bounds for 
$E^{\sigma,\tau}$ and $E^{\frozen,\sigma,\tau}$
with $\sigma,\tau\in\{\RomII,\RomIII,\Ising\}$) of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Let
$Q^{\sigma,\tau}=E^{\sigma,\tau}+\tilde{Q}^{\sigma,\tau}$ as in Definitions~\ref{d:Q} and \ref{d:tQ}. Then, for $N$ large enough, we have
	\[\bbE
	\Big|\Delta E^{\sigma,\tau}(q_d)\Big| 
	\le L^{O(1)}\bigg\{\eta\delta^{1/2} + \frac{\BUCKETS\delta}{N}
	\bigg\}
	\]
for all $\sigma,\tau\in\{\RomII,\RomIII,\Ising\}$. The same bound holds with $E^\frozen$ in place of $E$.
\begin{proof}
This is similar
to the proof of Corollary~\ref{c:Q.first.quenched}. Recall 
that Lemma~\ref{l:qv.simplification} implies
	\[
	\Big|\Delta E^{\sigma,\tau}(q_d)\Big| 
	\le O\bigg(
	\eta^2
	+\sum_{\rho\in\{\sigma,\tau\}}\bigg[
	\eta\Big(\Delta\tilde{Q}^\rho(q_d)\Big)^{1/2}
	+\Big( \Delta \bar{D}^\rho(q_d)\Big)^2
	\bigg]\bigg)\,.
	\]
By Lemmas~\ref{l:barD.II.second}--\ref{l:barD.Ising.second}, for all $\sigma\in\{\RomII,\RomIII,\Ising\}$ we have
	\[\E\Big[\Delta\bar{D}^\sigma(q_d)^2\Big]
	\le\frac{ L^{O(1)}\BUCKETS\delta}{N}
	\,.\]
By Lemma~\ref{l:tQ.first.quenched} and the bound $\E[(\MAX_N)^2]\le L^{O(1)}$ from Proposition~\ref{p:Y.kolmogorov}, for all $\sigma\in\{\RomII,\RomIII,\Ising\}$ we have
	\[
	\E\bigg[\Big(\Delta\tilde{Q}^\sigma(q_d)\Big)^{1/2}\bigg]
	\le L^{O(1)} \delta^{1/2}\,.
	\]
Combining the bounds gives the claim, recalling that $\eta\ll\delta$ from Assumption~\ref{a:params}.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

\item Suppose $z=0$ and $\widehat{\delta}>0$. For any $r> 0$, $\frac{V(-r)+r}{r}$ has distribution $\mathcal{B}(\frac{\widehat{\delta}}{2},\frac{\delta}{2})$.
\item The family $(P^z_*,z\ge 0)$ defines a time-homogeneous Feller process. For any $z\ge 0$, the process  $\left(V(-r)+r,\, r\ge 0\right)$ is a homogeneous $(\mathscr{W}^*_r)_{r\ge 0}$-adapted Feller process starting from $z$. 
\item Suppose $z>0$ and write $\mathrm{x}:=\inf\{r\ge 0\,:\, V(-r)<z\}$.  We have $\frac{z}{\mathrm{x}+z}\sim\mathcal{B}(\frac{\delta}{2},1)$ and conditionally on  $\{{\rm{x}}= x \}$, $\frac{ V(-x)+x}{x+z}\sim \mathcal{B}(\frac{\delta+\widehat{\delta}}{2},1)$.
\end{enumerate}

body:
Measured 2026-09-05 on the EMIT and OCO-2 stacking pools (70 cells, the pool protocol, full calibration, paired). Given that the long-only gain is the estimation variance the constraint removes at the rows the stack is scored on, the amount of constraint was chosen with the evaluation inputs: a blend w(t) between the simplex and least-squares stacks with t minimising the cross-validated calibration error plus the excess bootstrap variance of the blend at the evaluation rows over the calibration rows, and a per-row version t_i = 1/(1 + kappa v_i/median v) that leans to the simplex where least squares is uncertain. P24 (a) HELD: on EMIT the per-cell blend reads +0.08 vs the simplex and beats least squares on 39 of 40 cells; (b) HELD: on OCO-2 t* is at or above 0.5 on 30 of 30 cells and the blend reads +0.66 vs least squares; (c) REFUTED: the per-row blend vs the per-cell blend is +0.70 on Y2 and -0.14 on EMIT overall; falsifier (blend worse than the simplex by more than 1 on EMIT, or than least squares by more than 0.3 on OCO-2) not triggered. Fresh-split replication (P25, split C, SPLIT_SEED 11, the criterion uses no evaluation targets): P25 (a) HELD: on split C the EMIT blend reads +0.63 vs the simplex and beats least squares on 35 of 40 cells; (b) HELD: on OCO-2 the blend reads +0.84 vs the simplex (wins 30 of 30) and +0.65 vs least squares; (c) HELD: t* averages 0.34 on EMIT and 0.67 on OCO-2; falsifier (blend worse than the simplex by more than 1 on EMIT, or than least squares by more than 0.3 on OCO-2) not triggered. Bootstrap-size stability (P28, B = 16 against B = 8 on split B): P28 (a) HELD: t*(16) equals t*(8) on 86 pct of the 70 cells and is within 0.2 on 100 pct; (b) HELD: the blend's mean gain against the simplex moves from +0.08 to +0.06 on EMIT and from +0.83 to +0.83 on OCO-2, and the both-endpoints win count on OCO-2 is 30 of 30 at B = 16; falsifier (agreement below 50 pct or a gain moving by more than 0.5) not triggered. Break test: a fixed midpoint t = 0.5 matches the criterion on OCO-2 (+0.96 / +1.01 against +0.83 / +0.84 on the two splits) but loses 1.6 and 4.4 pct on EMIT where the criterion stays at +0.08 and +0.63 - the criterion's value is knowing, without labels, when not to leave the simplex; the EMIT shortfall against the hindsight-best t is the bias-shift term of the risk identity. Scarce calibration (P30, 240 of the calibration rows per cell, split B): P30 (a) HELD: at n = 240 the simplex beats least squares by +14.10 on EMIT (full calibration +8.83); (b) REFUTED: t* averages 0.22 on EMIT and the blend reads -2.61 vs the simplex; (c) HELD: on OCO-2 the blend beats both endpoints on 30 of 30 cells and the simplex reads +2.27 vs least squares (full calibration -0.18); falsifier (blend worse than the simplex by more than 1 on EMIT) TRIGGERED. The observable part of the bias shift (P31): adding t^2 (D_ev - D_cal), the shift in the two bases' mean squared disagreement between the evaluation and calibration rows, to the criterion - P31 (a) REFUTED: the R'-blend reads -0.71 vs the simplex on EMIT split B (R-blend +0.08) and +0.71 on split C (R-blend +0.63); (b) HELD: on OCO-2 the R'-blend is -0.11 vs the R-blend on split B and -0.12 on split C; (c) REFUTED: mean t** 0.39 against t* 0.33 on EMIT, share of the hindsight optimum 0.07 -> -0.62; falsifier (R'-blend worse than the R-blend by more than 0.3 on any corpus or split) TRIGGERED. Per-output mixing weights (P34, the criterion decoupled across outputs): P34 (a) REFUTED: the per-output blend reads -0.41 vs the per-cell blend on EMIT split B and -0.53 on split C; (b) HELD: on OCO-2 -0.02 and -0.08 on split C; (c) REFUTED: on Y2 the share of outputs at t_d = 0 is 0.20 and at t_d >= 0.5 is 0.34; falsifier (per-output worse than per-cell by more than 0.3 anywhere) TRIGGERED. A nearest-neighbour proxy for the bias shift (P35, the simplex's out-of-fold residuals at the nearest calibration rows standing in for its bias at the scored rows): P35 (a) REFUTED: the full-shift blend reads -0.69 vs the R-blend on EMIT split B and -0.12 on split C; (b) HELD: on OCO-2 -0.08 and -0.14 on split C; (c) REFUTED: cross-only vs full on EMIT -0.05 vs -0.62 (split B); falsifier (either variant worse than the R-blend by more than 0.3 anywhere) TRIGGERED. Scarce calibration, the ratio-metric criterion (P41, 240 calibration rows, split B, three-vertex form, registered and R_1 choices side by side): P41 (a) HELD: at n_cal = 240 the R_1 blend reads +1.17 vs the simplex on EMIT (within 1.0; the registered three-vertex blend reads -1.83); (b) HELD: on OCO-2 the R_1 blend beats both endpoints on 30 of 30 cells (at least 25); (c) HELD: R_1 vs the registered blend on EMIT +1.38 (at least +1.0); falsifier (R_1 worse than the simplex by more than 2.0 on EMIT) not triggered. So the P30 caveat is confined to the squared-loss criterion; the criterion in the score's own metric keeps the simplex where it should at scarce calibration. P44: the shipped tool against the driver (P44): P44 (a) REFUTED: the tool's mixing weight is within 0.2 of the driver's on 14 (squared) and 11 (ratio) of 14 cells; (b) HELD: the tool's blend scores within 1 pct of the driver's on 12 / 12 of 14; (c) HELD by the clause's wording (worse than both endpoints by more than 1 pct while the driver beats one: none); under the stricter test the analyzer was first written with (worse than the better endpoint by more than 1 pct): one cell, emit s102 Y3 (ratio); falsifier not triggered by the clause's wording, TRIGGERED under the stricter test. P55: the seed-102 diagnostic (P55): P55 (a) REFUTED: with the target norms at the scored rows the tool's ratio choice is within 0.2 of the driver's on 0 of 3 cells; (b) REFUTED: with the shipped convention at B = 32 on 2 of 3 (at most one); (c) REFUTED: on Y3 arm A stays at the least-squares endpoint; falsifier TRIGGERED (the draw decides - raise B before the ratio metric is the default).
the members' predictions on the rows to be scored are available (transductive setting); their targets are not
the blend w(t) = (1 - t) w_simplex + t w_leastsquares is linear in t, so the cross-validated and bootstrap predictions of every t come from the two base estimators' predictions; the criterion is the 5-fold cross-validated squared relative error on the calibration rows plus the excess pairs-bootstrap variance (B = 8) of the blend at the evaluation rows over the calibration rows
