[Definition def: plus minus interface of arXiv:2606.13147, 'Scaling limits of the single-curve interface and outermost loops in the planar random fiel'] Let $$\mathtt{Dob}^+:=\partial\Lambda_N\cap \{z=(z^{(1)},z^{(2)})\in\mathbb Z^d, z^{(2)}\geq 0\},\quad \mathtt{Dob}^-:=\partial\Lambda_N\cap \{z=(z^{(1)},z^{(2)})\in\mathbb Z^d, z^{(2)}<0\}$$
    denote the upper and bottom half parts of the boundary of the box $\Lambda_N.$ Then the Dobrushin boundary condition (denoted $\pm$) is the boundary condition that being plus on $\mathtt{Dob}^+$ and minus on $\mathtt{Dob}^-.$ Now given any configuration $\sigma\in\{-1,1\}^{\Lambda_N}$ satisfying Dobrushin boundary condition, we define the upmost plus--minus boundary interface $\gamma=\gamma(\sigma)$ as follows.

Let
$
\mathtt{Plus}(\sigma)=\{z\in\Lambda_N:\sigma_z=1\}
$
denote the set of plus spins. By definition, we have
$
\mathtt{Dob}^+\subset \mathtt{Plus}(\sigma).
$
Since $\mathtt{Dob}^+$ is connected in $\mathbb Z^2$, there exists a unique connected component of $\mathtt{Plus}(\sigma)$ containing $\mathtt{Dob}^+$, which we denote by $\mathtt{ConPlus}(\sigma)$.

Define
\[
\Lambda^+(\sigma)
=
\big\{
z\in\Lambda_N:
\text{every path from }z
\text{ to }\partial\Lambda_{N+1}
\text{ intersects }
\mathtt{ConPlus}(\sigma)
\big\},
\]
and let
$
\Lambda^-(\sigma)=\Lambda_N\setminus\Lambda^+(\sigma).
$
Intuitively, $\Lambda^+(\sigma)$ is obtained by filling in all holes of $\mathtt{ConPlus}(\sigma)$.

We then define
\[
\gamma^+(\sigma)
=
\{x\in\Lambda^+(\sigma):
\exists y\in\Lambda^-(\sigma)
\text{ with }
x\sim_* y
\}
\setminus \mathtt{Dob}^+,
\]
and
$\gamma^-(\sigma)=\partial_{\mathrm{ext}}\Lambda^+(\sigma)\setminus \mathtt{Dob}^-.$
Here $x\sim_* y$ means that $x$ and $y$ are $*$-neighbors. By planar duality, $\gamma^+$ forms a connected set of plus spins, while $\gamma^-$ forms a $*$-connected set of minus spins. Hence
$
\gamma=(\gamma^+,\gamma^-)
$
defines a plus--minus interface. Moreover, $\gamma$ is the upmost interface, since every $*$-connected minus path from $\mathtt{Dob}^-$ to $\mathtt{Dob}^-$ must intersect $\gamma^+$.

Finally, let $\Sigma_\gamma$ denote the collection of configurations satisfying $\gamma(\sigma)=\gamma$.
It is easy to see that 
$\Sigma_\gamma=\{\sigma\in\{-1,1\}^{\Lambda_N}: \sigma_{\mid \mathtt{Dob}^+\cup\gamma^+}=1, \sigma_{\mid \mathtt{Dob}^-\cup\gamma^-}=-1\}.$
For convenience, write
$
\mu^\pm_{\Lambda_N,\epsilon h}(\gamma)
=
\mu^\pm_{\Lambda_N,\epsilon h}(\Sigma_\gamma),
$
and similarly
$
\mu^\pm_{\Lambda_N,0}(\gamma)
=
\mu^\pm_{\Lambda_N,0}(\Sigma_\gamma),
$
where the superscript $\pm$ indicates Dobrushin boundary conditions.
title: Definition def: plus minus interface of arXiv:2606.13147

Then \(u(x,y)\) is the solution to the Poisson equation \eqref{Poisson_eq}.
Moreover, \(u(x,y)\in C^2\). For all \((x,y)\in \mathbb{R}^n\times \mathbb{R}^m\), \(D_xu(x,y)\) and \(D^2_{xx}u(x,y)\) is linear growth, that is for all \((x,y)\in\mathbb{R}^m\times \mathbb{R}^n\), there exists a constant $L_u>0$ such that 
$$|D_xu(x,y)|\vee|D^2_{xx}u(x,y)|\le L_u(1+|x|+|y|).$$
And \(D_yu(x,y), D^2_{xy}u(x,y), D^2_{yy}u(x,y)\) is globally bounded, that is there exists a constant $L_u>0$ such that 
$$|D_yu(x,y)|\vee|D^2_{xy}u(x,y)|\vee|D^2_{yy}u(x,y)|\le L_u.$$
Moreover, when \(Y\) is independent of \(x\), \(\sup_{x\in \mathbb{R}^m}|u(x,y)|\le C(1+|y|)\). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Theorem thm:optimal-four-mark of arXiv:2609.01690, 'Iterated-sumset spectra: The complete exponent law and its rank geometry'] For every $h\geq2$, put
\[
 D_h^{\max}=\binom{h+2}{2}+\mathbf 1_{\{2\nmid h\}}.
\]
Then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{\qquad \eta_0(h)=D_h^{\max}.\qquad}
\end{equation}
Writing
\[
 Q_h=1+\binom{h+1}{2},
\]
the minimum is attained by
\begin{equation}
 A_h^\star=\{0,1,Q_h,D_h^{\max}\}.
\end{equation}
Equivalently,
\[
 R_h^{-1}(4)=\binom{h+2}{2}+1+\mathbf 1_{\{2\nmid h\}}
\]
in the positive-label interval convention.

[Definition {\cite[Definition 4.10 of arXiv:2608.30973, 'Pseudo-Anosov flow and dynamics on guts'] {Gabai1983_FoliationsAndTheTopologyOf3Manifolds_PUB},[AgolZhang2022_GutsInSuturedDecompositionsAndTheThurstonNorm_ARXv1]}]
Let \((N,\gamma)\) be a taut sutured manifold and let \(S\) be the maximal set of pairwise disjoint non-parallel product annuli and product disks in \(N\).
We define the \emph{sutured guts} \(\mathrm{Guts}(N)\) of \((N,\gamma)\) as the sutured manifold obtained from \((N,\gamma)\) by decomposing along \(S\) and discarding \emph{windows}, namely, product sutured manifold components.

The sutured guts is well-defined up to isotopy class of inclusion map by classical JSJ decomposition theory \autocite{Johannson1979_HomotopyEquivalencesOf3ManifoldsWithBoundaries_PUB} \autocite{JacoShalen1979_SeifertFiberedSpacesIn3Manifolds}.

[Theorem 1 of arXiv:2505.20799, 'A note on the improved sparse Hanson-Wright inequalities'] Assume that $\{\delta_{i}, 1\le i\le n \}$ and $\{\zeta_{i}, 1\le i\le n \}$ are two independent sequences of random variables, where $\delta_{i}\sim\textnormal{Bernoulli}(p_{i})$ are independent and $\zeta_{i}$ are independent centered $\alpha$-sub-exponential random variables.
	Consider a random vector $\xi=(\xi_{1}, \cdots, \xi_{n})$  with $\xi_{i}=\delta_{i}\cdot\zeta_{i}$. Let $A=(a_{ij})_{n\times n}$ be a symmetric fixed matrix. Then for $0<\alpha\le 2$ and $t\ge 0$
	\begin{align}
		&\mathbb{P}\{\vert \xi^\top A\xi-\mathbb{E}\xi^\top A\xi\vert\ge L(\alpha)^{2}t  \}\nonumber\\
		\le& 2\exp\left(-c(\alpha)\min\left\{ \frac{t^{2}}{\sum_{k}a_{kk}^{2}p_{k}+\sum_{i\neq j}a_{ij}^{2}p_{i}p_{j}}, \left(\frac{t}{\Vert A\Vert_{l_{2}\to l_{2}}}\right)^{\alpha/2}  \right\}      \right),\nonumber
	\end{align}
where $L(\alpha)=\max_{i}\Vert \zeta_{i}\Vert_{\Psi_{\alpha}}$ and $c(\alpha)$ is a positive constant depending only on $\alpha$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Let (x_s,y_s), 1<=s<=m, be a binary-labelled dataset with m>=1, y_s in {-1,1}, and empirical label mean b=(1/m) sum_s y_s satisfying |b|<1. For a prediction g(x), the mixed-input curriculum paper uses L_cov(g,y,x)=max{0,1-y*b-g(x)*(y-b)}. Definition2 states this for a binary-valued estimator; Theorem3 applies the same formula to a real neural-network score. Since y^2=1, L_cov=(1-y*b) max{0,1-y*g(x)}. Thus b=0 recovers the hinge loss, and the under-represented label class receives the larger multiplicative weight.
Binary labels; finite nonempty dataset; empirical label mean strictly between -1 and1.
The algebraic weighted-hinge identity holds for every real score.

Suppose that, for every \(x\in J\), the relevant side branches of \(y\mapsto\Phi(x,y)\) in the fixed-\(x\) construction are strictly monotone: the right branch, containing \(b(x)\), is strictly increasing, and, whenever \(a(x)>-x\), the left branch, containing \(a(x)\), is strictly increasing. 
    
    Then the boundary functions are continuous on \(J\). More explicitly, if \(a(x)>-x\) on \(J\), then both \(a(\cdot)\) and \(b(\cdot)\) are continuous on \(J\). If \(a(x)=-x\) on \(J\), then \(b(\cdot)\) is continuous on \(J\), while \(a(x)=-x\) is continuous automatically.

[Prop propconvquad of arXiv:2608.25865, 'Instability of Böhm's Einstein metrics'] Let $(\gamma_i)$ be a sequence of smooth functions such that, for all $i\in \mathbb{N}$, $\operatorname{supp}(\gamma_i)\subset (0,\mathfrak{T}_i)$ and $\gamma_i \in \ker (J_i)$. Let $Q_i=\langle \Delta_L^i\cdot ,\cdot \rangle_i$, where $\langle \cdot ,\cdot \rangle_i$ denotes the $L^2$ scalar product for the metric $g_i$. We assume that for all $p\in \mathbb{N}$, $\gamma_i^{(p)}$ converges uniformly to some $\gamma_\infty^{(p)}\in C^\infty([0,\pi],\mathbb{R})$ such that $\operatorname{supp}(\gamma_\infty)\subset (0,\pi)$. We also assume that there exists a closed interval $K\subset (0,\pi)$ such that $$\bigcup_{i\in \mathbb{N}\cup \{\infty\}}\operatorname{supp}(\gamma_i)\subset K.$$
Then $$Q_i(T_i(\gamma_i))\underset{i\to +\infty}{\longrightarrow} Q_c(T(\gamma_\infty)).$$
title: Prop propconvquad of arXiv:2608.25865

[Theorem 10 (I-MMSE formula, Guo, Shamai and Verdú\cite{GuoShamaiVerdu2005}) of arXiv:2607.21392, 'Gaussian Convexity Principles for Sharp Moderate Deviations of Gaussian Maxima and Critica'] Let $U$ be an $m$-dimensional random vector with $\E\|U\|^2<\infty$, let $G\sim \cN(0,I_m)$ be independent of $U$, and for $\gamma\ge 0$ set
\[
Y^{\gamma}=\sqrt\gamma\,U+G.
\]
Then the mutual information (measured in nats) satisfies
\[
\frac{d}{d\gamma} I(U;Y^{\gamma})=\frac12\,\E\bigl[\|U-\E[U\mid Y^{\gamma}]\|^2\bigr].
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: I-MMSE formula, Guo, Shamai and Verdú\cite{GuoShamaiVerdu2005}

[Lemma lem: another bound on the difference of times of arXiv:2601.05361, 'Noise sensitivity in last-passage percolation'] There exist constants $0<c, C<\infty$ such that the following holds. For every $n\ge1$, $v\in {\mathbb{Z}}^2_{\geq0}$ and $1\le s\le\frac{1}{18}|v|_1^{1/3}$ such that $|v|_1\le n$ and $|v_2-v_1|\le s|v|_1^{2/3}$, we have with $w=n\mathbf{e}_+-v$ and $k=\lfloor 2s|v|_1^{2/3}\rfloor+1$ that

$$
{\mathbb{P}}\Big(\hat{\omega}_{(j-1)\mathbf{e}_2+\mathbf{e}_1}^V(\hat{\lambda}^-)\leq \Delta'_j \leq \hat{\omega}_{(j-1)\mathbf{e}_2+\mathbf{e}_1}^V(\hat{\lambda}^+)\text{ for all }-k\le j\le k\Big)\ge1-C\exp(-cs^3).
$$
Moreover, the weights $(\omega^V_{j\mathbf{e}_2}(\lambda))_{j\in{\mathbb{Z}}}$ and $(\hat\omega^V_{\mathbf{e}_1+j\mathbf{e}_2}(\lambda'))_{j\in{\mathbb{Z}}}$ are independent for every choice of $\lambda$ and $\lambda'$.

body:
[Prop mr of arXiv:2411.06571, 'Moment-based approach for two erratic KPZ scaling limits'] Let $Z_{s,t}$ be a family of $\mathcal M(\Bbb R^2)$-valued random variables indexed by $-\infty <s\le t<\infty$ with $s,t\in\Bbb Q,$ all defined on some complete probability space $(\Omega,\mathcal F,\Bbb P)$. Suppose that the following are true: 
    \begin{enumerate}
    

    \item $Z_{s_j,t_j}$ are independent under $\Bbb P$ whenever $(s_j,t_j)$ are disjoint intervals.

        \item For all $f\in C_c^\infty(\Bbb R^2)$ and all $\psi\in C_c^\infty(\Bbb R)$ with $\int_\Bbb R\psi=1$, we have that $$\int_{\Bbb R^4 } \delta^{-1}\psi(\delta^{-1}(y-w))\cdot f(x,z) Z_{t,u}(dy,dz) Z_{s,t}(dx,dw)  \to \int_{\Bbb R^2} f(x,z) Z_{s,u}(dx,dz)$$ in probability as $\delta\to 0$, whenever $s<t<u$.

        \item For $n\in \Bbb N$ and $\phi,\psi\in C_c^\infty(\Bbb R)$ we have that \begin{align*}\Bbb E\bigg[ \bigg( \int_{\Bbb R^2}& \phi(x) \psi(y)Z_{s,t}(dx,dy) \bigg)^n \bigg] \\&= \int_{\Bbb R^{n}} \prod_{k=1}^n \phi(x_k) \mathbf E_{\mathrm{BM}^{\otimes n}}^{(x_1,...,x_n)} \bigg[\prod_{k=1}^n \psi(B^k_{t-s}) e^{\sum_{1\le i<j\le n} L_0^{B^i-B^j}(t-s)} \bigg] dx_1 \cdots dx_n.
        \end{align*}
        The expectation on the right side is with respect to a $n$-dimensional Brownian motion $(B^1,...,B^n)$ started from $(x_1,...,x_n)$, and $L_0^X$ denotes the local time at 0 of the semimartingale $X$.
    \end{enumerate}
    Then 
    there exists a $C(\Bbb R^4_\uparrow)$-valued random variable $\tilde Z$ defined on the same probability space, such that $(Z_{s,t},f) = \int_{\Bbb R^2} f(x,z) \tilde Z_{s,t}(x,z)dxdz$ almost surely, for all $(s,t)\in\Bbb Q^2$ (with $s<t$) and $f\in C_c^\infty(\Bbb R^2)$. 
    
    Furthermore, there exists a space-time white noise $\xi$ on $\Bbb R^2$, defined on the same probability space, with the property that $\tilde Z_{s,t}$ are the \textbf{propagators} of (equation she of the paper) driven by $\xi$: for all $s,x\in \Bbb R$ the function $(t,y)\mapsto \tilde Z_{s,t}(x,y)$ is a.s. the It\^o-Walsh solution of the equation (equation she of the paper) started from time $s$ with initial condition $\delta_x(y)$. In particular, the finite-dimensional marginal laws $(Z_{s_1,t_1},...,Z_{s_m,t_m})$ are $\mathrm{uniquely\; determined}$ by Conditions (1) - (3), for any finite collection of indices $s_j\le t_j$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: (1+1)-dimensional variant of Theorem 1.3 in \cite{Ts24}

body:
[Lemma 8 of arXiv:2607.19873, 'Local limit theorem for the operator norm of products of random matrices'] Let $M$ be a compact metrizable group acting freely on the compact space $\wt B$. 
Let $\rho: M \to {\rm GL}_d(\bb C)$ be a continuous linear representation for some integer $d \geq 1$. 
Then, for every $b \in B = \wt B / M$, there exists a unique complex vector space structure
on the fiber $\pi^{-1}(b)$ such that, for any $\wt b \in \wt B$ with $\wt b M = b$,
the map 
\begin{align*}
\psi_{\wt b}:  \bb C^d  &    \longrightarrow  \pi^{-1}(b)  \notag\\
v & \longmapsto  (\wt b, v) M
\end{align*}
is a linear isomorphism.

[Lemma 3 (Location of conformal factor extremum) of arXiv:2608.26619, 'Uniqueness of Positively Curved Ancient Ricci Flows on Surfaces with Boundary'] Let $g(\psi,\theta,t) = u(\psi,t)g_{0}$, $0\leq t< T$ be a radially symmetric {Ricci flow with boundary} (i.e. not dependent on $\theta$) with the initial data $u(\psi,0) = u_0(\psi)$ satisfying $\partial_\psi u_0 \geq 0$. Then for $0\leq t<T$ and all $\psi\in[0,\frac{\pi}{2}]$ we have
    $$\partial_\psi u(\psi,t)\geq0.$$
    Consequently, the conformal factor $u(\psi,t)$ always achieves its maximum value on the boundary $\{\psi = \pi/2\}$ and its minimum value at the pole $\{\psi=0\}$, whenever the initial data exhibits the same behavior. Furthermore, if the inequality is strict away from the pole, it remains so throughout the evolution.

Let a finite nonempty binary-labeled data set (x_i,y_i), y_i in {-1,+1}, and a real-valued predictor Phi(theta;x) with theta in R^d be given. For each fixed x, theta -> Phi(theta;x) is locally Lipschitz and admits the chain rule: for every locally absolutely continuous arc z, (Phi(z(t);x))'=<h,z'(t)> for every h in its Clarke subdifferential at z(t), for almost every t. Assume common positive homogeneity degree L>0: Phi(a theta;x)=a^L Phi(theta;x) for every a>0. Put q_i(theta)=y_i Phi(theta;x_i), q_min(theta)=min_i q_i(theta), and E(theta)=sum_i exp(-q_i(theta)), without averaging by sample size. Let theta:[0,infinity)->R^d be a locally absolutely continuous Clarke gradient-flow trajectory satisfying theta'(t) in -partial^C E(theta(t)) almost everywhere. Assume there is a finite t0 with E(theta(t0))<1. Every accumulation point u of theta(t)/||theta(t)||_2 as t->infinity has q_min(u)>0, and theta_star=u/q_min(u)^(1/L) satisfies the Clarke KKT conditions for minimizing (1/2)||theta||_2^2 subject to q_i(theta)>=1 for every i. Explicitly there are lambda_i>=0 and h_i in partial^C q_i(theta_star) with theta_star=sum_i lambda_i h_i and lambda_i(q_i(theta_star)-1)=0 for every i, in addition to feasibility. This gives stationarity of every limiting direction. It does not assert that the entire direction trajectory converges, nor that its KKT points are local or global margin optima. The exponential-loss gradient-flow part of Theorem 4.4 is stated here; the source's separate smooth gradient-descent learning-rate hypotheses are not being imported.

[Lemma 24 (Uniform curvature-response profiles) of arXiv:2608.30211, '2608.30211'] For every $\varrho\in[0,1]$, problem
\eqref{eq:intro-curvature-response} has a unique solution
$\chi_\varrho\in H^1(\R_+)$.  In addition,
\begin{equation}
 \chi_\varrho\leq0,\qquad
 [0,1]\ni\varrho\longmapsto\chi_\varrho
 \text{ is continuous into }H^1(\R_+)\cap C_b^1(\R_+),
\end{equation}
and there are constants $C,c>0$, independent of $\varrho$, such that
\begin{equation}
 |\phi_\varrho'(y)|+
 \sum_{j=0}^2|\chi_\varrho^{(j)}(y)|
 \leq Ce^{-cy}\qquad(y\geq0).
\end{equation}
At the Neumann endpoint this gives $\chi_1=0$.

Let T be a first-order theory in a language L, and let lambda = max(|L|, aleph_0). If T has an infinite model, then T has a model of every cardinality kappa >= lambda; moreover, every infinite L-structure M has, for each cardinal kappa with lambda <= kappa <= |M|, an elementary substructure of cardinality kappa, and elementary extensions of every cardinality >= max(|M|, lambda). In particular a first-order theory in a countable language with an infinite model has models of every infinite cardinality; first-order logic cannot pin down an infinite cardinality (Skolem's paradox: countable models of set theory exist if any do).

Let G_n=(V_n,E_n) be finite simple undirected graphs, with |V_n| even and tending to infinity, maximum degree at most a fixed integer Delta, and every connected component having at least three vertices. Let E_n' be a uniformly random perfect matching of V_n and let G_n^*=(V_n,E_n union E_n'), using the graph-union model of the source. The discrete-time simple random walk on G_n^* exhibits total-variation cutoff with probability tending to one. For each fixed epsilon in (0,1/2), there is C(Delta,epsilon)>0 such that, with probability tending to one, t_mix(epsilon)-t_mix(1-epsilon)<=C(Delta,epsilon) sqrt(log |V_n|). Its t_mix(1/4) is of order log |V_n| with probability tending to one. This does not identify the optimal deterministic matching, does not require connected base graphs, and does not cover unbounded base degree without further conditions.

\(\P(\xi_i=1)=p_i\). We denote
\[
W\coloneqq\sum_{i=1}^n\xi_i,
\qquad
\lambda\coloneqq\sum_{i=1}^np_i,
\]
and let \(P\sim\Pois(\lambda)\). Then
\begin{align}
\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}
\left|
\P(W=k)-e^{-\lambda}\frac{\lambda^k}{k!}
\right|
\le
2\sum_{i=1}^np_i^2.

\end{align}
Equivalently, under the previous total-variation convention, we have
\begin{align}
d_{\mathrm{TV}}\bigl(\mathcal L(W),\mathcal L(P)\bigr)
\le
\sum_{i=1}^np_i^2,

\end{align}
where \(\mathcal L(W)\) and \(\mathcal L(P)\) denote the laws of \(W\) and \(P\), respectively. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Thm 3 (Explicit Main Theorem for $n=2$ over Rational Numbers) of arXiv:2609.00974, 'On Algebraic Integrability\\ of Vector Fields \\ with Rational Function Coefficients\\ tha'] Let $f,g\in \mathbb{Q}(X)$ be nonzero rational functions.
    Let $D=f(x)\frac{\partial}{\partial x}+g(y)\frac{\partial}{\partial y}$ be a derivation on the field $\mathbb{Q}(x,y)$.

    Then the following are equivalent:
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item There exists a non-constant $F\in \mathbb{Q}(x,y)$ such that $D(F)=0$.
        \item One of the following is true:
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item All complex residues of $\frac{1}{f}$ and $\frac{1}{g}$ are zero.
        \item There exists irreducible polynomials $f_1,\ldots,f_n\in \mathbb{Q}[x],g_1,\ldots,g_m\in\mathbb{Q}[y]$ and rational numbers $c_1,\ldots,c_n, d_1,\ldots,d_m \in\mathbb{Q}$ such that
        \[

        \]
        \item There exists a quadratic extension $L/\mathbb{Q}$, irreducible polynomials $f_1,\ldots,f_n\in \mathbb{Q}[x]$, $g_1,\ldots,g_m\in\mathbb{Q}[y]$ that split over $L$ into conjugate factors $f_i=f_{i1}f_{i2}$ and $g_j=g_{j1}g_{j2}$, and $c_1,\ldots,c_n\in L\setminus \mathbb{Q}$, $d_1,\ldots,d_m\in L\setminus \mathbb{Q}$ satisfying $c_i+\overline{c_i}=0,d_j+\overline{d_j}=0$ such that

        \frac{1}{g}=\sum_{i=1}^m \frac{d_i (g_{i1}'g_{i2}-g_{i2}'g_{i1})}{g_i}.

body:
[Theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] Given a twice differentiable function $f:\mathbb R^N\to\mathbb R$, in order for $x\in\mathbb R^N$ to be a local extremum, we must have $f'(x)=0$, and:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f''(x)\geq0$ is needed for $x$ to be a local minimum.

\item $f''(x)>0$ guarantees that $x$ is a local minimum.

\item $f''(x)\leq0$ is needed for $x$ to be a local maximum.

\item $f''(x)<0$ guarantees that $x$ is a local maximum.
\end{enumerate}

 \longrightarrow
 e^{\phi(0)}\left\lVert D_y^2q\right\rVert_{L^2(s^\alpha\,\mathrm d s\,\mathrm d\gamma_s)}^2
 \qquad(r\downarrow0).
\end{align*}

body: [Proposition 3 of arXiv:2512.19517, 'Spiking and Resetting'] For any $\sigma\geq 0$, and $0<a<b\leq 1$, let us define the analytic function $\begin{split}Z(\cdot,\sigma:a,b):z\in D_{\sigma}(a,b)\mapsto Z(z,\sigma:a,b):=\frac{1}{\sigma+f(0)+(1-z)f(0)(1/a-1/b)}\in\mathbb{C}\end{split}$ on the open disc $D_{\sigma}(a,b)$ of radius $R_{\sigma}(a,b)$, where $\begin{split}R_{\sigma}(a,b)=1+\cfrac{\sigma+f(0)}{f(0)(1/a-1/b)}>1\.\end{split}$ Then for any $z\in D_{\sigma}(a,b)$ we have $\begin{split}\lim_{\varepsilon\to 0}Z^{\varepsilon}(z,\sigma:a,b)=Z(z,\sigma:a,b)\.\end{split}$

body:
[Proposition 7 of arXiv:2609.02850, 'Canonical-row Chern flow on Bott--Samelson towers:\\ realizable-volume models for Schubert'] For every field $\kk$, the class $\RV$ has the following properties.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item It is invariant under permutations of variables and nonnegative
rational linear substitutions, including coordinate restriction.
\item It is closed under products.
\item If $f\in\RV$, then every ordinary coordinate derivative
$\partial_x^\gamma f$ lies in $\RV$.
\item It is closed under coordinatewise lower and upper truncations in the
divided-power basis.
\item It is invariant under common divided-power translations:
\[
 \sum_\alpha c_\alpha x^{[\alpha]}\in\RV
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \sum_\alpha c_\alpha x^{[\alpha+\gamma]}\in\RV.
\]
\item If $f\in\RV$, then its factorial normalization $\Nrm(f)$ lies in
$\RV$.
\item If $F_1,F_2$ have realizable factorial normalizations, then
$\Nrm(F_1F_2)$ lies in $\RV$.
\item Full polarization preserves $\RV$.
\item Membership is invariant under arbitrary field extension; for
polynomials with rational coefficients, it depends only on
$\operatorname{char}(\kk)$.
\end{enumerate}

Let $D$ be an  open subset of $\sX$.
Then for each $z_0\in \partial D$ and $R\in (0, R_0/16),$    there exists $C=C(z_0, R)>1$   such that

\E_x\tau_{D\cap B(z_0, R)}\leq C \, \E_x\tau_{D\cap B(z_0, R/2)}, \quad x\in D\cap B(z_0, R/4).
\end{equation}
 If  assumptions (A2') and (A5) hold, then the multiplicative constant $C$ in \eqref{e:2.12} depends only on $R.$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

satisfies \Cref{Assum:MaillardDimension} for some $D>1$. Assume that the jumps in \(W_{n}'\) are i.i.d. copies of

 \frac{\max \lvert W_{n}' \rvert }{n^{\frac{1}{2D}+\varepsilon}} \xrightarrow[n \to +\infty]{(\P)} 0.

[Theorem thm:introduction-compact-open of arXiv:2607.25616, 'Stealthy point processes and lattice induction'] Let $G$ be a second-countable locally compact abelian group and let
$(X,\mu)$ be an essentially free probability-preserving Borel
$G$-space.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $G$ has a compact open subgroup, then $(X,\mu)$ admits a
stealthy cross-section.
\item If $G=\mathbb Q_p$, then $(X,\mu)$ admits a generating
stealthy cross-section.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Definition 17 (Fiber-equivalent torus fibrations) of arXiv:2608.30027, 'Under Ricci flow, a 3-torus goes flat'] Let
\[
        \pi_i:M\to S^1_i,\qquad i=0,1,
\]
be torus fibrations.  The target circles are not part of the fixed data and may
be different.  Choose a basepoint \(x\in M\) and, for each \(i=0,1\), an identification
\(\pi_1(S_i^1,\pi_i(x))\cong\ZZ\), and let
\[
        \alpha_{\pi_i,x}:\pi_1(M,x)\longrightarrow\ZZ,
\]
be the surjective homomorphism induced by \(\pi_i\).  Changing the
identification changes \(\alpha_{\pi_i,x}\) by a sign.  Equivalently, \(\pi_i\)
determines a cohomology class \([\pi_i]\in H^1(M;\ZZ)\), well-defined up to
sign.  We say that \(\pi_0\) and \(\pi_1\) are \emph{fiber-equivalent}
if
\[
        [\pi_0]=\pm[\pi_1]\in H^1(M;\ZZ).
\]
Equivalently, after choosing a common basepoint,
\[
        \ker\alpha_{\pi_0,x}=\ker\alpha_{\pi_1,x}\subset\pi_1(M,x).
\]
For a different basepoint, the two kernels are changed by the same conjugacy
convention.  Thus, in fiber-subgroup language, the definition says that the
images of the two fiber fundamental groups agree, up to this usual conjugacy
ambiguity.
title: Fiber-equivalent torus fibrations

[Definition def:allHspaces of arXiv:2609.03980, 'Decay Rates and Domain Dependence of a Coupled Wave-Heat System with Spatially Dependant H'] Let $\Gamma$ be a relatively open subset of the boundary $\partial \Omega$ of some bounded Lipschitz domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$. We define the following subspaces of $L^2(\Omega)$.
    \begin{align*}
    H^1_0(\Omega) & \coloneq  \{f\in H^1(\Omega)~|~ {\operatorname{tr}}(f) = 0\},\\
        H^1_\Gamma(\Omega) & \coloneq  \{f\in H^1(\Omega)~|~ {\operatorname{tr}}^{\Gamma}(f) = 0\},\\
        H^{\operatorname{div}}_0(\Omega)& \coloneq   \{f\in H^{\operatorname{div}}(\Omega)~|~ {\operatorname{tr}}_N(f) = 0\},\\
        H^{\operatorname{div}}_\Gamma(\Omega)& \coloneq   \{f\in H^{\operatorname{div}}(\Omega)~|~ {\operatorname{tr}}^{\Gamma}_N(f) = 0\},\\
        H^\Delta(\Omega)& \coloneq \{f\in H^1(\Omega)~|~ \nabla f \in H^{\operatorname{div}}(\Omega)\},\\
         H^\Delta_0(\Omega)& \coloneq \{f\in H^1_0(\Omega)~|~ \nabla f \in H^{\operatorname{div}}(\Omega)\},\\
          H^\Delta_\Gamma(\Omega)& \coloneq \{f\in H^1_\Gamma(\Omega)~|~ \nabla f \in H^{\operatorname{div}}(\Omega)\}.
    \end{align*}
    The first two spaces are equipped with the usual $H^1$-norm, the third and fourth with the usual $H^{\operatorname{div}}$-norm,
    and the latter three spaces with the norm $$
        \|f\|_{H^\Delta(\Omega)}^2  \coloneq  \|f\|^2_{H^1(\Omega)}+ \|\Delta f\|^2_{L^2(\Omega)}
    $$
title: Definition def:allHspaces of arXiv:2609.03980

body: Theorem (campaign status: proved): (S14 eq (4).) For every m >= 2, d_m <= C_int * (m - H(Q|W)) with C_int = 2/(3 - log_2 5) = 2.949539... . Proof: with beta = log_2(4/3), m=2 gives L_{Q|W} >= 2-log_2 3 = beta while d_m = 1; m=3 gives L_{Q|W} >= 3-log_2 5 with d_m = 2, which is EXACTLY the claimed inequality; for m >= 4, floor(m/2) disjoint private edges give L_{Q|W} >= beta*floor(m/2), and C_int*beta > 6/5 follows from (4/3)^5 > (8/5)^3 i.e. 128000 > 124416, so m = 4,5 are immediate and for m >= 6, C_int*beta*floor(m/2) > (6/5)(m-1)/2 = 3(m-1)/5 >= (m+3)/3 >= ceil((m+1)/3). Notes: m = 3 is the tight case (equality by construction), which is why C_int is what it is. The chain 3(m-1)/5 >= (m+3)/3 requires exactly m >= 6, and the integer certificate 128000 > 124416 is exact. All steps re-verified numerically here.

ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: A Feller topology for limits of reversible Markov chains structural attempt Result: The suggested unweighted heat-kernel metric can be infinite in a basic admissible example. For Brownian motion on the two-torus, the squared row-distance integrated against exp(-t)dt equals sum_(k in Z^2) |1-exp(2pi*i*k.h)|^2/[1+8pi^2*|k|^2]. At h=(1/2,0), every odd k1 has numerator4. Each dyadic annulus contains order N^2 such terms of order N^-2, so the series diverges. A repair is to use w(t)=exp(-t)/(1+G(2t)), where G is the integrated diagonal heat trace: Fubini gives finite weighted row norm for almost every state. Check: Parseval computes the row norm exactly; integrating the nonnegative Fourier series is justified by Tonelli. For the repaired weight, the average row squared norm is integral w(t)*G(2t)dt<=1. This produces an almost-everywhere finite Hilbert-space pseudometric after identifying indistinguishable rows. Obstruction: Brownian motion already has a good usual topology, so the divergence refutes only the illustrative formula, not the existence conjecture. Completing a heat-kernel embedding can add states; proving valid transition kernels and the Feller property on that completion is still missing.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-p0235-a-feller-topology-for-limits-of-reversible-markov-chains
No independent review
title: Attempt on A Feller topology for limits of reversible Markov chains

body: Let X_1, X_2, ... be independent random variables and fix a constant c > 0. For each i define the truncation Y_i = X_i 1(|X_i| <= c). Then the series sum_{i=1}^infinity X_i converges almost surely if and only if all three of the following series converge: sum_i P(|X_i| > c), sum_i E[Y_i], and sum_i Var(Y_i). If one of the three series diverges, the partial sums of sum X_i do not converge almost surely. [Durrett, Probability: Theory and Examples]
title: Kolmogorov's Three-Series Theorem

Let T be a measure-preserving transformation of a probability space (X, B, mu) and let P and Q be countable measurable partitions with H_mu(P) < infinity and H_mu(Q) < infinity. Write P_n for the join of T^{-i}P over 0 <= i <= n-1 and h_mu(T,P) = lim_n (1/n) H_mu(P_n) (the limit exists by subadditivity and equals the infimum over n). Then h_mu(T, Q) <= h_mu(T, P) + H_mu(Q | P). Two standard consequences: if P refines Q then H_mu(Q | P) = 0 and hence h_mu(T, Q) <= h_mu(T, P), so the partition entropy is monotone under refinement; and |h_mu(T,P) - h_mu(T,Q)| <= H_mu(P | Q) + H_mu(Q | P), i.e. the map P -> h_mu(T,P) is 1-Lipschitz for the Rokhlin metric. WHERE IT FAILS: finiteness of H_mu(P) and H_mu(Q) is used - with infinite-entropy partitions both sides can be infinite and the inequality carries no information. The inequality is one-sided: nothing bounds h_mu(T,P) from below in terms of h_mu(T,Q) unless the conditional entropy in the other direction is also controlled. It is an inequality between the entropies of PROCESSES, not of the partitions: H_mu(Q) <= H_mu(P) + H_mu(Q|P) is the (easier) static statement and must not be quoted in its place.
(X,B,mu) is a probability space and T preserves mu (invertibility is not needed)
P and Q are countable measurable partitions
H_mu(P) < infinity and H_mu(Q) < infinity
entropies are taken with a fixed logarithm base throughout

[Lemma lem:B-inverse of arXiv:2602.07920, 'On the position matrix of single-shelf shuffle and card guessing'] The matrix $B$ is invertible. Its inverse $B^{-1}$ is lower triangular with
\begin{equation*}
  (B^{-1})(k,\ell)
  =
  \begin{cases}
    \displaystyle
    (-1)^{\,k-\ell}\,\frac{1}{(k-1)!}\binom{k-1}{\ell-1},
      & 1\le \ell\le k\le n,\\[6pt]
    0,& \ell>k.
  \end{cases}
\end{equation*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma lem:B-inverse of arXiv:2602.07920

body:
[Lemma 12 of arXiv:2607.27082, '2607.27082'] Let \(X=(X_t)_{t\ge0}\) be either
\begin{itemize}
    \item a Brownian motion on \(\mathbb{R}\) with variance parameter \(\sigma^2>0\), or
    \item a symmetric strictly \(\alpha\)-stable Lévy process on \(\mathbb{R}\), with
    \(1<\alpha<2\), whose Lévy measure is given by \eqref{Levygene}.
\end{itemize}
Then there exist constants \(t_1\in(0,1)\) and \(C>0\) such that
\begin{equation}
  \PP(\tau_1^+(X)\le t)\le Ct
  \qquad\text{for all }t\in(0,t_1].
\end{equation}
Moreover, the distribution function
\[
  F(t):=\PP(\tau_1^+(X)\le t),\qquad t>0,
\]
is continuous on \((0,\infty)\).

There is a constant $C_n<\infty$ such that for every $f\in L^1(\mathbb R^n)\cap H^1(\mathbb R^n)$, $\|f\|_{L^2(\mathbb R^n)}^{1+\frac2n}\le C_n\,\|f\|_{L^1(\mathbb R^n)}^{\frac2n}\,\|\nabla f\|_{L^2(\mathbb R^n)}.$ Both hypotheses are needed: the inequality interpolates the $L^2$ norm between the $L^1$ mass and the Dirichlet energy. It is the standard route from the energy identity to on-diagonal heat kernel bounds: if $u$ solves $\partial_tu=\mathrm{div}(A\nabla u)$ with $A$ measurable and uniformly parabolic and $u(0)=g\in L^1\cap L^2$, then $\|u(t)\|_{L^\infty}\le C(n,\lambda)t^{-n/2}\|g\|_{L^1}$, i.e. the kernel obeys $\Gamma(x,t;y,s)\le C(t-s)^{-n/2}$.

[Lemma 9 of arXiv:2607.25645, 'Estimates of the total variation distance between laws of Sobolev mappings on Gaussian spa'] Let $p\ge 2k$, and let
\[
f=(f_1,\ldots,f_k)
\quad\text{and}\quad
g=(g_1,\ldots,g_k)
\]
be such that
$
f_j,g_j\in C_b^\infty(\mathbb R^n),
$
and
\[
\max_{1\le j\le k}\|\nabla f_j\|_{L^p(\gamma_n)}\le b
\quad\text{and}\quad
\max_{1\le j\le k}\|\nabla g_j\|_{L^p(\gamma_n)}\le b.
\]
Then
\[
\Delta_f\le \prod_{j=1}^k|\nabla f_j|^2,
\]
and
\[
\|\Delta_f-\Delta_g\|_{L^{\frac{p}{2k}}(\gamma_n)}
\le
4k\,b^{2k-1}
\max_{1\le j\le k}\|\nabla f_j-\nabla g_j\|_{L^p(\gamma_n)}.
\]

[Defn 1 of arXiv:2609.03512, ''] Let $G$ be a simple connected graph with vertex set $V(G)=\{v_1,\ldots,v_n\}$, and let $m=(m_1,\ldots,m_n)$ be a vector of positive integers. The \emph{blow-up} $G\bigodot m$ is obtained from $G$ by replacing each vertex $v_i$ with an independent set
\[
V_i = \{v_i^1,\ldots,v_i^{m_i}\}
\]
of $m_i$ vertices, and joining $v_i^s$ to $v_j^t$ if and only if $v_iv_j\in E(G)$. We call $V_i$ the \emph{part of $G\bigodot m$ corresponding to $v_i$}, and say that $G\bigodot m$ is obtained from $G$ by \emph{multiplication of vertices} (Golumbic \cite{Graph-multiplication-Golumbic}, p.~53).

If $m_j=1$ for all $j\ne i$, we say $G\bigodot m$ is obtained from $G$ by \emph{multiplying the single vertex $v_i$}; if moreover $m_i=2$, this is called \emph{duplicating} $v_i$ (Henning and Southey \cite{Henning-Michael}). If $G$ has a vertex of degree $2$, \emph{degree-$2$ vertex duplication} denotes the operation of duplicating any such vertex.

For graphs $G_1,\ldots,G_k$, we write $\mathcal{M}(G_1,\ldots,G_k)$ for the family of all graphs obtainable from some $G_\ell$ by multiplication of vertices. Since $G\bigodot(1,\ldots,1)=G$, each $G_\ell$ itself belongs to $\mathcal{M}(G_1,\ldots,G_k)$.

Assumptions: n>=1, 0<=c<=n, d>=1; G(n,c/n) with iid standard-Borel marks independent of edges; common measurable permutation-invariant local rule F_(t,degree)(own mark; own state and neighbor states), independent of graph size and remote structure; initial state depends only on own mark; all iterates on full graphs and induced subgraphs lie in the same fixed Borel K subset R^d of diameter D<infinity; maximum-input Lipschitz constant <=rho in (0,1), uniformly over degree, marks and layers; nu_L is the root-output law of a similarly iid-marked PGW(c) tree with the same update rules; depth can depend arbitrarily on n. Let mu_(n,L) be the empirical output measure and nu_L the PGW(c) root-output law for a local GNN with a bounded invariant state set K subset R^d of diameter D and degree-uniform maximum-input contraction rho in (0,1). For every depth L, radius r and fixed partition of K into M Borel cells of diameter at most epsilon, E W1(mu_(n,L),nu_L) <=2D rho^r+2epsilon+(3D/2)sqrt(M(1+c)^(2r+2)/n). One may take M<=(1+D sqrt(d)/epsilon)^d. With b=log(1/rho), C_d=2+(3/2)(1+sqrt(d))^(d/2) and kappa=b/[2log(1+c)+(d+2)b], sup_L E W1 <=D[2/rho+C_d(1+c)^(2/(d+2))] n^(-kappa). D=0 gives exact equality. The bound also controls expected bounded-Lipschitz distance. Independent review pending; no literature-priority claim.

body: [Lemma 28 of arXiv:2609.04139, 'The conformally invariant metric on CLE$_4$ II:\\ existence of geodesics'] Let $K \subset \overline\BD$ be a connected compact set. Let $x \in \BD_{\BQ}$. Let $\tau$ be the first time $t$ that $\SCB_t(\SCL(x); D^\BD_{\Gamma_\BD})$ intersects $K$. [Definition 30 (Decision tree, stopping time {\cite[Definition~2.4) of arXiv:2605.30030, 'Critical exponents for planar random-cluster model with cluster-weight~$q=4$'] {duminil2022planar}}]
    A \emph{decision tree} is a pair~$\mathbf{T} = (e_1, (\psi_t)_{2\leq t\leq n})$ where~$e_1\in E$ and for each~$2\leq t\leq n$, the input of~$\psi_t$ is~$(e_{[t-1]},U_{[t-1]})$ and it returns~$e_t\in E\setminus\{e_1,\dots,e_{t-1}\}$. A \emph{stopping time} for~$\mathbf{T}$ is a random variable~$\tau$ taking values in~$\{1,\dots,n,\infty\}$, for which each~$\{\tau\leq t\}$ is measurable in terms of~$(e_{[t]}, U_{[t]})$.

[Proposition of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] For a graph $X$, with adjacency matrix $d\in M_N(0,1)$, we have:
$$(d^k)_{ij}=\#\Big\{i=i_0-i_1-\ldots-i_{k-1}-i_k=j\Big\}$$
That is, the $k$-th power of $d$ describes the length $k$ paths on $X$.

Let $\mathbb{F} = (\mathcal{F}_t)_{t \geq 0}$, $\mathbb{G} = (\mathcal{G}_t)_{t \geq 0}$ and $(\mathbb{F}^i = (\mathcal{F}^i_t)_{t \geq 0})_{i \in I}$ be filtrations on the same space. We denote
	\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*), nosep]
		\item $\mathcal{F} \vee \mathcal{G} \coloneqq \sigma(\mathcal{F} \cup \mathcal{G})$ and $\bigvee_{i \in I} \mathcal{F}^i \coloneqq \sigma(\bigcup_{i \in I} \mathcal{F}^i)$,
		
		\item $\mathbb{F} \lor \mathbb{G} \coloneqq (\mathcal{F}_t \lor \mathcal{G}_t)_{t \geq 0}$ and $\bigvee_{i \in I} \mathbb{F}^i \coloneqq (\bigvee_{i \in I} \mathcal{F}^i_t)_{t \geq 0}$,
		
		\item $\mathbb{F} \vee \mathcal{G} \coloneqq (\mathcal{F}_t \lor \mathcal{G})_{t \geq 0}$. 
	\end{enumerate}

body: [Corollary 6 (Law of Robustness for Discontinuous Functions) of arXiv:2603.02806, 'The Price of Robustness: Stable Classifiers Need Overparame'] Let n iid observations come from a law on a bounded path-connected input space X in dimension d, with c-isoperimetric input marginal. Let F be a finite class of classifiers X -> {-1,1}, with every positive-class preimage closed, and log|F|>=n. For epsilon,delta in (0,1), let R_*=min_{f in F} R_0-1(f). There is a universal K>0 such that if R_*>=epsilon, K/sqrt(n)<epsilon/3, and sqrt(2log(2/delta)/n)<epsilon/2, then with probability at least 1-delta, simultaneously for every f in F, empirical R_0-1(f)<=R_*-epsilon implies S(f)<max{(3K/epsilon)sqrt(c log|F|/(nd)), sqrt((8c/d)log(6K/epsilon))}.

body:
[Defi 11 of arXiv:2609.02261, 'Quantization and process'] Set $\gamma < 0$. We denote by  
  ${\cal M} ( \gamma , \R^{2n} )$ the set of families ($\nu_h)$ of bounded   measures on   $\R^{2n}$ satisfying,
    
    \be
     \widehat  \nu_h (u) = e^{h\varphi (u)}, \ee  
     
where   $\varphi$  is a function on   $\R^{2n}$ 
    written as $\varphi = \varphi_1 + \varphi_2  $ such that,

   
   i) the function $\varphi_1 $ is the symbol of a bounded operator in  $L^{\infty } (\R^{2n} )$ which is commuting with  translations. 
   
   
   ii) the function $\varphi _2 \in C^{\infty } (\R^{2n} )$.  For every $\alpha\in \N^{2n}$, there is   $A_{\alpha }>0$ such that,  for any $u\in\R^{2n}$,
  
   \be | \partial ^{\alpha }\varphi_2 (u) |
    \leq A_{\alpha } (|u|^2 +1).
  \ee
For every $u$ large enough,
  
      \be  {\rm Re}\, \varphi_2(u) \leq  \gamma |u|^2. \ee
title: Definition 11 of arXiv:2609.02261

[Cor 50 of arXiv:2609.03836, 'Koszul Orlik--Solomon Algebras from Non-supersolvable Arrangements'] \label[Cor]{prop:gquadratic}
    Let $M = P_f(M', M'')$ be a parallel connection.
    If $M'$ and $M''$ have G-quadratic (reduced) 
    Orlik--Solomon algebras then so does $M$.
    In particular, if $M$ and $N$ are supersolvable matroids, then for any $f\in M$, $g\in N$, both $\rOS(P_{f,g}(M, N))$ and $\OS(P_{f,g}(M, N))$ are G-quadratic. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

$$
X=\{(\sft_{t},x_{t}) ,\cN_{t}, P_{t,x})

such that   for any $(t,x)\in\bR^{d+1}$

body:
[Thm FirstPresentation of arXiv:2609.01501, 'Singularities of star cluster algebras'] Let $ \mathcal{Q} $ be an acyclic quiver with $ N $ vertices such that the vertices $ 1, \ldots, n $ are mutable 
	and $ n+1, \ldots, N $ are frozen.  
	Let $ K $ be a field
	and let $ \boldsymbol{x} = (x_1, \ldots, x_N ) $ be an $ N $-tuple of elements that are algebraically independent over $ K $.
	The cluster algebra $ \mathcal{A}(\mathcal{Q}) \subset K(\boldsymbol{x}) =  K(x_1, \ldots, x_n, \ldots, x_N) $ (defined over $ K $) corresponding to $ \mathcal{Q} $ is isomorphic to
	
	\begin{equation}
		 
		K[x_{n+1}^{\pm 1}, \ldots, x_{N}^{\pm 1}][x_1, \ldots, x_n, x_1', \ldots, x_n']
		/ \langle x_k x_k' - \prod_{i\rightarrow k} x_i^{b_{ik}} - \prod_{i \leftarrow k} x_i^{-b_{ik}} \mid k \in \{ 1, \ldots, n \} \rangle 
	\end{equation}
	where $ (x_1', \ldots, x_n') $ is another tuple of algebraically independent elements over $ K $, 
	the products range over those vertices $ i $ of $ \mathcal{Q} $ for which there is an arrow $ i \rightarrow k $ (resp.~$ i \leftarrow k $),
	and
	$ b_{ik} \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}} $ is the number of arrows $ i \rightarrow k $ which is negative if there are arrows $ i \leftarrow k $. 
	\\
	Moreover, 
	$ (x_k x_k' - \prod_{i\rightarrow k} x_i^{b_{ik}} - \prod_{i \leftarrow k} x_i^{-b_{ik}} \mid k \in \{ 1, \ldots, n \}) $ 
	is a Gr\"obner basis for the ideal which it generates with respect to any term order
	giving preference to $ x_1', \ldots, x_n' $ over $ \boldsymbol{x} $. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: {\cite{BFZ2005}}

[Proposition prop:CGO-PhS_int-by-parts of arXiv:2609.00257, 'Stability estimates for the initial-to-final-state inverse problem'] [zbMATH07801151]\sl 
Consider $F \in L^2(\Sigma)$ such that 
there exists $c > 0$ so that $e^{c|\mathrm{x}|} F \in L^2(\Sigma)$.
Let $u \in C([0,T]; L^2(\mathbb{R}^n))$ satisfy the conditions

\[
\left\{

		\begin{aligned}
		& (i\partial_\mathrm{t} + \Delta) u = F & & \textnormal{in} \enspace \Sigma, \\
		& u(0, \centerdot) = u(T, \centerdot) = 0 &  & \textnormal{in} \enspace \mathbb{R}^n.
		\end{aligned}

	\right.
\]

For every $\nu \in \mathbb{R}^n \setminus \{ 0 \}$ with $|\nu| < c$,
consider a measurable function 
$v^\nu : \mathbb{R} \times \mathbb{R}^n \rightarrow \mathbb{C}$ such that

\[ \sup_{\alpha \in \mathbb{N}_0^2} \big[ 2^{-|\alpha|/2} \| e^{- \nu \cdot \mathrm{x}} v^\nu \|_{L^2(\Pi_\alpha^\nu)} \big] + \sum_{\alpha \in \mathbb{N}_0^2} 2^{|\alpha| \theta} \| e^{- \nu \cdot \mathrm{x}} (i\partial_\mathrm{t} + \Delta) v^\nu \|_{L^2(\Pi_\alpha^\nu)} < \infty, \]
for some $\theta \in (0, 1/2)$. Then,

\[\int_\Sigma (i\partial_\mathrm{t} + \Delta) u \overline{v^\nu} = \int_\Sigma u \overline{(i\partial_\mathrm{t} + \Delta)v^\nu} \, \]
for all $\nu \in \mathbb{R}^n \setminus \{ 0 \}$ with $|\nu| < c$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition prop:CGO-PhS_int-by-parts of arXiv:2609.00257

body:
[Theorem thm:cheeger-M of arXiv:2606.27073, 'Retention Profiles and KL Contraction Bounds in Finite Markov Chains'] Let $A\subset S$ with $\pi(A)\le 1/2$ be a set achieving the Cheeger
constant~$h_P$, and assume $h_P \le 1 - \pi(A)$ (at equality the bound
below has zero numerator; see Remark~(rmk:cheeger-balanced of the paper)).
Then there exists $x^*\in A$ with $P(x^*,A)\ge 1-h_P$, and
\[
  M
  \;\ge\;
  r(x^*)
  \;\ge\;
  \frac{(1-h_P)\log\dfrac{1-h_P}{\pi(A)}
  +h_P\log\dfrac{h_P}{1-\pi(A)}}{\log\!\bigl(1/\pi(x^*)\bigr)}.
\]
The term involving $h_P$ is interpreted by continuity as $0$ when $h_P=0$.
In particular, for small $h_P$,
$M \gtrsim \log(1/\pi(A))/\log(1/\pi_{\min})$.

[Theorem thm_lip of arXiv:2510.00214, 'On the local well-posedness of randomly forced reaction-diffusion equations with $\bm{L^2}'] If $A>1$ satisfies
	\begin{equation}
		L_bK_b^{-1}\log(8AK_b)<1,
	\end{equation} 
	then there exists a predictable random field
	$u=\{u(t\,,x)\}_{(t,x)\in \mathscr{D}(\infty)}$ that is a mild solution to (equation SHE of the paper)
	and satisfies the following sub-Gaussian moment bound:
	\[
		\E\left( |u(t\,,x)|^k\right)
		\le (2A/t)^{k/4}\left( \|u_0\|_{L^2[0,1]} +  
		\sqrt{k} \right)^k \mathrm{e}^{4AK_b k t},
	\]
	valid uniformly for all numbers $k\ge1$ and all pairs $(t\,,x)\in\mathscr{D}(\infty)$.
title: Theorem thm_lip of arXiv:2510.00214

[Corollary cor:accelerated-rigidity-restated of arXiv:2605.17082, 'Spectral Purification in Reversible Markov Chains: Hidden Parameters, Observable Equivalen'] Under the Chebyshev-accelerated iteration with degree-$m$ polynomial $Q_m^\ast$ (as in (thm:variational of the paper)), the rigidity time satisfies
\[
T_{\mathrm{rigid}}^{\text{cheb}}(\delta) \;\le\; \frac{1}{m} \cdot \frac{\log(R_0 / (|c_2|^2 \delta))}{2 \log(1 / |Q_m^\ast(\lambda_3)|)},
\]
where $|Q_m^\ast(\lambda_3)| \sim (1 - \sqrt{1-\lambda_2^2}/\lambda_2)^m$ for large $m$. Optimizing over $m$ yields the $\sqrt{\kappa}$ speedup over the basic power iteration.

[Lem 16 of arXiv:2512.05687, '$L^p$-Boltzmann-Gibbs principle \\ via Littlewood-Paley-Stein inequality'] (Two-blocks estimate,
cf.\ Lemma 5.6 of \cite{BFS})
Let $p\ge 4$ and let $f$ be a local $L^{p'}(\mu_{u_0})$ function on
$\mathcal{X}_N$ for some $p'>p$ depending only on $\eta_{\La_{\ell_0}}$ 
such that $\tilde f(u_0)=0$ and $\tilde f'(u_0)=0$.  Then, there exists 
a constant $C = C(u_0,\ell_0)$ such that, for $\ell \geq  \ell_0$,  and 
a function $h$ on $[0,T]\times \T_N$, we have
\begin{align}  
&E_{\mu_{u_0}}\Big[\sup_{0\leq t\leq T}\Big|\int_0^t\sum_{x\in{\T_N}} h(s,x)\\
& \hskip 20mm \times\Big\{
E_{\mu_{u_0}}[f(\tau_x\eta_s^N)|\eta_s^{N,(\ell_0)}(x)]
-E_{\mu_{u_0}}[f(\tau_x\eta_s^N)|\eta_s^{N,(\ell)}(x)]\Big\} ds \Big|^p\Big] 
\notag\\
&\hskip 10mm  \leq CT^{(p-2)/2} N^{-p/2}\ell^{p/2} \|f\|^p_{L^{p'}(\mu_{u_0})}
\int_0^T \frac1{N}\sum_{x\in{\T_N}} |h(t,x)|^p dt.
\notag
\end{align}
On the other hand, when only $\tilde f(u_0)=0$ is known, we have
\begin{align}  
&E_{\mu_{u_0}}\Big[\sup_{0\leq t\leq T}\Big|\int_0^t\sum_{x\in{\T_N}} h(s,x) \\
& \hskip 20mm \times \Big\{E_{\mu_{u_0}}[f(\tau_x\eta_s^N)|\eta_s^{N,(\ell_0)}(x)]-E_{\mu_{u_0}}[f(\tau_x\eta_s^N)|\eta_s^{N,(\ell)}(x)]\Big\} ds \Big|^p\Big] 
\notag\\
&\hskip 10mm \leq CT^{(p-2)/2} N^{-p/2} \ell^p \|f\|^p_{L^{p'}(\mu_{u_0})}
\int_0^T \frac1N \sum_{x\in{\T_N}} |h(t,x)|^p dt.
\notag
\end{align}

[Proposition 31 of arXiv:2605.05864, 'Classification and Metrization of Classes of Smooth measures'] Let $\{\mu_n, \mu\} \subset {\cal D}$ and let $\{A^n, A\}$ be the corresponding PCAFs.
Assume that $d_{\cal D}(\mu_n, \mu) \to 0$ as $n \to \infty$. Then the following assertions hold:
\begin{itemize}
\item[\rm (1)] For any compact set $K \subset E$, there exists a subsequence $\{n_k\}$ such that the PCAFs $A^{n_k}$ converge to $A$ locally uniformly in $t$ on $[0,\infty)$ restricted to $K$, ${\mathbb P}_x$-a.s. for quasi every $x \in E$. That is,
$$
{\mathbb P}_x \left( \lim_{k \to \infty} \sup_{0 \le s \le t} \left| \int_0^s 1_K(X_u) \, dA^{n_k}_u - \int_0^s 1_K(X_u) \, dA_u \right| = 0 \text{ for all } t > 0 \right) = 1, \quad \text{q.e. } x \in E.
$$

\item[\rm (2)] Suppose there exists a compact nest $\{F_\ell\}$ satisfying the following tail estimate:
\begin{equation} 
\lim_{\ell \to \infty} \sup_{\nu \in {\cal S}_{c,00}^1} \left\{ \left( \sup_n \int_{F_\ell^c} U_1 \nu \, d\mu_n \right) \vee \int_{F_\ell^c} U_1 \nu \, d\mu \right\} = 0.
\end{equation}
Then, there exists a further subsequence $\{n'_k\}$ such that $A^{n'_k}$ converges to $A$ locally uniformly in $t$ on $[0,\infty)$, ${\mathbb P}_x$-a.s. for quasi every $x \in E$:
$$
{\mathbb P}_x \left( \lim_{k \to \infty} \sup_{0 \le s \le t} |A^{n'_k}_s - A_s| = 0 \text{ for all } t > 0 \right) = 1, \quad \text{q.e. } x \in E,
$$
where ${\cal S}_{c,00}^1 := \{ \nu \in {\cal S}_0 : \mathrm{supp}[\nu] \text{ is compact}, \nu(E) \le 1 \text{ and } \|U_1\nu\|_\infty \le 1 \}$.
\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition 31 of arXiv:2605.05864

body: In machine learning, the perceptron is an algorithm for supervised learning of binary classifiers. A binary classifier is a function that can decide whether or not an input, represented by a vector of numbers, belongs to some specific class. It is a type of linear classifier, i.e. a classification algorithm that makes its predictions based on a linear predictor function combining a set of weights with the feature vector.

[Corollary cor:skip-j of arXiv:2602.21315, 'The Instability of all Backoff Protocols\thanks{For the purpose of Open Access, the author'] Fix $\lambda >0$ and a send sequence~$\overline{p}$.
Let $X$ be the backoff process with birth rate~$\lambda$ and send sequence~$\overline{p}$. 
Let $J$ be a positive integer.
Let $\overline{p}'$ be the send sequence 
such that, for all $i\geq 0$, $p'_i = p_{i+J}$.
There is a real number $\lambda''\in (0,\lambda) $  such that for any   $\lambda' \in (0, \lambda'')$  the following holds.
Let $X'$ be the backoff process with birth rate~$\lambda'$ and send sequence~$\overline{p}'$. 
If $X'$ is not positive recurrent then $X$ is not positive recurrent.

In the Brysiewicz-Sinn algorithm (arXiv:2609.02818), given F: C^n -> C^m with p in V(F), let B in C^{n x s} be a matrix whose columns form a basis of ker(J_F(p)) where s = nullity(J_F(p)), and let C in C^{(m-r) x m} have rows spanning coker(J_F(p))^*. The quadratic obstruction system is the collection of s-variable quadratic forms Q_i(u) = (Bu)^T (sum_k C_{ik} H(f_k)(p)) (Bu) for i = 1, ..., m - r.
F: C^n -> C^m polynomial
p in V(F)
s = nullity(J_F(p))
r = rank(J_F(p))

[Lem 85 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] We have $\cN(0,1) \in \sM^{\sideal}(\alpha,0)$.

\begin{proof}
We repeat the part of Definition~\ref{d:SDE.classification} specifying the $\sideal$ class:
	\begin{center}
	\begin{tabular}[h]{r|cccccccc}
	\MSRheader\\
	\hline
	\SUPERPERFECTdefn
	\end{tabular}
	\end{center}
We will exhibit controls $(q_*,b,\sigma,q,p,\zeta,\zeta^{\Ising}) \in \Adm^{\sideal}(\alpha,0)$ such that $\mu(q_*,b,\sigma,p,\zeta) = \cN(0,1)$. To this end, we let
    \[
        (q_*,b,\sigma,p,\zeta) = (0,0,1,1,\delta_0),
    \]
    so that the process $X(t)$ defined by \eqref{e:formal.sde.main} is simply
    \[
        X(t) = \int_0^t \,dB(u) = B(t)\,,
    \]
and clearly we have 
	\[
	\mu(q_*,b,\sigma,p,\zeta)
	=
	\Law(X(1)) = \cN(0,1)\,.\]
    We then set $\zeta^{\Ising} = \delta_0$, and $w$ to be any progressively measurable control with $\bbE[(w_t)^2] = 1$ for all $t\in [0,1]$ such that $Y(t)$ defined in \eqref{e:formal.sde.ising} satisfies $|Y(t)| = 1$ almost surely.
    The fact that such a $w$ exists follows from Lemma~\ref{lem:Yt-process-always-is-completable} (where we set $q_0 = \gamma(1) = 0$, which makes $\tilde Y, \tilde W, \tilde w, \tilde \cF_Y$ therein degenerate). 

    The above controls clearly satisfy conditions \ref{it:1.2}, \ref{it:2.2}, \ref{it:3.5}, \ref{it:5.2}, \ref{it:6.2}, \ref{it:7.2}, and \ref{it:8.2}.
    Moreover, for the above choices of $b,\sigma$, we have $\Cost(t) = 0$, so condition~\ref{it:4.3} is satisfied.
    Thus these controls belong to $\Adm^{\sideal}(\alpha,0)$, and the claim follows.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lem 85 of arXiv:2608.29416

[Proposition 6 of arXiv:2604.25470, 'A mathematical analysis of hierarchical Hopfield models'] Fix $\kappa\in(0,1)$ and set $\theta=\kappa\log N_f$.
	Under our assumptions for a concept $\alpha$ let the clean cue
	$\eta^{(\alpha)}$ be given by \eqref{eq:concept-or}, and define stroke activations by
	\eqref{eq:stroke-threshold-rule}.
	Then, there exists $a=a(\kappa)>0$ such that, if $M\le N_f^{a-\varepsilon}$ for some
	$\varepsilon>0$, the stroke layer recovers the active stroke set exactly from the clean
	cue, i.e.
	\[
	x_\mu(\eta^{(\alpha)})=\mathbf 1\{\mu\in S_\alpha\}\qquad\text{for all }\mu\le M,
	\]
	with probability $1-o(1)$ as $N_f\to\infty$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition 37 (Timelike slice estimate) of arXiv:2608.31171, '\bf Finite-energy spacetimes with torus symmetry. \\ \Large Cauchy stability of Einstein--'] For any interval $[t_2,t_3]$ contained in $\Interval=[t_0,t_1]$, consider the function on~$\Sbb^1$ defined by
\be
\mathcal F_{[t_2,t_3]}(x) \coloneqq \int_{[t_2,t_3]\times\{x\}\times\Tbb^2} (2T_\chi^{11} + \Ebf_0(\Pbb) + \Ebf_0(\Qbb)) \Omega \, \dVundeux , \qquad x\in\Sbb^1 ,
\ee
where $\dVundeux=|t|\,\Omega \,dt\,dy\,dz$ is the volume form induced by~$g$.
There exists a constant $C>0$ depending only on $t_0,t_1$ (but not $t_2,t_3$), the initial energy~$\mathcal E(t_0)$, volume~$\mathcal V(t_0)$, initial bounded-variation norms of $\ell,\log\Omega,\Kpar$, and minimal conformal length~$\mathcal L_{\min}$ such that
\be
\|\mathcal F_{[t_2,t_3]}\|_{\BV(\Sbb^1)}
= \Var(\mathcal F_{[t_2,t_3]};\Sbb^1) + \| \mathcal F_{[t_2,t_3]} \|_{L^\infty(\Sbb^1)} \leq C .
\ee (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Timelike slice estimate

[Prop obj_0-1and1-2 of arXiv:2601.00119, 'The largest common subtree of two random trees'] Let $c>0$, $\alpha\in (0,1)\cup (1,2)$, and let $X_1,X_2,\dots$ be i.i.d.~random variables such that $\mathbf{P}(|X_1|>x)\leq c x^{-\alpha}$ for all $x>1$. If $1<\alpha<2$, then also assume that $X_1$ is integrable and that ${\mathbf E}[X_1]=0$. For each integer $m\geq 1$, set $S_m=\sum_{i=1}^m (X_i\wedge s m^{1/\alpha})$. Then, there exists a constant $C>0$ such that for any $m\ge 1$, $t\geq 0$, and $s\geq 1$,
\[\mathbf{P}(S_m\ge t m^{1/\alpha})\le C \exp(-t/s) .\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Prop obj_0-1and1-2 of arXiv:2601.00119

and two $d$-dimensional $\del{\mathcal{G}_t}_{t \in \sbr{0,1}}$-Brownian motions $B = \del{B_t}_{t \in \sbr{0,1}}$ and $\tilde{B} = \deln{\tilde{B}_t}_{t \in \sbr{0,1}}$
        and $\del{\mathcal{G}_t}_{t \in \sbr{0,1}}$-adapted processes $Z = \deln{Z_t}_{t \in \sbr{0,1}}$, $\tilde{Z} = \deln{\tilde{Z}_t}_{t \in \sbr{0,1}}$ such that

            \item $\pi$ is the joint law of  $(Z,\tilde{Z})$: $\pi = \deln{Z,\tilde{Z}}_{\#}\mathbb{P}$.
        \end{itemize}

Then if $\varsigma_1 \in (0,1]$ is sufficiently small, the following estimate holds
 for
$(\ubar,u) \in [\leftubar,\ubarboot) \times [\moreinterestingu_1,\moreinterestingu_2]$, where the implicit constant is \textbf{independent} if $\varsigma_0$ and $\varsigma_1$:
\begin{align}

	&  \int_{\characteristicdiamondtwoarg{[\leftubar,\ubar)}{[\moreinterestingu_1,u]}} 
			\left| 
				\multipliervectorfield \tander^{N-1} v 
			\right| 
			\left|
				\begin{pmatrix}
					(\muX v) \tander^{N-1} \mytr_{\gtorus}\upchi 
						\\
					(\angrmd^{\#} v) \cdot \upmu \angrmd \tander^{N-2} \mytr_{\gtorus} \upchi

					\Yvfsmallcoeff{A} (\angrmd^{\#} v) \cdot \upmu \angrmd \tander^{N-2} \mytr_{\gtorus}\upchi

body:
[Lemma L-Lip of arXiv:2507.01406, '{\Large On Iterated Lorenz Curves with Applications: The Multivariate Case }'] \noindent  For each $n\geq 1$, the map $L_{n}:[0,1]^{2}
\rightarrow \lbrack 0,1]$ is uniformly Lipschitz on $[0,1]^{2}$.
Consequently, since under the standing density assumption $L_{0}\in
C([0,1]^{2})$, the full family $(L_{n})_{n\geq 0}$ is relatively compact in $
C([0,1]^{2})$ with the uniform topology.

In particular, every sequence $\{L_{n_{k}}\}_{k=0}^{\infty }$ with $
n_{k}\rightarrow \infty $ admits a subsequence, again denoted by $
\{L_{n_{k}}\}$, and a limit $L^{\ast }:[0,1]^{2}\rightarrow \lbrack 0,1]$
such that 
\begin{equation}
\sup_{(x_{1},x_{2})\in \lbrack 0,1]^{2}}\left\vert
L_{n_{k}}(x_{1},x_{2})-L^{\ast }(x_{1},x_{2})\right\vert \rightarrow 0\quad 
\text{as }k\rightarrow \infty .  
\end{equation}
Moreover, each such $L^{\ast }$ is a continuous distribution function on $
[0,1]^{2}$, and its marginals 
\begin{equation}
L_{1}^{\ast }(x)=L^{\ast }(x,1),\qquad L_{2}^{\ast }(x)=L^{\ast }(1,x)

\end{equation}
are continuous strictly increasing distribution functions on $[0,1]$.
title: Lemma L-Lip of arXiv:2507.01406

[Proposition 7 of arXiv:2506.10856, 'The space of multifurcating ranked tree shapes: enumeration, lattice structure, and Markov'] The number of $t$ vectors in the string representation of multifurcating ranked tree shapes with $K$ internal nodes and $N$ leaves with $K_{0}(t)=k_{0}$ and $K_{1}(t)=k_{1}$ is the number $A_K(k_{0},k_{1})$ that satisfy the following recursion:
\begin{align} 
    A_K(k_{0}, k_{1}) &= A_{K-1}(k_{0}-1, k_{1}) \times (K-k_{0}-k_{1}) + \\
    &\qquad A_{K-1}(k_{0}-1, k_{1}+1)\times (k_{1}+1) + \nonumber \\
    &\qquad A_{K-1}(k_{0}, k_{1}-1)\times k_{0}.  \nonumber
    \nonumber
\end{align}
with initial values: $A_K(1,K-1)=1$, $A_K(K-1,0)=1$. If $(k_0, k_1) \notin \mathcal{K}_K$, then $A_K(k_0, k_1)=0$.
title: Proposition 7 of arXiv:2506.10856

[Theorem thm:terminal-transfer of arXiv:2604.25108, 'Terminal Defects, Growing Multiplicity, and Variance Extremality\\in the Double Dixie Cup '] Let $B_N\in\mathbb R$ and $C_N>0$.  Suppose that for every fixed $x$,
\begin{equation}
        M_N(B_N+C_Nx)\to \Lambda(x),
\end{equation}
where $\Lambda(x)\in[0,\infty)$, and
\begin{equation}
        \sum_{j=1}^N q_{N,j}(B_N+C_Nx)^2\to0.
\end{equation}
Then the Poissonized completion time $X_N$ satisfies
\[
        \mathbb P\left({\frac{X_N-B_N}{C_N}}\le x\right)\to e^{-\Lambda(x)}.
\]
If additionally
\[
        B_N\to\infty,\qquad {\frac{B_N}{C_N}}\to\infty,\qquad \sqrt{B_N}=o(C_N),
\]
then the same limit holds for the discrete completion time $T_N$.

body:
[Theorem 9 of arXiv:2609.04069, 'Positive and Negative Square Energies of $2$-Connected Graphs'] For $n\geq3$, we have, 
$$
 \begin{array}{c|c|c}
  \text{ }n & \spen(C_n) & \sneg(C_n)\\ \hline
  n\text{ even}
   & n & n\\[2mm]
  n\equiv3\pmod4
   & n-1+\sec(\pi/n) & n+1-\sec(\pi/n)\\[2mm]
  n\equiv1\pmod4
   & n+1-\sec(\pi/n) & n-1+\sec(\pi/n)
 \end{array}
$$
In particular,
$$
 \spen(C_n)\geq n
 \text{ if and only if }
 n\not\equiv1\pmod4,
 \qquad
 \sneg(C_n)\geq n
 \text{ if and only if }
 n\not\equiv3\pmod4.
$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 9 of arXiv:2609.04069

body:
[Lemma lem:joint of arXiv:2608.23742, 'Second-order fusion asymptotics for $\Sine_\beta$ correlation functions'] Let $m\ge2$, $\beta>0$, $m\beta>1$, set $\delta=m\beta/2$ and $d=m-1$, and write $\xi=\xi^{\beta,\delta}$. For $b=(b_1,\ldots,b_d)\in\mathbb R^d$ define
\[
H_b(t):=\mathbb E\prod_{j=1}^d|\xi(tb_j)|^\beta,
\qquad
A(b):=\sum_{j=1}^d b_j,
\qquad
B(b):=\sum_{j=1}^d b_j^2.
\]
Then, uniformly for $b$ in compact subsets of $\mathbb R^d$,
\begin{equation}
H_b(t)=1-\beta tA(b)\mathbb E S_1
+\frac{t^2}{2}\left[\beta^2A(b)^2\mathbb E S_1^2-\beta B(b)\mathbb E S_2\right]+o(t^2).
\end{equation}
For real $\delta$ the zero process is reflection symmetric, hence $\mathbb E S_1=0$.

body: Let J be a small category (the index or diagram shape) and D: J -> C a functor (a diagram of shape J) into a category C. A cone over D is an object X of C together with morphisms mu_j: X -> D(j), one for each object j of J, such that for every morphism alpha: j -> j' in J, D(alpha) o mu_j = mu_{j'} (composing with D(alpha) recovers the other leg of the cone). A limit of D is a cone (L, (pi_j)) that is universal among cones over D: for every other cone (X, (mu_j)) there is a unique morphism u: X -> L in C such that pi_j o u = mu_j for every j. Dually, a cocone under D is an object Y with morphisms nu_j: D(j) -> Y such that nu_{j'} o D(alpha) = nu_j for every alpha: j -> j' in J, and a colimit is a universal such cocone (Co, (iota_j)): for every cocone (Y,(nu_j)) there is a unique morphism v: Co -> Y with v o iota_j = nu_j for every j. Products, equalizers, and pullbacks are examples of limits; coproducts, coequalizers, and pushouts are examples of colimits.

body:
[Lemma lem:Bernoulli-basic of arXiv:2602.07920, 'On the position matrix of single-shelf shuffle and card guessing'] Let $(B_s)_{s\ge 0}$ be the Bernoulli numbers, defined by
\[
  \frac{z}{e^z - 1}
  = \sum_{s=0}^\infty B_s \frac{z^s}{s!},\qquad |z|<2\pi.
\]
Then:
\begin{enumerate}
  \item $B_0=1$, $B_1=-\frac12$, and $B_{2m+1}=0$ for all $m\ge 1$.
  \item For all integers $m\ge 1$,
  \[
    |B_{2m}|
    \le \frac{2(2m)!}{(2\pi)^{2m}}.
  \]
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Basic properties of Bernoulli numbers

[Defn 21 of arXiv:2608.13208, 'Universality in dimension $1$ of kinetically constrained lattice gases'] For an admissible flow $\phi$ we define (when
the sums converge): 
\begin{eqnarray}
\left\langle \phi,\phi\right\rangle  & = & \frac{1}{2}\mu\left[\left(\sum_{x\in\Z}\tau_{x}\phi(\eta,\eta^{-1,0})\right)^{2}\right],\\
\left\langle \phi^{1},\phi\right\rangle  & = & \frac{1}{2}\sum_{x\in\Z}\mu\left[\phi(\eta,\eta^{x-1,x})(\eta(x-1)-\eta(x))\right],
\end{eqnarray}
where $\tau_{x}$ is the translation by $x$.
title: Definition 21 of arXiv:2608.13208

[Lemma 9 of arXiv:2506.18558, '2506.18558'] Suppose that Assumptions {\rm\ref{A1}} and {\rm\ref{A2}} hold.  Let $F:\RR_{+}\times \RR^n\times\RR^m\rightarrow \RR$ satisfy that for any $t\ge0$, $x_1,x_2\in \RR^n$ and $y_1,y_2\in \RR^m$,
$$
|F(t,x_1,y_1)-F(t,x_2,y_2)|\le  C(|x_1-x_2|+|y_1-y_2|).
$$
Then, for any $T>0$, there is a constant $C_T>0$ such that for any $0\le  t_0<t\le  T$ and $Z_{t_0}\in\mathscr{F}_{t_0}$ with $\EE|Z_{t_0}|^2<\infty$,
\begin{align*}
\left|\EE\left[\int^t_{t_0}\left(F(s/\varepsilon,X^{\varepsilon}_s, Y^{\varepsilon}_s) -F(s/\varepsilon,X^{\varepsilon}_s, \hat Y^{\varepsilon}_s)\right) Z_{t_0}ds\right]\right|
\le  C_{T}(1+|x|+|y|) \left(\EE|Z_{t_0}|^2\right)^{1/2}\delta^{1/2}.
\end{align*}
title: Lemma 9 of arXiv:2506.18558

[Lemma lem:advancing-escape-final of arXiv:2602.21315, 'The Instability of all Backoff Protocols\thanks{For the purpose of Open Access, the author'] Consider the VEB setting, and let $\Psi = (g,\tau_g,j,\overline{z},\mathcal{S},\textup{advancing}) \in \ensuremath{\Psi^{\mathrm{BB}}(\Psi_0)}$ be a high-level state. 
Let $S$ be the (sole) set in $\mathcal{S}$ (Definition~(def:advancing-state of the paper)).
Suppose that $\overline{a} \in (\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0})^j$  is a $j^7$-AF-good beginning. Conditioned on the events $\Psi(\tau_g) = \Psi$ and $\overline{b}_{[j]}^{E_g}(\tau_g) = \overline{a}$, with probability at least $1-\exp(-400j/\lambda^2)$, 
the following events occur. 
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item For all $t$ in the range $\tau_g \le t \le \tau_g + (4/\lambda)^{2j}$, $\overline{b}_{[j]}^{E_g}(t)$ is a $(6j^{25},j^{27},2/(\xi j^3),2)$-RS-good beginning.
\item For all $t$ in the range $\tau_g + j^{22} \le t \le \tau_g + (4/\lambda)^{2j}$, $\overline{b}_{[j]}^{E_g}(t)$ is a $j^7$-AF-good beginning.
\item For all $t$ in the range $\tau_g \le t \le \tau_g + (4/\lambda)^{2j}$, $\mathcal{N}_S^{E_g}(t+1) \le \lambda|S|/80$.
\end{enumerate} 
Moreover, if these events do occur and $V$ is well-behaved, then the following hold:
\begin{enumerate}[(I)]
\item $\Psi(\tau_{g+1})$ is a $(j+1)$-advancing or $(j+1)$-filling state.
\item $\overline{b}_{[j]}^{E_{g+1}}(\tau_{g+1})$ is a $(j+1)^7$-AF-good beginning.
\item For all $t$ with $\tau_g \le t < \tau_{g+1}$,   $\mathcal{N}^E_S(t+1) \le \lambda |S|/80$. Moreover, $S$ is non-empty.
\end{enumerate}

ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Monotonicity of the ferromagnetic Ising spectral gap explicit structural calculation Result: The two-spin calculation supports the conjecture exactly. With interaction J>=0, let c=tanh(J) and update either spin with probability1/2. The eigenfunctions1, sigma1+sigma2, sigma1-sigma2, sigma1*sigma2-c have eigenvalues1,(1+c)/2,(1-c)/2,0. Hence the spectral gap is(1-tanh(J))/2, strictly decreasing for finite J. Check: Conditionally E[sigma1|sigma2]=c*sigma2. Applying the update kernel to the four displayed basis functions gives the eigenvalues directly. The stationary mean of sigma1*sigma2 is c, so the last function is centered. Obstruction: For a general graph, increasing J changes both the reversible measure and the Dirichlet form. Pointwise comparison of transition probabilities alone does not order the Rayleigh quotient because its variance denominator also changes.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-p0195-monotonicity-of-the-ferromagnetic-ising-spectral-gap
No independent review

# Absolute remainder obstruction in the Li-Nica displayed rescaling

Status: route-failure/source diagnostic, proof draft (unaudited). This is not a disproof of the intended correlation limit. It identifies what cannot follow solely from the printed absolute remainder estimate.

Source: Li-Nica arXiv:2310.12079v2, Section4.1, Eqs.(4.13), (4.15), (4.16), (4.18)-(4.20). The source defines its random big-O using bounds on all absolute moments, with constants independent of n and layer l. Its correlation recursion contains an O(n^(-3/2)) absolute remainder. The proof then sets q_l=l^2(1-rho_l).

An error R_(n,l) in rho_(l+1) contributes exactly -(l+1)^2 R_(n,l) to q_(l+1). Equivalently the normalized left side l^2 q_(l+1)/(l+1)^2 in Eq.(4.18) receives -l^2 R_(n,l). From the printed absolute bound alone, the resulting estimate is O(l^2 n^(-3/2)), not O(l^(-2) n^(-3/2)). For l proportional to n, the former is O(n^(1/2)), which is insufficient for an n-step diffusion approximation. Additional correlation-dependent remainder structure could repair this; the absolute estimate alone cannot.

This failure of implication has an exact deterministic counterexample. Take n=m^2, l=n and R_(n,l)=m^-3=n^-3/2. It satisfies every required pth absolute-moment bound with constant1. The transformed error l^2 R=m, whereas the printed l^-2 n^-3/2 scale is m^-7. Their ratio m^8 diverges. Thus no fixed big-O constant can deduce the latter from the former.

There is also a separate sign inconsistency in the displayed proof. The 1/n part of Eq.(4.16) begins with -2(1-rho_l)/n. Subtracting it in the update for 1-rho therefore produces +2q_l/n after multiplication by l^2, as Eq.(4.18) itself shows before simplification. Eq.(4.19) instead prints -2q_l/n. This observation is separate from C012's Ito comparison; both need source review by the named Claude reviewer.

The PDF first10pages independently confirm the theorem/log-SDE mismatch in Eqs.(4.7)-(4.8); the rescaling equations above were read from primary HTML. Nothing here asserts that the paper's exact, unprinted remainder lacks a stronger small-defect bound. It is the missing stronger bound, together with entrance control, that must be supplied to use this proof route rigorously. C004 supplies an independently checked compact reciprocal-angle generator by a different explicit good-event argument; C005-C006 attempt its entrance extension and remain unaudited.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:ac6fc90336358b7b629440d0887d9aece4dea339a362618c662b4195d0e8fa02","revision_digest":"sha256:74c1415743824d93a1642d1f51cf66595ea562aa52f025246e43228977073ce5","source_id":"own-work:T244-w691-C013:v1","source_revision":"2026-10-20-v1-unaudited","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

[Prop martingaledeouf of arXiv:2603.21634, 'Individual-based stochastic model with unbounded growth, birth and death rates: a tightnes'] Under the \hyperlink{gen}{general setting}, let $F \in \mathcal{C}^{1,1}([0,R_{\max}] \times \mathbb{R})$ and $\varphi \in \mathcal{C}^{1,1}(\mathbb{R}^{+} \times \mathbb{R}^{*}_{+})$. 
\begin{itemize}
\item[$\mathrm{(i)}$] Assume that for all $t \geq 0$,
$$\mathbb{E}\left( \displaystyle{\int_{0}^{t}\int_{\mathbb{R}^{*}_{+}}}b(x)\bigg| F_{\varphi_{s}}(R_{s},\mu_{s}+\delta_{x_{0}}+\delta_{x-x_{0}}-\delta_{x}) - F_{\varphi_{s}}(R_{s},\mu_{s}) \bigg| \mu_{s}(\mathrm{d}x) \mathrm{d}s \right) < + \infty,$$
and
$$\mathbb{E}\left( \displaystyle{\int_{0}^{t}\int_{\mathbb{R}^{*}_{+}}}d(x)\bigg| F_{\varphi_{s}}(R_{s},\mu_{s}-\delta_{x}) - F_{\varphi_{s}}(R_{s},\mu_{s}) \bigg| \mu_{s}(\mathrm{d}x) \mathrm{d}s \right) < + \infty.$$
Then $(\mathfrak{M}_{F,\varphi,t})_{t \geq 0}$ is a $(\mathcal{F}_{t})_{t \geq 0}$-martingale.
\item[$\mathrm{(ii)}$] Suppose in addition that for all $t \geq 0$,
$$\mathbb{E}\left( \displaystyle{\int_{0}^{t}\int_{\mathbb{R}^{*}_{+}}}b(x)\bigg[ F_{\varphi_{s}}(R_{s},\mu_{s}+\delta_{x_{0}}+\delta_{x-x_{0}}-\delta_{x}) - F_{\varphi_{s}}(R_{s},\mu_{s}) \bigg]^{2} \mu_{s}(\mathrm{d}x) \mathrm{d}s \right) < + \infty,$$
and
$$\mathbb{E}\left( \displaystyle{\int_{0}^{t}\int_{\mathbb{R}^{*}_{+}}}d(x)\bigg[ F_{\varphi_{s}}(R_{s},\mu_{s}-\delta_{x}) - F_{\varphi_{s}}(R_{s},\mu_{s}) \bigg]^{2} \mu_{s}(\mathrm{d}x) \mathrm{d}s \right) < + \infty.$$
Then $(\mathfrak{M}_{F,\varphi,t})_{t \geq 0}$ is a square-integrable martingale, with predictable quadratic variation given for all $t \geq 0$ by
\begin{align*}
\left\langle \mathfrak{M}_{F,\varphi}  \right\rangle_{t}  := & \hspace{0.1 cm} \displaystyle{\int_{0}^{t}\int_{\mathbb{R}^{*}_{+}}}b(x)\bigg[ F_{\varphi_{s}}(R_{s},\mu_{s}+\delta_{x_{0}}+\delta_{x-x_{0}}-\delta_{x}) - F_{\varphi_{s}}(R_{s},\mu_{s}) \bigg]^{2} \mu_{s}(\mathrm{d}x) \mathrm{d}s  \\
& + \displaystyle{\int_{0}^{t}\int_{\mathbb{R}^{*}_{+}}}d(x)\bigg[ F_{\varphi_{s}}(R_{s},\mu_{s}-\delta_{x}) - F_{\varphi_{s}}(R_{s},\mu_{s}) \bigg]^{2} \mu_{s}(\mathrm{d}x) \mathrm{d}s
\end{align*}
\end{itemize}
title: Prop martingaledeouf of arXiv:2603.21634

Let nearest-neighbor undirected edges of Z^d, d>=2, carry iid weights with essential infimum 0<r and essential supremum R<infinity, r<R. For each integer n>=1, let T_dir be the cost of the unique coordinate-monotone path from 0 to n*e1. Then P(T(0,n*e1)<T_dir)=0 if n(R-r)<=2r, and P(T(0,n*e1)<T_dir)>0 if n(R-r)>2r. At equality a tie may occur; the statement concerns strict improvement only.

[Theorem 14 of arXiv:2608.22534, 'Entropy power inequalities in compact groups'] Let $G$ be a connected, compact and metrizable topological abelian group, equipped with its Borel $\sigma$-algebra. Let $X,Y$ be independent random variables on $G$ with finite entropies. 
     There exists a continuous function (independent of $G$, $X$ and $Y$),
     $$
     f:(-\infty,0] \to [0,+\infty), \text{ such that } f(x) = 0 \text{ if and only if } x=0
     $$
     and 
        $$
        \delta_{\mathrm{EPI}} = h(X+Y)-\frac12h(X)-\frac12h(Y) \geq \max{\{f(h(X)),f(h(Y))\}}.
        $$
       

        In fact, we may take 
         \begin{align}
f(x) =
\begin{cases} 
\frac{-x^5-4x^6}{16+8x^4} & \text{if } -\frac{1}{8}\leq x\leq 0\\ 
f(-\frac{1}{8}) & \text{if } x < -\frac{1}{8}.
\end{cases}
\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

d >= 2
i.i.d. edge weights tau_e >= 0
P(tau_e = 0) < p_c
E[tau_e^2 (log tau_e)_+] < infinity (the '2 + log moments' condition)
||x||_1 > 1

GENERALITY, IN THE AUTHORS' OWN WORDS: 'The proof applies equally to absolutely continuous, discrete and singular continuous distributions and mixtures thereof, and requires only 2+log moments. The main result extends work of Benjamini-Kalai-Schramm and Benaim-Rossignol.' So the field already HAS distributional generality with no transfer argument, under a moment condition strictly weaker than bounded support.
METHOD: follows Benaim-Rossignol but represents each edge weight as a push-forward of an infinite Bernoulli sequence and bounds the entropy with the Gross two-point inequality, which needs a careful analysis of the discrete derivatives plus greedy lattice animals.
TWO PAPERS, DO NOT MERGE THEM: this is Damron-Hanson-Sosoe, 'Sublinear variance in first-passage percolation for general distributions', arXiv:1306.1197, Probab. Theory Relat. Fields 163 (2015). Their OTHER paper, 'Subdiffusive concentration in first-passage percolation' (arXiv:1401.0917), is the concentration inequality, not this variance bound.
SOURCE AND WHAT WAS CHECKED WHERE: the arXiv:1306.1197v2 abstract gives d >= 2, the C||x||/log||x|| form, and the 2+log moment condition in the authors' own words. It does NOT state P(tau_e = 0) < p_c; that hypothesis was read in Auffinger-Damron-Hanson, '50 years of first passage percolation', arXiv:1511.03262v2 (AMS University Lecture Series 68, 2017), theorem 'thm:DHS222', tex lines 1176-1179.
VERIFICATION STATUS: survey-claim for the complete hypothesis set (because the percolation hypothesis came from the survey, not the abstract), with the generality and the moment condition independently confirmed against the authors' abstract.
title: Damron-Hanson-Sosoe (2015): for d >= 2, if P(tau_e = 0) < p_c and E[tau_e^2 (log tau_e)_+] < infinity, then there is C > 0 with Var T(0,x) <= C ||x||_1 / log ||x||_1 for every x with ||x||_1 > 1. This '2 + log moments' result is the best UNCONDITIONAL variance upper bound known for lattice first-passage percolation, and as of August 2026 nothing has beaten its log factor on Z^d.

[Lemma 8 (Cauchy Property of the Penalized Sequence) of arXiv:2604.14893, 'Well-Posedness of Generalized Mean-Reflected McKean--Vlasov Backward Stochastic Differenti'] Under Assumptions (A1)--(A5), for a given $k\ge{}1$, there exists a constant $C_k>0$ independent of $m$ and $n$ such that for any $m,n\ge{}1$, the solution sequence $(Y^{n,k},Z^{n,k})_{n={}1}^\infty$ of the penalized equation satisfies the following estimate:
\[
\mathbb{E}\left[\sup_{0\le{} t\le{} T}|Y_t^{m,k} - Y_t^{n,k}|^2\right] + \mathbb{E}\left[\int_0^T |Z_s^{m,k} - Z_s^{n,k}|^2\dif s\right] \le{} C_k\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{m}}+\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}\right).
\]
Therefore, this sequence forms a Cauchy sequence in $S^2\times H^2$.
title: Cauchy Property of the Penalized Sequence

[Defi 9 (Classical symbols) of arXiv:2609.01105, 'Obstruction to quasi-invariance of Gaussian measures under transport flows on Riemannian M'] Let $m \in \mathbb{R}$. A function $p : \mathbb{R}^d \times \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}$ is a classical symbol of order $m$, and we write $p \in S_{\rm cl}^m$, if $p\in S^m$ and if for all~\(j\in \Nn\) there exists $p_{m-j}\in S^{m-j}$, homogeneous of degree $m-j$ in $\xi$, smooth for $\xi \neq 0$ such that 
\[
    p - \sum_{j=0}^N\omega(\xi)p_{m-j} \in S^{m-N-1}\quad \text{for all } N\geq 0,
\] 
where $\omega \in \mathcal{C}^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ vanishes in a neighborhood of $0$ and equals $1$ for $|\xi| \geq 1$. 
We write $\sigma_m(p)=p_m$ and we say that $p_m$ is the principal symbol of $p$.
title: Classical symbols

[Corollary cor:cyclicshift of arXiv:2607.22291, 'Rare subtree patterns in size-conditioned Bienaymé trees: Poisson approximation and declum'] Let $G$ be a $ \{0,1\}$-valued function defined on the set of all finite plane trees.  Let $U_n$ be a uniform vertex of $\mathcal T^n$, independent of
$\mathcal T^n$. Set also
 $\Psi_m(i)=\P(S_m=i)$, with the convention $\Psi_m(i)=0$ if $m<0$. Then
$$
\P(G(\mathcal T^n_{U_n})=1)
=
\frac{1}{\Psi_n(-1)}
\mathbb{E}\left[
\mathbbm{1}_{\{G(\mathcal T)=1\}}
\Psi_{n-|\mathcal T|}(0)
\right].
$$

[Corollary 15 of arXiv:2607.08242, 'Convergence of random sums in non-commutative probability'] Let $\{b_i\}$ be a sequence of self-adjoint variables with $\varphi(b_i)=0$, $\varphi(b_i^2)=1$, and $\sup_{i}|\varphi(b_i^m)|<\infty$ for each $m\in\mathbb{N}$. Set $a_n=b_1+\dots+b_n$ for each $n\in\mathbb{N}$. Let $\{w_n\}$ be a sequence of positive integers increasing to infinity. Let $\{N_n\}$ be non-negative integer valued rvs such that 
    $N_n/w_n\stackrel{\mathbb{P}}{\to}1$,
    
    and $\{(\frac{N_n}{w_n})^{m}\}$ be uniformly integrable for each $m\in\mathbb{N}$. 
    
        
    
    Then the following hold. \vskip5pt
    
    \noindent (i) If $\{b_i\}$ are free then 
    $\frac{a_{N_n}}{\sqrt{w_n}}\stackrel{*}{\to} s$.
    

    
    \vskip5pt
    \noindent (ii) If $\{b_i\}$ are independent then 
    $\frac{a_{N_n}}{\sqrt{w_n}}\stackrel{*}{\to} z$.
    
    
    \vskip5pt
    \noindent (iii) If $\{b_i\}$ are half-independent then 
    $\frac{a_{N_n}}{\sqrt{w_n}}\stackrel{*}{\to} r_S$.

body:
[Lemma Affine invariance of arXiv:2607.29020, 'Entropic Symmetrization Resistance'] \label[lemma]{lem:affine_invariance}
Let $X \in_R \mathbb{R}^d$ be discrete, 
let $f_Y \in \Sym(X)$, 
let $A$ be a linear bijection on $\mathbb{R}^d$
and let $b \in \mathbb{R}^d$. 
Then $f_{AY - b} \in \Sym(AX + b)$. 

Moreover, for any fixed $c>0$, $H(AY-b) \ge cH(AX + b)$ iff $H(Y) \ge cH(X)$, 
and for $d=1$ and nonzero $a \in \mathbb{R}$, $\Var(aY-b) \ge c\Var(aX+b)$ iff $\Var(Y) \ge c\Var(X)$. 

\begin{proof}
For the first claim it is sufficient to check the symmetry equations, 
and indeed
\[ 
f_{AX+b + AY-b}(z)

= f_{X+Y}(A^{-1} z)
= f_{X+Y}(-A^{-1} z)

= f_{AX+b + AY-b}(-z). 
\]

Also, $H(AY-b) = H(Y)$ and $H(AX+b) = H(X)$. 
Finally, $\Var(aY-b)= a^2\Var(Y)$ and $\Var(aX+b) = a^2\Var(X)$. 
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Affine invariance

body: [Corollary adj6 of arXiv:2609.03988, 'A $p$-summability approach to the weak maximizing property'] Let $1\leq p,q<\infty$. Suppose that $B_X$ is relatively weakly $p$-precompact, that $B_{Y^*}$ is relatively weakly $q$-precompact, and that $Y$ has the $\mathrm{sDPP}_{(p,q)}$. Then, the pair $(X,Y)$ has the $\mathrm{SMP}_p$ if and only if the pair $(Y^*,X^*)$ has the $\mathrm{SMP}_q$ for adjoint operators. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Let r and s be probability mass functions on a finite set with total variation distance c = (1/2) sum_x |r_x - s_x|, let alpha, beta >= 0, M = max(alpha, beta), m = min(alpha, beta) and delta = M - m. Then D = (1/2) sum_x |alpha r_x - beta s_x| satisfies max(delta/2, M c - delta/2) <= D <= delta/2 + m c. Both bounds are attained for every alpha, beta >= 0 and c in [0, 1]. Writing alpha = M, beta = m: the upper bound by r = (1 - c, c, 0), s = (1 - c, 0, c); when m > 0, the lower bound by r = (1 - c, c), s = (1, 0) if M c <= delta, and by r = (1 - c, c, 0), s = (k, 0, 1 - k) with k = M(1 - c)/m if M c >= delta. If m = 0 then D = M/2 for all r, s.

[Lemma lem:ricci-internal-hard of arXiv:2608.29403, 'Kac's Walk on Rotation Matrices Mixes in $\boldsymbol{\Theta(n^2)}$ Steps:\\ A Proof Disco'] Fix a complete squared-shell child through its monomer--dimer,
coefficient-pairing, ribbon, status, incidence, and Haar-residual data,
except that the complete reflection/status orbit and the complete
weak-order, equality, and finite-gap sum are retained inside the residual
component $\mathcal C_R$ containing the selected aggregate-Ricci root
$R$.  Suppose $\mathcal P_R=\varnothing$ and, after equal-time fusion,
$\mathcal C_R$ contains at least one independently token-bearing hard
resource: either a nonsingleton packet child for which the one-token
presentation has already proved a numerical factor
$\delta_P\le N^{-1}$, or a time-indexed linear Jacobi child
$-2N^{-1}W_i$.  An unsplit mixed/full-centered hard block with only unit
or $n^{-1/2}$ relative cost is not included.  A resolved fixed-column
child whose complete closed coefficient scalar has a proved factor
$\delta_P\le N^{-1}$ relative to the bare Euler carrier is included.
Nor is a resource in a different Haar-separated component.

Let $f_R\in\{1,2\}$ be the number of fundamental $p\vee r$ circuits hit
by the four Ricci legs, let
\[
 \mathfrak e_R=\frac Cn\|B\|_F\|B'\|_F,
\]
and let $\mathfrak a_{\Gamma,\mathcal C_R}$ be the remaining positive,
once-normalized circuit-anchored terminal majorant.  Then
\[
 \boxed{
 \sum_{\substack{\text{weak orders, equality blocks, finite gaps,}\\
                  \text{and typed states inside }\mathcal C_R}}
 |\operatorname{Contr}_{\Gamma,\mathcal C_R}|
 \le A_L^{r_R}(r_R+1)^B
      \mathfrak a_{\Gamma,\mathcal C_R}\mathfrak e_RN^{-1}.}
\tag{3.3.1w$_{12m}$}
\]
Consequently the complete packetless subfiber in which the Ricci
component has such a resource satisfies the shell bound on the right of
(eq:3.3.1w-12k of the paper).

[Lemma S-cocompleteness-repr of arXiv:2608.28504, 'Global $\bm\infty$-categories and global Thom spectra'] A $T$-$\infty$-category $\mathcal C$ is $S$-cocomplete if and only if the following three conditions are satisfied: 
\begin{enumerate}
\item The $T$-$\infty$-category $\mathcal C$ is fiberwise cocomplete. 
\item For every morphism $s\colon A\to B\in S$, the restriction $s^*\colon\mathcal C(B)\to \mathcal C(A)$ admits a left adjoint $s_{!}$. 
\item For any pullback
    \[
        \begin{tikzcd}
            X\arrow[d,"s'"']\arrow[dr,pullback]\arrow[r,"f'"] & A\arrow[d,"s"]\\
            C\arrow[r,"f"'] & B
        \end{tikzcd}
    \]
    in $\PSh(T)$ with $s$ in $S$ and $C\in T$, the restriction along $s'$ admits a left adjoint $s'_!$, and the Beck-Chevalley map $s'_!f'^*\to f^*s_!$ is an equivalence. 
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
