[Theorem thm:first-order-score of arXiv:2607.04514, 'Boundary-layer asymptotics for Gaussian-smoothed singular measures'] Let \(A>0\) and assume (ass:standing of the paper) with \(r\geqslant r_0\) (the value of \(r_0\) is
  specified below for each expansion). Then there exists \(\sigma_0 > 0\) such that, for every
  \((y,\sigma)\in\mathcal Y_{A,\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{S}},\sigma_0}\), \(x=\pi(y)\), \(a = a(y,\sigma)\), it
  holds that
  \begin{align*}
    \boldsymbol{s}_\sigma(y) &= \sigma^{-1}\big(\mathsf S_0(a,x,\sigma)
    + \sigma\mathscr R_{0,\boldsymbol{s}_\sigma}(a,x,\sigma)\big), \qquad r_0=2 \\
    \mathbf{H}_\sigma(y) &= \sigma^{-2} \big( \mathsf H_0(a,x,\sigma)
    + \sigma\mathscr R_{0, \mathbf{H}_\sigma}(a,x,\sigma)\big), \qquad r_0=3 \\
    \dot{\boldsymbol{s}}_\sigma(y) &= \sigma^{-2} \big(\dot{\mathsf S}_0 (a,x,\sigma)
    + \sigma \mathscr R_{0,\dot{\boldsymbol{s}}_\sigma}(a,x,\sigma)\big), \qquad r_0=3.
  \end{align*}
  Here, the coefficients \(\mathsf S_0\), \(\mathsf H_0\) and \(\dot{\mathsf S}_0\) are explicitly
  given by the formulas below and have all mixed derivatives up to order \(r-r_0+1\) in the
  variables \(a\), \(x\), and \(\sigma\), uniformly bounded for \(x\in\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{S}}\), \(\|a\|
  \leqslant A\), and \(0<\sigma\leqslant\sigma_0\):
  \begin{align*}
    \mathsf S_0 (a,x,\sigma) &= \mathbf J_\nu^\top (a,x,\sigma)\nabla_a \mathsf L_0(a,x), \\
    \mathsf H_0 (a,x,\sigma) &= \mathbf J_\nu^\top(a,x,\sigma)
    \mathrm{D}_a^2 \mathsf L_0(a,x) \,\mathbf J_\nu(a,x,\sigma), \\
    \dot{\mathsf S}_0(a,x,\sigma) &= -\mathsf S_0 (a,x, \sigma)
    - (\mathrm{D}_a\mathsf S_0(a,x,\sigma))[a].
  \end{align*}
  The functions \(\mathscr R_{0,\boldsymbol{s}_\sigma}\), \(\mathscr R_{0,\mathbf{H}_\sigma}\) and \(\mathscr R_{0,\dot{\boldsymbol{s}}_\sigma}\) have
  all mixed derivatives up to order \(r-r_0\) in the variables \(a\), \(x\), and \(\sigma\),
  uniformly bounded for \(x\in\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{S}}\), \(\|a\| \leqslant A\), and
  \(0<\sigma\leqslant\sigma_0\). Derivatives in \(x\) are computed in the stratum coordinate
  \(\theta\), after writing \(x=\Phi(\theta,0)\). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: Lemma (campaign status: audited-pass): After Theorem 1 each row is h_a(x) = q_a(x_C) + lambda_a*x_j for at most one j outside C (tag 19). Call j conditionally free if for SOME realized core value X_C = c both signs of X_j occur among points of S having that same core value. If a row uses a conditionally free j, evaluating on two such points gives q_a(c)+lambda_a and q_a(c)-lambda_a both in {+-1}; since lambda_a is nonzero these are the two distinct signs, so q_a(c) = 0 and lambda_a = +-1 (tag 20). body:
[Lemm l:cond-var-comparison of arXiv:2607.18194, 'Temperature chaos in directed polymers'] Let $X$ be a random variable such that $\mathbb{P}(|X|>m) \leqslant Ce^{-cm^{3/2}}$ for some $C,c>0$ and all $m\geqslant0$.
    Let $Y,Z$ be random $d$-dimensional vectors on the same probability space as $X$, for some $d\geqslant 1$.
    We have
    \begin{align*}
        \Bigl|
            \mathbb{E}[\Var(X|Y)] - \mathbb{E}[\Var(X|Z)]
        \Bigr|
        \leqslant C'\,\mathbb{P}(Y\ne Z)^{0.9}
    \end{align*} 
    for some $C'>0$ depending only on $C,c$.
    (The exponent $0.9$ can be replaced with any $\kappa<1$.) (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Corollary cor:accelerated-rigidity of arXiv:2605.17082, 'Spectral Purification in Reversible Markov Chains: Hidden Parameters, Observable Equivalen'] Under the Chebyshev-accelerated scheme $Q_m^\ast$, the rigidity time satisfies
\[
T_{\mathrm{rigid}}^{\mathrm{cheb}}(\delta) \le \frac{1}{m} \cdot \frac{\log(R_0 / (|c_2|^2 \delta))}{2 \log(1/\epsilon_m)} + 1, \qquad
\epsilon_m := \frac{1}{|T_m(1/\lambda_2)|}.
\]
For large $m$, $\epsilon_m \sim (1 - \sqrt{1-\lambda_2^2}/\lambda_2)^m$, yielding
\[
T_{\mathrm{rigid}}^{\mathrm{cheb}}(\delta) \lesssim \sqrt{\frac{\log(R_0 / (|c_2|^2 \delta))}{2(1-\lambda_2)}} = O\Bigl( \sqrt{T_{\mathrm{rigid}}(\delta)} \Bigr),
\]
a square-root speedup over the basic power iteration.

[Lemma l:time_regularity of arXiv:2607.15140, 'On the absence of blow-up in the 3D Navier-Stokes equations with transport noise'] Fix $R,M,\mu>0$, and let $p,q\in (2,\infty)$ be such that (equation eq:condition_pq_subcritical_scaling_cutoff of the paper) holds.
For all $b\in (2,\infty)$ and $T\in (0,\infty)$, let $w_{{\rm cut}}^N$ be the unique global $(p,q)$-solution to (equation eq:navier_stokes_cutoff of the paper) provided by Lemma (l:global_cutoff of the paper) for some $u_0\in \mathcal{B}_{p,q}(M)$. 
Set 
\begin{equation}

\mathcal{M}^N(t)\stackrel{{\rm def}}{=}\sum_{k,\alpha} \theta_k^N \int_0^t (\sigma_{k,\alpha}\cdot \nabla) w_{{\rm cut}}^N\,\mathrm{d} W^{k,\alpha}_s.
\end{equation}
Then there exist constants $K_T,\kappa,\gamma_0,\gamma_1>0$ independent of $u_0\in \mathcal{B}_{p,q}(M)$ and $N\geq 1$ such that 
\begin{align}

{\mathbf E} [\|\mathcal{M}^N \|_{C^{\gamma_0}(0,T;H^{-\gamma_1})}^{b}]
&\leq K_T N^{-\kappa b} (1+\|u_0\|_{B^{1-2/p}_{q,p}}^{b}),\\

{\mathbf E} [\|w_{{\rm cut}}^N \|_{C^{\gamma_0}(0,T;H^{-\gamma_1})}^{b}]
&\leq K_T (1+\|u_0\|_{B^{1-2/p}_{q,p}}^{b}),
\end{align}
where $\gamma_0,\gamma_1$ are additionally independent of $T>0$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition prop:tailrl-closed-form-weights of arXiv:2609.02987, 'Tail Likelihood Reinforcement Learning'] For every $i=1,\ldots,N$,
\begin{equation}
\omega\bigl(r_{(i)}\bigr)
=
\sum_{k=1}^{i}
\frac{r_{(k)}-r_{(k-1)}}{N-k+1}.

\end{equation}
Equivalently, all weights follow the recurrence
\begin{equation}
\omega\bigl(r_{(i)}\bigr)
=
\omega\bigl(r_{(i-1)}\bigr)
+
\frac{r_{(i)}-r_{(i-1)}}{N-i+1},
\qquad
\omega\bigl(r_{(0)}\bigr)=0.

\end{equation}
title: Closed-form empirical weights

body:
[Definition d:am-decbundle of arXiv:2510.13659, 'On the energy image density conjecture of Bouleau and Hirsch'] Let $\mu$   be a finite Borel measure on $\mathbb{R}^n$. Then the \emph{decomposability bundle} is a Borel map $T^{AM}_\mu: \mathbb{R}^n \to \Gr(\mathbb{R}^n)$ such that the following
		statements hold:
		\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
			\item Every Lipschitz function $f \in \Lip(\mathbb{R}^n)$ is differentiable at $\mu$-a.e.~$x \in \mathbb{R}^n$ with respect to the
			linear subspace $T_\mu^{AM}$, that is, there exists a linear function $df_x^{AM}: T^{AM}_\mu(x) \to \mathbb{R}$, such that
			\[ f(x+h) = f(x) + df_x^{AM}(h) + o(\lvert h\rvert)
			\quad \text{for } h \in T^{AM}_\mu(x). \]
			\item The previous statement is sharp:  there exists a Lipschitz function $f \in \Lip(\mathbb{R}^n)$
			such that for $\mu$-a.e.~$x \in \mathbb{R}^n$ and every $v \not\in T^{AM}_\mu(x)$ the derivative of $f$ at $x$ in the
			direction $v$ does not exist. More precisely, for $\mu$-a.e.~$x \in \mathbb{R}^n$, we have
			\[
			\liminf_{t \to 0} \frac{f(x+tv)-f(x)}{t} < \limsup_{t \to 0}  \frac{f(x+tv)-f(x)}{t}, \quad \mbox{for all $v \not\in T^{AM}_\mu(x)$}
			\]
		\end{enumerate}
title: Definition d:am-decbundle of arXiv:2510.13659

body:
[Lemma exp of arXiv:2411.06827, 'The Exponential Lie Series and a Chen--Strichartz Formula for L{\'e}vy Processes'] The basis change formula expressing the elements of $({\mathbb A}^0)^\ast$ in terms of the elements of ${\mathbb A}^\ast$ in ${\mathbb R} {\langle}{\mathbb A}{\rangle}$ is obtained as
$$
	w^0=\sum_{(i_1, \ldots ,i_\ell)}\frac{1}{i_1!\cdots i_\ell!}(i_1, \ldots,\, i_\ell)\circ w.
$$
where $w^0=a_1^0\cdots a_n^0$. Here, the sum runs over all multi-indices $(i_1, \ldots , i_\ell)$ such that $i_1+ \cdots + i_\ell=|w|$ where $|w|$ denotes the length of the word $w$ and  
\begin{equation*}
	(i_1, \ldots,\, i_\ell)\circ w := 
		[ a_1,\ldots , a_{i_1}]
		[ a_{i_1+1}, \ldots , a_{i_1+i_2}]\cdots
		[ a_{i_1+\cdots+i_{\ell-1}+1}, \ldots , a_{n}]
\end{equation*}
is the concatenation of the repeated bracket product of the letters in each subword as indicated. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] Consider the Bessel and free Bessel laws, depending on parameters $s\in\mathbb N\cup\{\infty\}$ and $t>0$, which are the following compound Poisson/free Poisson laws,
$$b^s_t=p_{t\varepsilon_s}\quad,\quad 
\beta^s_t=\pi_{t\varepsilon_s}$$
with $\varepsilon_s$ being the uniform measure on the $s$-th roots of unity. Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item At $s=1$ we recover the Poisson laws $p_t,\pi_t$.

\item At $s=2$ we recover the real Bessel laws $b_t,\beta_t$.

\item At $s=\infty$ we have the complex Bessel laws $B_t,\mathfrak B_t$.
\end{enumerate}

[Corollary cor:stein of arXiv:2510.22778, 'Free denoising diffusion models'] For \emph{any} $\theta$, not only a minimiser, define the free score discrepancy
$\mathcal S_{t}(\theta):=\tau\big[(\widehat\xi_{t}-\xi_{\mu_{t}}(X_{t}))^{2}\big]$,
the free (Fisher-divergence-type) analogue of a Stein discrepancy between the learned
and true conjugate variable at time $t$. Then
\begin{equation}
  \mathcal S_{t}(\theta)=\frac{1}{v_{t}^{2}}\Big(\mathcal L_{t}(\theta)-c_{t}\Big),
  \qquad
  \mathcal L_{t}(\theta):=\tau\Big[\big(g_{\theta}(X_{t},t)-\sqrt{\alpha_{t}}X_{0}
  \big)^{2}\Big],
\end{equation}
with $c_{t}$ as in (equation eq:bias-variance of the paper), exactly -- with no approximation and no
constant to be estimated. Consequently $\mathcal L_{t}(\theta)-c_{t}\ge0$ always, with
equality iff $\mathcal S_{t}(\theta)=0$.

[Lemma 16 of arXiv:2608.26565, 'A Horizon-Free Extrinsic Penrose Inequality'] Let $N\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a domain. Suppose that for some open set $U$,
	\[
	\partial N\cap U=\Sigma_1\cup\Sigma_2,
	\]
	where $\Sigma_1$ and $\Sigma_2$ are smooth faces whose intersection
	$\Gamma=\Sigma_1\cap\Sigma_2$ is compact and smooth. Assume that the faces
	meet transversely along $\Gamma$ and that $N$ lies locally on their inner
	sides. With respect to the outward normals of $N$, suppose
	\[
	H_{\Sigma_1}\geq0,
	\qquad
	H_{\Sigma_2}\geq0
	\]
	near $\Gamma$. Then, for every neighborhood $V\Subset U$ of $\Gamma$,
	there exists a domain $\widetilde N$ differing from $N$ only inside $V$.
	Its boundary is smooth near $\Gamma$ and satisfies
	\[
	\widetilde N\triangle N\Subset V,
	\qquad
	\partial\widetilde N=\partial N
	\quad\text{outside }V,
	\qquad
	H_{\partial\widetilde N}\geq0
	\quad\text{on the modified part}.
	\]

[Lemma lm:3.7.howard.newman of arXiv:2411.02046, 'Speed of Convergence and Moderate Deviations of FPP on Random Geometric Graphs'] For any~$d \ge 2$ and~$\uppsi \in (0,1/4)$, there exists~$c_\uppsi > 0$ such that the following holds. Let~$\{q_1,q_2,\ldots\}$ be a finite or infinite sequence of elements of $\mathbb R^d$ so that there exists~$k^* \in \mathbb N$ such that the following three properties hold: first,
    \[
    \|q_{i+1}-q_i\|\le \|q_i\|^{3/4} \text{ for all }i \ge k^*;
    \]
    second, 
    \[
    \|q_i\| \ge 3^{1/\uppsi} \text{ for all }i \ge k^*;
    \]
    and third,
    \[\mathrm{dist}(q_i,\overline{o q_j})\leq \|q_j\|^{1-\uppsi} \ \ \text{ for all $i,j$ with $j \ge k^*$ and ~$i \le j$}.\]
    Then, for all~$i,j$ with~$j > i \ge k^*$, we have
    \begin{equation*} 
        \uptheta(q_i,q_j) \le c_\uppsi~\|q_i\|^{-\uppsi}.
    \end{equation*}

body: [Lemma implication-of-uniform-lipschitz of arXiv:2608.12056, 'Deviation inequalities for U-processes of growing order, with applications to half-space d'] Let $X_1, X_2,\ldots$ be i.i.d. copies of a random variable $X \in \mathbb R$ with absolutely continuous distribution. Assume that $\mathbb E X= 0$ and $\mathrm{var}(X) = 1$. Define $Y_n = \frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}\sum_{j=1}^n X_j$, and let the density of $Y_n$ be denoted $f_n$. If $f_n$ is Lipschitz continuous with Lipschitz constant $L$ uniformly for all $n \geq n_0$, then $f_n(x) \rightarrow \phi(x)$ uniformly over all $x \in \mathbb R$ as $n \rightarrow \infty$, where $\phi$ is the density of the standard normal law. Consequently, $f_n$ is also uniformly bounded.
title: Lemma implication-of-uniform-lipschitz of arXiv:2608.12056

body: In mathematics, a presentation is one method of specifying a group. A presentation of a group G comprises a set S of generators—so that every element of the group can be written as a product of powers of some of these generators—and a set R of relations among those generators. We then say G has presentation $$\langle S\mid R\rangle .$$

body: Certificate (campaign status: audited-pass): For every n >= 4 an independent set U of C_n of size ceil(n/3) exists with all cyclic gaps of length 2 or 3: n = 3k -> |U| = k, gaps 3,...,3; n = 3k+1 -> |U| = k+1, gaps 2,2,3,...,3; n = 3k+2 -> |U| = k+1, gaps 2,3,...,3. The residuals L_u = A+B_u = e_0+e_u are linearly independent because the e_u coordinate occurs only in L_u. With F_empty = -A, F_{i} = B_i, F_{i,i+1} = C_i one has F_{u} - F_empty = L_u and F_{u,v} - F_{v} = L_u, so every clique form is congruent mod span{L_u} to the form obtained by deleting its U-vertices. Deleting an independent U removes exactly 2|U| cycle edges. Notes: Proves feasibility in ALL THREE congruence classes mod 3, not only 3 | n. All gaps >= 2 (independence) AND <= 3 (domination) are both load-bearing -- see coverage_check_enforces_dominating_gaps.

body:
[Corollary cor:subcritical of arXiv:2608.30831, 'Sharp discrete Hardy constants in dimensions three and four\\ and strict upper bounds from'] For $N=3,4$, let $h_N$ be the supersolution in Lemma~(lem:N3 of the paper) or
Lemma~(lem:N4 of the paper), respectively, and define
\begin{equation}
 V_N(n):=\frac{(-\Delta_{\!d} h_N)(n)}{h_N(n)}-\frac{A_N}{|n|^2},
 \qquad n\in X_N.
\end{equation}
Then $V_N(n)>0$ for every $n\in X_N$, and
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal E_N[u]-A_N\mathcal D_N[u]
 \ge\sum_{n\in X_N}V_N(n)|u(n)|^2
\end{equation}
for every finitely supported $u$ with $u(0)=0$.
Thus the form on the left is subcritical, although $C(N)=A_N$.
In particular, $A_N|n|^{-2}$ is not a pointwise optimal Hardy weight.

\[
(-\Delta)^s\psi_B(x)
=
c_B-\langle A_Bx,x\rangle,
\]
where
\begin{equation}
c_B
=
\kappa_{n,s}
\int_{\partial E_B}\mu_{B,s}(d\theta)
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}
A_B
=
\kappa_{n,s}
\left[
B\int_{\partial E_B}\mu_{B,s}(d\theta)

2s
\int_{\partial E_B}
(B\theta)\otimes(B\theta)\,
\mu_{B,s}(d\theta)

body: A family $\Pi$ of probability measures on a metric space is tight if for every $\varepsilon>0$ there is a compact $K$ with $\mu(K)>1-\varepsilon$ for all $\mu\in\Pi$; by Prokhorov's theorem a tight family is relatively compact for weak convergence, and on a Polish space the converse holds.

body:
[Definition def:delta_close of arXiv:2411.13133, 'Connectivity of the adjacency graph of\\ complementary components of the $\SLE$ Fan'] Fix $\kappa \in (0,4)$ and let $h$ be a whole-plane GFF with values modulo a global multiple of $2\pi\chi$. Let $D$ be a bounded open set containing $0$, let $\delta > 0$ and define $D_\delta = \{z \in \mathbf{C} \colon d(z, D) < \delta\}$. For $\theta \in \mathbf{R}$ let $\eta_{\theta}$ be the flow line of $h$ starting from $0$ with angle $\theta$ and for any set $A$ let $\tau_\theta(A) = \inf\{t \geq 0\colon \eta_\theta(t) \notin A\}$.
For $\theta \neq 0$, $\eta_0$ and $\eta_\theta$ are said to be \emph{$\delta$-close until $\eta_0$ exits $D$} if the following conditions hold. For all $t \in (0, \tau_0(D)]$ there exist $t_1, t_2, t'_1, t'_2$ where $0 < t_1 < t < t_2 < \tau_0(D_\delta)$ and $0 < t'_1 < t'_2 < \tau_\theta(D_\delta)$ such that for each $j = 1,2$, $\eta_0(t_j) = \eta_\theta(t'_j)$ and at this point $\eta_\theta$ hits $\eta_0$ on the \emph{left} side of $\eta_0$  (if $\theta > 0$) with angle gap $\theta$ (as defined in [ms2017ig4]). Furthermore, for any $s \in [t_1, t_2]$ and $s' \in [t'_1, t'_2]$, we have $|\eta_0(s) - \eta_\theta(s')| < \delta$. If $\theta < 0$, we replace `left side' by `right side' above.
title: Definition def:delta_close of arXiv:2411.13133

body:
Let Omega be an open subset of R^n. A second-order operator in divergence form is Lu = -sum_{i,j} D_i(a^{ij}(x) D_j u) + sum_i b^i(x) D_i u + c(x) u, written Lu = -div(A grad u) + b.grad u + c u, where A = (a^{ij}) is a real n x n matrix-valued measurable function on Omega (not necessarily symmetric, not necessarily continuous) and b = (b^i), c are real measurable functions. L is uniformly elliptic with constants 0 < lambda <= Lambda if for a.e. x in Omega and all xi, eta in R^n: A(x)xi.xi >= lambda|xi|^2 and |A(x)xi.eta| <= Lambda|xi||eta|; one normally also assumes b, c in L^infinity(Omega). Only the symmetric part of A enters the ellipticity condition. Sign convention: with the leading minus sign, L = -Laplacian when A = I, b = 0, c = 0, so a subsolution (Lu <= 0) generalizes a subharmonic function, and the favorable sign of the zeroth-order coefficient is c >= 0. The ratio Lambda/lambda is the ellipticity ratio; the constants in the De Giorgi-Nash-Moser theory depend only on n and Lambda/lambda. For u in H^1_loc the expression Lu is defined only weakly (in the sense of distributions); no differentiability of A is required.
Omega is an open subset of R^n
a^{ij}, b^i, c are real measurable functions on Omega
lambda|xi|^2 <= A(x)xi.xi and |A(x)xi.eta| <= Lambda|xi||eta| for a.e. x and all xi, eta, with 0 < lambda <= Lambda
b, c in L^infinity(Omega)

\leqslant\mathrm{tr}(\bm{M}_3-\bm{M}_1).
\]

\mathrm{score}^{\mathrm{norm}}_\alpha(x)>

\]

[Proposition 1 (Deterministic score separation) of arXiv:2604.25470, 'A mathematical analysis of hierarchical Hopfield models'] Fix a target concept $\alpha$. On the event $\mathcal G_\alpha(\delta,\rho)$, one has
	for every competitor $\beta\neq\alpha$,
	\begin{equation}
	H_\alpha(x)-H_\beta(x)
	\ge ((1-\delta)L-t_*^{(\alpha)})-\rho.
	\end{equation}
	In particular, if
	\[
	t_*^{(\alpha)}+\rho < (1-\delta)L,
	\]
	then the winner-take-all decoder selects the correct concept:
	\[
	\widehat\alpha(x)=\alpha.
	\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition 4 of arXiv:2609.02175, '2609.02175'] Let $(M,g)$ be a compact Riemannian manifold with boundary.
	We say that $M$ admits a strictly convex foliation if there exist
	$T>0$ and a smooth function
	\[
	\rho:M\longrightarrow [0,+\infty)
	\]
	such that, for every $t\in[0,T)$, the level set
	\[
	\Sigma_t=\rho^{-1}(t)
	\]
	is a strictly convex hypersurface, $d\rho\neq0$ on $\Sigma_t$,
	$\Sigma_0=\partial M$, and
	\[
	M\setminus\bigcup_{0\leq t<T}\Sigma_t
	\]
	has empty interior.
title: Definition 4 of arXiv:2609.02175

body: [Lemma 4.2 of arXiv:1809.05092, 'Polynomial mixing time of edge flips on quadrangulations'] Let q be random quadrangulation distributed according to the uniform probability measure π on Qn and let ρq be the origin of q; define r(q) = maxv∈V(q) dgr(ρq, v) and S(q) = {v ∈V(q) | dgr(v, ρq) ≥ r(q) −1}. The random variable |S(q)| has exponential tails.
title: Lemma 4.2 of arXiv:1809.05092: Polynomial mixing time of edge flips on quadrangulations

body: [Definition def:free of arXiv:2603.28936, 'Composition of random functions and word reconstruction'] For all $i,j,\ell\geq 0$, we let $\mathfrak{P}^{i,j,\ell}$ be the set of tuples $(\tau,\tau';v,v')$ where $\tau, \tau'\in\mathfrak{P}$, $v$ is a vertex of $\tau$ at height $i$, $v'$ is a vertex of $\tau'$ at height $j$, such that $\tau_v(\ell)\stackrel{pl}{=} \tau'_{v'}(\ell)$. Then we let $\mathcal{F}_\ell(\tau,\tau';v,v'):= V(\tau)\cup V(\tau')\setminus V(\tau'_{v'}(\ell-1))$ be the set of \emph{free vertices}, and $f_\ell(\tau,\tau';v,v'):= |\mathcal{F}_\ell(\tau,\tau';v,v')|$ be their number.
title: Free vertices

[Theorem 4 of arXiv:2605.27742, 'Multidimensional Stein's method for asymptotic independence with invariant measures of dif'] Assume Conditions~\ref{cdn1} and \ref{cdn2}. Let $X$ be a $(l,u)$-valued real random
	variable and $Y = (Y_1, \ldots, Y_d)$ a real random vector such that both $X$ and $Y$
	belong to $\mathbb{D}^{1,2}$ and $\mathbf{E}[X] = m$. Then
	\begin{eqnarray}
		&&d_{\mathrm{W}}\!\left(\mathbf{P}_{(X,Y)},\, \mu \otimes \mathbf{P}_Y\right)\\
	&&	\leqslant \|S\|_{\infty}\,
		\mathbf{E}\!\left[\left|\frac{1}{2}a(X)
		- \left\langle \mathrm{D}(-L)^{-1}X,\, \mathrm{D}X\right\rangle\right|\right]
		+ \frac{2}{a(\mu_m)\,p(\mu_m)}
		\sum_{j=1}^d \mathbf{E}\!\left[\left|
		\left\langle \mathrm{D}(-L)^{-1}X,\, \mathrm{D}Y_j\right\rangle\right|\right],\nonumber
	\end{eqnarray}
	where $S$ is defined in Lemma~\ref{Lem:IngS}. If moreover $X$ and $Y$ belong to
	$\mathbb{D}^{1,4}$, then
	\begin{multline}
		d_{\mathrm{W}}\!\left(\mathbf{P}_{(X,Y)},\, \mu \otimes \mathbf{P}_Y\right) \\
		\leqslant \|S\|_{\infty}\,
		\mathbf{E}\!\left[\left(\frac{1}{2}a(X)
		- \left\langle \mathrm{D}(-L)^{-1}X,\,\mathrm{D}X\right\rangle\right)^2
		\right]^{1/2}
		+ \frac{2}{a(\mu_m)\,p(\mu_m)}
		\sum_{j=1}^d \mathbf{E}\!\left[
		\left\langle \mathrm{D}(-L)^{-1}X,\,\mathrm{D}Y_j\right\rangle^2

	\end{multline} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: In differential geometry, the Ricci curvature tensor, named after Gregorio Ricci-Curbastro, measures how a curved space locally differs from flat space by tracking how nearby geodesics spread apart or converge. Formally, it is a symmetric rank-two tensor obtained by taking a trace of the Riemann curvature tensor of a Riemannian or pseudo-Riemannian metric. In Riemannian geometry, the Ricci curvature in a given tangent direction may be interpreted as an average of the sectional curvatures of planes containing that direction. A further trace of the Ricci curvature yields the scalar curvature.
title: Ricci curvature

[Corollary cor:polytope-tolerant-testing of arXiv:2606.19763, 'Optimal Sparsification of Gaussian Processes'] Let $r\geq1$ and let $0\leq\eps_1<\eps_2<1$.
	Put
	\[
		\Delta := \eps_2-\eps_1
		\qquad\text{and}\qquad
		k := \alpha(r,\Delta/4)\,.
	\]
	There is a black-box query algorithm which makes $k^{\poly(\log k,1/\Delta)} = 2^{\poly(r,1/\Delta)}$ queries to an unknown target function $f:\R^n\to\zo$, and with probability at least $9/10$ has the following guarantee:
	\begin{itemize}
		\item If $\mathrm{OPT}_r(f)\leq \eps_1$, then it outputs ``accept.''
		\item If $\mathrm{OPT}_r(f)\geq \eps_2$, then it outputs ``reject.''
	\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Tolerant testing

body:
Fix a finite alphabet Sigma, block length n, message u, and a keyed randomized code with key K and encoder output X in Sigma^n. Suppose its decoding failure is at most a for every randomized channel C, acting on the input word alone, such that d_H(x,C(x))<=p*n almost surely for every x in Sigma^n. Let E be another randomized channel Sigma^n->Sigma^n, independent of K except through its input, and suppose P(d_H(X,E(X))>p*n)<=delta under the key, encoder and channel randomness. Then the decoding failure under E is at most a+delta. In particular robustness persists if a and delta are negligible in the security parameter. If the robustness premise is restricted to efficiently sampleable channels, also assume E and the budget comparison are polynomial-time computable; the clipping preserves that property.
Robustness to every almost-sure p-substitution-bounded channel in the relevant class.
E sees the word and its own randomness, with no additional secret-key side information.
The high-probability budget is averaged over the same key/encoder/channel experiment as the decoding guarantee.

[Theorem 2 of arXiv:2607.09246, 'Scaling limit of 1+1 dimensional directed polymer with power-law tail and spatial correlat'] Assume that conditions \textbf{(A)} and \textbf{(B)} hold. Let the tail exponent satisfy $\alpha \in (2, \frac{6}{3-2r}]$ and the sequence of inverse temperatures chosen as $\beta_N = \beta l(N^{3/2})^{-1}$. When the scaling $\beta_N N^{H/2} \to 0$ as $N \to \infty$ , then the normalized fluctuation of the log-partition function converges in distribution to a centered Gaussian distribution:
$$
    \frac{1}{\beta_N N^{H/2}} \left( \ln Z_N(\beta_N; \omega) - N \sum_{j=2}^{p'} \frac{\beta_N^j}{j!} \mathbb{E}_{\mathbb{Q}}[\bar{\xi}^j] \sum_{y=-\infty}^{\infty} \psi_y^j \right)  \stackrel{D}{\longrightarrow} \mathcal{N}(0, \sigma_H^2),
$$
where \(p'\) is any fixed integer satisfying
\[
        1\le p'<\alpha,
        \qquad\text{and}\quad
        \frac{N\beta_N^{p'+1}}{\beta_NN^{H/2}}\longrightarrow0 ~\text{as}~N\to\infty.
\]
The variance $\sigma_H^2$ is given by the integral:
$$
    \sigma_H^2 = 2H(2H-1) \int_0^1 \int_{\mathbb{R}^2} \rho(t,x)\rho(t,y)|x-y|^{2H-2} \,dx \,dy \,dt.
$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 2 of arXiv:2607.09246

[Theorem of arXiv:2411.12522, 'Canonical insurance models: stochastic equations and comparison theorems'] Let  $(V^i)$ and  $(\bar V^i)$  be the state-wise prospective reserves of canonical insurance models $(\alpha, \Lambda, \Phi, B, b)$ and $(\bar \alpha, \bar \Lambda, \bar \Phi, B, b)$, where on each compact interval the differences {$\bar\Lambda - \Lambda$ shall} have finite variation. Let $ V :=\sum_i I^i V^i $, and let $R^{ij} := b^{ij} + V^j - V^i$.
\begin{itemize}
	\item[(a)]  \textbf{Pessimistic actuarial  basis:} If the differences $\bar\Lambda - \Lambda$ and $\bar\Phi - \Phi$ satisfy  
	\begin{align*}
		\mathds{1}_{\{ R^{ij}(t) \geq 0\}} \big( \bar \Lambda^{ij}-\Lambda^{ij}\big) (\mathrm{d} t) &\geq 	0,\\
		\mathds{1}_{\{ R^{ij}(t) \leq 0\}}  \big( \bar \Lambda^{ij}-\Lambda^{ij}\big) (\mathrm{d} t)&\leq 	0,\\
		\mathds{1}_{\{ V^i(t) \geq 0\}}  \big( \bar \Phi^i  -\Phi^i  \big)(\mathrm{d} t) &\leq 	0,\\
		\mathds{1}_{\{V^i(t) \leq 0\}}  \big( \bar \Phi^i  -\Phi^i  \big) (\mathrm{d} t)&\geq 	0
	\end{align*}
	 for    $t \geq 0$, $i,j \in \mathcal{Z}$, $i\neq j$, then it  holds that 
	$$ \bar V^i(t) \geq  V^i(t),  \quad t \geq 0, \, i \in \mathcal{Z}.$$ 
		
	\item[(b)] \textbf{Optimistic actuarial basis:} If the differences $\bar\Lambda - \Lambda$ and $\bar\Phi - \Phi$ satisfy 
\begin{align*}
	\mathds{1}_{\{ R^{ij}(t) \geq 0\}} \big( \bar \Lambda^{ij}-\Lambda^{ij}\big)(\mathrm{d} t) &\leq 	0,\\
	\mathds{1}_{\{ R^{ij}(t) \leq 0\}}  \big( \bar \Lambda^{ij}-\Lambda^{ij}\big)(\mathrm{d} t) &\geq 	0,\\
	\mathds{1}_{\{ V^i(t) \geq 0\}}  \big( \bar \Phi^i -\Phi^i  \big)(\mathrm{d} t) &\geq 	0,\\
	\mathds{1}_{\{V^i(t) \leq 0\}}  \big( \bar \Phi^i  -\Phi^i  \big)(\mathrm{d} t)  &\leq 	0
\end{align*}
for 	 $t \geq 0$, $i,j \in \mathcal{Z}$, $i\neq j$, then it holds that 
$$ \bar V^i(t) \leq  V^i(t),  \quad t \geq 0, \, i \in \mathcal{Z}.$$  	
\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Unnumbered theorem of arXiv:2411.12522, 'Canonical insurance models: stochastic equations and compari'

body:
Let Omega in R^n be open. H^1_0(Omega) = W^{1,2}_0(Omega) is the closure of C_c^infinity(Omega) in the norm ||u||_{H^1} = (||u||_{L^2}^2 + ||grad u||_{L^2}^2)^{1/2}; W^{1,p}_0(Omega) is the W^{1,p}-closure, 1 <= p < infinity. If Omega is bounded, the Poincare inequality ||u||_{L^2(Omega)} <= diam(Omega) ||grad u||_{L^2(Omega)} holds for u in H^1_0(Omega), so ||grad u||_{L^2} is an equivalent norm on H^1_0(Omega); and the embedding H^1_0(Omega) into L^2(Omega) is compact (Rellich), with no boundary regularity needed. If Omega is bounded with C^1 boundary there is a bounded trace operator T from W^{1,p}(Omega) to L^p(boundary), 1 <= p < infinity, with Tu = restriction of u for u in W^{1,p} continuous up to the boundary, and W^{1,p}_0(Omega) = kernel of T. Lattice facts: for u in H^1(Omega) and real k, (u - k)^+ is in H^1_loc(Omega) (in H^1(Omega) when k >= 0 or Omega is bounded) with grad (u - k)^+ = 1_{u > k} grad u a.e.; in particular grad u = 0 a.e. on every level set {u = k}. For bounded Omega and u in H^1(Omega) one says u <= k on the boundary (in the H^1 sense) if (u - k)^+ is in H^1_0(Omega), and defines sup over the boundary of u as inf{k real : (u - k)^+ in H^1_0(Omega)}; u = g on the boundary means u - g in H^1_0(Omega). These notions need no regularity of the boundary.
Omega open in R^n; bounded for the Poincare inequality, Rellich compactness and the boundary-inequality notion
C^1 boundary for the trace theorem
1 <= p < infinity for W^{1,p}_0 and the trace
title: Sobolev Space H^1_0 and Boundary Values in the Sobolev Sense

[Cor 18 of arXiv:2607.13849, 'Rearranged Stochastic Heat Equation with an Entropy Gradient Structure'] For $\delta >0$, 
let $(X_t, \mathscr{J}_t)_{0 \le t \le T}$ be a weak limit in $\mathcal{C}([0,T], \mathcal{H}^{-1}_{\mathrm{Sym}}(\mathbb{S})\times \mathcal{H}^{-(3+\delta)}_{\mathrm{Sym}}(\mathbb{S}))$  of the sequence of pair processes $\{(X_t^{(h)},\mathscr{J}_t(X^{(h)}))_{0 \le t \le T}\}_{{h \in T/{\mathbb N}^*}}$ when $h\searrow 0$. 
Then, for any $t\in [0,T]$,
\begin{align*}
\frac{1}{2}\mathbb{E}\int_0^T\int_{\mathbb{S}}\frac{1}{|D_{\mathbf{x}}{X}_{t}(\mathbf{x})|}\mathrm{d}\mathbf{x}\mathrm{d}t \leq C_{(T,\mathbb{E}\|X_0\|_2)},
\end{align*}
where $C_{(T,\mathbb{E}\|X_0\|_2)}$ is a constant only depending on $T,\lambda$ and  
${\mathbb E}[ \| X_0 \|_2]$.
title: Cor 18 of arXiv:2607.13849

    $$

[Theorem thm-limit of arXiv:2507.09922, 'A scaling limit for Vlasov equations with electrostatic fluctuations'] Assume that the initial condition $f_0$ belongs to $(L^1\cap L^3)(\mathbb{T}^3\times \mathbb{R}^3)$ with finite kinetic energy
  $$\mathcal K(f_0)= \int_{\mathbb{T}^3\times \mathbb{R}^3} |v|^2 f_0(x,v)\, dx dv<+\infty. $$
Let $W_N$ be a sequence of smooth noises whose covariance functions $Q_N$ verify the condition (equation condition-covariance of the paper). For any $N\ge 1$, let $f^N$ be a weak solution to the stochastic Vlasov equation
  \begin{equation}
  d f^N + v\cdot\nabla_x f^N\, dt + (E_{\rho^N} + B v\times \bm{e}_3) \cdot\nabla_v f^N \, dt + \sum_k \sigma^N_k \cdot\nabla_v f^N \, d W^k_t = \kappa \Delta_v f^N\, dt
  \end{equation}
with initial condition $f^N_0= f_0$. Then any convergent subsequence of $\{f^N\}_N$ converge weakly, in the topology of $C\big([0,T], H^{-\epsilon }_{x,v, loc} \big)$, to weak solutions of (equation limit-Vlasov of the paper). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Scaling limit

body: In mathematics, especially spectral theory, Weyl's law describes the asymptotic behavior of eigenvalues of the Laplace–Beltrami operator. This description was discovered in 1911 (in the $d=2,3$ case) by Hermann Weyl for eigenvalues for the Laplace–Beltrami operator acting on functions that vanish at the boundary of a bounded domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb {R} ^{d}$. In particular, he proved that the number, $N(\lambda)$, of Dirichlet eigenvalues (counting their multiplicities) less than or equal to $\lambda$ satisfies $$\lim _{\lambda \rightarrow \infty }{\frac {N(\lambda )}{\lambda ^{d/2}}}=(2\pi )^{-d}\omega _{d}\mathrm {vol} (\Omega )$$

[Definition of arXiv:2412.02777, 'How to quantify the coherence of a set of beliefs'] A \textit{positive spanning set} of a set $S\subseteq \mathbb{R}^N$ is a subset $B\subseteq S$ with the property that for any $\boldsymbol s \in S$, there exist coefficients $c_{\boldsymbol b}\in \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ for each $\boldsymbol b \in B$ where only a finite number of $c_{\boldsymbol b}$ are non-zero and
    $$\boldsymbol s = \sum_{\boldsymbol b \in B} c_{\boldsymbol b}\boldsymbol b.$$

DRAFT; independent referee pending. Let sigma>0 and W_0=0 be a real continuous adapted chordal Loewner driver, with dg_t=2/(g_t-W_t)dt. If exp(sigma(Log g'_t(z)-Log(g_t(z)-W_t))) is a full complex continuous local martingale in the same usual filtration for every z=im, m a positive integer, before swallowing, then W has bracket 8t/(1+sigma), zero drift, and W/sqrt(8/(1+sigma)) is Brownian motion. Recover the semimartingale premise from a local inverse of the nonzero observable; Ito's imaginary finite-variation equation removes signed drift. This conditional route does not establish discrete observable convergence.
Consistent continuous logarithms
Both real and imaginary parts are local martingales
No random time-dependent normalization
title: DRAFT: complex observable identifies the Loewner driver

            \rho > 0 \quad \text{and}\quad \ell < 2\alpha.

    \item If $\beta = 2$ and $\gamma \in (0,1]$, then,~(equation E:fde of the paper) has a
          random field solution if both conditions in~(equation E:main of the paper) hold.

  \end{enumerate}

[Theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] The following objects are counted by the same numbers $C_k$, called Catalan numbers, given by $C_0=C_1=1$ and $C_{k+1}=\sum_{a+b=k}C_aC_b$:
\begin{enumerate}
\item The length $2k$ loops on $\mathbb N$, based at $0$.

\item The noncrossing pairings of $1,\ldots,2k$.

\item The noncrossing partitions of $1,\ldots,k$.

\item The length $2k$ Dyck paths in the plane.
\end{enumerate}

For each d let B_d be a positive self-adjoint trace-class operator on a closed V_d subset L2(Omega_d,tau_d), extended by zero on V_d-perp, with ordered eigenvalues mu_(d,j)>=0, orthonormal eigenfunctions phi_(d,j), and finite positive T_d=Tr(B_d). Use its canonical positive spectral kernel k_d=sum_j mu_(d,j)phi_(d,j)phi_(d,j)^T. Let N=N(d)->infinity, and let v(d)>=0 be one cutoff sequence. Assume (A1) for every fixed real q>=1 there is C(q) uniform in d such that ||g||_L2q<=C(q)||g||_L2 for every g in span{phi_(d,1),...,phi_(d,v)}; (A2) there are fixed delta2>0,C2<infinity such that N^(2+delta2)Tr(B_(d,>v)^2)<=C2[Tr(B_(d,>v))]^2 eventually; (A3) there are fixed delta3>0,C3<infinity such that N^(1+delta3)||B_d||_op<=C3 T_d eventually. Draw theta_1,...,theta_N independently from tau_d and let Q_ij=k_d(theta_i,theta_j)1_(i!=j). Then there is a fixed delta_prime>0 with E||Q||_op=O(N^(-delta_prime))Tr(B_d). The same cutoff v is used in A1 and A2, and the moment constants are uniform along that cutoff sequence.

[Lemma lem:esp-variance of arXiv:2606.28031, 'Insurance risk models in a heterogeneous time-dependent population: scaling limits and rui'] Assume that $X^{\mathrm c}, X^{\mathrm i}$ and $Y^{\mathrm c}, Y^{\mathrm i}$ have  finite second moments. Then, 
\begin{align*}
&\mathbb{E}[V(t)]=\mathbb{E}[X^{\mathrm c}(1)]\int_0^t\mathbb{E}[F(s)]\,{\mathrm d} s+\mathbb{E}[Y^{\mathrm c}(1)]\int_0^t\mathbb{E}[1-F(s)]\,{\mathrm d} s,\\
&\mathrm{Var}(V(t))=\mathrm{Var}(X^{\mathrm c}(1))\, \int_0^t \mathbb{E}{{\left[F^2(s)\right]}}\,{\mathrm d} s+\mathrm{Var}(Y^{\mathrm c}(1))\,\int_0^t\mathbb{E}\SBRA{{{\left(1-F(s)\right)}}^2}{\mathrm d} s\\
&\hskip 2.5cm+\PAR{\mathbb{E}[X^{\mathrm c}(1)]-\mathbb{E}[Y^{\mathrm c}(1)]}^2\mathrm{Var}\PAR{\int_0^t F(s)\,{\mathrm d} s},
\\
&\mathbb{E}[W(t)]=\mathbb{E}[X^{\mathrm i}(1)]\int_0^t\mathbb{E}[I(s)]{\mathrm d} s+\mathbb{E}[Y^{\mathrm i}(1)]\int_0^t\mathbb{E}[N-I(s)]\,{\mathrm d} s,\\
&\mathrm{Var}(W(t))=
\mathrm{Var}(X^{\mathrm i}(1))\,\int_0^t \mathbb{E}{{\left[I(s)\right]}}\,{\mathrm d} s+\mathrm{Var}(Y^{\mathrm i}(1))\,\int_0^t\mathbb{E}{{\left[N-I(s)\right]}}\,{\mathrm d} s,\\
&\hskip 2.5cm+\PAR{\mathbb{E}[X^{\mathrm i}(1)]-\mathbb{E}[Y^{\mathrm i}(1)]}^2\mathrm{Var}\PAR{\int_0^tI(s)\,{\mathrm d} s}.
\end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition 39 of arXiv:2608.27630, 'Oriented planar maps and \\ annular mating of trees'] Under the finite measure $\MA^{1, 1\dagger}(a,b)$, we have the following description of the conditional law of $\eta$ and $\wt\eta$ given $\phi$.
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
    \item Given $\phi$ and $\eta$, the conditional law of $(y,\wt\eta)$ is as follows. The distribution of $y\in  C_\tau$ is the probability measure proportional to the LQG length measure with respect to $\phi$; given $y$, $\wt\eta$  has the law as      $\SLE_\kappa(-\frac{\kappa}{2},\kappa-2,-\frac{\kappa}{2};\frac{\kappa}{2}-2)$ in $\cA_\tau\backslash\eta$ from $y$ and targeted at $(-i)^+$, with  the force points   located at $y^-$, the endpoint of $\eta$, the leftmost point of $\eta\cap C_0$ and $y^+$, respectively. 
    \item  Conditioned on $(y,\wt\eta)$ and $\phi$, $\eta$ has the law as   $\SLE_\kappa(-\frac{\kappa}{2},\kappa-2,-\frac{\kappa}{2};\frac{\kappa}{2}-2)$ in $\cA_\tau\backslash\wt\eta$ from $-i$ and targeted at $y^+$, with the force points located at $(-i)^-$, the endpoint of $\wt\eta$, the the leftmost point of $\wt\eta\cap C_\tau$ and $(-i)^+$, respectively.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: [Abstract of arXiv:2609.02590, 'Directional Optimal Sub-Gamma Scales for Infinitely Divisible Laws'] Fixing the quadratic proxy in a sub-gamma bound at the true variance leaves a scale to optimize, and a two-sided infinitely divisible law generally requires different scales in the two directions. For a centered law with finite nonzero variance, we normalize its Kolmogorov canonical measure and multiply the resulting variable by an independent $\operatorname{Beta}(1,2)$ variable. The signed remainder obtained in this way gives exact variational formulas for the right and left scales. We prove that a directional scale vanishes exactly when the L\'evy measure has no jumps in that direction, establish reflection, scaling, convolution, L\'evy-time, and opposite-jump perturbation rules, and recover the L\'evy triplet from the remainder law. The formulas give the two Gamma scales for bilateral Gamma laws and, for centered Skellam laws, the exact transition points $p_{\pm}=(2\pm\sqrt{3})/4$ between local and interior control; when positive jumps are rare, the right scale is asymptotic to $1/\log(1/p)$. The pair therefore records jump direction and the mechanism that controls the variance-exact sub-gamma pole.
title: Abstract of arXiv:2609.02590: Directional Optimal Sub-Gamma Scales for Infinitely Divisible Laws

[Theorem eq:cluster-lower-bound-alt of arXiv:2601.07808, 'Supercritical long-range percolation on graphs of polynomial growth: the truncated one-arm'] \label[theorem]{thm:cluster_lower_bound}
    Let $G$ be a transitive graph of polynomial growth with $d \geq 2$, and suppose that $J : V \times V \to \mathbf{R}_+$ is a transitive kernel with $J(x,y) = \Theta(d_G(x,y)^{-d \alpha})$ with $\alpha > 1$.
    
    Let $\beta > \beta_c$ be sufficiently large.
    
    Let $\delta > 0$ and $c>0$ be such that $\# S(r) \leq c r^{d - \delta}$ for all $r \in \mathbf{N}$.
    
    Then there exists $A = A(\beta,G,J) > 0$ such that for all $k \in \mathbf{N}$
    
    \begin{equation}
    
        \exp
        \left(
            - 
            A  
            k^{
                \max(
                    2-\alpha, 
                    (d-1)/d
                ) 
                +
                (1-\delta)/d
            } 
            (\log r)^{
                \mathbf{1}
                \left(
                    \alpha=1+1/d
                \right)
            }
        \right)
        \leq 
        \mathbf{P}_{\beta}
        \left(
            k 
            < 
            \# K 
            < 
            \infty
        \right).
    \end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem eq:cluster-lower-bound-alt of arXiv:2601.07808

[Definition of arXiv:2608.26564, 'Real ideal points, Conway spheres, and left-orderable Dehn fillings'] Let $M$ be a compact orientable 3-manifold, and let $\mathcal{C} \subset X(M)$ be an irreducible algebraic curve. Let $\widetilde{\mathcal{C}}$ be the smooth projective model of $\mathcal{C}$, and let $x \in \widetilde{\mathcal{C}} \setminus \mathcal{C}$ be an ideal point. Let $H \subset \pi_1(M)$ be a finitely generated subgroup, and let $r: X(M) 	o X(H)$ be the restriction map. Following Tillmann [tillmann], we say that $x$ \emph{has a limiting character on $H$} if the induced rational map $\widetilde{\mathcal{C}} 	o X(H)$ is defined at $x$. Since the character ring of the finitely generated group $H$ is generated by finitely many trace functions, this is equivalent to requiring that every $I_\gamma$, $\gamma \in H$, have a finite value at $x$. In this case, the value $\chi_{x, H} \in X(H)$ is called the \emph{limiting character of $x$ on $H$}. Equivalently, if $
u: (\Delta, 0) 	o (\widetilde{\mathcal{C}}, x)$ is a local analytic parametrization with $
u(0) = x$ and $
u(t) \in \mathcal{C}$ for $t 
eq 0$, then the limiting character on $H$ is the character

	\chi_{x, H}(\gamma) = \lim_{t 	o 0}I_\gamma(
u(t)) \ \ \ \ \ \gamma \in H
\end{equation*}

Let L be a finite lattice with bottom 0 != top 1. A cross-cut is an antichain C, containing neither 0 nor 1, that meets every maximal chain from 0 to 1. Call S inside C spanning when its join is 1 and its meet is 0, and let q_k be the number of spanning k-subsets. Then mu(0, 1) = sum_{k >= 2} (-1)^k q_k (G.-C. Rota, 1964). If 1 does not cover 0, the atoms form a cross-cut and mu(0, 1) = sum over sets S of atoms with join 1 of (-1)^|S|. The chain-meeting condition is needed: in the Boolean lattice of subsets of {1, 2}, the antichain {{1}} misses the chain empty < {2} < {1, 2}, has no spanning subset, and gives 0 while mu = 1.
L a finite lattice with 0 != 1

body:
[Proposition 25 (Maximum principle for dissipated-energy Einstein--Navier--Stokes flows) of arXiv:2608.31171, '\bf Finite-energy spacetimes with torus symmetry. \\ \Large Cauchy stability of Einstein--'] Fix a Navier--Stokes triple $(\mathscr F,\chi,\mathscr B)$ that is admissible (\autoref{def-pot-admissible-triple}) and torus-adapted (\autoref{def-NS-torus-adapted}). Let $(\Phi,\Psi,\zeta)$ be a sufficiently regular dissipated-energy Einstein--Navier--Stokes areal flow on $[t_0,t_1]\times\Tbb^3$, and assume that the density $\mu>0$ is positive. Then the range of the function $\Sbb^1\ni x\mapsto\bigl(\Gammaunpar_\chi(t,x),\Gammazero(t,x)\bigr)$ is a subset of~$\RR^4$ that does not depend on areal time $t\in [t_0,t_1]$.  In particular, for $t\in[t_0,t_1]$ and $m=2,3$, one has 
\be

\aligned \inf_{\Sbb^1}\Gammaun_m^\chi(t_0,\cdot) & \leq\Gammaun_m^\chi(t,x)\leq\sup_{\Sbb^1}\Gammaun_m^\chi(t_0,\cdot), \\
\inf_{\Sbb^1}\Gammazero_m(t_0,\cdot) & \leq\Gammazero_m(t,x)\leq\sup_{\Sbb^1}\Gammazero_m(t_0,\cdot).\endaligned
\ee
The second line also holds at vacuum.
At vacuum, the first line is understood as the statement that if $C_1\rho_\chi\leq 2T_\chi^{0m} \leq C_2 \rho_\chi$ for some $C_1,C_2\in\RR$ at initial time then this inequality holds for all times.
The convex hull of the range of $\Gammaunpar_\chi$ is thus preserved in time, without density assumption. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Maximum principle for dissipated-energy Einstein--Navier--Stokes flows

let \(\lambda\in(0,\lambda_{\max}^{\mathrm{tRLMC}}].\)
There holds

body: Within a BSS-type multiscale variance-halving program on Z^2 (hypothesis set: concentration envelope H1a at scale Q, anti-concentration floor H4, chaos input CH), write Q_s ~ s^alpha and the model's TRUE variance Var(X_s) ~ s^{2 chi}. Then rho_s = Q_s^2/Var(X_s) ~ s^{2(alpha-chi)} and the halving step demands chaos strength eps <~ s^{-4(alpha-chi)}. Constant-strength chaos - the only strength BSS-type constructions deliver - therefore requires alpha <= chi, while H1a (true concentration at scale Q) forces alpha >= chi: within the hypothesis set alpha = chi EXACTLY. The envelope exponent is fixed by nature, not by the theorem being chased: D in the halving lemma is the true variance (a standing assumption, not a free parameter), and the target rate n^{1-eps} is the OUTPUT of telescoping, never an input to any rung. Independent cross-check: reading D as inductive would let Efron-Stein plus one hypothesis alone deliver the conclusion with the whole apparatus idle. Refereed 2026-08-09 (two independent kills of the inductive reading). Provenance: campaign CRUX sections 2, 3b (resolved banner), 7; referee verdict iter 68.
title: Envelope-variance pinning in BSS-type multiscale FPP programs (conditional)

body:
[Theorem thm:rank-frequency of arXiv:2609.01690, 'Iterated-sumset spectra: The complete exponent law and its rank geometry'] Fix $h\geq2$ and $k\geq3$.  For every $n\in\mathcal R(h,k)$, the function
\[
 F^{(k)}_{h,n}(q)=
 \#\left\{A\in\binom{[q]}k:|hA|=n\right\}
\]
is a quasipolynomial in $q-1$ (and hence in $q$).  Its degree is exactly
\[
 \deg F^{(k)}_{h,n}=k-r_{h,k}(n).
\]
In particular, there is an explicitly computable positive rational number
$c_{h,k,n}$ such that
\begin{equation}
 F^{(k)}_{h,n}(q)
 =c_{h,k,n}q^{k-r_{h,k}(n)}
  +O_{h,k}\!\left(q^{k-r_{h,k}(n)-1}\right).
\end{equation}
The possible frequency exponents therefore belong to
$\{2,3,\ldots,k\}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Complete rank--frequency stratification
The existence of on/off super Brownian motion (ooSBM), Blath and Jacobi \cite{blath2023off}

$$(\varepsilon_1 \varepsilon_2)^{-1/8}\mathbb{P}(E_{\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2}^{\rm m^{th}}(z_1, z_2))+

{\theta_2(q^{1/4})\sqrt{|\log q|}}\sum\limits_{\substack{|n| \geq m-1 \\ n = m \mod 2}}2^{m-1}(-1)^{\frac{n-m}{2}}\left( \binom{\frac{n+m}{2}}{\frac{n-m}{2}}+\binom{\frac{n+m}{2}-1}{\frac{n-m}{2}-1}\right)\hat q^{2n^2},
$$
where $\hat q$ is the complementary nome to nome $q$,
which in turn, by Lemma (lem:parametr of the paper),

[Prop 10 of arXiv:2605.23659, '2605.23659'] Let \(i \in I\) and \(f(i) = j\).
  Suppose
  \[
  \Psi^{(i)}(q) \sim c q^{\alpha}K(q) \quad \text{and} \quad 
  \psi^{(j)}(q) \sim c' q^{\beta}H(q) \quad (q \to 0)
  \]
  for \(c \geq 0\), \(c' > 0\), \(\alpha,\beta \in [0,1]\), and slowly varying functions \(K,H\) at \(0\).
  Then we have
  \begin{align}    
  \Psi^{\ast,(i)}(q) \sim C q^{\alpha \beta}G(q) \quad (q \to 0), 
  \end{align}
  where 
  \[
  C := c(c')^{\alpha} \quad \text{and} \quad G(q) := H(q)^{\alpha}K(q^{\beta}H(q)).
  \]
  In particular, \(G\) is slowly varying at \(0\), and whenever \(c > 0\), the function \(\Psi^{\ast,(i)}\) is regularly varying at \(0\) with exponent \(\alpha\beta\).

body:
[Perron 1 of arXiv:2606.24584, '2606.24584'] Let $A \in M_n$, $n \geq 2$, be irreducible with nonnegative entries. Then the following hold.
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item There exists a  number $\mu > 0$, called the Perron--Frobenius eigenvalue of $A$, such that $\mu$ is a simple eigenvalue of $A$ and any other eigenvalue $\lambda$ of $A$ verifies $|\lambda| \leq \mu$. Thus $\rho(A)=\mu$.

\item The Perron–Frobenius eigenvalue of $A$ fulfils the row-sum inequalities
\begin{equation}
\min_{1\leq i \leq n} \sum_{j=1}^{n} a_{ij} \leq \mu \leq  \max_{1\leq i \leq n} \sum_{j=1}^{n} a_{ij}.
\end{equation}

\item The matrix $A$ is similar to $e^{2\pi i /h} A$ and the spectrum of $A$ is invariant under multiplication by $e^{2\pi i /h}$.

\item If $h>1$, there exists a permutation matrix $P$ such that
\begin{equation}
            P^{\intercal}AP =
            \begin{bmatrix}
        0&\!\!\!\smash{A_{{1,2}}}&\!\!\!0&\!\!\!\cdots&\!\!0 \\
        0&\!\!\!0&\!\!\!\smash{A_{{2,3}}}&\!\!\!\cdots&\!\!0 \\[-4pt]
        \vdots&\!\!\!\vdots&\!\!\!\vdots&\!\!\!\ddots&\!\!\vdots \\
        0&\!\!\!0&\!\!\!0&\!\!\!\cdots&\!\!\smash{A_{{h-1,h}}} \\
        \smash{A_{{h,1}}}&\!\!\!0&\!\!\!0&\!\!\!\cdots&\!\!0
\end{bmatrix},
\end{equation}
where the non-zero blocks are square matrices.

\item If $h=1$, then the limit $$\lim_{m \to \infty} \frac{A^m}{\mu^m}$$ exists. This limit is called the \emph{Perron projection} of $A$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition prop:subcritical of arXiv:2604.13968, 'Divisible sandpiles via random walks in random scenery'] Let~$G = (V,E)$ be an infinite, locally finite, connected graph with
		degree bounded by~$d$ and satisfying the spectral dimension bound~(equation eq:return-bound of the paper) for some $d_s>0$ and $A<\infty$.
		Let $(\xi(v))_{v\in V}$ be i.i.d.\ and independent of the walk with
		$\mathbb{E}[\xi] \in [-\infty, 0)$ and $\mathbb{E}[(\xi^+)^p]<\infty$ for some $p>1+2/d_s$.
		Then for every $q\in[1,(p-1)(d_s/2\wedge 1))$,
		\[
		\sup_{x\in V}\mathbb{E}_x\bigl[(\sup_n S_n)^q\bigr]<\infty\,.
		\]
		In particular, if $(p-1)(d_s/2\wedge 1)> 1$---which holds whenever $d_s<2$ (under the stated moment condition) or $d_s\geq 2$ and $p> 2$---then $\sup_\tau\mathbb{E}_x[S_\tau\mid\xi]<\infty$ almost surely.

[Proposition 3 of arXiv:2608.25221, 'Representing MAX functions using two-hidden-layer ReLU networks'] For any collection of real numbers $\alpha_{\mathcal{O}} \in \R$ indexed by the orbits $\mathcal{O}\in \mathcal{P}/\Sigma_N$, there exists an index set $\mathcal{T}$ indexing a set of ordered pairs $\{(\eta^T_L, \eta^T_R): T \in \mathcal{T}\}$ of vectors in $\{y \in \Z^N_+: \|y\|_1 = k\}$ and a set of real numbers $\{c_T\in \R: T \in \mathcal{T}\}$, such that 
    $$\sum_{\mathcal{O}\in \mathcal{P}/\Sigma_N}\alpha_{\mathcal{O}}G_{\mathcal{O}}(x) = \sum_{T \in \mathcal{T}}c_T \max\{\langle \eta^T_L, x\rangle, \langle \eta^T_R, x\rangle\}\qquad \forall x \in \mathcal{C}.$$
\medskip

    Moreover, each $c_T$ is given by a linear combination of the $\alpha_{\mathcal{O}}$ coefficients. Therefore, there exists a matrix $M \in \R^{\mathcal{T}\times (\mathcal{P}/\Sigma_N)}$ such that \begin{equation}M\alpha = c,\end{equation} where $\alpha \in \R^\mathcal{P}$ is obtained by collecting all the $\alpha_P, P\in \mathcal{P}$ into a vector, and $c \in \R^\mathcal{T}$ is obtained from $c_T, T \in \mathcal{T}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Thm main of arXiv:2412.09535, 'Local limit theorem for joint subgraph counts'] Let $p \in (\lambda, 1-\lambda)$ and let $\mathcal{H}$ be a downwards closed set of nonisomorphic connected graphs with at least two vertices (in the sense of (def:downwards-closed of the paper)). Then, for every $\eps > 0$ and permissible $(y_H)_{H \in \mathcal{H}}$ (in the sense of (def:permissible of the paper)) we have
\[\abs*{\setp[\gamma_{H} = y_H\;\forall H\in \mathcal{H}] \prod_{H \in \mathcal{H}} \paren*{(p(1-p))^{e(H)/2}\sigma_{H}} - \prod_{H \in \mathcal{H}} \mathcal{N}(y_H/\sigma_{H})} \lsim_{ \mathcal{H}, \lambda, \eps} n^{-1/2+\eps},\]
where $\sigma_{H}^2 = \Var[\gamma_{H}]$ and $\mathcal{N}(z) = (2\pi)^{-1/2} e^{-z^2/2}$ is the standard normal probability distribution function. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Corollary 12 (leave probability and exit distribution) of arXiv:2605.13648, 'Sticky CIR process with potential: invariant measure and exact sampling'] \label[corollary]{cor:leave-zero}
  Let $T_\alpha\sim\operatorname{Exp}(\alpha)$ be independent of the sticky process $u$, with $u_0=0$.
  The probability that $u_{T_\alpha}\neq 0$  is
  \[
    p_{\mathrm{leave}}
    = \frac{\mu}{\mu+\Phi},
    \qquad
    \Phi = \frac{1}{G_\alpha(0,0)},
  \]
  where $G_\alpha$ is the reflecting resolvent kernel of \cref{green-function}.
  Conditional on $u_{T_\alpha}\neq 0$, the exit position is drawn from
  the density
  \begin{equation}
    \nu_\alpha(dy) = Z_\nu^{-1}\,U(a,b,z_y)\,m'(y)\,dy,
    \qquad Z_\nu = |\mathcal{W}|/\alpha.
  \end{equation}

[Cor 4 of arXiv:2605.26669, '2605.26669'] Building on Theorem \ref{thm2}, we establish that the sequence $(Z_n)_{n\ge 0}$, defined in (\ref{Z-1}), fulfills the criteria outlined in  Theorem 3.1 of Shi et al. \cite{S-M-1}. As a result, we can derive the law of the iterated logarithm for $(Z_n)_{n\ge 0}$. Under the condition that $\frac{-b p}{(a+b)p+c(1-p)}<-\frac{1}{2}$, the following limit holds
$$
\limsup_{n\rightarrow \infty} \left(\frac{n}{2 \log \log n}\right)^{1/2} \left(Z_{n+1}-\frac{1}{2}\right)=\frac{\sigma}{(2 \alpha +1)^{\frac{1}{2}}},
$$
where $\alpha:=\frac{b p}{(a+b)p+c(1-p)}-1$,  and
$
\sigma^2:=\frac{p(a-b)^2+c^2(1-p)}{4\big((a+b)p+c(1-p)\big)^2}.
$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Cor 4 of arXiv:2605.26669

body:
[Thm 3 of arXiv:2607.03360, 'Smoluchowski-Kramers Approximation Meets Khasminskii Averaging Principles in Nonequilibriu'] Suppose the coefficient $G:=gg^\top/2$ is non-degenerate in $y$ uniformly with respect to $x$ and the drift $f$ satisfies the weak recurrence condition 
\bea\ad
\lim_{|y| \to \infty} \sup_{x\in \rr^{d_1}} \bqv{y,f(x,y)}=-\infty.
\eea 
Assume that $f,g\in C_b^{\vartheta, \dl}$ with $0< \dl \leq 1$ and $\vartheta \geq 0$. Then for every $Z\in C_p^{\vartheta, \dl}$ satisfying \eqref{cen-cond}, there exists a unique solution $u\in C_p^{\vartheta,2+\dl}$ to Poisson equation \eqref{Poi-eq} satisfying \eqref{cen-cond} given by 
\bea\ad 
u(x, y)= \int_0^\infty \EE Z(x, y_t^x)dt.
\eea
Moreover, there exists a constant $\wdh n>0$ such that
\begin{itemize}
\item[(i)] (Case $\vartheta=0$) for any $x\in \rr^{d_1}$ and $y\in \rr^{d_2}$,
\beq{u-der-y}
|u(x, y)|+|\nabla_y u(x, y)|+ |\nabla_y^2 u(x, y)| \leq C_0 (1+|y|^{\wdh n}),
\eeq
where $C_0> 0$ depends only on $d_1, d_2$ and $\|f\|_{C_b^{0,\dl}}$, $\|g\|_{C_b^{0,\dl}}$ and $[Z]_{C_p^{0,\dl}}$;
\item[(ii)] (Case $\vartheta>0$) for any $y \in \rr^{d_2}$,
\bea
\|u(\cdot,y)\|_{C_b^{\vartheta}} \leq C_0 C_\vartheta (1+|y|^{\wdh n}),
\eea
where $C_\vartheta>0$ depends on $d_1, d_2$ and $\|f\|_{C_b^{\vartheta,\dl}}$, $\|g\|_{C_b^{\vartheta,\dl}}$ and $[Z]_{C_p^{\vartheta,\dl}}$.
\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Thm 3 of arXiv:2607.03360

[Proposition 22 (Three-point argument, Steps 5.a--c)) of arXiv:2605.28677, 'Weak universality for stochastic reaction-diffusion models\\ with long-range correlated no'] Let $[\beta]\geq0$ and assume 
that \eqref{est_Pi} holds for $\Pi_{x\beta'}$ for all populated $\beta'\preceq\beta$,

Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item there exist $\pi^{(\n)}_{xy\beta}$ for $|\n|<|\beta|$ such that 

\begin{equation}
(\Gamma_{xy}\Pi_y)_\beta = \Pi_{x\beta} \, ,

and $(\Gamma_{xx})_\beta^\gamma = (\mathrm{id})_\beta^\gamma$ for all $\gamma$, 
provided both hold also for all populated $\beta'\prec\beta$, 
and provided $(\Gamma_{xy}\Pi_y)_{\beta'}=\Pi_{x\beta'}$ holds for all populated $\beta'\prec\beta$,

\item \eqref{est_pin} holds for $\pi^{(\n)}_{xy\beta}$ and thus 
\eqref{est_Gamma} holds for $(\Gamma_{xy})_\beta^\gamma$ for all $\gamma$. 
\end{enumerate}

\[
  P_{X_{\Ind(M)}(G)}(t;\bbk)
  =\sum_{w\in W}
  T_{M|\DesR(w)}(0,1)
  t^{2\ell(w)+r_M(\DesR(w))}.
\]
The identity term is $1$, since the empty matroid has $T(0,1)=1$ and rank zero.

AUTHOR PROOF DRAFT, unaudited; novelty is unestablished. Uniform hard-edge gap for independent shifted real Gaussian rectangular smoothing. If 1+delta<=p/n<=Kappa, ||S||op<=C and 0<t_minus<=t<=t_plus, then with K=max(1,C+8sqrt(t_plus(1+Kappa))), C0=max(1,2sqrt(3/t_minus)) and epsilon=(6 K C0^Kappa)^(-1/delta), P(s_min(S+sqrt(t/n)G)<=epsilon)<=2exp(-n)+2^(-n). Add P(||S||op>C) for an independent random input. Deterministic limiting positive singular laws have a common gap on compact positive heat intervals. Elementary supporting lemma; no novelty or target completion claimed.
Real iid standard Gaussian noise independent of the input.
Aspect ratio bounded away from one and infinity.
Positive compact heat interval; input operator-norm event as stated.

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:d87bbd10a7055b41fd8b18c127a2cbc7713cc1091251a6b2107442c44f67cb1f","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/d8/d87bbd10a7055b41fd8b18c127a2cbc7713cc1091251a6b2107442c44f67cb1f.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:9548f3adc68903b67cd441efcd18bebcb2f7ac02a496d314a765992a9a4498a7","bundle_entry_key":"shifted-rectangular-gaussian-smoothing-gap-w718","bundle_id":"population.t287-rectangular-reference-c1-and-noncentered-comparison-v1","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"Gaussian channels and extensive-rank matrix inference","draft":"w718/bundle_009.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.gaussian_channels:shifted-rectangular-gaussian-smoothing-gap-w718","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# Supporting hard-edge lemma for rectangular Gaussian smoothing

Claim: w718-T287-024, version 1. Kind: moved; target: 2. Status: proof (unaudited). This is an elementary supporting lemma for the checked rectangular-reference route, not a claim of a new random-matrix theorem or completion of Target 2.

## Statement

Let n,p be positive integers and let delta>0, Kappa>=1+delta satisfy 1+delta <= p/n <= Kappa. Let G be an n by p real matrix of independent standard normal entries. Let S be any deterministic n by p real matrix with operator norm at most C, where C>=0. The same conclusions hold conditional on a random S independent of G. Fix 0<t_minus<=t_plus<infinity. Define

L=8 sqrt(1+Kappa),
K=max(1,C+sqrt(t_plus)L),
C0=max(1,2 sqrt(3/t_minus)),
epsilon=(6 K C0^Kappa)^(-1/delta).

For each t in [t_minus,t_plus], put Y_t=S+sqrt(t/n)G. Then

P(s_min(Y_t)<=epsilon) <= 2 exp(-n)+2^(-n).                 (1)

Here s_min is the least of the n singular values, equivalently inf_{||x||=1} ||Y_t^T x||. The bound is uniform in t and S, but is not asserted as a simultaneous event for an uncountable collection of t. If S is random independent of G without an almost sure norm bound, add P(||S||op>C) to the right side.

Consequently, suppose empirical singular-value laws of Y_t converge in probability to deterministic laws eta_t, and P(||S_n||op>C)->0 for some fixed C. Then for every t in the stated interval, eta_t([0,epsilon))=0. Thus the same epsilon is a gap for all these deterministic limiting laws. No assertion of a positive gap at square aspect ratio is made.

## Proof

1. A Euclidean unit sphere in R^d has an r-net with at most (1+2/r)^d elements, for 0<r<=1. Indeed take a maximal r-separated set. The open radius r/2 balls about its points are disjoint and lie in the radius 1+r/2 ball, so comparing their volumes gives the bound. Maximality gives coverage. This proof uses finite-dimensional Euclidean volume only.

2. Take 1/4-nets A and B in the unit spheres of R^n and R^p. For every matrix Z, approximation of both maximizing unit vectors gives

||Z||op <= 2 max_{x in A,y in B} |x^T Z y|.

For fixed x,y and Z=G/sqrt(n), x^T Z y is a centered normal of variance 1/n. The elementary normal tail bound P(|N(0,1)|>u)<=2 exp(-u^2/2), obtained by exponential Markov inequalities for both signs, yields

P(||G/sqrt(n)||op>L)
 <= 2 exp((n+p) log 9 - n L^2/8)
 <= 2 exp(-n).

The last inequality follows from p<=Kappa n, L^2=64(1+Kappa), and log 9<3. In particular, outside an event of probability at most 2 exp(-n), ||Y_t||op<=C+sqrt(t_plus)L<=K.

3. For any fixed unit x in R^n, Y_t^T x is a p-dimensional normal vector with arbitrary deterministic mean S^T x and covariance (t/n)I_p. Its density is bounded everywhere by (n/(2 pi t))^(p/2), independently of that mean. For R>0, the volume bound

vol(B_p(R)) <= (2 pi e/p)^(p/2) R^p

follows by integrating exp(-lambda ||u||^2) on R^p: the integral over the ball is at least exp(-lambda R^2) times its volume; choose lambda=p/(2R^2). Therefore

P(||Y_t^T x||<=2epsilon)
 <= (2 sqrt(e n/(p t)) epsilon)^p
 <= (C0 epsilon)^p.                                    (2)

Using the maximum density rather than a centered small-ball formula makes the arbitrary-shift hypothesis explicit.

4. Since K>=1 and epsilon<1, take an epsilon/K-net A_epsilon of the sphere in R^n, with cardinality at most (3K/epsilon)^n. If s_min(Y_t)<=epsilon and ||Y_t||op<=K, there is a unit x with ||Y_t^T x||<=epsilon, and a net point x0 at distance at most epsilon/K. The triangle inequality gives ||Y_t^T x0||<=2epsilon. A union bound and (2) give

P(s_min(Y_t)<=epsilon, ||Y_t||op<=K)
 <= (3K/epsilon)^n (C0 epsilon)^p
 <= (3K C0^Kappa epsilon^delta)^n
 = 2^(-n).

Here C0>=1, p<=Kappa n, p-n>=delta n, and 0<epsilon<1 justify each inequality. The event ||Y_t||op<=K was used only for the deterministic net approximation. It was not multiplied as an independent event with the small-ball probabilities.

5. Add the operator-norm exceptional probability from step 2 to prove (1). Conditional on an independent random S with ||S||op<=C, the same net, density bound and constants apply. Integrating the conditional inequality proves the random-input statement with the extra probability P(||S||op>C); it is unnecessary and generally incorrect to assume independence of the two exceptional events.

6. To pass to limiting laws, fix a continuous nonnegative function f supported in [0,epsilon), with f<=1. The empirical integral of f is zero unless s_min(Y_t)<epsilon. Thus its expectation tends to zero by (1) and the input-norm condition. Its convergence in probability to the deterministic integral against eta_t, together with boundedness, implies that integral is zero. Approximating indicators of [0,epsilon') for epsilon'<epsilon by such continuous tests gives eta_t([0,epsilon))=0. Constants do not depend on t, so the deterministic conclusion holds for each t with the same gap. This does not exchange a probability bound with an uncountable union.

## Gaussian-product application and limitations

For S=UV^T/n with independent standard normal U (n by M) and V (p by M), and bounded positive ratios M/n and p/n, apply the same two-sphere Gaussian net argument to U/sqrt(n) and V/sqrt(n). Their operator norms are bounded by fixed constants with exceptional probability tending to zero. The deterministic inequality ||UV^T/n||op<=||U/sqrt(n)||op ||V/sqrt(n)||op supplies the required C. The noise matrix is independent of both factors. Hence any deterministic limiting singular laws supplied by the already checked real population-Wishart theorem have this gap on compact intervals t>0 whenever p/n stays bounded away from one.

This lemma supplies no density regularity, no entropy differentiation, and no MMSE limit by itself. Its constants are deliberately crude. The least trusted step of the larger route remains algebraic boundary regularity and the singular-logarithm chain rule, not the elementary union bound above.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:965a7f6569046bdab574a5d8dade402280c470a6610623c9409c56ed763549bc","revision_digest":"sha256:762ffbc60d1a44b7d6b7b9f148692dce3f8fd290c35553753083c63fc18fcacf","source_id":"owner:w718:T287:shifted-rectangular-gaussian-smoothing-gap-w718","source_revision":"2026-10-21 w718-T287-024 version1, proof unaudited","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

[Lemma 2 (Positive local maxima use one cluster) of arXiv:2608.24007, '2608.24007'] Consider the constrained maximization problem
\[
    \max_{b_1,\ldots,b_K,\rho_1,\ldots,\rho_K}
    F(b_1,\ldots,b_K,\rho_1,\ldots,\rho_K),
\]
where
\[
    F(b_1,\ldots,b_K,\rho_1,\ldots,\rho_K)
    :=
    -\frac{\zeta}{K\sqrt6}
    \sum_{c=1}^K
    b_c\varphi(b_c)\rho_c^3,
\]
subject to
\[
    \sum_{c=1}^K\frac{b_c^2}{R^2}
    +
    \sum_{c=1}^K\rho_c^2
    =
    1.
\]

Every constrained local maximum of $F$ with positive objective value has
exactly one nonzero predictive coordinate $\rho_c$. Moreover, if
$\rho_c=0$, then the corresponding routing coordinate $b_c$ also vanishes.

body: In multivariable calculus, the implicit function theorem is a theorem that provides sufficient conditions under which a planar curve specified by an equation F(x, y) = 0 can also be specified as the graph of a function y = g(x), so that for each point (x, y) on part of the curve, one has y = g(x). An example is the unit circle, whose points satisfy x^2 + y^2 = 1, which can locally be solved by y = sqrt(1 - x^2), expressing the top semicircle as a graph. It is not always possible to solve the equation for y algebraically, and the implicit function theorem gives analytic conditions under which there exists a function g whose graph belongs to the given curve, and, in some formulations, also gives a way of constructing approximations to g.

[Proposition 7 of arXiv:2609.02808, 'Minimizers of Laplace eigenvalues under a lower curvature bound'] The map $u\mapsto e^{2u}\round$ is a bijection, modulo the conformal group of
$(\Sph^2,\round)$, between
\[
\mathcal{U}=\bigl\{\,u\in C^\infty(\Sph^2)\ :\ 1+\Delta_0 u-e^{2u}\ge0\ \text{on }\Sph^2\,\bigr\}
\]
and the class $\Cc$. Under this identification the area functional is
$\Area(e^{2u}\round)=\int_{\Sph^2}e^{2u}\dd$, and the eigenvalue functional
\eqref{eq:functional} is the $k$-th eigenvalue of the weighted problem
\begin{equation}
\Delta_0\phi=\la\,e^{2u}\phi\qquad\text{on }\Sph^2 ,
\end{equation}
where $\Delta_0$ is the Laplacian on $(\Sph^2,\round)$.

[Corollary 18 of arXiv:2609.00567, 'Hodge--Tate splitting and Akizuki--Nakano vanishing in positive characteristic'] Let \(k\) be a perfect field of characteristic \(p>0\), and let
\(X\) be a \(k\)-scheme.
Let $L_1,\ldots,L_r$ be line bundles on $X$.
If \(X\) is \(n\)-quasi-\(F\)-split, then
\[
\setP_X\left(\bigoplus_{i=1}^r L_i\right)
\]

Own work, independently checked proof (urn:mb-agent:7a4f9e38007c2a28 PASS on w717-T282-C03 v1). Sample-split normalized Lipschitz features satisfy Montanari-Saeed domain Gaussianity on every bounded readout ball when ||W||_op=o(sqrt(m)) and ||W||_F/sqrt(m) is bounded. For augmented Gaussian teacher coordinates B^T x, the uniform bounded-Lipschitz projection discrepancy is at most 2 Lip(f) R L ||W||_op/sqrt(m). Restricted subgaussianity also holds. For m/n proportional, compact bounded readout domains, nonnegative globally Lipschitz losses (nonconvex allowed), locally uniformly Lipschitz penalties, and independent subgaussian noise, Theorem 1 gives minimum-value universality against matched joint Gaussian feature/teacher rows. Explicit spiked matrices W=A+s_m u v^T, ||A||_op<=C, ||u||=||v||=1, are covered for s_m=o(sqrt(m)). Exact sample-split one-step ReLU matrices from the brief have ||W1||_op=O_P(1) under the specified Rademacher initialization and eta=O_P(1), so no spiked-RF approximation is needed in this bounded-readout regime. Scope: Unaudited explicit corollary, not claimed as a new general universality theorem. Excludes fixed per-neuron spike r>0, readout radii growing with m, unbounded squared loss in this corollary, and test-error universality. Projection rate is not a rate for minima. Data-normalized eta tightness remains an assumption.

[Lemma lemmacska of arXiv:2608.09589, 'On stochastic stability of systems\\ driven by red noise\thanks{The authors gratefully ack'] Let $W\in \mathbb{R}^{d}\times [0,1]$ and $Q\in\mathbb{R}^{d}$ be independent random variables, 
$G:\mathbb{R}^{d}\times [0,1]\to\mathbb{R}^{d}$ a measurable function,
$A\in\mathcal{B}(\mathbb{R}^{d}\times [0,1])$ with $\mathbb{P}(W\notin A)>0$.
Assume also that
$\mathrm{Law}(G(W)|W\notin A)=\mathrm{Law}(Q)$. 
Then 
$$
\mathrm{Law}(G(W)1_{\{W\in A\}}+Q1_{\{W\notin A\}})=\mathrm{Law}(G(W)).
$$

[Theorem 1 of arXiv:2604.20617, 'Structured random perturbations of \\ tridiagonal twisted Toeplitz matrices'] Consider the symbol defined on $[0,1] \times \T$
\[ a(x,z) = d(x) z^{-1} + b(x) + c(x) z, \]
where $b,c,d$ are continuous complex-valued functions on $[0,1]$. Let $\mu_n$ be the sequence of eigenvalue-counting measures
\[
\mu_n = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{\lambda \in \mathrm{sp}(R_n(a))} \delta_{\lambda}.
\]
Then $\mu_n$ converges weakly to the measure $\mu$ defined by
\[
\mu=\int_0^1 \alpha_x~dx,
\]
where $\alpha_x$ denotes the arcsine measure on the complex interval
\[
\bigl[b(x)-2\sqrt{d(x)c(x)},\, b(x)+2\sqrt{d(x)c(x)}\bigr].
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 1 of arXiv:2604.20617

[Prop 12 of arXiv:2604.12233, 'An upper bound on the smallest singular value of dense random combinatorial matrices'] Let $p \in(0, 1/2]$ be a fixed constant.
    Let $d, n$ be large enough positive integers such that $d=p n$. 
     There exist constants $C_{\ref{prop: inver_cons_pcons}}, c_{\ref{prop: inver_cons_pcons}}, \delta, \rho\in (0, 1)$ depending on $p$ only such that the following holds. Let $M$ be a random $m\times n$ matrix, $n/2\le m\le n$, whose rows are independent random  vectors drawn uniformly from the set of $n$-dimensional $0/1$ vectors having exactly $d$ ones. Then

body:
[Proposition prop:spectral-structure of arXiv:2607.05693, 'Free multiplicative convolution and Erlang moments in monitored quantum transport'] The limiting law $\mu_\tau$ has an atom at $1$ of mass
\[
  \mu_\tau(\{1\})=(1-\tau)_+.
\]
Consequently, the mass away from the atom at $1$ is $\min\{1,\tau\}$. Moreover,
the Stieltjes-transform equation has a real branch point at
\[
  x_*(\tau)=\tau \mathrm{e}^{1-\tau}.
\]
At $\tau=1$ this branch point reaches $1$, precisely where the atom at $1$
disappears.

\begin{remark}
Beenakker [Beenakker2501] computes the $\tau=1$ moments for the
\emph{orthogonal} version of the model, in which
$Q_N=\prod_{n=1}^N\bigl(I-u^{(n)}(u^{(n)})^\top\bigr)$ is a product of $N$
real rank-$(N-1)$ projectors, and obtains
\[
  \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\,\mathbb{E}\bigl[\Tr(Q_NQ_N^\top)^p\bigr]
  =\frac{(p/\mathrm{e})^p}{p!}.
\]
This agrees exactly with the law identified here: setting $\tau=1$ in
(equation eq:moment-formula of the paper) and using $G_p(1)=p^{p-1}$ (a short induction,
or Cayley's formula for the number of labelled rooted trees on $p$
vertices) gives
\[
  m_p(1)=\mathrm{e}^{-p}\frac{p^{p-1}}{(p-1)!}
  =\mathrm{e}^{-p}\frac{p^p}{p!}
  =\frac{(p/\mathrm{e})^p}{p!}.
\]
Our rigorous results are stated for the complex (unitary) ensemble, whereas
Beenakker's computation is for the real (orthogonal) one; the two limiting
moment sequences coincide because the leading-order free limit does not
depend on the symmetry class, the difference appearing only in the $1/N$
corrections. Beenakker further notes, following a question of Bulatov, that
at $\tau=1$ the squared singular values are \emph{approximately} distributed
as $\mathrm{e}^{-\pi X^2}$ with $X$ standard normal, and asks for a direct
explanation. The measure $\mu_1$ identified here is the exact limiting law:
the approximate Gaussian form is its Stirling approximation, with the factor
$\pi$ originating from Stirling's constant in
$(p-1)!\sim\sqrt{2\pi p}\,(p/\mathrm{e})^{p-1}$.
\end{remark} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Atom and branch point

[Defn 11 (Majority rule) of arXiv:2606.22960, '2606.22960'] Let \((T_n,(B_v)_{v\in[n]})\) be the broadcast-coloured tree of size \(n\), where
	\(B_v\in\{-1,1\}\) denotes the colour of vertex \(v\).
	The {\it majority rule} estimator is the \(\{-1,1\}\)-valued random variable
	\[
	\widehat B_{\mathrm{maj},n}
	:=
	\begin{cases}
		1, & \sum_{v=1}^n B_v > 0,\\
		-1, & \sum_{v=1}^n B_v < 0,\\
		\xi_n, & \sum_{v=1}^n B_v = 0,
	\end{cases}
	\]
	where \(\xi_n\) is independent of the broadcasting process and satisfies
	\[
	\mathbb P(\xi_n=1)=\mathbb P(\xi_n=-1)=\frac12.
	\]
	Its error probability is defined by
	\[
	R_{\mathrm{maj}}(n,q):=\mathbb P\!\left(\widehat B_{\mathrm{maj},n}\neq B_1\right),
	\qquad
	R_{\mathrm{maj}}(q):=\limsup_{n\to\infty} R_{\mathrm{maj}}(n,q).
	\]
title: Majority rule
Scaled barrier convergence

[Theorem thm:heat_kernel_sly of arXiv:2607.04002, 'Collisions of random walks in unimodular random graphs: applications to the random geometr'] Under the regime assumptions, there exists an event~$\Omega_1 \subseteq \Omega$ with~$\mathbb{P}(\Omega_1) = 1$, universal constants~$C_1,\delta > 0$ and a family of random variables~$\{T_x(\omega):x \in \mathbb{Z}^d\}$, with the property that~$T_x(\omega) < \infty$ when~$\omega \in \Omega_1$ and~$x \in \mathcal C_\infty(\omega)$, such that for all~$x \in \mathcal C_\infty(\omega)$:
$$ q_t(x,x) \leq C_1 \cdot t^{-d/(s-d)} \log^\delta(t) \quad \text{for } t \ge T_x(\omega). $$
Moreover, for any~$\eta > 0$, there exists~$C(\eta) > 0$ so that for each~$x \in \mathbb{Z}^d$, 
$$ \mathbb{P}( T_x > k \mid  T_x < \infty) \leq C(\eta) \cdot k^{-\eta}. $$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem 13 of arXiv:2607.19873, 'Local limit theorem for the operator norm of products of random matrices'] Let $\mu$ be a Borel probability measure on $G$. 
Assume that the action of $G$ on $\wt B$ satisfies the moment condition \eqref{moment-assumption-01} and 
that the action of $G$ on $B$ satisfies the contraction property \eqref{contraction-property-on-B}. 
Then, for every $\wt b \in \wt B$, there exists a Borel probability measure $\wt \nu_{\wt b}$ on $\wt B$ such that, for any continuous 
function $\varphi$ on $\wt B$, we have 
\begin{align*}
 \frac{1}{n} \sum_{k=0}^{n-1}  P_{\mu}^k \varphi(\wt b) 
=  \frac{1}{n} \sum_{k=0}^{n-1}  \bb E \varphi(g_k \cdots g_1 \wt b) 
\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}  \int_{\wt B} \varphi(\wt b') \wt \nu_{\wt b}(d \wt b'). 
\end{align*}
Moreover, this convergence holds uniformly over $\wt b \in \wt B$, and we have the following harmonicity property: for any $\wt b \in \wt B$, 
\begin{align*}
\wt \nu_{\wt b} = \int_G \wt \nu_{g \wt b} \mu(dg). 
\end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 13 of arXiv:2607.19873

body:
[Proposition of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] The Fourier transform of the binomial law $b_{np}$ is given by:
$$F_f(x)=(1-p+pe^{ix})^n$$
Also, the Fourier transform of the negative binomial law $c_{mp}$ is given by:
$$F_f(x)=\left(\frac{p}{1+(p-1)e^{ix}}\right)^m$$
In particular, in both cases we can see that $\log F$ is linear in $n/m$, as it should.

body: [Corollary 27 of arXiv:2605.05864, 'Classification and Metrization of Classes of Smooth measures'] The Green-tight class \(\mathcal{K}_\infty(R_1)\) is a closed subset of \((\mathcal{D}, d_{\mathcal{D}})\). In particular, if \(R_1f\) has a lower semi-continuous version for any non-negative function \(f\in C_c\), then \((\mathcal{K}_\infty(R_1), d_{\mathcal{D}})\) is a complete metric space.

[Theorem 1 of arXiv:2609.00720, 'Improved bounds for the variant of lazy cops and robbers\\ on generalized hypercubes'] If $m\geq2$ and $d\geq1$ are fixed integers, then, as $n\to\infty$,
\[
 c_{\mathrm L}^{(d)}(Q(n,m))
 =O\!\left(\frac{{(m+1)}^n}{n^{d+1/2}}\right).
\]
In particular, setting $d=1$ yields
\[
 \cL(Q(n,m))
 =O\!\left(\frac{{(m+1)}^n}{n^{3/2}}\right).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 1 of arXiv:2609.00720

[open-problem result I0084, 2026-10-10: GPT solver (Codex gpt-6.1-sol, max), Claude referee KEEP, not refereed by a person; established: For the positive classical strictly 1/2-stable semigroup (Laplace transform e^{-t√λ}), the measure μ = Z⁻¹Σ_{n≥1} 2^{-n²}δ_{-2ⁿ} has all absolute moments finite, yet μ∗S_t is non-unimodal for every t > 0; so Conjecture 5.5 as literally stated (no symmetry assumption) is false, while the symmetric classical, α ≥ 1, and free cases remain open.] Let Z=sum_{n>=1}2^(-n^2) and mu=Z^(-1)sum_{n>=1}2^(-n^2)delta_(-2^n). Every positive absolute moment of mu is finite. For the positive classical strictly 1/2-stable semigroup S_t with Laplace transform exp(-t sqrt(lambda)), mu*S_t is not unimodal for any t>0. Consequently Hasebe-Ueda Conjecture 5.5 is false as universally stated.
Classical convolution on R.

Unimodality with a finite real mode, as defined in the source.

[Lemma 36 of arXiv:2607.18862, 'Tamed Euler Schemes for Singular SDEs with Multiplicative L\'{e}vy Noise'] Let Condition ($\sH_\sigma^g$) holds and let $f\in L_{p}(\mR^d)$.
	
	(i) Suppose $p\in [1,\infty]$ and  $r<t_n$. Then 
	\be
	\|T_{r,t}f-T_{r,t_n}f\|_{p}\leq N\frac{1}{n}(t-r)^{-1}\|f\|_{p},
	\ee
	where the constant $N$ depends only on $d,p,c_0,C_1$.
	
	(ii) Suppose $p\in (2d/\beta,\infty]$. Then 
	\be
	\|F_{r,t}^nf-F_{r,t_n}^nf\|_{p}\leq N\frac{1}{n}\bigg[(t-r)^{\frac{\alpha}{2}-2}+(t-r)^{-\frac{1+\beta}{2}}\bigg]\|f\|_{p},
	\ee
	where the constant $N$ depends only on $d,p,c_0,C_1$.

[Lemma lem:continuous-version of arXiv:2412.01645, 'Regularisation by Gaussian rough path lifts of fractional Brownian motions'] Let $s \in [0,1]$, $k\in\mathbb{N}$ and $f \in \mathcal{C}^1({\mathbb{R}}^{kd})$. Then, for each $x_1,\ldots,x_k \in {\mathbb{R}}^d, t_1,\ldots,t_k \in [s,1]$, with probability one, we have
    \begin{equs}                       
        \mathbb{E}_s f(\phi^{s,x_1}_{t_1},\ldots,\phi^{s,x_k}_{t_k})= \mathbb{E}_s^Bf(\phi^{s,x_1}_{t_1},\ldots,\phi^{s,x_k}_{t_k}). 
    \end{equs}
    Moreover, the random fields in (equation eq:swap_filtrations of the paper) have continuous modifications in the variables $x_1,\ldots,x_k$ and $t_1,\ldots,t_k$.
title: Lemma lem:continuous-version of arXiv:2412.01645

[Lemma 29 of arXiv:2607.18862, 'Tamed Euler Schemes for Singular SDEs with Multiplicative L\'{e}vy Noise'] (i) Let $\mB$ be a Banach space and a locally integrable function $f:\mR^d\to \mB$  with $\nabla f\in \mL_{loc}^1(\mR^d,\mB^d)$. There exists a Lebesgue null set $E$ such that for all $x,y\in E$, 
		\be 
		\|f(x)-f(y)\|_{\mB}\leq 2^d\int_{0}^{|x-y|}\fint_{B_r}\|\nabla f\|_{\mB}(x+w)+\|\nabla f\|_{\mB}(y+w)dwdr,
		\ee
		where  $\fint_{B_s}:=\frac{1}{|B_s|}\int_{B_s}$. Furthermore, if $\nabla f\in \mL^p(\mR^d;\mB^d)$ for some $p\in(d,\infty]$, then there exists a constant $C_{d,p}>0$ such that
		\be 
		\|f(x)-f(y)\|_{\mB}\leq C_{d,p}|x-y|^{1-d/p}\|\nabla f\|_{\mL^p(\mR^d;\mB)}.
		\ee
		
		(ii) For $p\in(1,\infty]$, there exists a constant $N_{d,p}>0$ such that for all $f\in \mL^p(\mR^d)$, the maximal function $\sM f$ satisfies
		\ce 
		\|\sM f\|_p\leq N_{d,p}\|f\|_p.
		\de (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma 29 of arXiv:2607.18862

	if $$|\phi(x)-\phi(x')|\leq |x-x'|[1+U(x)+U(x')]^d$$
	$\phi(x)$ is said to be $(U,d)$-polynomially bounded if
	$|\phi(x)|\leq (1+U(x))^d$.

\begin{proof}
    Let $\YY \in S_\star(\lambda,\mu)$.
    Then for any $i \in [r]$,

        \lambda_i \BBb_i
        \le \Cost(\YY;\lambda)
        \le \Budget(\YY;\mu)
        = \frac{1}{\alpha}
        \bigg(
            \sum_{j=1}^s
            \mu_j
            (\www_j)^{1/2}
        \bigg)^2
        \le \frac{1}{\alpha}
        (\mu,\www)
        = \frac{1}{\alpha}\,,
    \]
where the last equality uses that $\www \in \cW_\mu$. Since $(\lambda,\mu) \in \Lambda$, this implies $\BBb_i \le 1/(\alpha \iota)$. It follows that
    \[
        \epsilon_1 \alpha^2 \iota^3 \sum_{i=1}^r (\BBb_i)^2
        \le \epsilon_1 \iota r
        \stackrel{\eqref{e:r-s-bd}}{\le} \epsilon_1\,,
    \]
and the conclusion follows.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition 21 (Singular mass) of arXiv:2608.03353, '\bfseries A Direct Route to Markov Chain Convergence\\[2mm] \Large via Asymptotic Equivale'] For finite measures $\alpha, \beta : \XXA \to [0,\infty)$ put
\[
  \sing(\alpha \mid \beta) := \alpha(\XX) - \sup\, \Sigma(\alpha\mid\beta)
  \;\in\; [0,\alpha(\XX)],
  \qquad
  \Sigma(\alpha\mid\beta) := \bigl\{\, \gamma(\XX) \ :\ \gamma \le \alpha,\ \gamma \ll \beta \,\bigr\},
\]
the supremum being over the masses of all nonnegative measures
$\gamma : \XXA \to [0,\infty)$ lying below $\alpha$ and absolutely continuous with
respect to $\beta$. The set $\Sigma(\alpha\mid\beta)$ is nonempty, since
$\gamma := 0$ is admissible.

The bar is read as in \ref{conv:kernelnotation}: the reference measure stands to the
right of it. Both orders occur below and they say different things, and the criterion
of Theorem \ref{thm:crit} asks that both vanish in the limit, which is why the
reference measure has to be displayed rather than fixed by a subscript; see
Remark \ref{rem:singmass}.
title: Singular mass
