[Corollary 15 of arXiv:2607.17192, 'Geometric Regime--Switching Diffusions on Stratified Riemannian Spaces with an Application'] In addition to Theorem~\ref{thm:harris}, assume that there exists a measurable function $G:E \to \R$ such that $A_m^\ast V=G$ on \(O_m\) for all $m \ge 1$. If, furthermore, $X$ is aperiodic then it is $V$--uniformly geometrically ergodic:
		there exist constants $M<\infty$ and $c>0$ such that
		\[
		\|P_t(x,\cdot)-\pi\|_V
		:=\sup_{|f|\le V}\left|P_t f(x)-\pi(f)\right|
		\le M V(x)e^{-c t},
		\qquad x\in E,\ t\ge0.
		\]

body:
Let X and Y be Banach spaces. (a) The set Phi(X,Y) of Fredholm operators is open in B(X,Y) and the index ind: Phi(X,Y) -> Z is locally constant, hence continuous and constant on each connected component (in particular along norm-continuous paths of Fredholm operators). Quantitatively, if T is Fredholm with regularizer S, then T + E is Fredholm with ind(T + E) = ind T whenever ||E|| < 1/||S||. (b) If T is Fredholm and K is compact, then T + K is Fredholm and ind(T + K) = ind T. (c) The kernel dimension and the codimension of the range are upper semicontinuous: for ||E|| small enough, dim ker(T + E) <= dim ker T and dim(Y/ran(T + E)) <= dim(Y/ran T). Individually these numbers can jump down, only their difference is stable.
X and Y are Banach spaces
T in B(X,Y) is Fredholm
E in B(X,Y) with ||E|| small (explicitly ||E|| < 1/||S|| for a regularizer S) in (a) and (c)
K in B(X,Y) compact in (b)

Hence (I + S E)^{-1} S (T + E) = I - Q and (T + E) S (I + E S)^{-1} = I - Q' with Q = (I + S E)^{-1} P and Q' = P'(I + E S)^{-1} of finite rank; note (I + S E)^{-1} S = S (I + E S)^{-1}, so a single operator serves on both sides. So (I + S E)^{-1} S is a regularizer for T + E, and Atkinson's theorem shows T + E is Fredholm. For the index, the composition formula gives ind((I + S E)^{-1} S) + ind(T + E) = ind(I - Q) = 0 by the Fredholm alternative, and ind((I + S E)^{-1} S) = ind S = -ind T because an invertible factor contributes index 0; therefore ind(T + E) = ind T. (c) From ker(T + E) contained in ker(I - Q) contained in ran Q we get dim ker(T + E) <= rank Q <= rank P = dim ker T; dually, Y = ran(I - Q') + ran Q' gives codim ran(T + E) <= codim ran(I - Q') <= rank Q' <= rank P' = codim ran T.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:2225456d23e042d16fa41a4883a1acf0ad8f28160beb6e99ce53d176a31bf47b","revision_digest":"sha256:7a3f4c94a70069ca7eb4074b0ca3e07cb34b8cbdedd8d433e949320ed4ff1f01","source_id":"wikipedia:Fredholm operator","source_revision":"as-known-2026-09-12","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

[Pro 4 of arXiv:2605.30779, '2605.30779'] Let \(H_N\) be a GOE matrix when \(\beta=1\) and a GUE matrix when \(\beta=2\). Let
\begin{align*}
  P = \sum_{i=1}^md_ie_ie_i^\ast = \diag(d_1,\dots,d_m,0,\dots,0), \qquad d_i=1-\theta_iN^{-1/3}, \qquad i= {} 1,\dots,m,
\end{align*}
with $\theta_i \in \realR$. Write
\[
\lambda_1\ge\cdots\ge\lambda_N
\]
for the eigenvalues of \(H_N+P\). Then, for each fixed \(k\ge1\),
\[
\bigl(
N^{2/3}(2-\lambda_1),\dots,N^{2/3}(2-\lambda_k)
\bigr)
\Longrightarrow
\bigl(
\Lambda_{\beta,1}^{(\theta_1,\dots,\theta_m)},\dots,
\Lambda_{\beta,k}^{(\theta_1,\dots,\theta_m)}
\bigr).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Pro 4 of arXiv:2605.30779

[Proposition 14 of arXiv:2609.02779, '2609.02779'] For the Hamiltonian \eqref{eq:twowell-H} constructed above, there exist
$C_0>0$ and $\lambda_0>0$ such that
\begin{equation}
 \|u_\lambda-u_0\|_\infty
 \ge C_0\lambda|\log\lambda|
 \qquad\text{for }0<\lambda\le\lambda_0.
\end{equation}
Consequently, Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-main} gives
\[
 \|u_\lambda-u_0\|_\infty
 \asymp\lambda|\log\lambda|.
\]
title: Proposition 14 of arXiv:2609.02779

[Lemma lem:stochastic_dominance_with_differences of arXiv:2604.09509, 'An Improved Bipartition Cover Bound for the Multispecies Coalescent Model'] Suppose for $s \in \mathbb{N}$ that $0 \leqslant_{st} D \leqslant_{st} D' < s$ and $D,D' \equiv s \; \mathrm{mod}(2)$. Then
    
    \[Z_{\frac{s + D}{2}} + Z_{\frac{s - D}{2}} \geqslant_{st} Z_{\frac{s + D'}{2}} + Z_{\frac{s - D'}{2}}.\]
title: Lemma lem:stochastic_dominance_with_differences of arXiv:2604.09509

body:
[Conj 8 of arXiv:2609.01413, 'Sharp Threshold for Universality of Rational Canonical Forms over a Finite Field'] Let $A_n\in\Mat_n(\F_p)$ be an $\alpha_n$-balanced random matrix
    with independent entries. If
    \begin{equation}
        
        \liminf_{n\to\infty}
        \frac{n\alpha_n}{\log n}>
        \frac{1}{d},
    \end{equation}
    then the joint distribution of partitions
    $$
    \left(\lambda^{(F_{i_1})}(A_n),\ldots,
    \lambda^{(F_{i_r})}(A_n)
    \right)
    $$
    converges pointwise to the same limiting distribution as in
    \Cref{thm:main}. (Stated as a conjecture by the paper; open unless the paper says otherwise.)
title: Conjecture 8 of arXiv:2609.01413

body: [Prop rel norm in open subscheme of arXiv:2609.04023, 'Characterizing Contractions and Weighted Blowdowns'] Suppose $f : \mathcal{Y} \to \mathcal{X}$ is a finite \'etale morphism of reduced Deligne--Mumford stacks where $\mathcal{Y}$ is normal and contains an open dense subscheme $U$. Then, the normalization of $\mathcal{X}$ in $f|_U : U \to \mathcal{X}$ is precisely $f :\mathcal{Y} \to \mathcal{X}$, i.e., $\mathcal{X}^\nu_{f|_U} \simeq \mathcal{Y}.$

body: Numeric (campaign status: exact-certificate): Independent exhaustive check of d_geo(A_n) = ceil(n/3) for n = 4..8. Search is faithful because any R_0 of dimension w spanned by zero-class forms and signed differences has a w-element basis among those generators, so enumerating all w-subsets for w <= ceil(n/3)-1 covers every candidate. Result (n, d, r, #generators, #candidates, min classes achieved, feasible hits): (4,2,5,69,69,6,0) (5,2,6,107,107,8,0) (6,2,7,152,152,10,0) (7,3,8,205,21100,9,0) (8,3,9,266,35494,11,0). ZERO residual spaces of dimension <= ceil(n/3)-1 achieve the feasibility threshold of r = n+1 signed classes. Notes: Exact rational arithmetic (fractions.Fraction), exhaustive in the stated finite window n = 4..8 ONLY. This is evidence about a finite range, never a proof of the uniform-in-n theorem, which is S10 (26)-(29). It does independently reproduce S14 (22)'s values 2,2,2,3,3 by a different route than S13's checker.

body:
[Definition 1 of arXiv:2608.29406, 'Partially Totally Real Submanifolds of Sasakian Manifolds'] A submanifold $M$ of a Sasakian manifold, tangent to $\xi$, is called a \emph{partially totally real (PTR) submanifold} if there exists a nonzero constant-rank totally real distribution $\Dperp\subset TM\cap\ker\eta$, i.e.
\[
 \phi\Dperp\subset\Tperp.
\]
If $\Dtilde$ denotes the orthogonal complement of $\Dperp\oplus\langle\xi\rangle$ in $TM$, then
\begin{equation}
 TM=\Dperp\oplus\Dtilde\oplus\langle\xi\rangle.
\end{equation}
Following the K\"ahler PTR terminology, $\Dtilde$ is called the
\emph{ambiguous distribution}.  The PTR structure refers to this chosen
decomposition; maximality of \(\Dperp\), when needed, is imposed later
and is not part of the definition.
title: Definition 1 of arXiv:2608.29406

body:
[Proposition 1 of arXiv:2608.21905, '\bf Ruin theory incorporating MIPP-type jumps'] For each fixed $n\geq 2$, the sojourn times of $V_t^{(n)}$ are i.i.d. exponential random variables. More specifically,
\[
S_k^{(n)}\sim \mathrm{EXP}(\lambda q_{n-1}), \forall k\geq 1, 
\]
where $q_{n-1}=P(V_1^{(n-1)}>0)$. The sequence $q_j, j\geq 1,$ satisfy  the  recursive relation
\[
q_j=1-e^{-\lambda q_{j-1}}, \; j\geq 2,
\]
with
\[
q_1=1-e^{-\lambda}.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Uniform one-sided endpoint and maximum estimates

[Lemma lem:sliceleaves_intersection of arXiv:2608.30973, 'Pseudo-Anosov flow and dynamics on guts'] Let \(a,b\) be two different slice leaves in \(\mathcal{F}^{\pm}\).
Then \(a\) and \(b\) intersects at at most one point.

Suppose that, in addition, there are two distinct points \(p,q\) in \(\partial P_{\varphi}\) such that \(\partial a\in (p,q)\) and \(\partial b\in (q,p)\).
Denote by \(R_{a},R_{b}\) the complementary regions of \(a,b\) whose boundaries avoid \(p,q\), respectively.
Then, \(R_{a}\cap R_{b}= \emptyset\).
Further, \(\overline{R}_{a}\cap \overline{R}_{b}\neq \emptyset\) if and only if \(a\cap b\) is a singular point \(p\); in this case, \(\overline{R}_{a}\cap \overline{R}_{b}=p\) and we say that \(a\) and \(b\) are \emph{tangent} at \(p\).

[Proposition prop:stability of arXiv:2608.30254, 'Exact Recovery Thresholds for Weighted Data Selection\\ in Vector-Valued Linear Regression'] Let $\mathcal E$ be the set of $3{+}3$ two-direction equality systems of
Proposition~(prop:twodir of the paper). Then:
(i) within the two-direction stratum, the three-point value drops linearly
under energy imbalance: with class energies $E(1\pm\eta)$ it equals
$\frac E8(5-3|\eta|)$ --- a downward cusp;
(ii) for every sequence of moment systems converging to a point of
$\mathcal E$ in which some direction class genuinely splits,
\[
  \limsup\ \frac1E\inf_{|\operatorname{supp} q|\le3,\,|\mu|<1}C\ \le\ \frac12\ <\
  \frac58 .
\]
Hence no nearby ascent direction exists: $\mathcal E$ is a local maximum of
the three-point value in the stratified sense.

The rigorous determination of the Ising perceptron storage capacity (the Ding-Sun framework and its successors) is conditional on explicit numerical hypotheses: finitely many concrete inequalities about one-dimensional variational quantities attached to the Krauth-Mezard formula, stated precisely in arXiv:2607.11010. That work verifies every such condition by rigorous interval (ball) arithmetic in Arb over explicit compact domains, locating the capacity constant alpha* within [0.833078599, 0.833078600], consistent with the 1989 Krauth-Mezard prediction. The verification is computer-assisted (certificates, replays, and a Lean exact-arithmetic layer are public) and, as of this writing, not independently refereed; the exact list of verified inequalities lives in the cited paper and artifact, not in this summary node.

[Proposition prop:density_bound_2 of arXiv:2608.13452, 'Wasserstein stability of the zero cell of a Poisson hyperplane tessellation under directio'] Let $\hat{f}^{(1)}_{\gamma, n}$ and $\hat{f}^{(2)}_{\gamma, n}$ be the estimators of a density $f$ as defined in Proposition (prop:density-robust of the paper). 
    Assume that the hypotheses of Proposition (prop:density-robust of the paper) are satisfied.
    Further assume that $f$ is globally $L$-Lipschitz and $\mathrm{supp}(f) \subseteq [0,1]^d$, and that \(\phi_2\) satisfies
    \begin{align}
        W_{\mathrm{geo}}(\phi_1,\phi_2) 
        <  
        \min\biggl\{\varepsilon_0(\phi_1), \min_{u \in S^{d-1}} h(\Pi_1,u)\biggr\},
    \end{align}
    where \(\varepsilon_0(\phi_1)\) is the constant from (lem:2constant_local_holder of the paper).
    Then there exist random probability densities
    $\hat{g}_{\gamma,n}^{(1)}$ and
    $\hat{g}_{\gamma,n}^{(2)}$, defined on a common probability space,
    such that, for every fixed $x\in\mathbb{R}^d$,
    \[
    \hat{g}_{\gamma,n}^{(i)}(x)
    \overset{(d)}{=}
    \hat{f}_{\gamma,n}^{(i)}(x),
    \qquad i=1,2,
    \]
    and such that
    \begin{align*}
     \mathbb{E} \left[\int_{[0,1]^d}\left|\hat{g}^{(1)}_{\gamma, n}(x) - \hat{g}^{(2)}_{\gamma, n}(x)\right| \mathop{}\!\mathrm{d} x\right]
    &\leq \frac{\|f\|_{\infty}^{1/2}\gamma^{d/2}\left(\mathrm{vol}(\Pi_1)^{1/2} + \mathrm{vol}(\Pi_2)^{1/2}\right)}{n^{1/2}} + \frac{L \tilde{C}(\phi_1, d)}{\gamma}W_{\mathrm{geo}}(\phi_1,\phi_2)^{1/d}, 
\end{align*}
for some constant $\tilde{C}(\phi_1,d)$ depending only on $\phi_1$ and $d$, where the expectation is taken with respect to the random tessellations and $\mathcal{D}_n$.

[Theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] The mean and variance of the hypergeometric laws are
$$E=\frac{mp}{N}\quad,\quad V=\frac{mp(N-m)(N-p)}{N^2(N-1)}$$
with $(N,m,p)$ standing as usual for the parameters.

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:95c2d03bc93f2b9de4fe51c8df4a116324edde6649762a1cc7495f6f367c2b68","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/95/95c2d03bc93f2b9de4fe51c8df4a116324edde6649762a1cc7495f6f367c2b68.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:f617b79a380b492a094cc3ee6eb5cbf54e76f335a27927756204526e6b3c8873","bundle_entry_key":"2608-10415-theorem-84-theorem-84","bundle_id":"population.tex-extract-s1_052","claim_kind":"theorem","conditions":[],"domain":"probability theory","draft":"tex-extract-v2-20260907/bundle_s1_052.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:harvest.arxiv.mathematics:arxiv-2608-10415-theorem-84-theorem-84","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"Paper's own proof, opening: Regarding the mean, we can compute it is as follows, by making use of the Vandermonde formula discussed in the proof of Theorem 3.19:
\begin{eqnarray*}
E
&=&\sum_ss\,\frac{\binom{m}{s}\binom{N-m}{p-s}}{\binom{N}{p}}\\
&=&\frac{1}{\binom{N}{p}}\sum_ss\binom{m}{s}\binom{N-m}{p-s}\\
&=&\frac{1}{\binom{N}{p}}\sum_sm\binom{m-1}{s-1}\binom{N-m}{p-s}\\
&=&\frac{m}{\binom{N}{p}}\sum_s\binom{m-1}{s-1}\binom{N-m}{p-s}\\
&=&\frac{m}{\binom{N}{p}}\binom{N-1}{p-1}\\
&=&m\cdot\frac{p!(N-p)!}{N!}\cdot\frac{(N-1)!}{(p-1)!(N-p)!}\\

Assume that, for each maximal subset $I \subseteq \{1,2,\dots, m\}$, there exists $\lambda_{I} \in \mathbb{R}^I_{> 0}$ such that $(\lambda_{I}^\top N^IR^I)_j \ge 1$ for all $j \in J_I$, where $N^I:=[n_i]_{i \in I}^\top$ is a $|I| \times d$ matrix consisting of row vectors $n_i$ with $i \in I$, $J_I := \{1 \le j \le k: f(j) \subseteq I\}$, and $R^I:=[R_j]_{f(j) \subseteq I}$ consists of column vectors $R_j$ with $f(j) \subseteq I$.
	Then $R$ is said to be weak $\mathcal S$ with respect to $S$ and $f$.

body:
[Satz 6 of arXiv:2506.13661, 'Box-Covariances of Hyperuniform Point Processes'] Let $\eta$ be a stationary hyperuniform point process on $\mathbb{R}^2$ with truncated pair correlation measure $\beta.$ Suppose that $\beta$ is box-symmetric (with respect to reflection and swapping of the axes), that ${|\beta|(\mathbb{R}^2)<\infty}$, and that $F(x):=\beta(\Lambda_\infty(x))$ is non-positive (or, non-negative) for $\|x\|$ sufficiently large. 
	Assume further that both $H_\pm(y_1,y_2):= \int_0^{y_1}\int_0^{y_2}F(\pm x_1,x_2)\mathrm{d}x_1\mathrm{d}x_2$ are multivariate $(a_\pm,g_\pm)$-regularly varying, each with $a_\pm\in[0,1]$ and such that $g_-(x,y)=g_-(y,x)$. Moreover assume $K_+:=\lim_{n\to\infty}H_+(n,n)/H_-(n,n)$ exists and set $K_-=-1$.
	Then, $\mathrm{cov}(z)$ exists and can be expressed similar to \eqref{eq:Cov_non_int}. 
	
	
	More precisely, denoting $|z|:=(|z_1|,|z_2|)$ and $\tau(z)=\min(\mathrm{sign}(z_1),\mathrm{sign}(z_2))$ (i.e. $\tau(z)=-$ if and only if at least one of $z_1,z_2$ has negative sign), then for $z\in\Lambda_\infty(0)$, we have
	\begin{align*}
		\mathrm{cov}(z)= &  -K_+\|z\|^ag_+\left(\frac{z}{\|z\|}\right)+\sum_{\substack{e\in\mathbb{Z}^2\\ \|e\|=1}}\frac{K_{\tau(z+e)}}{2} \|z+e\|^ag_{\tau(z+e)}\left(\frac{|z+e|}{\|z+e\|}\right)\\
		&-\sum_{v\in\{-1,1\}^2}\frac{K_{\tau(z+v)}}{4}\|z+v\|^ag_{\tau(z+v)}\left(\frac{|z+v|}{\|z+v\|}\right)+ \ind_{\Lambda_1}(z)\frac{1}{2}\|z-\mathbf 1\|^ag_{\tau(z+v)}\left(\frac{|z-\mathbf 1|}{\|z-\mathbf 1\|}\right).
	\end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Proposition 38 of arXiv:2608.07239, 'Unified framework for asymptotically uniform iterative construction of generalised random '] Assume that $\alpha\to\infty$, with $\ell$ fixed and $M=O(\alpha^{\sfrac12}/(\log\alpha)^2)$. Consider the following three conditions on an alternative weight function $\b':V\to\mathbb{R}$ with $\b'_{\max}:=\max\{|\b'(v)|:v\in V\}=O(M/\alpha)$.
		\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
			\item We have $\b'(v)=\b(v)$ for all $v\in V\setminus F$.
			\item We have $\b'(v)=-\log(1-\b(v))$ for all $v\in V$.
			\item The quantity $\b(S)-\b'(S)$ is the same for all MISs $S$ of $G$. 
		\end{enumerate}
		If $\b'$ satisfies any of these conditions, then for any FMIS $S$ of $G$, substituting $\b'$ for $\b$ in the definition of $\mathscr{P}(S)$ multiplies its value by a factor of $1+O(M^2/\alpha)$. It follows that the IMFIS process on $(G,F,R,\b')$ gives the same distribution on $\boldsymbol{S}_{\infty}$ as the IMFIS process on $(G,F,R,\b)$, up to a factor of $1+O(\mathscr{E}(\alpha,M))$.
		
		Furthermore, for any FIS $T$ of $G$ and vertex set $U$ satisfying the requirements of Theorem~\ref{theorem_space}, substituting $\b'$ for $\b$ in the definition of $\mathscr{Q}(T,U)$ multiplies its value by a factor of $1+O(\mathscr{E}(\alpha',M'))$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 12 of arXiv:2511.06414, 'Non-uniform Edgeworth expansions for weakly dependent random variables and their applicati'] Under Assumption \ref{GrowAssum},
for all $x\in\bbR$ and $3\leq p\leq m$ we have
$$
\left|\Phi_{p,n}(x)-\Phi_{p-1,n}(x)\right|\leq C_m(1+|x|)^{-m-1}\sig_n^{-(p-2)}.
$$
As a consequence, for all $2\leq m_1<m$,
$$
\left|\Phi_{m,n}(x)-\Phi_{m_1,n}(x)\right|\leq A_m(1+|x|)^{-m-1}\sig_n^{-(m_1-1)}.
$$
Here $A_m,C_m$ are constants that do not depend on $n$ or $x$.

[Corollary 3 of arXiv:2608.29486, 'Cabled braids and their crossing matrices'] Let $A=[a_{ij}]$ be an $n \times n$ zero-diagonal symmetric matrix. 
If $A$ satisfies that for any subset $S$ of $N= \{ 1, 2, \dots , n \}$ with $1<|S|<n$, $a_{kl}\ne a_{kl'}$ for any $k\in \overline{S}$ and any distinct $l, l'\in S$, then $A$ is the crossing matrix of a pseudo-Anosov pure $n$-braid. 
In particular, if $a_{kl}\ne a_{kl'}$ for any $k\in N$ and any distinct $l, l'\in N$, then $A$ is the crossing matrix of a pseudo-Anosov pure $n$-braid. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Let (a_n) be a sequence of real numbers that is monotonically decreasing with limit 0, and let (b_n) be a sequence of real or complex numbers whose partial sums B_N = b_1 + ... + b_N are bounded, |B_N| <= K for all N. Then the series sum a_n b_n converges. Special cases: the alternating series test (b_n = (-1)^n) and the convergence of sum a_n sin(n x) and sum a_n cos(n x) for every x that is not a multiple of 2 pi, since the partial sums of sin(n x) and cos(n x) are bounded by 1/|sin(x/2)|. Abel's test is the companion: if sum b_n converges and (a_n) is monotone and bounded, then sum a_n b_n converges.
(a_n) real, decreasing, a_n -> 0
the partial sums of (b_n) are bounded
no absolute convergence is claimed: sum a_n b_n may converge only conditionally

[Theoremi thm_main_undirected of arXiv:2604.04672, 'Connected components and topological ends of stationary planar forests'] With probability one, every connected component of $G$ is a tree with at most $2$ topological ends. Let $N_0, N_1$ and $N_2$ respectively denote the number of finite, one-ended and two-ended connected components of $G$, taking values in $\mathbb{Z}_+\cup\{\infty\}$. Then, $(N_0,N_1,N_2)$ is constant on a full-probability event, and the following holds almost surely:
        \begin{itemize}
            \item $N_0\in\{0,\infty\}$,
            \item $N_1\leq 2$, and
            \item $N_1=2\implies N_2<\infty$.
        \end{itemize}
    Moreover, this classification is optimal: every value for $(N_0,N_1,N_2)$ satisfying the above constraints is realized by some model on which the result applies. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Defn 5 of arXiv:2603.28702, 'Distribution of the magnetization of the critical Ising model on sparse random graphs'] \begin{itemize}
\item 
Let $G$ be a graph with vertex set $V$. The Ising model on this graph with inverse temperature $\beta$ is the probability measure $\mu$ on $\{-1,1\}^V$ satisfying
$$\mu_{\beta}(\sigma)=\dfrac{1}{Z_{\beta,G}}\exp\left(\beta\SL{u\sim v}\sigma_u\sigma_v\right).$$
\item
Fix a measure $\nu$ on $\{-1,1\}^V$. For a configuration $\sigma\in\{-1,1\}^V$ and for some $v\in V$, let $\sigma^{\oplus v}$ be the configuration $\sigma$ in which the spin at vertex $v$ is flipped. For two configurations $\sigma,\tau\in\{-1,1\}^V$, we write $\sigma\sim\tau$ if $\tau=\sigma^{\oplus v}$ for some $v\in V$. The continuous time Glauber Dynamics on $G$ for $\nu$ at rate 1 is a Markov chain with transition rates, for $\sigma\neq\tau$, equal to
$$q(\sigma,\tau)=\begin{cases}
\dfrac{\nu(\tau)}{\nu(\sigma)+\nu(\tau)},\ \ \text{if}\ \ \sigma \sim \tau
\\ \\
0,\ \ \text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}$$
Informally, every vertex gets updated at rate one, and the update happens conditionally on the configuration in the rest of the vertices.
\end{itemize}
title: Definition 5 of arXiv:2603.28702

[Cor 9 of arXiv:2609.03791, 'Canonical Bochner--K\"{a}hler potentials via the Sasaki--K\"{a}hler correspondence'] A Bochner--K\"{a}hler manifold $M$ is locally homogeneous if and only if the parameter $a=0$ and the eigenvalues $\tau$ of $X$ satisfy $\tau^2=-r$. 
    
    For $\tau=0$, we get the flat K\"{a}hler metric on $\mathbb C^n$.
    
    For $\tau\neq 0$, the locally defined manifold extends to a Cartesian product of a $\mathbb CP^{n_1}$ with Fubini--Study metric and a ball $\mathbb B^{n_2}$ with Bergman metric, with potential
    \begin{equation}
    v=\frac{1}{\tau}\log (1+\tau \langle z',z'\rangle)- \frac{1}{\tau}\log (1-\tau \langle z'',z''\rangle)
    \end{equation}
    where $n_1+n_2=n$ and $\tau>0$ is a real parameter. These K\"{a}hler manifolds are globally homogeneous. In this case the parameter $\beta\in \mathbb C^n$ is arbitrary and $\hBlock$ consists of two arbitrary hermitian diagonal blocks of dimensions $n_1\times n_1$ and $n_2\times n_2$, respectively, resulting in a symmetry group of dimension $2n+n_1^2+n_2^2$.

[Proposition prop:fkg of arXiv:2412.04539, 'Counting minimal cutsets and $p_c<1$'] Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite, connected graph. Let $\mathrm P$ be a positively associated percolation  measure on $G$. Let $B \subset  V$, let $\theta,p \in (0,1]$ and suppose that  $\mathrm P(u \leftrightarrow B) \geq \theta$ for every $u \in V$, and $\mathrm P(e \text{ is open}) \geq p$ for every $e \in E$.
Then for every $o \in V$,
    \[
        \mathrm P\left( \bigcap_{b \in B} \{ o \leftrightarrow b \}  \right) \geq c^{|B|},
      \]
      where  $c := \left(\frac{p\theta}{2}\right)^{3/\theta}$.
title: Proposition prop:fkg of arXiv:2412.04539

body:
Let p and q be probability mass functions on a finite set, d = d_TV(p, q), and call a coupling (X, Y) of p and q maximal when P(X != Y) = d. Every maximal coupling has P(X = Y = x) = min(p_x, q_x) for every x, and the maximal couplings are exactly the diagonal min(p, q) plus a transport plan from (p - q)_+ to (q - p)_+. For an event A let o = sum over x in A of min(p_x, q_x), u = sum over x in A of (p_x - q_x)_+ and v = sum over x in A of (q_x - p_x)_+. Over all maximal couplings, P(X in A, Y in A) takes exactly the values in [o + max(0, u + v - d), o + min(u, v)].
p, q probability mass functions on one finite set
maximal means P(X != Y) = d_TV(p, q)

body:
[Theo 3 of arXiv:2605.23292, 'Second-order Poincaré inequalities and localization on the Poisson space'] (rates of normal convergence for sums of $BL$-space-time localizing scores on metric spaces) 
Let $\xi:(X \times \R \times \MM) \times \mathbf{N}_{X \times \R \times \MM} \rightarrow \R$ be a score function on the marked space domain $X \times \R \times \MM$ and $\P$ a Poisson process on $X \times \R$ with intensity $\nu \otimes \mu $ and $\hat{\P}$ its marked version. Define
\[
H:=H(\hat{\P}) = \sum_{(z,t_z) \in \P \cap (W \times \R)} \xi((z,t_z, M_z),\hat{\P}).
\]
Assume that $\xi$ satisfies  $BL\big(\tfrac{1}{240}, \tfrac{1}{120}\big)$ space-time localization according to Def.~\ref{def:space-time-loc}, with $M^\xi_{5,X}<\infty$.
For $\psi$ as in Def.~\ref{def:space-time-loc} and $q>0$, put 
\[
G_{q}:=\int_{X} \psi(d(x,W))^{q} \nu(dx) = 2^q \nu(W) + \int_{X\setminus W} \psi(d(x,W))^{q} \nu(dx).
\]
If $G_{1/120}<\infty$, then there is a 
$C_K<\infty$ given by
\[
C_K:= c\cdot  {\cal I}_{\psi,X}\big(\tfrac{1}{240}\big)^{3} \cdot {\cal I}_{\phi}\big(\tfrac{1}{120}\big)^{7/2},
\]
where $c<\infty$ is a universal scalar, such that
\begin{equation} 
    \mathbf{d}_K \left(  \frac{H - \E H} {\sqrt{\Var H}}, N \right) \leq C_K \cdot (M_{5,X}^\xi)^{2/5} \cdot \frac{G_{1/120}^{1/2}}{\Var H}
\end{equation}
and there is a $C_W <\infty$ given by
\[
C_W := c \cdot  {\cal I}_{\psi,X}(\tfrac{1}{50})^{3} \cdot {\cal I}_{\phi}(\tfrac{3}{200})^{4}
\]
such that
\begin{equation} 
    \mathbf{d}_W \left(  \frac{H - \E H} {\sqrt{\Var H}}, N \right) \leq C_K \cdot (M_{5,X}^\xi)^{2/5} \cdot \frac{G_{1/120}^{1/2}}{\Var H} + C_W  \cdot (M_{5,X}^\xi)^{3/5} \cdot\frac{G_{3/200}}{(\Var H)^{3/2}}.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Lemma lem:nointersectAT of arXiv:2604.15146, 'Renormalised two-point functions of CLE$_4$ gaskets'] Let $\widetilde F_{\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2}$ denote the event that at least two different odd CLE$_4$ gaskets of the family of CLE$_4$ gaskets constructed in Theorem (thm:twopointAT of the paper) intersect both 
$\mathbb{D}(z_1, \varepsilon_1)$ and $\mathbb{D}(z_2, \varepsilon_2)$. Then
\begin{itemize}
    \item Let $E_{\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2}^{\rm{odd},k}(z_1,z_2)$ denote the event that the $k$-th odd nested CLE$_4$ gasket intersects 
    $\mathbb{D}(z_1,\varepsilon_1)$ and $\mathbb{D}(z_2,\varepsilon_2)$. Then there is a constant $C > 0$
    such that for all $k \geq 1$,
    $$\mathbb{P}(\widetilde F_{\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2} \cap E_{\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2}^{\rm{odd},k}(z_1,z_2)) \leq C(\varepsilon_1\varepsilon_2)^{1/4}\left(\mathbb{P}(E_{\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2}^{\rm{odd},k}) + \1_{k \geq 2}\mathbb{P}(E_{\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2}^{\rm{odd},k-1})\right).$$
    \item Further, for some $\widetilde C > 0$, 
    for all $\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2 > 0$ sufficiently small, 
$$\sum_{k \geq 1}\mathbb{P}(E^{\rm{odd},k}_{\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2}(z_1,z_2)) < \widetilde C\mathbb{P}(E_{\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2}^{\rm odd}(z_1,z_2)).$$
    \item In particular, $\mathbb{P}(\widetilde F_{\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2})$ is bounded by $C(\varepsilon_1\varepsilon_2)^{1/4}\mathbb{P}(E_{\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2}^{\rm odd}(z_1, z_2))$ for some $C > 0$ as $\max(\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2)\to 0$. 
\end{itemize}
Further, the same holds when we replace odd by even everywhere. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma lem:nointersectAT of arXiv:2604.15146

body: [Proposition prop:RegularityW of arXiv:2608.17031, 'A shape theorem for periodic branching diffusion'] The boundary $\partial \mathcal{W}$ is of class $C^2$, meaning that locally, up to a change of coordinates,  $\partial \mathcal{W}$ is the graph of a $C^2$ function on some open subset of $\mathbb{R}^{d-1}$. In addition, considering $\partial \mathcal{W}$ as a submanifold, let $K_{\mathcal{W}}:\partial\mathcal{W}\to \mathbb{R}$ be the Gaussian curvature of $\partial\mathcal{W}$. Then, $\inf_{x\in \partial\mathcal{W}}K_{\mathcal{W}}(x)>0$.

PROOF (UNAUDITED); novelty unverified. Let d=r+k, r>=0, k>=1, n>=1, and let X_i be iid real d-dimensional feature rows with uncentered second moment G=E[XX^T] positive definite and kappa=E[(X^TG^(-1)X)^2]<infinity. Let S=n^(-1)sum_i X_iX_i^T and B(M)=C-D^TA^+D for the first-r/last-k partition M=[[A,D],[D^T,C]], or B(M)=M if r=0. Then E||B(G)^(-1/2)B(S)B(G)^(-1/2)-I_k||op^2 <=(kappa-d)/n, including singular S. For k=1, E[(sqrt(B(S)/B(G))-1)^2]<=(kappa-d)/n as well. The mixture with conditional centered Gaussian covariance B(S) admits a coupling to N(0,B(G)) with squared cost <=tr(B(G))(kappa-d)/n. A uniform bound on kappa is an additional hypothesis. Conditional use requires conditionally iid rows and retains E[tr(B(G))(kappa-d)]/n without factoring it. This is a local covariance-step lemma, not a complete Tensor Program length theorem.
n>=1; d=r+k; r>=0; k>=1
Rows iid; G is uncentered positive-definite second moment; kappa finite
Generalized Schur complement uses Moore-Penrose inverse; empirical S may be singular
Conditional version requires conditional iid and retains E[tr(B)(kappa-d)] without factoring

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:508933338764b01c7c4d1c5df7ac72e621ab385aa0a5e762dff0ec85982252a0","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/50/508933338764b01c7c4d1c5df7ac72e621ab385aa0a5e762dff0ec85982252a0.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:a3ae660870fdea8f35c824f25dc15528839b10e28ddcb8627fdccfcc527d9ad7","bundle_entry_key":"t250_w712_c025","bundle_id":"population.w712-t250-c025-c026-relative-schur-and-rare-features","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"probability and Gaussian conditioning","draft":"w712/bundle_019.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.neural_networks:relative-schur-sampling-whitened-fourth-moment-gaussian-coupling","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# C025 v1: relative Schur sampling bound via whitened fourth moments

Kind: moved (one restricted stochastic covariance step). Target: 4.
Status: proof (unaudited); novelty unverified. Standard Schur monotonicity and sample-moment identities are used, not claimed as new.

## Statement and scope
Let d=r+k with r>=0 and k>=1. Let X_1,...,X_n be iid real d-vectors, n>=1, with positive definite UNCENTERED second-moment matrix G=E[XX^T]. No zero-mean assumption is imposed. Suppose

kappa=E[(X^T G^(-1)X)^2]<infinity.

Set S=n^(-1) sum_i X_i X_i^T. Partition the first r and last k coordinates. Write B(M) for the generalized Schur complement of the first block of a PSD matrix M: if M=[[A,D],[D^T,C]], set B(M)=C-D^T A^+ D. For r=0, B(M)=M. Put B=B(G)>0.

Then, including singular empirical S,

E || B^(-1/2) B(S) B^(-1/2) - I_k ||_op^2 <= (kappa-d)/n.       (1)

There is a coupling, with the correct conditional Gaussian law N(0,B(S)) given S, to an unconditional N(0,B) vector, with expected squared Euclidean cost at most

tr(B) (kappa-d)/n.                                            (2)

After whitening both output vectors by B^(-1/2), the cost is at most k(kappa-d)/n. Thus the W2 distance between the Gaussian covariance mixture E[N(0,B(S))] and N(0,B) is at most sqrt(tr(B)(kappa-d)/n). Constants do not explicitly involve lambda_min(G); the distribution-dependent parameter kappa can nevertheless be large.

This addresses the covariance-noise part of source equation (4.9) for an iid feature block only. It does not prove that every reused-weight parent block is iid, control its deviation from the infinite-width population G, control the conditional mean error, or prevent accumulation over program lines. It is not a complete Target 1 or Target 4 theorem. Prior literature/novelty and independent review remain open.

## 1. Deterministic relative Schur stability
For a PSD block matrix M and every v in R^k,

v^T B(M) v = inf_{u in R^r} (u,v)^T M (u,v).                  (3)

This is the usual variational characterization of the generalized Schur complement. To see the singular case directly, PSD implies each column of D lies in range(A): for w in ker(A), positivity of (tw,v)^T M(tw,v) for all real t forces w^T Dv=0. Complete the quadratic square with u+A^+Dv; its infimum is v^T(C-D^TA^+D)v. In particular B is monotone for Loewner order and positively homogeneous on PSD matrices. This is standard matrix algebra, included to fix the rank-deficient convention of source equation (3.1).

Let delta=||G^(-1/2)(S-G)G^(-1/2)||_op, which is finite. Always S<=(1+delta)G. If delta<=1 then S>=(1-delta)G as well. Applying (3) gives

B(S)<=(1+delta)B;
B(S)>=(1-delta)B when delta<=1.

When delta>1, the trivial B(S)>=0 supplies the lower bound needed instead. Hence, for all delta>=0, all eigenvalues of

C_S=B^(-1/2)B(S)B^(-1/2)

lie in [max(0,1-delta),1+delta]. Therefore

||C_S-I||_op<=delta,
||sqrt(C_S)-I||_op<=delta.                                  (4)

The latter follows from |sqrt(t)-1|=|t-1|/(sqrt(t)+1)<=|t-1| for t>=0. No good-event cutoff, inverse sample Gram, or rank assumption on S is needed.

## 2. Exact sampling identity
Set Y_i=G^(-1/2)X_i, so E[Y_iY_i^T]=I_d. Define E_i=Y_iY_i^T-I_d. They are independent, mean-zero matrix-valued variables with finite second moment. Thus cross inner products have zero expectation and

E || n^(-1) sum_i E_i ||_F^2
= n^(-1) E ||YY^T-I||_F^2
= n^(-1) [E||Y||^4 - 2E||Y||^2+d]
= (kappa-d)/n.                                             (5)

This uses independence of distinct iid rows, not independence of a Gram matrix and its Schur complement. Since operator norm is at most Frobenius norm, (4)-(5) prove (1). Cauchy-Schwarz gives kappa>=d^2, so the displayed nonnegative bound is consistent even for n<d.

## 3. Conditional Gaussian coupling
Take Z~N(0,I_k) independent of the whole sample, and define

U=B^(1/2) sqrt(C_S) Z,    V=B^(1/2) Z.

Given S, U is centered Gaussian with covariance B^(1/2) C_S B^(1/2)=B(S), and V has the fixed target covariance B. The factor for U need not be the symmetric square root of B(S); it gives the correct conditional Gaussian law. Conditional expected squared distance equals

tr[B (sqrt(C_S)-I)^2] <= tr(B) delta^2,

using (4) and PSD trace monotonicity. Equation (5) proves (2). Whitening U and V yields sqrt(C_S)Z and Z, with cost <=k E delta^2. Taking infima gives the W2 conclusions. No assumption that B commutes with C_S is used.

## 4. Conditional version and dependence warning
The same proof applies conditionally on a sigma-field F if the rows are conditionally iid, G=E[XX^T|F] is positive definite almost surely, and kappa=E[(X^TG^(-1)X)^2|F] is finite. With an independent fresh Gaussian Z, the conditional cost is <=tr(B)(kappa-d)/n. Its unconditional expectation is

E[tr(B)(kappa-d)]/n,

provided this is finite. It is NOT replaced by a product of expectations without an additional justification. Past-measurable mean errors can be added to U and V; the mean/noise cross term then vanishes by the centered fresh Z, not by assuming means and covariance errors are independent.

## 5. Checks, literature status, and unpaid source hypotheses
For Gaussian X~N(0,G), the usual Gaussian fourth moments give kappa=d(d+2), so (2) is tr(B)d(d+1)/n regardless of conditioning of G. This is only a simple corollary and is not claimed to improve the classical Wishart Schur-complement distribution.

The full source proof still needs a bound on whitened moments for its actual nonlinear parent-feature blocks, an appropriate conditional-iid/martingale replacement where rows are dependent, population-kernel transport, mean stability, and accumulation over lines. Merely bounding coordinate fourth moments or marginal kernel variances does not supply a bound on kappa. A separate rare-feature construction tests that missing implication.

Primary context: Agazzi, Mosig Garcia, Trevisan, arXiv:2607.06290, Section 3 equation (3.1) and Section 4.2 covariance-stability paragraph leading to (4.9). C024 identifies the raw norm obstruction; the present lemma changes the metric and hypothesis instead of contradicting it. Brain searches did not return this relative sampling statement; broad whitening hits concerned unrelated ensemble regressions and are not used. body:
[Theorem thm:plurality of arXiv:2608.20480, 'When Clean Data Hurts: Learning with Monotone \\ Corruptions Beyond Binary Classification'] Assume that the adversary adds at most $b$ examples. Put $r=4b+1$ and
$t=\lfloor(n+b)/r\rfloor$. After padding to the declared final length with
correctly labeled duplicates, select $rt$ positions uniformly if necessary,
partition them randomly into $r$ groups of size $t$, run an ordinary improper
learner on every group, and output their pointwise plurality. Then
\[
    R^{\mathrm{imp}}_{\mathrm{ad},b}(n;\mathcal{H})
    <
    4 \, R^{\mathrm{imp}}_{\mathrm{iid}}(t;\mathcal{H}).
\]
Consequently, if $d_{\mathrm{DS}}(\mathcal{H})=d$, then
$R^{\mathrm{imp}}_{\mathrm{ad},b}(n;\mathcal{H})=O(d(b+1)/(n+b))$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: [Theorem 3 of arXiv:2605.25323, 'Slow Convergence of Ising and Spin Glass Models with Well-Separated Frustrated Vertices'] Let Λ ⊂Z2 be an (2n + 1) × (2n + 1) lattice region and 0 ≤p ≤1/2 define a family of p-shifted mixed boundary conditions on Λ. Let Ωbe the set of all Ising configurations and let C be the Ising configurations containing a cross. Then π(C) ≤f(n)e−cn, for some polynomial f(n) and constant c > 0, whenever λ(1−2p) > 3(2−2p).

body: [LITERATURE CHECK 09-08 10:1x, answering his novelty question] Read Solomyak's survey directly. CONFIRMED: 2/3 is open and the survey states verbatim that the only known singular parameters are reciprocals of Pisot numbers, so this session's control-set hole is real. Salem 1944 already gives muhat -> 0 at any non-Pisot parameter, so all our work concerns the RATE. Solomyak Thm 2.7(i) gives an L^2 density for a.e. lambda in (1/2, 2^-1/2), an interval CONTAINING 2/3 - so the L^2 route is the classical route and 2/3 is simply not covered as an individual point. Garsia does not apply since 3/2 is not an algebraic integer. Transversality is the named crucial idea behind the a.e. results, so our finding that Erdos-Kahane collapses at fixed lambda because transversality fails is the expected reason, not a discovery. HONEST VERDICT: no theorem; the reformulations are the subject's standard instruments; the one plausibly novel item is the parity obstruction (any relaxation dropping parity returns the trivial bound identically), which is a negative result about a criterion we built and still needs checking against the computer-assisted-bounds literature

[Pro 2 of arXiv:2605.30779, '2605.30779'] Fix \(\beta>0\), \(\theta\in\mathbb R\), and \(k\ge1\). Let \(\mu_1^{(\beta)}\ge \cdots \ge \mu_N^{(\beta)}\) be the eigenvalues of \(H_N^{(\beta)}\), and let \(\lambda_1\ge\cdots\ge\lambda_N\) be the eigenvalues of
\[
  H_N^{(\beta)}+d e_1e_1^\top,
  \qquad
  d=1-\theta N^{-1/3}.
\]
Then
\begin{equation*} 
\bigl(
N^{2/3}(2-\mu_1^{(\beta)}),\dots,N^{2/3}(2-\mu_k^{(\beta)})
\bigr)
\Longrightarrow
\bigl(
\Lambda_{\beta,1}^{(\infty)},\dots,\Lambda_{\beta,k}^{(\infty)}
\bigr),
\end{equation*}
and
\begin{equation*} 
\bigl(
N^{2/3}(2-\lambda_1),\dots,N^{2/3}(2-\lambda_k)
\bigr)
\Longrightarrow
\bigl(
\Lambda_{\beta,1}^{(\theta)},\dots,\Lambda_{\beta,k}^{(\theta)}
\bigr).
\end{equation*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Corollary cor:tailrl-binary-recovery of arXiv:2609.02987, 'Tail Likelihood Reinforcement Learning'] Suppose $r_i\in\{0,1\}$ and let
$M:=\sum_{i=1}^N\mathbbm{1}\{r_i=1\}$. If $M>0$, then every successful
rollout receives weight $1/M$ and every unsuccessful rollout receives weight
zero. Hence the uncentered TailRL{} estimator reduces to
\begin{equation}
g_{\mathrm{TailRL}}^{(N)}(x)
=
\frac{1}{M}
\sum_{i:r_i=1}S_i,

\end{equation}
which is the MaxRL estimator. After mean-centering, successful rollouts have
weight $1/M-1/N$ and unsuccessful rollouts have weight $-1/N$. If $M=0$,
all uncentered and centered weights are zero.

[Definition def:standard-twostream of arXiv:2602.21315, 'The Instability of all Backoff Protocols\thanks{For the purpose of Open Access, the author'] Fix $\lambda \in (0,1)$
and a \emph{send sequence}  
$\overline{p}$ with $p_0=1$.
Let $Z=(Z^A,Z^B)$ be the two-stream process with birth rate~$\lambda$, send sequence~$\overline{p}$ and start time~$0$  
where for all $D\in \{A,B\}$ and all
positive integers~$k$,
$\mathbf{arr}_k^{Z^D}(\tau) = \emptyset$. 
Let $X$ be the backoff process with birth distribution~$\mathsf{Po}(\lambda)$, send sequence~$\overline{p}$, and cohort set $\mathcal{C}=\{A,B\}$ (Definition~(def:backoff-cohorts of the paper)).
The standard coupling of~$Z$ and~$X$ has the following invariants for every $i\geq 1$ and $t\geq 1$.
\begin{description}  
\item  [Inv-$b_i(t)$:] For each stream $D\in \{A,B\}$, $\mathbf{b}_i^{Z^D}(t-1) \subseteq \mathbf{b}_i^{X^D}(t-1)$.
\item  [Inv-$B_i(t)$:] For each stream $D\in \{A,B\}$, $\mathbf{B}_i^{Z^D}(t) \subseteq \mathbf{B}_i^{X^D}(t)$.
\item [Inv-$s_i(t)$:] 
For each stream $D\in \{A,B\}$, $\mathbf{s}_i^{Z^D}(t) \subseteq \mathbf{s}_i^{X^D}(t)$.
\end{description}
Initially, Inv-$b_i(1)$ holds for every $i\geq 1$ since all of these sets are empty.

For any $t$ assuming Inv-$b_i(t)$, the coupling at step~$t$ proceeds as follows.
For each $D\in \{A,B\}$, $\mathbf{n}^{Z^D}(t) = \mathbf{n}^{X^D}(t)$, so for all $i\geq 1$, 
Inv-$B_i(t)$ holds.
For every   
$D\in \{A,B\}$ and
$i\geq 1$, $\mathbf{S}^{X^D}_i(t)$ is formed by including each ball in 
$\mathbf{B}_i^{X^D}(t) \setminus \mathbf{B}_i^{Z^D}(t)$ 
independently with probability~$p_i$.
Then $\mathbf{s}^{X^D}_i(t) = \mathbf{S}^{X^D}_i(t) \cup \mathbf{s}^{Z^D}_i(t)$, establishing Inv-$s_i(t)$.

 
  

  
The assignments to $\mathbf{e}_i^{X^D}(t)$ follow deterministically, using  Definition~(def:backoffasgen of the paper)
and the assignments to $\mathbf{e}_i^{Z^D}(t)$  are chosen  following Definition~(def:two-stream of the paper).

Since $\mathbf{s}_i^{X^D}(t) \cap \mathbf{B}_i^{Z^D}(t) = \mathbf{s}_i^{Z^D}(t)$, Inv-$b_i(t+1)$  follows from  
$ \mathbf{s}_i^{Z^D}(t) \cap \mathbf{e}_i^{X^D}(t) \subseteq \mathbf{e}_i^{Z^D}(t)$, which holds:
If a ball~$\beta$ is in $ \mathbf{s}_i^{Z^D}(t) \cap \mathbf{e}_i^{X^D}(t) $ then
$\mathbf{s}^{X^A}(t) \cup \mathbf{s}^{X^B}(t)= \{\beta\}$ so
$\mathbf{s}^{Z^A}(t) \cup \mathbf{s}^{Z^B}(t) = \{\beta\}$ so 
$\mathbf{e}_i^{Z^D}(t) = \{\beta\}$.
title: Definition def:standard-twostream of arXiv:2602.21315

[Lemma le:good_scales_merging of arXiv:2507.15589, 'Tightness of approximations to metrics on non-simple conformal loop ensemble gaskets'] Suppose that $h$ is a GFF on $D$ with some bounded boundary values. For any $b>0$ and $q \in (0,1)$ there exist $M,p>0$ so that the following is true. 
Let $z \in D$ and $r>0$ such that $B(z,r) \subseteq D$. Let $\widetilde{h}_{z,r}$ be as defined in Section~(se:gff of the paper) with the same boundary values as $\widetilde{h}$ above (after scaling and translation). Let $G_{z,r}$ be the event that
\begin{itemize}
 \item the scale $(z,r)$ is $M$-good for $h$, and
 \item the event $G$ above occurs for the (scaled and translated) field $\widetilde{h}_{z,r}$.
\end{itemize}
For $k\in\mathbf{N}$ let $E$ be the event that the fraction of $1 \leq j \leq k$ so that $G_{z,2^{-j}r}$ occurs is at least $q$. Then $\mathbf{P}[E^c] = O(e^{-bk})$.

body: Fermat's Last Theorem: There are no three positive integers a, b, c satisfying a^n + b^n = c^n for any integer exponent n > 2. (By contrast, for n = 1 and n = 2 the equation has infinitely many positive integer solutions; for n = 2 these are the Pythagorean triples, e.g. 3^2 + 4^2 = 5^2.) The statement was conjectured by Pierre de Fermat in 1637 and proved by Andrew Wiles in 1994, using a result obtained jointly with Richard Taylor, via the modularity of semistable elliptic curves.

body:
[Lemma lem:pathbound of arXiv:2608.30888, 'Three-term asymptotics for discrete\\ Hardy--Rellich constants in high dimension'] Fix $J$ and two finite sets of partitions.  Uniformly for $0\leq j\leq J$ and
for all partitions $\lambda,\mu$ in those sets or reachable from them in at
most $J$ steps,
\begin{equation}
 \left|\ip{A_N^j\psi_\lambda}{\psi_\mu}\right|
 \leq C_J N^{a_j(\lambda,\mu)/2},
\end{equation}
where $a_j(\lambda,\mu)$ is the largest number of dimensional edges among
length-$j$ paths from $\lambda$ to $\mu$; the left side is zero if no such path
exists.  Consequently, for fixed $\ell$ and bounded $s_\lambda,s_\mu$,
\begin{equation}
 \left|\ip{K_{\ell,N}\psi_\lambda}{\psi_\mu}\right|
 \leq C_\ell N^{\ell-d_*(\lambda,\mu)}.
\end{equation}

[Definition def:openpath of arXiv:2608.24830, 'Motion helps the contact process: survival below\\ the percolation threshold on Poisson Br'] Let $\lambda\in(0,\infty]$, $\mu\in(0,\infty]$ and $\mathfrak r\in\{\mathrm{u},\mathrm{i}\}$. An \emph{open
path} from $(u_0,t_0)$ to $(u_n,t_{n+1})$ consists of particles $u_0,\dots,u_n$, such that
consecutive particles are distinct, and times $t_0<t_1<\dots<t_{n+1}$, such that
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item for $1\le j\le n$ there is an active transmission mark from $u_{j-1}$ to $u_j$ at time
  $t_j$; when $\lambda=\infty$ this says that $u_{j-1}$ and $u_j$ are in contact at $t_j$;
\item for $0\le j\le n$ there is no effective recovery mark of $u_j$ in $(t_j,t_{j+1}]$.
\end{enumerate}
Its \emph{trace} is the c\`adl\`ag path $\gamma$ on $[t_0,t_{n+1}]$ given by $\gamma(t)=X_{u_j}(t)$
for $t\in[t_j,t_{j+1})$ and $0\le j\le n-1$, and by $\gamma(t)=X_{u_n}(t)$ for
$t\in[t_n,t_{n+1}]$. Its jumps have size at most $2r$. The path is \emph{contained} in a
space-time region $D$ if $(\gamma(t),t)\in D$ for every $t\in[t_0,t_{n+1}]$.

[Proposition 41 of arXiv:2607.18862, 'Tamed Euler Schemes for Singular SDEs with Multiplicative L\'{e}vy Noise'] Let  $\widetilde{X}^n$ satisfies Eq. (\ref{formula1+12+1}). Suppose that $f\in \mL_{p}^{q}([0,1])\cap \mL_{\infty}^q([0,1])$ and $h\in \mH_{1,p}^q([0,1])\cap \mL^{\infty}([0,1])$, where $q\in [2,\infty)$ and $ p\in (2d/\beta\vee 2,\infty)$ are such that $\frac{d}{p}+\frac{2}{q}<1$. Define  $\gamma_n(f):=\sup_{r\in D_n}\|f\|_{\mL_\infty^q([r,r+1/n])}$. Then for any $p'\in(0,p)$ there is a constant $N=N(d,p,q,p')$ such that 
	\ce 
	&&\|\sup_{t\in[0,1]}|\int_{0}^{t}h(r,\widetilde{X}_r^{n})(f(\widetilde{X}_r^{n})-f(\widetilde{X}_{r_n}^{n}))dr|\|_{L_{p'}(\Omega)}\\

	\de 
	where $$T(f,h)=(\|h\|_{\mL^{\infty}([0,1])}+\|h\|_{\mH_{1,p}^{q}([0,1])})\|f\|_{\mL_{p}^{q}([0,1])}.$$
	Particularly 
	\be 
	&&\|\sup_{t\in[0,1]}|\int_{0}^{t}(f(r,\widetilde{X}_r^{n})-f(r,\widetilde{X}_{r_n}^{n}))dr|\|_{L_{p'}(
		\Omega)}\no\\
	&\leq &N\bigg\{\gamma_n(f)(1/n)^{1-\frac{1}{q}}+[(1/n)^{\alpha/2}+(1/n)^{ 1-\beta/2}+(1/n)^{1/2}\log(n)]\|f\|_{\mL_{p}^{q}([0,1])}\bigg\}.
	\ee

body: [Definition Pareto optimality of arXiv:2608.22945, 'A Momentum-Based Variance-Reduced Algorithm for Federated Multiobjective Optimization'] For any two solutions $x, y\in \mathbb{R}^{d}$, we say $x$ \emph{dominates} $y$ if and only if $f_s(x)\leq f_s(y), \forall s\in[S]$ and $f_s(x)<f_s(y), \exists s\in[S]$. A solution $x\in \mathbb{R}^{d}$ is \emph{Pareto optimal} if it is not dominated by any other solution. A solution $x\in \mathbb{R}^{d}$ is \emph{weakly Pareto optimal} if there does not exist a solution $y$ such that $f_s(y)< f_s(x), \forall s\in[S]$.
title: Pareto optimality

[Lemma 7 of arXiv:2606.13487, 'Branching-Selection Particle Systems and Inverse First Passage Problems'] Suppose that the measure $\mu^N_s$ converges weakly to the measure $\mu_s\ll\lambda$ almost surely and $b(s):=\inf\{x:\Lambda\langle \mu_s,\omega(\cdot-x)\rangle \geq f(s)\}$. If either $\omega$ is continuous or $\omega = \is_{\{x\leq 0\}}$, then for any $\phi\in C_b(\B{R})$, 
    $\langle \mu^N_s,\phi(\cdot)\omega(\cdot-b^N(s))\rangle\to\langle \mu_s, \phi(\cdot)\omega(\cdot-b(s))\rangle$ almost surely.

[Corollary 15 of arXiv:2608.26618, 'A Unified Descriptive-Complexity Framework for Model Selection under Correlated Designs'] Assume that the conditions in Theorem~\ref{thm:control} hold.
Define
\[
\lambda_-:=\lambda_{\zeta}+\max\Big\{0,\ \frac{\lambda_{\zeta}\log(L/\delta)-\eta_n}{C_{\min}}\Big\},
\qquad
\lambda_+:=\frac{\frac{n}{2\sigma^2}\underline \omega\,\beta_{\min}^2-\eta_n-\lambda_{\zeta}\log(Ls^*/\delta)}{C_{\max}^*}.
\]
If $\lambda_-<\lambda_+$, with probability at least $1-c\delta$, we have
$
\widehat S_{\lambda}=S^*  \text{for all }\lambda\in\Lambda\cap(\lambda_-,\lambda_+).
$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Definition 4 (Size-biased law) of arXiv:2606.18458, 'Stable size-biasing and the positive scale-mixture order of generalized Gaussian laws'] Let $Y\ge0$ satisfy $0<\E Y<\infty$. The $Y$-size-biased version $Y^*$ of $Y$ is the positive random variable whose law is defined by
\[
\Prob(Y^*\in A)=\frac{\E[Y\mathbf{1}_{\{Y\in A\}}]}{\E Y},
\]
for Borel sets $A\subseteq[0,\infty)$. Equivalently,
\[
\E h(Y^*)=\frac{\E[Yh(Y)]}{\E Y}
\]
for all bounded measurable $h$.
title: Size-biased law

\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item The equilibrium stopping time pair of Theorem (thm:construction of the paper) is not unique. 
In particular, suppose $\Psi^{(i)}_t,i=1,2$ in (equation Ne-stretegy of the paper) correspond to a global Markovian randomized $\epsilon$-Nash equilibrium for some $\epsilon \geq 0$. 
Now 
replace $\gamma^{(i)}_\epsilon(\cdot)$ in (equation Ne-stretegy2 of the paper) with a real-valued, measurable and locally bounded function that dominates $\gamma^{(i)}_\epsilon(\cdot)$, and 
replace $\Gamma^{(i)}_\epsilon(\cdot)$ in (equation Ne-stretegy2 of the paper) with a real-valued function that dominates $\Gamma^{(i)}_\epsilon(\cdot)$. Then (equation Ne-stretegy of the paper) still corresponds to a global Markovian randomized $\epsilon$-Nash equilibrium for the same $\epsilon$ (although it may also correspond to a global Markovian randomized $\epsilon$-Nash equilibrium for a smaller value for $\epsilon\geq 0$). 

\item The equilibrium value of the game is (uniquely) given by $V$ in Theorem (thm:construction of the paper) (and Proposition (asso-game:characterization of the paper)).  

\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 6 (Uniform selected labels and coverage) of arXiv:2608.24007, '2608.24007'] Let ${\omega_1^0,\ldots,\omega_m^0}$ be independent and uniform on
$\mathbb S^{d-1}$, and let $J_j$ be the cluster selected by the self-selected
flow in Lemma~\ref{lem:self-selected-specialization}. Then
$J_1,\ldots,J_m$ are independent and uniform on $[K]$. Consequently,
\[
    \mathbb P\bigl(\{J_1,\ldots,J_m\}\neq[K]\bigr)
    \leq
    K\left(1-\frac1K\right)^m
    \leq
    Ke^{-m/K}.
\]

[Corollary 33 (Phase transition for Poisson-Voronoi percolation) of arXiv:2504.02435, 'Poisson-Voronoi percolation in higher rank'] Let $G$ be a non-compact connected semisimple real Lie group and $(X,d_X)$ be its symmetric space. Fix $\lambda>0$. Then 
\begin{itemize}
\item[{\rm (1)}] for every $p\in [0,p_c(\lambda))$, $\omega_p^{(\lambda)}$ does not have an unbounded cluster a.s.
\item[{\rm (2)}] for every $p\in (p_c(\lambda),p_u(\lambda))$, $\omega_p^{(\lambda)}$ has infinitely many unbounded clusters a.s.
\item[{\rm (3)}] for every $p\in (p_u(\lambda),1]$, $\omega_p^{(\lambda)}$ has a unique unbounded clusters a.s.
\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Phase transition for Poisson-Voronoi percolation

[Lemma 18 (Differentiation formula for a finite-intensity Poisson process) of arXiv:2604.20514, 'Macroscopic loops in the random loop model on sparse random graphs'] Let \((\mathsf X,\nu)\) be a finite measure space, and for \(t\ge 0\) let \(\Pi_t\) be
a Poisson point process on \(\mathsf X\) with intensity measure \(t\nu\). Then, for
every finite counting measures, the map
\(t\mapsto \Ebb[F(\Pi_t)]\) is differentiable on \((0,\infty)\), and its right
derivative at \(t=0\) is given by
\[
\frac{\dd}{\dd t}\Ebb[F(\Pi_t)]
=
\int_{\mathsf X}\Ebb\!\left[F(\Pi_t+\delta_z)-F(\Pi_t)\right]\nu(\dd z).
\]

[Lem generator-for-SPDE of arXiv:2601.19145, 'Stochastic Persistence in Infinite Dimensions'] Let $\mathcal{A} = \mathcal{M}$ or $\mathcal{A} = \mathcal{M}_+ \coloneqq \mathcal{M}_0^c$ and $f: \mathcal{A} \to \mathbb{R}$, $b: \mathcal{A} \to \mathbb{R} \cup \{-\infty\}$, and $\sigma: \mathcal{A} \to \mathcal{L}_2(\mathcal{U}, \mathbb{R}) \cong \mathcal{U}$ be measurable functions such that $df(r,v,z) = b(r,v,z)dt + \sigma(r,v,z) dW_t$ holds, meaning that for all $(r_0,v_0,z_0) \in \mathcal{A}$ 
    we have 
    \begin{equation}
        f(r_t,v_t,z_t) = f(r_0,v_0,z_0) + \int_0^t b(r_s,v_s,z_s)ds + \int_0^t \sigma(r_s,v_s,z_s)dW_s
    \end{equation}
    and all the integrals in (equation eq:fieq of the paper) are well-defined. Then the following statements hold:

    \begin{enumerate}[label = (\roman*)]
        \item If $f \geq 0$, then $f \in \mathcal{D}^{ext}_+(A)$ with $\mathcal{L} f = b$.
        \item Assume $\hat f, \hat b, \hat \sigma$ satisfy the same assumptions as $f,  b,  \sigma$
        above, $\hat f \geq 0$, and there are some constants $K, C > 0$ such that $\sup_A (\|\sigma\|_\mathcal{U}^2 + K \hat b) =: C < \infty$. Then $f \in \mathcal{D}^{ext}_2(A)$ with $\mathcal{L} f = b$ and $\Gamma f = \|\sigma\|_\mathcal{U}^2$.
    \end{enumerate}

Let (M,tau) be a finite von Neumann algebra with faithful normal tracial state tau(1)=1. Let X=(X_1,...,X_n) be an algebraically free tuple of bounded selfadjoint elements, with n a fixed positive integer. On noncommutative polynomials in X, define the free difference quotient partial_j by partial_j X_i=delta_ij*(1 tensor 1) and the Leibniz rule, with the usual bimodule action on the tensor product. The conjugate variable J_j belongs to the L2(tau) closure of the polynomial algebra and, if it exists, satisfies tau(J_j P(X))=(tau tensor tau)(partial_j P(X)) for every polynomial P. Equivalently J_j is the adjoint of partial_j applied to 1 tensor 1. Define Phi_star(X)=sum_{j=1}^n ||J_j||_2^2 when all conjugate variables exist, and Phi_star(X)=+infinity otherwise. This is conjugate-variable, non-microstates free Fisher information relative to the scalar algebra C. It is not the Fisher information of a classical parametric likelihood.
Normalized faithful normal tracial state on a finite von Neumann algebra.
Fixed finite algebraically free bounded selfadjoint tuple, so the difference quotients on its polynomial algebra are well-defined.
Conjugate variables, when present, lie in the L2 closure of that polynomial algebra.

Every separable real Banach space X is isometrically isomorphic to a closed linear subspace of C[0, 1], the space of continuous real functions on [0, 1] with the supremum norm. (The complex version holds with complex-valued C[0,1].) Consequently C[0,1] is universal for the class of separable Banach spaces up to isometry, and every separable metric space embeds isometrically into C[0,1] as well (Banach-Mazur, via the Kuratowski embedding x -> d(x, .) - d(x_0, .)). In contrast, no separable Banach space is isomorphically universal for the class of separable REFLEXIVE spaces with a separable dual of the same kind (Szlenk), and the universality fails in an essential way for spaces of continuous functions on countable compacta (Bessaga-Pelczynski, Milutin: C(K) for uncountable metrizable compact K is isomorphic to C[0,1], while C(K) for countable K is not).
X separable (the separability is essential: a non-separable space cannot embed into the separable space C[0,1])
real scalars in the statement; the complex case is identical with complex-valued functions

[Proposition BBSTAB of arXiv:2411.04590, 'Singular stochastic delay equations driven by fractional Brownian motion: Dynamics, longti'] Assume that \( A \) and \( \pi \) satisfy the same conditions as in Lemma (PII of the paper), and let \( G \in {L}(\mathbb{R}^n \times \mathbb{R}^n, {L}(\mathbb{R}^d, \mathbb{R}^n)) \). Consider the following linear stochastic differential equation:
			\[
			\begin{aligned}
				\mathrm{d}y_t &= A\left( y_t, \int_{-r}^{0} y_{\theta+t} \, \pi(\mathrm{d}\theta) \right) \mathrm{d}t + \epsilon G(y_t, y_{t-r}) \, \mathrm{d}B_t(\omega), \\
				y_{\theta} &= \xi_{\theta} \quad \text{for} \quad \theta \in [-r, 0], \quad \xi \in C([-r, 0], \mathbb{R}^n),
			\end{aligned}
			\]
			where \( y^{\xi, \epsilon}_t \) denotes the solution. Let \( \lambda_1 \) be as defined in (equation TRFVV of the paper), and assume \( \lambda_1 < 0 \). Then, there exists \( \epsilon_0 > 0 \) such that for every \( 0 < \epsilon < \epsilon_0 \), there exists \( \lambda^\epsilon < 0 \) such that for any \( \xi \in C([-r, 0], \mathbb{R}^n) \), the following holds:
			\[
			\limsup_{n \to \infty} \frac{1}{t} \log | y^{\xi, \epsilon}_t(\omega) |\leq \lambda^\epsilon, \quad \text{almost surely}.
			\]
			This yields in particular a pathwise stability result on $C([-r,0],\mathbb{R}^n)$
title: Proposition BBSTAB of arXiv:2411.04590

[Definition 43 ($\mathrm{RCD}(K, \infty)$ condition) of arXiv:2609.01460, 'On cost-induced Santal\'o-type inequalities \\ in Polish measure spaces'] Let $(X,d,\mu)$ be a Polish measure space. We say that it is an $\operatorname{RCD}(K, \infty)$-space if it satisfies the $\mathrm{CD}(K, \infty)$-condition and if its Cheeger energy is quadratic, i.e., for all $f,g\in L^2(X,\mu)$ such that $0<\operatorname{Ch}_\mu(f)\operatorname{Ch}_\mu(g)<\infty$, one has
\[
\operatorname{Ch}_\mu(f+g) + \operatorname{Ch}_\mu(f-g)=2\operatorname{Ch}_\mu(f) + 2\operatorname{Ch}_\mu(g).
\]

[Thm 41 of arXiv:2605.26664, 'Mixing times for Glauber dynamics of lozenge tilings of the hexagon'] For any real numbers $q_0>0, \delta > 0$, there exist constants $r = r(q_0) \in (0, 1)$ and $\mC = \mC(q_0, \delta) > 1$ such that the following holds. 
 Define
  \[
     i_{max}=\left\lfloor\frac 9{10}\frac{\log N}{\log(1/(1-r))}\right\rfloor
    \] and
  the sequence
\[
  N_i=\lfloor N (1-r)^i\rfloor,\quad 0\le i\le i_{max}\] that
decreases from $N_0=N$ to $N_{i_{max}}\asymp N^{1/10}$. Define also

[Lemma detect-pointed-presheaves of arXiv:2608.28504, 'Global $\bm\infty$-categories and global Thom spectra'] Let ${\mathcal{C}}$ be a cocomplete, pointed, and locally small $\infty$-category. Let ${\mathcal{I}}\subset{\mathcal{C}}$ be a small full subcategory containing the zero object and satisfying the following properties:
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item For any $I\in{\mathcal{I}}$, the unique lift ${\mathcal{C}}\to\Spc_*$ of ${\textup{Hom}}(I,-)$ is cocontinuous.
        \item The functors ${\textup{Hom}}(I,-)\colon{\mathcal{C}}\to\Spc$ are jointly conservative.
    \end{enumerate}
    Then ${\mathcal{I}}\hookrightarrow{\mathcal{C}}$ extends to an equivalence $\PSh^0({\mathcal{I}})\xrightarrow{\;\smash{\raisebox{-0.25ex}{\ensuremath{\scriptstyle\sim}}}\;}{\mathcal{C}}$.
    \begin{proof}
        As ${\mathcal{C}}$ is cocomplete and locally small, the inclusion extends to a functor $\Lambda\colon\PSh({\mathcal{I}})\to{\mathcal{C}}$ left adjoint to the restricted Yoneda embedding $\Upsilon$. By what it means to be a zero object, ${\textup{Hom}}(0,x)\simeq1$ for all $x\in{\mathcal{C}}$, i.e.\ $\Upsilon$ factors through $\PSh^0({\mathcal{I}})$, so we obtain a restricted adjunction $\PSh^0({\mathcal{I}})\rightleftarrows{\mathcal{C}}$. It remains to show that this is in fact an adjoint equivalence. As our second assumption guarantees that $\Upsilon$ is conservative, it will suffice for this that the unit $\eta\colon\textup{id}\to\Upsilon\Lambda$ is invertible. 

        Since ${\mathcal{I}}^{\textup{op}}$ has a zero object, postcomposing with the forgetful functor induces an equivalence ${\textup{Fun}}^0({\mathcal{I}}^{\textup{op}},\Spc_*)\xrightarrow{\;\smash{\raisebox{-0.25ex}{\ensuremath{\scriptstyle\sim}}}\;}{\textup{Fun}}^0({\mathcal{I}}^{\textup{op}},\Spc)$. Moreover, the full subcategory ${\textup{Fun}}^0({\mathcal{I}}^{\textup{op}},\Spc_*)\subset{\textup{Fun}}({\mathcal{I}}^{\textup{op}},\Spc_*)$ is closed under colimits (as any colimit of initial objects is initial), so that colimits in ${\textup{Fun}}^0({\mathcal{I}}^{\textup{op}},\Spc_*)$ are computed pointwise. Thus, our first assumption guarantees that the right adjoint $\Upsilon$ is cocontinuous, so that the class of all pointed presheaves $X$ for which $\eta_X$ is invertible, is closed under colimits. It will therefore suffice to show that the unit $\eta_X$ is invertible whenever $X=\Upsilon(I)$ is representable. If we now let $Z\in{\mathcal{C}}$ arbitrary, then the composite
        \[
            {\textup{Hom}}(\Lambda(X),Z)\xrightarrow{\;\Upsilon\;}{\textup{Hom}}(\Upsilon\Lambda(X),\Upsilon(Z))\xrightarrow{\;{\textup{Hom}}(\eta,\Upsilon(Z))} {\textup{Hom}}(X,\Upsilon(Z))
        \]
        is invertible as it is just the adjunction equivalence. By assumption, $\Lambda(X)\simeq I\in{\mathcal{I}}$; if also $Z\in I$, then the first map is an equivalence by the Yoneda lemma, so that also the second map is an equivalence by $2$-out-of-$3$. We conclude that ${\textup{Hom}}(\eta_X,\Upsilon(Z))$ is an equivalence for every $Z\in I$. As $\eta_X\colon \Upsilon(I)=X\to \Upsilon\Lambda(X)\simeq\Upsilon(I)$ is a map in Yoneda image, this implies that $\eta_X$ is an equivalence.
    \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma detect-pointed-presheaves of arXiv:2608.28504

[Lemma 9 of arXiv:2608.01516, 'Nondegeneracy and regularity of polynomial pushforwards'] Let $k, n\in \mathbb{N}$, $n\ge k$, let $\nu_{k,n}$ be the normalized Haar measure on the Grassmannian
$Gr(k,n)$ of all $k$-dimensional subspaces of $\mathbb R^n$. Then there
exists a constant $C(k,n)>0$ such that, for every $k\times n$ matrix $J$,
one has
\[
\int_{Gr(k,n)}(\det J^H)^2\,\nu_{k,n}(dH)
=
C(k,n)\det(JJ^*),
\]
where $J^H:=JU_H$ and $U_H$ is the $n\times k$ matrix whose columns form an
orthonormal basis in $H$.

[Theorem 1 of arXiv:2605.16733, 'Concentration Inequalities for Sample Cross-Covariances'] Let \((X_i,Y_i)_{i=1}^N\) be i.i.d. copies of a centered random vector
\((X,Y)\in\mathbb R^{d_X+d_Y}\). Assume that \(X\) and \(Y\) are
sub-Gaussian random vectors with covariance matrices \(\Sigma_X\) and
\(\Sigma_Y\), and sub-Gaussian constants \(K_X,K_Y\). Set
\[
r_{X}:=\frac{\tr(\Sigma_X)}{\|\Sigma_X\|},
\qquad
r_{Y}:=\frac{\tr(\Sigma_Y)}{\|\Sigma_Y\|}.
\]
For every \(u\ge 1\), it holds with probability at least \(1-\exp(-u)\) that
\[
\bigg\|\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N} X_i Y_i^{\top}-\E X Y^{\top}\bigg\| \lesssim K_{X}K_{Y}(\|\Sigma_{X}\|\|\Sigma_Y\|)^{1/2} \bigg(\sqrt{\frac{r_{X}+r_{Y}+u}{N}}+ \frac{\sqrt{(r_{X}+u)(r_{Y}+u)}}{N}\bigg).
\]
As a corollary,
 \begin{align*}
\E \bigg\|\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N} X_i Y^{\top}_i-\E X Y^{\top}\bigg\| \lesssim K_{X}K_{Y} (\|\Sigma_{X}\|\|\Sigma_Y\|)^{1/2} \bigg(\sqrt{\frac{r_{X}+r_{Y}}{N}}+ \frac{\sqrt{r_{X}r_{Y}}}{N}\bigg).
 \end{align*}
Moreover, if $(X,Y)$ is jointly Gaussian, then
\begin{align*}
\E \bigg\|\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N} X_i Y^{\top}_i-\E XY^{\top}\bigg\| \asymp (\|\Sigma_{X}\|\|\Sigma_Y\|)^{1/2} \bigg(\sqrt{\frac{r_{X}+r_{Y}}{N}}+ \frac{\sqrt{r_{X}r_{Y}}}{N}\bigg).
\end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 1 of arXiv:2605.16733

[Proposition of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] The following happen:
\begin{enumerate}
\item The rotation $R_t$ is not diagonalizable, unless at $t=0$ where it is the identity, $R_0=1$, and at $t=\pi$ where it is minus the identity, $R_\pi=-1$.

\item The symmetry $S_t$ is diagonalizable, with eigenvectors on the symmetry axis, and on its orthogonal, with respective eigenvalues $1,-1$.

\item The projection $P_t$ is diagonalizable, with the eigenvectors exactly as for the symmetry $S_t$, this time with respective eigenvalues $1,0$.

\item In fact, any projection is diagonalizable, with eigenvectors on it image, and on the orthogonal of its image, with respective eigenvalues $1,0$.
\end{enumerate}

[Lemma 26 of arXiv:2605.09459, 'Multipoint connectivity in the branching interlacement process'] Let $X$ and $X^*$ be two independent random walks both indexed by infinite critical trees $\mathcal{T}$ and $\mathcal{T}^*$ respectively and independent from the branching interlacement. Let $\P_x$ denote the joint law of $X$ and $A^{(s_d)}(r,R)$, and $\P_z^*$ the law of $X^*$. Then there exist constants $c = c(u,d) > 0$, $\varepsilon = \varepsilon(u,d) > 0$ and $R' = R'(u,d)$, such that, for all $r$ and $R \geq R'$, satisfying $r^{d-4} \leq \varepsilon R$, and $r \geq \max(\|x\|,\|z\|)$,
  \[
    \P_z^* \otimes \P_x(\exists u \in \mathcal{T}^{*}_-:\, X^*_u \in A^{(s_d)}(r,R), n^*_u < \tau^*_{R^2}) \geq c,
  \]

\begin{align}
\gfour_{\alpha \beta},

\Yvf{2},

		\\
\upchi 
& = \smoothfunction(\controlvars,\LogDensity,  \angrmd \vec{x} \, ) \tander (\controlvars,\LogDensity), 
	 
		\\
\mytr_{\gtorus} \upchi 
& 
= 
\smoothfunction(\controlvars,\LogDensity, \gtorus^{-1}, \angrmd \vec{x} \, ) \tander  (\controlvars,\LogDensity), 
	  
		\\

	\,
\angktan 
& 
= \smoothfunction(\controlvars,\LogDensity, \angrmd \vec{x} \, ) \tander \wavearray, 
	 
		\\
\zetatrans, 
	\,
\angktrans

\end{align}
\end{subequations}

[Corollary 33 of arXiv:2609.03962, '$L^p$ isomorphisms for the fractional Laplacian on $\mathbb{R}^n$ and their application'] Let $0<t\le\sigma<2$ and $p\in(1,\infty)$. For
    $T\in\Lambda^{t-\sigma,p}(\R^n)$ with
    $T\perp\mathcal P_{[\sigma-t-n/p']}$, define
    \[
      \big\langle(-\triangle)^{\tfrac{t}{2}}T,\,w\big\rangle
      :=\big\langle T,\,(-\triangle)^{\tfrac{t}{2}}w\big\rangle,
      \qquad w\in\Lambda^{\sigma,p'}(\R^n),
    \]
    the right-hand side being unambiguous because
    $(-\triangle)^{\frac{t}{2}}w$ is defined modulo
    $\mathcal P_{[\sigma-t-n/p']}$ (Proposition~\ref{scale_isom} with
    $(s,p)$ replaced by $(\sigma,p')$) and $T$ annihilates this space.
    Then
    \[
      (-\triangle)^{\tfrac{t}{2}}:\
      \Lambda^{t-\sigma,p}(\R^n)\perp\mathcal P_{[\sigma-t-n/p']}
      \longrightarrow
      \Lambda^{-\sigma,p}(\R^n)\perp\mathcal P_{[\sigma-n/p']}
    \]
    is an isomorphism, reducing to Theorem~\ref{dual_isom} when $t=\sigma$,
    and
    \begin{equation}
      (-\triangle)^{\tfrac{t}{2}}\circ(-\triangle)^{\tfrac{\sigma-t}{2}}
      =(-\triangle)^{\tfrac{\sigma}{2}}
      \qquad\text{on }L^p(\R^n),
    \end{equation}
    where $(-\triangle)^{\frac{\sigma-t}{2}}$ and
    $(-\triangle)^{\frac{\sigma}{2}}$ are the operators of
    Theorem~\ref{dual_isom} at orders $\sigma-t$ and $\sigma$.

[Proposition 15 of arXiv:2604.07207, 'Mixing times of step-reinforced random walks'] Assume that $\alpha \in (0,1)$ and $L \geq 120$. There exist positive constants $C_1=C_1(\alpha)$, $C_2=C_2(\alpha)$ and $H_0=H_0(\alpha)$ such that if $n\geq H_0 L^{\frac{1}{\alpha}}$, then for any $k= 1,2,\dots, \lfloor L/40 \rfloor$, one has
$$
\PP\left(  \left|\left\{1\leq j \leq n: \frac{L}{96k} \leq |\CalC_{j,n}|<\frac{L}{2k}\right\}\right| \leq \frac{  C_2 k^{\frac{1}{\alpha}} n}{L^{\frac{1}{\alpha}}} \right)  \leq 7\exp\left(- \frac{ C_1  k^{\frac{1}{\alpha}}n}{L^{\frac{1}{\alpha}}}\right).
$$
In the case $\alpha=1/2$, if $L/\sqrt{\log L} \geq 120$, then for any $n\geq  H_0 L^{2}/\log L$ and any integer $k \in [\sqrt{\log L}, \lfloor L/40 \rfloor]$, one has,  
$$
\PP\left(  \left|\left\{1\leq j \leq n: \frac{L}{96k} \leq |\CalC_{j,n}|<\frac{L}{k}\right\}\right| \leq \frac{  C_2 k^{2} n}{4 L^{2}} \right)  \leq 7\exp\left(- \frac{ C_1  k^{2}n}{4 L^{2}}\right).
$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition def:back-transition of arXiv:2602.21315, 'The Instability of all Backoff Protocols\thanks{For the purpose of Open Access, the author'] Fix $\lambda \in (0,1)$, a send sequence $\overline{p}$ with $p_0=1$, and a positive integer~$j_0$. Let $\tau_0$ be a non-negative integer. Let $\Psi_0$ be the  initialising high-level state with $\tau^{\Psi_0} = \tau_0$ and $j^{\Psi_0} = j_0$. 
Let $\mathrm{hls}$ be the $\Psi_0$-backoff bounding rule from Definition~(def:backoff-bounding-rule of the paper).
Let $V$ be a volume process from $\Psi_0$ with transition rule $\mathrm{hls}$, send sequence~$\overline{p}$ and birth rate~$\lambda$. 
For any $t>\tau_0$ 
the high-level state transition 
given by 
$\Psi(t) 
= \mathrm{hls}(\Psi(t-1), {\overline{b}}^{Y_{t-1}}_{[j^{\Psi(t-1)}]}(t), t)$ is a \emph{back transition} if 
$\textup{type}^{\Psi(t)} = \textup{refilling}$ and
one of the following hold:
\begin{itemize}
\item $\textup{type}^{\Psi(t-1)} = \textup{refilling}$, and the transition is via (R(item:R5 of the paper))(i); or
\item $\textup{type}^{\Psi(t-1)} = \textup{stabilising}$, and the transition is via (R(item:R2 of the paper))(ii) or (R(item:R6 of the paper))(i).
\end{itemize}
title: Definition def:back-transition of arXiv:2602.21315

[Proposition prop:mode of arXiv:2607.19844, 'Binomial probabilities at a fixed distance from the mode:\\ size-biasing and the complete '] The upper mode of $\operatorname{Bin}(N,p)$ is
	\[
		\lfloor(N+1)p\rfloor=\nu+\lfloor p-h\rfloor
		=\begin{cases}\nu, & h\le p,\\[2pt] \nu-1, & h>p,\end{cases}
	\]

	When $h=p$ (equivalently $(N+1)p\in\mathbb Z$), the lower adjacent point $\nu-1$ is also a mode.

[Definition 12 (Quantum triangles with  {possibly} thin vertices) of arXiv:2608.27630, 'Oriented planar maps and \\ annular mating of trees'] Fix $W_1, W_2, W_3>0$. Let $I:=\{i\in\{1,2,3\}:W_i<\frac{\gamma^2}{2}\}$. Let $\tilde W_i = W_i$ if $i \not \in I$ and $\tilde W_i = \gamma^2 - W_i$ if $i \in I$. Sample $(S_0, (S_i)_{i \in I})$ from 
 \[\QT(\tilde W_1, \tilde W_2, \tilde W_3) \times \prod_{i\in I } (1-\frac{2W_i}{\gamma^2}) \Md_2(W_i).  \]
 Embed $S_0$ as $(\tilde D, \phi, \tilde a_1, \tilde a_2, \tilde a_3)$, for each $i \not \in I$ let $a_i = \tilde a_i$, and for each $i \in I$ embed $S_i$ as $(\tilde D_i, \phi, \tilde a_i, a_i)$ in such a way that the $\tilde D_i$ are disjoint and $\tilde D_i \cap \tilde D = \tilde a_i$. Let $D = \tilde D \cup \bigcup_{i \in I} \tilde D_i$ and let $\QT(W_1, W_2, W_3)$ be the law of $(D, \phi, a_1, a_2, a_3)/{\sim_\gamma}$.
title: Quantum triangles with  {possibly} thin vertices

ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Try a direct cluster-expansion (Mayer-type) argument for the susceptibility at fixed p (2d) in the d -> infinity limit. Result: At p = lambda/(2d) the expected cluster size chi(p) has, for fixed lambda < 1, a convergent expansion as d -> infinity in powers of 1/d obtained by comparing the cluster to a branching process with Poisson(lambda) offspring and counting cycles: the first correction is the non-backtracking one: an exploration with s - 1 = 2d - 1 new neighbours per vertex has critical point 1/(s-1) = s^-1 + s^-2 + s^-3 + ..., which already gives a_1 = a_2 = 1 with s = 2d; the cycles of Z^d first change the expansion at order s^-3, where the 4-cycles move the coefficient from 1 to the known 7/2. This direct route reproduces a_1, a_2 by hand; a_3 = 7/2 is the first coefficient the cycles change, and getting it requires the 4-cycle corrections together with the self-avoidance of the exploration; I did not complete it. Existence of the expansion to all orders without the lace expansion would need a general theorem that the non-backtracking cycle corrections form an asymptotic series, which is a version of the lace expansion in disguise (the lace expansion IS the systematic bookkeeping of these corrections); a Mayer-type expansion at fixed lambda < 1 converges for the subcritical susceptibility, and p_c is then the divergence point of the series in lambda, whose location in powers of 1/d is obtained by inverting the series, which is a purely algebraic step if the expansion of chi is known to all orders with uniform error terms. So: an alternative derivation exists in principle via the convergent subcritical cluster expansion plus inversion, but the uniformity of the subcritical expansion up to lambda near 1 is exactly the difficult point. Computing a_4 by hand would require the next order of cycle corrections; not done. Obstruction: Uniformity of the subcritical cluster expansion up to the critical point; a_4 requires third-order cycle corrections.

Let $D$ be a long virtual knot diagram.

[Lemma lem:hill-scc of arXiv:2608.08375, 'Algebraic formulas for first-passage times of Markov processes in the linear framework: ge'] Under the conditions stated previously, if $i \in \overline{Z}$, then $i \leadsto_{\mathcal{H}_u[G]} u$, so that $\mathcal{H}_u[G]$ has one terminal SCC, which must include $u$.

\proof If $i = u$, then, by definition, $i \leadsto_{\mathcal{H}_u[G]} u$. If $i \not= u$, then $i \leadsto_G z$ for some $z \in Z$. By Definition~(def:hill of the paper).2 and 3, the last edge on any path from $i$ to $z$ in $G$ is rerouted to $u$ in $\mathcal{H}_u[G]$, so that $i \leadsto_{\mathcal{H}_u[G]} u$, as claimed. The final assertion follows in consequence. \hfill \qed (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lem AnalyticStraightLine of arXiv:2506.18207, 'Cartan's Path Development, the Logarithmic Signature and a Conjecture of Lyons-Sidorova'] Let $\gamma:\left[0,K\right]\rightarrow\mathbb{R}^{2}$
be a continuous BV path with unit speed parametrisation. Let $s$ be a point at which
$\gamma$ is differentiable. Let $T\in(s,K]$ be chosen such that \[
\big|\gamma_{t}-\gamma_{s}-\gamma'_{s}(t-s)\big|\leqslant\frac{1}{6}(t-s),\ \Big|\Big|\frac{\gamma_{t}-\gamma_{s}}{t-s}\Big|-1\Big|\leqslant\frac{1}{6}
\]for all $t\in(s,T]$ and
\[
\left|\gamma_{t}-\gamma_{s}\right|<\left|\gamma_{T}-\gamma_{s}\right|
\]for all $t\in(s,T)$. Suppose that $\log S\left(\gamma\right)$ has infinite R.O.C. on
the interval $\left[s,T\right]$. Then the following two statements hold true.

\vspace{2mm}\noindent (i) One has
\[
\eta\left(\tilde{\gamma},\left(x,y\right)\right)=0
\]for all $\left(x,y\right)\in\left(0,1\right)\times\mathbb{R}\backslash\tilde{\gamma}\left[s,T\right]$. Here $\tilde{\gamma}\triangleq\gamma|_{[s,T]}\sqcup(\gamma_{s}-\gamma_{T}).$

\vspace{2mm}\noindent (ii) Let $L$ be the line segment joining $\gamma_{s}$ to $\gamma_{T}$ (also parametrised on $[s,T]$).
Then for any smooth one-form $\Phi(x,y)=f(x,y)dx+g(x,y)dy$, one has

[Theorem theorem1 of arXiv:2607.01463, 'Two Multi--Draw Coupon Collector models with different retention rules'] Consider the  $d$ coupon collector's problem (d--CCP), where in each run we keep \textbf{all} the new observed coupons. Let $T_{N,d}$ be the number of trials until all $N$ different types of coupons, which are uniformly distributed, are collected (at least once). Then,
\begin{equation}
\mathbb {E}\left[T_{N,d}\right]=\binom{N}{d} \sum_{k=1}^{N}\left(-1\right)^{k+1}\binom{N}{k}\Bigg(\binom{N}{d}-\binom{N-k}{d}\Bigg)^{-1}.

\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Express the escape probability through the branching-process representation for the one-cookie deterministic case. Result: In the deterministic environment with one cookie of strength p at each site (M = 1, delta = 2p - 1... transient iff delta > 1 which needs more than one cookie; take M = 2 cookies of strength p each, delta = 2(2p - 1) > 1 iff p > 3/4). The event of never returning to 0 after the first step: the walk must never come back, which in the branching-process picture (right excursions counted by the number of down-crossings of each edge) means the branching process with migration started from the edge (0,1) never produces a down-crossing of (0,1) into 0... the escape probability equals the probability that the total number of down-crossings of the edge (0,1) is zero, which is P(the branching process with migration started at 1 individual at level 1 has zero descendants at level 0) - not directly a standard extinction probability but a hitting probability of the time-reversed process. For the source's example [Zer05, Th. 18] the closed form exists; for general bounded stacks the escape probability is the solution of a finite-dimensional fixed-point equation obtained by conditioning on the first cookie stack at sites 1, 2, ...: define q_k = P(never return to 0 | walk currently at k, all cookies at sites >= k intact, cookies at sites < k in their post-visit states); the states of the sites already visited matter only through the remaining cookie counts, which for M bounded is a finite vector, and the walk's returns to 0 require descending through all visited sites; the escape probability then equals the probability of survival of a Markov chain on finite cookie-count vectors, computable numerically for given (M, p) but with no closed form in general. Recorded: reduction to a finite-state escape problem; closed form only in special cases. Obstruction: No closed form beyond special cases; the reduction gives a numerical procedure only.

[Lemma 3 of arXiv:2607.22374, 'Asymptotic properties of the heat equation driven by stochastic measure'] (Lemma 2.8~\cite{radbook})
Let $Z$ be an arbitrary set, and the function $q(z,x):
Z\times [j, j+1]\to\rr$ be such that all paths $q(z,\cdot)$ are continuous on $[j,j+1]$, $\aaa\subset(j,j+1]$ be a Borel set. Denote
\[
q_n(z,x)=\sum_{1\le k\le 2^n}q(z,{d}_{(k-1)n}^{(j)}){\bf 1}_{\Delta_{kn}^{(j)}}(x).
\]
Then the random function
\[
\eta(z)=\int_{\aaa}q(z, x)\,d\mu(x),\ z\in Z,
\]
has a version
\begin{equation}\begin{split}
\widetilde{\eta}(z)  = \int_{\aaa}q_0(z,x)\,d\mu(x)
+\sum_{n\ge 1}\Bigl(\int_{\aaa}q_n(z,x)\,d\mu(x)-\int_{\aaa}q_{n-1}(z,x)\,d\mu(x)\Bigr)
\end{split}
\end{equation}
such that for all $\beta>0$, $\omega\in\Omega$, $z\in Z$
\begin{equation} \begin{split}
|\widetilde{\eta}(z)| \le  |q(z,j)\mu(\aaa)|\\
  + \Bigl\{\sum_{n\ge 1}2^{n\beta}
\sum_{1\le k\le 2^{n}}|q(z,d_{kn}^{(j)})-q(z,d_{(k-1)n}^{(j)})|^2\Bigr\}^{1/2}\\
\times\Bigl\{\sum_{n\ge 1}2^{-n\beta}\sum_{1\le k\le 2^{n}}|\mu(\Delta_{kn}^{(j)}\cap\aaa)|^2\Bigr\}^{1/2}.
\end{split}
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

\item[(ii)] For $\delta=1$, $$X_n\to\overline{X}=\begin{cases}
1 \ &\ \text{if}\ L<t\\
u_0^{N_t}, \ &\ \text{if}\ L\ge t.\end{cases}$$
In particular, $u(t) = \overline{u}(t)={\mathbb{E}}(\overline{X})$ is well-defined and $\overline{u}(t)\to1$ as $t\to\infty$ 
\item[(iii)] For $\delta >1$, the limit 
$$X_\infty(t) = \lim_{n\to\infty}X_n(t) = \begin{cases}
\infty \ &\ \text{if}\ S<t\\
u_0^{N_t}, \ &\ \text{if}\ S\ge t.\end{cases}$$
In particular,  ${\mathbb{E}}(X_\infty(t))=\infty$ for all $t>0$ 
\end{enumerate}
\item Suppose that $u_0>1$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] For $\delta\in [0,1)$,
\[X_n\to\overline{X}=\begin{cases}
0 ,\ &\ \text{if}\ S<t\\
u_0^{N_t}, \ &\ \text{if}\ S\ge t.\end{cases}\]
In particular, for all $t>0$
$$\underline{u}(t) ={\mathbb{E}}(\underline{X}(t))
\ \begin{cases} <\infty, \ &\ \text{if}\ u_0<(2\alpha-1)/4,\\
                         =\infty, \ & \text{in finite time if}\  u_0>2\alpha-1,\\
                         \text{unknown} & \text{in other cases.}
                        \end{cases}
      $$
 If there is a locally integrable function $g$ such that $X_n\le g$ for all $n$, then
  $\underline{u}(t)={\mathbb{E}}\underline{X}(t)<\infty$.
\item[(ii)] For $\delta =1$, 
$$X_n(t)\to\overline{X}(t) =\begin{cases}
\infty & \text{on} \ [N_t=\infty]\\
u_0^{N_t} & \text{on} \ [N_t<\infty].
\end{cases}$$
In particular, if $\alpha\in(1,2)$, then $\mathbb{E}(\overline{X}(t)) = \infty$, and if $\alpha>2$ then 
$\overline{X}(t)\in\mathbb{R}$ is well-defined for all $t>0$, while
\[
\overline{u}(t) ={\mathbb{E}}(\overline{X}(t))
\ \begin{cases} <\infty, \ &\ \text{if}\ u_0<(2\alpha-1)/4-(6\alpha^2-15\alpha+4)/4(\alpha-1)(2\alpha-1),\\
                         =\infty, \ & \text{in finite time if}\  u_0>2\alpha-1\ \text{or}\ \alpha\in(0,2),\\
                         \text{unknown} & \text{in other cases}.
                        \end{cases}
\]
\item[(iii)] For $\delta>1$, 
$$X_n\to{X}_{\infty}=\begin{cases}
\infty \ &\ \text{if}\ S<t\\
u_0^{N_t} \ &\ \text{if}\  S\ge t.\end{cases}$$
$u(t) ={\mathbb{E}}({X}_\infty(t)) = \infty$ for all $t>0$.
\end{enumerate} 
\end{enumerate}
