ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Examine whether the Gaussian free field characterisation can be made asymptotically exact. Result: DLP show t_cov ≍ |E| (E max GFF)^2; the later result of Ding (2012, 'Asymptotics of cover times via Gaussian free fields: bounded-degree graphs and general trees') gives asymptotic equality t_cov ~ |E| (E max eta)^2 for bounded-degree graphs when t_cov/t_hit -> infinity, and Zhai (2018) proved the asymptotic formula for general graphs under the same condition. Given the asymptotic formula, a (1+eps) approximation of t_cov reduces to a (1+eps) approximation of E max of a Gaussian vector with given covariance (the Green function), which is a deterministic computational problem: computing E max of a Gaussian vector to within 1+eps is not known to be in deterministic polynomial time in general (the majorizing-measure/generic-chaining bounds are only within constants; exact computation of Gaussian maxima expectations is #P-hard in some formulations). So the question reduces, for graphs with t_cov/t_hit -> infinity, to the deterministic approximability of E max of a Gaussian vector with a graph-Laplacian covariance; a positive answer would follow from a deterministic FPTAS for Gaussian expected maxima on such covariances, which is open; graphs with t_cov ≍ t_hit (e.g. cycles, where the cover time is dominated by hitting times) need a separate treatment and are the easier case since hitting times are computable exactly. Reduction recorded. Key identity: t_cov ~ |E| (E max GFF)^2 when t_cov/t_hit -> infinity (Ding; Zhai), so (1+eps)-approximation reduces to approximating a Gaussian expected maximum. Obstruction: No deterministic (1+eps) algorithm for Gaussian expected maxima with general covariance.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-c0116-deterministic-1-epsilon-approximation-of-the-cover-time
No independent review; result status attempted_unsolved

$$

[Prop P:temporal-est of arXiv:2604.10020, 'The directed landscape in half-space'] Take $n < n+r \le 2n \in \mathbb{N}$, and parameter $\alpha \ge 1/2 - n^{-1/6}$. For any $x, y_2\in \llbracket0, n/1000 \rrbracket$, denote $y_1 = \lfloor x + n(y_2-x)/(n + r) \rfloor$, and 
$u_1 = [x, 0; y_1, n]_\textsf{L}$, $u_2 = [x, 0; y_2, n + r]_\textsf{L}$.
Take any $\epsilon > 0$ satisfying the constraints:
\begin{equation}
	
	C_0 \max \left(\frac{|x-y_2|^2}{n^2}, ((1/2 - \alpha)\vee 0)^2\right) < \epsilon < C_* r^{-1/3},
\end{equation}
where $C_0>0$ is a universal constant, and $C_*>0$ is any large enough number. 
Then for a constant $c>0$ depending only on $C_*$, we have
$$
\mathbb{P}\left( \left|\bar X(u_1) - \bar X(u_2)\right| \ge \epsilon r \right) \le 2\exp\left(-c \epsilon^{3/2} r \right).
$$
title: Prop P:temporal-est of arXiv:2604.10020

DRAFT proof (unaudited), T318-C8 v1. Let a test input x have an arbitrary finite-dimensional Gaussian law, let A be PSD, V=xprime A x, q=EV, and f=xprime delta with deterministic delta conditional on the training environment; f and V need not be independent. Put R=Ef^2 and v=Var(V)<infinity. Then abs(E[(1+f^2)/(1+V)]-(1+R)/(1+q))<=sqrt(3v)(1+R), and abs(E log(1+V)-log(1+q))<=sqrt(v). This follows from the noncentral scalar Gaussian bound Ef^4<=3R^2 and the 1-Lipschitz reciprocal/log functions on nonnegative arguments. The ratio error is relative to 1+R, so a uniform lower risk bound can survive even when R is unbounded as a regularization parameter approaches zero: first require 1/(1+q)-sqrt(3v)>0, then insert a common lower bound on R. For any PSD covariance C, teacher w and fitted vector w_hat in a subspace S, the bound (w_hat-w)prime C(w_hat-w)>=wprime C^(1/2) P C^(1/2)w holds with P the orthogonal projection onto (C^(1/2)S)^perp. A Euclidean nullspace projection does not supply the same bound. These two facts yield C8 realized-teacher non-tightness of global likelihood-temperature minimizers in C7 offset-linear random features; that application requires all C7 assumptions and is not a probability-one escape claim. No novelty or independent-audit claim.
Finite-dimensional Gaussian test input, PSD quadratic denominator, scalar linear Gaussian numerator as stated; conditional training quantities fixed.
For the lower-risk substitution the relative coefficient must be positive; no independence of numerator/denominator.

body: In mathematics, the multiplicative ergodic theorem, or Oseledets theorem provides the theoretical background for computation of Lyapunov exponents of a nonlinear dynamical system. It was proved by Valery Oseledets in 1965 and reported at the International Mathematical Congress in Moscow in 1966. A conceptually different proof of the multiplicative ergodic theorem was found by M. S. Raghunathan. The theorem has been extended to semisimple Lie groups by V. A. Kaimanovich and further generalized in the works of David Ruelle, Grigory Margulis, Anders Karlsson, and François Ledrappier.

[Theorem 37 (Theorem 3.4 in \cite{nv1}) of arXiv:2609.00183, '2609.00183'] There exist $\delta_R(n)>0$ and $C_R(n)>0$ such that the following argument holds.
For any $R>0$, let $\{B_{r_j/5}(x_j)\}_{x_j\in S}\subset B_{3R}(0)$ be mutually disjoint
with $x_j\in B_R(0)$, and let
\[
\mu=\sum_j \omega_k r_j^k\delta_{x_j}.
\]
If for every $B_r(y)\subset B_{2R}(0)$ we have
\[
\int_{B_r(y)}\left(\int_0^r D_\mu^k(z,s)\frac{ds}{s}\right)\,d\mu(z) \leq \delta_R^2 r^k,
\]
then
\[
\mu(B_R(0))=\omega_k\sum_{i \in I}r_i^k\le C_R(n)R^k.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 3.4 in \cite{nv1}

Let (X_n)_{n=1}^\infty be independent real random variables, and fix c > 0. Define the truncated variables Y_n = X_n \mathbf{1}_{\{|X_n| \le c\}}. Then the series \sum_{n=1}^\infty X_n converges almost surely if and only if all three of the following series converge: (1) \sum_{n=1}^\infty \mathbb{P}(|X_n| > c) < \infty; (2) \sum_{n=1}^\infty \mathbb{E}[Y_n] \text{ converges in } \mathbb{R}; (3) \sum_{n=1}^\infty \text{Var}(Y_n) < \infty.
(X_n) independent
c > 0 constant

[Corollary 3 (Maximal EPI on connected compact groups) of arXiv:2608.22534, 'Entropy power inequalities in compact groups'] Let $G$ be a compact and metrizable topological abelian group,
equipped with its Borel $\sigma$-algebra. For any pair
of independent random 
variables $X,Y$ on $G$,
$$h(X+Y)\geq \max\big\{h(X),h(Y)\big\}.$$
Moreover, suppose that $G$ is connected and 
$\max{\{h(X),h(Y)\}} = h(Y) >-\infty$. Then we have
equality if and only if either $Y$ is uniformly distributed
on $G$ or $h(X)=-\infty$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Maximal EPI on connected compact groups

[Corollary 10 of arXiv:2608.03922, 'Absolute continuity of two-dimensional polynomial random vectors'] Let $M>0$ and let $d,n\in\mathbb N$. Let
$\mu=\mu_1\otimes\cdots\otimes\mu_n$,
where each $\mu_j$ is a probability measure with density $\varrho_j$ satisfying
\[
0\le \varrho_j(x_j)\le M
\quad \forall x_j\in\mathbb R,
\quad \forall j\in\{1,\ldots,n\}.
\]
Then, for every $f\in \mathcal{P}_d(\mathbb{R}^n)$, one has
\[
[f]_\infty
\le
2(8d^2(1+M))^d\|f\|_{L^1(\mu)}.
\]

  \]

[Thm 13 of arXiv:2607.03924, 'Tree Coordinates and Range Martingales for Positive Operator-Valued Measures'] Let $\left(K_{E},P,V\right)$ be the range space
dilation from \prettyref{sec:3}. Self-adjoint operators $T\in B\left(K_{E}\right)$
satisfying 
\[
TP\left(B\right)=P\left(B\right)T,\qquad B\in\mathcal{B}\left(\Omega_{m}\right),
\]
are in one-to-one correspondence with bounded range martingales $\left\{ X_{w}\right\} $.
The correspondence is given by 
\begin{equation}
U^{*}_{n}TU_{n}=\bigoplus_{\left|w\right|=n}X_{w},\qquad n\geq0.
\end{equation}

Method: Relaxation of linear-polymer coagulation and fragmentation structural calculation Result: The cluster-count coordinate K has exact rates K->K+1 at beta*(n-K) and K->K-1 at K*(K-1)/n. Its deterministic equilibrium density mu solves mu^2=beta*(1-mu), and linearizing the density drift gives restoring rate beta+2*mu=sqrt(beta^2+4*beta). At beta=b/n this is order n^-1/2. Replacing K by its stationary mean inside the exponential has the wrong Jensen direction and is not a proof of the desired upper bound.

body: In algebra and number theory, Wilson's theorem states that a natural number n > 1 is a prime number if and only if the product of all the positive integers less than n is one less than a multiple of n. That is (using the notations of modular arithmetic), the factorial $(n-1)!=1\times 2\times 3\times \cdots \times (n-1)$ satisfies $$(n-1)!\ \equiv \;-1{\pmod {n}}$$

body:
[Theorem thm:limit of arXiv:2606.30475, 'Ancestries in random $d$-DAGs'] As $n\to\infty$, the number of ancestors of $i$ in $G_n$ satisfies the following:
 \begin{enumerate}[(i)]
  \item For $i=o\big(n^{(d-1)/d}\big)$, we have $n^{-1} a_i(n)\stackrel{\mathbb{P}}{\longrightarrow} 1$.
  \item For $i\sim \alpha n^{(d-1)/d}$ with $\alpha>0$, we have $n^{-1} a_i(n) \stackrel{\mathrm{d}}{\longrightarrow} \Xi_\alpha$, where $\Xi_\alpha$ is a random variable on $[0,1]$ with cumulative distribution function
  \begin{equation}
   \mathbb{P}(\Xi_\alpha\leq \gamma) = 1 - e^{-\frac{\alpha^d}{d-1}\big((1-\gamma)^{1-d}-1\big)}.
  \end{equation}
  Moreover, the convergence also holds for all moments.
  \item For $i=\omega\big(n^{(d-1)/d}\big)$ and $i=o(n)$, we have $(i/n)^d a_i(n)\stackrel{\mathrm{d}}{\longrightarrow} \mathsf{Exp}(1)$, where the convergence also holds for all moments.
  \item For $i\sim \beta n$ with $0<\beta \leq 1$, we have $a_i(n)\stackrel{\mathrm{d}}{\longrightarrow} \mathsf{Geo}(\beta^d)$, again with convergence of all moments.
 \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 5 (Local relative-energy identity) of arXiv:2608.30715, 'Endpoint Energy Atoms Force Local Pressure Concentration in Three-Dimensional Navier--Stok'] Let \(\psi\ge0\) be smooth on \([\tau,t]\times\Omega\). Then
\begin{equation}
 \begin{aligned}
 &\frac12\int_\Omega\psi(t)\abs{r_\tau(t)}^2\dd x
 +\nu\int_\tau^t\int_\Omega\psi\abs{\nabla r_\tau}^2\dd x\dd\rho\\
 &=
 \frac12\int_\tau^t\int_\Omega
 (\partial_\rho\psi+u\cdot\nabla\psi+\nu\Delta\psi)
 \abs{r_\tau}^2\dd x\dd\rho\\
&\quad+
 \int_\tau^t\int_\Omega
 \psi\,\nabla\pi_w\cdot g_\tau\dd x\dd\rho
 +\int_\tau^t\int_\Omega
 \pi_w c_\tau\cdot\nabla\psi\dd x\dd\rho .
 \end{aligned}
 
\end{equation}

[Proposition 13 of arXiv:2606.16164, 'A Low-Regularity Semigroup Sewing Lemma via Quotient Structures'] Let $h\in Z\hat C(\Delta_T^3;B_\alpha)$ and let $(r^\tau)_{\tau\in[0,T]}$ be a compatible frozen increment family over $h$. For $0\le s\le t\le T$, define $R_{ts}:=r^t_{ts}$. Then
\[
R\in C(\Delta_T^2;B_\alpha)\  \text{\,and\,} \ \hat\delta R = h.
\]
Moreover, if $\gamma\in(0,1)$ and for every $0<\varepsilon<\gamma$, $$ \sup_{\tau\in[0,T]}\|r^\tau\|_{\gamma-\varepsilon,\alpha+\varepsilon;\tau}<\infty,$$ then
$R\in E^{\gamma}(\Delta_T^2; B_\alpha)$ and for every $0<\varepsilon<\gamma$,
\begin{equation}

\|R\|_{\gamma-\varepsilon,\alpha+\varepsilon}
\le
\sup_{\tau\in[0,T]}
\|r^\tau\|_{\gamma-\varepsilon,\alpha+\varepsilon;\tau}.
\end{equation}
Similarly, if 
$$\sup_{\tau\in[0,T]}\|r^\tau\|_{1,\log;\tau,\alpha}+\sup_{\tau\in[0,T]}\|r^\tau\|_{1-\varepsilon,\alpha+\varepsilon;\tau}<\infty$$
for every $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, then $R\in E_{\log}^{1}(\Delta_T^2; B_\alpha)$ and
\[
\|R\|_{1,\log;\alpha}\le\sup_{\tau\in[0,T]}\|r^\tau\|_{1,\log;\tau,\alpha}, \quad \|R\|_{1-\varepsilon,\alpha+\varepsilon}\le\sup_{\tau\in[0,T]}\|r^\tau\|_{1-\varepsilon,\alpha+\varepsilon;\tau}.
\]
title: Proposition 13 of arXiv:2606.16164

body:
[Proposition 12 of arXiv:2609.01460, 'On cost-induced Santal\'o-type inequalities \\ in Polish measure spaces'] Let $d\in \N$ and $\alpha>0$. Let $\Omega:\R_+\to \R_+$ be a measurable function such that 
    \[
    0 < \int_{0}^{\infty}\Omega\left(t^\alpha\right)t^{d-1}\,dt < +\infty.
    \]
    Then, for every star body $L\subset \R^d$, it holds that
    \begin{equation}
    
    \vol[d](L) = \frac{1}{d} \frac{\int_{\R^d}\Omega\left(\|x\|_{L}^\alpha\right)\,dx}{\int_0^\infty \Omega\left(t^\alpha\right)t^{d-1}\,dt}.
    \end{equation}
title: Proposition 12 of arXiv:2609.01460

[Lemma 26 of arXiv:2604.00630, 'The contact process on a bipartite spatial network'] Let~$\pi=(\pi_0,\ldots,\pi_\ell)$ be a combinatorial path of length~$\ell$ with~$k$ distinct vertices; assume that~$\pi_\ell \notin\{\pi_0,\ldots,\pi_{\ell-1}\}$. Let~$T$ be the discovery tree of~$\pi$.  Then, the expected number of paths~$\Gamma$ in~$\mathcal G$ that start at the root, have combinatorial path equal to~$\pi$, and have all vertices blue, except for the last, which is red, is:
			\[
				\prod_{\substack{m \in T\backslash \{\pi_\ell\}:\\ \mathrm{dist}_{T}(\pi_0,m) \text{ is even}}} \mathscr U_{\deg_T(m)} \cdot\prod_{\substack{m \in T\backslash \{\pi_\ell\}:\\ \mathrm{dist}_{T}(\pi_0,m) \text{ is odd}}} \mathscr V_{\deg_T(m)}\cdot \int_0^{\mathfrak{u}_1} u^{-\gamma_1}\;\mathrm{d}u
			\]
			if~$\ell$ is even, and
			\[
				\prod_{\substack{m \in T\backslash \{\pi_\ell\}:\\ \mathrm{dist}_{T}(\pi_0,m) \text{ is even}}} \mathscr U_{\deg_T(m)} \cdot\prod_{\substack{m \in T\backslash \{\pi_\ell\}:\\ \mathrm{dist}_{T}(\pi_0,m) \text{ is odd}}} \mathscr V_{\deg_T(m)}\cdot \int_0^{\mathfrak{u}_2} v^{-\gamma_2}\;\mathrm{d}v 
			\]
			if~$\ell$ is odd. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma 26 of arXiv:2604.00630

body:
[Definition Driver--Sengupta measure of arXiv:2602.08591, 'The Yang--Mills measure on compact surfaces as a \\ universal scaling limit of lattice gau'] Let $(\rho_t)_{t>0}$ be as above and let $\mathbb{G}$ be a finite graph on $\mathcal{S}$. 
The \emph{Driver--Sengupta measure} associated with $(\rho_t)_{t>0}$ and $\mathbb{G}$ is the probability measure on $G^{\mathbb{E}_+}$, denoted by $\mathrm{DS}(\rho,\mathbb{G})$, whose density with respect to the product Haar measure $\mathrm{d} g$ on $G^{\mathbb{E}_+}$ is given by
\[
\mathrm{d} \mathrm{DS}(\rho,\mathbb{G})\big((g_e)_{e \in \mathbb{E}_+}\big) 
 = \frac{1}{Z_{\rho,\mathbb{G}}}
   \prod_{F \in \mathbb{F}} \rho_{\sigma(F)}\big(\mathrm{Hol}(g,\partial F)\big)\, \mathrm{d} g.
\]
Here $\partial F$ is the oriented boundary of $F$, the time parameter $\sigma(F)>0$ is the area of $F$, and $Z_{\rho,\mathbb{G}}$ is the normalizing constant.
title: Driver--Sengupta measure

Let d>=1, L>=m>0 and R>0. Let U:R^d->R be C1, have an everywhere-existing Hessian and globally L-Lipschitz gradient, with grad U(0)=0. Put Omega=R^d minus B(0,R). Assume V(x)=U(x)-(m/2)||x||_2^2 is convex on Omega in this precise sense: V(sum_j a_j x_j)<=sum_j a_j V(x_j) whenever a_j>=0, sum_j a_j=1, all x_j belong to Omega and their barycenter also belongs to Omega. Put mu(dx) proportional to exp(-U(x))dx and kappa=L/m. For epsilon in (0,1), initialize X_0~N(0,I_d/L). Run the unadjusted Langevin algorithm X_{k+1}=X_k-h grad U(X_k)+sqrt(2h)G_k with independent G_k~N(0,I_d), choosing h=c exp(-16 L R^2) kappa^{-1} L^{-1} epsilon^2/d for a sufficiently small positive absolute constant c. Then the number of iterations needed for total-variation distance to mu at most epsilon is at most ceil(C exp(32 L R^2) kappa^2 (d/epsilon^2) log(d/epsilon^2)) for an absolute C. The bound is polynomial in d only when its displayed parameter dependence is also polynomial.

[Thm t:thm_q of arXiv:2504.07255, 'A Tail-Respecting Splitting Numerical Scheme\\ for L\'evy-Driven SDEs With Superlinear Dri'] Let assumptions
$\mathbf{H}^{\mathrm{Lip}_+}_A$,
$\mathbf{H}_{A_x,A_{xx}}$,
$\mathbf{H}_{a,b,c}^{\mathrm{Lip}_b}$, and
$\mathbf{H}_{\nu,p}$
 hold. Then, 
 for any $T\in[0,\infty)$ and $q\in (0,p)$ there is convergence
\begin{equation}\begin{aligned}
\sup_{t\in[0, T]} \mathbf{E} \|X_t^n-X_t\|^q \leq_C h_n^{\bar \delta}(1+\|x\|^p),
\end{aligned}\end{equation}
with the convergence rate
\begin{equation}\begin{aligned}
\bar\delta=\frac{p-q}{\chi}\wedge\frac{q}{2}\wedge 1.
\end{aligned}\end{equation}
In particular, if $\chi=0$, i.e., if the drift $A$ has bounded first derivatives, the convergence rate reduces to
\begin{equation}\begin{aligned}
\bar\delta=\frac{q}{2}\wedge 1.
\end{aligned}\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Tang, Chen and Liu, Beyond Quadratic Loss: The Stability Phase Diagram of Adam, arXiv2609.18314v1, Theorem3, treats L(x)=k|x|^n with k>0,n>2,1/2<beta1<1,0<beta2<1,v0>0,epsilon=0 and the imposed recurrence v_next=beta2*v. Conditional on attraction to either nonzero fixed point of the rescaled dynamics, the source concludes eventual absence of EoS-triggered spikes when beta1*beta2^(-n/(2*(n-2)))<1. Rescaling x_t=q^t*y_t with q=beta2^(1/(2*(n-2))) gives a second-order recurrence whose previous-position coefficient is beta1*beta2^(-n/(2*(n-2))). The imposed variance recurrence omits the ordinary squared-gradient addition. This theorem therefore does not cover n=2, positive epsilon, standard v0=0, or generic convergence to a quadratic unstable origin. Section3 Figure3(a) instead reports a numerical quadratic beta-boundary from finite trajectories, not a theorem about standard-initialization basin measure.

body: In probability theory, Markov's inequality gives an upper bound on the probability that a non-negative random variable is greater than or equal to some positive constant. \beq 
	\ol \caL (\SNR) = \E_\caX \left[ \prod_{i<j} \frac{p(\sqrt{N} W_{ij} - \sqrt{\SNR N} x_i x_j)}{p(\sqrt{N} W_{ij})} \prod_k \frac{p_d(\sqrt{N} W_{kk} - \sqrt{\SNR N} x_k^2)}{p_d(\sqrt{N} W_{kk})} \right].
\eeq
title: Likelihood ratio for i.i.d. prior

$$
\cD_{r,n}(x):=\left|\bbP(W_n\leq x)-\Phi(x)-\varphi(x)\sum_{j=1}^{r}B_n^{-j}H_{j,n}(x)\right|\leq C_n(1+|x|)^{-s}B_n^{-r}
$$
where $C_n\to 0$
and  $H_{j,n}$ are polynomials with uniformly bounded coefficients and degrees not depending on $n$.
title: Non Uniform Exapnsions

 B_{\mathrm{Jac}}.}
 
\end{equation}
Consequently
\begin{equation}
 \operatorname{rank}\Pi_{\mathrm{sel}}
 =
 \operatorname{rank}C_{\mathrm{Betti}}.
 
\end{equation}

Across a Stokes ray, if
\(\Gamma^+=S\Gamma^-\), then
\[
 \mathcal P_{\mathrm{th}}^+
 =
 S\mathcal P_{\mathrm{th}}^-,
 \qquad
 C_{\mathrm{Betti}}^+
 =
 C_{\mathrm{Betti}}^-S^{-1}.
\]
Hence \(\Pi_{\mathrm{sel}}\) and its rank are unchanged.  Confluence may
produce poles or ramification in the analytic period factors at the
boundary of \(\mathfrak C\), but never in the integral Betti matrix.
At a finite confluence the Morse basis itself ceases to exist; its two
lateral coordinate matrices remain integral and are related by
Picard--Lefschetz monodromy.

Owner campaign draft, proof (unaudited); standard finite-population identities, independent audit and novelty assessment pending. Let P0=P on R^d have finite second moment, n>=1, h>=0, and r=0. Each generation draws n conditionally iid samples from Pt and forms their equal-weight Gaussian KDE with covariance h^2 I_d; bandwidth is constant within a trajectory. Let a=1-1/n, v0=tr Cov(P), mt=mean(Pt), and vt=E tr Cov(Pt), using the KDE's divisor-n covariance. For t>=1, vt=a^t v0+n d h^2(1-a^t), and E|mt-m0|^2=v0(1-a^t)+d h^2[t-n(1-a^t)]. Thus expected second moment about m0 is v0+t d h^2, although fixed-h within-generation variance approaches n d h^2. At h=0 the mean martingale converges in L2 to random M_infinity and E W2^2(Pt,delta_M_infinity)=2a^t v0. For n tending to infinity and t_n/n tending to infinity, centered expected variance tends to zero if and only if n h_n^2 tends to zero; h_n tending to zero alone is insufficient. If n h_n^2 tends to finite lambda, vt_n tends to d lambda. Covariance calculations do not determine the complete positive-bandwidth limit distribution or keep the random mean near m0 for all times. Proof: C003 v2, T356/proofs/review/c003_v2.md.

[Theorem 3 (Stationary-entry hitting) of arXiv:2605.14511, 'Clumsy and Careless:\\ Stationary-Entry Flux in Non-monotone Coupon Collectors'] Let $x_n$ be a sequence of initial states.  Assume
\[
        \pi_n(A_n)\to0,
        \qquad
        \mu_n\to0.
\]
Suppose there are integers $b_n,h_n,r_n\to\infty$ such that
\[
        h_n=o(b_n),\qquad b_n\mu_n\to0,
        \qquad \alpha_n(h_n)=o(b_n\mu_n),
\]
and such that the following two assumptions hold.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textnormal{(M\arabic*)},leftmargin=2.4em]
\item \textbf{Stationary one-block law.}  With
\[
        N_n^{(b)}:=\sum_{t=1}^{b_n}E_t,
\]
one has
\[
        \Pbb_{\pi_n}(N_n^{(b)}\ge1)=b_n\mu_n(1+o(1)).
\]
\item \textbf{Negligible initial burn-in.}  For this sequence $x_n$,
\[
        \Pbb_{x_n}(T_{A_n}\le r_n)=o(1),
        \qquad
        \|P_n^{r_n}(x_n,\cdot)-\pi_n\|_{\TV}=o(1),
        \qquad
        r_n\mu_n=o(1).
\]
\end{enumerate}
Then
\[
        \mu_n T_{A_n}\Rightarrow \Exp(1)
\]
under $\Pbb_{x_n}$.

[Corollary Weak Simplex Conjecture of arXiv:2607.14087, 'Stochastic Domination of Gaussian Maxima: A Resolution of the Weak Simplex Conjecture'] \label[corollary]{cor:wsc}
Let $m=d+1$, let $x_1,\ldots,x_m$ be unit vectors in $\mathbb R^d$, and let the
message $I$ be uniform on $\{1,\ldots,m\}$.  Under the channel
\[
  Y=\lambda x_I+Z,
  \qquad Z\sim\mathcal N(0,I_d),\quad \lambda>0,
\]
the average probability of correct maximum-likelihood decoding is no larger
than for a regular simplex.  For every fixed $\lambda>0$, equality holds if
and only if the $x_i$ form a regular simplex.  Thus the regular simplex is the
unique maximizer up to rotation and relabeling. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Weak Simplex Conjecture

[Lemma lem:nonback of arXiv:2602.21315, 'The Instability of all Backoff Protocols\thanks{For the purpose of Open Access, the author'] Fix a real number $\lambda \in (0,1)$ and a send sequence $\overline{p}$ with $p_0=1$. Let $j_0$ be a
sufficiently large integer.  
Let  
$\Psi_0$ be the initialising state with
$j^{\Psi_0} = j_0$ and $\tau^{\Psi_0} = \tau_0$.  
Let $\mathrm{hls}$ be  
the $\Psi_0$-backoff bounding rule from Definition~(def:backoff-bounding-rule of the paper).
Let $V$ be a volume process from~$\Psi_0$ with transition rule~$\mathrm{hls}$, send sequence~$\overline{p}$ and birth rate~$\lambda$.   For any
$t \ge \tau_0$, 
let   $T(t) = \{\tau_0,\ldots,t\}$.
Then  the following statement holds  for
every $t >  \tau_0$ and
every tuple
$ 
\overline{\psi}_{T(t-1)} = (\psi_{\tau_0},\dots,\psi_{t-1})$  of high-level states 
such that  
$\mathbb{P}( \overline{\Psi}_{T(t-1)} = \overline{\psi}_{T(t-1)}) > 0$ and 
$\textup{type}^{\psi_{t-1}} \in \{ \textup{refilling},\textup{stabilising}\}$, where
$j=j^{\psi_{t-1}}$.  
If
$\overline{\Psi}_{T(t-1)} = \overline{\psi}_{T(t-1)}
$ 
then 
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item for all $t'$ in the range $t-1 \leq t' \leq \mathrm{back}\textnormal{-}\mathrm{exit}(t-1)$, $j^{\Psi(t')} = j$,
\item for all $\hat{t}$ in  the range $t-1 \le \hat{t} < \mathrm{back}\textnormal{-}\mathrm{exit}(t-1)$ with  $\textup{type}^{\Psi(\hat{t})} = \textup{stabilising}$,  
$\mathrm{trans}(\hat{t}) \leq \hat{t} + j^{\phi+72}$, 
\item 
If $\mathcal{M}_{[j-1]}^{\psi_{t-1}}(\tau^{\psi_{t-1}}) \leq 
2j^{44} 
$ then
for all 
$\hat{t}$ in the range $t-1 \le \hat{t} < \mathrm{back}\textnormal{-}\mathrm{exit}(t-1)$
with $\textup{type}^{\Psi(\hat{t})} = \textup{refilling}$,   
$\mathrm{trans}(\hat{t})  \leq \hat{t} + j^{\phi+{46}}$, and
\item 
If $\mathcal{M}_{[j-1]}^{\psi_{t-1}}(\tau^{\psi_{t-1}}) \leq 
2j^{44} 
$ then
$\mathrm{back}\textnormal{-}\mathrm{exit}(t-1) \leq t-1 + j^{\phi+73}$. 
\end{enumerate}

Version 1, Target 1, kind bound; proofs (unaudited), 20 October 2026.

## C033: discrete-time semigroup subtraction

Let a=1/(3pi), b=1/(6pi^2), and A,B be the differential operators in C032.
One step of duration 1/n has P_n=I+A/n+B/n^2+O(n^(-5/2)) on positive
compacts. A diffusion step has exp(A/n)=I+A/n+A^2/(2n^2)+O(n^-3), for
sufficiently smooth local tests. Thus the local weak-error operator is

    C=B-A^2/2
     =(8u+a/5+b/u)D+(4u^2-3au/5)D^2.               (3)

This is an algebraic identity, not a global semigroup expansion at zero.
Direct differentiation gives

    A^2=(4u+2a)D+(14u^2+6au+a^2)D^2
                  +(8u^3+2au^2)D^3+u^4 D^4.

Subtracting half of this from C032's B proves (3); the third- and fourth-
derivative terms cancel exactly. Their inclusion before subtraction was
necessary. A global modified diffusion with this C is not asserted:
the drift b/u is singular and its second-order coefficient can be negative
near zero at finite n.

## C034: a rigorous logarithmic divergence of the limiting Duhamel functional

Use the reviewer-PASS C017 diffusion dU=(2U+a)ds+sqrt(2)U dW, U0=0,
and its semigroup P_s. Fix t>0 and f(u)=1-exp(-u). Define, for 0<epsilon<t,

    I_epsilon(t)=integral_epsilon^t E[(C P_(t-s)f)(U_s)] ds,
    D_t=(D P_t f)(0)=E[J_t exp(-U_t)],
    J_t=exp(t+sqrt(2)W_t).

Then 0<D_t<infinity, and there is a finite H_t such that

    I_epsilon(t)=(D_t/(2pi))log(1/epsilon)+H_t+O_t(sqrt(epsilon)). (4)

This statement concerns the specified cutoff integral for the limiting SDE.
It does not replace epsilon by 1/n inside a network weak-error theorem.

Proof of regularity. The solution from initial value u is U_v^u=U_v^0+uJ_v.
Consequently D^j P_v f(u)=E[J_v^j f^(j)(U_v^0+uJ_v)] for j>=1.
All these derivatives are bounded uniformly for 0<=v<=t, because Gaussian
exponentials J_v have every positive moment. Differentiation under expectation
is justified by these dominating moments. The time derivative of D P_v f
is bounded too: Af and (Af)' are bounded (polynomials times exp(-u)), and
the semigroup identity P_v f-f=integral_0^v P_r Af dr allows differentiation
in u. In particular, with h(s,u)=D P_(t-s) f(u),

    |h(s,u)-D_t|<=C_t(s+u), 0<=s<=t, u>=0.          (5)

The same bounded-derivative estimates apply to D^2 P_(t-s)f.

Proof of the entrance estimate. The explicit solution gives

    U_s=a integral_0^s exp((s-r)+sqrt(2)(W_s-W_r)) dr.

Let M_s=sup_(r<=s)|W_r| and H_s=s+2sqrt(2)M_s. Then
exp(-H_s)<=U_s/(as)<=exp(H_s). Brownian scaling and the Gaussian tail of
M_1 show, for each fixed t,

    E(1/U_s)<=C_t/s,
    E|1/U_s-1/(as)|<=C_t/sqrt(s), 0<s<=t.           (6)

For the second inequality use |1/(U_s/(as))-1|<=exp(H_s)-1 and
E(exp(H_s)-1)<=C_t sqrt(s). The moments of U_s of each fixed order are
O_t(s^j), by the same pathwise bound.

Equations (5)-(6) imply

    E[h(s,U_s)/U_s]=D_t/(as)+O_t(s^(-1/2))+O_t(1).

The nonsingular terms in C have bounded expectation near s=0, by the
derivative and U_s moment bounds. Therefore

    E[(C P_(t-s)f)(U_s)]= (b/a)D_t/s+O_t(s^(-1/2)). (7)

The difference between the integrand and (b/a)D_t/s is integrable at zero.
Integrating it proves (4), including its remainder. Finally b/a=1/(2pi).

## Consequence and the unpaid step

The natural candidate network leading correction for this bounded test is
(D_t/(2pi))log(n)/n, with a theta0-dependent constant/n at the next order.
This is a prediction, not proved network asymptotics. A proof still needs
uniform control while u approaches zero, a matching scale and remainder,
and the accumulated exact-to-regularized bounded-test comparison through
the entrance. A lower-cutoff contribution might alter or cancel a formal
coefficient unless controlled. C029's deterministic logarithmic offset is

\[

[Theorem 1 (Noiseless optimality of the full model) of arXiv:2609.02790, 'Full-Model Optimality for Tunable Linear Generative Priors in Compressed Sensing'] Fix an invertible matrix \(G_n\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) with singular value
decomposition
\[
    G_n=U\Sigma V^\top,
    \ \Sigma=\operatorname{diag}(\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_n),
    \
\sigma_1\ge\cdots\ge\sigma_n>0,
\]
where \(U,V\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) are orthogonal.
For each \(k\in[n]\), define the rank-\(k\) linear generative model
\[
    \mathcal G_k:=U_k\Sigma_k\in\mathbb R^{n\times k},
    \qquad
    \Sigma_k:=\operatorname{diag}(\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_k),
\]
where \(U_k\) consists of the first \(k\) columns of \(U\).
Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have i.i.d.\
\(\mathcal N(0,1)\) entries, where \(2\le m\le n\).
Let \(z^\star\sim\mathcal N(0,I_n)\) be independent of \(A\), and define
\[
    x^\star:=G_nz^\star,
    \qquad
    y:=Ax^\star .
\]
For each \(k\in[n]\), let \(\widehat x(k)\) be the reconstruction signal obtained
from the model \(\mathcal G_k\) according to the reconstruction rule
\eqref{eq0}, and let \(E(k)\) denote the expected reconstruction error
defined in \eqref{eq:recon err}.\footnote{The quantity \(E(k)\) is
interpreted as an extended-real-valued expectation. In particular,
\(E(m-1)=E(m)=+\infty\); see
Proposition~\ref{prop:boundary-divergence}.}
Then
\[
    E(n)\le E(k)
    \qquad\text{for every }k\in[n].
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Noiseless optimality of the full model

\hfix(\mathfrak{h}_0;y,t) := \sup_{x\in \R} \big(\mathfrak{h}_0(x) + \mathcal{L}(x,0;y,t)\big).
\end{equation} For multiple initial data this provides a coupling of full-space KPZ fixed points.

(ii) There exist constants \(C_{low},C_{up},\varepsilon_{0} > 0\)
such that for every \(0 < \varepsilon < \varepsilon_{0}\)
and every intrinsic \(\varepsilon\)-net
\(\{ x_{1},\ldots,x_{N}\}\) of \(M\) with
\(N = N_{\varepsilon}(M)\), the family

\[\mathcal{A}_{\varepsilon} = \{ B_{M}\left( x_{1},\varepsilon \right),\ldots,B_{M}\left( x_{N},\varepsilon \right)\}\]

is a full homological certificate at every radius \(r\)
with
\(C_{low}\,\varepsilon \leq r \leq C_{up}\, \operatorname{reach}(M)\). In
particular, full certificates of size \(N_{\varepsilon}(M)\)
exist.

[Theo 5 (Feldman--H\'ajek) of arXiv:2609.01105, 'Obstruction to quasi-invariance of Gaussian measures under transport flows on Riemannian M'] \cite[Theorem 2.25]{DaPratoZabczyk2014}\\
Let~\(\nu_1\) and~\(\nu_2\) be two centered Gaussian measures over a Hilbert space $H$ with covariance operators~\(Q_1\) and~\(Q_2\). Then $\nu_1$ and $\nu_2$ are either mutually singular or mutually absolutely continuous with respect to each other. The latter happens if and only if 
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
    \item measures~\(\nu_1\) and~\(\nu_2\) have the same Cameron--Martin space $Q_1^{\mez}(H)=Q_2^{\mez}(H)=:H_0$;
    
    \item $Q_1^{-\mez}Q_2^{\mez}(Q_1^{-\mez}Q_2^{\mez})^* - \mathbf{1} \in \mathfrak{S}_2(\bar H_0)$. 
\end{enumerate}
In the first item, $Q_i^{\mez}(H)$ is the range of the operator $Q_i^{\mez}$, and in the last item, $\bar H_0$ stands for the completion of $H_0$ under the $H$ norm, and the adjoint is understood with respect to $H$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Defn Inner product on affine standard module of arXiv:2506.01306, 'Asymptotic of Coulomb gas integral, Temperley-Lieb type algebras and pure partition functi'] Let $x, y \in V_{n,m}$ be two radial $(n,m)$-link states and $a,b \in \mathbb{C}$. Define the inner product $\langle x \mid y \rangle_{n,m}$ as follows:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item Reflect $x$ across a vertical axis (mirror image).
    \item Glue $x$ to $y$ vertically, forming a closed link diagram called $\mathcal{G}(\alpha, \beta)$.
    \item If all defects pair, and $m$ closed loops are formed, then
    \[
    \langle x \mid y \rangle_{n,m} := a^{n_a}b^{n_b}.
    \]
    where $n_a$ and $n_b$ denote the numbers of contractible and non-contractible loops formed in the diagram $\mathcal{G}(\alpha, \beta)$, and $a, b$ are loop weights.
    \item Otherwise, if any defects remain unpaired, then $\langle x \mid y \rangle_{n,m} := 0$.
\end{enumerate}
title: Inner product on affine standard module

Own-work draft, proof (unaudited), C004 version 2; priority not established. Let d,m>=1, R0>=1 and Sigma be a positive semidefinite d by d matrix with trace(Sigma)<=1. Let nu be any law on pairs (a,w) with |a|<=R0 and Euclidean ||w||<=R0. For two independent iid size-m samples from nu, define rho((a,w),(b,v))=|a-b|+||Sigma^(1/2)(w-v)||. The expected minimum mean rho cost over neuron permutations is at most r_m=inf over positive integers k,q of [4R0/q+2R0/sqrt(k+1)+2sqrt(2)R0 sqrt(q^(k+1)/m)]. In particular it is O(R0 sqrt(log(log(m)+e)/log(m))) as m tends to infinity, with an absolute constant uniform in d, Sigma and nu. Singular Sigma is allowed; no inverse is used. The proof partitions the coefficient and leading covariance coordinates and controls the unmatched empirical cell masses. Exact finite checks are not an independent audit.

[Thm 5 (\cite{kannanKL2021}) of arXiv:2609.03268, 'Poincare Polynomials of Heavy-Light Hassett Spaces'] Fix $m\ge2$ and $n\ge 4$ and consider the weight vector $w=w_{m,n}:=(1^m, \epsilon^{n-m})$. 
            Let 
            $$R=\Z[x_I: I\subsetneq \{2,\ldots, n\};\ \{2,\ldots, m\}\cap I \neq \varnothing; \ |I|>1]$$ 
            be the polynomial ring over $\Z$ on $2^{n-1}-2^{n-m}-m$ variables. Then there is a quotient map $R\onto A(\DMumford{w})$. Furthermore, the kernel of this quotient map is the ideal generated by the following elements:
            \begin{enumerate}
                \item $x_I x_J$ for each pair $I,J$ such that $I\cap J\notin \{I,J, \varnothing\} $;
                \item For each $\{i,j\},\{k,l\}\in {\{2,\ldots, n\}\choose 2}$ with $i,k\le m$, 
                $$\sum_{I: \{i,j\}\subseteq I, \{k,l\}\not\subseteq I} x_I - \sum_{I: \{k,l\}\subseteq I, \{i,j\}\not\subseteq I} x_I.$$
            \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem thm4.4 of arXiv:2508.12951, '\textbf{On the central limit question for strictly stationary, reversible Markov chains}'] Suppose $(g_1, g_2, g_3, \dots)$ is a sequence of positive
numbers such that $g_n \to \infty$ as $n \to \infty$.
Then there exists a (real) strictly stationary, countable-state,
irreducible, aperiodic Markov chain 
$X := (X_k, k \in \mathbb Z)$ which is reversible and has
the following properties: \hfil\break
(i) There exists a positive constant $C$ such that
$P(|X_0| \leq C) = 1$; \hfil\break
(ii) $\alpha(n) \leq \beta(n) << g_n \cdot n^{-1}$ as $n \to \infty$ 
(see Notations (nt2.1 of the paper));  \hfil\break
(iii) conclusions (iii) and (iv) in Theorem \ref {thm3.4} hold; and \hfil\break
(iv) defining ${\bf h}(n) := n^{-1} \textrm{\rm Var}(\sum_{k=1}^n X_k)$ for every $n \in \mathbb N$, one has that
\begin{align}

&{\bf h}(n)\ \leq\ g_n\ \ {\rm for\ every}\ n \in \mathbb N;\ \ \ {\rm and} \\

&{\rm for\ every}\ N \in \mathbb N,\ \ \ 
\limsup_{n \to \infty} \frac {{\bf h}(N n)} {{\bf h}(n)}\ =\ N. 
\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm4.4 of arXiv:2508.12951

body:
[Corollary 27 (The two zones, geometrised) of arXiv:2608.15805, 'Spectral duality structures and the Fisher--Rao geometry of reset distributions'] In the canonical realisation, for every $a$ and drift for which the
vertex condition \textup{(V)} holds --- in particular for $a=3,4$
by Proposition~\ref{prop:walk-V}, and for $5\le a\le8$ by the
numerical evidence of Remark~\ref{rem:walk-V-numeric} --- the
starting sites split into two consecutive zones about the
midpoint,
\[
\underbrace{+\ \cdots\ +}_{z<a/2}\quad
\underbrace{\bigl[\,0\,\bigr]_{a\ \mathrm{even}}}_{z=a/2}\quad
\underbrace{-\ \cdots\ -}_{z>a/2}\, ,
\]
where $\pm$ denotes the constant sign of
$\partial_\gamma C(e_z,\cdot)$. Two things must be distinguished.
That every orbit $\{z,a-z\}$ straddles the midpoint and contributes
exactly one site to each sign class is forced by the orbit
structure alone, and is independent of the parity of $a$. That the
class below the midpoint is the one labelled $+$, on the other
hand, is not: it depends on the orientation chosen for the
directors and on the global sign $\varepsilon$ of \textup{(V)}, and
is fixed here by the canonical orientation together with the sign
of the constant $-2q^{a}$ computed in
Proposition~\ref{prop:walk-V}. When $a$ is even the midpoint is
itself a site, the unique fixed point of $\sigma$, and it is
exactly reset-neutral; when $a$ is odd the value $a/2$ is not an integer, so no site is a
fixed point of $\sigma$, none is invariant, and the two index
ranges $z<a/2$ and $z>a/2$ exhaust the sites with no neutral index
between them. \textup{(}The ``zones'' are sets of integer sites
throughout, not regions of a continuum.\textup{)} This is the two-zone theorem
of Paper~I, obtained here as a corollary of the geometry: the two
zones are the two sides of the separatrix, the neutral site --- when
it exists --- is its intersection with the vertex set, and the
midpoint is fixed by the site involution $\sigma$, whose fixed
point it is, while the associated spherical reflection $R_L$ fixes
the separatrix pointwise; the two are distinct structures, kept
apart by Proposition~\ref{prop:three-involutions}. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: The two zones, geometrised

body:
[Proposition 14 (Transport kernels) of arXiv:2606.18458, 'Stable size-biasing and the positive scale-mixture order of generalized Gaussian laws'] For $0<p\le q$, define, for bounded measurable $h:\R\to\R$,
\[
K_{p,q}h(x)=\E h(V_{p,q}x),
\]
where $V_{p,q}$ has the unique factor law. Then $K_{p,q}$ is a Markov operator and
\[
\E h(X_p)=\E K_{p,q}h(X_q).
\]
Moreover, for $0<p\le q\le r$, the operators compose on test functions according to
\[
K_{q,r}(K_{p,q}h)=K_{p,r}h.
\]
The composition is evaluated using independent copies of the factor laws.

body:
A basis of a vector space V over a field F is a subset B that is linearly independent and spans V, so every vector has a unique finite linear combination in elements of B. The dimension dim_F(V) is the cardinality of any basis of V; all bases have the same cardinality.
V is a vector space over a field F
title: Basis and Dimension

body: A sequence (a_n) converges to L if for every epsilon > 0 there is N such that |a_n - L| < epsilon for all n >= N. The limit, when it exists, is unique. Convergent sequences are bounded; limits respect sums, products, quotients (nonzero denominator), and order (limits of a_n <= b_n satisfy lim a_n <= lim b_n).
title: Limit of a Sequence

[Definition def-point process of arXiv:2505.24043, 'Weak solutions of Navier-Stokes Equation with purely discontinuous L\'evy Noise'] Suppose that $(X, \mathscr{B}_X) $ is a non-empty measure space  and
$\bigl( {\Omega}, {\mathscr{F}}, {\mathbb{P}} \bigr)$ is a probability space. A {random} point process (on $X$ and on $\bigl( {\Omega}, {\mathscr{F}}, {\mathbb{P}}  \bigr)$) is a map \[
p: \Omega \to \Pi_X
\]
which is ${\mathscr{F}}/\mathscr{B}(\Pi_X)$-measurable.
Hereafter, when there is no ambiguity we just say a point process instead of random point process.

If $p: \Omega \to \Pi_X$ is a point process, then
 we will write $p(t,\omega)$ for the value of $p(\omega)$ at $t \in D(p(\omega))$.
Moreover, see Definition (def-point function of the paper), when we will write $p(t,\omega)$ we will implicitly imply that $t\in \mathrm{Dom}(p(\omega))$.
title: Definition def-point process of arXiv:2505.24043

Q_i = \sum_{\tau} c_\tau \cdot \mathsf{M} _\tau 
\),
 we have
\[
\frac{1}{C_F}F(  Q_i)
=
I+Q_i/C_F + \frac{1}{C_F}\cdot 
\sum_{j\ge2}
\left(
    \sum_{\tau\in\textsf{Old}\text{-}\mathcal{P}_j(Q_i)}
    c_\tau\mathsf{M} _\tau
    +
    \sum_{\tau\in\textsf{New}\text{-}\mathcal{P}_j(Q_i)}
    c_\tau\mathsf{M} _\tau
\right).
\]
Moreover,
\[

\]

[Prop 11 of arXiv:2609.01105, 'Obstruction to quasi-invariance of Gaussian measures under transport flows on Riemannian M'] Let $p \in S^m(\mathbb{R}^d\times\mathbb{R}^d)$. Let $U, V$ be two open sets of $\Rr^d$, $V$ being convex, and let $\chi : U \to V$ be a smooth diffeomorphism satisfying $\|\Jac \chi^{-1} - I_d\|_{L^{\infty}(V)} <1$. 
Let $\psi \in \mathcal{C}^{\infty}_c(V)$ and $\rho \in \mathcal{C}_c^{\infty}(U)$ 
such that~\(\rho\) is equal to~\(1\) on a neighborhood of $\chi^{-1}(\operatorname{supp} \psi)$. If~\(f\) is compactly supported in~\(V\) set~\(C_\chi f\) the function corresponding to~\(f\circ \chi\) on~\(U\) and~\(0\) outside~\(U\). Operator~\(C_\chi\) is a bijection between functions compactly supported in~\(V\) and functions compactly supported in~\(U\).
Set 
\[
Q = \psi C_{\chi}^{-1} \rho \Op(p) \rho C_{\chi}\psi,
\]
and define $J(x,y)=\displaystyle\int_0^1 \Jac \chi^{-1}(tx+(1-t)y)^\top\mathrm{d}t$ for $x, y \in V$.

Then, there exists $q\in S^m(\Rr^d \times \Rr^d)$ such that $Q=\psi\Op(q)\psi$, and 
moreover, $q$ admits the following asymptotic expansion on a neighborhood of $\supp \psi$ included in~\(V\):
\begin{equation}
    
        q(x,\xi) \sim \sum_{\alpha \in \mathbb{N}^d} \frac{\rho(\chi^{-1}(x))}{i^{|\alpha|}\alpha !} \partial_y^\alpha \left.\partial_{\xi}^\alpha \left(\rho(\chi^{-1}(y))p\left(\chi^{-1}(x),J(x,y)^{-1}\xi\right)\left\vert\frac{\det \Jac \chi^{-1} (y)}{\det J(x,y)}\right\vert\right)\right\vert_{y=x}.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] The circular measure $\varepsilon$ of a rooted bipartite graph $X$ is given by
$$d\varepsilon(q)=d\nu((q+q^{-1})^2)$$
where $\nu$ is the associated positive spectral measure.

[Cor 17 of arXiv:2609.00739, '2609.00739'] Fix $x_0\in\R^2$ and $R>0$.  Let $a_j\in W^{1,\infty}(B_R(x_0))$ satisfy
\[
 a_-\leq a_j\leq a_+,
 \quad
 \frac{R\norm{\nabla a_j}_{L^\infty(B_R(x_0))}}{a_-}\leq\frac{1}{2}.
\]
Let $\frac{\eps_j}{R}\to0$, and let $u_j\in H^1(B_R(x_0);\R^k)$ be weak
solutions of
\[
 -\eps_j\Delta u_j+\frac{a_j}{\eps_j}\nabla V(u_j)=0
 \quad\text{in }B_R(x_0),
\]
with $\norm{u_j}_{L^\infty(B_R(x_0))}\leq L$.  Suppose
\[
 e_{\eps_j,a_j}(u_j)\dd x\stackrel{*}{\rightharpoonup}\nustar,
 \quad
 \frac{a_jV(u_j)}{\eps_j}\dd x
 \stackrel{*}{\rightharpoonup}\zetastar
\]
on $B_R(x_0)$.  After reducing $\eta_0$ by a universal numerical factor,
the following assertions hold.
\begin{enumerate}[label=$(\theenumi)$]
\item If
$\nustar(\overline{B_r(x)})<\eta_0r$ and
$\overline{B_r(x)}\subset B_R(x_0)$, then
$\nustar\left(B_{\frac{r}{2}}(x)\right)=0$.
\item If $x\in\supp\nustar$ and
$\overline{B_r(x)}\subset B_R(x_0)$, then
\[
 \nustar(B_r(x))\geq\eta_0r.
\]
\item For every ball $B_r(x)$ with
$\overline{B_r(x)}\subset B_R(x_0)$,
\begin{equation}
 \nustar\left(B_{\frac{r}{2}}(x)\right)
 \leq C(V,a_-,a_+,L)\zetastar\left(B_{\frac{3r}{4}}(x)\right).
\end{equation}
\end{enumerate}

[Lemma 8 (the constant-field Fourier representation) of arXiv:2609.01093, 'Ideal MHD below the classical well-posedness threshold'] With $(\tau,\xi)$ the spacetime Fourier variables, $\lambda$ as in
\eqref{eq:Bmult}, and $\tau_\pm=\tau\pm\lambda$, one has
\begin{equation}
 \widetilde{\mathcal Bf}=\mathrm i\lambda\widetilde f,
 \qquad
 \widetilde{\mathcal A^+f}=\mathrm i\tau_+\widetilde f,
 \qquad
 \widetilde{\mathcal A^-f}=\mathrm i\tau_-\widetilde f,
 \qquad
 \widetilde{\Box f}=-\tau_+\tau_-\widetilde f .
\end{equation}
Consequently $D_\pm=-\mathrm i\mathcal A^\pm$ are commuting self-adjoint
operators on $L^2(dt dy)$ and, for every Borel function $\Phi$,
\begin{equation}
 \Phi(D_+,D_-)f
 :=\big(\Phi(\tau_+,\tau_-)\widetilde f\big)^\vee
\end{equation}
on its maximal domain.  Moreover
\[
 \mathrm e^{r\mathcal B}f(t,y)=f(t,y+r\Binf),
 \qquad
 \mathrm e^{r\mathcal A^\pm}f(t,y)=f(t+r,y\pm r\Binf),
\]
so these groups are isometries on every $L^p$ and unitary on $L^2$.  In particular,
\begin{equation}
 [\Lambda^{\sreg},\mathcal B]=0
 \qquad(\sreg\in\Real),
\end{equation}
and all corresponding Fourier-multiplier commutators vanish.

[Theorem thm:stab of arXiv:2604.13968, 'Divisible sandpiles via random walks in random scenery'] Let~$G = (V,E)$ be an infinite, locally finite, connected graph with
		degree bounded by~$d$, and let $(\sigma(v))_{v\in V}$ be i.i.d.\ random variables
		with $\mathbb{E}[\sigma(v)] = \mu \in [-\infty,1)$.
		\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
			\item If $\mathbb{E}[(\sigma(v)^+)^p] < \infty$ for some $p > 3$, then
			$\sup_{v \in V}\mathbb{E}[u_\infty(v)^q] < \infty$ for every $q\in[1,(p-1)/2)$; in particular $\mathbb{P}(\sigma \text{ stabilizes}) = 1$.
			\item If $|B(o,r)|\leq C r^{d_f}$ for some $o\in V$, some $C>0$, some $d_f\geq 1$, and all $r\geq 1$, and if $\mathbb{E}[(\sigma(v)^+)^p] < \infty$ for some $p > d_f$, then $\mathbb{P}(\sigma \text{ stabilizes}) = 1$.
		\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 12 of arXiv:2506.20789, 'Central limit theory for Peaks-over-Threshold partial sums of long memory linear time seri'] Let $\gamma\in (0,1)$. Then the following hold:
  \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
    \item
    For all $y,z\in\mathbb{R}$,
\begin{align}
    
    g_{\gamma}
    (z+y)
    \ \lesssim \
    g_\gamma(z)
    \cdot
    (1\lor |y|)^{1+\gamma}\,.
  \end{align}
  \item
    Let $a,b\in\mathbb{R}$ with $a<b$. Then, for all $z\in\mathbb{R}$,
\begin{align}
    
    \int_a^b g_\gamma(z-w)\,\mathrm{d}w
    \ \lesssim \
    g_\gamma(z)
    \cdot
    ((b-a) \lor 1)^{1+\gamma}
    \,.
  \end{align}
  \end{enumerate}
  Here $\lesssim$ denotes inequality up to a constant $C_{\gamma}>0$ depending only on $\gamma$.

[Proposition lemma:frechet of arXiv:2505.02685, 'On the Spectral Expansion of Monotone Subsets of the Hypercube'] Suppose $F : L^2(V) \to \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}$ has continuous partial derivatives with respect to the standard
    basis $\{e_u\}_{u \in V}$, that is, for each $u \in V$ the $L^2(V) \to \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}$ function 
    \[
        \partial_u F(f) = \lim_{t \to 0} \frac{F(f + t e_u) - F(f)}{t}
    \]
    is continuous. Then $F$ is (Fréchet) $C^1$ and its gradient $\nabla F : L^2(V) \to L^2(V)$ is
    given by
    \[
        (\nabla F(f))(u) = |V| \cdot \partial_u F(f)
    \]
    for each $f \in L^2(V)$ and $u \in V$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: Every convex body K in R^n contains a unique ellipsoid E of maximal volume, and K is contained in the n-fold dilation of E about its center (sqrt(n)-fold when K is centrally symmetric). John's characterization: E is the unit ball exactly when there are contact points and positive weights forming an isotropic decomposition of the identity. The theorem bounds how far any norm is from a Euclidean one (Banach-Mazur distance at most sqrt(n)) and drives algorithmic rounding of convex bodies.

body:
[Df Join of arXiv:2605.14910, 'Sharp Phase Transition for the Formation of Infinite Tubes'] Two topological $(k-1)$-spheres $S$ and $S'$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$ are said to be \emph{joined with width at most $w$}, denoted by $S\approx_wS'$, if there exists an open $k$-tube of width at most $w$ whose initial sphere is $S$ and terminal sphere is $S'$.
  We say that $S$ is \emph{joined to infinity with width at most $w$}, and write $S\approx_w\infty$, if there exists an infinite open $k$-tube of width at most $w$ whose initial sphere is $S$.
  Furthermore, if there exits some $w>0$ such that $S\approx_w\infty$, then we simply say that $S$ is \emph{joined to infinity}, and denote this by $S\approx\infty$.
title: Join

[Corollary C:elpp-result of arXiv:2604.10020, 'The directed landscape in half-space'] Take $\alpha>0$ and the field $X$ from Section (sssec:constru of the paper).
Let $W:\mathbb{Z}^2\to\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ be an array of independent random variables, such that for each $j\in\mathbb{Z}$ and $i \in \mathbb{Z} \setminus \{1\}$,
$$
W(1, j) \sim \operatorname{Exp}(\alpha), \qquad W(i, j) \sim \operatorname{Exp}(1).
$$
Then for each $(1,1)\le (n,m)\in\mathbb{Z}^2_{\ge}$, we have
$$
\max_{0 \le i \le m - 1}X(1, 1; n + i, m - i) \stackrel{d}{=} W(1, 1; n, m).
$$
title: Corollary C:elpp-result of arXiv:2604.10020

body:
[Theorem 1 (Averaged macroscopic-loop bounds) of arXiv:2604.20514, 'Macroscopic loops in the random loop model on sparse random graphs'] Fix \(u\in[0,1]\) and \(\theta>0\).

\begin{enumerate}[label=\textnormal{(\roman*)}]
    \item \textbf{Random regular graphs.}
    Let \(d\ge 3\), let \(G_n\) be the random \(d\)-regular graph on \(n\) vertices, and let \(p_{d,n}\) denote its law. Assume
    \[
    d>2c_{\theta,u}
    =
    2\bigl(1+\theta\max\{u,1-u\}\bigr).
    \]
    Then there exist \(\eta>0\), \(s>0\), and \(c>0\) such that for every \(a\ge 0\),
    \[
    p_{d,n}\!\left(
    \frac1s\int_a^{a+s}\Pbb^{G_n}_{\theta,t,u}(A_\eta)\,\dd t \ge c
    \right)\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}1.
    \]

    \item \textbf{Sparse Erd\H{o}s--R\'enyi graphs.}
    Let \(\lambda>0\), and let \(G_n\sim G(n,\lambda/n)\). Assume
    \[
    \lambda>2c_{\theta,u}
    =
    2\bigl(1+\theta\max\{u,1-u\}\bigr).
    \]
    Then there exist \(\eta>0\), \(s>0\), and \(c>0\) such that for every \(a\ge 0\),
    \[
    \Pbb\!\left(
    \frac1s\int_a^{a+s}\Pbb^{G_n}_{\theta,t,u}(A_\eta)\,\dd t \ge c
    \right)\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}1.
    \]

    \item \textbf{Simple bounded-degree configuration model.}
    Let \(G_n\) be the simple graph obtained from the configuration model with degree sequence \((d_i^{(n)})_{i=1}^n\), that is, the pairing model conditioned on simplicity. Assume that
    \[
    1\le d_i^{(n)}\le \Delta
    \qquad\text{for all }i,n,
    \]
    and
    \[
    \frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n d_i^{(n)}\to \rho.
    \]
    If
    \[
    \rho>2c_{\theta,u}
    =
    2\bigl(1+\theta\max\{u,1-u\}\bigr),
    \]
    then there exist \(\eta>0\), \(s>0\), and \(c>0\) such that for every \(a\ge 0\),
    \[
    \Pbb\!\left(
    \frac1s\int_a^{a+s}\Pbb^{G_n}_{\theta,t,u}(A_\eta)\,\dd t \ge c
    \right)\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}1.
    \]
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Averaged macroscopic-loop bounds

[Theorem 6 of arXiv:2609.01362, '{Double cluster swapping for spin models: \\Pfaffian relations and sharpness}'] Let $P$ belong the class $\Ec$. Then, there exists $\beta_c \in (0,\infty]$ such that
	\begin{itemize}
		\item (Disordered phase) if $\beta < \beta_c$, then there is finite susceptibility $\chi(\beta) < \infty$. Moreover, if $J$ is finite-range then there exists $c = c(\beta) > 0$ such that
			\[
			\left< \vp_o \vp_x \right>_{\beta}^+ \leq \exp( - c \, d(0,x)).
			\] 
		\item (Ordered phase) there is $c > 0$ such that for all $\beta \geq \beta_c$, the susceptibility is infinite and
			\begin{equation}
			\left< \vp_o \right>_{\beta}^+ \geq c  \,\frac{\beta - \beta_c}{\beta}.
			\end{equation} 
	\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

    E[1/(n theta_L); all layers nondegenerate] = infinity.

Here nondegenerate means neither vector is extinct and their angle is
strictly positive. The assertion follows directly from reviewer-PASS C003:
conditional on any nondegenerate previous state, the next reciprocal angle
has infinite expectation even on nondegenerate next states. The probability
of nondegenerate survival through each finite number of layers is positive
(restrict to open Gaussian-row sets giving two positive, nonproportional
output coordinates). Tonelli's theorem therefore propagates C003 to any
positive depth. Assigning a bounded cemetery value does not repair this
continuous near-collinearity divergence. Conditioning the entire finite path
on nondegeneracy also leaves the mean infinite, since its conditioning event
has positive probability and its unnormalized reciprocal integral is infinite.

Consequently an identity E U_n(t)=E U_t+c(t)/n+o(1/n), for the raw network
reciprocal at floor(nt)>=1, is false as stated. Each finite Monte Carlo sample
has a finite average, which can approximate the central part of the law, but
not this infinite expectation. A finite observable must be specified, for
example min(U_n,R) at fixed R, or the explicitly regularized good-event chain.
For fixed R the diffusion reference is E min(U_t,R), not E U_t. No uniform
error allowing R->infinity after a rate expansion has yet been proved.

## C029: deterministic ReLU offset contains log(depth), not just a constant

Let theta_(l+1)=F(theta_l) be the infinite-width ReLU angle recursion,
with fixed theta_0 in (0,pi), where

    cos F(theta)=[sin(theta)+(pi-theta)cos(theta)]/pi.

Put r_l=1/theta_l, a=1/(3pi), b=1/(6pi^2). There is a finite constant
C(theta_0), depending on the entire initial deterministic orbit, such that

    r_l = a l + (1/(2pi)) log l + C(theta_0)
                   + O_theta0(log(l)/l),  l->infinity.             (D)

The fixed offset is therefore not exactly 1/theta_0, and the correction
cannot consist solely of an initial constant number of layers.

Proof. The cosine equation and Taylor's theorem give

    F(theta)=theta-a theta^2-(a^2/2)theta^3+O(theta^4),
    1/F(theta)-1/theta=a+(3a^2/2)theta+O(theta^2)
                      =a+b theta+O(theta^2).                      (E)

To justify the expansion despite the derivative of arccos at one, use
F=2 arcsin(sqrt((1-cos F)/2)). Factoring theta^2 in 1-cos F leaves a
positive analytic factor near zero; the remaining square root and arcsin
have convergent Taylor expansions there. The positive branch gives (E).

The strict inequality 0<F(theta)<theta implies theta_l decreases to zero.
Thus r_l increases to infinity, and (E) implies

    r_(l+1)-r_l=a+b/r_l+O(r_l^(-2)).

The increments tend to a, so r_l/l->a by averaging the increments. In
particular r_l is bounded above and below by positive multiples of l for
large l. Summing the O(1/l) correction gives r_l=al+O(log l). Now define
H_l=r_l-al-(b/a)log l for l>=1. Then

    H_(l+1)-H_l
       =b/r_l-(b/a)log(1+1/l)+O(r_l^(-2))
       =O(log(l)/l^2).

This is absolutely summable. Hence H_l converges to C(theta_0), with
tail O(log(l)/l). Since b/a=1/(2pi), this proves (D).

For L=floor(nt), fixed t>0, (D) yields the precise deterministic expansion

    r_L/n = a t + [log n/(2pi)+log t/(2pi)+C(theta_0)
                     -a {nt}]/n + O_theta0,t(log n/n^2).           (F)

The fractional-part term is essential unless nt is integral. This is a
theorem for the deterministic map, not for the finite-width chain: its
leading a t differs from the stochastic mean a(exp(2t)-1)/2. In particular,
one may not simply add (F) to that stochastic mean and call it a network
rate. The singular b/(nu) term suggested by (E) is a warning that matching
the entrance to a higher-order compact generator can create log(n)/n terms.
Showing their coefficient, cancellation, or absence for a specified bounded
network observable is still open in this note.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:3d7df9f2e51673034c933127493e891f934b33deb918593bd355f53d6e87ca80","revision_digest":"sha256:89b76734d3eecc1aa1a1e6461d2ae719c0a7a31d2a3401415dfd3abc343dfc91","source_id":"own-work:T244-w691-C029:v1","source_revision":"2026-10-20-v1-unaudited","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

[Lemma le:good_scales_merging_multiple of arXiv:2507.15589, 'Tightness of approximations to metrics on non-simple conformal loop ensemble gaskets'] Suppose that $h$ is a GFF on $D$ with some bounded boundary values. For any $b>0$ and $q \in (0,1)$ there exist $M,p>0$ so that the following is true. 
Let $z \in D$ and $r>0$ such that $B(z,r) \subseteq D$. Let $\widetilde{h}_{z,r}$ be as defined in Section~(se:gff of the paper) with the same boundary values as $\widetilde{h}$ above (after scaling and translation). Let $G_{z,r}$ be the event that
\begin{itemize}
 \item the scale $(z,r)$ is $M$-good for $h$, and
 \item the event $G$ above occurs for the (scaled and translated) field $\widetilde{h}_{z,r}$.
\end{itemize}
For $k\in\mathbf{N}$ let $E$ be the event that the fraction of $1 \leq j \leq k$ so that $G_{z,2^{-j}r}$ occurs is at least $q$. Then $\mathbf{P}[E^c] = O(e^{-bk})$.

[Proposition prop:sym_tilted_explicit of arXiv:2609.01581, 'Concentration of additive functionals of Stratonovich-type'] Let $\mathcal{L}_S = p_{\textrm{s}}^{-1}\nabla\cdot(p_{\textrm{s}} D\nabla)$ and $\mathcal{L}_A = v_{\textrm{s}}\cdot\nabla$
be the symmetric and antisymmetric parts of the Markov generator
from Eq.~(equation eq:markov_gen_decomposition of the paper).
For $f \in
D(\mathcal{L})$, the tilted generator for \emph{density observables} has symmetric and
antisymmetric parts, 
\begin{align}
  \widetilde{\mathcal{L}}_k^\rho f= \mathcal{L}_S f + kV f,
  \qquad
  \widehat{\mathcal{L}}_k^\rho f= \mathcal{L}_A f,
  
\end{align}
and the tilted generator for \emph{current observables} decomposes as
\begin{align}
  \widetilde{\mathcal{L}}_k^J f
  & = \mathcal{L}_S f + k(v_{\textrm{s}}\cdot U) f + k^2(U\cdot DU)f\nonumber\\
  
  \widehat{\mathcal{L}}_k^J f
  &= \mathcal{L}_A f + 2k(DU)\cdot\nabla f + kp_{\textrm{s}}^{-1}\nabla\cdot(p_{\textrm{s}} DU) f,  
  
\end{align}
where $\widetilde{\mathcal{L}}_k^A = \tfrac12\bigl[\mathcal{L}_k^A + (\mathcal{L}_k^A)^\dagger\bigr]$
and $\widehat{\mathcal{L}}_k^A = \tfrac12\bigl[\mathcal{L}_k^A - (\mathcal{L}_k^A)^\dagger\bigr]$
denote the symmetric and antisymmetric parts in $L^2(\mu)$ for $A \in \{\rho, J\}$
from Definition~(def:sym_tilted of the paper).

[Theorem 2 of arXiv:2604.07579, 'Topology of Percolation Clusters: Central Limit Theorems beyond the Lattice'] Let $G$ be the Cayley graph of an amenable group $\Gamma$
    admitting a finite-index left-orderable subgroup $H$, with
    $n=[\Gamma:H]$. Consider Bernoulli bond percolation with parameter $p\in(
    0,1)$, an exhaustive F{\o}lner sequence $(A_{r})$, and let $\mathcal{A}$
    be its orbit under $\Gamma$. Then there exists an $H$-fundamental set of
    edges $\tilde E\subset E$ such that, if the stationary $\mathcal{A}$-functional
    $F$ stabilizes in sequence and satisfies a finite moment condition on $\tilde
    E$, then:
    \begin{enumerate}
      \item $\displaystyle \lim_{r\to\infty}\frac{1}{|A_{r}|}\Var_{p}\!\bigl
        (F(A_{r})\bigr)=\sigma^{2}$;

      \item $\displaystyle |A_{r}|^{-1/2}\bigl(F(A_{r})-\E_{p}[F(A_{r})]\bigr
        )\ \overset{d}{\Longrightarrow}\ \mathcal{N}(0,\sigma^{2})$,
    \end{enumerate}
    where
    \[
      \sigma^{2}= \frac{1}{2n}\sum_{e\in\tilde E}\E_{p}\!\left[\E_{p}\!\left
      [D_{e}^{\infty}\,\middle|\,\mathcal{F}_{e}\right]^{2}\right].
    \]
    Here $D_{e}^{\infty}$ is the limit in probability of $D_{e}(\omega,xA_{r}
    ):=F(\omega,xA_{r})-F(\omega^{e},xA_{r})$ as $r\to\infty$ (the limit
    does not depend on $x$), and $\mathcal{F}_{e}$ is the $\sigma$-algebra
    generated by the edges preceding or equal to $e$ in an $H$-invariant total order on
    $E$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 2 of arXiv:2604.07579

[Lem 17 of arXiv:2608.21090, 'Ornstein--Uhlenbeck process conditioned to have restricted $L_2$-norm'] Fix $r>0$ and $z_0\in\C$. Let $f$ be holomorphic on $B_{r'}(z_0)$ for some $r'>r$. Then
    \[f(z)=\sum_{k=0}^\infty \frac{f^{(k)}(z_0)}{k\,!}(z-z_0)^k\]
    for all $z\in B_r(z_0)$ and
    \[\left|f(z)-\sum_{k=0}^n \frac{f^{(k)}(z_0)}{k\,!}(z-z_0)^k\right|\leq \max_{\abs z'-z_0\abs=r}\abs f(z')\abs\frac{\abs z-z_0\abs^{n+1}}{r^{n+1}}\frac{1}{1-\frac{\abs z-z_0\abs}{r}}.\]

[Propn 3 of arXiv:2606.13487, 'Branching-Selection Particle Systems and Inverse First Passage Problems'] Let $(\mu_t^N)_{t\geq 0}$ be the measure-valued process describing the $(\omega,f,\Lambda,N)$-BBM process, and define $b^N(t):=\inf\{x:\Lambda\langle \mu_t^N,\omega(\cdot-x)\rangle\geq f(t)\}$. Then for any bounded $\omega$ and any test function $\phi(x,t)\in \C{BC}^{2,1}(\B{R}\times [0,\infty),\B{R})$ we have
    \begin{align}  \langle \mu_t^N,\phi(\cdot,t)\rangle = \langle \rho^N, \phi(\cdot,0)\rangle &+ \int_0^t \langle \mu_s^N, \frac12 \phi_{xx}(\cdot,s) + \phi_t(\cdot,s)+f(s)\phi(\cdot,s)\rangle \\
    &- \frac{f(s)\langle \mu_s^N,\phi(\cdot,s)\omega(\cdot-b^N(s))}{\langle \mu_s^N,\omega(\cdot-b^N(s))\rangle} ds
    \nonumber + M_t^{N,W} + M_t^{N,b},
    \end{align}
    where $M^{N,W}_t$ is a continuous local martingale and $M^{N,b}_t$ is a local martingale, with $\B{E}[[M^{N,W}]_t],\B{E}[[M^{N,b}]_t]\to 0$ as $N\to\infty$ for fixed $t\geq 0$.

[Lemma 3 (Specialized maxima) of arXiv:2608.24007, '2608.24007'] Fix $c\in[K]$ and $\zeta,\tau\in\{\pm1\}$. On the one-cluster feasible branch,
write
\[
    f(b)
    :=
    -\frac{\tau\zeta}{K\sqrt6}
    b\varphi(b)
    \left(1-\frac{b^2}{R^2}\right)^{3/2},
    \qquad |b|<R,
\]
and let
\[
    I:=\{b\in(-R,R):f(b)>0\}.
\]
Then $I$ is a connected open interval. For all sufficiently large $R$, $f$
has a unique critical point $b^\star\in I$, which is a strict local maximum
and satisfies
\[
    b^\star=-\tau\zeta+O(R^{-2}).
\]
The corresponding direction
\[
    \omega^\star
    =
    \tau\sqrt{1-\frac{(b^\star)^2}{R^2}}\,v_c
    +
    \frac{b^\star}{R^2}\mu_c
\]
is a strict local maximum of $\Psi_\zeta$ and obeys
\[
    \omega^\star
    =
    \tau v_c
    -
    \frac{\tau\zeta}{R^2}\mu_c
    +
    O(R^{-2}).
\]

[Definition of arXiv:2606.21556, 'Mean field limit of non-exchangeable interacting diffusions on co-evolutionary networks'] We define the fibered Wasserstein space of order \(p,q \in [1,\infty)\) as 
	\[
		\mathcal{P}_{p,q,\nu}(\mathcal{X}\times [0,1]) := \left\{\mu \in \mathcal{P}_{\nu}(\mathcal{X}\times [0,1]) : \int_{0}^{1}W_p(\mu^{\xi},\delta_{x_0})^q d\xi < \infty\right\},
	\]
	where \(x_0\) is an arbitrary fixed point in \(\mathcal{X}\). For any \(\mu,\bar{\mu} \in \mathcal{P}_{p,q,\nu}(\mathcal{X}\times [0,1])\), we define the distance 
	\[
		d_{W_p,q}(\mu,\bar{\mu}) := \left( \int_{0}^{1} W_p(\mu^{\xi},\bar{\mu}^{\xi})^q d\xi \right)^{1/q}.
	\]

body:
[Lem lemma:delta-map of arXiv:2411.11676, 'Surface sums for lattice Yang--Mills in the large-$N$ limit'] Let $s = (\ell_1, \ldots, \ell_n) \in \mathcal{S}_o$ be a non-null string, and let $\delta = \delta(s)$. For each positive splitting $s' \in \mathbb{S}_+(\mathbf{e}_s, s)$, we have that there is some $1 \leq h_{s'} \leq \delta_1 - 1$ such that 
$$\delta(s') \leq (\delta_1 - h_{s'}, h_{s'}, \delta_2, \ldots, \delta_n).$$ 
Moreover, the map $s' \mapsto h_{s'}$ on the domain $\mathbb{S}_+(\mathbf{e}_s, s)$ can be chosen to be injective. 

Similarly, for each negative splitting $s' \in \mathbb{S}_-(\mathbf{e}_s, s)$, either 
$$\delta(s') \leq (\delta_1 - 2, \delta_2, \ldots, \delta_n),\qquad \Big(\delta(s') \leq (\delta_2, \ldots, \delta_n)\quad  \text{if}\quad \delta_1 = 2\Big),$$ 
or there is some $1 \leq g_{s'} \leq \delta_1 - 1$ such that  
$$\delta(s') \leq (\delta_1 - g_{s'}, g_{s'}, \delta_2, \ldots, \delta_n).$$ 
Moreover, the map $s' \mapsto g_{s'}$ (whose domain is a suitable subset of $\mathbb{S}_-(\mathbf{e}_s, s)$) can be taken as injective.
title: Lem lemma:delta-map of arXiv:2411.11676

[Theorem thm:main of arXiv:2507.16188, 'The noisy voter model with general initial conditions'] Fix $\theta\in(0,1]$ and $q\geq2$. Let $G=(V,E)$ be a connected graph on $n$ vertices satisfying (eq:expansion of the paper) for some $\mathfrak{c}_0>0$ and $\upalpha\in(0,1)$, and let $\mathsf{x}_0$ be an arbitrary initial condition. Then the $q$-state noisy voter model on $G$  
and noise probability $\theta$ started from $\mathsf{x}_0$ satisfies
\begin{equation}
t_\textsc{mix}^{\mathsf{x}_0}(\varepsilon) = (1+

o(1)
)\max\Big\{T_{\mathsf{x}_0}, \frac{1}{4\theta}\log n\Big\}\,,
\end{equation}
where the $o(1)$-term is $ O\big(\log^{-\upalpha/2} n\big)
$ with a constant 

depending on $\varepsilon,\theta,q,\mathfrak{c}_0,\upalpha$ (but not $G$ or $\mathsf{x}_0$).

In particular, for any sequence of connected graphs $G^{(n)}$ with $n$ vertices satisfying (eq:expansion of the paper) for the same $\upalpha,\mathfrak{c}_0$, and any sequence of initial conditions $\mathsf{x}_0^{(n)}$, the $q$-state noisy voter model on $G^{(n)}$ with noise probability $\theta$ has cutoff at $\max\{T_{\mathsf{x}_0^{(n)}}, \frac{1}{4\theta}\log n\}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 3 of arXiv:2608.30138, 'High-frequency wave propagation for the viscoelastic wave equation with singular memory'] Let $I_h$ be as in \r{Ih0}, 
where $b$ is smooth, supported in $U$, and bounded uniformly in $h$ together with all of its derivatives. 

Then $I_h b$ has an asymptotic expansion in powers of $(h/\lambda)^{p+k}$, $k=0,1,2,\dots$, with principal term
\[
I_h b = C_p m_0(x) b(t,x,h)  (h/ \lambda )^p   + O(h^{p+1})\quad \text{in $C^k$},
\] 
for every $k$. 
More generally, 
\[
I_h b\sim
\sum_{j\ge0} 
C_{p+j}(h/ \lambda )^{p+j}\,\frac1{j!}
\sum_{\ell=0}^j
\binom{j}{\ell}
m_\ell (x)\,
(-\partial_t)^{j-\ell}b(t,x,h)  \quad \text{in $C^k$}. 
\]

[Theorem supercritical case JW of arXiv:2607.00731, 'Sharp Asymptotics for the Largest Component in the Subcritical Regime of Preferential Atta'] Assume that $\alpha=\alpha(n)\to a\in(0,\infty]$. Let $m_c=\frac{\alpha n}{2(\alpha+1)}$, suppose that $\varepsilon=\varepsilon(n)>0$ satisfies $\varepsilon=o(1), \varepsilon^3 n\to\infty .$ Then, for $m=\lfloor m_c(1+\varepsilon)\rfloor,$ we have
\[
L_1(G^\alpha_{n,m})
=
\frac{2}{1+2/a}\,\varepsilon n\,(1+o_p(1)),
\]
with the convention $1/\infty=0$.

In particular, if $\alpha=\alpha(n)\to\infty$ and
$\alpha\varepsilon\to\infty$, then, for $m=\left\lfloor \frac{n}{2}(1+\varepsilon)\right\rfloor,$
we have
\[
    L_1(G^\alpha_{n,m})
    =
    2\varepsilon n\,(1+o_p(1)).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem thm:torus of arXiv:2604.21142, 'Gaussian fluctuations for Internal DLA on cylinders'] Let $\a_2, \ldots, \a_K : {\ensuremath{\mathbb R}}  \to {\ensuremath{\mathbb R}} $ be differentiable functions with bounded derivatives, where $K \geq 2$ is an integer independent of $N$, and fix $y_0 > 0$. Let
	\[ \phi(\underline x, y) = \sum_{k=2}^K \a_k(y)\, f_k^N(\underline x) \]
be the corresponding test function on ${\ensuremath{\mathbb Z}} _n^d \times {\ensuremath{\mathbb R}} $, and let $\varphi(\underline x, y) \coloneqq \phi(\underline x, y/a_N)$ on ${\ensuremath{\mathbb Z}} _n^d \times {\ensuremath{\mathbb Z}} $. Then with $T = N \lfloor y_0 a_N \rfloor$,
	\[ \frac{1}{\sqrt{N a_N}} \langle \! \langle D_T,\, \varphi \rangle \! \rangle
	\Rightarrow \ensuremath{\mathcal N}\!\left(0\,, \sum_{k=2}^K \a_k(y_0)^2\, \frac{1 - e^{-2\g_k y_0}}{2\g_k} \right) \]
as $n \to \infty$, where $\g_k \coloneqq \lim_{n\to\infty} a_N \sqrt{2(1 - \l_k(N))}$.

body:
[Theorem thm:house of arXiv:2605.10617, 'Logarithmic scaling of selective sweep curves:\\ from tents to houses'] Let $(H^N_0,H^N_1)$ be as in Definition~(defHN of the paper).
    Then, conditional on the event of fixation $\{\mathcal T_1^N < \infty\}$, for $i\in\{0,1\}$, 
    \begin{itemize}
      \item[I.1)] the rescaled sequence of fixation times
        $\sigma_{\rm fix}^N:=\frac{\mathcal T_1^N}{ \varphi_N^{-1}\log N}$ converges, as $N \to \infty$, in probability to~$\frac{2(1-b)}{a}$,
      \item[I.2)] for any $\varepsilon >0$,  the sequence $H_i^N$ converges as $N\to \infty$ in probability to $h_i$, with respect to the uniform distance when restricted to the set $D^\varepsilon_i$ defined as
  \begin{equation}
  D_1^\varepsilon:= \mathbb{R}\setminus [0, \varepsilon), \qquad D_0^\varepsilon:= \mathbb{R} \setminus\left(\tfrac{2(1-b)}a-\varepsilon, \tfrac{2(1-b)}a+\varepsilon \right),  
  \end{equation}
     \item[I.3)] in the case $b=0$ the uniform convergence in probability of $H_i^N$ to $h_i$  holds on $\mathbb{R}$,
     \medskip
     \item[II)] the sequence $(H_i^N)$, viewed as random elements of $\mathcal D$,
       converges, as $N\to \infty$ in probability to~$h_i$. Hereby, $\mathcal D$ is equipped with the Skorokhod $M_1$~topology.
     \end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma lem:edges of arXiv:2608.30254, 'Exact Recovery Thresholds for Weighted Data Selection\\ in Vector-Valued Linear Regression'] Let $w_{ij}=p_ip_jd_{ij}$. Then $\sum_{i<j}w_{ij}=1$,
$\sum_{i<j,\,t_i\ne t_j}w_{ij}B_{ij}=0$, and
\[
  \sum_{\substack{i<j\\ t_i\ne t_j}}w_{ij}\Wnorm{B_{ij}}^2
  \;=\;2E-2\sum_{G}\Bigl(P_G\!\!\sum_{i\in G}p_i|z_i|^2
      -\Bigl|\sum_{i\in G}p_iz_i\Bigr|^2\Bigr)\ \le\ 2E ,
\]
where $G$ ranges over the classes of equal direction and
$P_G=\sum_{i\in G}p_i$. In particular some valid pair has
$\Wnorm{B_{ij}}^2\le2E$.

[Lemma lem:singulargap of arXiv:2505.12187, 'Speeding up quantum Markov processes through lifting'] Given an ergodic QMS generator $\mathcal{L}$ with an invariant state $\sigma \in \mathcal{D}_+(\mathcal{M})$, let $s(\mathcal{L})$ be the singular value gap of $\mathcal{L}$, $C \ge 1$ and $\nu > 0$ be constants in exponential convergence (equation ex:expdecay of the paper), and  let $t_{\rm rel}$ be the relaxation time (equation eq:trelax of the paper). Then, it holds that 
\begin{align*}
\nu \le (1 + \log C) s(\mathcal{L})\,,\quad
    t_{\rm rel} \ge  \frac{1}{2 s(\mathcal{L})}\,.
\end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Definition def:fromfilling of arXiv:2602.21315, 'The Instability of all Backoff Protocols\thanks{For the purpose of Open Access, the author'] The initial setting is defined as follows:
Fix $\lambda \in (0,1)$ and a send sequence $\overline{p}$ with $p_0=1$ such that,
for all $i \ge 1$, $W_i \le (4/\lambda)^i$.
Let $j_0$ be a sufficiently large positive integer
where all strongly-exposed bins are in $[j_0-1]$.
Fix an initialising high-level state $\Psi_0$  with  $\tau^{\Psi_0} = \tau_0$ and $j^{\Psi_0} = j_0$. 
Let $\mathrm{hls}$ be the $\Psi_0$-backoff bounding rule from Definition~(def:backoff-bounding-rule of the paper).  
Let $V$ be a volume process from $\Psi_0$ with transition rule $\mathrm{hls}$, 
 send sequence~$\overline{p}$, and birth rate~$\lambda$  (Definition~(def:volume-process of the paper)).
For any
$t \ge \tau_0$, 
let   $T(t) = \{\tau_0,\ldots,t\}$.
Fix $t>\tau_0$, 
 and fix a tuple  
$ 
\overline{\psi}_{T(t-1)} = (\psi_{\tau_0},\dots,\psi_{t-1})$  of high-level states 
such that  
$\mathbb{P}( \overline{\Psi}_{T(t-1)} = \overline{\psi}_{T(t-1)}) > 0$, 
$\textup{type}^{\psi_{t-1}} = \textup{filling}$, 
$\tau^{\psi_{t-1}} = t-1$, and $z_j^{\psi_{t-1}} = 0$ where $j=j^{\psi_{t-1}}$.
Consider the evolution of~$V$, conditioned on
$\overline{\Psi}_{T(t-1)} = \overline{\psi}_{T(t-1)}$.

Define the following quantities, sets, and stopping times.
\[
\tau_{j,\mathrm{full}} = \min\{t'  \geq t \colon \textup{type}^{\Psi(t')} = \textup{failure} \mbox{ or }j^{\Psi(t')} = j+1\}.\]
Let $O_0 = t-1$. For all positive integers $x$, let
\begin{align*}
I_x &= \min(\{\tau_{j,\mathrm{full}}\} \cup \{t > O_{x-1} \colon 
\mbox{$\Psi(t-1) \rightarrow \Psi(t)$
is via (R(item:R2 of the paper))(ii) from $j$-filling to $j$-refilling
} \}).\\
O_x &= \min(\{\tau_{j,\mathrm{full}}\} \cup \{t > I_{x} \colon 
\mbox{$\Psi(t-1) \rightarrow \Psi(t)$
is via  (R(item:R6 of the paper))(i) from $j$-stabilising to $j$-filling
} \}).
\end{align*}
Let 
\begin{align*} 
A &= \lceil 4(4 j)^{\phi} W_j\rceil.\\
\mathrm{Ready} &  
= \{ T'\geq t-1 \colon  
\mbox{ $\Psi(T')$ is a $j$-filling state,  
$T' + j^{24} \leq t+A$, and
$
F_j^{\Psi(T')}(T'+1) \ge \mu_j^{\overline{\gamma}} $ }
\}. 
\\
t_{\mathrm{min}} &= \min(\{t+A\} \cup \mathrm{Ready}).
\end{align*}
title: Definition def:fromfilling of arXiv:2602.21315

[Proposition prop:affine-sig of arXiv:2606.28869, '\bfseries A General Theory of Paths:\\ \large Signatures, Jump Lifts, and Expected Signatu'] Fix $m<\infty$. There is a finite vector $U_t$ collecting the expected-signature coordinates $\mathbb{E}\inner{\mathrm{Sig}^{(m)}_{0,t}}{w}$ together with state-weighted coordinates $\mathbb{E}[X_t^{\gamma}\inner{\mathrm{Sig}^{(m)}_{0,t}}{w}]$ for all $|\gamma|+|w|\le m$, and there is a constant matrix $A_m$ depending on the affine characteristics in (equation eq:affine-generator of the paper) such that
\begin{equation}
\frac{\,\mathrm{d}}{\,\mathrm{d} t}U_t=A_mU_t,
\qquad
\mathbb{E}[\mathrm{Sig}^{(m)}_{0,t}]=\Pi_m e^{tA_m}U_0,

\end{equation}
where $\Pi_m$ selects the coordinates with no state weight.
title: linear closure of the affine expected signature

body:
[Definition 1 of arXiv:2608.19065, 'Boundedly exchangeable graphs'] An adjacency measure on $S$ is a simple measure $\xi$ on $S^2\times\{0,1\}$ such that
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
    \item there is a simple measure $\nu$ on $S$ with $\xi(C\times\{0,1\}) = \nu^{\otimes 2}(C)$ for every $C \in \Bcal(S)^{\otimes 2}$,
    \item $(\theta \otimes \mathrm{id})\,\xi = \xi$, where $\theta(x,y)=(y,x)$ and $\mathrm{id}$ denotes the identity function on $\{0,1\}$.
\end{enumerate}
For $B\in\mathcal{B}(S)$, the $B$-restriction of $\xi$ is the adjacency measure $\xi\vert_{B \times B \times \{0,1\}}$, which we denote by $\xi\vert_B$ for brevity.

[Theorem thm:main_CPMRE of arXiv:2606.10257, 'Downward conditional monotonicity gives survival and extinction for contact processes in r'] Consider the CPMRE described above with increasing infection rate vector $\beta=(\beta_0,\beta_1,\ldots,\beta_{k-1})$, decreasing recovery rate vector $\mu=(\mu_0,\mu_1,\dots,\mu_{k-1})$, 
	and irreducible, monotone environmental process with generator matrix $T$. Let the initial environmental distribution at each site be arbitrary.	
	\begin{longlist}
		\setlength{\itemindent}{28pt}

		\setlength{\labelsep}{0.4em}
		\item If the MMPP with $\beta,T$ is DCM and 
		$\frac{\beta^*}{\max_j\mu_j}>\lambda_c$, 
		then the CPMRE survives (strongly).
		\item If the permutation-reversed MMPP with $\widehat\mu,\widehat{T}$ is DCM and 
		$\frac{\max_j\beta_j}{\mu^*}\leq\lambda_c$, 
		then the CPMRE goes extinct.
	\end{longlist} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: CPMRE survival and extinction

[Lemma 35 (A globally smooth representative of the bulk statistic) of arXiv:2608.07820, 'Linear Spectral Statistics for Entrywise-Transformed Spiked Wigner Matrices under Shifted '] Fix \(\Gamma\) satisfying (G1)--(G4), and let
\(\varphi_1,\ldots,\varphi_k\) be analytic near
\(\overline{D_\Gamma}\).  There exist
\(\widetilde\varphi_\ell\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R)\) such that, for both

\begin{equation}
 \Tr\widetilde\varphi_\ell(M_N)

\end{equation}
with probability \(1-o(1)\).  In the supercritical case,
\(\widetilde\varphi_\ell\) vanishes on a fixed neighborhood of
\(\rho_\theta\).

body: Rouche's theorem: Let C be a simple closed contour (one without self-intersections) such that C together with its interior is contained in a region on which the complex-valued functions f and g are holomorphic. If |g(z)| < |f(z)| for every z on C, then f and f + g have the same number of zeros in the interior of C, each zero counted with its multiplicity. (The hypothesis forces f, and hence f + g, to have no zeros on C itself.)
title: Rouché's theorem

[Corollary 10 of arXiv:2603.28226, '2603.28226'] In the setting of Proposition~\ref{prop:global-joint-sharpness}, take $\beta=1$. Then every decomposition
\[
 f=g+h+k,
 \qquad 0\le k\le\lambda,
\]
satisfies
\[
 \mathbb P\Bigl(\sup_{n\ge1}|\mathbb E_n[g]|>0\Bigr)=1
 \qquad\text{or}\qquad
 \Bigl\|\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}|\mathbb E_n[h]-\mathbb E_{n-1}[h]|\Bigr\|_1
 \ge2(1-p)\|f\|_1.
\]
Consequently, no pair of constants $c_1<1$ and $c_2<2$ can simultaneously replace the coefficients in Theorem~\ref{thm:stein-gundy}\textup{(a)--(b)} under the same condition $0\le k\le\lambda$.

There are exactly 3566 self-avoiding walks of length 11 that start at (0,0), stay in the strip 0 <= y < 3, and avoid the sites (3,0), (5,0). [Prop cocycles into Aut(N) reduce to lattice stabiliser of arXiv:2605.16921, '${\ASL_n}(\mathbb Z)$ invariant random subsets of $\mathbb Z^n$'] Let $N$ be a nilpotent Lie group of the form $\mathbb{Z}^d \ltimes N_0$ with $d \geq 3$ and $N_0$ connected simply connected, and let $\Gamma \subset N$ be a lattice and $H \subset \Gamma$ be a subgroup. Let $\Delta \subset \Aut(N)$ be a subgroup such that $\delta(H) = H$ and $\delta(\Gamma)$ is commensurable with $\Gamma$ for every $\delta \in \Delta$. Let $(X, \nu)$ be an ergodic $\SL_d(\mathbb{Z})$-system and $\alpha: \SL_d(\mathbb{Z}) \times X \to \Delta$ be a map satisfying the cocycle equation modulo inner automorphisms of $H$ in $\Delta$.

    Then there exist a finite group extension $\pi: \tilde{X} \to X$, a lattice $\Gamma' \subset N$ containing $H$ and a measurable map $\phi: \tilde{X} \rightarrow \Delta$ such that 
    $$ \phi(\gamma\cdot\tilde{x}) \alpha(\gamma,  \pi(\tilde{x})) \phi(\tilde{x})$$ belongs to $\{\delta \in \Delta : \delta(\Gamma') = \Gamma'\}$ for all $\gamma \in \SL_d(\mathbb{Z})$  and almost all $\tilde{x} \in \tilde{X}$.
title: Prop cocycles into Aut(N) reduce to lattice stabiliser of arXiv:2605.16921

[Dfn 38 of arXiv:2507.08909, 'Annealed almost periodic entropy'] Let $\phi:\A \to \rmM_k$ and $\psi:\A \to \rmM_\ell$ be completely positive.  A \textbf{joining} of them is a completely positive map $\theta:\A\to \rmM_{k+\ell}$ such that
\[\theta(a)[K] = \phi(a) \qquad \hbox{and} \qquad \theta(a)[L] = \psi(a) \qquad (a \in \A).\]
In particular, the \textbf{diagonal joining} is defined by
\[\rm{diag}(\phi,\psi)(a) := \left[\begin{array}{cc} \phi(a) & 0\\ 0 & \psi(a)\end{array}\right] \qquad (a \in \A).\]

Joinings of more than two completely positive maps are defined similarly.  If $\phi$ is a positive functional and $k$ is a positive integer, then we write $\phi\otimes I_k$ for the diagonal joining of $k$ copies of $\phi$.

[Proposition \cite{Trinh-Trinh-Jacobi} of arXiv:2412.01015, 'Classical beta ensembles and related eigenvalues processes at high temperature and the Mar'] Assume that the initial measure $\mu_0^{(N)}$ converges weakly to a probability measure $\mu_0$. Then the following hold.
	\begin{itemize}
		\item[\rm (i)] For each $n = 1, 2,\dots,$ the sequence of moment processes $S_n^{(N)}(t) = \bra{\mu_t^{(N)}, x^n}$ converges in probability as random elements in $C([0, T])$ to a deterministic limit $m_n(t)$, which is defined inductively as the solution to the following initial value ODE
		\begin{align*}
			&m_n'(t) = -n(2c+a+b+n+1) m_n(t) + n(a+n)m_{n-1}(t)\\
			&\qquad\qquad + cn \sum_{i=0}^{n-1}m_i(t) m_{n-1-i}(t) - cn \sum_{j=1}^{n-1} m_j(t) m_{n-j}(t),\\
			&m_n(0) = \lim_{N\to \infty} \bra{\mu_0^{(N)}, x^n}, \quad (n \ge 1).
		\end{align*}
Here $m_0(t) \equiv 1$.

		\item[\rm(ii)] For any $t \ge 0$, let $\mu_t$ be the unique probability measure with moments $\{m_n(t)\}$. Then the sequence $\mu_t^{(N)}$ converges in probability to $(\mu_t)_{0 \le t \le T}$ as random elements in the space of continuous maps from $[0,T]$ to the space of probability measures on $[0,1]$ endowed with the uniform topology.
	\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: \cite{Trinh-Trinh-Jacobi}

[Theorem 3 (=Theorem \ref{invtpoly}) of arXiv:2609.00448, 'Equivariant formality and representation theory'] Let $G$ be a compact connected Lie group of rank $n$, $S$ a torus subgroup of dimension being $n-1$, $T$ a maximal torus of $G$ containing $S$, $\mu\in \chi(T)$ a primitive character of $T$ such that $S=\text{ker }\mu$, $L$ a primitive weight in the weight lattice $\mathfrak{t}^*_\mathbb{Z}$ corresponding to $\mu$ after exponentiation, and $W$ the Weyl group of $G$. Define
	\[\Phi_L:=\left(\prod_{w\in W/W_{[L]}} wL\right)^{n(L)}\in \text{Sym}^*(\mathfrak{t}^*)^W,\]
	where $W_{[L]}$ is the stabilizer of $[L]:=\{\pm L\}\in \mathfrak{t}^*/\{\pm 1\}$, $n(L)=1$ or 2 depending on whether $\displaystyle\prod_{w\in W/W_{[L]}}wL$ is $W$-invariant or $W$-anti-invariant, i.e. 
	\[\displaystyle w'(\prod_{w\in W/W_{[L]}}wL)=\text{sgn}(w')\prod_{w\in W/W_{[L]}}wL\text{ for all }w'\in W.\] 
	Then $(G, S)$ is isotropy formal if and only if $\Phi_L\notin (f_1, \cdots, f_n)^2$, where $f_1, \cdots, f_n$ are the fundamental $W$-invariant homogeneous polynomials on $\mathfrak{t}$, i.e. $\text{Sym}^*(\mathfrak{t}^*)^W=\mathbb{R}[f_1, \cdots, f_n]$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: =Theorem \ref{invtpoly}
